latestRelease.name: ProsperoTV 01.000.090
latestRelease.body:
## New since 01.000.080

### Watching

- **The TV's own remote.** With **Settings > System > HDMI > Enable HDMI Device Link** on (and the TV's CEC setting), the television's remote works in the menu and the player, beside the controller or instead of it. Arrows move, OK selects, Back goes back, Play / Pause plays or pauses, Rewind and Fast forward page through lists and step through a video, Channel − / + change the channel on live TV, and Menu opens the playback panel. Which keys reach the console is up to the television; arrows, OK and Back always do. The README has the full table.
- **Reaching the tabs.** Up from the top of a screen, or Circle on Live TV, focuses the tab bar; Left and Right change the tab there, and Down, Cross or Circle go back in. Left of Home is a Search button, and Left from the search field reaches the results.
- **Cross pauses.** During playback Cross pauses and resumes, as OK on a TV remote does; in the open channel list it still watches the channel. L2 now opens and closes the live channel list, and the phone remote has a **Channel list** button.

### Sources

- **Films and shows counted.** The Sources panel, the Settings tab and its At a glance panel show how many films and shows a source holds beside its channels, each on its own line in Sources. The channel figure counts live channels only, so a playlist's films and episodes no longer inflate it, and the header chip gives the total of all three. The counts refresh with the catalog and after an On Demand download finishes.

### Fixes

- **A channel in every category it belongs to.** Newer Xtream panels can file a live channel under several categories, and the app only read the first, so a category made up of such channels was missing from the list and from search. Every category the provider names now lists the channel, and a channel in any adult category is treated as an adult channel.

### Maintenance

- The interface kit, the OpenGL SDK and the owned-root helper are fetched from LedyBacer's copies of their original repositories, which are gone; the pinned commits and checksums are unchanged.

## Validation notes

Host tests cover the TV remote reader and its key mapping, tab focus and the search button, Cross and L2 in the player, the film and show counts read from saved lists and playlists, and Xtream channels with several categories.

## Thanks

Thank you to everyone who made this version:

- **ThatGuyKalvin** ([GitHub](https://github.com/ThatGuyKalvin)), for the TV remote, the tab bar and search controls, and the film and show counts.
- **Oliv3rmoon** ([GitHub](https://github.com/Oliv3rmoon)), for listing a channel in every category its provider names.
- **Cold** ([GitHub](https://github.com/JMUtechnologies)), for the report of the missing category.
- Everyone who tests ProsperoTV and reports what they find. The full list is in the [README](https://github.com/ThatGuyKalvin/ProsperoTV#thanks).

## Installing by hand

- `PPSA99003.zip`: extract it and upload the complete `PPSA99003` folder to `/data/homebrew`, replacing the old one after closing the app. Keep your existing data under `/data/prosperotv`.
- `SHA256SUMS`: the checksum of the download.
- Coming from 01.000.015 or older: close ProsperoTV, delete `PPSA99003.ffpfsc` from `/data/homebrew` if you used the image, then upload the folder and restart ShadowMountPlus or the console.

Release files are built by this repository's GitHub Actions from the version tag on the release commit from `main`.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/ThatGuyKalvin/ProsperoTV/compare/01.000.080...01.000.090

repos.name: ps5-theme
repos.description: Custom home-screen themes for jailbroken PS5 consoles (etaHEN plugin or standalone payload): backgrounds, icons, sounds, fonts and home music as read-only overlays.
repos.readme: # PS5 Themes (ps5-theme) Custom home-screen themes for jailbroken PS5 consoles on firmware 13.60 and below, as an [etaHEN](https://github.com/GronedWaffel/etahen-11.00-13.60) plugin or a standalone payload. Change the home screen's backgrounds, icons, sounds, fonts and home music, keep as many themes as you like, and switch between them from the console, a phone or a computer. The system is never written: every theme is a read-only overlay held in memory, so the console is stock again the moment the plugin stops, and the plugin puts your theme back each time etaHEN starts. ![A theme on the console: Yakuza 0's home background and font, and the icon style on every tile of the home row, the console's own All Apps tile too](docs/screenshots/console-home.jpg) ![The theme library](docs/screenshots/library.png) Version 1.80. Developed and tested on a PS5 with firmware 13.42, both with etaHEN 2.5B (unified build) and on its own from PS5 Payload Manager. > **About the screenshots.** They were taken from the author's own console. > The test themes in them use Peanuts and Yakuza 0 artwork, and the games > shown in the photos use their publishers' artwork; all of it belongs to its > rights holders and is not part of this project. In the manager's screenshots > the console's own pictures (its interface icons and artwork) and games' and > apps' icons are shown as plain striped stand-ins on purpose: system files > stay on the console and are never redistributed. The photos of the > console's screen show its interface as it appears. ## Contents - [What it does](#what-it-does) - [Requirements](#requirements) - [Install](#install) - [Running without etaHEN](#running-without-etahen) - [Your first theme](#your-first-theme) - [Documentation](#documentation): the guides and the technical pages in [`docs/`](docs/) - [Firmware support and known limits](#firmware-support-and-known-limits) - [Removing](#removing) - [Development Approach](#development-approach) - [Acknowledgements](#acknowledgements) - [Licences and trademarks](#licences-and-trademarks) ## What it does - **Themes tile and web manager.** A **Themes** tile on the home screen opens the manager in the console's browser. The same manager works from any phone or computer on your network at `http://:8095`. - **Build a theme from parts.** Pick a part from the list, as in the console's Settings, and add a file: background, icons, home music, system sounds, fonts, animations, video, textures and other images, the home screen's own tiles and the interface's icons. Each part in the list shows a small picture of what the theme puts there, and Previous, Next and the browser's Back step between parts. - **Icon style.** Give every game's and app's icon one look: its own icon in a circle, rounded square, hexagon or other shape over a colour, the theme's background or a picture of yours, and the home screen's own tiles (PlayStation Store, Game Library, Media Gallery and the rest) with them. Games installed later are styled by the plugin itself once their install is over, and a game installed again gets the theme's pictures back by itself (see [Games and apps](docs/manager.md#games-and-apps)). - **Game and app icons.** Change the icon, background and logo of any installed game or app, homebrew and PlayStation Network artwork included. The Game Library shows them at once, and the home screen after rest mode; games and apps keep starting as before (see [Changing game and app icons safely](docs/challenges.md#changing-game-and-app-icons-safely)). - **Any file, fitted for you.** One image fills every size of an asset. Any audio file is converted to the exact format and loudness of the sound it replaces, including the console's ATRAC9 home music. The browser does this, and the console checks every file again. - **Appearance themes.** Replace the Control Center's bottom panel, the corner piece by the clock and the home screen artwork of the PlayStation, PlayStation 2, 3 and 4 themes, with placement and see-through parts, and a preview drawn from the very textures the console will use (see [Appearance themes](docs/appearance-themes.md)). - **Fonts.** Replace the text fonts the home screen and Settings draw with, for the home screen only (see [Fonts](docs/fonts.md)). - **Home music editor.** Pick the part of a song to use, an optional loop part, the order they play in, how the joints sound and the loudness, then hear it before you apply it. Or make a [playlist](docs/home-music.md#playlists) of up to 8 songs that play one after another. - **Wake-up sound.** Replace the sound the console plays as it wakes from rest mode (see [The wake-up sound](docs/home-music.md#the-wake-up-sound)). - **Interface sounds.** Replace the sounds of moving between items, selecting, going back and the rest, and the PlayStation 1 to 4 Appearance themes' own, from any audio file, written in Sony's own sound format and layout (see [Sounds](docs/manager.md#sounds)). - **Preview pictures.** Each theme's card shows its background, or any picture you choose, so you can tell themes apart at a glance. - **Save and Discard.** Changes are kept as unsaved until you save them, and Discard puts the theme back as it was. - **Clear progress.** Applying shows what the console is doing and how far it has got. - **Mix and match.** Make a new theme from parts of the ones you have: each part, or each element of it (a background area, a game's icon, one interface sound), taken from the theme you choose (see [Mix and match](docs/manager.md#mix-and-match)). - **Library tools.** Duplicate, export to a `.zip`, import a `.zip` or a folder (drag it in), and delete. - **Comes back by itself.** The applied theme is put back every time etaHEN starts the plugin, after a reboot or an update. Only **No theme** stops it. - **Leaves room for the console.** The plugin keeps 1 GB of the console's storage free for its own saves and records, and refuses a file that would eat into it (see [When the console's storage is nearly full](docs/manager.md#when-the-consoles-storage-is-nearly-full)). - **Safe through rest mode.** Nothing of a theme goes into the home screen while the console is starting it, nor into any app's sandbox while the home screen restarts, and all of it comes out the moment the home screen stops, the plugin crashing included (see [A home screen that never came back](docs/challenges.md#a-home-screen-that-never-came-back) and [A console that didn't wake (again)](docs/challenges.md#a-console-that-didnt-wake-again)). If the console ever doesn't wake, hold its power button until it beeps twice and switches off, then start it: the theme comes back with the plugin. Send the Activity log with what happened. - **Never writes the system.** Nothing under `/system` or `/system_ex` is opened for writing, only media files can be themed, and every file is checked against the system file it replaces (see [what the checks cover](docs/how-it-works.md#what-the-checks-cover-and-what-they-dont)). ## Requirements - A PS5 on firmware 13.60 or below, jailbroken, running etaHEN or any jailbreak with the standard ELF loader (see [Running without etaHEN](#running-without-etahen)). Tested on 13.42 with [etaHEN 2.5B unified](https://github.com/GronedWaffel/etahen-11.00-13.60/releases/tag/v2.5B-unified.1), which covers 11.00 to 13.60 except 11.40. - A phone or computer on the same network is the easiest way to add files. The console's own browser works for applying and switching themes. - To build from source: Docker. Nothing else on the host. ## Install 1. Copy `ps5-theme.plugin` to `/data/etaHEN/plugins/` on the console. 2. Turn on auto-start, so it runs whenever etaHEN runs. Either: - create an empty file `/data/etaHEN/plugins/ps5-theme.plugin.auto_start`, or - turn on auto-start for it in the etaHEN Toolbox plugin list. 3. Start it from the Toolbox, or jailbreak again. On its first start the plugin lists the home screen's own assets (before any theme is mounted), starts the manager on port **8095**, adds the **Themes** tile, and shows a notification with the address to open from a phone or computer. **Updating:** copy the new `.plugin` file over the old one in `/data/etaHEN/plugins/`. Within about 20 seconds the running plugin finds it, starts it through etaHEN's ELF loader and hands over to it. Your theme stays on the screen the whole time, and no Toolbox or restart is needed, which matters after rest mode, when etaHEN's Toolbox is often gone. An open manager page reloads itself with the new version. (This works from 1.23 on: to get 1.23 itself from an older version, restart the console once.) A newer `ps5-theme.elf` or `.plugin` in `/data/ps5-theme/update/` works the same way, with or without etaHEN. Once the new version runs, it also takes the place of the older copies installed in etaHEN's plugin folder and PS5 Payload Manager's payload folders, so the next start runs the new version too, and then the file in the update folder is removed (since 1.62). **If the manager can't be reached:** start ps5-theme again (from the Toolbox or PS5 Payload Manager). The new copy takes over from the running one even when that one doesn't answer, and keeps your theme. If that doesn't help, start `ps5-theme-stop.elf` from a payload loader or PS5 Payload Manager, then start ps5-theme again. It stops the running copy and leaves your theme on the screen, apart from the games' and apps' pictures until ps5-theme runs again (see [Stopping without a restart](docs/how-it-works.md#stopping-without-a-restart)). No restart is needed in either case. ## Running without etaHEN The plugin doesn't need etaHEN, only a jailbreak: a kernel exploit and the standard PS5 ELF loader (port 9021) that ps5-payload-sdk programs run under. It gets its own privileges, and everything else is its own code. Every release has both files, which contain the same program: - `ps5-theme.elf`: for any ELF loader, such as [PS5 Payload Manager](https://github.com/itsPLK/ps5-payload-manager); - `ps5-theme.plugin`: for etaHEN, the same program with etaHEN's header. **With PS5 Payload Manager:** - **Install it from its repository** (from 1.73 on): in Payload Manager, **Settings → Manage Sources**, add `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Blaze414/ps5-theme/main/pldmgr/repository.json`. PS5 Themes then shows with its logo, version, author and description, and each new release appears as an update (see [Building](docs/building.md#ps5-payload-managers-repository)). - **Or start it by hand:** put `ps5-theme.elf` in a folder under `/data/pldmgr/payloads/` (or import it from USB) and launch it from the manager. It then does everything it does under etaHEN: the web manager, the Themes tile, and putting the selected theme back. - **Start it after every jailbreak:** add it to the manager's autoload list. - **Update it:** put the newer `ps5-theme.elf` in `/data/ps5-theme/update/` (or replace the installed one). Within about 20 seconds the running copy finds it, starts it through the ELF loader and hands over, keeping your theme on the screen. The new version then takes the place of the copy Payload Manager starts (`/data/pldmgr/payloads/local/ps5-theme/` on newer versions of Payload Manager), so autoload starts the new version next time. Every build carries its version inside the program, which is how a plain `.elf` is recognised. **Keeping both as a backup:** you can set up `ps5-theme.elf` in Payload Manager and `ps5-theme.plugin` with auto-start in etaHEN at the same time. Only one copy ever runs: when the second one starts, it finds the first, and it exits if it isn't newer or takes over if it is. So whichever way starts first, you get one copy, and the newest one. **What's different without etaHEN:** nothing starts it at boot unless your jailbreak or Payload Manager does. Both ways have been run on a PS5 with 13.42: `ps5-theme.elf` from PS5 Payload Manager, and `ps5-theme.plugin` from etaHEN. If something works differently on your setup, the Activity page says what happened. ## Your first theme 1. Open the **Themes** tile, or `http://:8095` on a phone or computer. 2. Press **New theme**, give it a name and press **Create**. 3. Its edit page opens. Choose **Background** in the list and drop in a picture. Add home music, icons or sounds the same way. The guides to [backgrounds](docs/backgrounds.md) and [home music](docs/home-music.md) go step by step. 4. Press **Save** in the bar at the bottom, then **Apply**. 5. Give it a few seconds. The home screen may show the console's own look for a moment while it switches. 6. **To hear new home music,** move to a game or app on the home screen that has its own music, so the console switches to that music, then come back. The console keeps playing the music it already had loaded and only picks up the theme's music when it starts the home music again. To change only the music, make a theme with just **Home music**. Everything else stays stock. ## Documentation | Page | What's in it | |---|---| | [Backgrounds](docs/backgrounds.md) | Changing the home screen's backgrounds: a step-by-step guide, where each background is used, what it needs, and how they are made | | [Home music](docs/home-music.md) | Giving the home screen your own music (one song or a playlist): a step-by-step guide to the music editor, when you hear it, what it needs, and how it is made; and your own [wake-up sound](docs/home-music.md#the-wake-up-sound) | | [Changing game and app icons](docs/games-and-apps.md) | Installed games' and apps' icons, backgrounds and logos; the console's own tiles; interface icons | | [Appearance themes](docs/appearance-themes.md) | The Control Center's panels and the home screen artwork of the PlayStation 1 to 4 themes: a step-by-step guide, what it needs, how it depends on the anniversary assets, and how they are made and stored | | [Fonts](docs/fonts.md) | Replacing the console's text fonts, and which ones the home screen uses | | [A tour of the manager](docs/manager.md) | Every page and control of the web manager | | [How it works, and why](docs/how-it-works.md) | Overlays instead of writing the system, sandbox views, checks, staging, updating and stopping | | [Theme format](docs/theme-format.md) | What a theme folder and its export contain | | [Challenges and how they were solved](docs/challenges.md) | The problems met on the console and their solutions, including [changing game and app icons safely](docs/challenges.md#changing-game-and-app-icons-safely) and [finding the Appearance artwork](docs/challenges.md#the-appearance-themes-artwork) | | [Testing](docs/testing.md) | The automated tests, the [tests on the console](docs/testing.md#tests-on-the-console), and [each problem found on the console with the test that keeps it fixed](docs/testing.md#problems-found-on-the-console-and-the-tests-that-keep-them-fixed) | | [Testing on your own console](docs/hardware-testing.md) | Trying a release on your PS5: the steps, what you should see, how to get back if something goes wrong, and how to report it | | [Building from source](docs/building.md) | Building the plugin and the tools, [checking that a release is exactly what its source builds](docs/building.md#reproducible-builds), and the project layout | | [Security](docs/security.md) | Who can reach the plugin, what protects the system, fuzzing, [reporting a security problem](docs/security.md#reporting-a-security-problem) | | [Architecture](docs/architecture.md) | For contributors: the parts, threads and locks, what the plugin keeps on the console, applying a theme step by step, and what happens when something fails | | [Design decisions](docs/decisions.md) | The hard choices, each with what forced it, what else was considered and what it costs | | [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) | The rules no change may break, how to make and test a change, and how to report bugs | Links to this page's old sections (from earlier release notes) land here; the table says where each one is now. ## Firmware support and known limits - Built for firmware up to 13.60; tested on 13.42 with etaHEN 2.5B unified. - On other firmware, the asset list, sandbox views and tile registration are all discovered on the console, but they haven't been tried there. If a theme doesn't show, leave and re-enter the home screen, or jailbreak again; the theme is put back at start either way. - New home music is heard only once the console starts its home music again: move to a game or app that has its own music, then come back (see [Home music](docs/home-music.md#when-you-hear-it)). Its position is kept by the console (see [Music that starts part-way through](docs/challenges.md#music-that-starts-part-way-through)). - After rest mode, the plugin covers the new views ShellUI's restarted apps make (see [Stock again after rest mode](docs/challenges.md#stock-again-after-rest-mode)). An app that read its background before the overlay arrived may show stock until it reloads; **Apply again** brings it back at once. etaHEN's own Toolbox stopping after rest mode is outside this plugin. - Background and icon sorting is by file name. Anything it misses is under **Other images**. - The home screen's layout can't be themed (it is code). Its colours are in the interface's palettes: **Edit colours** changes the widgets, the Control Center, the button hints, the text and the accent (see [Colours](docs/appearance-themes.md#colours)). - The sound when the console is switched on plays before the jailbreak, so a theme can't change it. The sound as it wakes from rest mode can. - Interface pictures: the console reads its resource files when the interface starts, so changed ones show after rest mode or a restart. The numbered test drew nothing beside the **Games** and **Media** tabs on 13.42. Whether the console draws your own picture inside a vector icon hasn't been seen on the console yet. - etaHEN's plugin **Stop** ends the plugin at once, with no chance to tidy up: overlays stay until you choose **No theme** in the library, start the plugin again, or reboot. With games' icons or a font in the theme, choose **No theme** (or use `ps5-theme-stop`) before stopping it that way: an overlay left in the home screen's own folders when it restarts at rest mode can keep it, or every app, from starting until the console restarts. ## Removing 1. Choose **No theme** in the library. 2. Delete `/data/etaHEN/plugins/ps5-theme.plugin*` and `/data/ps5-theme/`. 3. Delete the **Themes** tile from the home screen. ## Development Approach This project explores AI-assisted development for PS5 homebrew, with an emphasis on practical validation rather than accepting generated code at face value. Claude Code was used to assist with implementation, debugging and iterative improvements. Development was guided by testing on physical PS5 hardware, examining application logs, investigating observed failures and verifying fixes on the console. The project combines hardware testing with host-side automated tests to exercise application behaviour, error handling and recovery scenarios. The aim is to evaluate how AI-assisted development can be used to build a useful console utility while maintaining a focus on reliability, safety and reproducibility. AI assistance does not replace testing or eliminate the need for continued review. Firmware compatibility and known limitations are documented separately. ## Acknowledgements This project stands on the work of people who share what they learn with everyone. My deepest gratitude to each of them. Without their work, their openness and the time they gave freely, none of this would exist. - **etaHEN**, by LightningMods and its contributors, and **[GronedWaffel](https://github.com/GronedWaffel)** for the [11.00–13.60 unified build](https://github.com/GronedWaffel/etahen-11.00-13.60) this was built and tested on. etaHEN is the foundation everything here runs on: the plugin format, auto-start and the Toolbox card installer, whose approach the Themes tile follows. - **[ps5-payload-dev/sdk](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk)**, by John Törnblom and contributors: the toolchain, the kernel access and the examples the whole plugin is built with. - **[kstuff-lite](https://github.com/EchoStretch/kstuff-lite)**, by EchoStretch, which ships with the etaHEN build this was developed on. - **[LibAtrac9](https://github.com/Thealexbarney/LibAtrac9)**, by Alex Barney (MIT License): the ATRAC9 codebooks and bitstream layout behind the encoder and the plugin's checks, and one of the two reference decoders in the tests. Without it, home music would not have been possible. - **[FFmpeg](https://ffmpeg.org/)** and its ATRAC9 decoder, the second independent reference in the codec tests. - **[vgmstream](https://github.com/vgmstream/vgmstream)**, by Adam Gashlin, bnnm and contributors (ISC licence): its HE-VAG decoder and predictor table are how the manager plays the interface's sounds and writes new ones. - **[ShadowMountPlus](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus)** by drakmor, **[PS5-File-Explorer](https://github.com/juma-sayeh/PS5-File-Explorer)** by juma-sayeh and **[onionHEN](https://github.com/aydencharles/onionHEN)** by aydencharles, whose home-screen app registration and navigation work etaHEN's Toolbox card builds on, and through it the Themes tile. - **[ps5-webkit-autoloader](https://github.com/itsPLK/ps5-webkit-autoloader)** by itsPLK, which showed that a home-screen app can open a page served by a payload on the console itself. - **[PSDevWiki](https://www.psdevwiki.com/ps5/)** and everyone who documents the PS5 there, in particular `param.json` and its `deeplinkUri`. - **Zstandard and xxHash**, by Yann Collet and the zstd contributors: the format specification (RFC 8878) and the educational decoder that the plugin's decoder follows. - **Microsoft's Direct3D documentation** of the BC7 format, which the texture encoder follows. - **[PS5Themes](https://github.com/MasterPS0/PS5Themes)** by MasterPS0, whose theme packs showed which files hold the home screen's tab icons, tile icons and per-tile backgrounds. - **[PS5SX2](https://github.com/Swordpdf/PS5SX2)** by Swordpdf and **[ATRACTool-Reloaded](https://github.com/XyLe-GBP/ATRACTool-Reloaded)** by XyLe-GBP, studied while working out how to get music onto the home screen. - Everyone in the PS5 homebrew community who tests, reports and explains: your write-ups and answers made the hard parts possible. ## Licences and trademarks Copyright (C) 2026 Blaze414 - **ps5-theme is free software under the GNU General Public License, version 3 or (at your option) any later version** (GPL-3.0-or-later). The full text is in [`LICENSE`](LICENSE). You may use, study, change and share it; if you share a changed version, it must stay under the same licence with its source available. It comes with no warranty. - Why the GPL: the plugin is built with [ps5-payload-sdk](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk), whose kernel interface is GPL-3.0-or-later (© John Törnblom), so the plugin as built is under the same terms. - The ATRAC9 tables are generated from LibAtrac9, © 2018 Alex Barney, MIT License (`licenses/LibAtrac9.txt`), which allows their use in a GPL project. - The HE-VAG predictor table is from vgmstream, © 2008-2025 Adam Gashlin et al., ISC licence (`licenses/vgmstream.txt`), which allows the same. - No system files are included. The plugin works with the files on your own console, and the stock copies it keeps never leave it. - "PlayStation", "PS5" and "ATRAC" are trademarks of Sony Interactive Entertainment Inc. or Sony Group Corporation. latestRelease.name: ps5-theme 1.80
latestRelease.body:
Custom home-screen themes for jailbroken PS5 consoles on firmware 13.60 and below. Runs as an etaHEN plugin or on its own from any ELF loader. Tested on firmware 13.42, both with etaHEN 2.5B (unified build) and from PS5 Payload Manager.

## Which file?

- **`ps5-theme.plugin`**: for etaHEN. Copy it to `/data/etaHEN/plugins/` and turn on auto-start.
- **`ps5-theme.elf`**: the same program for [PS5 Payload Manager](https://github.com/itsPLK/ps5-payload-manager) or any ELF loader (port 9021). No etaHEN needed. New: Payload Manager can install it from this project's repository, with its name, logo and version: add `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Blaze414/ps5-theme/main/pldmgr/repository.json`.
- **`ps5-theme-stop.elf`**: only for when the manager can't be reached. Start it from Payload Manager or a payload loader, then start ps5-theme again. It stops the plugin and leaves your theme on the screen. Put it in a folder of its own under `/data/pldmgr/payloads/`.

## Updating

- **From 1.23 or later:** put the new file in `/data/ps5-theme/update/` (or copy it over the old one). Within about 10 seconds the running plugin finds it and hands over, keeping your theme on the screen. No restart needed. The new version then takes the place of the older copies in etaHEN's and PS5 Payload Manager's folders, and the update folder empties itself. If your copy tool fills a file in after making it, upload it as `ps5-theme.elf.part` and rename it when it's done.
- **From 1.22 or older:** copy the new file and restart the console once.

## New since 1.64

**Making themes**
- **Mix and match** (1.65): a new theme made of parts of your others, down to single interface pictures and sounds.
- **Icon style** (1.66): every game's and app's icon in one shape (circle, rounded square, square, diamond, hexagon, triangle) over a colour, the theme's background or a picture of yours, and **the console's own home tiles too** (1.74): Welcome, PlayStation Store and Plus, Game Library, Media Gallery, the Media home's tiles and the disc tiles, each drawn as it will look. Games installed later are styled by the plugin itself, 2 minutes after their install settles, and the console says so by name (1.73, 1.76).
- **The console's own icons in the manager** (1.66): the edit page's parts list is drawn with the console's own interface icons, read from the console as the page runs.
- The manager follows the console: games installed or removed show without reloading (1.72). A theme can change files in up to 256 folders (1.75).

**Faster**
- **Applying the same theme again takes about 2 seconds**, from 36 on 1.77: no waits on folders the home screen keeps open, a game's folder read only when it changed, and the list of overlays written a line at a time. The home screen shows its own look for under 2 seconds while a theme switches. Activity's apply line now says how long each step took.
- The manager's page is sent compressed (a third of the size), and pictures are re-sent only when they changed. Through an apply, the library no longer redraws every second: the progress bar slides and nothing under the pointer changes.

**Safer**
- **Rest mode:** nothing of a theme goes into any app's sandbox while the home screen restarts, and an app's new folder views are covered only once the system has finished making them (1.80; 1.79 didn't wake once because of this). Since 1.68, nothing goes into the home screen's own sandbox until it runs, and everything comes out the moment it stops.
- **Discard** can no longer leave a theme empty when an upload or the icon styler is writing at the same moment, and a Discard cut off by a crash or a power loss is put right at the next start.
- An update copied in half is no longer missed; `ps5-theme-stop` asks the plugin over its web port first; a theme nested very deep can't crash the plugin; timers survive the console setting its clock; opening another theme while icons are being styled waits until they're done.

Everything in [1.64](https://github.com/Blaze414/ps5-theme/releases/tag/v1.64) is included. What each problem was and how it was solved: [Challenges](https://github.com/Blaze414/ps5-theme/blob/main/docs/challenges.md); how the bugs were found: [Testing](https://github.com/Blaze414/ps5-theme/blob/main/docs/testing.md#how-the-bugs-were-found).

### Checked

72 end-to-end tests on the host, each run in full, with mounts emulated and under ThreadSanitizer (no data race), including a seeded test of every combination of the manager's actions (12,000 requests over 10 runs); 15 parsers fuzzed (about 35 million inputs). On a PS5 with 13.42: the update from 1.79, Apply again in 2.0 seconds, and three rest-mode cycles in a row, each waking with the theme.

## Checksums (SHA-256)

```
91b8143abcf4a54ee84f3de6c167d95f07002b3f8cf5f51ff6508e9f245534de  ps5-theme.plugin
e27473f0f5d3a9c544ed075f3f0a0e831377e0ab5e6316dce81ad732a99c04eb  ps5-theme.elf
90a1ee926eba4277e1ed2827191151872e4d113de0c566614db51d1b4506230c  ps5-theme-stop.elf
```

repos.name: ps5-debugger
repos.description: PS5 debugger payload — userland TCP wire-protocol server hosted inside SceShellCore. GPL-3.
repos.readme:
# ps5debug-NG GUI

![Preview Image](./assets/preview.png)

This is a graphical user interface for interacting with the debugger payload.
Note that this application is under active development, and has only been 
tested on Windows and firmware 11.60.

This app is a GUI built around the ps5debug payload from OpenSourcereR, all credits go to them.

If any issues arise please open an issue.

### Features

- Memory viewer
- Memory scanner
- Process list
- Process memory dump
- Process memory edit
- Memory dump
- Logging

### Known issues

- Memory scanner might fail or crash the PS5, use with caution.
- Only Windows support for the moment, but Linux, MacOS, Android and iOS will follow soon.

### How to use

- To use the GUI, remember to first inject the `ps5debug-NG.elf` into the system.

### ps5debug-NG ELF

A debugger payload for jailbroken PlayStation 5 consoles. Ships a userland
command server that runs inside SceShellCore, letting remote clients inspect
and manipulate running processes, the kernel itself, and the system UI over a
simple TCP protocol.

ps5debug-NG is inspired by Ctn's `ps5debug 1.0b5` and is wire-compatible with
it - existing clients should work without modification. It is licensed under
GPL-3.

Discord Server: [Team Reaper](https://discord.gg/7bjtgZf4PY)

---

## Supported firmwares

The kernel kpatch routine in [installer/source/main.c](installer/source/main.c)
recognises the following firmware families. Booting on an unsupported FW prints
`port_outer: kpatch SKIP - unsupported FW magic 0x...` to the kernel log and
aborts cleanly.

| Family | Point releases recognised                       | Status                                    |
|--------|-------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|
| 3.xx   | 3.00, 3.10, 3.20, 3.21                          | Fully Verified                            |
| 4.xx   | 4.00, 4.02, 4.03, 4.50, 4.51                    | Fully Verified                            |
| 5.xx   | 5.00, 5.02, 5.10, 5.50                          | Fully Verified                            |
| 6.xx   | 6.00, 6.02, 6.50                                | Fully Verified                            |
| 7.xx   | 7.00, 7.01, 7.01.01, 7.20, 7.40, 7.60, 7.61     | Fully Verified                            |
| 8.xx   | 8.00, 8.20, 8.40, 8.60                          | Fully Verified                            |
| 9.xx   | 9.00, 9.05, 9.20, 9.40, 9.60                    | Fully Verified                            |
| 10.xx  | 10.00, 10.01, 10.20, 10.40, 10.60               | Fully Verified                            |
| 11.xx  | 11.00, 11.20, 11.40, 11.60                      | Fully Verified                            |
| 12.xx  | 12.00, 12.02, 12.20, 12.40, 12.60, 12.70        | Fully Verified                            |
| 13.xx  | 13.00, 13.20                                    | Fully Verified                            |

The point releases above are the exact FW magic values recognised by the switch
in [installer/source/main.c](installer/source/main.c); that file is the source
of truth. Clients can read the running FW with `CMD_FW_VERSION`, which returns
the firmware as a decimal `uint16_t` (e.g. `900` for 9.00, `1240` for 12.40).

---

## Primary Features

### Process inspection and manipulation
- **Enumerate processes** (process name + pid list).
- **Read and write target memory** in streamed chunks.
- **List virtual memory maps** - ranges, protections, backing names.
- **Query process metadata** - name, path, titleId, contentId.
- **Identify the foreground app** (`0xBDDD0006`) - returns pid + titleid +
  contentid + process name + the game's version, parsed server-side from the
  title's `param.sfo`. Useful for clients that need to know what's currently
  running without listing every process.
- **Server-side stack walk** (`CMD_PROC_READ_STACK`) - the server walks the
  RBP chain itself (up to 64 frames) and bundles each frame's saved-RBP,
  return address, frame-local bytes, and a 200-byte code window around the
  return address into one response. Clients avoid paying many TCP round-trips
  per stack frame.
- **Change memory protection** on arbitrary target regions.
- **Allocate / free / hint-allocate** memory inside any target process. Plain
  allocations are served from a server-side **per-pid arena** (one hijack per 16 MB
  segment, then zero-hijack sub-allocation) so heavy concurrent allocation no longer
  trips the thread-hijack crash; transparent to clients, toggleable via `0xBDAACC24`.

### In-target code execution
- **Call arbitrary functions** with up to six SysV ABI register arguments and
  read back `rax` (`CMD_PROC_CALL`) - serviced kernel-side via `sys_proc_cmd`.
- **Install an RPC stub** (`CMD_PROC_INTALL`, opcode `0xBDAA0005`; note the
  source spelling). In the current build this handler is a stub that returns a
  `0` handle and performs no injection.
- **Load ELFs** into a target process - either jump to the entry point
  immediately (`CMD_PROC_ELF`) or return the entry for later invocation
  (`CMD_PROC_ELF_RPC`).

### Full userland debugger
- **Attach** to a single target with `CMD_DEBUG_ATTACH` (sets up an async
  interrupt channel back to the client).
- **Software breakpoints** - up to **30** slots, transparent `0xCC` injection.
- **Hardware watchpoints** - up to **4** DR0-DR3 slots with read / write /
  read-write and 1/2/4/8-byte granularity.
- **Thread control** - list, suspend, resume, single-step, per-thread step.
- **Full register access** - general-purpose, FPU + YMM (AVX), debug registers,
  and the FS/GS segment base addresses (TLS pointers).
- **Continue / stop / halt** the whole process from one command.
- **Asynchronous interrupt packets** delivered on a separate TCP connection so
  the client never polls.

### Kernel access
- Get the **kernel base address**.
- **Read** arbitrary kernel memory.
- **Write** arbitrary kernel memory.

### Built-in Zydis disassembler
Large memory regions never leave the PS5. Three server-side decoder commands
keep bandwidth low:
- `CMD_PROC_DISASM_REGION` - packed 32-byte-per-instruction stream with
  control-flow, memory-operand, and RIP-relative metadata.
- `CMD_PROC_EXTRACT_CODE_XREFS` - all resolved RIP-relative operand targets in
  a region, streamed (not deduplicated server-side).
- `CMD_PROC_FIND_XREFS_TO` - only instructions whose RIP-relative target equals
  a specific address.

### Built-in Keystone assembler (x86-64)
A cross-compiled LLVM-MC Keystone (x86-only, no exceptions / no RTTI, static
~4 MB) is embedded in the payload, exposed via the raw-literal opcode
`0xBDAA0024`. Lets clients assemble asm text into machine code on the console
itself.
- Pure userspace - needs no attached process and no `CMD_PROC_AUTH` handshake.
- Request: `u64 base_addr; u32 ks_opt_syntax;` + asm text (NUL not required).
  `ks_opt_syntax` defaults to Intel; pass 1/2/4/8/0x10 for Intel/ATT/NASM/MASM/GAS.
- Response: `CMD_SUCCESS` + `u32 byte_len; u32 insn_count;` + machine bytes,
  or `CMD_ERROR` + `u32 ks_errno; u32 msg_len;` + Keystone's human-readable error.
- The opcode is deliberately a raw literal (no `CMD_*` macro) so the published
  `CMD_*` set that some clients enumerate stays unchanged.

### Memory scanning
- **Value scan** (`CMD_PROC_SCAN`) - single-pass, 12 value types × 13 compare
  modes (exact, fuzzy, bigger/smaller, between, increased, decreased, changed,
  etc.).
- **Iterative scan** (`SCAN_START` → `SCAN_COUNT` → `SCAN_GET`) - narrows a
  result set over many passes. The client holds the candidate list and streams
  it back each pass; the server re-reads memory and re-compares.
- **AOB scan** (`CMD_PROC_SCAN_AOB`) - byte patterns with a per-byte wildcard
  mask.
- **Multi-pattern AOB scan** (`CMD_PROC_SCAN_AOB_MULTI`) - many patterns in
  one pass.
- **Auth-gated** - only the iterative scan trio (`SCAN_START` / `SCAN_COUNT` /
  `SCAN_GET`) requires a prior `CMD_PROC_AUTH` handshake; the value scan and the
  AOB scans do not.

### Turbo scan family (v1.3.0, additive + capability-gated)
A faster, opt-in scan path (`CMD_PROC_TURBOSCAN_*`, `0xBDAACC10`-`0xBDAACC16`) that
runs alongside the legacy and iterative scanners, which are byte-for-byte
unchanged. A client detects it via `CMD_PROC_TURBOSCAN_CAPS` and falls back to the
iterative trio when it (or a specific engine) is absent. Result format mirrors the
iterative scan, so clients reuse one parser.
- **SIMD comparator** - typed AVX2 (256-bit) exact-match inner loop, ~25-32x the
  per-element compare of the legacy path (`TSE_SIMD_COMPARE`).
- **Server-resident result sets** (`TSE_SERVER_RESIDENT`) - the survivor set can
  live in a per-connection server buffer instead of being re-uploaded each pass;
  rescans refresh each survivor's baseline so "since last scan" deltas work without
  the client holding state. `CMD_PROC_TURBOSCAN_GET` fetches values on demand.
- **Unknown-initial-value scans** (`TSE_SNAPSHOT`) - a membership bitmap + value
  snapshot (RAM, or an NVMe `/data` file for large regions) drives
  increased/decreased/changed narrowing with no known starting value, materialising
  to a compact record list once survivors get sparse. By default the seed **drops
  all-zero slots** (most memory is zeroed and rarely useful); `TS_SNAPSHOT_INCLUDE_ZEROS`
  keeps them.
- **Multi-segment scans** (`TSE_SNAPSHOT_SEGMENTS`) - a single session can cover a
  list of disjoint regions (`TS_SNAPSHOT_SEGMENTS` + a trailing segment list) instead
  of one contiguous range, for both an unknown-value snapshot (`TS_SNAPSHOT`) and a
  known-value server-resident scan (`TS_SERVER_RESIDENT`). The slot/record space spans
  only the mapped segments, so unmapped gaps between selected modules/sections are never
  read and storage scales with the selected bytes - letting a scattered selection use
  the turbo server-side path instead of falling back to per-section streaming. (When a
  segmented resident scan overflows the server buffer it declines with an empty result
  stream and the client streams per-section itself.)
- **Snapshot storage tuning** (`TSE_SNAPSHOT_CONFIG`, `CMD_PROC_TURBOSCAN_CONFIG`) - the
  client can set the **RAM threshold** (how large the value store may be before it spills
  to disk; default 512 MiB) and the **spill directory** (default `/data`; the encrypted
  internal partition can be slow, so an extended NVMe `/mnt/ext1` or USB `/mnt/usb0` is
  often much faster). Spill writes use 16 MiB chunks.
- **Aliasing read engine** (`TSE_ALIASING`, opt-in, default off) - maps the
  target's physical pages into the server's address space via guarded page-table
  writes so the scan reads in place at DRAM bandwidth instead of copying.
  Layout-agnostic (4K / 2MB / 1GB pages); enabled per request with
  `TS_USE_ALIASING`, and always falls back to the normal read path on any
  guard/verify miss (mdbg is the floor).
- **Parallel compare** (`TSE_PARALLEL_COMPARE`, opt-in, default off) - with
  `TS_PARALLEL_COMPARE` on an aliased exact-match streaming scan, the server splits
  the scan across worker threads. This is for **single-connection** clients: a
  multi-connection client parallelizes better by opening more connections (the server
  threads per connection) and should leave this clear. Don't set both - they
  over-subscribe. Same wire result either way.
- **Rescan aliasing** (`TSE_RESCAN_ALIASING`, opt-in, default off) - with
  `TS_RESCAN_ALIASING` on a `COUNT` rescan, full-size (gap-bridged, contiguous)
  survivor windows read via the aliasing engine instead of mdbg (~2-3x on
  dense/moderate-density rescans; the win grows as survivors stay dense). Tiny
  scattered windows and any alias miss stay on mdbg. The survivor set is
  per-connection, so it is single-connection by nature; a multi-connection client
  must not enable it across many connections at once. Same wire result either way.
- **Region classify** (`0xBDAACC16`) - returns every readable region with its cache
  attribute (uncached `PCD` leaf-PTE bit) and a measured read throughput, so the client
  can offer the user a per-region "exclude uncached/slow" choice (e.g. the GPU/Garlic
  blob, which reads ~40 MB/s and is rarely worth scanning). The server never drops
  anything - exclusion is the client's opt-in, user-overridable decision, default scan
  everything. The opcode is a raw literal (no `CMD_*` macro) so the enumerated `CMD_*`
  set stays unchanged.
- **Auth-gated** - `TURBOSCAN_START` / `_COUNT` / `_GET` / `_END` require the
  `CMD_PROC_AUTH` handshake (like the iterative trio); `TURBOSCAN_CAPS` does not.

### System UI integration
- **Push notifications** to the user's screen with arbitrary UTF-8 text.
- **Print** to the kernel console.
- **Reboot** the console.

### Klog forwarder
- TCP **3232** streams the kernel log to a connected client (host-side
  `klog reader` style). Survives suspend/resume the same as the main server.

### Discovery
- A UDP broadcast responder on port `1010` echoes a handshake magic
  (`0xFFFFAAAA`) so clients can find the PS5 on the LAN without hard-coding
  an IP.

### Rest-mode support
- The payload **survives suspend / resume** without needing to be reloaded.
  A supervisory loop polls the network periodically: when the console drops
  into rest mode the server exits cleanly, and as soon as the network comes
  back the server restarts and a fresh "online" notification fires.
- Clients see a clean disconnect on port 744 when rest mode begins and can
  simply reconnect after wake.

### Performance-oriented design
- Non-blocking sockets with `TCP_NODELAY`, `SO_KEEPALIVE`, large transfer
  chunks.
- Zydis amalgamation compiled at `-O3 -DNDEBUG` for maximum decode throughput.
- Link-time dead stripping (`-ffunction-sections -fdata-sections
  -Wl,--gc-sections`).
- Interrupt packets streamed over a dedicated side channel to avoid blocking
  the command loop.

---

## Architecture

The deployable artifact `ps5debug-NG.elf` is a two-component build:

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                       ps5debug-NG.elf                        │
│                                                              │
│   ┌───────────────────┐    injects   ┌───────────────────┐   │
│   │   installer ELF   │─────────────▶│   debugger ELF    │   │
│   │ (umtx-loaded PIE) │              │ (in SceShellCore) │   │
│   └───────────────────┘              └────────┬──────────┘   │
│                                               │              │
│                              ┌────────────────▼─────────┐    │
│                              │  - TCP server   :744     │    │
│                              │  - debug async  :755     │    │
│                              │  - klog forward :3232    │    │
│                              │  - UDP bcast    :1010    │    │
│                              └──────────────────────────┘    │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

- **installer** - umtx-loaded SDK PIE. Finds SceShellCore, sets up the
  target's KEX state and syscall-origin filter, then calls the SCE-side
  `inject_remote_thread_create` primitive to run the embedded debugger as
  a SceShellCore-internal thread.
- **debugger** - runs inside SceShellCore once injected. Implements the
  wire protocol, breakpoints / watchpoints / single-step, memory scan, RPC,
  and ELF inject. Built into `debugger/build/debugger.elf`, then embedded as
  a `.rodata` blob into the installer via `.incbin`.

Running the wire protocol from inside SceShellCore is what lets `PT_ATTACH`
on game pids look kernel-side like an SCE-originated debug attach, which
PS5's AppContext gating allows. A standalone process doing `PT_ATTACH` gets
the game flagged and stops progressing.

---

## Network protocol at a glance

| Port  | Proto | Direction      | Purpose                              |
|-------|-------|----------------|--------------------------------------|
| 744   | TCP   | client → PS5   | Command server                       |
| 755   | TCP   | PS5 → client   | Async debug interrupts               |
| 3232  | TCP   | PS5 → client   | Kernel log forwarder                 |
| 1010  | UDP   | bidirectional  | Discovery beacon (`0xFFFFAAAA`)      |

Every command begins with a 12-byte header:

```c
struct cmd_packet {
    uint32_t magic;      // 0xFFAABBCC
    uint32_t cmd;        // 0xBDAA..., 0xBDBB..., 0xBDCC..., 0xBDDD...
    uint32_t datalen;    // length of request body that follows
};
```

Followed by the command's fixed request struct (if any) and any trailing
variable-length payload. The reply shape is per-command: most replies begin
with a `uint32_t` status word (some commands send two, and the info/version
commands send their data with no status word at all) - see
[PROTOCOL.md](PROTOCOL.md) for the exact sequence of each.

**Note on status words.** The status `uint32_t` on PS5 is transmitted with
its bit pairs swapped (`net_send_int32` swaps even/odd-bit positions). Clients
must account for the swap - either un-bitswap the incoming word and compare to
the server-side constants (`CMD_SUCCESS = 0x40000000`, etc., as the example
below does), or compare the raw word against the pre-swapped values
(`CMD_SUCCESS = 0x80000000`, etc.). Subsequent payload bytes are sent raw.

**Full protocol specification:** [PROTOCOL.md](PROTOCOL.md) - every command,
every packet struct, every enum, every status code, with `file:line`
citations.

---

## Command coverage

| Namespace     | Count | Examples                                                   |
|---------------|-------|------------------------------------------------------------|
| Info / ping   | 5     | `VERSION`, `FW_VERSION`, `BRANDING`, `PLATFORM_ID`, `NOP`  |
| Process       | 35    | `READ`, `WRITE`, `MAPS`, `CALL`, `SCAN_*`, `TURBOSCAN_*`, `DISASM_*` |
| Debug         | 20    | `ATTACH`, `SET_BREAKPOINT`, `GETREGS`, `GET_FSGS_BASE`, `STEP`, `CONTINUE` |
| Kernel R/W    | 3     | `KERN_BASE`, `KERN_READ`, `KERN_WRITE`                     |
| Console       | 6     | `NOTIFY`, `PRINT`, `REBOOT`, `INFO`, `END`, `FOREGROUND_APP` |
| **Total**     | **69**|                                                            |

---

## Building

Prerequisites (Ubuntu / Debian):

```sh
sudo apt install bash clang-18 lld-18
```

Build:

```sh
./build.sh
```

This builds the SDK first (one-time, cached), then the debugger, then the
installer (which embeds the debugger), then publishes `ps5debug-NG.elf` at
the top level. Subsequent runs only rebuild what changed.

Clean (including the SDK install):

```sh
./build.sh clean
```

---

## Deploying

`ps5debug-NG.elf` is loaded onto the PS5 via a umtx-based ELF loader (e.g.
elfldr from etaHEN-class loaders).

You should see a system notification confirming the payload is alive:

```
ps5debug-NG by OSR v1.3.0 loaded!
Firmware: 9.00
Coded by OpenSourcereR
Special thanks to
golden, Ctn,  SiSTRo, EchoStretch, 
Sonic-Iso & Pharaoh2k!  ❤
```

(`Firmware:` shows the running console's firmware, e.g. `9.00` or `12.40`.)

---

## Writing your own client

The protocol is deliberately simple - a raw TCP client in any language can
drive it. Example: pinging the server and reading its branding string, in
Python (don't forget the bit-pair swap on the status word):

```python
import socket, struct

PACKET_MAGIC = 0xFFAABBCC
CMD_BRANDING = 0xBD000501
CMD_SUCCESS  = 0x40000000

def bitswap32(x):
    x &= 0xFFFFFFFF
    return ((x << 1) & 0xAAAAAAAA) | ((x >> 1) & 0x55555555)

s = socket.create_connection(("<PS5_IP>", 744))
s.sendall(struct.pack("<III", PACKET_MAGIC, CMD_BRANDING, 0))
(status_raw,) = struct.unpack("<I", s.recv(4))
assert bitswap32(status_raw) == CMD_SUCCESS
(length,) = struct.unpack("<I", s.recv(4))
print("server branding:", s.recv(length).decode())
```

See [PROTOCOL.md](PROTOCOL.md) for the exact byte layout of every command,
response, and async interrupt packet.

---

## Source layout

```
.
├── build.sh                 # one-command full build
│
├── common/                  # headers + sources shared by both components
│   ├── include/             # protocol.h, sdk_shim.h, net.h, proc.h, ...
│   └── source/
│
├── debugger/                # in-SceShellCore wire-protocol debugger
│   ├── Makefile  source/  include/
│   └── third_party/         # Zydis (decoder) + Keystone (assembler)
│
├── installer/               # umtx-loaded SceShellCore installer
│   ├── Makefile  source/
│   └── source/embedded_inner.S   # embeds debugger.elf via .incbin
│
├── ps5-payload-sdk/         # vendored John Törnblom SDK
└── third_party/             # keystone-0.9.2 full source (for rebuilds)
```

Three source files (`kern_rw_fast.c`, `proc_elf.c`, `proc_remote.c`) and
`main.c` exist in **both** `debugger/source/` and `installer/source/` because
they genuinely diverge between the two builds - same code specialized for
each component's role.

---

## SDK pin

The vendored SDK is **ps5-payload-sdk v0.38** (commit
`6ae1470fd50c5791e8a8bb728627e657e36eb55a`, dated 2026-04-02). Upstream:
https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk

To upgrade the SDK:

```sh
./build.sh clean
rm -rf ps5-payload-sdk
curl -fsSL https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk/archive/refs/tags/<TAG>.tar.gz \
  | tar xz -C /tmp
mv /tmp/sdk-<TAG_WITHOUT_v> ps5-payload-sdk
./build.sh
```

---

## Credits

- **jogolden** - original public `ps4debug` and the wire protocol this project
  indirectly inherits.
- **Ctn & SiSTRo** - `ps5debug` authors; this project is wire-compatible with
  their implementation.
- **DeathRGH** - Frame4 author. Inspiration.
- **John Törnblom** - `ps5-payload-sdk`, the vendored SDK / toolchain.
- **Zydis** - x86 disassembler used in decoder-only mode (`ZYAN_NO_LIBC`,
  `-DNDEBUG`). Third-party, unmodified; MIT-licensed.
- **Keystone** - LLVM-MC-based assembler; cross-compiled here for the PS5
  payload (x86-only, `-fno-exceptions -fno-rtti`, static).
- **EchoStretch, Sonic-Iso, Pharaoh2k** - contributions and testing.
- **OSR** (OpenSourcereR) - author.

repos.description: Native Emby client for PlayStation 5
repos.readme:
![Emby5 Home Screen](docs/Home.jpg) # Emby5 for PS5 **A native Emby and Jellyfin client for a PS5 that runs homebrew.** It browses your libraries, plays films, shows and music with the PS5's own video decoder, and adds Live TV, video on demand and Seerr requests. The app is `PPSA99515`, its tile is called **Emby5**. This is version 1.2.9. Emby5 contains no media, channels or subscriptions: it plays what your own server and providers give you.

## Features - **Emby and Jellyfin**, found on your network or by address (reverse proxies included), with several saved users and servers and Jellyfin Quick Connect. - **Browsing**: Home rows, films, shows, seasons, episodes and music, with sorting, filters, A–Z, search, trailers by QR code, and 32 themes. - **Native playback**: H.264 and HEVC (4K, Main 10) on the hardware decoder, HDR10 and HLG, AV1 in software; Direct Play, Direct Stream or the server's transcode; upscaling. - **Audio and subtitles**: track choice, subtitle search, styling and delay, and HDMI bitstream for AC-3, E-AC-3 and DTS core. - **Episodes**: skip intros and recaps, the next episode, and "Are you still watching?". - **Music** with a mini player, queue, shuffle, repeat and lyrics. - **Live TV** from your server, Xtream Codes and M3U/M3U8, with your own groups and a full TV guide; **VOD** from Xtream catalogues. - **Seerr**: discover and request films and shows. ## Getting started 1. Download `Emby5-.zip` from [the releases](https://github.com/bornaradusin/Emby5/releases), unzip it, and copy the `PPSA99515/` folder to `/data/homebrew/` on the console (or install it through ProsperoStore). 2. Start **Emby5**, choose your server from the ones found on your network or enter its address, and sign in. To update, close Emby5 and copy the new `PPSA99515/` folder over the old one. Your accounts and settings are in `/data/Emby5/`: don't delete it. ## The wiki Everything else is in the [wiki](https://github.com/bornaradusin/Emby5/wiki): | | | | --- | --- | | [Installing and updating](https://github.com/bornaradusin/Emby5/wiki/Installing-and-updating) | putting Emby5 on the console, updating, where it keeps its data | | [Servers and accounts](https://github.com/bornaradusin/Emby5/wiki/Servers-and-accounts) | Emby and Jellyfin, Quick Connect, several users | | [Browsing and search](https://github.com/bornaradusin/Emby5/wiki/Browsing-and-search) | Home, libraries, details pages, search, artwork | | [Playback](https://github.com/bornaradusin/Emby5/wiki/Playback) and [Audio and subtitles](https://github.com/bornaradusin/Emby5/wiki/Audio-and-subtitles) | formats, upscaling, episodes, tracks, subtitles, HDMI bitstream | | [Music](https://github.com/bornaradusin/Emby5/wiki/Music), [Live TV](https://github.com/bornaradusin/Emby5/wiki/Live-TV), [VOD](https://github.com/bornaradusin/Emby5/wiki/VOD) and [Seerr](https://github.com/bornaradusin/Emby5/wiki/Seerr) | the other tabs | | [Settings](https://github.com/bornaradusin/Emby5/wiki/Settings) and [Appearance](https://github.com/bornaradusin/Emby5/wiki/Appearance) | every tile, languages, updates, themes | | [Controls](https://github.com/bornaradusin/Emby5/wiki/Controls) | every button | | [Troubleshooting](https://github.com/bornaradusin/Emby5/wiki/Troubleshooting) | known limitations, and what to do when something doesn't work | ## Reporting a problem Report problems as [GitHub issues](https://github.com/bornaradusin/Emby5/issues), with your Emby5 version (**Settings › System › Installed version**), whether your server is Emby or Jellyfin, and what happened. ## Building ```bash bash scripts/setup-toolchain.sh eval "$(bash scripts/setup-toolchain.sh --env)" (cd app && bash scripts/build.sh --release) ``` The zip is `app/build/app/Emby5-.zip`. See [Building from source](https://github.com/bornaradusin/Emby5/wiki/Building-from-source) for what you need, the build's options and releasing. ## Credits and licence Emby5 builds on [Jelly5](https://github.com/02dnot/Jelly5) by 02dnot (the original idea and work), [Nuvio PS5](https://github.com/theghostonline/Nuvio-PS5) by Husam Osman / theghostonline (the application and playback foundations), [EVO Player PS5](https://github.com/sainsaji/EVO-PLAYER-PS5) by sainsaji (the native media engine), [ProsperoTV](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ProsperoTV) by BlackBearReloaded (reference and inspiration for Live TV), [PS5 Homebrew UI](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-homebrew-ui) by BlackBearReloaded (the designs behind 30 of the themes), the [PS5 Payload SDK](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk) and PacBrew, and open-source libraries including FFmpeg, libass, FreeType, HarfBuzz, cJSON, NanoSVG, OpenSSL, libcurl and zlib. See [Credits and licence](https://github.com/bornaradusin/Emby5/wiki/Credits-and-licence) and [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md). Emby5 is free software under the **GNU General Public License 3.0 or later** ([LICENSE](LICENSE)). Third-party components keep their own licences and copyright notices. Emby5 is unofficial homebrew provided **without warranty**, and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Emby LLC, the Jellyfin project, Sony Interactive Entertainment, Jelly5 or any other project named here. *Emby*, *Jellyfin*, *PlayStation*, *PS5* and *DualSense* belong to their owners and are used only to describe compatibility.

## What's new

### TV guide
- New full TV guide in Live TV: press **Square**. Channels down the left, the time across, a block for each programme and a line at the current time, with the focused programme's details at the top.
- **Up/Down** change channel, **Left/Right** move through the programmes, **L1/R1** change group, **X** watches the channel, **Square** or **Circle** go back to the channel cards.
- Works with Emby and Jellyfin Live TV, Xtream providers and M3U playlists. For M3U, Emby5 uses the guide the playlist names (`url-tvg`), or one you enter in **Settings > Live TV > M3U TV guide (XMLTV) URL** (`.xml` or `.xml.gz`).
- M3U channels now also show what's on now and next on their cards and in the player.

### Playback
- New **Volume boost** in **Settings > Playback**: Off, +50 %, +100 %, +200 % or +300 %, with a limiter so loud scenes don't distort. HDMI bitstream is off while it's on.
- New **Network buffer** in **Settings > Playback**: 30 seconds (the default), 1, 2 or 5 minutes, for servers reached over the internet or a weak Wi-Fi.
- Changing the audio track now shows that it's switching, instead of looking frozen.
- Tracks without a language now read "Unknown language - track 2", so they can be told apart.
- The playback information panel (**L3**) now shows dropped frames, and stays open for the next video if you left it open.
- Live TV and VOD now use your playback settings (night mode, HDMI bitstream, volume boost, network buffer) too.

### Languages
- Fixed 24 texts that stayed in English in every language, such as "Play" on VOD pages, "Mark all as played" and some Live TV and VOD status texts.

## Installation and updating

1. Close Emby5 completely.
2. Download **Emby5-1.2.9.zip** from the assets below, not a source-code archive.
3. Extract the ZIP to obtain the **PPSA99515/** folder.
4. Copy the complete folder into **/data/homebrew/**. For an update, merge and overwrite the existing application files.
5. Wait for the transfer to finish, then launch Emby5 and confirm **1.2.9** under **Settings > System > Installed version**.

repos.name: lineup
repos.description: Reorder the PS5 home-screen game row with the controller. Homebrew for jailbroken PS5, built with PS5 React.
repos.readme:
# Lineup

Reorder the game row on your PS5 home screen with the controller. Lift a game, carry it, drop it,
save.

[Português](README.pt-BR.md)

![Lineup with Street Fighter 6 focused at position 13, just past the home screen's edge](docs/images/home-edge.png)

Lineup is a homebrew app for jailbroken PS5 consoles. The system orders the home row by when you last
opened each game, and it offers no way to arrange it yourself. Lineup reads the row and lets you lay it
out on the TV. Its local service then writes the new order where the home screen keeps it.

## Features

- **Lift, move, drop.** ✕ lifts the focused game, the D-pad carries it and ✕ drops it. ◯ while carrying
  puts it back.
- **Every profile.** Each console profile has its own row, shown with its picture. Switch from the
  Options menu.
- **Home screen edge.** The home screen shows only the first 12 games. A divider in the row and a mark
  on the ruler show where that edge falls, and games past it read "not on the home screen".
- **Pinned games.** □ pins the focused game where it stands when you save. Opening other games no longer
  pushes it out of its place; the rest of the row still follows the system's rule. Options can pin the
  whole row, unpin all, or remove pinned games from every profile. Works from 1.3.0 on.
- **Sort A to Z**, discard changes, and a count of the games that changed.
- **Media tab.** L1 and R1 switch between the Games and Media tabs. Media apps move and pin like games, each tab
  with its own pins.
- **Applies on exit.** Saving closes the app, and the home screen comes back with the new order. No
  restart needed.
- **Updates in the app.** Lineup checks for a new release when it opens and shows its notes (Options →
  Updates turns that off), downloads it when you choose **Update**, and opens again on the new version. Options → Updates can
  also go back to the previous version. This works from 1.2.0 on.
- **English and Brazilian Portuguese**, chosen from the console's system language.

![The Options menu](docs/images/options.png)

## Requirements

- A PS5 running a jailbreak with **kstuff** and an **ELF loader on port 9021** (elfldr, or etaHEN's).
  Lineup sends its service to that loader when it opens.
- **ShadowMountPlus**, to register the app on the home screen.

Tested on firmware **13.60** with kstuff, elfldr 0.26 and ShadowMountPlus. Other firmware versions are
untested.

## Install

Download the files from the [latest release](https://github.com/bps2414/lineup/releases/latest).

- **exFAT image (easiest).** Copy `Lineup-<version>.exfat` into `/data/homebrew/` over FTP, or into a
  `homebrew/` folder on an exFAT USB drive. ShadowMountPlus mounts it and adds Lineup to the home screen
  within a few seconds.
- **Folder.** Unzip `Lineup-<version>.zip` and upload its `PPSA99077/` folder to
  `/data/homebrew/PPSA99077` over FTP.

Use one or the other. Both register title ID `PPSA99077`.

## Use

| Button | On the row | While carrying |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ✕ | Lift the focused game | Drop it here |
| D-pad | Move focus | Carry the game |
| □ | Pin or unpin the focused game | Pin or unpin it |
| △ | Save | |
| L1 / R1 | Games tab / Media tab | |
| Options | Options menu | |
| ◯ | Quit (asks to save unsaved changes) | Put the game back |

Opening a game afterwards still moves it to the front, as it always does, unless a pinned game holds
that place.

## Safety

- Writes go through the **lineupd** service only, in one SQLite transaction. The new order reuses the
  index values the row already holds, so no value grows past what the system expects.
- Before each save, lineupd copies the database to `/data/lineup/backups/` (the 5 newest are kept) and
  runs SQLite's `quick_check` first. It runs `integrity_check` after the write.
- If the row changed since Lineup read it (you opened a game meanwhile), the save is refused and the
  row reloads.

## How it works

The app is written in React and runs natively on the console through
[PS5 React](#ps5-react). A small C service, `lineupd`, ships inside the app folder. The app starts it
through the ELF loader, and it answers on `127.0.0.1:9077`. It reads the per-profile tables in
`/system_data/priv/mms/app.db` and writes the new order back. Pinned games are kept in place by SQLite
triggers it adds to that database; `POST /pins/off` and `POST /pins/uninstall` take them out again.

See [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) for the components, the service's HTTP API and what
was learned about how the home screen stores its row.

## PS5 React

[PS5 React](https://github.com/half144/ps5-react), by half144, is a framework for standalone,
fullscreen PS5 homebrew written in React and JSX. It runs the app through QuickJS and Embedded React,
draws the interface in software and presents it with OpenGL, and gives the app controller input,
focus navigation, animation, a subset of Tailwind classes, HTTP and filesystem access. It also has a
native macOS preview, and builds a PS5 application folder from the same code.

The framework lives in [`ps5-react/`](ps5-react) in this repository, with one addition Lineup needs:
`Payloads.start(name)` plus a build step. The build step compiles an app's own `payloads/*.c` into
ELFs, and `Payloads.start` sends one of them to the console's ELF loader. Everything else is as
published.

## Building

Linux or WSL: `scripts/test.sh`, `scripts/build.sh`, `scripts/package.sh <version>`. See
[docs/BUILDING.md](docs/BUILDING.md). CI builds every push, and tags `vX.Y.Z` publish a release with the
exFAT image, the zip and the full source.

## Credits

PS5 React — created by half144 and PS5 React contributors.
https://github.com/half144/ps5-react

The framework's own dependencies keep their licenses and notices: see
[ps5-react/NOTICE](ps5-react/NOTICE) and the `notices/` folder in every build. Lineup's interface uses
the Inter typeface (SIL Open Font License) and sounds derived from Google's Material Design sound
resources (CC BY 4.0).

## License

GPL-3.0-or-later, with the PS5 React attribution term in
[ps5-react/LICENSE-ATTRIBUTION](ps5-react/LICENSE-ATTRIBUTION). See [LICENSE](LICENSE).

Lineup is not affiliated with or endorsed by Sony Interactive Entertainment. "PlayStation" and "PS5"
are trademarks of their owners. Use at your own risk.

1.4.3 was not released; its changes ship here.

repos.name: visor-ps5
repos.description: Mirror a Meta Quest 2 to the TV from a jailbroken PS5 - no PC, nothing to install on the headset
repos.readme:
Visor

Watch your Meta Quest 2 on the TV, straight from a jailbroken PS5.
Português

![Visor home screen](docs/home.png) Visor is a PS5 homebrew that mirrors a Quest 2 headset to the TV. The PS5 talks to the headset directly over Wi-Fi: no PC in the middle and nothing to install on the Quest. - Finds headsets on the network by itself - One eye, cropped to 16:9, instead of the raw double image - Quality presets (resolution, bitrate, frame rate) or manual values, H.264 or H.265 - Live reframing with the D-pad while watching - Home screen shortcut on the PS5 - English and Portuguese ## Requirements - A jailbroken PS5 with an ELF loader listening on port 9021 (every current jailbreak has one). Nothing else: no websrv, no Homebrew Launcher. - A Quest 2 in developer mode with ADB over Wi-Fi turned on. This needs a USB cable and a computer once per headset reboot: ``` adb tcpip 5555 ``` - PS5 and headset on the same network. ## Install 1. Download `visor.elf` from the [releases](../../releases). 2. Send it to the PS5 like any other payload, for example: ``` socat -t 99999999 - TCP::9021 < visor.elf ``` 3. A notification says Visor is ready and a **Visor** icon shows up on the home screen. Open it from there. `visor.elf` is a single file: it unpacks itself to `/data/visor`, adds the icon and stays in the background to open the app when the icon is pressed. Like every payload it is gone after a console restart, so send it again after jailbreaking (or add it to your loader's autoload list). The icon and your settings stay. The first time you connect, put the headset on: it asks whether to allow USB debugging. Tick "Always allow". ## Controls | Screen | Button | Action | | --- | --- | --- | | Menus | D-pad / Cross / Circle | Move / select / back | | Watching | Options | Show or hide stats and hints | | Watching | D-pad | Reframe the picture | | Watching | L1 / R1 | Zoom out / in | | Watching | Circle | Stop | Reframing restarts the stream (about a second), because the crop happens on the headset. ## Limits - **No audio.** Capturing it would mute the headset for whoever is wearing it. - **Quest 2 only for now.** Other headsets have different screens, so the eye crop would be off. "Both eyes" in the settings works on anything. - The headset has to be awake (on your head) to stream. - The home screen icon is a web shortcut, so the console opens its browser window first and leaves it in front of Visor. Press Circle once to dismiss it. ## How it works Visor carries a small ADB client. It connects to the headset on port 5555, pushes the [scrcpy](https://github.com/Genymobile/scrcpy) server, starts it with the chosen crop and quality, and decodes the video stream with FFmpeg into an SDL2 texture. The UI is RmlUi. The app is launched as a regular PS5 application by the homebrew loader from [websrv](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/websrv), built into `visor.elf`. ## Building On Ubuntu 24.04 (WSL works), `sudo bash tools/setup-wsl.sh` installs the compilers and the [ps5-payload-dev](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/pacbrew-repo) toolchain. Then: ``` bash tools/build-ps5.sh # dist/visor.elf bash tools/send-elf.sh dist/visor.elf # send it to the console ``` The log of the last run is `/data/visor/visor.log` on the console. `curl http://:8744/` opens the app without touching the controller. ``` ``` There is also a PC build for working without the console: ``` bash tools/run-coretest.sh # ADB + stream + decode, saves a frame bash tools/uishot.sh out.bmp "down ok" # renders a screen headlessly ``` ## License GPL-3.0. Third-party parts are listed in [NOTICE.md](NOTICE.md).

repos.name: PS5-Log-Collector
repos.description: Portable Windows app for streaming, timestamping, and saving KLOG from jailbroken PS5 consoles over TCP — no  Netcat or extra runtime required.
repos.readme:
# PS5 Log Collector [English](README.md) · [Русский](README.ru.md)

A portable Windows application for collecting KLOG and KStuff/game debug output from a jailbroken PlayStation 5 — without Netcat or command-line tools. ## Highlights - Connects directly to `klog.elf` / `klogsrv` over raw TCP. - Provides a separate Game DEBUG session for [`ps5debug-NG` v1.3.0](https://github.com/OpenSourcereR-dev/ps5debug-NG). - Provides a KStuff Metrics session for metrics-enabled `kstuff.elf` plus `debug-reader.elf`. - Adds an in-app **SM+** workspace for downloading the saved ShadowMountPlus `debug.log`. - Keeps the ELF-loader connection open after upload to capture the payload's stdout/stderr stream. - Detects the foreground game and records structured trap/signal events with thread and register context. - Optionally sends a user-selected ELF payload to an active console loader on port `9021`. - Uses port `3232` by default, with an editable host and port. - Displays incoming KLOG data in a responsive live viewer. - Adds an ISO 8601 timestamp with milliseconds and the PC time-zone offset to every line. - Saves the complete session from the moment the connection was established. - Clears the visible log view without stopping capture; the complete session remains available to save. - Preserves partial lines when capture is stopped or the remote side disconnects. - Switches between English and Russian without restarting. - Remembers the selected language and last endpoint. - Ships as one self-contained EXE, with no separate .NET installation. - Does not bundle or invoke Netcat or Telnet. Example output: ```text [2026-09-13T22:42:15.123+03:00] kernel: example message ``` ## Requirements - A jailbroken PlayStation 5 capable of running `klog.elf` or a compatible `klogsrv` payload. - Game DEBUG additionally requires `ps5debug-NG` v1.3.0 running on the console. - The PC and console connected to the same local network. - Windows 11 x64 is the primary supported target. - Windows 10 22H2 x64 is best-effort and should be tested with the current release. ## Quick start 1. Download the latest Windows EXE from the [Releases page](../../releases/latest). 2. Start `PS5LogCollector.exe`. 3. Select **KLOG**. 4. Enter the console IP address. 5. Either activate `klog.elf` manually, or choose your ELF file and select **Send to console** while a compatible loader is active on port `9021`. 6. Keep the KLOG port at `3232` unless the payload uses a custom port, then select **Connect**. 7. Use **Stop** to end capture and **Save log** to export the complete session as UTF-8 text. Saving is also available while capture is active. Cancelling the Save dialog does not interrupt the connection or discard the session. ### Game DEBUG — KStuff Metrics 1. Select **DEBUG → KStuff Metrics** and enter the console IP address. 2. Optionally choose the matching metrics-enabled `kstuff.elf` and send it through the loader on port `9021`. 3. Choose `debug-reader.elf` and select **Start metrics capture**. 4. The app sends the reader, closes only the upload direction, and reads its stdout/stderr over the same `9021` connection. 5. Select **Stop capture** before closing the payload, then save the complete session. The reader prints periodic snapshots of kstuff metrics, kstuff message/word logs, syscall statistics, and ioctl-com statistics. The matching kstuff build must expose the shared observation area; the application cannot make an ordinary kstuff build produce these metrics. ### Game DEBUG — Debugger Events Select **Debugger Events** for the existing `ps5debug-NG` workflow: command port `744`, reverse event port `755`, and structured trap/signal packets. This is a separate diagnostic source and is not the same as KStuff Metrics stdout. KStuff Metrics captures the reader payload's stdout/stderr, not ordinary game stdout. Classic application/SDK stdout is expected to require DECI5 TTY and remains a later transport. KLOG, DEBUG, and SM+ run as separate sessions in v0.5.0. ### SM+ — ShadowMountPlus ([API reference](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus/blob/1.7/docs/api.md)) 1. Open **SM+** in the left navigation and enter the PS5 IP address. 2. Select **Fetch debug.log**. The app first tries the ShadowMountPlus HTTP API on port `10101`. 3. If the API is unavailable, expand the FTP fallback and use the console FTP port (commonly `1337` or `2121`) and the saved path `/data/shadowmount/debug.log`. The FTP user field is intentionally blank by default; fill it only when the console FTP service requires a username. 4. Review the downloaded file, then use **Save log** to write the original text without adding timestamps or other lines. This is a one-shot download of the saved file; live ShadowMountPlus monitoring is intentionally not part of this phase. The HTTP API is normally loopback-only, so ShadowMountPlus must be configured to bind its API to the local network (for example, `api_bind_address=0.0.0.0`). The API has no authentication, so expose it only on a trusted LAN. It may return only the tail when the file is larger than its response limit, and the status bar reports that condition. ## Connection troubleshooting - **Connection refused:** confirm that `klog.elf` is active and listening on the selected port. - **Timed out:** verify the PS5 IP address, local network connectivity, and firewall rules. - **No new messages:** KLOG may be quiet until the console produces new kernel output. - **Connection closed:** restart the payload if necessary, then connect again manually. The application uses the same raw TCP stream as: ```shell nc 3232 ``` Telnet mode is intentionally not implemented because the upstream service exposes a raw socket rather than the Telnet protocol. ## Privacy and safety KLOG and Game DEBUG files can contain device identifiers, game identifiers, thread names, memory addresses, filesystem paths, network details, or other diagnostic information. Review and redact logs before posting them publicly. PS5 Log Collector only connects to the host and ports entered by the user. It does not upload logs, include telemetry, or perform a jailbreak. Payload transfer happens only after the user explicitly chooses a local ELF file and selects **Send to console**. ## Architecture - `src/Ps5LogCollector.Core` — KLOG transport, ShadowMountPlus HTTP/FTP retrieval, same-socket ELF/stdout capture, ps5debug-NG protocol, session lifecycle, event parsing, temporary spool, and full-session export. - `src/Ps5LogCollector` — WPF/Fluent interface, localized resources, Save dialog, and persisted user preferences. - `tests/Ps5LogCollector.Core.Tests` — dependency-free regression suite covering TCP, timestamps, ShadowMount HTTP API parsing, ps5debug-NG framing, event parsing, detach, export, and localization parity. The live text control retains a bounded recent window for UI performance, while the temporary session spool preserves the complete exportable log. ## Disclaimer This is an independent diagnostic utility and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Sony Interactive Entertainment. “PlayStation” and “PS5” are trademarks of their respective owners. Use the application only with systems and software you are authorized to access.
