latestRelease.body:
🚀 BlackBox v1.12.6

This release fixes critical crashes, browser issues, and update system shutdowns reported in version 1.12.5.

🛠️ Changelog


👾 Bug Fixes & Stability

• Hero Visuals: Fixed crashes occurring during hero visual loading.
• Camera Adjustment: Resolved an issue where the "Adjust Camera" dialog would unexpectedly open (including during fast scrolling).
• Browser & Downloads: Fixed browser verification and download streams; the browser now correctly opens during downloads.
• Storage Management: Cleaned up the USB/storage list to display only actually connected drives, removing ghost "External storage" lines.

👤 UI & Quality of Life (QoL)

• Accounts Screen: The logged-in email/username is now properly displayed.
• Security: The TorBox key is now visible while typing.
• Localization: Completed translations for 10 languages and corrected the overall Settings layout.

🔄 Update System Improvements

• Self-Contained Installer: The download service is now fully included in the package; a separate blackbox.elf is no longer required.
• Safe Shutdowns: Removed service reload/execv paths. The console will no longer shut down abruptly after an update, utilizing a safe shutdown (_exit) instead.
• Diagnostics: The log file is now located next to the package (/data/homebrew/diag.log) with a 2 MB rotation limit.

💾 Installation Instructions

1. Open BlackBox.
2. The update will install automatically within a few seconds.
3. ⚠️ Do not close the console during installation.
4. Upon initial startup, the new version will automatically switch the download service to its internal version 1.12.6.

repos.name: SwanStationPS5
repos.description: SwanStationPS5: a PlayStation 1 emulator running natively on jailbroken PS5, based on SwanStation.  https://discord.gg/Drx8tsqq3B
repos.readme:
--- ## What is SwanStationPS5? SwanStationPS5 is a PlayStation 1 emulator that installs as an app on the PS5 home screen. It started as a fork of [PSXS5](https://github.com/SynoPiia/PSXS5) by SynoPiia, and it is no longer one. PSXS5 draws its interface on the CPU, with SDL2's software renderer into a canvas that Vulkan only displays; SwanStationPS5 is now 100% Vulkan, the game's picture and the whole interface drawn by the GPU, so the two frontends no longer line up. It runs every game on SwanStation. Its frontend (the shelf, menus, controls and tools) began as PSXS5's and has been reworked since to be 100% Vulkan. It drives the SwanStation core: SwanStation is the only emulator. - The emulator is [SwanStation](https://github.com/libretro/swanstation) (DuckStation's libretro core): accurate, and drawn on the PS5's GPU through Vulkan at up to 16x the PS1's resolution, with PGXP. It runs without a BIOS dump on its built-in OpenBIOS, but `SCPH1001.BIN` is highly recommended for good emulation. - You pick a game from a cover-flow shelf with your covers. - RetroAchievements, cheats for every game, save states and quick resume. ## Also on Xbox Series X|S SwanStation is also available for the **Xbox Series X|S** as a UWP app: [SwanStationUWP](https://github.com/darkxex/SwanStationUWP). Download it from its [releases](https://github.com/darkxex/SwanStationUWP/releases) page. It needs the console in Xbox **developer mode**. Each release carries the app package (`.msix`), its signing certificate (`.cer`) and the `Microsoft.VCLibs` x64 dependency: trust the certificate, install the dependency, then install the package. SwanStationUWP is a separate project with its own releases and issues; everything else in this README is about the PS5 app. ## Screenshots

## Highlights - **The shelf and menus on the GPU too.** The interface is drawn through Vulkan, with a floor reflection under every cover. When you start a game, the case's lid opens and the CD spins, with the sound of a disc spinning up. - **Always 4K.** The picture is sent to the TV at 4K, and it falls back to 1080p if the TV lacks the mode. - **Up to 16x resolution on the GPU.** SwanStation renders through Vulkan: native, 2x, 4x, 8x or 16x (4x by default), at full speed. - **No more wobbly 3D.** PGXP (precise geometry) keeps polygons still and textures straight. - **One emulator, nothing to choose.** Every game runs on SwanStation. Memory cards are saved per game. - **SwanStation's own options.** 104 of its core options (MSAA, texture filter, widescreen hack, PGXP details, controller ports, CPU overclock...) in Settings → Display, Graphics, Controls and System. They are in English and only on the console. - **Five themes.** Neon Arcade (the default), Classic, Memory Card (light and dark, a grid of covers) and Record Shelf (spines on a shelf), each with its own colours and fonts. Around a 4:3 picture: black, the current background or a 90s TV, or the game's own artwork frame (off by default). - **Games on a drive, by one name.** *Games folder on drives* (`psx` by default, typed with an on-screen keyboard) is looked for on `/mnt/ext0/`, `/mnt/ext1/` and `/mnt/usb0/` to `/mnt/usb7/` at once, so it still works when the console numbers your drives differently. - **Games on an NFS server.** Keep your games on a PC or a NAS and play them over the network: add the server in Settings > System > NFS shares. They show on the shelf like a drive's, a background thread reads the disc ahead of the game, and a server that goes away just takes you back to the library. See [Games on an NFS server](#games-on-an-nfs-server). - **Play your own PS1 discs from a USB CD drive.** Put a PS1 disc in a USB CD drive and SwanStationPS5 copies it to your games folder (a `.bin` and a `.cue`, with a progress bar and the game's cover), adds it to the shelf and starts it. Once a disc is installed, putting it in again just starts the game. With the disc daemon this works even with the app closed. See [Playing from a USB CD drive](#playing-from-a-usb-cd-drive). - **Discs without opening the app.** Send `SwanStationPS5-DiscDaemon.elf` (a file of the release) once to your console's ELF loader and leave it running: a disc put in the drive is installed with the console's own notifications (name, percentage and time left), and then the game opens by itself. - **Multi-disc games.** Change disc from the in-game menu and it happens as soon as you choose; the disc you leave a game on is the one it starts on next time. A `.m3u` playlist of `.chd` discs gets its serial (and so its cover and data) from the first disc's name. - **Analog mode on at start.** A DualShock starts in analog mode in the games that use the sticks, unless the game's entry says to start in digital mode (the ANALOG button combo still switches it). - **The DualSense as a light gun.** Point the controller at the screen in GunCon games (Time Crisis, Point Blank...); R2 fires. - **Adaptive triggers.** R2 feels like a gas pedal in racing games, and R2 / L2 can be the gas and brake. - **Profiles.** Each person keeps their own memory cards, save states, settings, play time and RetroAchievements sign-in. - **Text guides and manuals.** Read a walkthrough `.txt` or a manual's pages from the in-game menu. - **Game art.** Title screens and gameplay pictures in Details, and the game's own artwork around the picture. - **Quick resume.** Leave a game and pick it up later: the shelf offers *Continue* (with a picture of where you were) or *Start over*. - **Rewind and fast forward.** Hold the touchpad and press L2 to go back a few seconds, or R2 to speed through cutscenes. - **Save states with pictures.** Ten slots per game, each showing a thumbnail and how long ago it was saved. - **Widescreen.** SwanStation's widescreen hack (Settings → Graphics) draws the 3D picture in 16:9. - **CRT look.** Light or strong scanlines, and the current background or a 90s TV around the picture. - **Shaders for the picture** (Settings → Display → Shader): LCD3x (a handheld's LCD) and zfast LCD, four NTSC ones (320px or 256px, S-Video or Composite) that recreate the analog TV signal, and CRT looks: CRT Royale Fast and CRT Royale (detailed, with bloom and a phosphor mask; heavy), CRT Newpixie, CRT Hyllian NTSC, CRT Mattias, CRT Lottes and CRT Pi. - **Generate frames.** AMD FSR 3's frame interpolation adds frames between the game's real ones. x2 puts one between each two: a 30 fps game is shown at 60, and with *Video output* at 120 Hz a 60 fps one at 120. x4 puts three: with *Video output* at 120 Hz a 30 fps game is shown at 120. At 60 Hz it only doubles. SwanStation tells the app when a picture is a repeat, so it starts from the game's real rate. The shaders run after it, CRT Royale Fast and NTSC included. - **Show FPS that tells the truth.** It shows the emulated frames, the game's own rate when the game repeats pictures (`60.0 FPS (game 25.0)`) and, while frames are generated, the frames you actually see and how many are made for each of the game's (`100.0 FPS (game 25.0) | FG x4`). - **HD texture packs.** The *Load HD textures* switch turns on SwanStation's texture replacement; put a pack's PNG files in `/data/SwanStationPS5/cache/textures//` (for example `SCUS-94900`). - **PS1 homebrew.** Homebrew discs boot too: [Yume Nikki PS1](https://eliasdaler.itch.io/yume-nikki-ps1) and [Doki Doki Literature Club PSX](https://www.psxhomebrewgames.com/2025/09/doki-doki-literature-club-psx.html) are confirmed. - **PSXS5 friendly.** It still reads PSXS5's games and BIOS folders (see [supported folders](#supported-folders-for-games-and-bios)), so a PSXS5 library keeps working. - **Close the app from the controller.** Hold O for 2 seconds. Menus show the title from the game database, and the game menu has pills with the serial and the folder. - **Up to 4 players.** A multitap for the games that support it: each PS5 controller is a player. - **Fan translations.** Put a `.ppf` patch next to a game and SwanStationPS5 applies it when the game starts. - **Memory card manager.** See the saves on every game's card with each save's own icon (animated, as on a PS1), export cards for other emulators, import `.mcr`, `.mcd`, `.srm` or `.gme` cards. - **Achievements list.** Every achievement of the game you're playing, with badges, in two tabs: *Achievable* (closest first) and *Achieved*. - Counted achievements (18/80 dragons) show a progress bar, and a small tracker pops up in game when they move. - **Settings from your phone.** Turn it on and scan the QR code: a settings page opens on any phone on the same network. - **Updates from GitHub.** SwanStationPS5 finds a new release when it starts and installs it by itself a second after opening (or from *Settings → About*), into the folder the app is running from: `/data/homebrew`, or an extended or USB drive. After an update it asks once whether to start from the new version's factory settings (✕ resets, ○ keeps yours). - **Native app.** A real home-screen title (`PPSA98510`) with its own icon and art. Nothing is streamed and no PC is needed while you play. - **A shelf for your games.** A cover flow with depth, 3D jewel cases, a reflection under every cover and a soft click as you browse. - Covers are matched by the serial read from each disc, so every region gets its own art. - Missing covers download on the console. - Your own art wins: a `cover.png`/`.jpg` in the game's folder, or an image in `/data/SwanStationPS5/covers/` named like the game's title, its disc file or its serial (`Crash Bandicoot.png`, `SCUS-94900.jpg`). - Or pick one by hand: on the shelf press **Triangle** (Details), then **Square**, and choose any image from `covers/` or the game's folder. - **Plays every common format.** `.cue`/`.bin`, `.chd`, `.pbp` (including multi-disc), `.iso`, `.img`, `.mdf`, `.ccd` and `.m3u` playlists for multi-disc games. - **Sharp on a 4K TV.** - Output: 1080p, 1440p or 4K (Settings → System → SwanStationPS5), changed at once. - Internal resolution: native up to 16x with SwanStation. - Aspect ratio: auto, 4:3, 16:9, 16:10, 1:1 pixels or stretch, and *Crop black edges* to hide the black lines at the top and bottom. - *Manual crop*, under Aspect ratio: open the preview with the touchpad, and Left / Right stretch or narrow the picture (always keeping its aspect ratio, which is shown) while Up / Down move it up or down. Square goes back to the original area. - Integer scaling and smooth final scaling on or off (sharp pixels by default). - **Built for full speed.** 60 fps (50 for PAL games). SwanStation renders on the GPU, and so do the shelf and the menus; everything reaches the TV through Vulkan. - **RetroAchievements.** Earn [RetroAchievements](https://retroachievements.org) as you play. - Unlocks and leaderboard results pop up on screen. - Optional hardcore mode. - See [RetroAchievements](#retroachievements). - **Cheats for every game, automatically.** SwanStationPS5 knows all 1,961 PlayStation cheat files of libretro-database (GameShark, Action Replay...), and DuckStation's cheat database (about 4,500 more files) for games libretro has nothing for. - When a game starts it finds that game's file and downloads it: no setup. - Toggle codes per game from the in-game menu. - **Save states.** 10 slots per game, plus memory cards saved per game. - **DualSense ready.** - The classic digital pad by default, or the DualShock with analog sticks and rumble (Settings → Controls → Controller). - On digital-only games, the left stick drives the D-pad. - Cross confirms and Circle goes back in the menus. - **Your BIOS, or none.** SwanStation works best with a BIOS dump of your own console for the game's region (`scph5500.bin` Japan, `scph5501.bin` USA, `scph5502.bin` Europe in `bios/`; the PC tool names them for you). Without one, SwanStation uses its built-in OpenBIOS, which is less compatible. - **Five languages.** English, Français, Português (Portugal), Español (Latinoamérica) and 日本語, under Settings → System → Language. - **Quiet interface sounds.** Five styles (Soft, Wood, Pop, Chime, Classic), a volume setting, or off. - **A PC tool for your library.** `tools/SwanStationPS5_sync.py` prepares your games on Windows and uploads them over FTP: - unpacks archives - writes missing `.cue` sheets and `.m3u` playlists - fetches covers and cheats - **Logs that help.** A session log and a crash report (with addresses for the symbol map) stay on the console. ## Playing from a USB CD drive The PS5 has no laser for CDs, so PS1 discs are played from an external **USB CD drive**. SwanStationPS5 does not read the disc while you play: it **installs** it first (copies it to `.bin` and `.cue` in your games folder, the same as a dump you made yourself) and plays that copy. That way the game runs at full speed and works with every feature (save states, rewind, cheats, RetroAchievements). It only copies discs you own. ### The flow, with the disc daemon (the app can be closed) 1. **Once per console start**, send the payload `SwanStationPS5-DiscDaemon.elf` (it is attached to every [release](../../releases/latest), next to the zip; it is not inside the zip) to the ELF loader of your console, with the app closed: ```bash socat -t 99999999 - TCP::9021 < SwanStationPS5-DiscDaemon.elf ``` A notification says it is ready. Leave it running; sending a newer copy replaces the old one. 2. **Plug in the USB CD drive and put in a PS1 disc.** The console's own notifications show `Installing : 37% - 5 min 30 s left...`. The time left comes from the speed the drive has just had, since a CD reads faster towards its edge. 3. **The game starts by itself.** When the copy ends, SwanStationPS5 opens, skips its opening animation and starts the game at once, on the disc you put in. 4. **Next time**, the same disc (or a disc of the games folder) just says `Loading ...` and opens the game: nothing is copied twice. The game stays on your shelf, so you no longer need the disc. To cancel an installation, take the disc out (what was copied is deleted). If the drive reads nothing for 30 seconds, or the disc has too many bad sectors, the installation stops with a notification that says why. A disc that is not a PS1 game is ignored. ### The flow, with the app open With SwanStationPS5 open, the app looks after the drive itself and the daemon stays out of the way (they never use it at the same time). Put the disc in while you are on the shelf: a card shows `Installing ...` with its cover and a bar, and the game starts when it ends. **Hold O** to cancel (what was copied is deleted, and the same disc does not start again until you take it out). ### Good to know - **Games of several discs** go in one folder: install disc 1, then disc 2... and SwanStationPS5 turns them into one game with a `.m3u` playlist. The game starts on the disc you put in, and you change disc from the game menu. - The cover is downloaded while the disc is copied. Homebrew discs without a serial are installed too, with no cover. - Where it goes: `/data/SwanStationPS5/games/ []/`. Delete a game from its Details (hold Triangle) to free the space. - The daemon needs the console to be jailbroken, as the app does, and writes its log to `/data/SwanStationPS5/logs/disc-daemon.log`. - It is not in the zip because it is not a part of the app: it is a payload you load like any other. Build it yourself with `make disc-daemon` (`dist/SwanStationPS5-DiscDaemon.elf`). - Not every USB CD drive may work. If yours does not, send the logs (`SwanStationPS5.log` and `disc-daemon.log`) with your bug report. ## Supported folders for games and BIOS ### GAMES: one folder per game, in any of these places The games are looked for in all of these folders at once. Inside each, **one folder per game** with every file of the game in it (`.cue` + `.bin`, `.chd`, `.pbp`, `.iso`, `.m3u`...): | Where | Folder | |---|---| | **The console** (the default) | `/data/SwanStationPS5/games//` | | The console, from PSXS5 | `/data/PSXS5/games//` | | **A USB drive** | `/mnt/usb0` to `/mnt/usb7`, then `SwanStationPS5/games//` | | An extended storage | `/mnt/ext0` or `/mnt/ext1`, then `SwanStationPS5/games//` | | **An NFS server** | the folder you add in Settings > System > NFS shares, one folder per game (see [Games on an NFS server](#games-on-an-nfs-server)) | On each USB drive and extended storage these four also work (`` is `/mnt/usb0` to `/mnt/usb7`, `/mnt/ext0` or `/mnt/ext1`): - `/SwanStationPS5/games//` - `/SwanStationPS5//` (without `games`) - `/PSXS5/games//` (PSXS5's folder) - `/PSXS5//` Example on a USB drive: `/mnt/usb0/SwanStationPS5/games/Crash Bandicoot/Crash Bandicoot.chd`. You can also pick one folder name for drives in Settings > System > SwanStationPS5 > Games folder on drives (`psx` by default): it is looked for on `/mnt/ext0/`, `/mnt/ext1/` and `/mnt/usb0/` to `/mnt/usb7/` at once, since the drive's number changes with the ones plugged in. With `psx`, a game goes in `/mnt/usb0/psx//` (or `/mnt/usb1/psx/...` and so on). Leave the field empty to turn it off. ### BIOS: one folder, no subfolders | Priority | Folder | |---|---| | 1st | `/data/SwanStationPS5/bios/` | | 2nd (only if the first has no `.bin`) | `/data/PSXS5/bios/` (PSXS5's folder) | Put the BIOS files directly in the folder, not in a subfolder, and keep their standard names: `SCPH1001.BIN` (recommended), `scph5500.bin` (Japan), `scph5501.bin` (USA), `scph5502.bin` (Europe), `scph101.bin`. A BIOS on a USB drive or extended storage is not read. With no BIOS, SwanStation uses its built-in OpenBIOS. *Settings → About* shows which one is in use. > On a USB drive or extended storage SwanStationPS5 needs `/data` unlocked to list the folders (see below). Sandboxed, it only shows the games listed in `/data/SwanStationPS5/library.txt`. ## Games on an NFS server You can keep your games on a PC or a NAS and play them over your network, with no copy to the console. The console has no NFS client of its own, so SwanStationPS5 carries one ([libnfs](https://github.com/sahlberg/libnfs)): only the app sees the share. It is read only, and the BIOS, saves, states and covers stay on the console. ### 1. Share the games folder from the server Put one folder per game inside the folder you share (the same as in [Supported folders](#supported-folders-for-games-and-bios): `.cue` + `.bin`, `.chd`, `.pbp`, `.iso`, `.m3u`...), and export it over NFS to the console's address: - **Windows:** run an NFS server such as WinNFSd with the folder and an alias, for example `winnfsd.exe D:\psx /psx`. The alias (`/psx`) is the path you type in the app. - **Linux, or a NAS** (Synology, QNAP, TrueNAS...): turn NFS on, and export the folder read only to the console. On Linux, in `/etc/exports`: `/srv/psx 192.168.1.0/24(ro,no_subtree_check)`. If the console is refused, try adding `insecure` to the options. - NFS v3 is used by default. A server that only speaks v4 needs `?version=4` at the end of the address. ### 2. Add it in the app 1. Open **Settings > System > NFS shares**. The on-screen keyboard opens with an example (`nfs://192.168.1.85/psx`). 2. Type the address of your server and the exported folder, with `nfs://` in front: `nfs:///`. For example, `nfs://192.168.1.50/psx`. Several shares go separated by `;`. 3. Press Apply. The app connects and reloads the library. A notice says `NFS share connected.` or why it could not, and the games of the share show on the shelf. Useful options go after a `?`: `?version=4` (NFS v4 only), `?nfsport=2049&mountport=1058` (fixed ports, when the server has no portmapper), `?uid=1000&gid=100` (who the server sees). The folder you type can also be inside what the server exports. ### Good to know - **Opening the app never waits for the server.** The shares mount in the background and the library is scanned again when they are ready. - **Reconnecting.** If the server was closed and opened again, or was off when you opened the app, go to **Settings > Library > Rescan library**: it checks the shares again and mounts the ones that are not. A rescan also takes you back to *All games*. - **Smooth playing.** While a game runs, a background thread reads the disc image ahead of the game and keeps up to 256 MiB of it in memory, so the game does not wait for the network on every read. The memory goes back when you close the game; nothing is written to the console. - **If the connection is lost in the middle of a game** (the server is closed or the network goes), the game is left, the library is reloaded and a notice says *NFS communication was lost*. - **Not connecting?** The notice says why: the server did not answer, the connection was refused or closed, the name was not found, the server denies the console, or the folder is not exported (it then lists what the server does export, so you can copy the right path). ## Games on an NTFS disk A USB disk or hard drive formatted as NTFS (the format of most Windows disks) works with no copy to the console. The console cannot mount NTFS, so SwanStationPS5 reads the disk itself, read only; only the app sees it. The reader comes from [PS5-NTFS-BROWSER](https://github.com/abcde6543/PS5-NTFS-BROWSER) (GPL-3.0-or-later, without its writing part). - Put one folder per game in a `psx` folder (or the name set in Settings > System > Games folder on drives) or in `SwanStationPS5/games` on the disk, as in [Supported folders](#supported-folders-for-games-and-bios). - Plug the disk in, and open **Settings > Library > Rescan library**: the games show on the shelf. Settings > System > NTFS disks turns this off. - MBR and GPT disks work. Encrypted (EFS, BitLocker) files cannot be read. Compressed NTFS files work but read slower. - Turn the disk off in Windows properly (not Fast Startup, which leaves it unfinished): otherwise its latest changes may not show. - If the disk is unplugged in the middle of a game, the game is left and a notice says *The NTFS disk was disconnected*. ## What you need - **A jailbroken PS5** with [etaHEN](https://github.com/etaHEN/etaHEN) and kstuff loaded. Development happens on firmware 13.60. - **[ShadowMountPlus](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus)**, loaded at every boot. It puts SwanStationPS5 on the home screen from `/data/homebrew/PPSA98510/`. - **An FTP client**, such as etaHEN's FTP server on port 2121 with FileZilla, or the included PC tool. - **Your own games**, dumped from discs you own. - **Optional: your own PS1 BIOS**, dumped from your own console. Without one, SwanStation uses its built-in OpenBIOS, which is less compatible. > **No BIOS files, games, keys or cheats with copyrighted content are included with SwanStationPS5, and none will be provided.** You have to supply your own legally made backups. ## Getting started 1. **Download** `PPSA98510.zip` from the [latest release](../../releases/latest) and extract it. Inside is the `PPSA98510` folder. The PC tool is in the repository (`tools/SwanStationPS5_sync.py`). 2. **Install the app.** Copy the `PPSA98510` folder to `/data/homebrew/` on the PS5 over FTP. Then set its permissions to `777`: in FileZilla, right-click the folder → *File permissions* → `777`, recurse into subdirectories. Without this, the PS5 says *"Can't start the game or app"* (CE-107750-0). The PC tool does all of this for you: ```bash python tools/SwanStationPS5_sync.py app --app-dir PPSA98510 --host ``` 3. **Restart ShadowMountPlus** (or the console). SwanStationPS5 appears on the home screen. 4. **Start SwanStationPS5 once.** It creates its folders in `/data/SwanStationPS5/` (see [below](#folders-on-the-console)) and shows an empty shelf that tells you where games go. 5. **Add your games** to `/data/SwanStationPS5/games/`, **one folder per game**, with every file of the game inside it: ```text /data/SwanStationPS5/games/Final Fantasy VII/ FF7 Disc 1.cue, FF7 Disc 1.bin, ... (any format above) /data/SwanStationPS5/games/Crash Bandicoot/ Crash Bandicoot.chd ``` Or let the PC tool prepare and upload a whole folder of games (see [PC tool](#pc-tool)). > **Shelf still empty?** When etaHEN doesn't unlock `/data`, SwanStationPS5 can't look into the games folder and only shows the games listed in `/data/SwanStationPS5/library.txt`, which the PC tool writes when it uploads. For games you copied another way (FileZilla, a file manager, a USB drive), let the tool list them: > ```bash > python tools/SwanStationPS5_sync.py index --host --fix-cues > ``` > `--fix-cues` repairs `.cue` files that point at a `.bin` that was renamed, for example to `BREATH~1.BIN` by a FAT32 copy. 6. **Optional, but add your BIOS.** `SCPH1001.BIN` is highly recommended for good emulation. Put your own dump directly in `/data/SwanStationPS5/bios/`, not in a subfolder, and keep its standard name. `scph5501.bin` (US), `scph5500.bin` (Japan) and `scph5502.bin` (Europe) also work, as does `scph101.bin`. *Settings → About* shows whether it was found. From a PC: `python tools/SwanStationPS5_sync.py bios scph5501.bin --host `. 7. **Restart SwanStationPS5.** Covers download the first time, then the shelf opens with your games. > **Where do things go?** Games: `/data/SwanStationPS5/games//`. BIOS: `/data/SwanStationPS5/bios/`. SwanStationPS5 creates both folders the first time it starts; you can also create them yourself over FTP. ### Unlocking /data (so SwanStationPS5 can see your games) A PS5 app can read and write files in `/data`, but it can't list folders unless something running on the console unlocks it. SwanStationPS5 asks every time it starts. Any one of these answers: | On your console | What to do | |---|---| | **[LegacyJB](https://github.com/Phoenixx1202/LegacyJB)** | Load it with your payloads at each boot. It unlocks any app. | | **etaHEN** | Turn on *Legacy CMD server* in the etaHEN toolbox. SwanStationPS5 asks on port 9028. | | **PS5SX2 Helper** (the PS2 emulator's helper) | It only unlocks apps listed in `/data/whitelist.txt`. Use *Settings → System → Allow SwanStationPS5 in PS5SX2 Helper*, then reload the helper or restart the console. | The log shows the result: `storage: unlocked`, or `storage: sandboxed (...)` with the reason. Sandboxed still works, but SwanStationPS5 then only knows the games in `/data/SwanStationPS5/library.txt` (written by the PC tool's `upload` and `index` commands). ### Folders on the console ```text /data/homebrew/PPSA98510/ the app /data/SwanStationPS5/ ├── games// your games, one folder per game (a cheats.cht here overrides the library) ├── bios/ optional: your BIOS dump (scph*.bin) ├── covers/ your own cover images (named like the game, or picked on the shelf); │ downloads in default/ and 3d/, picks in custom/ ├── cheats/ the .cht library ├── saves/ memory cards, one per game ├── states/ save states, 10 slots per game ├── logs/SwanStationPS5.log the session log (send this with bug reports) ├── retroachievements.ini RetroAchievements sign-in (token only) └── SwanStationPS5.ini settings ``` ## Covers for games without one Covers are downloaded by the game's serial. A game that is not found (a homebrew, a translation, a hack) shows a plain title card until you give it a cover. ### Copy the image yourself (FTP, USB or the PC tool) Name the image like the game's disc file, without the extension. For `yume_nikki.cue`, the cover is `yume_nikki.png`, and it goes in one of these places: | Where | File name | |---|---| | The game's own folder, next to the `.cue` | `yume_nikki.png`, or just `cover.png` | | `/data/SwanStationPS5/covers/` | `yume_nikki.png`, the game's title (`Yume Nikki.png`) or its serial (`SLPS-01234.png`) | ```text /data/SwanStationPS5/games/Yume Nikki/ ├── yume_nikki.cue ├── yume_nikki.bin └── yume_nikki.png ← the cover ``` SwanStationPS5 looks for covers in this order and uses the first it finds: 1. `cover` or the disc file's name in the game's folder. 2. The game's title, the disc file's name or the serial in `covers/`. 3. Covers already downloaded (`covers/default/`, `covers/3d/`), then a download by serial. ### Good to know - Formats: `.png`, `.jpg` and `.jpeg`, with the extension in lowercase. Other formats (`.webp`, `.bmp`, `.gif`) are not read. - Large images are scaled down to 640 px tall, so there is no need for more. - If the new cover does not show up, restart SwanStationPS5 so it scans the library again. ## Controls **On the shelf** | Button | Does | |---|---| | D-pad or left stick | Browse the games | | L1 / R1 | Category (All games, Recently played, Favorites...) | | Cross | Play | | Triangle | Game details (hold Triangle there to delete the game's files) | | Square | Settings | | R3 | Favorite | | Touchpad | Memory cards | | OPTIONS | Sort order | | Circle | Back | **In a game** | Button | Does | |---|---| | OPTIONS | PS1 START | | Touchpad tap | PS1 SELECT | | Hold L3 + R3 for 1 second | The SwanStationPS5 menu (*Settings → Controls → Game menu combination* can change it to the touchpad, or OPTIONS + touchpad) | | Hold the touchpad + R2 | Fast forward | | Hold the touchpad + L2 | Rewind (turn on *Settings → System → Rewind*) | | Hold the touchpad + Square | Screenshot (in `/data/SwanStationPS5/screenshots`) | | Hold the touchpad + Triangle / Circle | Start or pause / reset the speedrun timer | | R3 (light gun games) | Re-centre the aim | | Left stick | Analog stick; on digital-only games it also drives the D-pad (*Left stick as D-pad* in Settings) | The **SwanStationPS5 menu** has: - resume - save and load state (slots 0–9), and the auto-saves - disc change, for multi-disc games - cheats, and *Find a code* to make your own - achievements - the manual and text guides, when the game has them - settings - reset - quit to the shelf It also shows the time and how long you've been playing. **Text guides:** put a walkthrough or FAQ (`.txt`) in the game's folder, or in a `guides` folder inside it, and read it from the SwanStationPS5 menu → Guide. **Manuals:** page images (`1.jpg`, `2.jpg`...) in `/manual/`. ## Settings | Section | Settings | |---|---| | Display | Aspect ratio, texture filtering (including MMPX), shader (LCD3x, CRT Royale and Royale Fast, Newpixie, Hyllian NTSC, Mattias, Lottes, Pi, zfast LCD, NTSC), crop black edges, integer scaling, smooth final scaling, scanlines, border, game artwork border, brightness, colours, FPS counter, load HD textures, double frames, and SwanStation's display options | | Graphics | Internal resolution (native to 16x), PGXP, true colour, supersampling, and SwanStation's enhancement options (MSAA, PGXP details...) | | Controls | Controller (digital or DualShock), left stick as D-pad, vibration, light bar, players (multitap), player order, dead zone, stick response, rumble feel, trigger effects, gas and brake on R2 / L2, light gun, button mapping, and SwanStation's controller port options | | Achievements | Account, your profile, unlock pop-ups and their style, progress tracker, hardcore mode | | Library | Theme, cover style, download missing covers, sort, your library, memory cards, rescan | | System | SwanStationPS5 (start the BIOS, games folder on USB drives, NFS shares), region, PS1 startup intro, fast CD loading, known game fixes, SwanStation's console and advanced options, quick resume, rewind, auto-save, who's playing (profiles), settings from your phone, language, unlocking `/data`, PS5SX2 Helper whitelist | Video settings apply while you play. Internal resolution, PGXP, region, BIOS, controller and SwanStation's options apply from the next game. ## RetroAchievements SwanStationPS5 never asks for your password on the console. You sign in once from your PC: the tool swaps your password for a login token, and only the token is copied to the PS5. ```bash python tools/SwanStationPS5_sync.py ra-login --host ``` Restart SwanStationPS5 and it signs in by itself. Start a game, and if it has an achievement set, a banner shows how many you have unlocked. With several profiles (Settings → System → Who's playing), each person signs in for their own profile, using its name as shown on the console: ```bash python tools/SwanStationPS5_sync.py ra-login --host --profile "Player 2" ``` - **Your profile** (Settings → Achievements) shows your points, the games you've mastered, recent unlocks and the games closest to mastery. Covers show a trophy badge with your progress. - **Hardcore mode** (Settings → Achievements) turns off loading states and cheats, as RetroAchievements requires. Turning it on restarts the running game. - Hardcore mode follows RetroAchievements' [hardcore compliance requirements](https://docs.retroachievements.org/general/hardcore-compliance-requirements.html): cheats, save states, quick resume, rewind and autosave are off; turning it on resets the running game; fast-forward is off; there is no slow motion or frame advance. The user agent sent to the server is `SwanStationPS5/ (PS5) rcheevos/`. - Without a connection, unlocks are kept and sent when the console is back online. - Games are recognised by the same disc hash RetroArch uses, so the usual RetroAchievements-compatible dumps (Redump) work. When a version isn't in any set (some PlayStation Store or patched images), SwanStationPS5 says so. ## Cheats Nothing to install: when a game starts, SwanStationPS5 finds its file among libretro-database's PlayStation cheats and downloads it (the first time, the list appears a few seconds into the game). Games without a file there have no cheats. In a game, open the SwanStationPS5 menu → **Cheats** and switch codes on and off. Cheats tied to one level ("... Stage") can freeze the game when the level ends: turn them off before. Your choice is remembered per game. To use your own codes, put a `cheats.cht` in the game's folder. ## PC tool `tools/SwanStationPS5_sync.py` runs on Windows with Python 3 (and [7-Zip](https://www.7-zip.org/) for archives). ```bash python tools/SwanStationPS5_sync.py plan --source "D:\Games\PS1" # what it would do, read-only python tools/SwanStationPS5_sync.py sync --source "D:\Games\PS1" --host # prepare + upload, one game at a time python tools/SwanStationPS5_sync.py covers --host # covers for your games python tools/SwanStationPS5_sync.py cheats --host # the cheat library python tools/SwanStationPS5_sync.py bios scph5501.bin --host # your own BIOS dump python tools/SwanStationPS5_sync.py ra-login --host # RetroAchievements python tools/SwanStationPS5_sync.py app --app-dir PPSA98510 --host # install or update the app ``` `sync` handles the whole library, one game at a time: - unpacks `.7z` / `.rar` / `.zip` archives, including archives inside archives and split archives - writes missing `.cue` sheets and `.m3u` playlists for multi-disc games - skips duplicates - uploads to `/data/SwanStationPS5/games/` - sets the permissions It remembers what is already on the console, so you can run it again whenever you add games. ## Known limitations - **SwanStation works best with a BIOS** for the game's region; without one it uses its built-in OpenBIOS, which is less compatible. - **Sandboxed mode.** If etaHEN won't unlock `/data`, SwanStationPS5 still runs: it reads the game list the PC tool uploads (`library.txt`) instead of listing the folder. - **Closing from the PS button** crashed the console once during testing while `/data` was unlocked through etaHEN. If it happens to you, set *Settings → System → Unlock /data with etaHEN* to Off and let us know. - The PS5's own keyboard and on-screen keyboard aren't used, so text entry (like the RetroAchievements sign-in) happens on the PC. ## Building from source To build the PS5 app on Linux or WSL (Ubuntu 24.04): ```bash sudo apt install clang-18 lld-18 llvm-18 make ninja-build ccache pkg-config python3 python3-venv tar unzip wget git clone https://github.com/darkxex/SwanStationPS5.git cd SwanStationPS5 git submodule update --init --recursive third_party/rcheevos git submodule update --init third_party/swanstation make # -> dist/PPSA98510/ and dist/PPSA98510.zip make disc-daemon # -> dist/SwanStationPS5-DiscDaemon.elf, the disc daemon payload python3 tools/make_release.py # optional: build the payload and the app, and pack PPSA98510.zip ``` `make` builds SwanStation (`tools/build-swanstation.sh`) and rcheevos (`tools/build-rcheevos.sh`) as static libraries, links the RADV Vulkan driver (`tools/fetch-radv.sh`), compiles `src/` and signs `eboot.bin`. `APP_VULKAN=0` builds without Vulkan and SwanStation. | Path | What | |---|---| | `src/main.c` | screens and main loop | | `src/core/host.c` | libretro host for the built-in cores | | `src/core/swanstation_options.c` | SwanStation's core options, made by `tools/gen_swanstation_options.py` | | `src/ra/` | RetroAchievements | | `src/ui/` | cover flow, text, sounds | | `src/platform/` | PS5 video output, input, heap, scaling filters | | `tools/SwanStationPS5_sync.py` | the PC tool | | `payload/discd.c` | the disc daemon payload, built by `make disc-daemon` into `dist/SwanStationPS5-DiscDaemon.elf` | | `tools/make_release.py` | builds the payload and the app, packs PPSA98510.zip (with `--ip`, also uploads the app to the console) | | `tools/make_dds.py` | converts the two backgrounds to the BC7 `pic0.dds` / `pic1.dds` | | `tools/make_art.py` | generates the icon and the home-screen art | | `docs/boilerplate/` | documentation of the PS5 app boilerplate SwanStationPS5 is built on | ## repos.name: TitaniaPy
repos.description: A Python CLI tool that parses, analyzes, and decrypts PS5 PUP/BLS files on PC — no console required. Features BLS extraction, Layer 3 firmware decryption, PBKDF2/KMB key derivation, and entropy-based key testing. One key away from full PUP decryption for all firmware versions.
repos.readme:
# PS5 PUP Decrypt Tool

PC-based Python tool for parsing and decrypting PS5 PUP (PlayStation Update Package) files. No console needed.

## Status

The tool handles 3 of 4 crypto layers. **Layer 1 (PUP container encryption) is the one missing piece** — see [RESEARCH_POST.md](RESEARCH_POST.md) for the full technical write-up and what's needed.

| Layer | Purpose | Status |
|-------|---------|--------|
| 0 | PBKDF2 master key derivation | Solved |
| 1 | PUP container encryption | **Blocked — key not public** |
| 2 | PUP segment-level encryption | Blocked (depends on Layer 1) |
| 3 | Inner firmware encryption | Solved |

## Setup

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

Requires Python 3.10+, [pycryptodome](https://pypi.org/project/pycryptodome/), and [capstone](https://pypi.org/project/capstone/) (for automated handler disassembly).

## Usage

```bash
# Show PUP file structure (BLS container + PUP header)
python main.py info PS5UPDATE.PUP

# Extract inner entries from BLS container
python main.py extract PS5UPDATE.PUP -o output_dir/

# Decrypt inner firmware blobs with known Layer 3 keys
python main.py decrypt firmware_blob.bin -k emc_ipl_header

# Bruteforce-test an unknown blob against all known keys
python main.py bruteforce unknown_blob.bin

# Analyze entropy of a binary blob
python main.py analyze blob.bin

# Show all known keys and derivation results
python main.py keys

# Decompress a zlib-compressed segment
python main.py decompress segment.bin -o decompressed.bin
```

## Files

### Core Tool
| File | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `main.py` | CLI entry point — 7 commands |
| `keys.py` | All known PS5 keys (ROM, keyseeds, OTP/KDF, Titania, firmware) |
| `bls.py` | BLS (SLB2) outer container parser |
| `pup.py` | PUP inner structure parser |
| `crypto.py` | AES-128-CBC/ECB, PBKDF2, Layer 3 decrypt functions |
| `firmware.py` | Inner firmware decryptor with entropy analysis |

### Key Extraction (for jailbroken PS5)
| File | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `ps5_key_extract.c` | C payload — 5 approaches to extract the missing PUP container key |
| `analyze_dump.py` | Parses the dump, tests key candidates, and auto-disassembles handlers to find the key source |

### Documentation
| File | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `RESEARCH_POST.md` | Full technical write-up of findings |
| `EXTRACTION_GUIDE.md` | Step-by-step walkthrough for running the extraction |

## Key Extraction Payload (V2)

 * **V4 has replaced V2 (ps5_key_extractV4.c &
ps5_key_extractV4.elf)**
 
* **!!V4 possesses abilities
to flash southbridge WITHOUT a backup.!!**
 

If you have a jailbroken PS5 on FW 13.60 or below, `ps5_key_extract.c` implements a **chained extraction strategy**:

**The chain: Approach 2 → automated RE → Approach 5**
1. Dump the `pup_update0` ioctl/open/close handler code (only needs kernel R/W)
2. Run `analyze_dump.py` on PC — it auto-disassembles the handlers and finds the key source
3. Re-run the payload with the `-a <address>` command it gives you

**All five approaches:**
1. **CCP LSB Key Slot Dump + Queue Registers** — Reads all 128 hardware key slots AND queue config registers (shows which slots are CPU-readable)
2. **Full EncryptService Handler Dump** — Dumps 16KB each of `d_ioctl`, `d_open`, and `d_close` handlers plus the full `cdevsw` struct
3. **Instrumented PUP Decrypt** — Invokes `DecryptHeader` ioctl with type=1 (system update key) between pre/post LSB snapshots to catch key loading
4. **Kernel Memory Scan** — Searches near crypto-related strings
5. **Targeted Address Read** — Re-run mode: reads a specific kernel or physical address after RE reveals the key location

```bash
# Full scan — run all approaches
./ps5_key_extract

# Targeted read — using the address from analyze_dump.py's recommendations
./ps5_key_extract -a 0xFFFFFFFF82345678
./ps5_key_extract -a 0xFFFFFFFF82345678 -s 256

# Analyze on PC (tests keys + auto-disassembles handlers)
python analyze_dump.py pup_key_dump.bin --pup14 PS5UPDATE14.00.PUP --pup14_1 PS5UPDATE14.10.PUP

# Save handler .bin files for manual Ghidra/IDA analysis
python analyze_dump.py pup_key_dump.bin --save-handlers
```

**Requirements:** FreeBSD 11 amd64 cross-compiler, kernel R/W via Byepervisor Reborn + Relapse + etaHEN or similar. You'll need to provide your framework's `kernel_read64` / `kernel_copyout` functions.

## Contributing

The tool is one key away from full PUP decryption. If you have console access and can run the extraction payload or dump the EncryptService, open an issue or DM.

---

*All research conducted on personally owned hardware for educational purposes. Referenced keys are publicly documented on psdevwiki.*

latestRelease.name: PS5_Key_ExtractV4-Read-Only
latestRelease.body:
* Goal: Extract the PUP container decryption key from a jailbroken PS5. This is the one missing key needed to decrypt PS5 firmware update files (PUP files) on PC.
---
* Target: The AMD CCP v5 (Cryptographic Co-Processor) and Sony’s EncryptService kernel driver (/dev/pup_update0). The PS5 uses this hardware+driver combo to decrypt firmware — the key lives in the CCP’s private key slots, which the CPU normally can’t read.
---
* Attack surface (default scan, no flags):

 * **CCP MMIO registers**
 * — reads the hardware’s public/private slot masks to see which key slots exist and which are CPU-accessible
Kernel cdevsw — finds Sony’s PUP decrypt driver in kernel memory, dumps the ioctl handler code (the function that actually calls the CCP to decrypt)
 * **CCP command queue**
 * — triggers a decrypt operation, then reads the raw CCP command descriptors the driver submitted. These reveal the exact AES mode, key size, and which slot number holds the key
Kernel symbol table — resolves sceSblServiceCrypt, sceSblSsDecryptPupHeader, etc. to get their addresses and dump their code.
---
Attack surface (with flags):

 * **-p <slot>** — submits a CCP PASSTHROUGH command to copy a private key slot’s contents to readable memory. This is the extraction step — it bypasses the CPU read mask by having the CCP itself do the copy
* **-d** — feeds a real encrypted PUP header to the decrypt ioctl and captures the output (decryption oracle)
---
* **What it doesn’t touch:**
*  No writes to flash, NVS, syscon, or kernel memory. The default scan is 100% read-only. Only -p writes (a single 32-byte CCP command descriptor).

repos.name: afterglow
repos.description: Radio and visuals for PS5: 222 free internet radio stations, your own USB music, and 56 beat-synced scenes. Native homebrew app.
repos.readme:
# Afterglow **Radio and visuals for PS5.** 222 free internet radio stations in 17 genres, your own music from USB, and 56 audio-reactive scenes that move in time with the beat. [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/DevvNirvana/afterglow?label=release&color=e8a33d)](https://github.com/DevvNirvana/afterglow/releases/latest) [![Licence](https://img.shields.io/badge/licence-GPL--3.0--or--later-blue)](LICENSE) [![PS5](https://img.shields.io/badge/PS5-firmware%2013.60-0070d1)](#install) [![Title ID](https://img.shields.io/badge/title%20ID-PPSA47770-555)](#install) [Download](https://github.com/DevvNirvana/afterglow/releases/latest) · [Screenshots](#screenshots) · [Install](#install) · [Controls](#controls) · [Radio](#radio) · [Build](#build)
Afterglow is a native homebrew app for the PS5 (OpenGL 4.6, no emulation, no web view). The player changes its look with the genre, shows the album art of the song on air, announces every new song, keeps the songs you like, takes short commands ("play bollywood 90s", "next", "show calm scenes"), and the visuals can run themselves like a VJ. > Status: tested on a PS5 (firmware 13.60, Relapse). Title ID PPSA47770. ## Highlights - **222 stations, 17 genres.** Electronic first (Techno, House, Trance, Drum & Bass, Bass, Hard Dance, EDM, Synthwave, Chill), then Pop, Hip-Hop, R&B, Bollywood & Desi, Latin, K-Pop, Afrobeats and Arabic. Only public streams, played live. - **56 scenes in six packs,** drawn with OpenGL shaders and tied to the music. Paint Swirl opens the app. - **Beat sync.** The scenes lock to the measured tempo, and Auto-VJ cuts at the end of a phrase. - **My Music.** Songs from a USB drive (MP3, AAC, Ogg Vorbis, Opus) with their tags and covers. - **Genre skins.** Every channel dresses the whole screen in its own style. - **Commands.** Hold Triangle and type what you want. - **Crossfade, station logos, album art, liked songs.** ## Screenshots Pictures rendered by the app's PC preview build, with a stand-in radio. The visuals are the same code and shaders as on the console. ### Genre skins Moving through the channels, the whole screen changes its clothes: Techno, House, Trance, Synthwave, Bollywood, Latin, K-Pop, Afrobeats and Arabic. ### Scenes | Gallery: art objects | Calm: for winding down | | :---: | :---: | | | | | **Trip: psychedelic feedback** | **Club and Retro** | | | | ### Around the app | Song card | Command box | | :---: | :---: | | | | | **Scene list** | **Settings** | | | | ## Install 1. Download `PPSA47770.zip` from the [latest release](https://github.com/DevvNirvana/afterglow/releases/latest). 2. Unzip it, so you have the `PPSA47770` folder. 3. Copy that folder to `/data/homebrew/` on the console (FTP works). 4. Wait about ten seconds for the console to register it, then launch Afterglow from the home screen. It needs a PS5 on firmware 13.60 running the Relapse jailbreak. For your own music, plug a USB drive into the console; see [My Music](#radio). ## What is in it - **Genre skins.** Every channel has its own type, colours, banner and list styling: a Teletech-style warehouse look for Techno (red ticker tape, corner brackets, glitching title), a spinning record for House, rings of light for Trance, hazard tape for Drum & Bass, LFO waves for Bass, strobing chevrons for Hard Dance, sweeping lasers for EDM, a sliced sun over a grid for Synthwave, drifting bokeh for Chill, bubbles for Pop, halftone and paint drips for Hip-Hop, silk for R&B, marigold garlands and a turning mandala for Bollywood, cut-paper flags and a blooming flower for Latin, a sea of lightsticks for K-Pop, woven kente and a talking drum for Afrobeats, an eight-point star lattice and a swinging lantern for Arabic. Moving through the channels, the whole screen changes its clothes. - **Station logos** in the station list and on the now-playing cover, from Radio Browser, fetched as they come on screen and cached. - **Album art.** The song title a station sends is looked up in MusicBrainz and the cover comes from the Cover Art Archive (both free and open). It is cached on the console. A record (or a CD) slides out of the cover while the music plays. Without a cover, the station gets a generated one in its genre's style. - **56 scenes in six packs:** the originals, a Trip pack of psychedelic scenes and Milkdrop-style feedback presets, a Club pack, a Gallery pack of scenes like art objects (gold-mended pottery, stained glass, paper cuts, ferrofluid, a snowflake), a Calm pack for winding down (tide pool, aurora, lanterns, rain on glass, moonlit sea, jellyfish) and a Retro pack. Paint Swirl opens the app; the best scenes come first in the list. - **Beat sync:** a beat tracker measures the tempo and where the beats fall; the scenes move at the music's pace, pulses land on the beat even where a kick is buried, loops last a beat, a bar or a phrase, and Auto-VJ cuts at the end of a phrase. - **Your own music:** songs on a USB drive (MP3, AAC, Ogg Vorbis, Opus) show up in *My Music* with their titles, artists, albums and embedded covers, and play one after another with the same visuals, song cards and likes. - **Commands:** hold Triangle over the visuals (or type in the radio's search) and write what you want: "play bollywood 90s", "play some k-pop", "next station", "like this song", "show trippy scenes", "party mode", "sleep in 30 minutes", "turn it up". Everyday names work ("hindi", "reggaeton", "dnb", "nineties"). - **Crossfade:** a new station (or the next song from the drive) blends in over the one playing; Off, 2, 3 or 5 seconds. - **Song card:** when a new song starts, a card shows its cover, title and artist in the genre's style (in the corner, across the middle, or off), also while the controls are hidden. Long titles shrink and wrap to fit. - **Liked songs and history:** Square over the visuals likes the song on air. The radio has a *Liked songs* channel and a *Song history* of the last 50 songs; Cross on a song tunes in to its station. The liked songs are also written to `liked-songs.txt` in the app's storage, to read on a PC. - **Scene list:** Cross opens all 56 scenes by pack; the one under the focus plays behind the list as you move. Square stars a scene, and Auto-VJ can use only your starred scenes. - **Auto-VJ** picks scenes that suit the genre on air and cuts on the drop. The tempo (BPM) shows in the corner. - **Sound:** a Loudness setting (+6 or +12 dB, held by a peak limiter so it does not distort), EQ presets (Flat, Bass boost, Club, Vocal) and an output meter in the settings. The music volume starts at 8 of 10 (the kit's default was far too quiet for radio). - **Station idents:** a new station is announced in its genre's style. - **Settings** (Options): mode, trip level, palette (including one taken from the album art), look, flashing on or off, display (Normal, Party with big type and a clock, Ambient: slow and dim), song card, Auto-VJ scenes (Genre, Favorites or Calm), beat sync, a sleep timer, volume, loudness, EQ, crossfade, sensitivity, beat rumble and resuming the last station at start. ## Scenes | Pack | Scenes | | --- | --- | | Afterglow | Paint Swirl, Orb, Nebula, Ember Peak, Pulse Tunnel, Cathedral Rays, Hall of Candles, Prism | | Trip | Wormhole, Mirror Maze, Kaleidoscope, Fractal Bloom, Vortex, Hypnotic, Dimension, Kaleido Melt, Acid Bloom, Echo Orb, Smoke Signals, Silk, Liquid Dream, Starfall, Neon Smear, Spiral Rings, Melting Bars | | Club | Liquid Chrome, Rave Tunnel, Bubble Pop, Strobe Lasers, Scope, Classic Bars | | Gallery | Stained Glass, Kintsugi, Paper Cut, Crystal Growth, Coral Labyrinth, Halftone Pop, Lissajous Loom, Origami, Ferrofluid, Ridgelines | | Calm | Tide Pool, Aurora Veil, Lantern Drift, Moon Tide, Cloud Sea, Deep Sea Glow, Slow Ink, Rain on Glass, Sand Ripples, Fireflies | | Retro | Skyline, Green Rain, Mode Seven, Polygon 95, Demo Plasma | Every scene follows 16 spectrum bands, the waveform, the beat and the beat clock. The feedback presets draw each frame over the last one, zoomed, turned, warped, mirrored and faded, so everything leaves trails; the trip level (D-pad up and down) sets how far they melt. Paint Swirl, Orb and Prism are ported from React Bits by David Haz (see `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`). ## Controls Over the visualiser: | Button | Action | | --- | --- | | Circle | Open the radio | | L1 / R1 | Previous / next station (or song) | | L3 | Play / pause | | Cross | The scene list (Square stars a scene, Circle goes back) | | D-pad left/right | Next or previous scene | | D-pad up/down | Trip level: Calm, Normal, Melt | | Square | Like the song on air (again: unlike) | | L2 | Next palette | | R3 | Auto-VJ on or off | | Left stick | Steer the camera | | R2 | Drive: push the light up | | Triangle | Hide or show the overlay (for clean recordings); hold it for the command box | | Options | Settings | In the radio: | Button | Action | | --- | --- | | D-pad | Move; left and right switch between channels and stations | | Cross | Play the station (next/previous then stay in that channel); on a song, tune in to its station | | Square | Add to or remove from Favorites; on a song, like or unlike it | | Triangle | Search by name, style, genre or country, or type a command ("play techno") | | L1 / R1 | Previous / next station | | R2 / L2 | Play-pause / stop | | Options | Check every station (in the background) | | R3 | Show only stations that passed the check | | Circle | Back to the visualiser | ## Radio The radio is laid out like a satellite-radio receiver: **channels** on the left (Favorites, Recently played, Liked songs, Song history, All stations, My Music, then seventeen genres: Techno, House, Trance, Drum & Bass, Bass & Dubstep, Hard Dance, EDM & Dance, Synthwave, Chill & Electronica, Pop & Hits, Hip-Hop & Rap, R&B & Soul, Bollywood & Desi, Latin, K-Pop, Afrobeats, Arabic), the **stations** of the channel in the middle, and **now playing** on the right: the cover, the station, the song, the format, the time on air and the transport. The stations are in `assets/radio/stations.txt`, one per line: `Category | Name | Style | Country | Format | Stream address`, optionally followed by `| Logo address`. To use your own list without rebuilding, put a `stations.txt` in the install folder (`/data/homebrew/PPSA47770/stations.txt`); it is read instead. - **Formats:** MP3; AAC and AAC+ on the console (FAAD2); Ogg Vorbis (stb_vorbis) and Ogg Opus (libopus), chained streams included, with their song titles. FLAC and HLS (`.m3u8`) do not play yet. - **My Music:** the app looks for songs on the USB drives the console mounts (`/mnt/usb0` to `/mnt/usb7`), any folder up to six deep, at most 4,000 songs, and again whenever a drive is plugged in or taken out. MP3, AAC (`.aac`), Ogg and Opus play; `.m4a`, FLAC and WAV are not listed yet. - **Network:** libcurl with OpenSSL on the console, set up the way BlackBearReloaded's console-tested apps do (`src/platform/ps5/console_curl.c`). - **Checking stations:** Options in the radio tries every station and marks it green or red; R3 then hides the red ones. From a PC, `python tools/check-stations.py --write-good good.txt` does the same. - **Saved on the console:** favourites, recently played, the last check, the song history, the liked songs, the visualiser's settings and the album art cache, in the app's own storage. - **Bollywood & Desi:** 23 stations (Bollywood hits and classics, Punjabi, Tamil, filmi) from Radio Browser's checked list. Song titles sent in Devanagari or other Indian scripts are not drawn yet (the fonts are Latin); the song card is skipped for them. - **Latin, K-Pop, Afrobeats, Arabic:** 16, 13, 14 and 12 stations from the same checked list (reggaeton, salsa and bachata; idol pop and city pop; Afrobeats, Amapiano and Afro House from Lagos, Accra and Johannesburg; Arabic pop, tarab, raï and chaabi). Song titles in Korean or Arabic script are not drawn yet either. Stations whose terms forbid third-party players (SomaFM, for one) are left out. If a station asks to be removed, it is removed. Album art is looked up politely: at most one MusicBrainz request a second, with a User-Agent that names the app, and every answer is cached. ## How it listens The app plays its music, and the radio, through the kit's mixer. Afterglow taps the music inside the mixer (so the picture stays in time with what you hear), runs a 2048-point FFT, groups it into 16 bands spaced by pitch, normalises them automatically, smooths them like a VU meter, detects beats from jumps in the bass and drops from the bass returning after a breakdown. See `src/audio/` and `src/concepts/afterglow.cpp`. ## Build Linux, WSL or Docker (see `CLAUDE.md` for the Windows Docker commands): ```bash make # PS5 app folder and ZIP in dist/ make test-unit # unit tests with sanitizers tools/host-snapshots.sh build/snapshots afterglow # PC preview pictures HUI_WARM=30 tools/host-snapshots.sh build/snapshots afterglow # with feedback trails grown ``` The home-screen backgrounds are rendered by the app itself (`HUI_POSTER=pic0.png tools/host-snapshots.sh out afterglow 3840 2160`) and converted with `python3 tools/png-to-dds.py` (BC7, as the console wants). Copy `dist/PPSA47770/` to `/data/homebrew/` on the console and launch it like any other native homebrew title. ## Credits and licence Afterglow is built on [ps5-homebrew-ui](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-homebrew-ui) by BlackBearReloaded (its renderer, UI kit, mixer and background music), the [PS5 Payload SDK](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk) by John Törnblom, [minimp3](https://github.com/lieff/minimp3) by lieff, [stb_image](https://github.com/nothings/stb) by Sean Barrett, libcurl, OpenSSL and FAAD2 from PacBrew, three scenes ported from [React Bits](https://github.com/DavidHDev/react-bits) by David Haz, and the free fonts Bebas Neue, Michroma, Monoton, Bungee, Permanent Marker and Righteous. Album information comes from [MusicBrainz](https://musicbrainz.org) and covers from the [Cover Art Archive](https://coverartarchive.org). GPL-3.0-or-later; see `LICENSE` and `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`. The kit's original README is in `docs/UI-KIT-README.md`.

Afterglow 1.0.6: an internet radio and music visualizer for PS5.

# OmniPad PS5 🎮🚀 ### Universal Controller Engine & Web Control Center for PlayStation 5 (FW 7.00 – 13.60) [![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/Platform-ProsperoOS%20%2F%20FreeBSD-003791?style=for-the-badge)](docs/FIRMWARE_1360_GUIDE.md) [![Firmware](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firmware-7.00%20%E2%86%92%2013.60%20(Relapse)-00b4d8?style=for-the-badge)](docs/FIRMWARE_1360_GUIDE.md) [![Language](https://img.shields.io/badge/Language-C99%20%2F%20POSIX-f59e0b?style=for-the-badge&logo=c&logoColor=white)](src/) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-GPL%20v3.0-blue?style=for-the-badge)](LICENSE) > ### ⚖️ Legal Disclaimer & Fair Use Notice > This is an independent open-source research project developed strictly for **educational, accessibility, and hardware interoperability purposes** (allowing third-party controllers and adaptive peripherals to function on the console). > > - **No Proprietary Code:** This repository contains no proprietary Sony Interactive Entertainment code, no game DRM circumvention, and no cryptographic keys. It builds against the open-source community SDK (`ps5-payload-sdk`). > - **Nominative Fair Use:** "PlayStation", "PS5", "DualSense", "DualShock", "Xbox", "Nintendo", and any other product names or trademarks mentioned belong exclusively to their respective holders. They are used purely for descriptive and compatibility identification purposes under nominative fair use. --- ## 📌 Motivation & The Origin Story > 💬 *"Honestly? This whole project started because I was just a guy who wanted his **Machenike G5 Pro Max SE** controller working on his PS5."* I wanted to play 3-player and 4-player local games on my jailbroken PS5 (running FW 13.60 with `kstuff` and `shadowmountplus`). However, existing community tools either lacked 2.4GHz USB dongle hotplug support or broke on FW 13.60's user profile assignment screen (`0x803B0006`). **OmniPad PS5** is the result of solving that exact problem: building a low-level C subsystem for jailbroken PlayStation 5 consoles that provides **dynamic 250Hz USB Hotplug** (4ms polling) for 2.4G dongles and wired cables, while safely bypassing the profile assignment block. --- ## 🙏 Standing on the Shoulders of Giants (Credits & Origins) This project is an open-source consolidation, enhancement, and evolution built directly upon pioneering research and code shared by talented developers across the PS5 homebrew community. Sincere gratitude and foundational credit belong to: - 🎮 **sinfiltros**: Creator of [AnyPad-PS5](https://github.com/sinfiltros/AnyPad-PS5) — laid the groundwork for `libScePad` virtual DualSense emulation and native Bluetooth HCI/L2CAP research. - 🔌 **StonedModder / a-ddr**: Authors of [PoorDS4](https://github.com/a-ddr/PoorDS4) and Ghostcontrol — provided vital reference implementations for USB HID parsing, controller wake-up handshakes (Switch Pro, DS3), and asynchronous FreeBSD `/dev/ugen` polling. - 💉 **MegaCadeDev**: Author of [YetAnotherControllerEnabler](https://github.com/MegaCadeDev/YetAnotherControllerEnabler) — pioneering research into `SceShellUI` ptrace code cave injection to overcome the `0x803B0006` profile assignment screen. - 🛠️ **ChendoChap, SpecterDev, flatz & ps5-payload-sdk contributors**: Authors of the `ps5-payload-sdk`, `kstuff`, and kernel debugging tools making native C payloads possible. - 🚀 **LightningMods & etaHEN Team**: For their tireless dedication to the PS5 homebrew ecosystem. --- ## 🏛️ Architecture ```mermaid graph TD subgraph S1["1. Supported Peripherals"] USB["2.4GHz Wireless Dongles & USB Cables
(Machenike G5 Pro/SE, 8BitDo, Xbox, Switch Pro, DS4, DS3)"] end subgraph S2["2. OmniPad PS5 Core (Native C)"] HOTPLUG["Dynamic USB Hotplug Driver
(250Hz Polling / 4ms Tick)"] NORM["Canonical Input Normalizer
(pad_packet_t & Deadzones)"] SLOTS["3-Slot Multi-Device Multiplexer
(Virtual DualSense Pool)"] WEB["Web Server & REST API
(Port 8095 - Dark UI)"] TCP["Local LAN Testing Socket
(Port 9045 - TCP Stream)"] USB --> HOTPLUG HOTPLUG --> NORM NORM --> SLOTS SLOTS <--> WEB SLOTS <--> TCP end subgraph S3["3. ProsperoOS Kernel & ShellUI"] KERNEL["libScePad Virtual Device
(Type 3 DualSense)"] KLOG["Kernel Log Monitor /dev/klog
(64-bit Device ID Matching)"] SHELLUI["SceShellUI Injector
(Code Cave + W^X Safe Interception)"] SLOTS --> KERNEL KERNEL --> KLOG SLOTS -.->|On Connect| SHELLUI end subgraph S4["4. User Gameplay Experience"] GAMES["PS5 Games & Emulators
(Native Controller Recognition)"] KERNEL --> GAMES end ``` --- ## 🌟 Key Features | Feature | Details | |---|---| | **Dynamic USB Hotplug (250Hz)** | Plug & play any 2.4G dongle or USB cable on the fly (4ms tick latency). | | **Bypass Error `0x803B0006`** | Non-destructive `ptrace` code cave in `SceShellUI` respecting W^X protections. | | **Multi-Player (Up to 4 Players)** | 3 virtual DualSense slots (Players 2–4) + 1 official DualSense (Player 1). | | **Dynamic Bus Discovery** | Automatically scans `/dev/ugen*.*` nodes across PS5 Fat, Slim (CFI-2000), and Pro (CFI-7000). | | **Embedded Web Dashboard** | Dark UI dashboard on port 8095 for real-time slot status, battery monitoring, and manual controls. | | **LAN Test Port** | Inject test frames over TCP port 9045 without needing physical hardware connected. | --- ## 🕹️ Controller Compatibility & Hardware Testing Status (v1.0.4) > 🔬 **Developer Hardware Testing Disclosure:** > OmniPad PS5 is maintained by an independent solo developer. Currently, the developer physically owns and tests on a **Machenike G5 Pro Max SE** (2.4GHz USB Dongle & USB-C Cable). > > Support for **Xbox Series X\|S, Xbox One, DualShock 4, DualShock 3, and Switch Pro** was written based on official USB HID/GIP specifications, reference open-source drivers, and automated test suites. Because physical hardware was not on the developer's test bench during initial release, **these decoders are currently considered EXPERIMENTAL**. If you own these controllers, your testing reports and feedback are warmly welcomed to help fine-tune and verify them! > ⚠️ **Important Connection Notice (v1.0.4):** > OmniPad PS5 v1.0.4 operates **exclusively via USB ports** (physical USB cables and supported 2.4GHz USB wireless dongles). **Direct wireless Bluetooth pairing through the console's internal antenna is currently in active development for v1.1.0 and is NOT active in v1.0.4.** | Controller Brand | Supported Connection (v1.0.4) | Hardware Testing Status | Notes | |---|---|:---:|---| | **Machenike G5 Pro / G5 Pro Max SE** | Bundled 2.4GHz USB Dongle or USB-C Cable | 🟢 **Verified on PS5 Hardware** | Fully tested & verified in real 3-player gameplay on FW 13.60. Plug & play at 250Hz. | | **Microsoft Xbox Series X\|S & Xbox One** | Physical USB-C / Micro-USB Cable **OR** 8BitDo USB Adapter | 🟡 **Experimental (Spec-Implemented)** | Decodes GIP `0x20` input & `0x07` Guide packets via wired USB. *(Needs community testing on console)*. | | **Microsoft Xbox 360** | Wired USB Cable (`045e:028e`) | 🟡 **Experimental (Spec-Implemented)** | XInput wired report parser implemented. | | **Sony DualShock 4** | Physical Micro-USB Cable | 🟡 **Experimental (Spec-Implemented)** | 64-byte USB HID parser implemented. *(Direct BT in v1.1.0)*. | | **Sony DualShock 3 (PS3)** | Physical Mini-USB Cable | 🟡 **Experimental (Spec-Implemented)** | USB magic wake packet (`0x03f4`) implemented. *(No Bluetooth)*. | | **Nintendo Switch Pro** | Physical USB-C Cable | 🟡 **Experimental (Spec-Implemented)** | 3-step USB activation handshake implemented. *(Direct BT in v1.1.0)*. | | **8BitDo Wireless USB Adapter (v1 / v2)** | USB 2.4G Dongle | 🟡 **Experimental (Spec-Implemented)** | Bridges wireless controllers into USB HID/XInput. | | **Generic PC USB Gamepads** | Standard USB Cable (HID / XInput) | 🟡 **Experimental (Spec-Implemented)** | Standard 10-byte HID normalization. | --- ### 🔍 Transparent Clarifications: Microsoft Xbox Controllers To avoid any confusion or unmet expectations, please note the exact state of Xbox hardware support: 1. **Direct Bluetooth Pairing:** **NOT supported in v1.0.4.** Xbox One / Series X\|S controllers communicate via Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) requiring SMP AES-128 cryptographic pairing over the console's internal radio. This stack is actively being finalized for **v1.1.0**. 2. **Official "Xbox Wireless Adapter for Windows" (Microsoft Dongle):** **NOT supported.** The official Microsoft PC dongle uses a proprietary Wi-Fi Direct / GIP protocol that is not recognized by the FreeBSD/ProsperoOS USB driver. 3. **How to use Xbox Controllers Today in v1.0.4:** - **Option A (Wired):** Connect via a **data-capable** USB-C (Series X\|S) or Micro-USB (Xbox One) cable directly to any PS5 USB port. *(Ensure your cable has data lines; charge-only cables will not transmit inputs).* - **Option B (Wireless via Third-Party USB Adapter):** Pair your Xbox controller to an **8BitDo Wireless USB Adapter 2** plugged into the PS5. The 8BitDo adapter bridges the wireless signal into standard USB inputs. --- ### ⚠️ What to Expect & What NOT to Expect in v1.0.4 - ❌ **No Direct Console Bluetooth Yet:** You cannot currently put a controller into Bluetooth sync mode and connect directly to the PS5 without a USB cable or USB adapter. (Coming in v1.1.0). - ❌ **No Gyroscope / Motion Controls:** IMU sensors (accelerometer/gyro) report neutral values. Games strictly requiring motion controls must use the official DualSense on Player 1. - ❌ **No DualSense Adaptive Triggers / Haptics:** Non-DualSense controllers do not have Sony's proprietary force-feedback trigger motors. Standard rumble is handled natively where supported. - ❌ **No Multi-touch Touchpad Surface:** The touchpad is mapped as a single digital click (used by games to open maps or menus). - ℹ️ **Player 1 vs Virtual Slots:** OmniPad emulates **Players 2, 3, and 4** (3 virtual DualSense slots). The primary console user (Player 1) uses the official physical DualSense. *For full technical details and VID:PID tables, see [docs/COMPATIBILITY.md](docs/COMPATIBILITY.md).* --- ## 🚀 Quick Start & Usage Tutorial > 💡 **Pre-compiled Binary:** You do **not** need to compile anything from source. Download the ready-to-run `OmniPad-PS5.elf` directly from the [**GitHub Releases**](../../releases) tab (**v1.0 Beta Test**). --- ### Step 1: Load the Payload Send `OmniPad-PS5.elf` to your console using your preferred ELF loader or payload sender. *(A system notification will appear on the top right of your screen: `OmniPad PS5 v1.0.4 Ativo! Painel: porta 8095`)* --- ### Step 2: Connect Your Controller - **2.4GHz Dongles & USB Cables (Instant Plug & Play in v1.0.4):** Plug your USB dongle (e.g. **Machenike G5 Pro Max SE**, 8BitDo Wireless Adapter) or USB cable (DualShock 4, DualShock 3, Xbox, Switch Pro, etc.) into any front or rear USB port. The 250Hz hotplug driver recognizes it automatically within milliseconds. - **Direct Internal Bluetooth Wireless (In Development — Planned for v1.1.0):** Direct wireless pairing via the console's internal Bluetooth antenna (`bt_hci_usb`) is actively being finalized and will be exposed in the Web UI in the **v1.1.0** update. In v1.0.4, please use a USB cable or a wireless USB adapter/dongle (such as 8BitDo or manufacturer 2.4G dongles). --- ### Step 3: Assign User Profile (Bypassing Error `0x803B0006`) On firmwares like **13.60** (with `kstuff-1.13-fpkg-dr-test5` & `shadowmountplus v1.7 Beta 4`), profile assignment is automated via safe `SceShellUI` code caves: 1. Press the **PS / Home button** on your controller (or click **"Simulate PS Button"** in the Web Dashboard). 2. The official PS5 profile selection menu will appear on screen. 3. Choose the desired user profile for Player 1, 2, 3, or 4. --- ### Step 4: Live Web Dashboard (Port 8095) Open the control center from any smartphone, PC, or console browser on your local network: ``` http://:8095/ ``` - 🎮 **Slot Status:** Real-time visibility of all 4 player slots (connected gamepads and connection types). - ⚡ **Power Telemetry:** Live power status (`⚡ USB Cable / 5V` for wired controllers and dongles). - 🔘 **Simulate PS Button:** Remotely trigger the PS button to change accounts or open the system menu. - 🔄 **Disconnect Slot:** Free any individual slot instantly without unplugging hardware. --- ## 📚 Technical Documentation - [docs/COMPATIBILITY.md](docs/COMPATIBILITY.md) — Detailed controller compatibility and mappings. - [docs/FIRMWARE_1360_GUIDE.md](docs/FIRMWARE_1360_GUIDE.md) — FW 13.60 architecture, Relapse exploit, and code cave injection details. - [docs/HOW_IT_WORKS.md](docs/HOW_IT_WORKS.md) — In-depth breakdown of USB hotplug and virtual pad lifecycle. --- ## 📜 Credits & Acknowledgments Licensed under the **GNU GPL v3.0**. Fundamental credits to the community pioneers whose work inspired and paved the way: - **sinfiltros**: Author of [AnyPad-PS5](https://github.com/sinfiltros/AnyPad-PS5) for the native Bluetooth HCI/L2CAP stack. - **StonedModder / a-ddr**: Developers of [PoorDS4](https://github.com/a-ddr/PoorDS4) and Ghostcontrol for USB HID decoding and handshakes. - **MegaCadeDev**: Author of [YetAnotherControllerEnabler](https://github.com/MegaCadeDev/YetAnotherControllerEnabler) for SceShellUI injection insights. - The **ps5-payload-sdk**, **etaHEN**, and **kstuff** research teams.

### OmniPad PS5 v1.0.4 - Hotfix 1 (Build 19)

Hotfix release resolving profile selection stall, wired USB connection drops, and clarifying connectivity roadmap.

### 🚀 Highlights & Bug Fixes

* **Fixed Wired USB Stalls:** Restricted Xbox 360 keepalive packets strictly to genuine Microsoft hardware, eliminating USB-C pipeline stalls on ShanWan / Machenike G5 Pro Max SE and third-party controllers.
* **Clean Profile Picker (No Ghost "Connected" State):** Completely resolved an issue where profiles would appear as already connected after logging out in-game; now smoothly triggers the clean native PS5 profile picker.
* **Dynamic Handle Binding:** Added dynamic `scePadGetHandle` synchronization inside the main polling loop. As soon as you select your profile on the PS5 screen, your controller immediately takes over gameplay.
* **Extended 2.4G Standby Timeout:** Increased idle timeout for 2.4GHz dongles from 5 seconds to 60 seconds (1 minute), avoiding abrupt disconnections.
* **Safe Unbind Sequence:** Controller release now decouples MBus before destroying the virtual pad, avoiding kernel error `0x809B00FF`.
* **Documentation Transparency:** Clarified that direct internal Bluetooth is in active development for **v1.1.0** to ensure full hardware safety, focusing v1.0.4 on 250Hz USB & 2.4GHz dongles.

### 📦 Assets
* `OmniPad-PS5-1.0.4.elf` — Ready-to-run payload for PS5 (FW 7.00 - 13.60)

RPCS3
=====

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **This is a fork for the PlayStation 5 (a libretro core in
> [PS5_RetroArch](https://github.com/dmzebro/PS5_RetroArch)), not an official
> RPCS3 build; please do not report its problems to the RPCS3 team.**
>
> **No binaries of this fork are distributed, and none will be: you must compile
> it yourself from source.** RPCS3 is licensed GPL-2.0-only; the PS5 RetroArch
> title it runs in is GPL-3.0-or-later, and the two cannot be distributed
> together as one program. Build the whole title yourself with PS5_RetroArch's
> `tools/build-title.sh` (a development build: leave `PS5_RELEASE_TAG` unset),
> as its README describes under "PlayStation 3 (RPCS3): build it yourself", and
> keep what you build for your own console: do not share, upload or
> redistribute it.
>
> **Piracy is not condoned.** Use only your own PS3 system software
> (`PS3UPDAT.PUP`, from Sony's official update page) and legally obtained
> backups of games you own: discs you dumped yourself, or PSN purchases with
> their own licence files. No games, firmware or keys are provided.

[![GitHub Actions](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/RPCS3/rpcs3/rpcs3.yml?branch=master&logo=github&label=Actions)](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3/actions/workflows/rpcs3.yml)
[![RPCS3 Discord Server](https://img.shields.io/discord/272035812277878785?color=5865F2&label=RPCS3%20Discord&logo=discord&logoColor=white)](https://discord.gg/rpcs3)

The world's first free and open-source PlayStation 3 emulator/debugger, written in C++ for Windows, Linux, macOS and FreeBSD.

You can find some basic information on our [**website**](https://rpcs3.net/). Game info is being populated on the [**Wiki**](https://wiki.rpcs3.net/).
For discussion about this emulator, PS3 emulation, and game compatibility reports, please visit our [**forums**](https://forums.rpcs3.net) and our [**Discord server**](https://discord.gg/RPCS3).

[**Support the Lead Developers on Patreon**](https://rpcs3.net/patreon)

## Contributing

If you want to help the project but do not code, the best way to help out is to test games and make bug reports. See:
* [Quickstart](https://rpcs3.net/quickstart)

If you want to contribute as a developer, please take a look at the following pages:

* [Coding Style](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3/wiki/Coding-Style)
* [Developer Information](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3/wiki/Developer-Information)

You should also contact any of the developers in the forums or in the Discord server to learn more about the current state of the emulator.

### AI Use

Use of AI tools for research and reverse engineering purposes is permitted. However, contributors are expected to fully own and understand all code they submit. Any communication with the team — including code, code comments, and GitHub comments — must come from the human contributor, not an AI agent acting autonomously.

We have unfortunately seen a rise in untested and unverified AI-generated slop being submitted to this project. This wastes maintainer time and, in worse cases, such changes get merged and break functionality for all users. Repeated violations will result in a ban from the repository. Please be respectful of everyone's time.

**Pull requests opened by AI agents or automated tools must include a disclosure in the PR description** stating the scope of AI involvement — which parts were AI-generated and what human testing or review was performed prior to submission. PRs that omit this disclosure may be closed without review.

If you are unsure about your work, open a discussion issue to talk it through with the team, or reach out to a maintainer on [Discord](https://discord.gg/RPCS3).

## Building

See [BUILDING.md](BUILDING.md) for more information about how to setup an environment to build RPCS3.

## Running

Check our friendly [quickstart](https://rpcs3.net/quickstart) guide to make sure your computer meets the minimum system requirements to run RPCS3.

Don't forget to have your graphics driver up to date and to install the [Visual C++ Redistributable Packages for Visual Studio 2022](https://aka.ms/vs/17/release/VC_redist.x64.exe) if you are a Windows user.

## License

Most files are licensed under the terms of GNU GPL-2.0-only License; see LICENSE file for details. Some files may be licensed differently; check appropriate file headers for details.
