repos.name: PS5-NetDis
repos.readme:
NetDis

See every network port in use on a jailbroken PS5: who owns it, and who can reach it.

![NetDis on a TV: listening ports](docs/netdis-ports-tv.png) NetDis is a payload for a jailbroken PS5. It lists every TCP and UDP socket on the console: listening ports, open connections, and what is waiting to close. For each one it shows the process that owns it (and the game's title ID), the connection state, and whether other devices on your network can reach it. Everything is on a live page in the console's own browser, or on your phone. Use it to: - check which payloads are listening, and whether that's on the network or only on the console - see what a game or the system connects to - find what holds a port before starting a tool that needs it > The screenshots in this README come from a test run with sample data on a > PC, so the page looks exactly as it does on the console. ## Contents - [What you need](#what-you-need) - [Quick start](#quick-start) - [Using NetDis](#using-netdis) - [How it works](#how-it-works) - [Files on the console](#files-on-the-console) - [Limits](#limits) - [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting) - [Versions and releases](#versions-and-releases) - [Building from source](#building-from-source) - [Credits](#credits) ## What you need - A PS5 that is jailbroken and running an **ELF loader** on port `9021`. Firmware up to 13.60 works with the Relapse exploit, which provides one. - A way to send a payload: Payload Manager, the exploit's payload menu, or a computer on the same network (`socat` or `make test`). - Optional: [Payload Manager](https://github.com/itsPLK/ps5-payload-manager), to start NetDis automatically after each jailbreak. ## Quick start 1. **Download `NetDis.elf`** from the [latest release](https://github.com/eladharels/ps5-netdis/releases/latest) (or the zip, which also has this README and the changelog). 2. **Send it to the console** after jailbreaking: ```bash socat -t 99999999 - TCP::9021 < NetDis.elf ``` or pick it in Payload Manager. The console shows *"NetDis v1.0.0 running: http://<ps5-ip>:8070"*. 3. **Open NetDis.** On the home screen, go to **Media** and open the **NetDis** tile. It opens the page in the console's browser. On a phone or computer on the same network, open `http://:8070` instead. NetDis keeps running until the console restarts or goes into rest mode. Send it again after a reboot, or add `NetDis.elf` to Payload Manager's autoload list. ## Using NetDis ### Ports The **Ports** tab opens on the **listening ports**: everything waiting for connections. The four numbers at the top count: - listening ports - how many of them your network can reach - open connections - processes with sockets Each port shows: - **Port and protocol:** TCP or UDP, with a `6` for IPv6. - **Reachable from:** - **Network:** bound to every address, so other devices on your home network can connect. - **This console:** bound to `127.0.0.1` / `::1`, so only programs on the PS5 can reach it. - **One address:** bound to one specific interface. - **Process:** the program that owns the socket, its process ID, and the game's title ID if a game owns it. - **Usually:** what normally runs on that port number, such as *ELF loader* on 9021 or *Remote Play* on 9295. It's only a hint; the process column is the truth. Switch the view to **Connections** to see what's talking to what: ![NetDis connections](docs/netdis-connections-tv.png) Connections show the local and remote address and the TCP state: *ESTABLISHED*, *SYN_SENT* (still connecting), *TIME_WAIT* (closed, waiting to be cleaned up) and so on. Sockets that no process holds any more appear as *(no process)*. **All sockets** shows both lists together. - The page refreshes **every 2 seconds**. New sockets flash green. **Pause** freezes the list so you can read it. - Click a **column header** to sort; click again to reverse. - **Search** matches ports, addresses, states, process names and title IDs. - **TCP / UDP** filters by protocol. On a phone, each socket becomes a card, so nothing is cut off.
### Processes ![NetDis processes](docs/netdis-processes-tv.png) The **Processes** tab groups sockets by program. Listening ports are green; connections show where they go and their state. Search by process name, title ID or port. ### Logs and Settings ![NetDis settings](docs/netdis-settings-tv.png) - **Logs:** what NetDis did, with level and text filters, **Copy** and **Download**. **Diagnose** logs every socket found and how the TCP states were read. - **Settings:** - remove or reinstall the home screen tile - stop NetDis - **About**: the address for your phone, the build, which TCP-state mode is active (see below), and how many processes were inspected ### Updating and stopping - **Update:** send the new `NetDis.elf`. It asks the running copy to stop and takes its place, and you get *"NetDis restarted"*. - **Stop:** use **Stop** in Settings, or kill `NetDis.elf` in Payload Manager's process list. ## How it works ```mermaid flowchart LR procs["every process
(kern.proc.proc)"] --> fd["its open descriptors
(kern.proc.filedesc)"] fd --> socks["TCP/UDP sockets:
addresses, owner, fd"] pcb["kernel TCP list
(net.inet.tcp.pcblist)"] --> check{"record layout
matches SDK headers?"} check -- yes --> full["full TCP states
+ sockets with no owner"] check -- no --> listen["listening flag only"] socks --> merge["match by socket
(so_pcb)"] full --> merge listen --> merge merge --> api["/api/sockets
(cached 1 s)"] --> page["page :8070"] ``` 1. **Who owns what.** NetDis walks every process and reads its open file descriptors through `kern.proc.filedesc`, the interface FreeBSD's `procstat` uses. For each TCP/UDP socket that gives the local and remote address, the descriptor number and the owner. Its layout is a fixed, user-facing interface, so this part doesn't depend on Sony's kernel internals. The owning game's title ID comes from the system's app info. 2. **TCP states.** The kernel's TCP list (`net.inet.tcp.pcblist`) holds each connection's state, but its records embed internal kernel structures that Sony may have changed. - **Record sizes match the SDK headers:** NetDis reads the full states, and also lists closed connections no process holds any more (such as *TIME_WAIT*). - **They don't match:** NetDis takes only the listening flag, from a part it locates and checks first, and leaves other states blank. Settings > About shows which mode is active. 3. **The page.** Results are cached for a second, so several open pages share one collection. NetDis serves its page on port `8070`. The home screen tile is a small media app whose link opens `http://127.0.0.1:8070/` in the console's browser. ## Files on the console | Path | What it is | | --- | --- | | `/data/netdis/NetDis.log` | The log of the current run (`NetDis.log.1` is the previous run) | | `/data/netdis/no-tile` | Present if you removed the home screen tile | | `/user/app/NETD00001` | The home screen tile | ## Limits - **Snapshot, not a capture.** NetDis shows which sockets exist; it doesn't record traffic. Very short connections can open and close between two refreshes. - **Port hints are guesses.** The *Usually* column is based on the port number only. - **Your network.** NetDis's page is reachable by anything on your home network, like the ELF loader. Don't forward these ports to the internet. ## Troubleshooting | Problem | What to do | | --- | --- | | The list is empty | Open **Logs** and press **Diagnose**: it logs how many processes were read and any that failed. | | TCP states are blank | Settings > About says *listening only*: the kernel's TCP list layout differs on this firmware. Listening ports are still marked; send the Diagnose log to whoever helps you. | | The tile isn't on the home screen | In **Settings**, press **Install tile**, then filter the log for `tile`. | | *"port 8070 is busy"* | Another program uses port 8070, or the running NetDis didn't stop. Restart the console. | | The tile opens an error page | NetDis isn't running. Send `NetDis.elf` again (or add it to Payload Manager's autoload). | ## Versions and releases Every version is published on the [Releases page](https://github.com/eladharels/ps5-netdis/releases) with: - `NetDis.elf`, ready to send to the console - `NetDis-vX.Y.Z.zip`, which holds the same ELF plus this README and the changelog What changed in each version is in [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) and in each release's notes. The running version is shown in the start notification and under Settings > About. Version numbers follow [semantic versioning](https://semver.org): - **X:** goes up for changes that break your setup. - **Y:** goes up for new features. - **Z:** goes up for fixes. Publishing a new version (for maintainers): 1. In a pull request, put the new number in `VERSION` and add a `## [X.Y.Z] - date` section at the top of `CHANGELOG.md`. 2. Merge it into `main`. 3. The *release* workflow then: - runs the tests - builds with the pinned SDK (v0.44) - creates the tag `vX.Y.Z` - publishes the release with the changelog section as its notes It skips versions that already have a release. You can also start it by hand from Actions > release > Run workflow. ## Building from source ```bash sudo apt-get install make clang-18 lld-18 llvm-18 wget unzip zip python3 socat wget https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk/releases/download/v0.44/ps5-payload-sdk.zip sudo unzip -d /opt ps5-payload-sdk.zip export PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK=/opt/ps5-payload-sdk LLVM_CONFIG=/usr/bin/llvm-config-18 make # NetDis.elf make check # host tests: no SDK or console needed make dist # build/NetDis-vX.Y.Z.zip make test PS5_HOST= # send NetDis.elf and stream its log ``` ### Tests `make check` runs on a normal Linux PC with AddressSanitizer and UBSan: - the socket model: states, reachability, port hints - the JSON the page reads - the one-second cache and a failed collection - the web routes - a real server test: an idle connection doesn't block other requests, and a stop request is answered before the server exits ### CI GitHub Actions builds `NetDis.elf`, runs the tests and uploads the `NetDis` artifact on every push and pull request. An optional deploy job sends the build to your console. It needs a self-hosted runner on your home network, since GitHub's cloud runners can't reach the console. Configure it with these repository variables: | Variable | Default | Meaning | | --- | --- | --- | | `PS5_HOST` | unset: deploy skipped | Console IP | | `PS5_PORT` | `9021` | ELF loader port | | `PS5_RUNNER` | `ubuntu-24.04` | Runner label for the deploy job | The repository is public, so before adding a self-hosted runner, set Settings > Actions > General > *Require approval for all external contributors*. ### Layout | Folder | Contents | | --- | --- | | `netdis/` | Socket collection on the console (`platform_ps5.c`), the socket model and JSON (`sockets.c`), routes and cache (`routes.c`), the page (`ui.html`) and the icon (`assets/`) | | `common/` | Shared payload framework: web server, log, startup/replace/stop (`service.c`), notifications and home screen tile (`sys_ps5.c`), Logs and Settings tabs (`ui/`) | | `tools/` | `embed.py`: builds the page and icon into the ELF | | `.github/workflows/` | `build.yml` (tests and builds every push), `release.yml` (publishes a release for a version tag) | | `tests/` | Host tests | ## Credits - [ps5-payload-dev/sdk](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk), the PS5 payload SDK. - The home screen tile uses the approach introduced by John Törnblom's ftpsrv and used by Payload Manager. Sister project: [fps60](https://github.com/eladharels/ps5-60fps) unlocks 60 FPS in games with a known patch.

repos.name: any-pad
repos.description: bluetooth any pad in PS5
repos.readme: # AnyPad PS5: Free your PS5 from the DualSense **A Bluetooth controller bridge for jailbroken PS5 consoles.** **Un puente de mandos Bluetooth para PS5 con jailbreak.** **[English](#english) · [Español](#español)** · [Français](README.fr.md) · [Italiano](README.it.md) · [Português](README.pt.md) · [Deutsch](README.de.md) · [Русский](README.ru.md) · [简体中文](README.zh.md) · [繁體中文](README.zh-Hant.md) · [日本語](README.ja.md) · [한국어](README.ko.md) · [العربية](README.ar.md) --- # English AnyPad PS5 lets you use controllers from other platforms on your PS5. It connects them through the console's own Bluetooth chip and presents them to the system as virtual DualSense controllers. No USB dongle required. **Version 0.9.5-beta.** Tested on a PS5 fat, firmware 10.01, with a DualShock 4 and an 8BitDo SF30 Pro (Switch mode), in the console menus, in games and in emulators. **Available in twelve languages:** English, Spanish, French, Italian, Portuguese, German, Russian, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Japanese, Korean and Arabic. The AnyPad page follows the console language. --- ## About this project AnyPad PS5 started on 3 October 2026 at about 14:20 (Spanish time), the day I published its first version. The idea came from MissionControl, which lets the Nintendo Switch use controllers from other consoles. AnyPad may not have been the first project to use other controllers on the PS5: there were already projects that connected them by USB. But none connected them by Bluetooth, and AnyPad was the first to do it. I had an idea and I carried it out. The goal now is to make AnyPad work with more controllers. If you try it, please send me your log (see "Help us confirm compatibility" below): every log helps. The full source code is published in this repository under GPL-3.0-or-later (see "Open source, and working with an AI" below). If you develop an emulator and would like to integrate AnyPad, you are welcome to do so under that license. Write to me at [exposed.ct.ws@gmail.com](mailto:exposed.ct.ws@gmail.com) if you need help. One known issue remains: if the DualSense is switched off while AnyPad is running, it can stay blinking blue. I hope future projects do not have it. Projects forked from AnyPad, from the code I published, will very probably inherit this issue. It is part of AnyPad's legacy, and a sign that, at least in their Bluetooth part, they are forks of AnyPad. --- ## Open source, and working with an AI From version 0.9.5 the whole source code of AnyPad PS5 is published in this repository, under GPL-3.0-or-later: the Bluetooth host, the controller profiles, the AnyPad page, the tests and the build scripts. It includes a simulator, so a controller can be checked on a computer without a console. What I believe AnyPad really adds, more than the bridge itself, is **its communication system for integrating new controllers with the help of an AI**. While AnyPad is running, its page offers on your local network: - the log, in real time; - a few settings of the Bluetooth connection that can be changed while it runs, without restarting or rebuilding; - the pairing button. An AI assistant that has a terminal on a computer in the same network (for example Claude Code, Codex CLI or Gemini CLI) can follow what AnyPad does while you switch a controller on, propose a change, rebuild the ELF, upload it to the console and check the result in the next run. This is how AnyPad itself has been improved. The file **[AI-WORKFLOW.md](AI-WORKFLOW.md)** is a guide written for that assistant: how to connect, what it may and may not touch, how to test a change and how to add support for a new controller. You can give it to the assistant as the first instruction. Please keep in mind: - A chat in a web browser cannot reach your console. The assistant needs a terminal on a computer connected to the same local network as the PS5. AnyPad itself never connects to the internet. - The page has no PIN, as in every version: anyone on your local network can read the log and send commands to AnyPad. Use it only on a network you trust, and stop AnyPad when you finish. - The log contains the Bluetooth addresses of your controllers and the id of your console user. Review it before sharing it. ### Share what you (or your AI) learn If you adapt AnyPad to a controller, with or without an AI, please open an [issue](https://codeberg.org/elmonomalva0/Any-Pad-ps5/issues) with the controller model, the console firmware, the jailbreak, the AnyPad version, what you changed and why, and the log. If an AI helped you, say so and let it write the explanation: what the controller does differently, what was changed and how it was tested. I will review each proposal and integrate the compatible ones in later versions. A change must keep passing `make test` and must not alter how the DualShock 4 and the 8BitDo connect. ### Build from source You need the [ps5-payload-sdk](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk). ``` make test # host tests, with the Bluetooth simulator make ps5 PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK=/path/to/ps5-payload-sdk # the ELF in dist/ tools/build-elf-docker.sh /path/to/ps5-payload-sdk # or the same, inside a container ``` ### Please mention me If you make your own version of AnyPad, or you include it (or a part of it) in an emulator, a HEN, a payload or any other program, I would be very grateful if you mentioned **elmonomalvad0** and linked this project. The license, GPL-3.0-or-later, already requires you to keep the copyright notices and to distribute your changes under the same license. The mention is a request, not a condition, and it is what makes it worthwhile to keep sharing the work. ### Inside the code | Where | What it does | | --- | --- | | `src/host.c` | The Bluetooth Classic host: search, calls, pairing, L2CAP channels, SDP and HID | | `src/le.c` | Bluetooth LE: scanning, pairing with Secure Connections and identity exchange, HID over GATT | | `src/profiles.c` | One profile per family of controllers: ids, how to read its reports, wake-up sequence, rumble and lights | | `src/generic.c`, `maps/` | Any other HID gamepad, read through its own descriptor and an optional mapping file | | `src/hci_usb.c`, `src/usb_desc.c`, `src/evstream.c` | The HCI over USB with the console's Bluetooth chip, which is shared with the system | | `src/ps5_vpad.c` | Creates the virtual DualSense and feeds it | | `src/web.c`, `web/index.html` | The page and its API | | `src/ps5_main.c` | The main loop of the payload | | `tests/` | The Bluetooth simulators (`sim.c`, `sim_le.c`) and all the tests | Adding a controller is, in most cases, adding one profile in `src/profiles.c` and a test with the simulator. [AI-WORKFLOW.md](AI-WORKFLOW.md) explains the details. --- ## What is new in 0.9.5 - **Open source:** the whole code is published, with a guide for working with an AI assistant. ## What is new in 0.9 - **More compatible:** more controllers supported, and support for the two Bluetooth chips used in PS5 consoles. - **Bug fixes.** - **New graphical interface** for the AnyPad page. ## What is new in 0.8 ### Faster pairing Pairing is now much faster and more reliable. In our tests the DualShock 4 and the 8BitDo are found in a few seconds and are ready a few seconds later, where earlier versions often needed several attempts. ### More stable - **Smooth response:** controllers react fluidly while you play, without lag. - **Controllers switched on normally** (instead of in pairing mode) are now paired at the first attempt. - **Smarter handling** of controllers that are slow to answer or refuse a step. ### Configure PS For controllers without a usable PS button (Switch Pro, 8BitDo and others), the **Configure PS** button lets you choose **one button or a combination of three** that will act as the PS button. Choose how many, press them on the controller and hold them for one second: AnyPad detects them by itself. The setting is saved for that controller model. DualShock 4 and DualSense controllers have their own PS button, so this option does not appear for them. ### Twelve languages The AnyPad page follows the console language: English, Spanish, French, Italian, Portuguese, German, Russian, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Japanese, Korean and Arabic (right to left). Any other language falls back to English. --- ## ⚠️ Important: do not switch off the DualSense while AnyPad is running If the DualSense is switched off while AnyPad is running, it can enter the blinking blue mode and stop working until the console is restarted. So that the console does not switch it off by itself after a while without use, set: **Settings → System → Power Saving → Set Time Until Controllers Turn Off → Don't Turn Off** If you do not switch it off, everything works normally. --- ## ⚠️ Important: choose "Quick Play / Guest" for the external controller When you press PS on an external controller, the console asks who will use it. Choose **Quick Play / Guest**. Your main user keeps the DualSense, and you can go back to it at any time by picking up the DualSense. --- # Controller compatibility | Controller | Status | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | **DualShock 4** | ✅ **Verified** | Put it in pairing mode (Share + PS) every time you pair it. | | **8BitDo SF30 Pro (Switch mode)** | ✅ **Verified** | It shows up as a Switch Pro Controller. Use Configure PS for the PS button. | | **GameSir G7 SE** | ✅ **Verified** | | | **Nintendo Switch Pro Controller** | 🧪 **Supported, not tested yet** | Same protocol as the 8BitDo in Switch mode. | | **Xbox controllers** | ✅ **Working (reported by users)** | Users report them working since 0.8. If yours does not connect, please send me your log and its model. | | **Any other Bluetooth HID gamepad** | 🧪 **Generic profile** | May work without a specific profile. | **Controllers we believe are compatible** (supported in the code, not tested on a console yet): DualShock 4 v1, Hori Onyx, Razer Raiju Ultimate, Razer Raiju Tournament Edition, SCUF Vantage 2, Nintendo Switch Pro Controller, Nintendo Switch Online (SNES, N64, Mega Drive / Genesis), GameSir G3s, G4s, G7 Pro, T1s and T2a, Betop 2585N2, Bionik Vulkan, LanShen X1Pro, Xiaomi Mi Controller, Amazon Fire / iPega, iPega 9-series, 8BitDo SN30 Pro for Xbox Cloud Gaming, 8BitDo Ultimate 2.4G, SteelSeries, NVIDIA Shield controller (2017), Razer Serval, PowerA MOGA Hero, MOGA Pro and MOGA Pro 2, Atari VCS Modern controller, Hyperkin Scout, Mocute 050. If you try one of them, please send me your log. The full list, controller by controller, is in [COMPATIBILITY.md](COMPATIBILITY.md). --- # How it works AnyPad PS5 runs as a resident payload on a jailbroken PS5. It uses the console's own Bluetooth chip, **sharing it with the system**, to discover and pair controllers, read their input and present them to the PS5 as virtual DualSense controllers. It does **not** modify games, the PS5 firmware or the jailbreak. Your PS5 must already be able to run payloads. --- # How to use 1. **Load AnyPad.** Download `AnyPad-PS5-0.9.5-beta.elf` from [Releases](https://codeberg.org/elmonomalva0/Any-Pad-ps5/releases) and load it with the payload loader you normally use. 2. **Open the page.** Open **AnyPad** in the console's Media row, or open `http://:8095` from a phone or computer on the same network. 3. **Pair.** Press **Pair**, then put the controller in pairing mode, close to the console. | Controller | Pairing mode | | --- | --- | | **DualShock 4** | Hold **Share + PS** until the light bar flashes twice | | **8BitDo (Switch mode)** | Hold **Pair** for about 3 seconds, until the lights blink fast | | **Nintendo Switch Pro** | Press the small sync button next to the USB-C port | | **Other controllers** | Follow the manufacturer's instructions | 4. **Choose the user.** When the console asks, choose **Quick Play / Guest**. Several controllers can be used at the same time, together with the DualSense. --- # Every run starts clean AnyPad does not keep paired controllers between runs. Pair your controllers each time you start AnyPad. This avoids old pairings that no longer work and keeps the Bluetooth chip in a known state. If a controller that was switched off reconnects by itself and does not respond, switch it off and pair it again from the page. --- # Stopping AnyPad Always stop it with **Stop AnyPad PS5** on its page, also before running it again and before switching off or restarting the console. The **Exit** button only closes the page. --- # Troubleshooting ### No controller is found 1. Press **Pair** first and put the controller in pairing mode afterwards. 2. Make sure the controller really is in pairing mode (for example, the DualShock 4 light bar must flash twice). 3. If the controller was paired with another device before and still does not show up, reset it (DualShock 4: a paper clip in the small hole next to L2 for about 5 seconds; 8BitDo Pro 2: hold Pair for about 5 seconds) and try again. ### Another controller payload is running Another payload that uses the Bluetooth chip and port 8095 gets in the way. Stop it from its own menu before running AnyPad; AnyPad shows a notice when it detects this. ### The page does not open Check that AnyPad is running, that your phone or computer is on the same network as the PS5, and that you use the console's IP address with port `8095`. --- # Help us confirm compatibility If you can confirm that AnyPad PS5 works (or does not work) with a controller, please send the log (`/data/anypad/anypad.log`) to [exposed.ct.ws@gmail.com](mailto:exposed.ct.ws@gmail.com), with the controller model, the console firmware, the jailbreak and the AnyPad version. This helps a lot. ### Support the project Many people ask me to test other controllers and other console versions. Any help is very welcome to **port this project to PS4** and to **PS5 firmware 13.60**, and to support **more controllers**. I would love to have a console on firmware 13.60 as well as my 10.01. It is not mandatory, but anyone who wants to help the project can do so on my Throne page: **[throne.com/elmonomalvad0](https://throne.com/elmonomalvad0)** --- # Credits AnyPad PS5 is original code. These projects were studied to understand how things work, and their ideas were written anew for AnyPad. Thanks to their authors: - **[FGG-PlayPods](https://github.com/FGGstore/FGG-PlayPods)** (FGGstore): the idea behind the Bluetooth part, sharing the PS5's own Bluetooth chip with the system. - **[MissionControl](https://github.com/ndeadly/MissionControl)** (ndeadly): controller profiles by vendor and model, and the report layouts of many controllers. - **Ghostcontrol** (StonedModder): how to create a virtual DualSense on the PS5 and assign it to a user. - **[SplashDown](https://github.com/seregonwar/SplashDown)** (seregonwar) and **[shadPS4](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4)**: the virtual pad sequence and the pad data layout. - **[HearBridge-PS5](https://github.com/X-F1REBALL-X/HearBridge-PS5)** (X-F1REBALL-X): ideas on handling Bluetooth negotiation. - **[ps5-payload-sdk](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk)** (John Törnblom): the toolchain everything is built with. License: GPL-3.0-or-later ([LICENSE](LICENSE)). Author: **elmonomalvad0**, the same author as *sinfiltros* (the original AnyPad PS5 on GitHub). X: [@elmonomalvad0](https://x.com/elmonomalvad0) · Contact: exposed.ct.ws@gmail.com --- # Español AnyPad PS5 te permite usar en tu PS5 mandos de otras plataformas. Los conecta a través del propio chip Bluetooth de la consola y los presenta al sistema como DualSense virtuales. No hace falta ningún adaptador USB. **Versión 0.9.5-beta.** Probada en una PS5 fat, firmware 10.01, con un DualShock 4 y un 8BitDo SF30 Pro (modo Switch), en los menús de la consola, en juegos y en emuladores. **Disponible en doce idiomas:** español, inglés, francés, italiano, portugués, alemán, ruso, chino simplificado, chino tradicional, japonés, coreano y árabe. La página de AnyPad sigue el idioma de la consola. --- ## Sobre este proyecto AnyPad PS5 empezó el 3 de octubre de 2026, hacia las 14:20 (hora de España), el día que publiqué su primera versión. La idea partió de MissionControl, que permite usar en la Nintendo Switch mandos de otras consolas. Quizá AnyPad no fue el primer proyecto para usar otros mandos en la PS5: ya había proyectos que los conectaban por USB. Pero ninguno los conectaba por Bluetooth, y AnyPad fue el primero en hacerlo. Tuve una idea y la llevé a cabo. El objetivo ahora es que AnyPad funcione con más mandos. Si lo pruebas, por favor envíame tu log (mira «Ayúdanos a confirmar la compatibilidad» más abajo): cada log ayuda. El código fuente completo está publicado en este repositorio con licencia GPL-3.0-or-later (mira «Código abierto y trabajo con una IA» más abajo). Si desarrollas un emulador y quieres integrar AnyPad, puedes hacerlo bajo esa licencia. Escríbeme a [exposed.ct.ws@gmail.com](mailto:exposed.ct.ws@gmail.com) si necesitas ayuda. Queda un fallo conocido: si se apaga el DualSense con AnyPad en marcha, puede quedarse en azul parpadeante. Espero que los próximos proyectos no lo tengan. Los que sean forks de AnyPad, del código que publiqué, muy probablemente heredarán ese fallo. Es parte del legado de AnyPad, y una muestra de que, al menos en su parte Bluetooth, son un fork de AnyPad. --- ## Código abierto y trabajo con una IA Desde la versión 0.9.5 todo el código fuente de AnyPad PS5 está publicado en este repositorio, con licencia GPL-3.0-or-later: el anfitrión Bluetooth, los perfiles de mandos, la página de AnyPad, las pruebas y los scripts de compilación. Incluye un simulador, así que se puede comprobar un mando en un ordenador sin consola. Lo que creo que aporta de verdad AnyPad, más que el puente en sí, es **su sistema de comunicación para integrar mandos nuevos con la ayuda de una IA**. Mientras AnyPad está en marcha, su página ofrece en tu red local: - el log, en tiempo real; - algunos ajustes de la conexión Bluetooth que se pueden cambiar en caliente, sin reiniciar ni recompilar; - el botón de emparejar. Un asistente de IA que tenga una terminal en un ordenador de la misma red (por ejemplo Claude Code, Codex CLI o Gemini CLI) puede seguir lo que hace AnyPad mientras enciendes un mando, proponer un cambio, recompilar el ELF, subirlo a la consola y comprobar el resultado en la siguiente ejecución. Así se ha mejorado el propio AnyPad. El archivo **[AI-WORKFLOW.md](AI-WORKFLOW.md)** es una guía escrita para ese asistente: cómo conectarse, qué puede y qué no puede tocar, cómo probar un cambio y cómo añadir un mando nuevo. Puedes dársela al asistente como primera instrucción. Ten en cuenta: - Un chat en el navegador no llega a tu consola. El asistente necesita una terminal en un ordenador conectado a la misma red local que la PS5. AnyPad nunca se conecta a internet. - La página no tiene PIN, como en todas las versiones: cualquiera en tu red local puede leer el log y mandar órdenes a AnyPad. Úsalo solo en una red de confianza y detén AnyPad cuando termines. - El log contiene las direcciones Bluetooth de tus mandos y el id de tu usuario de la consola. Revísalo antes de compartirlo. ### Comparte lo que aprendéis (tú y tu IA) Si adaptas AnyPad a un mando, con o sin IA, abre por favor una [incidencia](https://codeberg.org/elmonomalva0/Any-Pad-ps5/issues) con el modelo del mando, el firmware de la consola, el jailbreak, la versión de AnyPad, qué has cambiado y por qué, y el log. Si te ha ayudado una IA, dilo y deja que escriba ella la explicación: qué hace distinto el mando, qué se cambió y cómo se probó. Revisaré cada propuesta e integraré las compatibles en versiones posteriores. Un cambio debe seguir pasando `make test` y no debe alterar cómo conectan el DualShock 4 y el 8BitDo. ### Compilar desde el código Necesitas el [ps5-payload-sdk](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk). ``` make test # pruebas en el ordenador, con el simulador Bluetooth make ps5 PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK=/ruta/al/ps5-payload-sdk # el ELF en dist/ tools/build-elf-docker.sh /ruta/al/ps5-payload-sdk # o lo mismo, dentro de un contenedor ``` ### Por favor, menciónome Si haces tu propia versión de AnyPad, o la incluyes (o una parte) en un emulador, un HEN, un payload o cualquier otro programa, te lo agradeceré mucho si mencionas a **elmonomalvad0** y enlazas este proyecto. La licencia, GPL-3.0-or-later, ya exige que conserves los avisos de copyright y que distribuyas tus cambios con la misma licencia. La mención es una petición, no una condición, y es lo que hace que merezca la pena seguir compartiendo el trabajo. ### Dentro del código | Dónde | Qué hace | | --- | --- | | `src/host.c` | El anfitrión Bluetooth Classic: búsqueda, llamadas, emparejado, canales L2CAP, SDP y HID | | `src/le.c` | Bluetooth LE: búsqueda, emparejado con Secure Connections e intercambio de identidad, HID sobre GATT | | `src/profiles.c` | Un perfil por familia de mandos: ids, cómo leer sus informes, secuencia de despertar, vibración y luces | | `src/generic.c`, `maps/` | Cualquier otro mando HID, leído con su propio descriptor y un archivo de mapeo opcional | | `src/hci_usb.c`, `src/usb_desc.c`, `src/evstream.c` | El HCI por USB con el chip Bluetooth de la consola, que se comparte con el sistema | | `src/ps5_vpad.c` | Crea el DualSense virtual y lo alimenta | | `src/web.c`, `web/index.html` | La página y su API | | `src/ps5_main.c` | El bucle principal del payload | | `tests/` | Los simuladores Bluetooth (`sim.c`, `sim_le.c`) y todas las pruebas | Añadir un mando es, en la mayoría de los casos, añadir un perfil en `src/profiles.c` y una prueba con el simulador. [AI-WORKFLOW.md](AI-WORKFLOW.md) explica los detalles. --- ## Novedades de la 0.9.5 - **Código abierto:** todo el código está publicado, con una guía para trabajar con un asistente de IA. ## Novedades de la 0.9 - **Más compatible:** admite más mandos y es compatible con los dos chips Bluetooth que llevan las PS5. - **Errores corregidos.** - **Nuevo entorno gráfico** en la página de AnyPad. ## Novedades de la 0.8 ### Emparejado más rápido El emparejado es ahora mucho más rápido y fiable. En nuestras pruebas, el DualShock 4 y el 8BitDo aparecen en pocos segundos y quedan listos pocos segundos después, cuando antes a menudo hacían falta varios intentos. ### Más estable - **Respuesta fluida:** los mandos reaccionan con suavidad mientras juegas, sin lag. - **Mandos encendidos de forma normal** (en vez de en modo emparejamiento): ahora se emparejan al primer intento. - **Tratamiento más inteligente** de los mandos que tardan en responder o rechazan un paso. ### Configurar PS Para los mandos sin un botón PS que funcione (Switch Pro, 8BitDo y otros), el botón **Configurar PS** permite elegir **un botón o una combinación de tres** que hará de botón PS. Eliges cuántos, los pulsas en el mando y los mantienes un segundo: AnyPad los detecta solo. El ajuste se guarda para ese modelo de mando. Los DualShock 4 y los DualSense tienen su propio botón PS, así que esta opción no aparece para ellos. ### Doce idiomas La página de AnyPad sigue el idioma de la consola: español, inglés, francés, italiano, portugués, alemán, ruso, chino simplificado, chino tradicional, japonés, coreano y árabe (de derecha a izquierda). Cualquier otro idioma usa el inglés. --- ## ⚠️ Importante: no apagues el DualSense con AnyPad en marcha Si el DualSense se apaga mientras AnyPad está en marcha, puede entrar en el modo azul parpadeante y no funcionar hasta reiniciar la consola. Para que la consola no lo apague sola tras un rato sin usarlo, configura: **Ajustes → Sistema → Ahorro de energía → Establecer tiempo hasta que se apaguen los mandos → No apagar** Si no lo apagas, todo funciona con normalidad. --- ## ⚠️ Importante: elige «Juego rápido / Invitado» para el mando externo Cuando pulsas PS en un mando externo, la consola pregunta quién lo va a usar. Elige **Juego rápido / Invitado**. Tu usuario principal conserva el DualSense, y puedes volver a él en cualquier momento cogiendo el DualSense. --- # Compatibilidad de mandos | Mando | Estado | Notas | | --- | --- | --- | | **DualShock 4** | ✅ **Verificado** | Ponlo en modo emparejamiento (Share + PS) cada vez que lo emparejes. | | **8BitDo SF30 Pro (modo Switch)** | ✅ **Verificado** | Aparece como Switch Pro Controller. Usa Configurar PS para el botón PS. | | **GameSir G7 SE** | ✅ **Verificado** | | | **Nintendo Switch Pro Controller** | 🧪 **Soportado, sin probar** | Mismo protocolo que el 8BitDo en modo Switch. | | **Mandos Xbox** | ✅ **Funcionan (según usuarios)** | Varios usuarios confirman que funcionan desde la 0.8. Si el tuyo no conecta, envíame tu log y el modelo. | | **Cualquier otro mando HID Bluetooth** | 🧪 **Perfil genérico** | Puede funcionar sin un perfil específico. | **Mandos que creemos compatibles** (soportados en el código, aún sin probar en una consola): DualShock 4 v1, Hori Onyx, Razer Raiju Ultimate, Razer Raiju Tournament Edition, SCUF Vantage 2, Nintendo Switch Pro Controller, Nintendo Switch Online (SNES, N64, Mega Drive / Genesis), GameSir G3s, G4s, G7 Pro, T1s y T2a, Betop 2585N2, Bionik Vulkan, LanShen X1Pro, Xiaomi Mi Controller, Amazon Fire / iPega, iPega 9-series, 8BitDo SN30 Pro para Xbox Cloud Gaming, 8BitDo Ultimate 2.4G, SteelSeries, mando NVIDIA Shield (2017), Razer Serval, PowerA MOGA Hero, MOGA Pro y MOGA Pro 2, mando Atari VCS Modern, Hyperkin Scout, Mocute 050. Si pruebas alguno, envíame tu log. La lista completa, mando por mando, está en [COMPATIBILITY.md](COMPATIBILITY.md). --- # Cómo funciona AnyPad PS5 se ejecuta como un payload residente en una PS5 con jailbreak. Usa el propio chip Bluetooth de la consola, **compartiéndolo con el sistema**, para buscar y emparejar mandos, leer sus botones y presentarlos a la PS5 como DualSense virtuales. **No** modifica juegos, el firmware de la PS5 ni el jailbreak. Tu PS5 ya debe poder ejecutar payloads. --- # Cómo usarlo 1. **Carga AnyPad.** Descarga `AnyPad-PS5-0.9.5-beta.elf` desde [Releases](https://codeberg.org/elmonomalva0/Any-Pad-ps5/releases) y cárgalo con el cargador de payloads que uses normalmente. 2. **Abre la página.** Abre **AnyPad** en *Contenido multimedia* de la consola, o `http://:8095` desde un móvil o un PC de la misma red. 3. **Empareja.** Pulsa **Emparejar** y después pon el mando en modo emparejamiento, cerca de la consola. | Mando | Modo emparejamiento | | --- | --- | | **DualShock 4** | Mantén **Share + PS** hasta que la barra de luz haga un doble destello | | **8BitDo (modo Switch)** | Mantén **Pair** unos 3 segundos, hasta que las luces parpadeen rápido | | **Nintendo Switch Pro** | Pulsa el pequeño botón de sincronización junto al puerto USB-C | | **Otros mandos** | Sigue las instrucciones del fabricante | 4. **Elige el usuario.** Cuando la consola lo pregunte, elige **Juego rápido / Invitado**. Se pueden usar varios mandos a la vez, junto con el DualSense. --- # Cada ejecución empieza limpia AnyPad no guarda mandos emparejados entre ejecuciones. Empareja tus mandos cada vez que arranques AnyPad. Así se evitan emparejados antiguos que ya no funcionan y el chip Bluetooth queda en un estado conocido. Si un mando que se apagó se reconecta solo y no responde, apágalo y vuelve a emparejarlo desde la página. --- # Apagar AnyPad Páralo siempre con **Apagar AnyPad PS5** en su página, también antes de volver a ejecutarlo y antes de apagar o reiniciar la consola. El botón **Salir** solo cierra la página. --- # Solución de problemas ### No encuentra ningún mando 1. Pulsa **Emparejar** primero y pon el mando en modo emparejamiento después. 2. Comprueba que el mando está de verdad en modo emparejamiento (por ejemplo, la barra de luz del DualShock 4 debe hacer un doble destello). 3. Si el mando estuvo emparejado antes con otro aparato y sigue sin aparecer, haz un reset (DualShock 4: un clip en el agujero junto a L2 unos 5 segundos; 8BitDo Pro 2: mantén Pair unos 5 segundos) e inténtalo de nuevo. ### Hay otro payload de mandos en marcha Otro payload que use el chip Bluetooth y el puerto 8095 interfiere. Páralo desde su propio menú antes de ejecutar AnyPad; AnyPad avisa en pantalla cuando lo detecta. ### La página no se abre Comprueba que AnyPad está en marcha, que tu móvil o PC está en la misma red que la PS5 y que usas la IP de la consola con el puerto `8095`. --- # Ayúdanos a confirmar la compatibilidad Si puedes confirmar que AnyPad PS5 funciona (o no funciona) con un mando, envía el log (`/data/anypad/anypad.log`) a [exposed.ct.ws@gmail.com](mailto:exposed.ct.ws@gmail.com), con el modelo del mando, el firmware de la consola, el jailbreak y la versión de AnyPad. Esto ayuda mucho. ### Apoya el proyecto Mucha gente me pide que pruebe otros mandos y otras versiones de la consola. Agradecemos cualquier ayuda para poder **portar este proyecto a PS4**, a las versiones **13.60 de PS5** y a **diferentes mandos**. Me encantaría tener una consola con el firmware 13.60 además de la mía, con el 10.01. No es obligatorio, pero quien quiera ayudar al proyecto puede hacerlo desde mi página de Throne: **[throne.com/elmonomalvad0](https://throne.com/elmonomalvad0)** --- # Agradecimientos AnyPad PS5 es código propio. Estos proyectos se estudiaron para entender cómo funcionan las cosas, y sus ideas se escribieron de nuevo para AnyPad. Gracias a sus autores: - **[FGG-PlayPods](https://github.com/FGGstore/FGG-PlayPods)** (FGGstore): la idea de la parte Bluetooth, compartir el propio chip Bluetooth de la PS5 con el sistema. - **[MissionControl](https://github.com/ndeadly/MissionControl)** (ndeadly): los perfiles de mandos por fabricante y modelo, y el formato de los informes de muchos mandos. - **Ghostcontrol** (StonedModder): cómo crear un DualSense virtual en la PS5 y asignarlo a un usuario. - **[SplashDown](https://github.com/seregonwar/SplashDown)** (seregonwar) y **[shadPS4](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4)**: la secuencia del mando virtual y el formato de los datos del mando. - **[HearBridge-PS5](https://github.com/X-F1REBALL-X/HearBridge-PS5)** (X-F1REBALL-X): ideas sobre la negociación Bluetooth. - **[ps5-payload-sdk](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk)** (John Törnblom): las herramientas con las que se compila todo. Licencia: GPL-3.0-or-later ([LICENSE](LICENSE)). Autor: **elmonomalvad0**, el mismo autor que *sinfiltros* (el AnyPad PS5 original en GitHub). X: [@elmonomalvad0](https://x.com/elmonomalvad0) · Contacto: exposed.ct.ws@gmail.com

**12 October 2026** · More compatible: more controllers supported, and support for the two Bluetooth chips used in PS5 consoles. Bug fixes and a new graphical interface for the AnyPad page. Please do not switch off the DualSense while AnyPad is running. If you try it with another controller, please send me your log.

**12 de octubre de 2026** · Más compatible: admite más mandos y es compatible con los dos chips Bluetooth que llevan las PS5. Errores corregidos y un nuevo entorno gráfico en la página de AnyPad. Por favor, no apagues el DualSense mientras AnyPad está en marcha. Si lo pruebas con otro mando, envíame tu log.

EN: run the ELF, open AnyPad (Media row), press Pair and then put the controller in pairing mode. Choose Quick Play / Guest when the console asks. Exit with the Stop AnyPad PS5 button.

ES: ejecuta el ELF, abre AnyPad (Contenido multimedia), pulsa Emparejar y después pon el mando en modo emparejamiento. Elige Juego rápido / Invitado cuando la consola lo pregunte. Sal con el botón Apagar AnyPad PS5.

repos.readme:
# etaHEN - AIO Homebrew enabler

![etaHEN](https://github.com/LightningMods/etaHEN/blob/main/etaHEN-Icon.jpg)

## 🚀 **Support the Project**

If you find this project useful and would like to support its continued development, consider buying me a coffee!
[![GitHub Sponsers](https://www.ko-fi.com/img/githubbutton_sm.svg)](https://github.com/sponsors/LightningMods)

## Building from Source

The Source code is provided in the Source code folder under GPLv3 with all the necessary files to build it as required under GPLv3 
However I will not be providing instructions on how to build it since any dev should know how to use cmake 

## Official PS5 exploit website 
- https://tinyurl.com/PS5IPV6 (requires you to manually send the payload but has the best stability)
- https://ps5jb.pages.dev/ (auto loads the payload for you, id recommend the IPV6 exploit over UMTX)

## Recommended self-host exploits
- [Modified IPV6 exploit for etaHEN support](https://github.com/LightningMods/PS5-IPV6-Kernel-Exploit)

## Payload PowerShell Script usage for Windows (send_payload.ps1)

if you haven't already, you will need to either enable script execution globally via 

```
Set-ExecutionPolicy Bypass
```
in an admin PowerShell window or run the script with this command after replacing the script path

```
powershell.exe -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File C:\Path\To\send_payload.ps1
```
**Script Usage**

```
.\send_payload.ps1 -Payload "C:\path\to\example.elf" -IP "192.168.xxx.xxx" -Port XXXX
```

**OR**

```
.\send_payload.ps1

cmdlet send_payload.ps1 at command pipeline position 1
Supply values for the following parameters:
(Type !? for Help.)
Payload: C:\path\to\example.elf
IP: 192.168.xxx.xxx
Port: XXXX
```
- Common Ports: SB elfldr 9021, exploit elfldr 9020

## Features
 - ★ etaHEN toolbox (debug settings replacement)
 - Custom etaHEN [Plugins](https://github.com/LightningMods/etaHEN-SDK/tree/main/Plugin_samples)
 - [Toolbox] Install the Homebrew Store on the console
 - [Toolbox] ★Rest Mode Options
 - [Toolbox] Remote Play Menu
 - [Toolbox] Plugin / Payload ELF Menu with auto start options
 - [Toolbox] External HDD Menu
 - [Toolbox] TestKit Menu  
 - [Toolbox] Kstuff menu
 - [Toolbox] Game Overlay Menu
 - [Toolbox] Cheats Menu (WIP)
 - [Toolbox] Controller Shortcuts
 - [Toolbox] PS5 webMAN Games menu
 - [Toolbox] Custom Game Options Menu
 - [Toolbox] Display Title IDs on Home menu
 - [Toolbox] Disable toolbox auto start
 - [Toolbox] Blu-Ray license activation 
 - [Toolbox] Disc auto eject for BD-J and LUA based exploits
 - [Toolbox] etaHEN credits and supporters
 - [Toolbox] Custom debug settings text and icon
 - [Toolbox] Auto open menu after etaHEN loads
 - [Toolbox] a number of different toolbox settings
 - React bundle (all FWs) & Self (only on 2.xx) FTP decryption Support
 - 2 seperate daemons for improved stability and reliability
 - The Util daemon will be auto restarted by the main etaHEN daemon
 - Custom System Software version (custom System info)
 - kstuff for fself and fpkg support 
 - etaHEN log in /data/etaHEN
 - (optional) System-wide controller shortcut to open itemzflow
 - Debug Settings
 - Game Dumper (Intrgrated with Itemzflow)
 - HEN config file for settings
 - Jailbreak IPC call (jailbreaks Homebrew apps)
 - Update blocker (unmounts update partition)
 - *Optional* Illusions cheats/patches [Plugin](https://github.com/LightningMods/etaHEN-SDK/tree/main/Plugin_samples/Illusion_cheats)
 - *Optional* FTP server on port 1337
 - *Optional* /data allowed inside apps sandboxes
 - Klog server on port 9081
 - elf loader on port 9021 (use Johns elfldr)

## etaHEN INI Configuration file

## DPI API details for tool creators 
etaHEN's Direct PKG Installer currently is very simple and is considered a WIP
the service flow is as follows

1. Connect to etaHEN's TCP server via port 9090 (using the PS5s IP)
2. Send a URL to etaHEN in the following json format
```
{ "url" : "http://xxxx" }
```
3. etaHEN will then send back the return value (0 on success)
```
{ "res" : "0" }
```
4. etaHEN will close the client socket after the return json is sent


## Jailbreaking an app (FPKG) using etaHEN (non-whitelist method, Network and Legacy CMD server toolbox setting required)

```
enum Commands : int {
  INVALID_CMD = -1,
  ACTIVE_CMD = 0,
  LAUNCH_CMD,
  PROCLIST_CMD,
  KILL_CMD,
  KILL_APP_CMD,
  JAILBREAK_CMD
};

struct HijackerCommand
{
  int magic = 0xDEADBEEF;
  Commands cmd = INVALID_CMD;
  int PID = -1;
  int ret = -1337;
  char msg1[0x500];
  char msg2[0x500];
};

int HJOpenConnectionforBC() {

  SceNetSockaddrIn address;
  address.sin_len = sizeof(address);
  address.sin_family = AF_INET;
  address.sin_port = sceNetHtons(9028); //command serve port
  memset(address.sin_zero, 0, sizeof(address.sin_zero));
  sceNetInetPton(AF_INET, "127.0.0.1", &address.sin_addr.s_addr);

  int socket = sceNetSocket("IPC_CMD_SERVER", AF_INET, SOCK_STREAM, 0);
  if (sceNetConnect(socket, (SceNetSockaddr*)&address, sizeof(address)) < 0) {
    close(socket), socket = -1;
  }

  return socket;
}

bool HJJailbreakforBC(int& sock) {

  // send jailbreak IPC command
  HijackerCommand cmd;
  cmd.PID = getpid();
  cmd.cmd = JAILBREAK_CMD;

  if (send(sock, (void*)&cmd, sizeof(cmd), MSG_NOSIGNAL) == -1) {
      puts("failed to send command");
      return false;
  }
  else {
    // get ret val from daemon
    recv(sock, reinterpret_cast<void*>(&cmd), sizeof(cmd), MSG_NOSIGNAL);
    close(sock), sock = -1;
    if (cmd.ret != 0 && cmd.ret != -1337) {
      puts("Jailbreak has failed");
      return false;
    }
    return true;
  }

  return false;
}

int main()
{

     int ret = HJOpenConnectionforBC();
     if (ret < 0) {
         puts("Failed to connect to daemon");
         return -1;
     }
     if (!HJJailbreakforBC(ret))
     {
          puts("Jailbreak failed");
          return -1;
     }

     return 0;
}
```

repos.name: exfat2ampr
repos.description: Convert PS5 game dumps to AMPR LZ4, right on the console. Made by V-10, LZ4 format by DLPSGAME.
repos.readme:
# exFAT2AMPR

![Testé et fonctionnel sur PlayStation 5](docs/tested-on-ps5.svg)

**Convertit vos jeux PS5 au format AMPR LZ4, directement sur la console.** Pas de PC : on choisit le jeu à la
manette, l'app le compresse et le range où vous voulez (SSD interne, SSD M.2 ou disque USB).

✅ Testé et fonctionnel sur PS5 par l'auteur (firmware 12.xx et 13.xx, kstuff, ShadowMountPlus 1.7).

## Ce que ça apporte

- **Des jeux plus légers** : jusqu'à moitié moins de place, selon le jeu (certains, déjà compressés, ne gagnent
  presque rien ; l'app estime le gain avant de commencer).
- **Tout se fait sur la console**, en arrière-plan, même pendant que vous jouez.
- **Rien n'est perdu** : chaque bloc est vérifié, une conversion interrompue (coupure, mode repos, disque plein)
  reprend où elle s'était arrêtée, et le jeu d'origine est gardé (sauf si vous demandez sa suppression).

## Ce qu'il faut

- Une PS5 jailbreakée avec **kstuff**.
- Un chargeur d'ELF sur le port 9021 (elfldr, etaHEN…).
- **ShadowMountPlus 1.7** ou plus récent.

## Installation

1. Copiez `PPSA99272.ffpkg` (page *Releases*) dans `homebrew/` à la racine d'une clé USB exFAT, ou par FTP dans
   `/data/homebrew/`. **Une seule copie.**
2. Redémarrez la console et lancez le jailbreak : **exFAT2AMPR** apparaît sur l'écran d'accueil.
3. Ouvrez l'app. Elle démarre son moteur toute seule.

Les mises à jour s'installent ensuite depuis l'app : **Réglages › Mises à jour**.

## Utilisation

1. Choisissez un jeu (□ pour en cocher plusieurs).
2. ✕ : options, puis destination, puis vérification avant le lancement.
3. La conversion tourne seule. Suivez-la dans l'onglet **Progression** (L1/R1 pour changer d'onglet).

Le jeu converti apparaît sur l'écran d'accueil grâce à ShadowMountPlus.

Le bouton **OPTIONS** sur un jeu ouvre son menu : optimiser, mettre à jour ses plugins, **réparer** un jeu
converti, **mettre de côté** une image en double, supprimer une copie, réglages.

Aussi depuis un téléphone ou un PC : la page web du moteur (adresse affichée dans l'app, port 6972, appairage
par code ou QR code).

## Bon à savoir

- **Gardez le jeu d'origine** tant que vous n'avez pas lancé la version convertie au moins une fois. Certains
  jeux ne fonctionnent pas une fois convertis (c'est le cas de jeux faits avec Unity, par exemple).
- L'app refuse de convertir un jeu qui n'utilise pas AMPR, et ne remplace jamais un dossier qui n'est pas un
  jeu converti.
- Un problème ? **Réglages › Diagnostic** crée un fichier à joindre à votre message (code d'appairage et adresse
  masqués).
- Langues : français, anglais, espagnol, italien, russe, portugais, chinois, thaï, vietnamien (plus l'arabe sur
  la page web).

Détails techniques (format, pause et reprise, profils, compilation) : [docs/TECHNIQUE.md](docs/TECHNIQUE.md).

## Crédits

- **V-10** : auteur d'exFAT2AMPR.
- **DLPSGAME** : le format LZ4 des jeux PS5.
- **drakmor** : l'émulateur AMPR (ampr_emu), ShadowMountPlus, pgo_stub et dlc_emu.
- **Yann Collet** : l'algorithme LZ4.
- **Alex Barney** : LibAtrac9, qui décode la musique d'accueil des jeux dans l'app.

## Licence

conditions supplémentaires (`NOTICE`) :

- toute copie ou version modifiée garde ce copyright et le crédit « Créé par V-10 » ;

- le nom « exFAT2AMPR » et son logo ne sont pas cédés : une version modifiée diffusée porte un autre nom et une
  autre icône.

Retirer le nom de l'auteur ou diffuser le programme sous un autre nom d'auteur met fin aux droits accordés par la
licence (article 8). Composants tiers : drakmor/ampr_emu (GPL-3.0), LZ4 (BSD-2), ps5-payload-sdk (GPL-3.0), LibAtrac9
(MIT), polices DejaVu Sans, Noto Sans Thai et Noto Sans CJK (SIL OFL 1.1).

latestRelease.name: exFAT2AMPR v1.104
latestRelease.body:
## exFAT2AMPR — convert your PS5 games to AMPR LZ4, right on the console

![Tested and working on PlayStation 5](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/exFAT2AMPR/exfat2ampr/main/docs/tested-on-ps5.svg)

Made by **V-10** · LZ4 format: **DLPSGAME** · AMPR emulator: drakmor/ampr_emu · free software (GPL-3.0)

Pick a game with the controller: the app compresses it on the PS5 and puts it where you want (internal SSD, M.2 SSD
or USB drive). Smaller games, every block checked, interrupted conversions resume, the original is kept.

### New in this version

- **Start-up check**: once a game is converted, the app checks what would stop it from starting (AMPR emulator
  missing or overridden, fakelib2, backport, fakelib disabled, eboot.bin not executable), fixes what it can and
  tells you the rest on the Progress screen. Repair (game menu, OPTIONS) runs the same check.
- **Time estimate per LZ4 level**: the check screen shows how long the conversion should take, and at level 10 to
  12 how long level 9 would take. The speed is learned on your console after each conversion. Level 10 to 12 kept
  from an older version is set back to 9 once (you can choose it again).
- **Start and close the app** (△ on the check screen): for an image, ShadowMountPlus only mounts it once no app
  is open; this starts the conversion and closes the app, which finds it again when reopened.
- **Every cover shows**: the console refused the app medium memory blocks and most covers stayed blank; the app
  now keeps its own memory, taken from the console's direct memory.
- **Each game's own music**: rest on a game and its home-screen music plays (the `snd0.at9` the game or the
  console keeps), cross-fading from one game to the next; silent for games without one. Settings › Game music.

### Earlier

- **Safer conversions** (1.95): an already converted game cannot be converted again; a source with links or unreadable files is refused; each uncompressed file gets a SHA-256 checked at the end; damaged resume data is refused. Details in `docs/HARDENING.md`.
- **Repair**, **Set aside**, original game protected, full destination shown, colour themes.

### Install

Requirements: jailbroken PS5 with kstuff, an ELF loader on port 9021 (elfldr, etaHEN…), ShadowMountPlus 1.7+.

1. Copy `PPSA99272.ffpkg` into `homebrew/` on an exFAT USB drive, or by FTP into `/data/homebrew/`. Keep one copy.
2. Restart the console and run the jailbreak: **exFAT2AMPR** appears on the home screen.
3. Open it. Next updates install from the app: Settings › Updates.

**Good to know**: keep the original until the converted game has started once; a few games (seen with Unity
games) do not run once converted. Problem? Settings › Diagnostic writes a file to attach to your report.

Tested and working by the author on firmware 12.xx and 13.xx. Presentation video attached
(`exfat2ampr-presentation.mp4`).

---

### En français

Choisissez un jeu à la manette : l'app le compresse sur la PS5 et le range où vous voulez (SSD interne, SSD M.2 ou
disque USB). Jeux plus légers, chaque bloc vérifié, conversions interrompues reprises, jeu d'origine gardé.

**Nouveautés**

- **Test de démarrage** : une fois le jeu converti, l'app vérifie ce qui l'empêcherait de démarrer (émulateur AMPR
  absent ou remplacé, fakelib2, backport, fakelib désactivé, eboot.bin non exécutable), corrige ce qu'elle peut et
  vous dit le reste sur l'écran Progression. Réparer (menu du jeu, OPTIONS) fait le même test.
- **Durée estimée par niveau LZ4** : l'écran de vérification indique la durée prévue et, aux niveaux 10 à 12, celle
  du niveau 9. La vitesse est apprise sur votre console après chaque conversion. Un niveau 10 à 12 gardé d'une
  ancienne version est ramené une fois à 9 (vous pouvez le remettre).
- **Lancer et quitter l'app** (△ sur l'écran de vérification) : ShadowMountPlus ne monte une image que lorsqu'aucune
  app n'est ouverte ; la conversion démarre et l'app se ferme, puis la retrouve à sa réouverture.
- **Toutes les jaquettes s'affichent** : la console refusait à l'app des blocs mémoire moyens et la plupart des
  jaquettes restaient vides ; l'app gère maintenant sa propre mémoire, prise dans la mémoire directe de la console.
- **La musique de chaque jeu** : arrêtez-vous sur un jeu et sa musique d'accueil joue (le `snd0.at9` que le jeu
  ou la console garde), en fondu d'un jeu à l'autre ; silence pour les jeux qui n'en ont pas. Réglages › Musique
  des jeux.

**Avant** : conversions plus sûres (1.95), Réparer, Mettre de côté, jeu d'origine protégé, dossier de destination
affiché, thèmes de couleurs.

**Installation** : PS5 jailbreakée avec kstuff, chargeur d'ELF sur le port 9021, ShadowMountPlus 1.7 ou plus.

1. Copiez `PPSA99272.ffpkg` dans `homebrew/` sur une clé USB exFAT, ou par FTP dans `/data/homebrew/`. Une seule
   copie.
2. Redémarrez la console et lancez le jailbreak : **exFAT2AMPR** apparaît sur l'écran d'accueil.
3. Ouvrez-la. Les mises à jour suivantes s'installent depuis l'app : Réglages › Mises à jour.

**Bon à savoir** : gardez le jeu d'origine tant que la version convertie n'a pas démarré une fois ; quelques jeux
(vu avec des jeux Unity) ne fonctionnent pas une fois convertis. Un problème ? Réglages › Diagnostic crée un fichier
à joindre à votre message.

Testé et fonctionnel par l'auteur sur firmware 12.xx et 13.xx. Vidéo de présentation jointe
(`exfat2ampr-presentation.mp4`, voix anglaise, sous-titres français).

repos.name: pulse-deck
repos.description: Dual-deck browser DJ app driven by a PS5 DualSense controller (React + Vite + WebHID + Web Audio)
repos.readme:
Pulse Deck

Turn a PS5 DualSense into a full two-deck DJ console — right in your browser.
Touchpad jog wheels. Gyro FX. Adaptive triggers. Beat-synced lightbar.
No drivers. No hardware mods. Just the controller already on your desk.

▶ Try the live demo in your browser — no install, just click START

--- ## Why DJ software is expensive, and mixing with a keyboard feels like filling out a spreadsheet. Meanwhile there's a haptically brilliant, gyro-equipped, touchpad-bearing controller sitting on your desk doing nothing. Pulse Deck maps **the entire DualSense** onto a real DJ workflow over **WebHID** — not the watered-down Gamepad API. The touchpad becomes a jog wheel. The gyro becomes an FX unit. The triggers push back on your fingers while the track plays. The lightbar is your VU meter. Open a browser tab. Press START. Drop in some tracks. Start mixing. ## Features ### 🎛 The DJ engine - **Two full decks** — play/cue state machine, hot cues, 4-beat loops, pitch faders, and PLL-based SYNC that actively corrects drift (±12% bend) - **Mixer** — equal-power crossfader, 3-band EQ, morphing low/high-pass filter, echo & reverb send FX - **Key lock** — tempo changes without the chipmunk effect, powered by SoundTouchJS - **Library** — searchable session library, browse and load entirely from the controller - **Waveforms & BPM detection** — click-scrub on the waveform, auto BPM analysis on load ### 🎮 DualSense superpowers - **Touchpad jog wheels** — left half scrubs Deck A, right half Deck B. Scratch or nudge mode; click the touchpad to toggle - **Gyro FX** — tilt the controller to open echo/reverb. Hold L3 to arm Deck A, R3 for Deck B - **Adaptive triggers** — L2/R2 are your channel faders, and they fight back: stiffness while playing, a buzz when the track is about to end - **Haptics** — downbeat pulses in your hands, cue thumps, clipping warnings - **Lightbar** — deck colors blended live by the crossfader, beat-synced pulse, red flash on clipping - **Player LEDs** — five dots as a master VU meter - **PS button = PANIC** — one press fades the master out. Every DJ's best friend - **Live remapping** — rebind any action from the in-app profile editor; it persists and follows you ### 🖥 Desktop app - Runs as a native Windows app via Electron, with an installer and a portable `.exe` - Full WebHID support wired up — no browser permission dance ## Quick start **Zero install — test it right now:** open **https://ezzy1231.github.io/pulse-deck/** in Chrome or Edge (any HTTPS page works for WebHID). Hit START, load your tracks, plug in the DualSense over USB. Or run it locally: ```bash npm install npm run dev ``` 1. Open `http://localhost:5173` 2. Hit **START** (browsers require a click before audio can play) 3. Load a couple of tracks with the **LOAD** button on each deck 4. Plug in your DualSense over **USB** and it just works > Bluetooth exposes standard gamepad inputs only. Touchpad, gyro, haptics, and lightbar need USB — raw HID reports aren't available over BT in the browser. ## Controller map (defaults) | Input | Action | | --- | --- | | D-pad ↓ / ← / → / ↑ | Deck A: play · cue · sync · loop | | ✕ / ○ / □ / △ | Deck B: play · cue · sync · loop | | L1 / R1 + deck buttons | Hot cues 1–4 | | L2 / R2 | Channel faders A / B (with adaptive trigger feedback) | | Left / right stick X | Filter A / B | | Left / right stick Y | Pitch bend A / B (hold L1/R1 for tempo) | | Create + left stick | Crossfader | | Create + right stick Y | Master volume | | Options | Toggle library browse | | Touchpad | Jog wheels (click to toggle scratch/nudge) | | L3 / R3 (hold) | Arm gyro FX for A / B | | PS | Panic — fade out master | Browse mode: D-pad or left stick to scroll · L1/R1 or ←/→ to pick target deck · ✕ or L2/R2 to load · ○ to close. Everything above is rebindable — open **Settings** from the header pill, hit REBIND, press a button. ## Keyboard | Key | Action | | --- | --- | | `Q` / `W` | Cue / play Deck A | | `O` / `P` | Cue / play Deck B | | `B` | Toggle library browse (arrows to move, Enter to load) | | `S` | Settings & mapping editor | ## Desktop app Grab the latest build from [Releases](https://github.com/ezzy1231/pulse-deck/releases/latest) — installer or portable, no toolchain needed. Or build it yourself: ```bash npm run electron # dev run as a desktop window npm run package # build the Windows installer + portable exe ``` Artifacts land in `release/`. The builds are unsigned, so SmartScreen will grumble the first time — *More info → Run anyway*. ## Under the hood - **Raw HID, not the Gamepad API** — the DualSense is parsed at the report level: sticks, buttons, gyro, touch coordinates, and the full output report (rumble motors, adaptive trigger effects, lightbar, player LEDs) at 250 Hz with live latency telemetry - **One typed event bus** — UI, audio engine, and controller layer never touch each other directly; `wire.ts` is the single wiring point - **Real DJ math** — equal-power crossfade, exponential pitch-rate integration with glide, PLL sync correction, 30 ms granular scratch - **Key lock that loops** — SoundTouch WSOLA time-stretching with loop-wrap reseeking, driven from the audio callback - **Feedback loop** — a 60 fps envelope engine maps beats, cues, clipping, and track endings onto haptics and the lightbar - **A hex log panel** in the controller card, because HID offsets deserve to be debuggable | Layer | Choice | | --- | --- | | UI | React 19 · Zustand · hand-rolled CSS | | Build | Vite 7 · TypeScript 5.9 (strict) | | Audio | Web Audio API — custom deck/engine graph | | Controller | WebHID (raw reports) + Gamepad API | | Pitch/time | SoundTouchJS · web-audio-beat-detector | | Desktop | Electron 44 · electron-builder | ## Project structure ``` src/ audio/ Web Audio engine + decks (key lock, scratch, sync) controllers/ DualSense HID, sensors, feedback, mapping profile, gamepad state/ Zustand store ui/ Decks, mixer, library, waveform, settings modal actions/ Typed event bus wire.ts Wires bus events to the engine electron/ Desktop shell (WebHID permissions included) spec/ The original product spec ``` ## Honest limitations - Full DualSense experience needs **USB** (Bluetooth: standard inputs only) - Key-lock loop wraps re-prime the stretcher — a tiny dip, roughly 50 ms - HID report offsets are reverse-engineered; if a firmware update shifts them, use the built-in hex log - Windows builds are unsigned ## Roadmap - Recording / mix export - Beatgrid editing with the jog wheels - MIDI-out for hybrid setups ## Credits Built on the shoulders of: [SoundTouchJS](https://github.com/cutterbl/SoundTouchJS) · [web-audio-beat-detector](https://github.com/chrisguttandin/web-audio-beat-detector) · [Zustand](https://github.com/pmndrs/zustand) · [Vite](https://github.com/vitejs/vite) · [Electron](https://github.com/electron/electron) DualSense HID protocol informed by [SDL](https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL) and the Linux `hid-playstation` kernel driver. ## Contributing PRs are welcome — controllers, effects, and UI polish especially. Fork it, break it, fix it, send it back. ## License MIT — use it, remix it, ship it. Just keep the copyright notice. See [LICENSE](LICENSE) for details. Bundled dependencies keep their own licenses (see Credits). ---

If this made you want to DJ, drop a ⭐ — it helps other people find it.
Now go make something loud.

repos.name: driftcheck5
repos.description: Controller tester for jailbroken PS5
repos.readme:
A controller tester for jailbroken PS5s: find stick drift without leaving the console.

--- DriftCheck is a native PS5 homebrew app that shows everything your DualSense reports and measures how healthy its analog sticks are. Run the rest test, let go of the sticks for three seconds, and it tells you whether they drift and which deadzone would hide it.

The screenshot is the app's own drawing code rendered on a PC with a scripted controller (`tools/preview.sh`): the right stick rests off-centre and falls short of the edge. ## What it shows - **Both analog sticks**, live, with their raw values and distance from the centre. - **Circularity**: rotate a stick all the way round and the app traces how far it reaches in each of 72 directions, green on the circle and yellow off it, and reports the average error. - **Rest test**: press and release **Options**, then let go of both sticks for 3 seconds. Each stick gets a verdict (OK, slight drift, drift, or "touched, redo") and a suggested deadzone, drawn as an orange ring. - **L2 and R2** as analog values from 0 to 255. - **Every button an app can read**: Cross, Circle, Square, Triangle, L1, R1, L2, R2, L3, R3, Options, the touchpad click and the D-pad. - **The touchpad**, with up to two fingers and their coordinates. - **The motion sensors**: accelerometer and gyroscope. DriftCheck tells them apart by which one reads gravity. Hold **Options** for 2 seconds to clear the circularity traces. ### Reading the results A healthy stick rests within a few percent of the centre. DriftCheck calls **5 %** and above slight drift and **10 %** and above drift. These thresholds are a starting point, not a measured standard; the number itself is what to compare between controllers or before and after a repair. The suggested deadzone is the resting distance rounded up plus two points. Set it in the games that let you. ### Limits - **Create and the PS button** never reach an app, so they can't be tested. - **One controller**: the one of the user who started the app. - **No battery level** yet. ## Install You need a jailbroken PS5 running an ELF loader on port 9021 (such as [elfldr](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/elfldr)), [kstuff](https://github.com/EchoStretch/kstuff-lite) and [ShadowMountPlus](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus). **With the installer (recommended).** Send `DriftCheck.elf` from the [releases](../../releases) to the loader: ```bash nc -q0 9021 < DriftCheck.elf ``` It writes the app to `/data/homebrew/PPSA98766/` and confirms with a notification; ShadowMountPlus adds the icon to the home screen within a few seconds. Send a newer `DriftCheck.elf` the same way to update. **By FTP.** Extract `PPSA98766.zip` and upload the `PPSA98766` folder to `/data/homebrew/`. The console only starts an app whose files are all 0777 and shows **CE-107750-0** otherwise. Some FTP servers store uploads with another mode (zftpd writes 0666); if yours does, run `python3 chmod-no-ps5.py [port]` afterwards. A diagnostic log is written to `/data/driftcheck/driftcheck.log`. ## Build On Linux or WSL with Clang (18 or newer), lld, Ninja, Make and Python 3: ```bash make # dist/PPSA98766/ and dist/PPSA98766.zip make installer # dist/DriftCheck.elf (builds the app first) make test # host unit and integration tests bash tools/preview.sh # build/preview.png, the screen with a fake controller ``` The first `make` fetches the pinned public PS5 payload SDK and zlib into `.deps/`. Pushing a tag equal to `contentVersion` in `sce_sys/param.json` (for example `01.000.000`) makes the GitHub workflow build, attest and publish `DriftCheck.elf`, `PPSA98766.zip` and `SHA256SUMS`. The stick math (`src/stick_analysis.*`) has no platform calls and is covered by the unit tests. The controller layout (`src/pad.cpp`) follows the PS5 SDL port's `PS5_PadData`, checked against the boilerplate's hardware-tested sample size and field offsets. ## Credits - Built on [ps5-native-app-boilerplate](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-native-app-boilerplate) by BlackBearReloaded: the build, FSELF signing, clean-room runtime and renderer, kept under `tools/`, `tooling/` and `runtime/`. Its documentation and examples were left out; they are in the boilerplate's repository. - [ps5-payload-dev](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev): the payload SDK, and the controller structures of its SDL port. ## License GPL-3.0-or-later, like the boilerplate it is built on. See [LICENSE](LICENSE). DualSense and PlayStation are trademarks of Sony Interactive Entertainment; DriftCheck is an unofficial project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Sony.
