latestRelease.name: XashPS5 V1.3
latestRelease.body:
## New
- **Vulkan rendering**: the game now runs on Mesa Zink over the RADV Vulkan driver (PS5_Vulkan by Mihawk). Whole frames go to the GPU at once: steady frame rate in 4K even in the heaviest fights.
- **4K by default**. 1440p and 1080p are still available in Options, Video, Video modes.
- **120 FPS on 120 Hz displays**: open Options, Video, Video modes and tick **120 Hz**. It is off by default. The console must also allow 120 Hz output (Settings, Screen and Video, Video Output).
- **Counter-Strike** (your own `cstrike` folder): game code and menus built in, with team selection, buy menu (D-pad up), MOTD and a **Change team** button in the pause menu.
- **USB keyboard and mouse** (or a wireless USB receiver): keys by position, mouse look, buttons and wheel, a cursor in the menus. QWERTY text by default, type `ps5_kb_layout fr` in the console for AZERTY. The DualSense keeps working at the same time.
- **Toggle crouch** on Circle, with a checkbox in Options, Gamepad (on by default).
- **New right-stick aim curve**: one circular deadzone and a response curve, precise small moves and fast full turns. Idea and tuning from mpereiraesaa/ps5-xash3d-halflife, thank you.
- A notification tells you what to copy when the game files are missing.

## Fixes
- The PS5 system keyboard could stay disabled after using an older build.
- No more crash when a file inside a `.pk3` archive is opened.

## Changed
- Quieter logs. Create `/data/xash_debug.txt` on the console for verbose output.
- The previous run's log is kept as `/data/xash_log_previous.txt`.

## Install
1. Download `PPSA19111.zip` and unzip it.
2. Copy your own `valve` folder into `PPSA19111/valve/`, plus `gearbox`, `bshift` and/or `cstrike` if you own them (delete the folders you don't use). Keep the `.cfg` files and `valve/extras.pk3` from the zip.
3. Counter-Strike also needs `extras.pk3` in `PPSA19111/cstrike/`: take it from the `cstrike` folder of `CS16Client-Linux-x86_64.tar.gz` in the releases of Velaron/cs16-client. It isn't included here because it contains game sounds and maps.
4. Send `PPSA19111/` to `/data/homebrew/` over FTP (etaHEN, port 2121), or install it from the homebrew store.
5. Launch **XashPS5 V1.3** from the home screen. The first launch takes a little longer while shaders are prepared.

**Upgrading from 1.2:** same title `PPSA19111`, your saves and settings are kept. If an update replaces the app folder, copy your game folders back into it.

No game data is included. You need your own Half-Life files.

## Known limitations
- Counter-Strike bots are not included yet.
- Internet server browser works; LAN works.
- Accented characters can't be typed from a USB keyboard yet.

## Thanks
Mihawk (PS5_Vulkan, PS5_Mesa, PS5_PayloadSDK), BlackBearReloaded (ps5-opengl, ps5-native-app-boilerplate, ProsperoTV, keyboard and mouse research), Velaron (cs16-client) and the ReGameDLL_CS team, mpereiraesaa (ps5-xash3d-halflife), FWGS (Xash3D FWGS, hlsdk-portable).

## Assets
- `PPSA19111.zip`: `eboot.bin`, `sce_module/libc.prx`, `sce_sys/`, `valve/` (`userconfig.cfg`, `autoexec.cfg`, `extras.pk3`), `gearbox/`, `bshift/` and `cstrike/` (`userconfig.cfg`), install notes
- `PPSA19111.zip.sha256`

repos.name: PS5_DevilutionX
repos.description: DevilutionX for the PlayStation 5: an installed title with controller, keyboard and mouse (source only)
repos.readme:
# DevilutionX for PlayStation 5

[![stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/griches/PS5_DevilutionX?style=flat)](https://github.com/griches/PS5_DevilutionX/stargazers)
[![release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/griches/PS5_DevilutionX)](https://github.com/griches/PS5_DevilutionX/releases/latest)
[![licence](https://img.shields.io/badge/licence-see%20LICENSING.md-orange)](LICENSING.md)

A PS5 homebrew build of [DevilutionX](https://github.com/diasurgical/devilutionX),
the source port of Diablo and Hellfire, as an installed title (`PPSA99308`) with
a controller, a keyboard and a mouse. The game draws its picture in software, as
it always has; SDL3's Vulkan renderer puts it on the screen through RADV, from
the [PS5 Vulkan](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Vulkan) stack.

It needs a PS5 that already runs homebrew, and **your own copy of Diablo**
(`DIABDAT.MPQ`). No game data, Blizzard artwork, Sony software or keys are
included here.

This is an unofficial build. DevilutionX has a PS5 port of its own
(`Packaging/ps5` upstream, launched through websrv); this one is separate and
is not supported by the DevilutionX project: please do not take its problems
to them.

**Free of charge, for non-commercial use.** A built `eboot.bin` links
DevilutionX (Sustainable Use License) with GPL-3.0 parts of the PS5 stack, and
the two licences' conditions do not fit together on one program:
[`LICENSING.md`](LICENSING.md) says where that stands.

## Status

Tested on one console (firmware 13.60, a 3840x2160 output) on 2026-10-12, with
the retail `DIABDAT.MPQ`, at DevilutionX `b0a3b7ba`. "Seen" means it ran there
and was looked at through [PS5 DevLoop](https://github.com/griches/PS5_DevLoop)
(a virtual controller and the title's own frames) or read in the console's
log; nothing else is claimed. Sound, the keyboard and the mouse were tried by
hand on the same console.

| Area | Seen on the console | Not yet verified |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Start-up | The intro film, the main menu, a new hero, and into Tristram | Hellfire (needs `hellfire.mpq`), the shareware `spawn.mpq` |
| Picture | Fills the screen at 960x540 (the default) and at 1280x720; Settings lists 1080p, 720p, 540p and 480p | 1080p and 480p in play; a 1080p television |
| Controller | Menus (Cross confirms, Circle goes back), walking with the left stick, the inventory, picking an item up, the game menu, the modifier hint overlays | Each button in play; rumble |
| Button prompts | The DualSense's symbols: "△ to use" on a potion, and the bindings in Settings > Padmapping | Every prompt in the game |
| Keyboard and mouse | Both libraries load and open at start-up. Played with a keyboard and a mouse by Gary Riches on the console (2026-10-12) | Each key and button; text entry; the prompts changing to the keyboard's wording |
| Saving | Save Game from the menu; the hero and the save found again after a restart | |
| Settings | Resolution changed and changed back; kept in `userdata/diablo.ini` | Every other option |
| Sound | Listened to by Gary Riches on the console (2026-10-12) | Music, speech and effects each checked against the PC game |
| Exit | Exit Diablo and Quit Game both close the title (exit status 0) | Closing it from the home screen |
| Multiplayer | | Not built: `NONET` is on |

Known limits:

- **The game menu is Options and the touchpad button together.** DevilutionX
  uses Start as a modifier (hold it to see what the other buttons do), and
  opens its menu with Start and Select; the touchpad's click is Select here,
  because the console keeps the Create button for itself.
- **A hero's name is the random one the game offers** unless a keyboard is
  plugged in: the console's on-screen keyboard is not opened.
- **Text from a keyboard is US layout.** The console gives key codes and no
  characters, so the driver makes the characters itself.
- **Assets are loose files** (`assets/`, `mods/`), not `devilutionx.mpq`:
  Ubuntu's `smpq`, which would pack them, aborts on arm64.

## Controls

**Controller.** These are DevilutionX's defaults for a PlayStation pad, read
from its source (`InitPadmapActions` in `Source/diablo.cpp`).

In menus: D-pad or left stick to move, **Cross** to confirm, **Circle** to go
back, **Square** to delete a hero.

In the game:

| Button | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Left stick, D-pad | Walk |
| Right stick | Move the pointer |
| Circle | Main action: attack, talk, and lift or place an item in the inventory |
| Triangle | Second action: pick up from the ground, open chests and doors, use an item in the inventory |
| Square | Cast the active spell |
| Cross | Open the quick spell list to choose the active spell; close a panel |
| L1 / R1 | Drink a health / a mana potion from the belt |
| L2 / R2 | Character sheet / inventory |
| L3 | Automap |
| R3 | Left mouse click at the pointer |

Two buttons change what the others do while held, and the game draws the
choices on screen while you hold them:

| Hold | Then | Does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Options | D-pad, face buttons | Opens a panel: the icons shown are character, inventory, map, quests, spell book |
| Touchpad button | Face buttons | Sets or casts a spell hotkey (the four empty squares) |
| Touchpad button | L2 / R2 | Quest log / spell book |
| Touchpad button | D-pad | Moves the pointer |
| Touchpad button | L1 or R3 | Left click (L1) / right click (R3); R1 is right click too |
| Options | Touchpad button | **The game menu** (save, options, quit) |

Settings > Padmapping lists every action with its button and changes any of
them.

**Keyboard and mouse** are the PC game's: left click to move and attack, right
click to cast, `I` inventory, `C` character, `Tab` the map, `Esc` the menu,
`1` to `8` the belt. The game switches its prompts between the two by whichever
you touched last: move the mouse and it says "Right click to use", press a
button on the pad and it shows the pad's symbol.

## Install

1. Unpack a [release](https://github.com/griches/PS5_DevilutionX/releases)'s zip,
   or build it (below), which fills `dist/PPSA99308/`.
2. Copy the `PPSA99308` folder to `/data/homebrew/PPSA99308/` on the console
   (`ps5/tools/vm.sh deploy` does it over FTP from a build).
3. Put your `DIABDAT.MPQ` beside `eboot.bin`, in `/data/homebrew/PPSA99308/`.
   `hellfire.mpq`, `hfmonk.mpq`, `hfmusic.mpq` and `hfvoice.mpq` go there too
   if you have Hellfire.
4. Launch "DevilutionX" from the home screen.

Settings and saves are kept in `/data/homebrew/PPSA99308/userdata/`.

If the tile does not appear, look in `/data/shadowmount/debug.log`:
ShadowMountPlus registers a folder when it first sees it, tries twice, and
loses its hook into the system when the console wakes from rest mode ("AppInstallAll
hook is no longer installed"). Restarting ShadowMountPlus registers the title.
Deploy the whole folder at once, icon included, so that the first try has
everything.

## Build

On macOS, through the Linux VM the other ports use (`ps5`, in Lima, with
PS5_Vulkan, PS5_Mesa and PS5_PayloadSDK under `~/ps5`):

```bash
git submodule update --init
ps5/tools/vm.sh build      # dist/PPSA99308/
ps5/tools/vm.sh deploy     # to the console, over FTP
ps5/tools/vm.sh run        # launch, and follow the console's log until the game quits
```

`gettext` must be installed in the VM (for the translations).

## How it works

- **`vendor/devilutionx`** is upstream at a pinned revision. What the console
  needs changed is `ps5/patches/devilutionx.patch`, applied before each build:
  where settings and saves go, no hardware pointer, and the screenshot hook
  for PS5 DevLoop. After editing the submodule, run
  `git -C vendor/devilutionx diff > ps5/patches/devilutionx.patch`. Upstream's
  files end their lines with CR LF: `ps5/tools/edit-source.py` replaces text
  without rewriting the rest.
- **`ps5/cmake/ps5-game.cmake`** is included by DevilutionX's own CMake build
  right after `project()`. It chooses SDL3, hands the build this port's
  patched SDL tree, sets the console's options (960x540, PlayStation
  prompts, no networking) and replaces the link with PS5_Vulkan's.
- **`ps5/sdl/`** holds SDL3's drivers for the console. The video driver gives
  SDL one display, whose size it asks of `VK_KHR_display`, and a window
  that is the whole screen; SDL's Vulkan renderer draws through RADV. The same
  driver reads the keyboard and the mouse once per event pump and turns them
  into SDL's events.
- **`ps5/src/platform.c`** is the console itself: the log, the pad,
  libSceMouse and libSceKeyboard, the sound output.
- **960x540** is the default because it is a whole number of the screen's
  pixels on both a 4K and a 1080p output, in the screen's shape. The game's
  original 640x480 view is "480p" in Settings.

Things the build had to be told, each with its comment in
`ps5-game.cmake` or `link-title.sh`: Lua looks for a separate maths library
and POSIX's `_setjmp`; SDL3_image builds without PNG support, silently, unless
it is shown the libpng DevilutionX fetched (no screenshots otherwise); zlib is
already inside the RADV archive.

## Test hooks

- `/app0/devloop-shot`: when PS5 DevLoop creates this file the game writes its
  next frame to `userdata/screenshots/` (`ps5loop.py grab --title devilutionx`).
  The picture is the game's own 8-bit frame, with a palette whose alpha is 0:
  drop the transparency before looking at it.
- `/app0/env.txt`: `NAME=value` lines for the environment, read before the
  game starts. `SDL_PS5_DISPLAY=1920x1080` overrides the output size.

## Artwork

The icon and the background were made for this port by Gary Riches with an
image generator: `ps5/art/`, and `ps5/art/make-title-art.sh` turns them into
`ps5/sce_sys/`. Nothing in them is Blizzard's.

latestRelease.name: DevilutionX for PlayStation 5 v0.1.0
latestRelease.body:
The first release: DevilutionX, the source port of Diablo and Hellfire, as a title on the PS5's home screen, played with a controller or a keyboard and mouse. Built from DevilutionX revision `b0a3b7ba`.

## What it does

- **An installed title**, with its own tile and background, not a payload: start "DevilutionX" from the home screen.
- **Controller, keyboard and mouse.** The game changes its prompts to whichever you touched last, and shows the DualSense's own symbols for the pad.
- **Widescreen, sharp.** 960x540 by default, a whole number of the screen's pixels on a 4K or a 1080p television. Settings also offers 1080p, 720p and the original 480p.
- Saves and settings are kept in the title's own folder.

## Install

1. Unpack `DevilutionX-PS5-v0.1.0.zip`. It holds one folder, `PPSA99308`.
2. Copy that folder to the console as `/data/homebrew/PPSA99308/`.
3. Copy `DIABDAT.MPQ` from your own copy of Diablo into the same folder, beside `eboot.bin`. For Hellfire, add `hellfire.mpq`, `hfmonk.mpq`, `hfmusic.mpq` and `hfvoice.mpq`.
4. Start "DevilutionX" from the home screen.

No game data is in this download. You need a PS5 that already runs homebrew, with ShadowMountPlus showing the folders in `/data/homebrew`. The [README](https://github.com/griches/PS5_DevilutionX#install) has the details, and the [controls](https://github.com/griches/PS5_DevilutionX#controls).

## Limits

- **The game menu is Options and the touchpad button together.** Options held alone shows a second set of actions.
- **No multiplayer.** Networking is not built.
- **A new hero gets the random name the game offers** unless a keyboard is plugged in: the console's on-screen keyboard is not opened.
- **A keyboard types in US layout.**
- If the tile does not appear after copying, restart ShadowMountPlus: it does not register new titles after the console has woken from rest mode.

## Not verified

Tried on one console (firmware 13.60, a 4K output): menus, a new hero, play in the town, the inventory, the button prompts, saving and loading, resolution changes and quitting were seen through a test rig; sound, the keyboard and the mouse were tried by hand. Hellfire, the shareware data, a 1080p television, long sessions and anything past the town have not been.

## Source and licences

Free of charge, for non-commercial use. This is a modified build of DevilutionX, which is under the Sustainable Use License 1.0; the console's start-up code and platform layer are under GPL-3.0. Those two licences set conditions that do not fit together on one program, and [LICENSING.md](https://github.com/griches/PS5_DevilutionX/blob/v0.1.0/LICENSING.md) says where that stands. `SOURCE.txt` in the zip names the revision of every part it was built from; this port's is `f84598f`.

Unofficial: not part of, or supported by, the DevilutionX project. Please do not take PS5 problems to them.

repos.name: PS5_DevTools
repos.description: Crash reports and memory graphs for homebrew on a jailbroken PS5: a resident payload that records every crash with backtraces and graphs each title's memory, with a dashboard on your network.
repos.readme:
# PS5 DevTools

[![stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/griches/PS5_DevTools?style=flat)](https://github.com/griches/PS5_DevTools/stargazers)
[![release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/griches/PS5_DevTools)](https://github.com/griches/PS5_DevTools/releases/latest)
[![licence](https://img.shields.io/badge/licence-GPL--3.0-blue)](LICENSE)

**Crash reports and memory graphs for homebrew on a jailbroken PS5, with no
change to the titles and no internet.**

When a port crashes on the console, all you normally get is "Something went
wrong with this game or app", or the title simply vanishes. DevTools is one
small payload that stays resident and watches every homebrew title you start:

- **Crash reports.** It attaches to each title as its debugger. When the title
  crashes it records the signal, the faulting address, every thread's
  registers and backtrace, a copy of the faulting stack, the loaded modules,
  the code at the fault and the last two minutes of memory use. Then it hands
  the crash back to the system. A notification on the TV says the report is
  saved.
- **Function names.** On the machine that built the title, the host tool finds
  the build's ELF (matched by a hash of the code on the console) and turns
  addresses into functions and source lines.
- **Memory and CPU graphs.** Every title is sampled once a second, for the last
  hour: resident memory, split into direct memory (what the GPU uses) and heap,
  with CPU and threads.
- **The console's own error history.** Every error dialog the system has shown,
  with its code, title and time.

![The dashboard: Super Mario Sunshine with its HD texture pack, 5.5 GiB resident, nearly all of it GPU memory](docs/dashboard.png)

Everything is kept on the console and served on the local network: a browser at
`http://<console>:9113/` shows the dashboard. Nothing is sent anywhere.

```bash
tools/ps5devtools.py load        # once per console boot (the ELF loader must be up, port 9021)
tools/ps5devtools.py serve       # the dashboard at http://localhost:8113/, with function names
tools/ps5devtools.py crashes     # or from the terminal
tools/ps5devtools.py report      # the newest report, symbolicated
```

> For homebrew development on a console you own. Tested on **firmware 13.60
> only**. The calls it relies on are undocumented and may differ elsewhere.

## A report

A real one, from `test-crash` on Super Mario Sunshine (its main thread sent to
address 0x10, as a call through a bad function pointer would):

```
Super Mario Sunshine (PPSA99312 00.009.000) SIGSEGV at libkernel.sprx+0x8a0b (called from)
  2026-10-14T13:20:11Z, pid 127, up 25 s, outcome: crashed
  fault address 0x10, signal 11 code 1, thread eboot.bin (101396)
  symbols: PS5_Sunshine/build/last-title.elf (matches)
  in the title's code: eboot.bin+0xed287c  __wrap_pthread_join

backtrace:
  #0            0x10  ?+0x0
  #1     0x800008a0b  libkernel.sprx+0x8a0b
  #2       0x12d287c  eboot.bin+0xed287c  __wrap_pthread_join
  #3        0x402861  eboot.bin+0x2861  main  (PS5_Sunshine/vendor/sms-pc-port/src/port_main.cpp:80)
  #4        0x400174  eboot.bin+0x174  _start
```

The thread was in a system call when the test sent it to 0x10, so its caller is
libkernel's system-call stub. `port_main.cpp:80` is the main thread's
`pthread_join` on the game thread, which is where it was waiting. "In the
title's code" is the first frame in the title's own executable, and the TV's
notification names it too. `report` also saves the full JSON and the text
under `captures/`.

`--all-threads` shows what every other thread was doing. In the same report,
the game thread was waiting for the next frame (its first two frames, in
libkernel, left out):

```
thread 102283
  #2        0x447c2c  eboot.bin+0x47c2c  (anonymous namespace)::reschedule(bool)  (PS5_Sunshine/vendor/sms-pc-port/platform/os/os_thread.cpp:374)
  #3        0x464976  eboot.bin+0x64976  VIWaitForRetrace  (PS5_Sunshine/vendor/sms-pc-port/platform/vi/vi.cpp:282)
  #4        0x4b2fd3  eboot.bin+0xb2fd3  JDrama::TVideo::waitForRetrace(unsigned short)  (cp932/libs/JSystem/src/JDrama/JDRVideo.cpp:43)
  #5        0x4af31e  eboot.bin+0xaf31e  JDrama::TDisplay::endRendering()  (cp932/libs/JSystem/src/JDrama/JDRDisplay.cpp:46)
  #6        0x708e10  eboot.bin+0x308e10  TApplication::gameLoop()  (cp932/src/System/Application.cpp:1375)
```

## Sending a report to a developer

Players do not need the source or the build to help. When a title crashes, open
`http://<console>:9113/` in any browser on the same network, click the crash and
use **Download JSON**, or copy the file from `/data/devtools/crashes/` over
FTP. Send that file to the title's developer, who reads it with function names
on the machine that built the title:

```bash
tools/ps5devtools.py report 20261014-132011-PPSA99312-127.json
```

The report says `(matches)` when the developer's ELF is the build the player
was running. The JSON holds the title's registers, a copy of each thread's
stack, its modules and its memory use. The stack is the game's own data at the
moment of the crash.

## What you need

- A jailbroken PS5 with an **ELF loader** on port 9021 (the usual payload chains
  start one).
- Python 3 on the host. For function names, `llvm-symbolizer`, `llvm-dwarfdump`
  and `llvm-nm` on the PATH, from Homebrew's `llvm`, or in the Lima VM that
  builds the titles, which the tool uses by itself.
- To build: the [PS5 payload SDK](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk).
  `tools/build.sh` finds it through `PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK`, or builds in the Lima VM.
- The console's address in `PS5_HOST`, or `PS5_HOST=` in `.env`.

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `load [ELF]` | send the payload to the ELF loader |
| `status` | the titles it has seen, and whether each is attached |
| `crashes` | the reports on the console |
| `report [ID or FILE] [--all-threads] [--elf PATH]` | one report, newest by default or a `.json` someone sent, with function names |
| `errors [--last N]` | the console's own error history |
| `serve [--port 8113] [--lan]` | the dashboard on this machine, with function names |
| `test-crash [PID] [--untraced]` | make an attached title take a real page fault (it closes) |
| `quit` | detach from every title and stop the payload |

## Which titles

Every title is sampled. A title is attached to for crashes when it has a folder
in `/data/homebrew`. To choose yourself, put title ids in
`/data/devtools/watch.txt`, one a line, or `all`, or `none`.

Function names need the build's ELF with its debug information. The tool looks
in every folder beside `PS5_DevTools` whose `sce_sys/param.json` names the
title, at its `build/*.elf`, and uses the one whose code matches the report.
`devtools.json` here can list more:

```json
{"elfs": {"PPSA99312": ["/path/to/eboot.elf"]}}
```

If no ELF matches, the report says so and names the newest one it used: rebuild
the title from the source that is on the console, or pass `--elf`.

## The API

One HTTP request per connection on port 9113:

| Request | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /` | the dashboard |
| `GET /api/status` | the payload and the titles it has seen |
| `GET /api/memory?pid=P&since=T` | a title's samples after unix time T |
| `GET /api/crashes` | report summaries, newest first |
| `GET /api/crash/<id>` | one report |
| `GET /api/errors` | the system's error history |
| `GET /api/log` | the payload's log |
| `DELETE /api/crash/<id>` | remove a report |
| `POST /api/test/fault?pid=P[&untraced=1]` | the test fault |
| `POST /api/quit` | detach from everything and stop |

Reports are files in `/data/devtools/crashes/`, readable over FTP too.

## How it works, and what the console showed (13.60)

- **Finding titles.** The process list (`kern.proc`), with `sceKernelGetAppInfo`
  for each process's title id. System processes (`NPXS…`) are skipped. A
  launch first appears as a process named `SceSysCore.elf`, which becomes
  `eboot.bin`; attaching waits for that and three seconds more, because
  attaching earlier failed or caught a stop from the launch.
- **Attaching.** `ptrace(PT_ATTACH)`, refused with a payload's own credentials.
  With the authid `0x4800000000010003` and full capabilities it is allowed.
  The SDK's `ptrace` is the bare system call, which returns an error as a
  positive number without setting `errno`; the payload wraps it.
- **Never taking a title down.** A debugger that exits takes the processes it
  is tracing with it: the first `quit` closed Sunshine. So before the payload
  leaves, by `quit` or by crashing, it stops each title and detaches. Verified:
  `quit` while attached leaves Sunshine running at the same CPU use.
- **At a crash.** The faulting thread's registers and siginfo, every thread,
  16 KiB of stack, and a backtrace by frame pointers, which our ports keep
  (`push rbp; mov rbp, rsp`). Then `PT_DETACH` with the signal, so the title
  dies of it untraced. A title still running 15 seconds later is marked
  `handled`; one that is gone, `crashed`, with the notification.
- **Module names.** The memory map has no paths on the PS5, so modules come from
  the kernel's list of the process's loaded objects (`/app0/eboot.bin`,
  `libkernel.sprx`, `libSceLibcInternal.sprx`, and so on).
- **Code is execute-only.** A title's code cannot be read even by its debugger,
  so the code at a fault, and the hash that identifies the build, come from its
  `eboot.bin` on disk. That file is a fake-signed SELF (FTP servers hand it out
  as a plain ELF); the payload finds the code segment inside it. The hash is
  FNV-1a 64 of the first 64 KiB of the segment loaded at address 0, as the
  host computes it from each candidate ELF.
- **Names you can trust.** The linker leaves the debug information of functions
  it removed at address 0, where it overlaps the start of the code (the SDK's
  `_start`, which has no debug information of its own). A lookup there finds an
  inlined piece of a removed function. So for each address the host checks with
  `llvm-dwarfdump` that the debug information puts it in a function the link
  kept, and otherwise uses the symbol table's name with no source line.
- **Memory.** `ki_rssize`, `ki_size`, `ki_runtime` and `ki_numthreads` once a
  second, and the map totalled by object type (`KERN_PROC_VMMAP`) every five.
  Direct memory is mapped as device memory and counts in the resident total.
  For Sunshine: 1.7 GiB resident, of which 1.46 GiB direct memory and 175 MiB
  heap, inside a 16 GiB anonymous reservation. The console answers none of the
  `vm.stats` sysctls, so there is no system-wide free figure.
- **The system's own crash handling.** A test fault left no `CE-108255-1` record
  in the error history whether DevTools was attached or not (`--untraced`), so
  attaching does not change what the system records. kstuff showed its own
  crash notice beside DevTools'.

## Limits

- System modules show as module and offset only.
- A crash in a leaf function of a system library can lose its caller.
- The payload listens on the local network with no authentication. Run it on a
  network you trust.
- Three reports at most per process, so a title that faults on purpose many
  times cannot fill the disk.
- Only one debugger can attach to a title: do not run gdbsrv or ps5debug on a
  title DevTools is watching.

## Related

[PS5 DevLoop](https://github.com/griches/PS5_DevLoop) drives the console from a
script: a virtual controller and screenshots.

## Licence

GPL-3.0-or-later. See `LICENSE`.

latestRelease.body:
The first release: crash reports and memory graphs for homebrew on a jailbroken PS5.

**To use it:** send `ps5devtools.elf` to your ELF loader (port 9021), then open `http://<console>:9113/` in a browser on the same network. Or clone the repo and run `tools/ps5devtools.py load`, then `tools/ps5devtools.py serve` for the dashboard with function names.

- Attaches to every homebrew title (folders in `/data/homebrew`) as its debugger. A crash is saved to `/data/devtools/crashes/` with registers, every thread's backtrace, the stack, modules, code at the fault and the two minutes of memory use before it, and the TV shows a notification.
- Samples every title's memory (GPU/direct memory, heap, other), CPU and threads once a second, for the last hour.
- Shows the console's own error history.
- On the machine that built the title, `tools/ps5devtools.py report` turns a report into function names and source lines, including a report a player sends as a `.json` file.

Tested on **firmware 13.60 only**, with Super Mario Sunshine and SwitchWaker. Stop it with `tools/ps5devtools.py quit` (or `POST /api/quit`), never by killing it: it detaches from your titles first.

repos.name: PS5_Dusklight
repos.description: Dusklight for PlayStation 5: a homebrew port on RADV (Aurora, Dawn WebGPU, SDL3). Bring your own disc image.
repos.readme:
# Dusklight for PlayStation 5

[![stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/griches/PS5_Dusklight?style=flat)](https://github.com/griches/PS5_Dusklight/stargazers)
[![release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/griches/PS5_Dusklight)](https://github.com/griches/PS5_Dusklight/releases/latest)
[![Track Dusklight](https://github.com/griches/PS5_Dusklight/actions/workflows/track-dusklight.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/griches/PS5_Dusklight/actions/workflows/track-dusklight.yml)
[![licence](https://img.shields.io/badge/licence-GPL--3.0%20as%20built-blue)](LICENSING.md)

A PS5 homebrew port of [Dusklight](https://github.com/TwilitRealm/dusklight), the
reverse-engineered reimplementation of a classic GameCube adventure. It draws
through Dusklight's own renderer ([Aurora](https://github.com/encounter/aurora) on
Dawn's WebGPU) on RADV, Mesa's Vulkan driver, from the
[PS5 Vulkan](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Vulkan) stack.

It needs a PS5 that already runs homebrew, and a disc image of the game that you
provide. No game data, Nintendo artwork, Sony software or keys are included, here
or in a build.

This is an unofficial port. It is not part of the Dusklight project and is not
supported by it: please do not take PS5 problems to them.

## Status

Tested on one console, on 2026-10-10 and 11, with the GameCube USA disc (GZ2E01).
"Seen" means it ran there and was watched, or read in the console's log; nothing
else is claimed.

| Area | Seen on the console | Not yet verified |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Start-up | Finds the disc image in the title's folder, boots into the game | Exit back to the home screen from the game's own menu |
| Rendering | 3840x2160 on a 59.94 Hz display, several minutes of play with no crash | Frame rate over a long session; 120 Hz; later areas of the game |
| Saving | A memory card file is created, and a save survived closing and restarting the title | |
| Button prompts | The DualSense's symbols on the game's buttons, on the file select and in play: Cross (A), Circle (B), Square (X), Triangle (Y), R1 (Z) | Other prompts (L, R, Start, the D-pad and stick pictures); a changed button mapping; the other regions' discs |
| Input | A DualSense plays the game | Each button of the mapping; rumble; a second controller |
| Sound | | Everything: the driver opens, nobody has confirmed what it sounds like |
| Shader cache | Aurora's pipeline cache opens and is written | That it is reused after a restart |

Known limits:

- **Objects can appear a frame late the first time a scene shows them.** Aurora
  compiles each new render pipeline on a worker thread and skips the draw until
  it is ready, as it does on every platform. They are cached once compiled.
- **Disc images: GameCube `.iso` or `.ciso` only.** Upstream reads RVZ, GCZ, WIA
  and WBFS through a Rust library; this port has its own small reader in its
  place (`ps5/nod/`). Wii discs are not supported.
- **No code mods, no updater, no Discord presence, no network.** They are turned
  off in this build. The mods in Dusklight's `mods/` folder (the randomizer, the
  Luau runtime and the rest) are code mods, so none is bundled, and a mod that
  needs the Luau runtime does not run. An asset-only `.dusk` (textures, files
  that replace the disc's) put in `/data/homebrew/PPSA99305/mods/` is listed and
  can be switched on in the Mods menu. Online mods cannot be browsed.
- **"Disc not verified" on the menu is expected.** The disc is found, not
  chosen, so it is never hashed; and a `.ciso` leaves out the disc's filler
  data, so its hash could not match the original's anyway.
- **The button symbols follow the default mapping.** The game draws a button as
  a coloured shape with a white letter, each letter a texture of its own; the
  port replaces those five textures with symbols from Kenney's Input Prompts
  (www.kenney.nl, CC0; `ps5/art/kenney/`, cut to size by `ps5/art/make-glyphs.py`,
  shipped in `res/ps5-glyphs/`, loaded as texture replacements named for the
  USA disc's textures), and turns the green tint of the A button blue. They say Cross for A, Circle for B, Square for X,
  Triangle for Y and R1 for Z, which is Dusklight's default mapping: remap the
  buttons and the symbols no longer match. A replacement of your own for the
  same texture wins, and turning texture replacements off in the settings turns
  these off too.
- **Texture packs: loose files or a `.dusk`, `.png` or `.dds`.** Files named the
  way Dolphin names them (`tex1_256x128_e6a4c7be9bf48305_14.dds`) are picked up
  from `/data/homebrew/PPSA99305/userdata/TwilitRealm/Dusklight/texture_replacements/`
  and its subfolders, or from the `textures/` folder of a `.dusk`. A `.dds` may
  be uncompressed 32-bit RGBA or BGRA, BC1 (DXT1), BC3 (DXT5), BC5 or BC7, with
  or without mipmaps; this port also takes the sRGB-tagged variants of those,
  which upstream refuses. BC2 (DXT3), BC4, BC6H and ASTC are not loaded, and a
  compressed texture's width and height must be multiples of 4. Seen on the
  console on 2026-10-12 with three test files in the loose folder: BC7 tagged
  sRGB with mipmaps, DXT5, and uncompressed RGBA; a real texture pack has not
  been tried. The game makes that folder at its first start, and from this
  build on opens it to the FTP server at every start: with v0.2.0 an upload
  into it is refused until the folder's permissions are changed.
- **No file dialog.** The disc image is found by where it is, not chosen.

## Install

Download `Dusklight-PS5-vX.Y.Z.zip` from the
[latest release](https://github.com/griches/PS5_Dusklight/releases/latest) and
unpack it: it holds one folder, `PPSA99305`. (Or build that folder yourself, see
Build.) It contains no game data.

**What the console needs**

- A PS5 that runs homebrew, with etaHEN (or an equivalent) loaded.
- ShadowMountPlus, which shows the folders in `/data/homebrew` as titles on the
  home screen.
- An FTP server on the console to copy files with (port 2121 here).

**Steps**

1. Unpack the release (or build: the result is the folder `dist/PPSA99305/`).
2. Copy that whole folder to the console as `/data/homebrew/PPSA99305/`, so that
   you have:

   ```text
   /data/homebrew/PPSA99305/eboot.bin
   /data/homebrew/PPSA99305/sce_sys/      (param.json, icon0.png, pic0.dds, pic1.dds)
   /data/homebrew/PPSA99305/sce_module/libc.prx
   /data/homebrew/PPSA99305/res/          (fonts and the menus' documents)
   /data/homebrew/PPSA99305/licenses/
   ```

   Copy `sce_sys/icon0.png` with the first upload: ShadowMountPlus will not
   register a title without its icon, and after two failed tries it skips that
   title until it is restarted.
3. Copy your disc image into the same folder, under any name ending in `.iso` or
   `.ciso`:

   ```text
   /data/homebrew/PPSA99305/your-disc.iso
   ```

   It has to be there, not elsewhere in `/data`: a title can only see its own
   folder. The game takes the first image it finds and remembers it.
4. Wait a few seconds for "Dusklight" to appear on the home screen, and start it.

Saves and settings are written to `/data/homebrew/PPSA99305/userdata/`. Copying a
new build over the folder leaves them, and the disc image, alone.

**The disc image.** Dusklight's own terms apply: dump your own copy of the game
([how](https://wiki.dolphin-emu.org/index.php?title=Ripping_Games)). If your dump
is RVZ or another compressed format, convert it to `.iso` with
[Dolphin](https://dolphin-emu.org/) or `nodtool` first.

## Build

The build runs on Linux (x86-64 or arm64; on a Mac, in a Linux VM) with Mihawk's
stack beside this repository:

```text
somewhere/
  PS5_Dusklight/     this repository
  PS5_Vulkan/        https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Vulkan   (with its RADV release archive built)
  PS5_Mesa/          https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Mesa
  PS5_PayloadSDK/    https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_PayloadSDK
```

Set that stack up first, by its own instructions, until `PS5_Vulkan` has
`.deps/native/radv-release/lib/libvulkan_radeon.ps5.a` and
`build/host/ps5-native-tool`. It needs **LLVM 22**: RADV built with an older clang
does not link into a title. Then:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/griches/PS5_Dusklight.git
cd PS5_Dusklight
ps5/tools/build.sh
```

`build.sh` does the rest, and the first run takes a while:

1. checks out Dusklight (`vendor/dusklight`) with Aurora and Borealis, and applies
   `ps5/patches/` to them;
2. fetches Dawn and SDL3 at the revisions Aurora pins into `.deps/`, and patches
   them for the console;
3. installs the payload SDK at this port's pin;
4. configures Dusklight's own CMake build with the SDK's toolchain and
   `ps5/cmake/ps5-game.cmake`, compiles about 3,000 files, links with RADV and
   writes `dist/PPSA99305/`.

Other tools, all in `ps5/tools/`:

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `deploy.sh` | Uploads `dist/PPSA99305/` over FTP (the console's address is `PS5_HOST` in `PS5_Vulkan/.env`). It never touches the disc image or `userdata/`. |
| `run.sh` | Launches the title through PS5_Vulkan's control payload and follows its log; symbolises a crash. |
| `package-release.sh VERSION` | Packs `dist/PPSA99305/` as a release zip with `SOURCE.txt`, the revision of every part. Refuses if a disc image or a save is in the folder. |
| `build-triangle.sh` | Builds a one-triangle WebGPU test in the game's place: the first thing to run when Dawn or the driver changes. |
| `vm.sh TOOL` | From macOS, runs one of the above inside a Lima VM named `ps5`. |
| `update-dusklight.sh` | Moves to upstream Dusklight's latest revision and re-applies the patches. |
| `check-patches.sh` | Says whether the Dawn and SDL3 patches apply to what Aurora now pins. |

## Keeping up with Dusklight

`vendor/dusklight` is a submodule at an upstream revision; nothing of Dusklight is
copied or forked here. What the console needs changed in Dusklight, Aurora and
Borealis is three small patches in `ps5/patches/`; Dawn and SDL3 have theirs
there too.

A [scheduled workflow](.github/workflows/track-dusklight.yml) runs
`update-dusklight.sh` every day. If the patches still apply to upstream's newest
revision, it commits that revision, so a fresh clone builds against the latest
Dusklight the patches fit. If one does not, it commits nothing and opens an issue.
It cannot build the game, so a revision it commits is not known to compile or
run: the Status table above is for the revision it was tested at
(`34a144a493`).

## How it works

```text
  Dusklight (the game's code)                     vendor/dusklight
        |
  Aurora ........ GameCube GX, pads, cards, DVD   vendor/dusklight/extern/aurora
        |              |               |
      Dawn           SDL3             nod
   (WebGPU)     ps5/sdl drivers    ps5/nod: .iso and .ciso
        |
  Vulkan: RADV + PS5 winsys, VK_KHR_display       PS5_Mesa, PS5_Vulkan
        |
  PS5 GPU
```

- **Dawn.** The fork Aurora uses already had a console port (Nintendo Switch):
  a Vulkan driver linked into the program and a native-window surface.
  `ps5/patches/dawn.patch` adds the PS5 beside it: RADV's entry point in place of
  a Vulkan library, and the console's one output as a `VK_KHR_display` surface.
- **SDL3.** Threads, time and files are FreeBSD's. `ps5/sdl/` adds a video driver
  (one display, a window that is the screen), an audio driver (AudioOut, 48 kHz
  stereo) and a joystick driver that presents each controller as a DualSense.
- **nod.** Aurora reads discs through nod, a Rust library. There is no Rust
  toolchain for the console, so `ps5/nod/nod.cpp` implements the part of nod's C
  API that is called, for plain and CISO GameCube images.
- **The console's quirks**, each found the hard way and explained where it is
  handled: constructors that ran in reverse (`ps5/tools/cc-init-array.sh`), an
  `lstat` that does not work for a title and other missing libc functions
  (`ps5/src/shims.c`), and where a title may write (`ps5/src/startup.c`).

## Credits

- [Dusklight](https://github.com/TwilitRealm/dusklight) by Twilit Realm and its
  contributors, on the [Twilight Princess decompilation](https://github.com/zeldaret/tp).
- [Aurora](https://github.com/encounter/aurora), [Borealis](https://github.com/encounter/borealis),
  [nod](https://github.com/encounter/nod) and the Dawn fork by Luke Street (encounter) and contributors.
- [PS5_Vulkan](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Vulkan), [PS5_Mesa](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Mesa),
  [PS5_PayloadSDK](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_PayloadSDK) and the
  [PS5 Vulkan Template](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_VulkanTemplate) by Mihawk:
  the driver, the platform layer and the tools this is built with.
- [ps5-payload-dev/sdk](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk) by John Törnblom.
- Mesa and RADV, Dawn, SDL, and the libraries listed in [LICENSING.md](LICENSING.md).
- Kenney (www.kenney.nl) for the button symbols, from Input Prompts (CC0).

## Licence

See [LICENSING.md](LICENSING.md). In short: the port's own files are MIT or Zlib,
one tool is GPL-3.0, and a built title is GPL-3.0 because of what it links. The
game itself is Nintendo's and is not part of this.

latestRelease.name: Dusklight for PlayStation 5 v1.0.0
latestRelease.body:
Version 1.0, with new home-screen art. Built from upstream Dusklight revision `34a144a493`, the latest on its `main`, as v0.3.0 was.

## Changed

- **New home-screen art.** The icon, the background behind the title and the splash while it starts are a new picture in the spirit of the game's own cover: a young swordsman and a black wolf, split by a seam of twilight, over carved stone in silver and sepia. The background and the splash are now the same picture.
- **Version 1.0.** The program is the same as v0.3.0's: upstream Dusklight has nothing newer to take.

## Install or update

1. Unpack `Dusklight-PS5-v1.0.0.zip`. It holds one folder, `PPSA99305`.
2. Copy that folder to the console as `/data/homebrew/PPSA99305/`, over the old one if you have an earlier version. Your disc image, saves, settings and texture packs in that folder are left alone.
3. New install only: copy your own GameCube disc image (`.iso` or `.ciso`) into the same folder.
4. Start "Dusklight" from the home screen. If the home screen keeps the old icon, remove the title from the home screen and let ShadowMountPlus add it again: the folder and its data are kept.

No game data is in this download. The [README](https://github.com/griches/PS5_Dusklight#install) has the details.

## Not verified

The new art has not yet been seen on the console's home screen. Sound, the full controller mapping and long sessions remain unconfirmed.

## Source

A built title is under GPL-3.0. `SOURCE.txt` in the zip names the revision of every part it was built from; this port's is `577c762`.

`Dusklight-PS5-v1.0.0.zip` sha256: `343f8829803ecba03e8cf3168f543543771e6511dfec4e6761c60bb6f4ab8e8d`

repos.description: Eternal Darkness: Sanity's Requiem on the PS5 (homebrew), built from Eternal Darkness Recomp and your own disc
repos.readme: # Eternal Darkness for the PlayStation 5 [![stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/griches/PS5_EternalDarkness?style=flat)](https://github.com/griches/PS5_EternalDarkness/stargazers) [![release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/griches/PS5_EternalDarkness)](https://github.com/griches/PS5_EternalDarkness/releases/latest) [![licence](https://img.shields.io/badge/licence-GPL--3.0-blue)](LICENSE) **Eternal Darkness: Sanity's Requiem** (GameCube, 2002) as PS5 homebrew, title `PPSA99314`, at 4K and 60 frames a second, built from [Eternal Darkness Recomp](https://github.com/griches/EternalDarknessRecomp) and **your own disc**. Version 0.9.5. > **European disc only.** You need your own image of the **European GameCube disc, > `GEDP01`**. The USA disc (`GEDE01`) is not supported. ## What you need - A PS5 that runs homebrew (etaHEN or similar), with **ShadowMountPlus** and an **FTP server** (port 2121). - Your own image of the European disc: an `.iso` or `.gcm` file (not a compressed RVZ or CISO). - On your computer: an FTP program (FileZilla, for example) and a program that opens `.7z` files (7-Zip on Windows, Keka or The Unarchiver on a Mac). ## Set it up ### 1. The game 1. Download `EternalDarkness-PS5-....zip` from the [latest release](https://github.com/griches/PS5_EternalDarkness/releases/latest) and unzip it. You get a folder called `PPSA99314`. 2. Copy that folder to the console over FTP, as `/data/homebrew/PPSA99314/`. 3. Copy your disc image into `/data/homebrew/PPSA99314/dump/`. Any file name works. ### 2. The HD textures (recommended) Two downloads, both DDS: | Download | What it is | Size | | --- | --- | --- | | **[Eternal Darkness HD Texture Pack](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1KGEr7dF2onTdzUFNp7Lia3p0D0I2-TaZ/view)** by Zombie | The game's textures redrawn at four times the detail | 2.9 GB `.7z` | | **[PAL supplement](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1BuoE0uL4K3xn5KfH8KYYtC6fk-6QiiiA/view)** by Eternal Darkness Recomp | What the pack misses on the European disc: the Jump to Game, Options and Language screens and the title menu's words, and highlights without hard edges | 13.2 MB `.zip` | 1. Unpack both on your computer. Each one gives you a folder. 2. Make a folder called `textures` in `/data/homebrew/PPSA99314/` and copy both folders into it. The pack is a few GB, so this takes a while. Leave both folders as they are: the supplement replaces some of the pack's textures on purpose, and a folder with *supplement* in its name always wins. DDS stays compressed in the console's graphics memory, a quarter of the room PNG takes. The pack is the work of **Zombie**, shared on the [Dolphin forums](https://forums.dolphin-emu.org/Thread-eternal-darkness-hd). ### 3. Check the folder When you're done it looks like this: ``` /data/homebrew/PPSA99314/ ├── eboot.bin, sce_sys/, res/, ... ├── dump/ │ └── your disc image (.iso or .gcm) └── textures/ ├── GED DDS 1.0/ └── Eternal Darkness HD Texture Pack PAL supplement/ ``` The first line is what came in the release zip. `GED DDS 1.0` is Zombie's pack; the folders' names don't matter. ### 4. Play 1. Start **Eternal Darkness** from the home screen. 2. The first start reads the game's program from your disc, which takes a second or two. Then the launcher shows your disc. 3. Choose **New game**. The defaults are already the best picture: 4K, widescreen, HD textures on and sharp baked shadows. In **Options > Game**, **HD textures** should say **On**, and its note gives the number of textures it found. ### If something's wrong - **It isn't on the home screen**: restart ShadowMountPlus (or the console). - **The launcher's Disc says None found**: the image isn't in `dump/`, or it's a compressed RVZ or CISO. A USA disc shows up but can't be played. - **HD textures says No pack**: the pack isn't inside `textures/`. Check the folder against the one above, then close the game and start it again: it looks for the pack as it starts. ### Updating Copy a new release's `PPSA99314` folder over the old one. Saves, settings, your disc and the textures stay as they are: saves and settings live in `/data/homebrew/PPSA99314/` (`saves/`, `settings.ini`, and the memory cards `ed-GEDP01-slot-a.dolcard` and `...-slot-b.dolcard`). The game's files (its program, graphics, sound and music) come from your disc. ## What is better than on the GameCube - **4K at 60 frames a second**, with full colour (no 6-bit banding). Options can also draw at 720p, 1080p or 1440p. - **120 frames a second** on a TV with a 120 Hz mode (VRR): **Options > Display > Frame rate** draws a blended frame between each of the game's own (turn on *Enable 120 Hz Output* in the console's Screen and Video settings). - **Cutscene fast-forward**: hold **R1** while a scene or movie plays to run it at up to four times the speed. - **Camera options** (Options > Game > Camera): the game's own fixed cameras, *Third person (beta)* (behind the character you play, turned with the right stick, up and down for closer or further, kept inside the room by the game's own collision) or *First person (beta)* (through their eyes, looking around with the right stick). Both hold still while you aim. - **Widescreen**: the game's own 16:9 mode (more of the room at the sides, not stretched) with the HUD and prompts at the screen's edges; 4:3 too. - **New baked shadows** (below): the rooms' light and shadow redrawn sharp. - **Crisp game text**: the game's lettering redrawn in two styles, *Sharp* or *Tome* (old typefaces), or *Original* as on the disc. - **HD texture packs** in Dolphin's format. - **Modern controls** and remapping, with PlayStation button prompts, the game's own prompts included (the icons below are the game's own): every GameCube button picture in the game, the Tome's controls page and the organ's notes included, shows your controller's buttons. - **Save anywhere**: the pause menu has four save slots that hold the whole moment, besides the game's own memory-card saves (slots A and B). - **A launcher**: Continue, New game or any save slot straight from the start. - **Problem reports**: if the game stops responding, stops or crashes, it says so on screen and writes a report to `saves/reports/` (fetch it over FTP and send it with a few words on what you were doing). - **Shaders ready**: the title ships the shader caches a console made, so a fresh install starts without compiling them. ## Controls | Action | Modern (default) | Original (GameCube positions) | | --- | --- | --- | | Move | | | | Attack / Confirm | or | | | Action / Cancel | | | | Target / Aim | or | | | Sprint | toggle, or hold | | | Creep | toggle | | | Reload | | | | Quickcast | | | | Spells | | | | Game's pause menu | | | | This port's menu (saves, options) | | | In the game's own menus L1 and R1 page left and right. **Options > Controls** switches layout, makes Sprint, Creep and Target hold or toggle, sets the stick deadzone and vibration, and **Button mapping** rebinds any action (that layout is *Custom*). ## The new baked shadows Eternal Darkness lights its rooms with pre-drawn light maps: the window light on the floors, the shadows under the furniture, the glow of the lamps. On the disc they are small and compressed, so at 4K their edges break up into blocks and smears. With **Options > Game > Baked shadows: Sharp** (the default) each room's light maps are rebuilt four times larger as the room loads, with the compression blocks evened out and edges doubled along their own direction, so light and shadow keep clean edges. **Original** shows them as on the disc. ## How it works - `vendor/edrecomp` is the recomp (a submodule): its host layer, launcher and build. What the console needs changed in it is `ps5/patches/edrecomp.patch`, every hunk behind `__PROSPERO__`. - `ps5/tools/setup-source.sh` fetches the two projects the recomp builds on at its pins (DolRecomp, GXRuntime) with its patches and then the console's (`ps5/patches/gxruntime.patch`), builds the recompiler for the build machine, and translates `main.dol` from the disc in `dump/` into `gamedata//`. - Graphics are GXRuntime's gxcore renderer on Aurora and Dawn (WebGPU), Dawn's Vulkan backend running on the RADV driver linked into the title ([PS5_Vulkan](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Vulkan)). `ps5/patches/dawn.patch` adds the console to Dawn: the driver linked in, and the output as a VK_KHR_display surface. SDL3 gets the console's video, audio and pad drivers (`ps5/sdl`, `ps5/patches/sdl.patch`). - `ps5/src/startup.c` runs before the game: klog, the title folder as the working folder (the recomp finds `generated/main.dol`, `dump/.iso`, `res/`, `saves/` and `settings.ini` there) and the caches in `cache/`. - `ps5/shader-cache` holds the shader caches a console filled (Dawn's `dawn_cache.db` and the driver's `radv-shader-cache`). `link-title.sh` puts them in `res/shader-cache` and `startup.c` copies them into place on a start that has none. Take them from a console again after a change to Dawn, Mesa or the shaders. ## Build From macOS, through the Lima VM `ps5` that holds the PS5 stack (PS5_Vulkan, PS5_Mesa, PS5_PayloadSDK, LLVM 22): ```sh git submodule update --init cp /path/to/GEDP01.iso dump/ # your own European disc ps5/tools/vm.sh build # -> dist/PPSA99314/ ps5/tools/vm.sh deploy # FTP to the console (PS5_HOST) ps5/tools/vm.sh run # launch and follow klog ``` On the console the title folder also needs the disc, `dump/.iso` under `/data/homebrew/PPSA99314/`; the title reads `generated/main.dol` out of it on its first start (`ps5/tools/console.sh game-files` copies both instead). `ps5/tools/package-release.sh VERSION` zips `dist/PPSA99314/` for a release, with an empty `dump/` for the disc. `ps5/tools/console.sh` also deploys and runs from macOS itself, for when the VM cannot reach the console, and writes the title's `env.txt`: `KEY=VALUE` lines the recomp reads as its environment (for example `ED_QUICKLOAD=saves/slot1.state` to start in a save, `AURORA_GPU_TIME_LOG=1` for frame times in klog). The home-screen art (`ps5/art`, converted by `ps5/art/make-title-art.sh`) is the port's own, made with ChatGPT in the look of the game's cover; nothing in it is from the game. The music that plays while the tile is highlighted is: the first 30 seconds of one of the game's insanity themes, in `ps5/sce_sys/snd0.at9`. `ps5/art/make-title-music.sh` remakes it from a disc (needs FFmpeg and [ps5-at9-converter](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-at9-converter) beside this repo). ## Licence GPL-3.0-or-later, as Eternal Darkness Recomp and GXRuntime. The PS5 layer (`ps5/src`, `ps5/sdl`, `ps5/tools`) comes from the author's other PS5 ports. The title carries every component's licence text in `licenses/` (the recomp's `THIRD_PARTY.md` lists them, and SDL, Dawn, Mesa and PS5_Vulkan are added).

latestRelease.body:
**Eternal Darkness: Sanity's Requiem** on the PlayStation 5 (homebrew, title `PPSA99314`) at 4K and up to 120 frames a second, built from [Eternal Darkness Recomp](https://github.com/griches/EternalDarknessRecomp) 0.9.5.

> **European disc only** (`GEDP01`). The USA disc is not supported. You need your own disc image (`.iso` or `.gcm`): the game's program, graphics, sound and music come from it.

### What's new in 0.9.5
- **Fixed:** glow showed through the black bars in cutscenes (a glowing ghost could be seen through them) and lifted HUD text over bright spots; glow and HDR highlights now stay off the bars, the HUD and fades

### New in 0.9.4
- **HDR** (HDR10) on an HDR TV: lamps, flames, magick and the brightest highlights go past white while the rest keeps the game's own look. On by default (*Options > Display > HDR*)
  - *Calibrate HDR*, just below it: three steps for your TV (the brightest it shows, how bright the picture is, how deep the blacks are)
- **Photo mode**: in game, hold **Create** to pause and frame the shot with a free camera
  - Left stick moves, right stick looks, L1/R1 go down and up, L2/R2 zoom, R3 resets (hold it and look to tilt), **Options** takes the photo
  - The face buttons, L3 and the d-pad switch HDR, glow, HD textures, shadows, ambient occlusion, the resolution and the ratio for the shot only
  - Photos are saved as PNGs in `/data/homebrew/PPSA99314/Eternal Darkness Photos/`
- **Ambient occlusion** (Off / Soft / Strong, *Options > Graphics*): soft shading where walls, floors and furniture meet
- **Glow** (Off / Soft / Strong, *Options > Graphics*) round lamps, flames, magick and glowing surfaces
- **Options** is one spread now: Display, Sound, Graphics, Controls and Game side by side
- The European disc starts in 60 Hz without asking
- Movies and menus show at a comfortable white in HDR
- In first person, the aiming arms no longer cut into the view
- The shader cache is retaken for this version, so the first start builds fewer pipelines

### Updating from 0.9.4 or earlier
Copy the new `PPSA99314` folder over the old one. Your saves, settings, disc and textures stay as they are.

### Install
1. Download `EternalDarkness-PS5-0.9.5.zip` below and unzip it: a `PPSA99314` folder.
2. Copy that folder to the console as `/data/homebrew/PPSA99314/` over FTP (include `sce_sys/icon0.png` in the first upload, or ShadowMountPlus won't register it).
3. Put your European disc image in `/data/homebrew/PPSA99314/dump/` (any name).
4. Start **Eternal Darkness** from the home screen (restart ShadowMountPlus if it doesn't appear). The first start reads the game from your disc.

Needs a PS5 that runs homebrew (etaHEN or similar) with ShadowMountPlus and an FTP server.

### Also in this version
- 4K at 60 frames a second, or 120 on a TV with a 120 Hz mode (VRR), full colour
- Camera options (beta): third person and first person beside the game's own fixed cameras
- Cutscene fast-forward: hold **R1** while a scene or movie plays
- The game's own 16:9 widescreen, with the HUD at the screen's edges (4:3 too)
- Sharp baked shadows
- The game's text redrawn crisp (Sharp or Tome)
- Dolphin HD texture packs in `/data/homebrew/PPSA99314/textures/`, PNG or DDS, with *supplement* folders beside the main pack
- Modern controls and remapping with PlayStation button prompts everywhere, including the Tome; Create opens the pause menu
- Save anywhere: four save slots in the pause menu, plus memory cards A and B
- Every component's licence in `licenses/`
- Problem reports in `saves/reports/`

Source: this repository at this tag, with the recomp at `1cb3fe6` (GPL-3.0).

repos.name: PS5_Ghostship
repos.description: Super Mario 64 for PlayStation 5 homebrew: Ghostship (libultraship) on the PS5 Vulkan stack. No game data included.
repos.readme:
# Mario 64 for PlayStation 5

[![stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/griches/PS5_Ghostship?style=flat)](https://github.com/griches/PS5_Ghostship/stargazers)
[![release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/griches/PS5_Ghostship)](https://github.com/griches/PS5_Ghostship/releases/latest)
[![licence](https://img.shields.io/badge/licence-GPL--3.0%20as%20built-blue)](LICENSING.md)

A PS5 homebrew port of [Ghostship](https://github.com/HarbourMasters/Ghostship)
(v3.0.0), HarbourMasters' native port of the 1996 Nintendo 64 game, compiled
from its decompilation on [libultraship](https://github.com/Kenix3/libultraship).
On the console it draws through libultraship's Vulkan renderer on RADV, from the
[PS5 Vulkan](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Vulkan) stack.

The build reads no ROM and holds no game data. The player copies their own ROM
beside the title, and the title converts it once, on the console.

## Status

**Runs on the console.** First run on 2026-10-12 on a PS5 at 3840x2160: the title
screen, the file select, a new game and the castle grounds, at a measured 60
images a second (frame interpolation; the game's logic stays at 30).

| Area | State |
| --- | --- |
| Game data | A US or JP `.z64` in the title's folder is found on the first start and converted to `sm64.o2r` in a few seconds. With neither file the title says what to copy where and closes |
| Picture | 3840x2160 on a 4K output, 16:9 |
| 60 fps | Measured at 3840x2160 on the title screen and the castle grounds |
| Menu | The touch pad's click opens Ghostship's settings menu. L1/R1 change tab, L2/R2 change section, the d-pad and Cross work the settings, Options asks to quit. The controls are listed along the bottom of the screen |
| HD textures | [SM64 Reloaded](#hd-textures-optional) seen working on the console |
| Saves, settings | `/data/homebrew/PPSA99310/userdata/` |
| DevLoop | `devloop-shot` in the title's folder (registered as `ghostship`) |
| Art | The icon and background are the port's own, made with an image generator (`ps5/art/`) |

Controls are Ghostship's defaults for a pad: left stick to move, Cross A,
Circle B, L2 Z, R2 R, L1 L, Options START, the right stick for the C buttons.
They can be changed in the menu under Settings, Controls.

## Install

Download `Mario64-PS5-vX.Y.zip` from the
[latest release](https://github.com/griches/PS5_Ghostship/releases/latest) and
unpack it: it holds one folder, `PPSA99310`. (Or build that folder yourself, see
Build.) It contains no game data.

**What the console needs**

- A PS5 that runs homebrew, with etaHEN (or an equivalent) loaded.
- ShadowMountPlus, which shows the folders in `/data/homebrew` as titles on the
  home screen.
- An FTP server on the console to copy files with (port 2121 here).

**Steps**

1. Copy the whole folder `PPSA99310` to the console as
   `/data/homebrew/PPSA99310/`, so that you have:

   ```text
   /data/homebrew/PPSA99310/eboot.bin
   /data/homebrew/PPSA99310/ghostship.o2r
   /data/homebrew/PPSA99310/config.yml
   /data/homebrew/PPSA99310/assets/       (what the ROM's conversion reads)
   /data/homebrew/PPSA99310/sce_sys/      (param.json, icon0.png, pic0.dds, pic1.dds)
   /data/homebrew/PPSA99310/sce_module/libc.prx
   /data/homebrew/PPSA99310/licenses/
   ```

   Copy `sce_sys/icon0.png` with the first upload: ShadowMountPlus will not
   register a title without its icon.
2. Copy your own Super Mario 64 ROM into the same folder, beside `eboot.bin`.
   It must be the Nintendo 64 game's US or JP release, in `.z64` format (big
   endian; convert a `.n64` or `.v64` dump first), under any name ending in
   `.z64`. The title checks the ROM against these hashes and takes no other:

   ```text
   /data/homebrew/PPSA99310/baserom.us.z64
   ```

   | Release | SHA-1 |
   | --- | --- |
   | US | `9bef1128717f958171a4afac3ed78ee2bb4e86ce` |
   | JP | `8a20a5c83d6ceb0f0506cfc9fa20d8f438cafe51` |

3. Wait a few seconds for "Mario 64" to appear on the home screen, and start it.
4. The first start says "ROM found" and asks whether to generate the game files:
   press **Cross**. It takes a few seconds, and the game starts. The ROM is not
   needed again and can be deleted from the console.

If you already have an `sm64.o2r` made by Ghostship 3.0.0 on a PC, copy that
into the folder in place of the ROM.

If "Mario 64" does not appear on the home screen, look in
`/data/shadowmount/debug.log`. "AppInstallAll hook is no longer installed" means
ShadowMountPlus has to be restarted before it will register a new title.

## HD textures (optional)

The port takes Ghostship texture packs unchanged. The one tried on the console is
**SM64 Reloaded** by GhostlyDark:

- Project: <https://github.com/GhostlyDark/SM64-Reloaded>
- Downloads: <https://github.com/GhostlyDark/SM64-Reloaded/releases/latest>

**1. Download the Ghostship version of the pack.** On the releases page, take the
file whose name contains `gs-o2r`:

| File | Size | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sm64-reloaded-v2.6.0-gs-o2r-hd.7z` | 99 MB | HD; the one used on the console |
| `sm64-reloaded-v2.6.0-gs-o2r-4k.7z` | 618 MB | 4K |

The other files on that page are for emulators and other ports and will not work.

**2. Unpack it.** It holds one `.o2r` file, for example
`SM64_Reloaded_v2.6.0_HD.o2r` (547 MB).

**3. Copy the `.o2r` to the console's `mods` folder:**

```text
/data/homebrew/PPSA99310/userdata/mods/SM64_Reloaded_v2.6.0_HD.o2r
```

The folder exists once the game has been started once.

**4. Switch the pack on in the menu.** Start the game, then:

1. Press the **touch pad** to open the menu.
2. Press **R1** once, to the **Enhancements** tab.
3. The **Graphics** section is the first one and is already selected (if another
   is, press **L2** until Graphics is).
4. Move down with the **d-pad** to **Use Alternate Assets**, under "Mods", and
   press **Cross** to tick it.
5. Press the **touch pad** to close the menu.

The setting is remembered. Untick the same box to go back to the original
textures. If the textures do not change when you tick the box, quit and start
the game again.

## Build

On Linux (on a Mac, in the Lima VM) with PS5_Vulkan, PS5_Mesa and PS5_PayloadSDK
beside this folder.

```sh
ps5/tools/vm.sh build            # from macOS; ps5/tools/build.sh inside the VM
ps5/tools/vm.sh assets           # ghostship.o2r, Ghostship's own assets, into dist/
ps5/tools/vm.sh deploy
ps5/tools/vm.sh run
```

`build.sh` runs `setup-source.sh` first, which applies the console's changes to
`vendor/ghostship` and its two submodules from `ps5/patches/` (every hunk behind
`__PROSPERO__` or `PS5`). While changing anything under `vendor/`, run
`ps5/tools/setup-source.sh --save` before a build.

`ps5/tools/vm.sh assets ROM.z64` also makes `sm64.o2r` on this machine, into the
ignored `game/` folder, and `ps5/tools/vm.sh console-files` uploads it: the
quicker loop while developing.

What the console needed:

- **SDL2.** libultraship is written for SDL2; `ps5/sdl/` holds SDL2 video, audio
  and pad drivers for the console (`ps5/patches/sdl.patch` registers them).
- **Vulkan with no loader.** RADV is linked into the title, so libultraship's
  Vulkan renderer and Dear ImGui's reach it through volk. OpenGL is compiled out.
- **shaderc**, built from source: the renderer writes its shaders as GLSL at run
  time.
- **No working directory.** A title cannot `chdir`, `getcwd` or `realpath`;
  `ps5/src/shims.c` answers the last two for `std::filesystem`.
- **The log.** A flush for every line made the ROM's conversion take twenty
  minutes; errors are flushed at once, the rest every two seconds.
- **The menu with a pad alone**: see Status.

`GHOSTSHIP_PS5_FPS=1` in `/data/homebrew/PPSA99310/env.txt` writes the frame
rate to the console's log every ten seconds.

## Licence

GPL-3.0 for the repository as a whole and for a built title: see
[`LICENSING.md`](LICENSING.md). No game data is stored here or built in.
"Mario" and "Super Mario 64" are Nintendo's; this project is not affiliated with
Nintendo, HarbourMasters or Sony Interactive Entertainment.
