latestRelease.body:
## Fixed

- The game no longer slows down the longer you play. The Vulkan renderer created new command buffers every frame and never freed them, so each frame took a little longer than the last, and after about ten minutes the slowdown was easy to see. It now reuses the same buffers, so the frame rate stays steady however long you play.

## Install

- Copy the folder `PPSA99310` from the zip over your existing `/data/homebrew/PPSA99310/`. Your ROM, converted game data, saves, settings and texture packs stay where they are.
- New install: see the [README](https://github.com/griches/PS5_Ghostship#install). You need your own Super Mario 64 ROM (US or JP, `.z64`).

repos.name: PS5_SwitchWaker
repos.description: The Wind Waker (GameCube) for PlayStation 5 homebrew: SwitchWaker on the PS5 Vulkan stack. No game data included.
repos.readme:
# Wind Waker (GameCube) for PlayStation 5

[![stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/griches/PS5_SwitchWaker?style=flat)](https://github.com/griches/PS5_SwitchWaker/stargazers)
[![release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/griches/PS5_SwitchWaker)](https://github.com/griches/PS5_SwitchWaker/releases/latest)
[![licence](https://img.shields.io/badge/licence-GPL--3.0%20as%20built-blue)](LICENSING.md)

A PS5 homebrew port of [SwitchWaker](https://github.com/centollOS/SwitchWaker), the
native port of the 2002 GameCube game (USA disc `GZLE01`, revision 0) compiled
from its decompilation and drawn with [Aurora](https://github.com/encounter/aurora).
It is laid out like [PS5_Dusklight](https://github.com/griches/PS5_Dusklight) and
uses the same console layer: Aurora on Dawn's WebGPU on RADV, from the
[PS5 Vulkan](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Vulkan) stack.

The build reads no disc and holds no game data: SwitchWaker's runtime-assets
mode compiles against stub headers and fills them from the player's own disc
image when the title starts.

## Status

**Runs on the console.** First run on 2026-10-12 on a PS5 at 3840x2160: the
title screen, name entry, the prologue and Outset, at 60 images a second
(frame interpolation; the game's logic stays at 30), with the DualSense's
symbols on the HUD. Played on the console as far as the forest on Outset, the
scenes that follow it, and the boss room of Dragon Roost Cavern; nothing else
has been seen there.

**[Version 1.0.3](https://github.com/griches/PS5_SwitchWaker/releases/tag/v1.0.3)** fixes a crash in Dragon Roost Cavern, in the rooms with
the hanging platforms. [Version 1.0.2](https://github.com/griches/PS5_SwitchWaker/releases/tag/v1.0.2) fixed a crash when the boss of Dragon
Roost Cavern appears, and stopped the whole class of fault behind it (an
integer division by zero) from ending the game anywhere else. [Version 1.0.1](https://github.com/griches/PS5_SwitchWaker/releases/tag/v1.0.1)
fixed a stop on a black screen at the end of the forest scene. See
[Development](#development) for what
they were. Copy the [new release](https://github.com/griches/PS5_SwitchWaker/releases/latest) over the old folder; saves carry on.

A release is the title's folder with no game in it: the player copies their own `GZLE01` disc image (`.iso`, `.gcm` or `.ciso`) into
`/data/homebrew/PPSA99309/` beside `eboot.bin`, and the title finds it (the
first one in its folder, then on a USB drive).

| Area | State |
| --- | --- |
| Disc | Found in the title's folder; a `.iso` and a `.ciso` have both been run on the console; `.gcm` has not. A missing or wrong disc closes the title with a console notification (the close is seen working; the notification's text has not been read on a television yet) |
| Picture | 16:9. The output is 3840x2160 unless the options menu's "Output resolution" says 2560x1440 or 1920x1080 (applied at the next start); the console scales it to the television. "Internal resolution" follows it ("Window size") or is fixed, which dynamic resolution needs |
| 60 fps | Held at 3840x2160 in the scenes above, by the frame counter on screen. Not measured over a long session |
| Shaders | A first start with no cache compiled 3,056 render pipelines in about 12 minutes. The title now ships the caches a console produced (`ps5/shader-cache`) and copies them into place when the console has none: the same start then compiles nothing. They must be taken from a console again after a change to Dawn, the driver or the shaders |
| Button prompts | The HUD shows Cross (A), Square (B), Circle (X), Triangle (Y), R1 for Z, R2 for R and a right stick for the C stick (`ps5/art/make-glyphs.py`, [Kenney's CC0 Input Prompts](https://kenney.nl/assets/input-prompts)). The options menu's hints name the DualSense's buttons. Not done: the button pictures inside message text (they are in the game's font). With an HD texture pack the pack's buttons are drawn instead: see [Button symbols with a pack](#hd-textures-optional) |
| Options menu | The touch pad's click opens it |
| Saves, settings | `/data/homebrew/PPSA99309/user/`; the first start asks to create a save file, as the game does on an empty memory card |
| HD textures | A Dolphin texture pack the player supplies replaces the game's textures (on when a pack is in `user/hd_textures`, off otherwise; see [HD textures](#hd-textures-optional)). Seen working on the console with Hypatia's pack on Outset and in its forest. The pack has an optional PlayStation button set for the HUD |
| Sound | Not checked by ear in this log |
| DevLoop | `devloop-shot` and `devloop-quit` in the title's folder (registered as `windwaker-gc`); the shot answers once the game's loop runs |
| Art | The icon and background are the port's own, cel-shaded, made with an image generator (`ps5/art/`) |

Controls: left stick to move, right stick for the camera (the C stick), Cross A,
Square B, Circle X, Triangle Y, R1 Z, L2 L, R2 R, Options START. The buttons are
mapped by position, where the GameCube pad has them around A, so the HUD's
symbols sit where the buttons do on the DualSense: the sword is on Square.
The symbol of an empty item slot sits in the middle of its bubble.

## Install

Download `WindWaker-PS5-vX.Y.Z.zip` from the
[latest release](https://github.com/griches/PS5_SwitchWaker/releases/latest) and
unpack it: it holds one folder, `PPSA99309`. (Or build that folder yourself, see
[Build](#build).) It contains no game data.

**What the console needs**

- A PS5 that runs homebrew, with etaHEN (or an equivalent) loaded.
- ShadowMountPlus, which shows the folders in `/data/homebrew` as titles on the
  home screen.
- An FTP server on the console to copy files with (port 2121 here).

**Steps**

1. Unpack the release (or build: the result is the folder `dist/PPSA99309/`).
2. Copy that whole folder to the console as `/data/homebrew/PPSA99309/`, so that
   you have:

   ```text
   /data/homebrew/PPSA99309/eboot.bin
   /data/homebrew/PPSA99309/initial_pipeline_cache.db
   /data/homebrew/PPSA99309/sce_sys/      (param.json, icon0.png, pic0.dds, pic1.dds)
   /data/homebrew/PPSA99309/sce_module/libc.prx
   /data/homebrew/PPSA99309/res/          (button symbols and shader caches)
   /data/homebrew/PPSA99309/licenses/
   ```

   Copy `sce_sys/icon0.png` with the first upload: ShadowMountPlus will not
   register a title without its icon.
3. Copy your disc image into the same folder, under any name ending in `.iso`,
   `.gcm` or `.ciso`:

   ```text
   /data/homebrew/PPSA99309/your-disc.iso
   ```

   It has to be there or on a USB drive, not elsewhere in `/data`: a title can
   only see its own folder. The game takes the first image it finds.
4. Wait a few seconds for "Wind Waker" to appear on the home screen, and start
   it. The first start asks to create a save file.

With no disc image, or one that is not the supported disc, the title closes and
the console shows a notification that says why.

Saves and settings are written to `/data/homebrew/PPSA99309/user/`. Copying a new
build over the folder leaves them, and the disc image, alone.

**The disc image.** Dump your own copy of the game
([how](https://wiki.dolphin-emu.org/index.php?title=Ripping_Games)). Only the USA
disc, `GZLE01` revision 0, is supported. If your dump is RVZ or another compressed
format, convert it to `.iso` with [Dolphin](https://dolphin-emu.org/) first.

## HD textures (optional)

The game's textures are the GameCube's, made for a 480-line picture. A texture
pack replaces them with redrawn, larger ones as the game draws them; nothing in
the game itself changes, and the option can be turned on and off while playing.
The port reads packs made for the [Dolphin](https://dolphin-emu.org/) emulator
for the USA disc (`GZLE01`). No pack comes with the title: each is its author's
own work, and you download it yourself.

The pack tried here is **Hypatia's "WWHD Mod" v2.0001a**, about 5,700 textures
covering most of the game. Its downloads are in the first post of
[its thread on the Dolphin forum](https://forums.dolphin-emu.org/thread-55004.html).
Take **"PC DDS Half Size"** (a `.7z` of 850 MB, 2.5 GB unpacked), which is the
one used here:
[direct download from the author's Google Drive mirror](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1qBK8YOeSAwLpNP3NUkwcXgvUnQPKlgj7/view?usp=sharing)
(`Hypatia WWHD Mod v2.0001a (DDS-Half).7z`). The port reads it as it is. The full-size one is four times larger for a picture that is hard
to tell apart, and the PNG one is not suitable.

1. Unpack the `.7z` on a computer. Inside is a folder `GZL`.
2. Copy what is **inside** `GZL` (the folders `Characters`, `Environments`,
   `HUD` and so on) to the console, into
   `/data/homebrew/PPSA99309/user/hd_textures/`. Create that folder if it is
   not there. Over FTP the 5,700 files take about ten minutes.
3. Start the game. A pack found in that folder is used from the start; the
   options menu (the touch pad's click) has Graphics > "HD textures" to turn it
   off and on, and remembers what you chose.

With no pack in that folder the option does nothing.

Seen on the console on 2026-10-12 with that pack: Outset at 3840x2160 and 60
images a second with the textures replaced, and its forest. Not played further
than that.

**Button symbols with a pack.** The pack replaces the HUD's buttons as well, with
its own GameCube ones, so the DualSense's symbols this port draws are lost while
it is on. To have PlayStation buttons with the pack, also copy the `HUD` folder
from its `-[Optional Textures]-/[HUD] Controller Buttons - Playstation` over
the `HUD` folder in `hd_textures`, replacing files: those label the buttons by
position, as this port maps them (Cross where A is, Square for B, Circle for X,
Triangle for Y). The button pictures inside message text stay the GameCube's
either way.

## Development

To try a change without the console:

```sh
cmake -S vendor/switchwaker/native -B build/native-mac -G Ninja \
    -DFETCHCONTENT_SOURCE_DIR_AURORA=$PWD/.deps/aurora -DCOS_AURORA_PREPATCHED=ON \
    -DCOS_RECOMPCORE_DIR=$PWD/.deps/recompcore \
    -DCOS_RUNTIME_ASSETS=ON -DCOS_ASSETS_DIR=$PWD/.deps/assets/GZLE01
ninja -C build/native-mac switchwaker
COS_BUILD_DIR=$PWD/build/native-mac COS_DISC=/path/to/GZLE01.iso COS_FPS60=1 \
    COS_BUTTON_GLYPHS=$PWD/ps5/art/glyphs vendor/switchwaker/native/tools/run.sh run \
    --preset sailing --aspect 16:9 --frames 700 --shot 690
```

**Finding a fault on the console.** The game's own `[cos]` lines go to the
console's log (klog, port 3232) with the driver's. A `[dev]` section at the end
of `user/settings.ini` sets developer variables at the next start, for example
`COS_TRACE=scene,res` for every scene created and every file opened. A scene
change that stays in one step logs `scene-req-watch` lines every 300 calls: the
step, and the processes still waiting to be deleted.

The stop that 1.0.1 fixes was found that way. Some actors declare their methods
as returning `bool` and the game's process framework calls them as returning
`int` and compares with `TRUE`. On x86-64 the rest of the register is undefined,
so a delete could be refused for ever and the next scene never came; on ARM (the
Mac, the Switch) it does not show. The framework now reads only the low byte
([`f_pc_method.cpp` in the patch](ps5/patches/switchwaker.patch)). On the Mac, `COS_EVENT_SWEEP_FOLLOW=1` lets
`run.sh event-sweep` go on through a stage change an event asks for.

The crash that 1.0.3 fixes is a third one. A hanging platform of Dragon Roost
Cavern whose ropes were cut on an earlier visit is created with them cut, and
the rope points are simulated from values nothing has set. A NaN among them
reaches the arctangent table as an index: the conversion to an integer gives
0x80000000, which the GameCube's 32 bit address wraps back to the first entry
and x86-64 turns into a read 4 GB below the table. The lookup now gives the
first entry for a NaN or a ratio outside the table ([`c_math.cpp` in the patch](ps5/patches/switchwaker.patch)).
It was found from a player's photograph of the console's error message: the
two addresses in it, less the load address 0x400000, name `cM_atan2s` and
`himo_move` in the release's ELF.

The crash that 1.0.2 fixes is the same kind of difference. The boss of Dragon
Roost Cavern turns towards the player with a step count that is still zero the
first time, an integer division by zero: the GameCube and ARM give a quotient
and go on, x86-64 raises SIGFPE. The three helpers involved now give 0
([`c_lib.cpp` in the patch](ps5/patches/switchwaker.patch)), and so that the next one elsewhere is not a crash,
the title handles SIGFPE itself: it finishes the division as ARM does (quotient
0, remainder the dividend), logs `integer division fault` with the address, and
goes on. The console's code cannot be read at run time, so the build lists
every division instruction of the linked title in `res/div-table.bin`
([`make-div-table.py`](ps5/tools/make-div-table.py)) and the handler looks the address up; a fault
that is not in the list is still a crash with the console's record.
`COS_DIV_TEST=1` in `[dev]` divides by zero once at the start to check it. On
the Mac, `COS_SAVE_LOAD_WALK=<frames>` makes `run.sh save-load` walk forward
from a loaded save (`COS_CARD_DIR` names a card folder holding a player's
`.gci`).

`COS_TEXTURE_DUMPS=1` writes every texture drawn into the cache folder's
`texture_dumps`, named as a replacement for it must be named.

## Build

As PS5_Dusklight: on Linux (on a Mac, in the Lima VM) with PS5_Vulkan, PS5_Mesa
and PS5_PayloadSDK beside this folder.

```sh
ps5/tools/vm.sh build     # from macOS; ps5/tools/build.sh inside the VM
ps5/tools/vm.sh deploy
ps5/tools/vm.sh run
```

`build.sh` runs `setup-source.sh` first, which patches `vendor/switchwaker`
(`ps5/patches/switchwaker.patch`, every hunk behind `__PROSPERO__`) and fetches
into `.deps/` Aurora at SwitchWaker's pin with its patches, Dolphin's DSP HLE
sources and the stub asset headers. While changing `vendor/switchwaker`, run
`git -C vendor/switchwaker diff > ps5/patches/switchwaker.patch` before a build.

## Licence

GPL-3.0 for the repository as a whole and for a built title: see
[`LICENSING.md`](LICENSING.md). No game data is stored here or built in.

latestRelease.name: Wind Waker for PS5 v1.0.3
latestRelease.body:
## Fixed

- A crash in Dragon Roost Cavern, in the rooms with the hanging platforms. It showed as the game closing, or as an error message naming `SIGSEGV`, and was most likely to happen on coming back to a room after cutting a platform's ropes, including after loading a save. Thanks to the player who photographed the error message: the addresses in it were enough to find the cause.

This fix was made from that report and has not yet been confirmed on a console in that room. If the game still closes there, an issue with a photo of the error message is the quickest way to get it found.

## Updating

- Replace the folder `/data/homebrew/PPSA99309/` with the one in this zip, or copy the new files over it. Your disc image, saves, settings and texture pack in that folder are kept if you copy over it.
- Copy the whole folder, not only `eboot.bin`.
- Saves from earlier versions carry on working.

## Install (new)

- Unpack the zip and copy the folder `PPSA99309` to the console as `/data/homebrew/PPSA99309/`.
- Copy your own disc image (`.iso`, `.gcm` or `.ciso`) into that same folder, beside `eboot.bin`.
- Start "Wind Waker" from the home screen. The first start asks to create a save file.
- Full steps, controls and the HD texture pack: see the README.

## Known limits

- Played on a console only through Outset Island and into the boss room of Dragon Roost Cavern; other areas are untested there.
- Button pictures inside dialogue text still show the GameCube's buttons.
- With an HD texture pack on, the pack's own button pictures replace the DualSense symbols; Hypatia's pack has an optional PlayStation button set that matches this mapping (see the README).
- Only the USA disc is supported.

Unofficial; not affiliated with SwitchWaker, Nintendo or Sony Interactive Entertainment. No game data is included. Licence: GPL-3.0, sources in `SOURCE.txt` inside the zip.

repos.name: TacHen
repos.description: TacHen beta: native PS5 menu and phone/PC web UI. Compatibility preview covers 67 exact profiles from 1.00–13.60; added firmware is untested. Original Beta 1 retained.
repos.readme:
# TacHen

**Beta 3 — GoldHEN Plugin Support; 67 exact PS5 firmware profiles from 1.00 to 13.60, including 11.40.**

The original **Beta 1 ELF remains available unchanged**. The separate compatibility ELF adds public offset tables; the added firmware support is **untested on hardware**. Firmware below 11.00 is theoretical compatibility, not a confirmed working claim.

TacHen brings a native controller menu and a console-hosted web interface with layouts for both phones and PCs together for payloads, packages, games, plugins, cheats, saves and file transfers.

## Download and start

1. Download from [Releases](https://github.com/GronedWaffel/TacHen/releases/latest): **TacHen-compatibility.elf** for the expanded firmware preview, or **TacHen.elf** for the unchanged original Beta 1 (11.00–13.60, excluding 11.40). Choose one ELF.

2. Reboot and jailbreak your PS5. Send the ELF with your payload sender or load it through your existing payload loader.

3. Wait for the startup notification, then hold **L3 + R3** to open TacHen. **Circle** goes back; L3 + R3 closes the menu.

4. For the web interface, open **http://YOUR-PS5-IP:8780** in your phone or PC browser on the same network. The layout automatically adapts to the screen: a mobile layout on phones and a desktop layout on PCs.

TacHen is a post-jailbreak payload, not an exploit. Use a fresh boot when replacing an already-running TacHen build. This release ELF selects its bundled runtime so an older saved update cannot replace the build you just downloaded.

## GoldHEN Plugin Support

Beta 3 introduces a compatibility bridge for GoldHEN plugin process-information and memory operations on PS5. Download **TacHen-compatibility.elf** for this update; the preserved original `TacHen.elf` does not include it. Import your plugin under Plugins, register its matching game/version, and load it once you are in the game.

**Initial compatibility:** the adapter currently recognizes the official Havana 1.2 `rdr3Payload_132.sprx`; a community tester reported it working without errors on PS5 13.42 with RDR2 1.32. Other GoldHEN plugins still need compatible API coverage and validation. See [the plugin compatibility notes](docs/PRX-CONTAINER-COMPATIBILITY.md).

## Features

- **Payloads:** download from a direct link, manage Downloads, load an ELF from console storage or USB, and set startup order/delays. Selecting an ELF in storage checks and loads it without extra confirmation screens.

- **Packages:** install directly from USB or console storage, manage downloaded packages, and receive packages through DPI v2. Local packages are read from their source rather than copied to the internal drive first. Keep the source drive connected until installation finishes.

- **Games:** browse installed and ShadowMount games, launch, mount and unmount, with automatic status refresh.

- **Plugins:** import and register `.plugin` and `.prx` modules for the intended game/version. It is recommended to start plugins only after you are in the game. Module compatibility depends on the plugin and exact game build.

- **Cheats:** import supported JSON, SHN/XML and MC4 files, or download the etaHEN/GoldHEN catalogs. Opening Cheats selects a matching pack for the running title and version; otherwise it opens the normal library. Cheats are enabled individually, never automatically by opening the page.

- **Saved games:** browse saves and export backups to USB or the FTP share.

- **Transfers:** view progress and use a two-pane file browser to copy files and folders between console storage and USB.

- **Display:** FPS and other game telemetry, optional IP display, dashboard title IDs and game versions, plus the dashboard Cheats action.

- **Phone, PC and tools:** a console-hosted website with mobile and desktop layouts, FTP share, and the MCP interface for compatible tools.

The built-in FTP share is on **port 2122**, rooted at `/data/tachen/share`; use `tachen` or `anonymous` with any password on your trusted local network. DPI v2 uses **port 12800** when enabled in Packages.

## Firmware and beta status

The compatibility ELF recognizes these exact versions; versions between listed entries are not implied:

- **1.xx:** 1.00, 1.01, 1.02, 1.05, 1.10, 1.11, 1.12, 1.13, 1.14.
- **2.xx:** 2.00, 2.20, 2.25, 2.26, 2.30, 2.50, 2.70.
- **3.xx:** 3.00, 3.10, 3.20, 3.21.
- **4.xx:** 4.00, 4.02, 4.03, 4.50, 4.51.
- **5.xx:** 5.00, 5.02, 5.10, 5.50.
- **6.xx:** 6.00, 6.02, 6.50.
- **7.xx:** 7.00, 7.01, 7.20, 7.40, 7.60, 7.61.
- **8.xx:** 8.00, 8.20, 8.40, 8.60.
- **9.xx:** 9.00, 9.05, 9.20, 9.40, 9.60.
- **10.xx:** 10.00, 10.01, 10.20, 10.40, 10.60.
- **11.xx:** 11.00, 11.20, 11.40, 11.60.
- **12.xx:** 12.00, 12.02, 12.20, 12.40, 12.60, 12.70.
- **13.xx:** 13.00, 13.20, 13.40, 13.42, 13.60.

**Testing status:** the 53 added profiles, including **11.40** and every listed firmware **below 11.00**, have not been hardware-tested with TacHen. Their public tables cover the required offsets and have been checked against pinned upstream sources. They should theoretically work, but that is not a guarantee that startup, the menu, plugins, packages, saves or every bundled component works on each version. No 14.00+ profile is included.

The original Beta 1 targeted 14 profiles on 11.00–13.60 excluding 11.40. Testers reported no known issues at its release; this was not an exhaustive per-firmware, game or plugin test matrix. **That report does not apply to the new compatibility build.** Original offsets and the published Beta 1 ELF are unchanged.

Compatibility builds keep their update selection in `/data/tachen/updates-compatibility`, separate from Beta 1's `/data/tachen/updates`. Both use the same normal settings and library. Reboot before switching ELFs; do not try to run both at once. Neither ELF performs a jailbreak or creates an exploit entry point for a firmware.

Please report the exact firmware, ELF/build identity, feature, game/version and reproduction steps. Capture instructions are in [the diagnostics guide](docs/SUPPORT-CAPTURES.md). The [firmware notes](docs/FIRMWARE-COMPATIBILITY.md) explain the sources, validation and limitations.


## Build and source

TacHen is GPL-3.0-or-later. Source is available in this repository and in the release source archive. See [BUILDING.md](BUILDING.md) for toolchain and dependency inputs. Release assets include checksums, build metadata and a third-party source bundle. Historical engineering notes live in [docs/DEVELOPMENT-NOTES.md](docs/DEVELOPMENT-NOTES.md).

## Credits

Thanks to the community testers and the authors whose work makes this possible: John Törnblom and the PS5 Payload SDK/libelfldr/libNineS contributors; LightningMods, etaHEN and OnionHEN contributors; EchoStretch and the kstuff contributors; Drakmor and ShadowMountPlus contributors; PLK and Payload Manager contributors; GoldHEN and cheat authors; ciss84; and the authors of the bundled open-source libraries.

TacHen's menu and workflows are its own; bundled components and adapted code retain their original authorship and licenses. See [NOTICE.md](NOTICE.md) for detailed attribution and provenance.

latestRelease.name: TacHen Beta 3 — GoldHEN Plugin Support | 1.00–13.60 Compatibility Preview
latestRelease.body:
## GoldHEN Plugin Support

**Download `TacHen-compatibility.elf` for this update.** Beta 3 introduces a compatibility bridge for GoldHEN plugin process-information and memory operations on PS5. It preserves the original plugin upload and applies complete game-hook writes through the adapter.

Reboot and jailbreak, load TacHen, then import/register your plugin for its matching game and version. Load plugins after entering the game. Do not load another HEN alongside TacHen.

**Initial compatibility:** the adapter currently recognizes the official Havana 1.2 `rdr3Payload_132.sprx`. A community tester reported it working without errors on PS5 13.42 with RDR2 1.32; this release contains the exact tested ELF. Other GoldHEN plugins are not yet covered by this adapter. [Compatibility details](https://github.com/GronedWaffel/TacHen/blob/main/docs/PRX-CONTAINER-COMPATIBILITY.md).

## Choose your ELF

- **TacHen-compatibility.elf:** Beta 3 with initial GoldHEN plugin support and the same 67 exact firmware profiles from 1.00 through 13.60 as Beta 2, including 11.40.
- **TacHen.elf:** preserved original Beta 1 for 11.00–13.60 excluding 11.40; it does **not** include the GoldHEN compatibility bridge.

The 53 added firmware profiles remain untested with TacHen. Every listed firmware below 11.00 is theoretical compatibility; 11.40 is also untested. See the [exact firmware list and limitations](https://github.com/GronedWaffel/TacHen/blob/main/docs/FIRMWARE-COMPATIBILITY.md). No new firmware offsets changed in this update.

Hold **L3 + R3** for the menu. The console-hosted website at `http://YOUR-PS5-IP:8780` supports **phones and PCs**. Use one ELF after a fresh jailbreak. TacHen does not provide a jailbreak entry point.

## Validation, source and credits

- **560 automated tests passed**, including execution of the native bridge, adapted SDK call, complete hook write, error handling and timeout behavior.
- Published ELF SHA-256: `54f0e98c3903086dc11c52609be7da1cf7024527aeaaf2162de49ec77049232f`.
- `TacHen-compatibility-source.zip` and GitHub's automatic source archives contain the new source. `TacHen-source.zip` matches the preserved original Beta 1 ELF. Build inputs, third-party sources, firmware references and checksums are included.
- The source package version remains beta.2 to preserve the exact tested build identity; this published release is Beta 3. The release manifest records the matching source commit and fingerprint.

Credit to 0x199 and illusion for Havana; SiSTRo and the GoldHEN SDK contributors for the documented plugin API; OpenGoldHEN contributors for additional behavioral references; and the PS5 Payload SDK, etaHEN, kstuff, ShadowMountPlus, Payload Manager and other authors listed in NOTICE.md. The compatibility bridge is TacHen code, not a redistribution of Havana or the reconstructed GoldHEN implementation.

repos.name: PKG-Master
repos.description: A tool for PS4/PS5 games that allows you to seemlessly convert files (example: eboot.bin -> eboot.elf) making it easier to use them with AnyPS5 and other project whilst not having to worry about encryption with ShadPKG (ShadPS4 support soon)
repos.readme:
# PKG Master

A minimal app for PS4/PS5 game files **you dumped legally yourself**.
It supports decrypting ps4 games through ShadPKG and setups AnyPS5 for you, turns
the game's executable (eboot.bin) into a standard .ELF file, unpacks packages, and can run a
decrypted PS5 game through [AnyPS5](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5).

**[⬇ Download the latest release](https://github.com/Guernica4u/PKG-Master/releases/latest)**:
unzip it and run `pkgmaster-gui.exe`. Nothing to install.

> Windows may say "Windows protected your PC" because the app isn't
> code-signed. Click **More info → Run anyway**.

## What it does

| Button | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| **Open file…** | Open a `.pkg`, or a single `eboot.bin` / `.prx` / `.sprx` / `.elf`. You can also drag a file onto the window or onto the `.exe`. |
| **Open folder…** | Open a decrypted game folder: a PS4/PS5 dump (the one holding `eboot.bin` or `eboot.elf`, `sce_module/` and `sce_sys/`) or a PS3 dump (with `PS3_GAME/` or `PARAM.SFO` and `USRDIR/`). Other folders are listed so you can click through them: a folder with a single `.pkg` opens it, and a folder with a single subfolder steps into it. |
| **⬅ / ⟳** | Back to what you had open before (like a browser), or reload what's open. |
| **Run shadPKG (PS4)…** | Shown for an open PS4 `.pkg`: runs your own `shadpkg.exe` on it (see [shadPKG](#shadpkg)). |
| **📚 Library** | Your saved games as icon tiles. Press **☆** next to a game's title to save it; games you run in AnyPS5 or RPCS3 are added for you. Click a tile to open the game (with **Start games when you open them from the Library** on in ☰ Settings, it also starts: PS5 games with an AnyPS5 run folder run `app.exe`, PS3 games start in RPCS3); right-click for **Open game files**, **Show in Explorer** and **Remove from Library**. See [Library](#library). |
| **History** | Everything the app has written, with **Revert** and **Show in Explorer**. See [History](#history). |
| **Convert to ELF…** | Turns the selected file (by default `eboot.bin`) from Sony's SELF format into a standard ELF64, which is the file type AnyPS5 needs. Saves into a new `<name>-elf` folder next to the game files by default. |
| **Extract all files…** | Shown for an unlocked `.pkg`: unpacks everything inside it into a normal folder. |
| **Run in AnyPS5…** | For a decrypted PS5 game folder: converts the executables, runs your AnyPS5 relinker, and sets up a ready-to-run folder inside your AnyPS5 folder. **Launch** then starts the open game's own run folder, and **Copy log** copies everything it printed. If the game closes, the log folds away; if it crashes, the crash shows in red, with a warning when it happens within 15 seconds (the game may not be supported by AnyPS5). Hidden for PS4 and PS3 games, which AnyPS5 can't run. |
| **Run in RPCS3** | For a dumped PS3 game folder: starts it in your own [RPCS3](#rpcs3). |
| **☰** | **Settings…** (start games from the Library, hide the log, and where AnyPS5, RPCS3 and shadPKG are), **Open data folder** and **About PKG Master** (version and Check for updates). |
| **Passcode** | Only shown for encrypted fake/debug packages. Usually 32 zeros. |

**Right-click** any file in a list for **Convert to ELF**, **Show in
Explorer**, **Copy path** and **Delete** (which moves it to the Recycle Bin).
Files inside a `.pkg` are read-only, so those only get Convert and Copy path.

### Library

Saved games live in `%APPDATA%\PKG Master\library.json`, with a small copy of
each icon in `library-icons\`. The log under the buttons folds away when you
open a different game, and it can't be dragged over the Run / Launch buttons.

### Updates

When a new version is out, PKG Master tells you when it starts. **Update now**
downloads it from this repo's releases, checks it against GitHub's SHA-256,
replaces the program and restarts it. Your settings, history, `shadpkg` and
`AnyPS5` folders are left alone. **Skip this version** stops it asking about
that release. If the app's folder can't be written to, it points you to the
download page instead.

### History

Every Convert, Extract, shadPKG and AnyPS5 run is recorded. If something was
already at the save location, the app backs it up first. **Revert** deletes
what the app wrote and puts the old version back. A failed operation is rolled
back automatically, so it never leaves half-written files. The history is kept
between sessions in `%APPDATA%\PKG Master\`; **Clear history** deletes the
backups to free the space.

### AnyPS5

[AnyPS5](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5) turns **PS5** games (title IDs
starting with `PPSA`) into Windows programs. It isn't included. The first time
you press an AnyPS5 button, PKG Master explains how to get it, and its
**Download for me** button fetches the official release from AnyPS5's GitHub
page, checks it against GitHub's SHA-256, unpacks it into an `AnyPS5` folder
next to `pkgmaster-gui.exe` (or `%LOCALAPPDATA%\PKG Master\AnyPS5` if that
folder can't be written to) and sets it up. **Cancel** stops the download.

To set it up by hand instead:

1. Unzip AnyPS5's `prx-windows-v….zip` (the folder with `libs/`) and put its
   `relinker….exe` in the same folder.
2. In PKG Master, click **AnyPS5 folder…** (or **Run in AnyPS5…**), then
   **I have it, pick the folder…** and choose that folder. Any `.exe` with
   "relinker" in its name is found automatically.
3. Click **Run in AnyPS5…**, then **Launch**.

PS4 games (`CUSA…`) aren't supported by AnyPS5, so the AnyPS5 buttons are
hidden for them. AnyPS5 is early software and only a few games work so far.

When AnyPS5 puts out a newer release than the one you have, an **Update AnyPS5**
button appears under the AnyPS5 row. It downloads the new release into a new
folder next to your current one (your old run folders stay where they are) and
switches to it.

### RPCS3

PS3 discs are encrypted with a key for each disc, so PKG Master works from
games you dumped on your own PS3 (custom firmware copies them off the disc
already decrypted). Open the dumped folder and press **Run in RPCS3**: PKG
Master starts your [RPCS3](https://rpcs3.net) with `--no-gui` on the game's
`USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN`. RPCS3 isn't included. The first time, PKG Master offers
**Download for me**, which gets RPCS3's official Windows build from its GitHub
releases (checked against GitHub's SHA-256) into an `rpcs3` folder next to
`pkgmaster-gui.exe`, or you can pick a `rpcs3.exe` you already have.

RPCS3 also needs the PS3 system software, which PlayStation gives away on its
[PS3 system software page](https://www.playstation.com/en-us/support/hardware/ps3/system-software/).
PKG Master explains the steps when it's missing: download `PS3UPDAT.PUP`, then
in RPCS3 choose **File > Install Firmware**. Convert to ELF isn't available for
PS3 games; RPCS3 runs them as they are.

### shadPKG

The **Run shadPKG (PS4)…** button runs [shadPKG](https://github.com/seregonwar/ShadPKG),
which isn't part of PKG Master and isn't included in the download.
Download `shadPKG.exe` from its
[official releases](https://github.com/seregonwar/ShadPKG/releases) and drop
it in the empty **`shadpkg`** folder next to `pkgmaster-gui.exe`. If it's
missing, the button tells you this and links to the download.

## What it won't do

- **No Sony keys are included, and retail packages can't be decrypted.**
  Packages from the PlayStation Store or a disc are encrypted with console
  keys. The legal route is to dump the game on your own console, which writes
  out the files already decrypted; PKG Master works from there.
- Encrypted or broken input fails with a clear message. The app never writes
  a plausible-looking but wrong file.

Use it only on games you own and are allowed to dump where you live.

## Building from source

The app is Rust (in [`app/`](app/)); the original command-line tool is
Python (in [`pkgmaster/`](pkgmaster/)). Both read the same formats and produce
byte-identical output, which [`app/tests/parity.py`](app/tests/parity.py)
checks.

```bash
# Desktop app (needs Rust, MSVC toolchain on Windows)
cd app
cargo build --release          # target/release/pkgmaster-gui.exe and pkgmaster-cli.exe
cargo test

# Python tool
python -m venv .venv
.venv/Scripts/pip install -e ".[dev]"
.venv/Scripts/python -m pytest -q
python app/tests/parity.py     # Rust vs Python, byte for byte
```

### Command line

`pkgmaster-cli.exe` (in the release zip) covers the basics:

```bash
pkgmaster-cli info    game.pkg [--passcode P]
pkgmaster-cli list    game.pkg
pkgmaster-cli convert game.pkg eboot.elf [--path sce_module/libc.prx]
pkgmaster-cli extract game.pkg out/
```

The Python tool (`pip install -e .`, then `pkgmaster --help`) has more:
`info`, `entries`, `list`, `tree`, `extract`, `convert` and `elf`, with
`--json` output. Exit codes: `0` ok, `2` bad file, `3` passcode needed or
wrong, `4` not supported yet.

### Formats supported

| | |
| --- | --- |
| PS4 `\x7FCNT` and PS5 `\x7FFIH` packages | yes |
| PFS filesystem, all three inode layouts | yes |
| Passcode-encrypted PFS (AES-XTS) | yes |
| PFSC-compressed files | yes |
| SELF → ELF (plaintext segments) | yes |
| Retail decryption | no, by design |

Format details are documented in [`HANDOFF.md`](HANDOFF.md).

## License

PKG Master is under the [MIT license](LICENSE). shadPKG and AnyPS5 are
separate projects with their own licenses; neither is included.

## Credits

Format details were cross-checked against
[LibOrbisPkg](https://github.com/maxton/LibOrbisPkg),
[orbis-pfs](https://github.com/videobitva/orbis),
[MkPFS](https://github.com/PSBrew/MkPFS),
[LibProsperoPKG](https://github.com/SvenGDK/LibProsperoPKG) and
[ps4_unfself](https://github.com/SocraticBliss/ps4_unfself). No third-party
code was copied. The app icon is egui's logo, from
[egui/eframe](https://github.com/emilk/egui) (MIT/Apache-2.0). AnyPS5 is by
[boykopovar and contributors](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5).

repos.name: ps5-linux-porting
repos.description: Evidence-driven notes and tools for porting the PS5 Linux loader across firmware
repos.readme:
# PS5 Linux Porting

This repository records the work needed to boot Linux on newer retail PS5
firmware, with firmware 11.60 as the active case study. It contains research
notes, hardware evidence, tester guides, and validation tools. Linux images,
loader binaries, and release downloads live in the linked source repositories.

This is not a Linux distribution, jailbreak bundle, or ready-to-run payload
release. Everything here is experimental and can crash the console or damage
data on the Linux USB drive.

## Start here

| Goal | Link |
|---|---|
| Test the unified CachyOS Image 4 prerelease | [Download Image 4](https://github.com/gzimbric/ps5-linux-image/releases/tag/cachyos1160-k73-image-4) and follow the [Image 4 tester guide](docs/cachyos1160-k73-image-4-tester-guide.md); the exact image is CI-verified but not yet hardware-booted |
| Use the latest hardware-booted CachyOS image | [Download Image 3](https://github.com/gzimbric/ps5-linux-image/releases/tag/cachyos1160-k73-image-3) and follow the [Image 3 tester guide](docs/cachyos1160-k73-image-3-tester-guide.md) |
| Boot the hardware-tested Ubuntu pair | [Ubuntu 24.04 tester guide](docs/ubuntu2404-tester-guide.md) |
| Test the older public CachyOS prerelease | [Image 2 tester guide](docs/cachyos1160-k73-image-2-tester-guide.md) |
| Read the complete 11.60 result | [Firmware 11.60 status](docs/11.60-status.md) |
| Review the sanitized hardware records | [Evidence index](evidence/README.md) |

## Current 11.60 status

Linux, wired SSH, and physical HDMI output have been observed on one regular
CFI-1115B running firmware 11.60. Run 15 remains the loader and display
baseline. Ubuntu and CachyOS have both booted through the upstream
`ps5-linux-loader` architecture with the Sonic-derived 11.60 display path.

Current gaming work is based on CachyOS and Linux 7.3 with rmux's PS5 patch
set. Keep these artifact boundaries separate:

| Area | Current evidence |
|---|---|
| Loader, HDMI, and SSH | Passed on the tested CFI-1115B. Other models and repeated cold-boot coverage remain open. |
| Ubuntu 24.04 build 3 | The exact CI image and DMA E820 loader pair booted once with visible HDMI, SSH, and the guide's 12 GiB USB check. |
| Local CachyOS Image 3 base | One exact unpublished raw image booted with HDMI and SSH. Its in-image Bluetooth path paired a wireless DualSense and exposed buttons, motion, and touchpad input. |
| Image 3 Wi-Fi follow-up | A stable-MAC NetworkManager configuration resolved the Plasma menu failure on the running system; WPA3, DHCP, and HTTPS passed. This live change was not in the original raw image. |
| Image 3 desktop round trip | Live source changes made Steam's **Switch to Desktop** action and the desktop shortcut back to Gaming Mode pass without compositor overlap. These changes were not in the original raw image. |
| Fan and clock policy | The published Image 3 service sends legacy servo pattern `3` before guarded GPU and CPU scaling. It does not force or measure maximum RPM; on the tested CFI-1115B the exposed target remained 86 °C. The tester guide applies and verifies a 65 °C target after every boot. With that hotfix active, a short bounded CPU load passed. |
| Public Image 3 prerelease | [Published for testing](https://github.com/gzimbric/ps5-linux-image/releases/tag/cachyos1160-k73-image-3) from source `16795eb` by successful workflow `39521098451`. Its exact downloadable artifact has now completed one identity-verified cold boot with HDMI, wired SSH, Plasma Wi-Fi, internal-Bluetooth DualSense input, both session directions and a 20-second bounded CPU load. |

The local hardware image and the public CI image have different raw-image
hashes. Their results remain separate. The downloadable prerelease now has its
own exact-image hardware result; the earlier local boot and live follow-ups are
still supporting evidence rather than substitutes for it.

Still pending for Image 3:

- two to four more cold boots and broader console coverage;
- Wi-Fi and DualSense reconnect after a cold boot;
- at least 60 minutes of concurrent Wi-Fi traffic and Bluetooth input;
- a later Steam Offline Mode test after the successful online bootstrap;
- a longer controlled load to assess thermal equilibrium and stability; and
- the performance opt-out, storage integrity, video decode, and longer
  stability checks in the tester guide.

## Downloads and tester guides

### Hardware-tested Ubuntu pair

Run 19 booted this exact pair once on the CFI-1115B:

- [Ubuntu 24.04 build 3 image](https://github.com/gzimbric/ps5-linux-image/releases/tag/ubuntu2404-1160-build-3)
- [Firmware 11.60 DMA E820 loader](https://github.com/gzimbric/ps5-linux-loader/releases/tag/firmware-11.60-dma-e820-run18)
- [Ubuntu 24.04 tester guide](docs/ubuntu2404-tester-guide.md)

### Public CachyOS Image 2 prerelease

Image 2 is public for testing, but no identity-verified boot of that exact
image is recorded. Its KDE Wi-Fi join and Steam desktop switch are known open
issues; the guide includes recovery steps.

- [CachyOS Image 2](https://github.com/gzimbric/ps5-linux-image/releases/tag/cachyos1160-k73-image-2)
- [Bounded 11.60 loader](https://github.com/gzimbric/ps5-linux-loader/releases/tag/firmware-11.60-dma-e820-bounded-run21)
- [Image 2 tester guide](docs/cachyos1160-k73-image-2-tester-guide.md)

### CachyOS Image 3

Image 3 is public as a tester prerelease. CI built and verified the one-file
archive, and that exact artifact has now completed one identity-verified cold
boot on the CFI-1115B. It remains a prerelease while repeated boots, cold
reconnect, coexistence soak, longer thermal/stability testing and the other
acceptance gates remain open. Keep its result separate from the earlier local
boot and live follow-ups.

- [CachyOS Image 3 public prerelease](https://github.com/gzimbric/ps5-linux-image/releases/tag/cachyos1160-k73-image-3)
- [Bounded 11.60 loader](https://github.com/gzimbric/ps5-linux-loader/releases/tag/firmware-11.60-dma-e820-bounded-run21)
- [Image 3 tester guide and acceptance gates](docs/cachyos1160-k73-image-3-tester-guide.md)
- [Image 3 CI, release and exact-image hardware evidence](evidence/11.60-cachyos-image3-ci.md)
- [Local Image 3 hardware evidence](evidence/11.60-cachyos-image3-local.md)

### Unified CachyOS Image 4 tester prerelease

Image 4 is one `linux-ps5 7.3.0-4` image for both Wi-Fi hardware paths. It
keeps the proven Marvell IW620 path and adds experimental MediaTek MT7921
support through the in-tree `mt7921e` driver. This is one image, not separate
Marvell and MediaTek editions. The loader still depends on the console's
hardware:

- IW620 consoles use `ps5-linux-loader-1160-dma-e820-bounded-wifi.elf`, which
  copies that console's own IW620 firmware to the USB drive.
- MediaTek consoles use `ps5-linux-loader-1160-dma-e820-bounded.elf`, because
  their required firmware is already packaged in the image.

The exact Image 4 artifact was built from `e82cefa` by successful hosted run
`39536824124`. CI verified the image, bounded-loader limits and single-file
archive, but no hardware boot has been recorded. MediaTek Wi-Fi has passed
source and structural checks, not a console test, and the MediaTek Bluetooth
path is unknown. Image 3 remains the newest CachyOS artifact with an
identity-verified hardware boot.

- [CachyOS Image 4 public tester prerelease](https://github.com/gzimbric/ps5-linux-image/releases/tag/cachyos1160-k73-image-4)
- [Image 4 tester guide and exact artifact identity](docs/cachyos1160-k73-image-4-tester-guide.md)
- [Bounded 11.60 loader prerelease](https://github.com/gzimbric/ps5-linux-loader/releases/tag/firmware-11.60-dma-e820-bounded-run21)

Image releases are published as one `.img.xz`. The build fails instead of
publishing numbered parts when the compressed image reaches the release size
limit.

## Before testing

- Use only a regular retail PS5 on firmware 11.60. Do not use a PS5 Pro or a
  different firmware.
- Flashing erases the selected USB drive. Confirm the whole device before
  writing an image.
- Use the exact image and loader pair named by its tester guide. Do not mix
  releases, older ELFs, boot files, or third-party root filesystems.
- Start from a full PS5 power-off. After Linux starts, do not use Linux suspend,
  hibernate, or GameOS Rest Mode; shut Linux down fully before another attempt.
- Keep wired Ethernet available as the diagnostic and SSH fallback.
- Gaming Mode to Plasma is not instant. After choosing **Switch to Desktop**,
  wait while Steam and Gamescope exit and Plasma starts. A clean measured pass
  took about 2.4 seconds, while an earlier transition that needed additional
  cleanup took about 27 seconds. Do not click repeatedly or power-cycle just
  because the transition takes several seconds.
- Published Image 3 can show **System policy prevents control of network
  connections** after returning to Plasma. The tester guide includes the
  targeted `steam`/NetworkManager Polkit hotfix; it is not part of the published
  image hash.
- Published Image 3 also leaves `systemd-networkd-wait-online` enabled even
  though NetworkManager owns the network. Its two-minute timeout does not mean
  Wi-Fi or Ethernet failed. The tester guide disables the unused waiter and
  clears its failed state; that cleanup is not part of the published hash.
- A fresh Image 3 build starts in Plasma so networking can be configured. Its
  first Gaming Mode setup needs internet; Offline Mode is a later-use test
  after Steam has saved the required account and game state.
- Published Image 3 needs the tester guide's 65 °C fan-target correction after
  every boot. The documented public range is 40-80 °C, lower values cool more
  aggressively, and Linux exposes no fan RPM or tachometer reading.
- Never copy another image's prebuilt `btusb.ko`. Bluetooth modules must be
  rebuilt for the exact kernel.
- The bounded Wi-Fi loader copies the console's own IW620 firmware to its USB.
  Never redistribute that firmware file. The Image 4 MediaTek path instead
  uses the bounded non-Wi-Fi loader and packaged MediaTek firmware;
  follow the [Image 4 tester guide](docs/cachyos1160-k73-image-4-tester-guide.md)
  rather than swapping loaders between chipset paths.
- Ubuntu starts with `ps5` / `ubuntu`; CachyOS uses `steam` / `steam`. Change
  the password immediately and keep the console on a trusted local network.

## Technical evidence

| Topic | Document |
|---|---|
| Full current result and evidence limits | [Firmware 11.60 status](docs/11.60-status.md) |
| Image 3 public CI artifact | [Image 3 CI, release and exact-image hardware evidence](evidence/11.60-cachyos-image3-ci.md) |
| Image 4 unified CI artifact | [Image 4 CI, release and unbooted hardware boundary](evidence/11.60-cachyos-image4-ci.md) |
| Image 3 local boot and live follow-ups | [Image 3 local evidence](evidence/11.60-cachyos-image3-local.md) |
| Historical CachyOS Linux 7.3 run | [Run 21 evidence](evidence/11.60-cachyos-k73-run-21.md) |
| Ubuntu CI image hardware boot | [Run 19 evidence](evidence/11.60-ubuntu-ci-run-19.md) |
| Display-port reconstruction history | [Sanitized run matrix](evidence/11.60-sonic-display-runs.md) |
| Remaining work | [Maintenance backlog](docs/maintenance-backlog.md) |
| Source and upstream revision pins | [Upstream references](docs/upstream-references.md) |
| Sonic's 13.60 artifact as a reference | [Sonic 13.60 binary reference](docs/sonic-13.60-reference.md) |

## Why this repository exists

A working hypervisor bypass is only one part of booting Linux. The loader also
has to preserve the bypass across rest and wake, stage the kernel and initrd,
move every CPU out of the hypervisor safely, install the memory map, and bring
up firmware-specific display and devices. Treating the port as a list of
offset substitutions caused many of the earlier failures; this repository
keeps the working path and the evidence for each boundary together.

## Repository map

| Path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `docs/` | Architecture, workflows, tester guides, current status, and upstream pins |
| `evidence/` | Sanitized hardware evidence without raw console data |
| `firmwares/` | Machine-readable firmware status manifests |
| `templates/` | Consistent hardware-run reports |
| `tools/` | Manifest, privacy, link, log, and media-validation helpers |

The canonical 11.60 loader source is on
[`gzimbric/ps5-linux-loader` `main`](https://github.com/gzimbric/ps5-linux-loader).
The image build source is on
[`gzimbric/ps5-linux-image` `main`](https://github.com/gzimbric/ps5-linux-image).

## Repository checks

Run the manifest, privacy, link, and unit checks with:

```sh
make check
```

To classify a locally captured 11.60 log without modifying it:

```sh
python3 tools/classify_1160_log.py /path/to/capture.log
```

## What is intentionally excluded

This repository does not contain:

- kernel or hypervisor images;
- decrypted firmware, console keys, or the IW620 Wi-Fi firmware;
- Linux disk images or release payloads;
- raw console logs, private network addresses, or local paths;
- built ELF, shellcode, or driver-module binaries; or
- loader and image source already maintained in the linked source repositories.

Hashes and small factual offsets are included only as provenance or validation

repos.name: Nuvio-maxd-releases
repos.description: Nuvio Max'd brings Nuvio to PS5 with synced watch progress, addon streams, episode skipping and experimental HDR10 playback. An unofficial native app, with public downloads and matching source.
repos.readme:
Nuvio Max'd

Your Nuvio library, profiles, addons and watch progress. On PS5.

Current release: 1.0.0.3
User guide · Downloads and release notes · Report a problem

Bring your Nuvio setup to the big screen. Sign in with your phone, choose a profile, browse addon catalogs and your saved library, and keep movie and episode progress in sync with your other Nuvio devices. The interface and integrated players run directly on the console; you do not need a PC running a companion server. **1.0.0.3 adds saved IPTV search, A–Z browsing and embedded chapters.** Search cached movie/show catalogs across your active profile’s IPTV providers, see provider-labelled results, and browse by initial. Supported files gain a Chapters playback-menu column and timeline markers. Playback reopen recovery, HEVC colour metadata fallback, artwork memory limits and subtitle/network library updates are included. Physical PS5 validation remains pending. See the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md) and [testing instructions](native-app/TESTING-1.0.0.3.md). | Feature | What you can do | | --- | --- | | **Live TV** | Add your own M3U playlist or Xtream Codes server; browse groups, search channels, and save favorites/recent selections separately for each profile. Lists support up to 100,000 channels / 128 MiB. EPG, recording and catch-up are not included; Xtream movies/shows use the separate IPTV Library tab. | | **IPTV Library** | A separate sidebar tab appears for VOD-capable Xtream accounts. Browse movie/show categories with A–Z navigation, search saved catalogs across the active profile’s providers, choose seasons/episodes and resume locally per profile. Saved catalogs survive provider outages. | | **Provider availability** | Guidance for server errors, missing titles, rejected access and request limits. Possible outages are distinguished from decoding failures. | | **Four-screen TV (experimental)** | Choose four SDR channels from Live TV’s sources/filters menu. D-pad focuses; Cross selects sound. Requires four provider connections; software previews are limited to 640×360. SD recommended. | | **Trailers** | Select Options → Watch trailer on movie/show details. Uses addon/TMDB metadata and supported public direct/YouTube formats; trailers do not update watch history or trackers. Some hosts/formats remain unavailable. | | **Anime skip timings** | Use AniSkip alongside IntroDB, with optional Anime-Skip client registration and conservative episode/timing validation. | | **Settings search** | Find settings by name, description or category and use their original controls. | | **Playback badges** | See resolution, HDR/SDR, selected audio channels, codecs and release types such as WEB-DL, Blu-ray and DVD-Rip. Actual playback facts override filename hints. | | **Recent sources** | See eligible cached sources while refreshing; Reload bypasses the bounded profile-specific session cache. | ## Library, profiles and sources | Feature | What you can do | | --- | --- | | **Phone sign-in** | Scan the QR code to link your Nuvio account and keep the login between launches. Guest use is also available. | | **Multiple profiles** | Choose, import or create up to six account profiles. Switch through **Settings → Account & Services → Profiles** after stopping playback. Account-backed PIN checks require a connection. | | **Separate profile data** | Keep history, resume positions, source lists and preferences scoped to the selected profile. Addon/plugin repository lists and watched history sync; individual scraper switches remain local. Inherited sources are read-only here. | | **Nuvio library and progress** | Browse saved titles and resume movies or episodes across devices using the same account and selected profile. Offline progress waits to sync when you reconnect. Guest progress stays on the PS5. | | **Tracking accounts** | Optional Trakt, SIMKL and MDBList connections with separate Library Source and Watch Progress selections; Nuvio remains default. Trakt phone pairing uses the bundled Max’d registration. SIMKL requires its own application configuration. | | **Standard addons** | Load enabled addons from your Nuvio setup or add a manifest URL, including setups using AIOMetadata and AIOStreams. Compatibility depends on the addon. | | **Provider plugins** | Add raw Nuvio JavaScript provider repository manifests and enable individual scrapers. Android DEX/CS3 plugins are not supported. | | **Catalogs and search** | Browse artwork, search titles, choose seasons and read episode descriptions with thumbnails and progress bars. | | **Stream selection** | Compare advertised resolution, HDR, language, codec, audio and file size; filter by addon. Your selection stays focused as results arrive. | | **Connected services** | Connect TorBox or Premiumize, or explicitly import supported connections from Nuvio Sync, to resolve cached original files. Optional background link preparation reduces waiting after selection. | | **Playback sources** | Play compatible direct/addon HTTP links. Peer-to-peer torrent playback is available separately and is off by default. | To use a provider repository, open **Settings → Addons → Add addon or plugin URL** and enter its raw `manifest.json` URL. Then select the repository on the **Addons** page and enable a provider. Providers start disabled; try one first. A GitHub directory URL is not a manifest. Some providers need unsupported APIs, extra configuration or browser challenges, so installing a repository does not guarantee streams. ## Video, audio and subtitles | Feature | What you get | | --- | --- | | **Native player by default** | Integrated playback for compatible H.264/HEVC and other supported media, with audio/subtitle track selection and playback details. | | **Optional EVO and VLC engines** | Choose **EVO Player 0.13.0** or **VLC 3.0.24** under **Settings → Video → Playback engine**. Both are experimental; the choice applies to the next stream. They retain their own compatibility limits. | | **Native-resolution GPU presentation** | Keep decoded picture dimensions, including compatible 4K sources, and convert YUV colour on the GPU. Source resolution is distinct from the actual HDMI signal. | | **Display choices** | Follow the configured PS5 resolution or choose an override. Request **60 Hz** or **Prefer 120 Hz** on compatible outputs; refresh changes require an app restart. | | **HDR choices** | Try experimental native HDR10 for compatible PQ/BT.2020 sources, or explicitly choose **Convert HDR to SDR**. Tone mapping preserves luminance and fits wide-gamut colours into SDR. HDR output needs console/TV confirmation. | | **Audio output** | Decoded PCM by default, with stereo or optional surround PCM. Auto/bitstream output for compatible AC-3, E-AC-3 and DTS core is experimental. TrueHD/DTS-HD remain decoded PCM. Keep surround off for optical stereo or TV speakers. | | **Volume and sync** | PCM volume/boost 50–300%, audio delay ±2 s and subtitle delay ±10 s. Set defaults in Settings or adjust from the playback Audio/Subtitles menu. Boost may clip loud peaks. | | **Preferred languages** | Set audio and subtitle language preferences. Automatic subtitles prefer suitable in-file tracks before addon subtitles; manual choices, including Off, are retained. | | **Subtitle rendering** | Styled ASS/SSA and bitmap/PGS subtitles, Unicode fallback fonts and text shaping. Adjust size, font, colour, outline/shadow, background and timing; style controls include previews. | | **Embedded chapters** | On supported files, open Options/Up, choose Chapters and press Cross to jump. Includes timeline markers and the current chapter name; requires at least two valid chapters. | | **Playback recovery** | Retain audio/subtitle choices, pause, audio sync and PCM gain after supported reopen operations. Recover missing HEVC colour tags without overriding explicit container metadata. VLC-owned HTTP failures retain authentication/cancellation instead of falling back to another access handler. | | **Seeking and buffering** | Set D-pad and shoulder-button seek intervals separately. Native/EVO read-ahead choices are 30, 60, 120 or 300 seconds. Seeking and network-recovery changes include HLS handling, with remaining engine-specific limits. | **EVO is an integrated video engine here, not the entire standalone EVO app.** Nuvio retains its interface and, for Native/EVO, its audio output, OpenGL renderer and HDR composition. Choosing EVO alone does not replace the complete output path. VLC is an optional integrated engine and still needs console testing. Native HDR10 can be rejected by the console/output combination. HDR10+ dynamic metadata, full Dolby Vision processing and forwarding source mastering metadata are not supported. A source's HDR/audio badges do not prove that the TV or receiver is receiving those formats. 120 Hz can improve film cadence but does not add motion interpolation or guarantee smooth playback. ## Watching and everyday use - **Skip Intro, Recap and Credits:** controller-button prompts appear when IntroDB supplies episode timings. Known post-credit scenes are preserved; missing timings leave playback unchanged. - **Next-episode autoplay:** prepare the next episode and offer a cancellable, adjustable countdown when a matching stream is ready. Pause/buffering holds the countdown, and autoplay can be turned off. - **Controller and Media Remote controls:** DualSense navigation plus supported PS5 Media Remote/HDMI-CEC navigation and playback controls. - **Organized settings:** Account & Services, Video, Audio, Subtitles, Playback, Appearance & Lighting, Addons, and App & Updates. - **Appearance and accessibility:** reduced motion, higher contrast, calmer backgrounds and optional interface sounds. These settings do not change video colours. - **Logo-inspired lighting:** a slow teal → white → pink/purple controller-light fade. Optional **Console light sync** follows it on supported systems, with approximate colours and a disable switch that restores the previous state. Unsupported systems leave console lighting unchanged. - **What's new:** a simple changelog after a version change, available again in Settings. - **Update reminders:** choose Homebrew Store, GitHub/manual, or Not sure as your install source. Reminders direct you to the appropriate update location; this is a saved choice, not automatic installer detection. - **In-app update checks:** check the public feed in Settings. Verified FFPFSC installation through the bundled helper is experimental; ZIP installs use manual replacement. Keep app data when updating. - **Playback diagnostics:** view log locations and collect playback, frame-timing, startup and crash information for troubleshooting. Remove tokens, passwords, authorization headers and stream URLs before sharing logs. - **Optional support:** a Ko-fi link and QR code in Settings. Donations are optional. ## What changed in 1.0.0.3 - A–Z IPTV browsing and provider-labelled search across saved movie/series catalogs. - Embedded chapter controls and timeline markers in Native, EVO and VLC. - Audio/subtitle reopen recovery and a conservative fallback for missing HEVC colour tags. - Bounded artwork queues, staging and cache metadata to reduce browsing memory pressure. - libass 0.17.5, curl 8.23.0, OpenSSL 3.5.9, JSON 3.12.0 and startup ordering maintenance. See [release notes](RELEASE_NOTES.md), [source](SOURCE.md) and [testing instructions](native-app/TESTING-1.0.0.3.md). ## Download and install You need a jailbroken PS5 and compatible homebrew payloads, including a suitable kstuff setup and [ShadowMount+](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus). Follow the loader's instructions for your firmware. The project targets firmware 9.00 and above where those tools work; coverage is incomplete and firmware below 9.00 needs further testing. Homebrew loader compatibility does not establish HDR/audio compatibility. | 1.0.0.3 download | Installation | | --- | --- | | [**PPSA99288.zip**](https://github.com/HandshakeHackin/Nuvio-maxd-releases/releases/download/v1.0.0.3-native-experimental/PPSA99288.zip) | Extract and copy the complete `PPSA99288/` folder into a location scanned by ShadowMount+, such as `/data/homebrew/`. The executable should be `/data/homebrew/PPSA99288/eboot.bin`, with no extra folder level. | | [**NuvioMaxd-1.0.0.3-native.ffpfsc**](https://github.com/HandshakeHackin/Nuvio-maxd-releases/releases/download/v1.0.0.3-native-experimental/NuvioMaxd-1.0.0.3-native.ffpfsc) | Place the image in a homebrew folder on storage scanned by ShadowMount+. | Use one installation format at a time. Close the app before replacing an image or folder, preserve your app data, and let ShadowMount+ finish scanning before launching. The title ID remains **PPSA99288**. Downloads include matching source, checksums and validation evidence. After launch, scan the account QR code or continue as Guest. For cross-device resume, use the same Nuvio account/profile on each device and select Nuvio Sync as the progress source on the other device. Configure addons normally; connect TorBox/Premiumize separately if you want their cached-file resolution. The [published-build user guide](https://github.com/HandshakeHackin/Nuvio-maxd-releases/blob/builds/v1.0.0.3/USER_GUIDE.md) covers controls, setup and troubleshooting. Check the version on the [ProsperoStore listing](https://prosperostore.net/app/PPSA99288/): catalog submission, maintainer approval and live deployment happen separately from a GitHub release. The 1.0 store update is prepared; [submit the prefilled catalog pull request](store/README.md) because the integration cannot create it upstream. ## Report a problem [Open an issue](https://github.com/HandshakeHackin/Nuvio-maxd-releases/issues) with your app version, firmware, playback engine, steps and expected/actual behavior. For provider-download failures, enable one provider, reproduce the problem and include the complete `provider: script download failed` log line. Shared logs must exclude credentials and stream URLs. Please reply to an existing matching issue rather than opening a duplicate. See the published [playback limits](https://github.com/HandshakeHackin/Nuvio-maxd-releases/blob/builds/v1.0.0.3/source/native-app/PLAYBACK_QUALITY.md) and [update guide](https://github.com/HandshakeHackin/Nuvio-maxd-releases/blob/builds/v1.0.0.3/source/native-app/UPDATING.md). ## Source and credits Nuvio Max'd is an **unofficial client**, previously named Nuvio PS5. It is not affiliated with Nuvio, Stremio or Sony. The project is distributed under the [GPL-3.0 license](LICENSE); included components retain their own notices. Every published release includes its matching source archive. Browse the [1.0.0.3 source](https://github.com/HandshakeHackin/Nuvio-maxd-releases/tree/builds/v1.0.0.3/source/native-app), [build guide](https://github.com/HandshakeHackin/Nuvio-maxd-releases/blob/builds/v1.0.0.3/source/native-app/README.md) and [third-party notices](https://github.com/HandshakeHackin/Nuvio-maxd-releases/blob/builds/v1.0.0.3/source/native-app/THIRD_PARTY.md). Versioned delivery branches use `builds/v`. The homepage may describe newer local work; the release tag and matching source identify each public build. Nuvio branding and account protocols come from [NuvioTVSmart](https://github.com/NuvioMedia/NuvioTVSmart). The native UI and integrated player are adapted from [Sp9nky's unofficial Stremio port](https://github.com/Sp9nky/unofficial-stremio-ps5-port), using [BlackBearReloaded's Prospero UI](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-homebrew-ui), the credited EVO/VLC and media libraries, and the other components listed in the notices. The 0.5.34 playback work also adapts ProsperoTube's scheduler and output-lifetime approach with its source and license attribution retained.
