latestRelease.name: Nuvio Max'd 1.0.0.3 — IPTV Library and playback updates
latestRelease.body:
# Max’d 1.0.0.3

## IPTV Library

- Added A–Z navigation for movie and series catalogs, with common accented letters grouped under their base letter and numbers/other scripts under #.
- Added search across saved movie and series catalogs from the active profile’s imported providers. Results identify the provider and content type; playback and episode lookup use the selected provider.
- Kept search offline-capable, bounded and cancellable, with duplicate removal and protection against stale replies after switching profiles or providers.
- Kept long provider badges inside their poster cards. IPTV titles and resume progress remain separate from addon catalogs and tracker history.

## Playback

- Added embedded chapter navigation and timeline markers for supported Native, EVO and VLC files. Open Options/Up, select the Chapters column, then press Cross to jump. The column appears only when at least two valid chapters exist.
- Improved recovery of the selected audio/subtitle track, pause state, audio sync and PCM gain after playback reopens. Explicit subtitles Off and downloaded external cues are preserved where supported.
- Added a bounded HEVC SPS/VUI fallback for missing colour metadata, while preserving explicit container tags. This does not add Dolby Vision output or change whether the console accepts HDR10 output.
- Limited artwork queues, decoded-image staging and cache metadata to reduce memory pressure during browsing and release resources on shutdown.

- Prevented VLC from retrying failed or canceled Nuvio-owned requests through an unauthenticated HTTP handler. Private stream headers and cancellation remain authoritative.

## Maintenance

- Updated libass to 0.17.5, curl to 8.23.0, OpenSSL to 3.5.9 and nlohmann/json to 3.12.0.
- Adjusted startup ordering to preload VideoDec2 before graphics initialization; decoder queries remain deferred until playback.
- Added checksum-verified dependency builds and refreshed VLC’s dependency links so older libraries cannot silently remain in the build.
- Updated the in-app changelog for this release. Existing automatic update reminders remain available under Settings → App updates.

Saved IPTV search covers catalogs already cached for the active profile; it does not download every provider catalog or search the Live TV guide. Open other categories or All categories to save more titles. Episodes keep their normal season order.

Host regressions and PS5 compile/link/import checks passed. Physical-console playback, old-firmware startup, HDMI/HDR and receiver behavior still need testing. Existing optional/experimental player, HDR and four-screen features retain their limitations.

Package revision: **06.000.003**. Title ID: **PPSA99288**. Close the app before updating and preserve saved user data. Homebrew Store availability follows catalog approval and deployment.

repos.name: afterglow-ps5
repos.description: Unofficial Music Assistant player and MilkDrop visualiser for jailbroken PS5
repos.readme: # Afterglow for PS5 An unofficial Music Assistant player for a jailbroken PS5. It joins Music Assistant as a speaker and plays through the console, shows the artwork, word-by-word lyrics and the queue, lets you browse and play with a DualSense, and draws MilkDrop visuals from the music you hear. It can also follow another speaker and draw what that speaker plays, without sounding a second copy. It is the PS5 twin of [Afterglow for LG webOS](https://github.com/HaydenGriffin/afterglow): the same poster design and the same Music Assistant account, written natively in C++ and OpenGL for the console. Afterglow is independent of, and not endorsed by, Music Assistant or Sony Interactive Entertainment. It is built on BlackBearReloaded's [ps5-homebrew-ui](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-homebrew-ui) and keeps its licence, GPL-3.0-or-later. ## What it does - **Plays on the PS5.** Afterglow connects to Music Assistant's Sendspin server, so the console appears in Music Assistant as a speaker called *Afterglow PS5*. Play to it from Music Assistant, or from Afterglow's own Browse. - **Follows a speaker.** Set the source to a speaker (or *Active speaker*) and the PS5 draws whatever it plays, through Music Assistant's MilkDrop Visualizer plugin, while staying silent itself. - **Album, Lyrics and Visuals views.** Album shows the whole artwork with the song, artist and up next. Lyrics shows timed lyrics with the current line leading, word by word when the lyrics carry word timing, and plain lyrics paged by hand. Visuals is MilkDrop on its own or with a track card, and MilkDrop can keep running behind the artwork. - **Lyrics from Music Assistant, with an online fallback.** When Music Assistant has none, the PS5 looks the song up on [LRCLIB](https://lrclib.net) itself (see [Privacy](#privacy)). **Lyrics timing** moves the words up to 10 s earlier or later (and can be kept for one song), **Retry lyrics** asks again, **Choose other lyrics** swaps wrong lyrics for another LRCLIB version, and **Go to a line** plays the song from a chosen line. - **Browse and Search.** Search with the system keyboard, recently played, favourite playlists, albums, songs and artists, radio, podcasts and audiobooks, artist pages. Play now, play next, add to the queue or start radio. - **Queue.** Play, move and remove upcoming songs; shuffle, repeat, crossfade, keep playing when the queue ends, volume and sleep timer. **Playing on** picks the speaker and says what each one plays; picking a silent one moves the music there. **Join** adds the console to the music playing elsewhere and **Move here** brings that music to it. **Speakers together** joins or leaves a sync group and sets each member's own volume. - **Playlists and tonight's programme.** Save the queue as a playlist, or add a song to one, named without a keyboard. With nothing playing, the idle poster offers the evening's songs set as a concert programme, which can be kept as a playlist. - **Presets.** 395 MilkDrop presets (393 enabled) through [projectM](https://github.com/projectM-visualizer/projectm). A preset scan measures each one on your console and keeps the ones that run smoothly. Presets can take their colours from the artwork, and favourites are shared with Music Assistant and your LG TVs. - **Sound & sync.** TV output compensation sets this PS5's delay in Music Assistant, so it plays in time with your other speakers; picture and lyrics timing have their own control. 30, 60 or 120 fps. - **Scan to save.** Details shows a QR code that opens the playing song on your phone, on the streaming service it came from. - **Check my setup.** A pass/fail list (Music Assistant, sign-in, this PS5 as a speaker, the MilkDrop Visualizer plugin, the clock, online lyrics, the preset scan), each failure with one plain next step. - **Light bar and Home.** The DualSense light bar takes the artwork's colour, and an optional Home section shows a few Home Assistant sensors and switches. ## Requirements - A PS5 that runs homebrew: a jailbreak with a homebrew enabler that starts native titles from `/data/homebrew/`, such as [ShadowMount Plus](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus), and an FTP server to copy the app across. The [setup guide](docs/install.md#1-what-you-need) has the details. - [Music Assistant](https://music-assistant.io/) 2.10 or newer on the same network, reachable by its numeric IPv4 address. To follow other speakers, also its **MilkDrop Visualizer** plugin. - For following, speakers Music Assistant streams to itself (Sonos, Chromecast, AirPlay, Squeezelite, ...). A speaker playing on its own, such as Spotify straight from the Spotify app, carries nothing to draw. > **Status:** Afterglow has run on one PS5, on system software 7.20; the pictures here are screenshots from it. > Checked there with 1.6.0: playback through the console at 59.9–60 fps, artwork, online lyrics, Browse, the > controls, the queue, the Display settings and lyric overlays, and the Home section. Signing in with the system > keyboard, the light bar and 120 Hz have been tested on a PC (unit tests, mock servers and the off-screen preview) > but not yet on a console. Other consoles, firmware versions and homebrew enablers haven't been tried. Reports > either way are very welcome. ## Install Download `PPSA99481.zip` from the [releases](https://github.com/HaydenGriffin/afterglow-ps5/releases), or build it (below). Extract it and copy the `PPSA99481` folder to `/data/homebrew/` on the console over FTP. Wait for your homebrew enabler to register the title, then start **Afterglow** from the home screen; it sits with the media apps, not the games. Sign in with Options → Settings → Account → **Sign in**: the system keyboard asks for Music Assistant's address, your username and password. The PS5 keeps its own long-lived token, named after the console, which you can revoke in Music Assistant or with **Log out**; the password is not stored. Then choose *Afterglow PS5* as the speaker in Music Assistant and play something. The [setup guide](docs/install.md) walks through every step, including the optional `afterglow.conf`. ## Controls On the poster or the visuals, with nothing open: | Button | Does | | --- | --- | | Cross | Play / pause | | L1 / R1 | Previous / next song | | D-pad left / right | Back / ahead 10 seconds | | D-pad up / down | Volume; pages plain lyrics in the Lyrics view | | Square | Visuals only, Visuals + track, Album, Lyrics | | Triangle | Lyrics over the visuals: off, one line, stage | | L2 / R2 | Previous / next preset; in the Lyrics view, lyrics earlier / later | | L3 | Lock the preset | | R3 | Favourite the preset | | Options | The playback controls and the Browse, Now playing, Queue and Settings sheets | | Hold Circle | Close Afterglow (1.5 s) | In the sheets, up and down move, left and right change a value, Cross selects, Circle goes back and Options closes everything. The full list is in [docs/AFTERGLOW.md](docs/AFTERGLOW.md#controls). ## Settings Press **Options** for the playback controls: a row of tiles (previous, play, next, back and ahead 10 s, favourite, Details, Display) and a strip with **Browse**, **Now playing**, **Queue**, **Settings** and, once configured, **Home**. Settings holds the source, visuals and presets, lyrics timing, sound and sync, the account and a status page, and **Check my setup**. Settings for this console are kept on the console and, with **Sync settings with Music Assistant** on, in your Music Assistant account; preset favourites are shared with your other Afterglows. Every row is described in [docs/AFTERGLOW.md](docs/AFTERGLOW.md). ## Privacy Afterglow talks to your Music Assistant server: Sendspin for the audio, its API for artwork, lyrics, the queue and your library, and the MilkDrop Visualizer relay when following a speaker. Artwork comes through Music Assistant's image proxy. With a Home section configured, it also talks to your Home Assistant, subscribing only to the entities you list. The one other service is lyrics. When Music Assistant has none for a song, the PS5 asks [lrclib.net](https://lrclib.net) directly over HTTPS, sending only the song's title and first artist (no account, token or device id). **Choose other lyrics** sends the same search, and a song whose lyrics you chose is fetched by that LRCLIB record's id. LRCLIB sees the request coming from your network. Turn **Online lyrics** off (Options → Settings → Lyrics) to stop it; it is on by default. **Check my setup** asks lrclib.net for one fixed record (`/api/get/1`: no song, nothing about you) to see that it answers, only when you run it and Online lyrics is on. The Scan to save code in Details is drawn on the console from the link Music Assistant already sent; nothing is sent. The console stores its Music Assistant token in the app's own storage (`/download0/hui/afterglow.auth`), never your password. A token or Home Assistant token you put in `afterglow.conf` sits in the install folder, which anything with FTP access to the console can read. There is no analytics or telemetry. The dev request path for checking a console from a PC is off unless you turn it on. ## Development The build runs in a Linux container (native on ARM64 and x86-64; on a Mac, Colima or another local Docker works) and cross-compiles for the PS5 with the public [PS5 Payload SDK](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk): ```sh docker build -f Dockerfile.afterglow -t afterglow-builder . docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/work" afterglow-builder make app # dist/PPSA99481/ and dist/PPSA99481.zip docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/work" afterglow-builder make test-unit docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/work" afterglow-builder make lint ``` The interface also renders on a PC, off-screen, with the same code and shaders. The README images above were captured on a PS5 running 1.6.0. To render a preview with made-up music and an invented cover: ```sh AFTERGLOW_PREVIEW=1 AFTERGLOW_COVER=docs/images/preview-cover.png AFTERGLOW_LYRICS=karaoke \ tools/host-snapshots.sh build/afterglow-preview afterglow ``` [docs/AFTERGLOW.md](docs/AFTERGLOW.md) covers the configuration file, the preset scan, the checks and what has not been verified on hardware. repos.name: ps5-solobridge
repos.description: PS5 game + system audio on a Focusrite Scarlett Solo (UAC2) over USB - resident payload for jailbroken PS5
repos.readme:
# ps5-solobridge

Play the PS5's audio (games **and** system/menu sounds) on a **Focusrite Scarlett Solo
3rd gen** connected to the console's USB port, on a jailbroken PS5.

The PS5 only accepts USB Audio Class 1 devices: the Scarlett Solo is UAC2-only, so the
console ignores it and only offers HDMI output. `solobridge` is a resident payload that
drives the Solo directly through FreeBSD's `/dev/ugen*` interface and feeds it the
console mix captured from the system capture service.

Tested on **firmware 13.60** with a Scarlett Solo 3rd gen (`1235:8211`).

## Features

- Game audio and system sounds (menu, notifications), also while in game
- Low latency: about 16-40 ms added by solobridge
- Resident: survives unplugging/replugging the Solo and the end of capture sessions
  (e.g. closing a game)
- Single instance, TCP control port (`status`, `stop`), log file
- Audio keeps playing on HDMI too: the capture is a copy of the mix

## Install

Build it (see below) or take `solobridge.elf` from the
[releases](https://github.com/hebiii994/ps5-solobridge/releases), then either:

- send it to the ELF loader (port 9021) with any payload sender, or
- copy it to `/data/pldmgr/payloads/local/solobridge/` for Payload Manager
  (the `installer` payload does this for you, `autoload` adds it to autoload).

Connect the Solo to a PS5 USB port. Sending the payload again while it is running
prints the status of the running instance instead of starting a second one.

```powershell
.\solobridge.ps1 status   # status and statistics
.\solobridge.ps1 stop     # stop
```

Log: `/data/solobridge/log.txt`.

## How it works

**Capture.** `libSceAvcap2` is the client of `av_capture_manager`, the system service
behind recording, broadcasting and Remote Play. Opened with Remote Play's audio source
it returns the full mix (game + system sounds) as 48 kHz stereo float32, in records of
1024 frames. This part comes from
[FGG-PlayPods](https://github.com/FGGstore/FGG-PlayPods) (GPL-3.0), which streams the
same mix to Bluetooth headsets.

**USB output.** The Solo is a UAC2 device: clock source entity, a streaming interface
with a synchronous isochronous OUT endpoint, 2 channels, 24 bit in 4-byte subslots.
solobridge selects alternate setting 1, sets the clock to 48 kHz with a class `SET_CUR`
request and writes one packet per 125 us microframe (6 frames) to the endpoint node
`/dev/usb/BUS.ADDR.EP`. On ugen each `write()` on an isochronous endpoint becomes one
packet.

**Latency.** The kernel FIFO of the endpoint accepts ~800 packets (100 ms). solobridge
keeps it almost empty (~6 ms ahead), estimating consumption from the clock. The ring
buffer is regulated on its minimum level (just before each 1024-frame capture record),
dropping or repeating at most one frame every 8 ms (0.26%, no audible pitch change) to
absorb clock drift. A large excess, like the backlog the capture service hands over
when a session starts, is skipped at once instead of being played back faster.

## Repository layout

| Folder | What it does |
|---|---|
| `solobridge` | The resident payload |
| `installer` | Installs `solobridge.elf` (embedded) in Payload Manager as a local payload |
| `autoload` | Adds `local/solobridge` to `/data/pldmgr/autoload.txt` (with backup, no duplicates) |
| `usbprobe` | Lists `/dev/ugen*` devices and decodes their descriptors (UAC1/UAC2) |
| `solotone` | Plays a 440 Hz test tone on the Solo: the minimal UAC2 streaming example |
| `hello` | Notification sample to check the build/send chain |
| `lsdir` | Lists `/data/pldmgr` showing small `.txt` / `meta.json` files |

Code comments are in Italian.

## Build (Windows + Docker)

The build runs in a Docker image with Ubuntu, clang-18 and
[ps5-payload-sdk](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk).

```powershell
docker build -t ps5sdk .
.\build.ps1 solobridge                 # -> solobridge\solobridge.elf
.\send.ps1 solobridge\solobridge.elf   # send to 192.168.88.2:9021, prints stdout
```

`send.ps1` takes `-PS5Host` and `-Port`; `build.ps1 <folder> clean` cleans.
On Linux/macOS just `export PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK=/opt/ps5-payload-sdk` and run `make` in a
folder. `installer` embeds `../solobridge/solobridge.elf`: rebuild it after changing
solobridge.

## Notes from testing (FW 13.60)

- Payloads run with `uid=1`; `/dev/ugen*` and `/dev/usb/*` are accessible.
- `USB_GET_DEVICEINFO` is not supported (errno 25) and root hubs `ugenX.1` cannot be
  opened (errno 6): `USB_GET_DEVICE_DESC` / `USB_GET_FULL_DESC` work.
- Before solobridge the Solo reports a 0 Hz sample rate: no system driver touches it.
- Sockets returned by `accept()` inherit `O_NONBLOCK` from the listener (FreeBSD).
- Docker Desktop on Windows may refuse to start with "listening on unix://...: The file
  cannot be accessed by the system" after a forced quit (stale AF_UNIX socket files).
  Quit Docker and rename the folder named in the error, e.g.
  `Rename-Item "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Docker\run" run.stale`.

## Other UAC2 devices

Only the Solo's VID/PID is matched (`solobridge/solo.c`), but the descriptor parsing is
generic. Other class-compliant UAC2 interfaces with a synchronous or adaptive OUT
endpoint may work by changing `SOLO_VID`/`SOLO_PID`; devices with an asynchronous
endpoint and a feedback endpoint would need feedback handling. Untested.

## License

GPL-3.0 (see `LICENSE`). The capture code is derived from FGG-PlayPods (GPL-3.0),
see `solobridge/NOTICE.md`.

repos.name: ps5-forwarder-manager
repos.description: Forwarder Manager: native PS5 homebrew app to create and edit home-screen forwarders (port of ps5-forwarder.mph.am)
repos.readme:
# Forwarder Manager

A native PlayStation 5 homebrew app that creates and edits home-screen
**forwarders**: tiles that launch another installed app (an emulator) with
launch arguments such as `--rom <file>`. It is a native port of the web tool
[ps5-forwarder.mph.am](https://ps5-forwarder.mph.am/) by Martin Pham, rewritten
from scratch to run on the console itself.

![Home: forwarders by target app](docs/screenshots/home.jpg)

| | |
| --- | --- |
| ![Create a forwarder](docs/screenshots/create.jpg) | ![Edit a forwarder](docs/screenshots/edit.jpg) |
| ![Choose where the icon comes from](docs/screenshots/icon-source.jpg) | ![SteamGridDB icon results](docs/screenshots/steamgriddb.jpg) |
| ![An icon's details before using it](docs/screenshots/steamgriddb-details.jpg) | |

The screenshots use demo forwarders for freeware and open-source games.

## What it does

- Lists the forwarders already in `/data/homebrew` and lets you edit or delete them.
- Creates a new forwarder: display name, target app, title ID, ROM file, an
  `--exit-after-game` flag, and launch arguments.
- Picks the ROM (and optional `.at9` music) with a built-in file browser over
  the console filesystem.
- Makes tiles for Nintendo Switch games played with
  [ProsperoEden](https://github.com/Swordpdf/ProsperoEden): pick a game with its
  cached title and cover, which also becomes the tile icon. Reads `game_files`
  from `/data/prosperoeden/config/prosperoeden.json` (default:
  `/data/prosperoeden`) and lists ROMs in its `roms/`, including games in their
  own folders. Names and TGA covers come from `/data/prosperoeden/covers`.
  Recognises `.nsp`, `.xci`, `.nsz` and `.xcz`; compressed games need a
  ProsperoEden version that supports them. Recognisable update/DLC filenames
  and title-ID tags are excluded; encrypted package contents are not read.
  A file browser remains available. Games inside the configured `roms/` keep
  their relative path, so tiles keep working when the game files folder moves;
  other files use their full path. To fix an existing tile that lost its
  folders, edit it, pick its game again, and save.
- Fetches tile icons and backgrounds from [SteamGridDB](https://www.steamgriddb.com/)
  or from any image file, encoding them to the exact
  formats the PS5 shell expects: a 512x512 PNG icon and 3840x2160 BC7 DDS
  backgrounds.
- Makes tiles for PC games streamed with
  [ProsperoLight](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ProsperoLight): pick one of
  its paired PCs and one of that PC's apps from a list with box art, which also
  becomes the tile icon. The tile starts the stream by itself (`--pc`, `--app`,
  `--exit-after-stream`). The lists are what ProsperoLight keeps under
  `/data/prosperolight/forwarder`; without them the PC and app are typed.
- Makes tiles for Xbox 360 games played with
  [PS5X360](https://github.com/BrinooTk/PS5X360): pick a game from the ones it
  finds in its default game folders (`/data/xbox360`, `xbox360` on USB and
  extended storage, its own `assets/roms`), with its cover or package
  thumbnail as the tile icon. Extracted games (`default.xex`), `.iso` images
  and Games on Demand/XBLA packages are found the way PS5X360 finds them. A
  game in a folder added in PS5X360's own settings, which other apps cannot
  read, is picked as a file or folder instead. The tile gives PS5X360 the
  game's full path as its only argument, which is how it starts a game; it
  takes no `--rom` and has no exit-after-game option. If the game then drops
  back to PS5X360's library with "Disc read failure", the game's data is
  incomplete, not the tile: Unreal Engine 3 games need every file of the
  disc, including `<Game>\Xbox360TOC.txt`, which some extraction and upload
  tools skip. PS5X360's detailed logs (stream on TCP 9100) name the missing
  file (`open-failed ... path=`).
- Makes tiles for PlayStation games played with
  [SwanStationPS5](https://github.com/darkxex/SwanStationPS5): pick a game from
  the ones it finds in its game folders (`/data/SwanStationPS5/games`,
  `/data/PSXS5/games`, and `SwanStationPS5` / `PSXS5` on USB and extended
  storage), with its cover as the tile icon. The tile starts it with
  `--rom <full path>` and, optionally, `--exit-after-game`; SwanStationPS5
  needs to accept those arguments, which it does from the version that adds
  forwarder support.
- Writes a complete tile folder (shared `eboot.bin` + `libc.prx`,
  `forwarder.json`, `sce_sys/param.json`, art) that ShadowMountPlus registers.

## Install

1. Download `PPSA99930.zip` from the latest
   [release](https://github.com/heydemoura/ps5-forwarder-manager/releases)
   (`SHA256SUMS` next to it has its checksum).
2. Unzip it and copy the `PPSA99930` folder to `/data/homebrew/` on the
   console, for example over FTP.
3. Let ShadowMountPlus register it, then start **Forwarder Manager** from the
   home screen.

To update, replace the folder with the one from a newer release. Your
forwarders live in their own folders and are kept.

## Requirements on the console

- A jailbroken PS5 with `elfldr` listening on port 9021.
- [ShadowMountPlus](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus) to register the
  generated tiles.

Nothing else needs to be loaded for the app to reach `/data/homebrew`. The
release bundles the exact-title one-shot helper from
[PS5-Lapy-JB-Daemon](https://github.com/ArkSama/PS5-Lapy-JB-Daemon)
(`lapy.elf`, with its MIT license in `licenses/`). At launch the app first asks
a Lapy daemon that is already running, if there is one; otherwise it hands its
own helper to `elfldr`, which lifts only this app out of its sandbox and then
exits. The app uses `/data` only after it has proved it can write, read and
list it.

Forwarders are made in the [PS5 Forwarder Format](https://github.com/heydemoura/ps5-forwarder-format),
a standard shared with emulators that create forwarders themselves. The format
lives in the `external/ps5-forwarder-format` submodule: its specification, the
`psfwd` library this app reads and writes forwarders with, the forwarder
program every tile runs, and an open-source launcher.

No separate launcher payload is needed. A tile cannot start another app
itself, so it asks a resident launcher on `127.0.0.1:10199`; when none is
running, the tile sends the launcher it carries to `elfldr` first. The app does
the same when it starts, and at each start it gives existing forwarders the
current forwarder program (only folders with a `forwarder.json` whose program
is a forwarder's are touched). A launcher that is already running, such as
ps5-app-launcher, is used as it is. Settings shows which one serves the tiles.

## Building

This repository is built on the
[ps5-native-app-boilerplate](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-native-app-boilerplate)
with the [ps5-homebrew-ui](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-homebrew-ui)
OpenGL kit. From a Linux or WSL host with Clang 18, lld, Make, Ninja and
Python 3:

```bash
git submodule update --init        # the PS5 Forwarder Format (or clone with --recursive)
make                       # fetches the SDK, ps5-opengl and PacBrew libcurl, then builds
make deploy PS5_HOST=<ip>  # uploads dist/<TITLE_ID>/ to /data/homebrew over FTP
```

The forwarder template and launcher come prebuilt from the format's
`template/` folder. `make standard-template` rebuilds them from the format's
sources inside the submodule; commit the result there.

The build always links PacBrew's libcurl (for the SteamGridDB HTTPS client,
since an elevated app cannot use `sceHttp`). SteamGridDB search needs an API
key built into the app: set `STEAMGRIDDB_API_KEY` in `.env` (see
`.env.example`) or the environment. Release builds get it from the
repository's `STEAMGRIDDB_API_KEY` Actions secret. Without a key the app
still works, with image files only.

Feature flags switch parts of the app off at build time. They are listed,
with their defaults, in `src/fwd/features.hpp`, and the app logs each one at
start (`[FWD] feature NAME=0|1`). Turn one on for a build with `FEATURES`:

| Flag | Default | What it controls |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PAYLOAD_TARGET` | off | The "Payload" (PPSA00000) target app |

```sh
make FEATURES="PAYLOAD_TARGET=1"
```

A forwarder whose target is switched off still loads: it shows its target's
title ID and edits as a generic target.

## Releases

Versions follow the PlayStation `contentVersion` format, `NN.NNN.NNN`
(`00.001.000` is the first release). To cut one, raise `contentVersion` in
`sce_sys/param.json`, add `docs/release-notes/<version>.md`, commit both, then
push a tag named exactly the version (no `v`). CI builds the app and publishes
a GitHub release with `PPSA99930.zip`, `SHA256SUMS` and those notes.
`docs/catalog/PPSA99930.json` is the record for the
[PS5 Homebrew Catalog](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-homebrew-catalog);
update its `version`, `artifact_url`, `sha256` and `icon_url` for each release
(the catalog's daily job can also propose the update).

## Layout

| Path | What |
| --- | --- |
| `src/main.cpp` | Entry point: elevation, then the kit frame loop |
| `src/app/` | The app and its screens (home, edit, file picker, art, SteamGridDB, settings) |
| `src/fwd/` | The forwarder model, the on-disk store, and the icon/DDS image encoders |
| `src/net/` | libcurl glue and the SteamGridDB API v2 client |
| `src/platform/` | Sandbox elevation (Lapy daemon, then the bundled Lapy helper) and app-root resolution |
| `src/{gfx,ui,audio,core,runtime}` | The ps5-homebrew-ui kit |
| `assets/forwarder-template/` | The shared launcher `eboot.bin` and `libc.prx` |

## Development harness

Because the build host has no controller, the app carries a dev-only harness
that is inert unless trigger files exist under `/data/ps5fwdgen-dev/`:

- `input.txt` - a line-per-command script (`up`/`down`/`cross`/`type:<text>`/
  `wait N`/`hold <button> N`/`shot`/`quit`) fed as synthetic input to the real screens, consumed
  once. `shot` saves a 1920x1080 PNG to the app's `download0`.
- `selftest.txt` - runs the real `write_forwarder()` once with test values.

These are read only when present and never affect normal use.

## Acknowledgements

Forwarder Manager could not reach `/data` without
[PS5-Lapy-JB-Daemon](https://github.com/ArkSama/PS5-Lapy-JB-Daemon). Many
thanks to **ArkSama / Team PHU**, who created Lapy and released it as open
source, and to [mpereiraesaa](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/PS5-Lapy-JB-Daemon)
for the exact-title one-shot helper this app bundles. Thanks as well to the
Lapy contributors, to Martin Pham for
[ps5-forwarder.mph.am](https://ps5-forwarder.mph.am/), and to the authors of
[ShadowMountPlus](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus),
[SteamGridDB](https://www.steamgriddb.com/), the
[ps5-native-app-boilerplate](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-native-app-boilerplate)
and the [PS5 payload SDK](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk).

Licensed GPL-3.0-or-later. Lapy's helper is MIT licensed (see
`licenses/Lapy-MIT.txt` in the release). See `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.

latestRelease.body:
Pick ProsperoEden games with their names and covers, including games kept in their own folders.

### Added

- **ProsperoEden game picker.** The Game row lists ROMs from ProsperoEden's game files folder, with their cached titles and covers. Selecting a game fills an empty display name and uses its cover as the tile icon, while keeping an icon you already chose. (#27)
- **Follow ProsperoEden's settings.** Reads `game_files` from `/data/prosperoeden/config/prosperoeden.json`, defaulting to `/data/prosperoeden`. Finds loose ROMs and games one folder down in `roms/`. Relative paths appear under the titles so games with the same name can be told apart. A file browser remains available for other ROMs. (#27)
- **ROM formats.** The picker recognizes `.nsp`, `.xci`, `.nsz` and `.xcz`. Compressed games require a ProsperoEden version that supports them. Recognizable update/DLC filenames and title-ID tags are excluded; encrypted package contents are not inspected, so add-ons with ambiguous names may still appear. (#27)

### Fixed

- **Forwarders for nested ProsperoEden games.** A game such as `roms/Mario Kart 8 Deluxe/Mario Kart 8 Deluxe.nsp` now keeps `Mario Kart 8 Deluxe/Mario Kart 8 Deluxe.nsp` in its launch arguments. Tiles keep working when the configured game files folder moves; ROMs selected outside that folder use their full path. Fixes #26. (#27)
  - To repair a tile created with a missing folder, edit it, select its game again, and save.
- **Reproducible builds.** Restored the pinned OpenGL SDK download through a mirror after the original repository became unavailable. Both original SHA-256 checks remain enforced. CI also runs the ProsperoEden library regression tests. (#27)

### Changed

- **SwanStationPS5 target name.** The target picker and home-screen tab now use the emulator's full name, SwanStationPS5. Its title ID and existing tiles are unchanged. (#25, by @darkxex)

### Thanks

- @Oliv3rmoon for reporting #26 and documenting ProsperoEden's game files setting, cover hashes and cached names.

### Requirements

- A jailbroken PS5 with elfldr on port 9021.
- ShadowMountPlus, to register the app and the forwarders it creates.

### Install

Unzip `PPSA99930.zip` and copy the `PPSA99930` folder to `/data/homebrew/`, replacing the old one. Your forwarders are kept. `SHA256SUMS` contains the ZIP's checksum.

repos.readme: # PS5 Wallpaper Modder Payload for jailbroken PS5 to change system wallpapers. ## Screenshot ![PS5 Wallpaper Modder Interface](screenshot.png) ## Requirements - PS5 with jailbreak - USB drive (exFAT or FAT32) - Images under 8 MB (JPG, PNG, or DDS) ## Features - Supports JPG, PNG, and DDS - Installs icon on PS5 home screen - Web interface with dark theme - Backup and Restore original wallpapers - Auto-open browser toggle (saved to /data/ps5_wallpaper/config.txt) - USB logs for debugging - 14 system screen destinations (select individually or all at once) ## How to Run 1. Copy ps5-wallpaper-modd.elf to USB 2. Run the payload using any loader (Ethernet, websrv, netcat, pldmgr, etaHEN) 3. Launch the app from PS5 home screen 4. Web interface opens at http://127.0.0.1:8095 ## How to Use - SELECT WALLPAPER: Scan USB and list images - BACKUP: Save original wallpapers to USB - RESTORE: Restore from backup - HELP: Show instructions IMPORTANT: Images must be under 8 MB. ## Supported Formats - JPEG (.jpg, .jpeg) - PNG (.png) - DDS (.dds) Note: The PS5 does not validate DDS content. repos.readme:
# ps5-remoteplay-get-pin
Generate Remote Play pairing PIN for offline activated accounts.

Apparently most of the checks preventing Remote Play from working on offline activated accounts are just in ShellUI, the `sceRemoteplayGeneratePinCode` function works without any patching, so after you pair you can even use it unjailbroken. 

## Usage
Full guide on setting this up from Modded Warfare: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8ijpU4-Qwz4

1. Offline activate your account using [offact](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/offact).
    - Download: https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/websrv/releases/
    - The auto-generated id is fine to use, you dont need a real psn id if you're fine with using chiaki.
    - To be able to use the official Remote Play app you'll need to set your proper account id associated with your psn account in offact.
1. Reboot the console if you have not done so since you offline activated your account.
    - From a quick test I did this step wasn't necessary, however others reported this as being a required step. You try sending the payload right away, pairing and reboot only if the pairing/connecting fails.
1. Inject this payload using john-tornblom's elf loader on port 9021.
    - The pairing pin and base64 encoded id will be displayed in a notification as well as printed to stdout.
        - To see stdout you can inject like this: `socat -t 99999999 - TCP:<yourps5ip>:9021 < rp-get-pin.elf`
    - Only the displayed account id will be accepted when pairing, which is the currently logged in user.
    - If you want to cancel the pairing you can send the payload again.
1. Connect with [chiaki](https://sr.ht/~thestr4ng3r/chiaki/), [chiaki-ng](https://streetpea.github.io/chiaki-ng/) or the official Remote Play app.

## Thanks
- Nicit - testing
- [astrelsky](https://github.com/astrelsky/) - ptrace examples
- [john-tornblom](https://github.com/john-tornblom/) - sdk and ptrace examples

repos.name: PS5-SELF-Decrypter
repos.description: A portable payload to decrypt PS5 SELF files from the filesystem to USB drive
repos.readme:
# PS5 SELF Decrypter

A payload that uses kernel arbitrary read/write to decrypt Signed ELFs (SELFs) from the filesystem and dump the
plaintext ELFs to USB drive.

## Notes
- Replace `PC_IP` and `PC_PORT` macros on lines 24-25 with your TCP server's IP/port
  - It's recommended you use logging to know how far the payload's progressed or if it's stalled
- Plug compatible USB drive into PS5 with at least 1GB of free space before running
- Files will be dumped to `[USB root]/PS5/`
- Should support 3.xx-4.xx, but not tested on all firmwares (open an issue for any problems)
- Currently, the payload assumes pre-jailbroken state (ie. escaped sandbox), adding jailbreak code here is a TODO
- If you notice log activity has stopped for more than a minute, hard powerdown the PS5 via power button for three beeps
  and restart the console and run again
- The console may panic in the midst of dumping files, this is fine, restart the console and run again
  - The payload will pick up where it left off and continue dumping from where it was halted previously
- Improvements to make the payload less janky are welcome

## TODO
- [ ] Add code to escape sandbox in case the environment isn't already jailbroken
- [ ] Perform better locking on shared data access to improve stability
- [ ] Clean up various functions

## Example log
```
[+] kernel .data base is ffffffff88e40000, pipe 12->13, rw pair 14->21, pipe addr is ffffa04b61800480
[+] firmware version 0x3000038 ( 3.000.038)
[+] got auth manager: 4
...
[+] dumping /system_ex/common_ex/lib...
[+] decrypting /system_ex/common_ex/lib/libSceJsc.sprx...
  [?] decrypting block info segment for 0
  [?] decrypting block info segment for 1
  [?] decrypting block info segment for 2
  [?] decrypting block info segment for 4
  [?] decrypting block info segment for 9
  [?] decrypting block info segment for 10
  [?] decrypting segment=1, block=1/593
  [?] decrypting segment=1, block=2/593
  [?] decrypting segment=1, block=3/593
  [?] decrypting segment=1, block=4/593
```

## Notes for offset porting
- One of the goals in writing this payload was keeping it somewhat easy to port to other firmwares, even without kernel
  .text dump
- The payload will use lib calls to determine the system version and tailor at runtime, assuming that firmware has
  support
- There are a total of 11 offsets, notes for finding them are as follows (these are not guaranteed, but based on observations):
  - `offset_authmgr_handle`: +0x30 bytes from pointer to "sdt" string (it should also usually be 0x4)
  - `offset_sbl_mb_mtx`: -0x20 bytes from pointer to "SblDrvSendSx" string
  - `offset_mailbox_base`: +0x8 bytes from `offset_sbl_mb_mtx`
  - `offset_sbl_sxlock`: +0x8 bytes from `offset_mailbox_base`
  - `offset_mailbox_flags`: -0x8 bytes from pointer to "req mtx" string
  - `offset_mailbox_meta`: -0x18 bytes from pointer to "req msg cv" string
  - `offset_dmpml4i`: -0x8 bytes from pointer to "invlgn" string
  - `offset_dmpdpi`: +0x4 bytes from `offset_dmpml4i`
  - `offset_pml4pml4i`: -0x1C bytes from pointer to "pmap" string
  - `offset_datacave_1/offset_datacave_2`: any two 0x4000 byte ranges that seem unused (likely dont need changing)

## Thanks
- ChendoChap (various reversing help and testing)
- Znullptr (testing)
- flat_z (kernel to work off of + various info)
- alexaltea (previous work w/ orbital for reference)

## License
Specter (Cryptogenic) - [@SpecterDev](https://twitter.com/SpecterDev)

This project is licensed under the unlicense license - see the [LICENSE.md](LICENSE.md) file for details.

repos.name: ps5-self-pager
repos.description: Yet another PS5 SELF decryptor
repos.readme:
# ps5-self-pager

It works by swapping `pagertab[OBJT_VNODE]` to point to `selfpagerops` instead of the `vnodepagerops` it normally is for the duration of the `mmap` call, this will cause the kernel to give us a self pager when mmapping a file, essentially replicating the removed `MAP_SELF` `mmap` flag, while bypassing its checks.

Supports PS5 firmware `1.00`-`13.40`

## Usage
There are a couple different builds in the releases to dump specific folders:
| Payload file name | File(s)/folder(s) it dumps |
| -------- | ------- |
| ps5-self-pager-game.elf | `/mnt/sandbox/pfsmnt` recursively (`app0` and `patch0` if exists, `app0-patch0-union` is skipped) |
| ps5-self-pager-full-system.elf | `/system` and `/system_ex` recursively |
| ps5-self-pager-system-common-lib.elf | `/system/common/lib` |
| ps5-self-pager-shellcore.elf | `/system/vsh/SceShellCore.elf` |

If a USB drive is plugged in, it will output the decrypted unsigned ELFs to `USB0/dump`, otherwise it will use `/data/dump` on the internal storage.

Send to [elfldr](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/elfldr) (port 9021) with a sender that can listen back to see logs:
- For a GUI option: https://github.com/Al-Azif/hermes-link
    - Select `Debug Log` in the menu to see logs
- If you have `PuTTY` installed, from `cmd` do:
    ```
    type ps5-self-pager.elf | "c:\Program Files\PuTTY\plink.exe" -raw -P 9021 IP_OF_YOUR_PS5
    ```
- Using socat:
    ```
    socat -t 9999999 - TCP:IP_OF_YOUR_PS5:9021 < ps5-self-pager.elf
    ```

Wait until you see `Done. Success: x, Failed: y` in the logs.

## Note
Since we are modifying the `pagertab`, there is a small window (~20-60 microseconds per mapping/segment, the actual decryption work happens on page fault, and by then we restored the `pagertab`) where if any process maps a file, it would receive a self pager, which would not be able to handle a regular file so the process would receive a `SIGSEGV` if the memory was accessed directly, and likely crash. However I would expect this to be rare, you might never encounter it. If this does happen it just crashes the game/process, not the entire console.

## Thanks/references
- https://github.com/PS5Dev/Byepervisor/blob/main/src/self.cpp
- https://github.com/OpenOrbis/OpenOrbis-PS4-Toolchain/blob/master/scripts/make_fself.py
- @EchoStretch for providing kernel .data dumps

repos.readme:
A game launcher for Linux you drive with a controller.
Your GOG, Steam, Epic, itch.io and emulated games in one library, played from the couch or on a Steam Deck.

Install · Docs · Changelog

> [!WARNING] > Early days (0.0.x). I use it every day, but expect rough edges. [Issues](https://github.com/ilyasturki/universe/issues) are welcome. ## Install x86_64 Linux with a systemd user session. ```sh # Arch (AUR). Add -bin to both names for the prebuilt build, -git to follow main. paru -S universe universe-desktop # Fedora 44 and newer (COPR) sudo dnf copr enable ilyasturki/universe sudo dnf install universe universe-desktop # SteamOS, Bazzite and others: under ~/.local, with Python 3.11 to 3.14 curl -fsSL https://github.com/ilyasturki/universe/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh # From a checkout, with cargo ./install.sh ``` On Nix, import the flake's `nixosModules.default` for the system and `homeModules.default` for the apps, each with `programs.universe.enable = true`. On GNOME, run `universe setup` once after the Arch or Fedora package. Then open **Universe Big Screen**, and a short setup finds your games. More: [every way to install](https://universe.ilyasturki.com/docs/getting-started/install/), [updating and uninstalling](https://universe.ilyasturki.com/docs/getting-started/update-uninstall/). ## Your whole library GOG, Steam, Epic and itch.io games, installed and updated from Universe. The first run brings in the games Lutris and Heroic installed and your emulators' ROM folders, and moves nothing. ![The library grid](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ilyasturki/universe/site-media/src/assets/media/library.webp) ## A page for every game Art, screenshots, play time, achievements, saves and disk use. Its settings are one button away: runner, Proton build, resolution, frame cap. ![A game's page](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ilyasturki/universe/site-media/src/assets/media/game-page.webp) ## Three looks Switch live from the settings, or install a theme as an add-on.

- **Universe**, the default look, is a port of my [Pegasus theme Reprise](https://github.com/ilyasturki/pegasus-theme-reprise), with the game's art behind everything. - **Switch 2** puts a row of games over a bar of round buttons, like the Switch 2's HOME menu. - **PS5** puts the game's world behind a row of tiles, with a hub for each game, like the PS5's home. Not affiliated with Nintendo or Sony. Nintendo Switch is a trademark of Nintendo; PlayStation and PS5 are trademarks of Sony Interactive Entertainment. ## HOME over a running game HOME pauses the game and opens over it. From there, take a screenshot, turn on MangoHud, cap the frame rate, change the volume, reconnect a controller or quit. ![Dead Cells running, then HOME over it: the dock, MangoHud turned on, back in the game and the volume level](docs/images/home-over-game.avif) ## Couch and Steam Deck - DualSense, DualShock 4, Xbox, Switch Pro and 8BitDo [controllers](https://universe.ilyasturki.com/docs/controllers/supported/), each with its own glyphs, and a guided setup for any other pad. Emulators get the pads you hold, one per player. - On a [Steam Deck](https://universe.ilyasturki.com/docs/getting-started/steam-deck/), it fits the 1280×800 screen. Back buttons run macros; refresh rate, power limit and fan curve are in the settings. - Added as a non-Steam game, it runs inside [Steam's Game Mode](https://universe.ilyasturki.com/docs/getting-started/steam-deck/#steams-game-mode). - [The Universe session](https://universe.ilyasturki.com/docs/getting-started/universe-session/) is a login session with the launcher on the whole screen and no desktop, like a console. ## Also - Record every session if you like. Videos and screenshots land in the Media tab. - Achievements from each store, with a banner over the game on unlock. - Saves backed up after every session, restored or exported from the game's page. GOG and Epic cloud saves synced. - Proton, Wine and 21 emulators, installed, updated and rolled back from the settings. - Modules, stores and themes made by others, installed from the settings as add-ons. - Hold B for the power menu: suspend, reboot or power off. - Runs on GNOME, KDE, Cinnamon, Sway, Hyprland, Niri, X11, or no desktop at all. - Universe Desktop, a GTK app for mouse and keyboard on the same library. GNOME's search finds your games. ## From a terminal `universe` does everything the apps do. Add `--json` to any command. ```sh universe # your library, last played first universe play "dead cells" # by id, a word or part of the title universe login gog # sign in to a store universe search hades --source gog # then universe install --source gog universe update # games behind, of every kind; --all shows each version universe saves backup "dead cells" # also list, restore, export and cloud universe doctor # what this system is missing universe status --json # the running game, for a script ``` Every command is in the [CLI reference](https://universe.ilyasturki.com/docs/reference/cli/). ## Docs [universe.ilyasturki.com/docs](https://universe.ilyasturki.com/docs/) has the guide: install, first run, controllers, every settings section, and a reference of the CLI, the launch settings and config.toml generated from the app. For development: - [`docs/api.md`](docs/api.md): the core, the CLI, config, modules and sources - [`docs/frontends.md`](docs/frontends.md): how the UI is built, and how to write another frontend - [`docs/extensions.md`](docs/extensions.md): modules, sources and themes that do not ship with Universe, and how to install them - [`CHANGELOG.md`](CHANGELOG.md): what each release changed, also under Settings › About in both apps ## License [MIT](LICENSE)

latestRelease.name: Universe 0.0.14
latestRelease.body:
### Added

- Settings › Game defaults › **Game updates** lists the games with a newer release out, in every look and in Universe Desktop: **A** installs a store's update, and **I have the latest version** confirms one you installed yourself. The games Universe can't check sit behind **Y**, to confirm by hand.
- The Universe look's top tabs each have an icon, the focused game's name shows in the middle of the tab bar, and the library has 9 columns.
  ![The library under the tab bar, each tab with its icon and the focused game named in the middle](https://github.com/ilyasturki/universe/releases/download/v0.0.14/library.webp)
- HOME opens the dock over a game started from Universe Desktop in gamescope, in your look, and its **Home** brings Universe Desktop's window back.
- KytyPS5 and SharpEmu run PlayStation 5 games, each a folder with its `sce_sys/param.json`.
- A sixth picture, the **Wallpaper**, fills the launch screen at 16:9.
- A game whose art was never fetched, such as one imported by an older version, gets its art, description and screenshots the next time Universe starts, and **Fetch missing art** fills missing descriptions too.
- The Media tab has a row of toggles, Up from the top row, to show screenshots, recordings and journal entries or hide them.
- A journal entry's card in the Media tab shows its first screenshot, and the entry's page puts its screenshots above its text.
- A book pulses in every look's top bar while a journal entry is being written.
- **Test vibration** on a controller's page makes the pad buzz.
- The dock's **Game** button shows the running game's art, and the controllers card of the dock and of the PS5 control center opens Settings › Controller.
- In the Universe look, settings rows that name a game, such as search results, show its banner.

### Changed

- The Universe look's game page is slimmer: one line above the buttons gives your play time, when you last played and whether an update is out, and the store's screenshots sit right of the description, **Right** moving into them. Game settings, media and achievements open from **···**.
  ![A game page with its play time, its buttons, the description and a column of screenshots](https://github.com/ilyasturki/universe/releases/download/v0.0.14/game-page.webp)
- A game's page shows its version with **Up to date** or **Update available** only when Universe knows where the game stands; the guess from file dates and its **May be out of date** are gone.
- **Mark as current** moved off the game page to **I have the latest version** in Game updates; `universe update <game> --mark-current` still does it.
- A right click on a cover opens the game menu, and a second one closes it; in the Switch 2 and PS5 looks it acts as press and hold.
- In the Universe look, What's new opens as a window over Home or Settings, and **B** closes it.
- Each store and feature row has a switch that shows whether it is on.
- The Universe look's Appearance no longer shows the theme's affiliation line.
- Universe Desktop gives a game's saves, cloud saves, Wine prefix and storage their own **Saves and Storage** page, which **Storage** opens too.
- Universe Big Screen reads the controller through SDL3, which the installer needs on the system for your controller: SteamOS 3.8 and Bazzite have it, Ubuntu 24.04 and older don't.
- A GOG game under Wine fetches GOG Galaxy's stand-in service on its first launch instead of the packages shipping it.

### Fixed

- A game that minimized itself behind the dock or during a pause comes back when you return to it.
- Universe Big Screen no longer crashes under Qt 6.12.
- More games get their art from GOG GamesDB, past brackets, version numbers and edition names in their titles.
- A launch drops the fonts a Wine or Proton prefix registered from `/nix/store` files since deleted.
- A journal entry put off by a restart no longer shows as being written.
- The Universe look's game page keeps its place through a library refresh, and the Media tab's viewer opens on the screenshot picked.
- Runner logos show in settings search results.
- **B** closes the folder picker in the Switch 2 and PS5 looks instead of going up a folder.
- Universe Desktop's game page draws its header at once and its body in one go, with nothing shifting.

### Performance

- Covers on home, the library and search load in reading order.

Full changelog: [v0.0.13...v0.0.14](https://github.com/ilyasturki/universe/compare/v0.0.13...v0.0.14)

---

**Install or upgrade**

- Arch Linux, from the AUR: `paru -S universe` (or `universe-bin`, `universe-git`), and `universe-desktop` for the GTK app
- Fedora 44 and newer: `sudo dnf copr enable ilyasturki/universe`, then `sudo dnf install universe universe-desktop`
- SteamOS, Bazzite and other distros: `curl -fsSL https://github.com/ilyasturki/universe/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh`, run again to upgrade
- Nix: the flake's Home Manager and NixOS modules (`inputs.universe.url = "github:ilyasturki/universe"`), `nix flake update universe` to upgrade

repos.name: BFpilot
repos.description: Lightweight PS5 file manager | browser based
repos.readme:
# BFpilot

Web-based file manager for the PS5. Runs as a single `bfpilot.elf`, accessible
from the console browser or another device on the same network.

[Downloads](https://github.com/ItsBlurf/BFpilot/releases) · [Release notes](docs/RELEASE_NOTES_NEXT.md) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md)

## Features

- Browse, copy, move, rename, delete and change permissions.
- Upload files and folders; download selections individually or as a TAR.
- Connect to SMB2/3 shares for file transfers, editing and PKG access.
- Extract ZIP/ZIPX, RAR, 7z and [other formats](docs/ARCHIVE_EXTRACTION.md),
  including supported encrypted and split archives.
- Queue multiple extractions, merge folders and review operation results.
- Search indexed paths, edit text files and view images.
- Load ELF/BIN/JS payloads and submit local or SMB-hosted PKGs for installation.

## Usage

Load `bfpilot.elf` through your ELF loader on port **9021**:

```sh
python3 payload_sender.py <PS5_IP> 9021 bfpilot.elf
```

Open **`http://<PS5_IP>:5905/`**. BFpilot registers a Media tile automatically;
no separate installer is needed. Reload the browser page after updating.

### Controller

| Button | Action |
| --- | --- |
| R1 | Open the highlighted item |
| Square | Toggle selection |
| X | Normal browser interaction |

R1 opens the highlighted item regardless of multi-selection.

## Compatibility

Tested on firmware **11.60**.

Direct SMB extraction is unsupported; copy the archive locally first. For SMB
installs, keep the server and source file available until installation finishes.
PKG queue acceptance does not confirm completed installation.

See [known limitations](docs/COMPATIBILITY_STRATEGY.md#known-limitations).
Keep backups of important files.

## Build

Built with [PS5 payload SDK 0.45](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk/releases/tag/v0.45)
and LLVM 23.1.4. GNU Make and Python are also required.

```sh
export PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK=/path/to/ps5-payload-sdk
make all
make inspect-imports
```

Windows: set `PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK` and run `build.cmd` from a configured toolchain
environment. Output: `bfpilot.elf`.

## Documentation

- [Archives](docs/ARCHIVE_EXTRACTION.md)
- [Installation and compatibility](docs/COMPATIBILITY_STRATEGY.md)
- [Temporary files and recovery](docs/PRIVATE_STAGING.md)
- [Transfers](docs/PERFORMANCE_STABILITY.md) and [upload troubleshooting](docs/UPLOAD_PERFORMANCE.md)
- [Folder-size API](docs/BACKGROUND_SIZE_API.md)

Settings and logs: `/data/BFpilot`. Binary checksums: [SHA256SUMS](SHA256SUMS).

## License

[MIT](LICENSE). See [NOTICE.md](NOTICE.md) for contributors and third-party licenses.

latestRelease.body:
# BFpilot 0.4.9

## Added

- SMB2/3 connections, share browsing, file operations, transfers and text editing.
- SMB-hosted PKG details, icons and installation sources; payload loading from SMB.
- Built-in archive service with AES ZIP and additional formats.
- Multiple-archive extraction with destination and merge/replace options.
- Individual selected-item downloads alongside combined TAR downloads.
- Results beside Logs and Exit for file, archive and PKG status.

## Fixed

- Large-folder copies waiting for a full file count before starting.
- Overwrite, merge, cancellation and recovery handling.
- Extracted-file permissions; new extracted files and directories use `0777`.
- RAR cancellation during output, contributed by oz5hk.
- PKG request handling and queue-status updates.
- Long paths, folder sizing, double-clicks and selection in large directories.
- Finished archive progress reappearing after reload and delayed replies after sleep.

## Changed

- Updated to PS5 payload SDK 0.45 and LLVM 23.1.4.
- Installer identity now uses the SDK firmware reading before the kernel-version fallback.
- Fixed Windows helper linking and rebuilds after SDK/compiler changes.
- English-only interface; Triangle/F1 search shortcut removed.
- R1 opens the highlighted item regardless of selection. Square selects;
  X keeps normal browser behavior with cursor.

## Known limitations

- Direct SMB extraction is unsupported; copy the archive locally first.
- A folder merge does not undo replacements that finished before a later error.
- PKG queue acceptance is separate from installation completion.

## Update

Load `bfpilot.elf` and reload the browser page. No separate helper is required.
Settings remain under `/data/BFpilot`. Checksums: [SHA256SUMS](https://github.com/ItsBlurf/BFpilot/releases/download/v0.5.0/SHA256SUMS).

repos.name: BFplayer
repos.description: A PS5 media and video player that also functions as a complete media library, with support for subtitles, multiple audio tracks, aspect-ratio adjustment, cropping, and many other playback settings.
repos.readme: # BFplayer **AI use notice:** BFplayer has been developed with OpenAI Codex. I direct the development and have spent many hours across multiple days testing builds and playback behavior on my own PS5. BFplayer is a native media library and player for jailbroken PlayStation 5 consoles. The standalone release installs its own tile in the Media section and does not require websrv or Homebrew Launcher. A separate websrv-ready ZIP is available for people who already use websrv and do not want BFplayer's standalone launcher running in the background. ## Features - Movies, TV shows, seasons, music, and playlists - Manual media sources with an optional whole-library import - DLNA/UPnP browsing for compatible NAS and LAN media servers - Direct HTTP(S), FTP, RTSP, RTMP, RTP, TCP, and UDP media URLs - Resume playback, favorites, search, sorting, and playback queues - Embedded and external subtitles with timing adjustment - In-player subtitle browser and optional SubDL search/download - Audio, video, subtitle, and chapter selection - Aspect-ratio, crop, and scaling controls - Local artwork or an automatically generated video preview - Persistent settings and rotating diagnostic logs - Clean reinjection: a newer payload replaces the resident launcher without creating a second tile or resetting the library Playback is powered by FFmpeg 7.0.1, SDL2, SDL_kitchensink, and libass. Decoding is currently software-based, so demanding 4K HEVC or AV1 files may not play smoothly. BFplayer preserves source resolution by default and switches the PS5 display to 3840x2160 for larger sources. Its direct 10-bit PS5 path presents BT.2020/PQ as native HDR10 without an HDR-to-SDR conversion. BT.2020/HLG is converted to PQ for the same native HDR10 output. An explicit `BFPLAYER_OUTPUT_POLICY=smooth` escape hatch can request proportional 1080p conversion, but it is never the default and is not used for native HDR. On the alpha.44 hardware build, the supplied 3840x2160 59.94 fps VP9 Profile 2 PQ WebM held about 59.9 fps at native 3840x2160 with zero steady-state misses and roughly 819 MiB peak resident memory. The equivalent HLG presentation workload also held 59.9 fps after warm-up. These are sample-specific measurements, not format guarantees. Decoding is still software-based, so demanding HEVC, AV1, unusual encodes, or slow storage/network sources can exceed the available CPU or I/O budget. Every video starts in **Best fit**, **Original** aspect, and **No crop** mode. The player uses the source stream's display ratio, including anamorphic pixel-ratio metadata, and falls back to the decoded frame dimensions when that metadata is unavailable. Manual scale, aspect, and crop overrides apply only to the current video. ## Install ### Standalone Media tile Download `bfplayer-standalone.elf` from the latest release and inject that payload after each jailbreak. It installs or updates the **BFplayer** tile in the Media section and stays resident to launch the player. Nothing needs to be copied to `/data/homebrew` beforehand. The payload creates and maintains its own runtime folder. Reinjection preserves the library, settings, sources, playback history, and logs. Repeated tile launches are coalesced, and a player-instance lock prevents two BFplayer processes from initializing PS5 video memory at the same time. ### websrv Download `BFplayer-websrv.zip` from the latest release and extract its `BFplayer` folder into a websrv homebrew root such as `/data/homebrew`, `/mnt/usb0/homebrew`, or `/mnt/ext0/homebrew`. The final entrypoint is `BFplayer/eboot.elf`. websrv launches the player directly, so this method does not use `bfplayer-standalone.elf`, the Media tile, port 9040, or BFplayer's resident launcher. See [docs/WEBSRV.md](docs/WEBSRV.md) for the exact package layout. ## Library controls | Button | Action | | --- | --- | | Cross | Open or play | | Circle | Go back inside a show or season; no action at the library root | | Triangle | Remove the selected movie or TV source (press twice) | | D-pad Left/Right | Change library category | | D-pad Up/Down | Move through the list | | L1/R1 | Previous or next page | | L3 | Add or remove favorite | | R3 | Change sort mode | | Touchpad | Add media | | Options | Open the main menu | The Add Media browser starts at `/`. Cross opens a folder or adds a movie, Triangle adds a folder as one TV show, and Square imports a folder as a mixed library. Mixed import treats loose video files as movies and child folders as TV shows. ## Network and NAS media Open **Options > Browse DLNA / NAS** to discover UPnP MediaServer devices on the same local network. BFplayer browses their ContentDirectory folders and plays compatible audio or video resources through FFmpeg. Discovery and browsing run on a cancellable worker with bounded response and listing sizes. For a server that exposes a direct stream, use **Options > Open network URL**. Direct SMB is not linked. A NAS can instead expose its library through DLNA, HTTP(S), FTP, or another supported streaming protocol. URLs containing username/password authority fields are rejected, and signed query values are redacted from logs and excluded from playback-history persistence. ## Playback controls | Button | Action | | --- | --- | | Cross | Pause or resume | | Circle | Change subtitle track | | Square | Change audio track | | Triangle | Change video track | | D-pad Left/Right | Short seek | | D-pad Down/Up | Long seek | | L1/R1 | Previous or next chapter | | L3/R3 | Volume down or up | | Touchpad | Show the full control list | | Options | Open playback menu | Display controls are available through the playback menu and controller shortcuts, including scaling, aspect ratio, and crop mode. ### External and online subtitles Open **Options > Subtitles** while a video is playing. The list contains embedded tracks, matching files found beside the video, and any subtitle chosen through **Browse subtitle files**. The browser starts in the video's folder and shows only folders and supported subtitle files. Optional online search uses the official SubDL API. In **Playback settings**, select **SubDL API key** and enter a key from a free SubDL account, then set **Download languages** to comma-separated codes such as `en,ar,fr`. BFplayer searches by the playing release filename, downloads in the background, stores the selected file under `/data/BFplayer/subtitles`, and activates it without restarting playback. The key is sent only in HTTPS request headers and is not written to logs or URLs. SubDL's own quotas and terms apply. For fan edits or unusual release names that cannot be identified from the filename, choose **Online subtitle providers > SubDL > Search by movie or show title** and enter the name. The provider screen also lists OpenSubtitles, Podnapisi, and Addic7ed in grey when they cannot be integrated without an approved API or unsupported website scraping. All vertical lists wrap from top to bottom and bottom to top. Holding D-pad Up or Down accelerates progressively for large libraries and folders. ## Logs Runtime logs are stored under: ```text /data/BFplayer/logs ``` The repository includes `collect-logs.ps1` for copying the current and previous logs from a console. More details are in [docs/DIAGNOSTICS.md](docs/DIAGNOSTICS.md). ## Building The project uses [ps5-payload-sdk](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk) and PacBrew v0.37. From the project directory: ```powershell . ..\..\ps5dev-env.ps1 .\build.ps1 -Configuration Release ``` Release artifacts are written to `dist/`. ## Notes - The dashboard title ID is `PSMC00001`. - The launcher listens only on `127.0.0.1:9040`. - Network services are intended for a trusted local network. - Network playback uses larger but bounded compressed-packet queues, reconnect handling, and audible-audio clocking. It does not allocate an unbounded frame cache. - Hardware and format behavior can vary by firmware, HEN, storage device, and media encoding. See [docs/STANDALONE_LAUNCHER.md](docs/STANDALONE_LAUNCHER.md) for launcher details, [docs/WEBSRV.md](docs/WEBSRV.md) for the websrv package, and [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) for bundled components and licenses. ## Contributors - **ItsBlurf:** I started and maintain BFplayer, make the project decisions, test it on my PS5, and handle releases. - **OpenAI Codex:** I use it to help with implementation, review, and documentation. ## Acknowledgements - [ps5-payload-websrv](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/websrv) for the BigApp and ELF loading foundation and the websrv homebrew format - [dlnaplay](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/dlnaplay) for the DLNA, audio-clock, and bounded-buffer design reference - [FFmpeg and ffplay](https://ffmpeg.org/) for the media and playback foundation - [PacBrew](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/pacbrew), SDL2, and SDL_kitchensink for making the PS5 playback stack possible - [VLC](https://www.videolan.org/vlc/) for the display aspect, crop, and scaling behavior used as a reference ## License GPL-3.0-or-later. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).

repos.name: PoorDS4
repos.description: Use a wireless DualShock 4 in native PS5 games on jailbroken consoles.
repos.readme:
# PoorDS4

Wireless DualShock 4 compatibility for native PS5 games and homebrew.

PoorDS4 forwards a DS4 connected to the console through the controller APIs used
by the running application. It runs in the background and follows application
changes. Native DualSense controllers keep their own input path.

[Download](https://github.com/ItsBlurf/PoorDS4/releases) ·
[Usage](docs/USAGE.md) · [Build](docs/BUILD.md) ·
[Compatibility](docs/FIRMWARE_SUPPORT.md) ·
[Report a bug](https://github.com/ItsBlurf/PoorDS4/issues)

## Getting started

1. Connect the DS4 to the PS5 and select the profile used by the game.
2. Load `PoorDS4.elf` through the console's ELF loader.
3. Start a native PS5 game or homebrew application. The payload attaches automatically.

Use the filename supplied with a published release when installing that release.
**v0.2.0** brings together the controller compatibility and recovery fixes
made since RC51.
See [what changed](CHANGELOG.md) and the [firmware requirements](docs/FIRMWARE_SUPPORT.md).

## Features

- DS4 buttons, sticks, analog triggers and controller data forwarded from Sony's console input source.
- Shared handling for state reads, queued reads and controller information.
- Per-controller source attribution and handle-generation recovery.
- Automatic application handoff and source rediscovery.
- Separate status and stop payloads for diagnostics and normal shutdown.
- Preserved first-failure reports and optional detailed controller logs.

Tests for controller routing, queued reads and recovery pass on Windows and
Linux. Earlier builds in this release line confirmed Eden input and Isaac
Repentance gameplay with a single DS4 or a DS4 + DualSense on firmware 11.60.
Multiplayer with several DS4s, other firmware versions and additional connection
orders need more testing.
The latest controller-table correction passes captured-code checks on a PS5,
and live Isaac reads receive connected DS4 input. Gameplay in the affected
tester setup still needs a retest.
The current build's input delivery, optional logging and normal recovery were
also checked in Eden on 11.60.

DS4 vibration does not work in this build. The DS4 also lacks the DualSense's
haptic actuators and adaptive-trigger hardware, so those effects are not
supported. Vibration support is a low priority for now, but ideas, technical
findings and pull requests are welcome.

## Payloads

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `PoorDS4.elf` | Start the background controller bridge. |
| `PoorDS4-status.elf` | Export current reader, bridge and controller diagnostics. |
| `PoorDS4-stop.elf` | Request normal shutdown of the running bridge. |

Load one controller bridge at a time. Use the stop payload before replacing a
running build. [Usage and troubleshooting](docs/USAGE.md) explains the runtime
states and diagnostic files.

## Development

The project uses [ps5-payload-sdk v0.43](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk/releases/tag/v0.43).
Build instructions and host regression checks are documented separately:

- [Build from source](docs/BUILD.md)
- [Testing and validation scope](docs/TESTING.md)
- [Architecture and source guide](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)
- [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md)

## Credits and license

PoorDS4 builds on [Ghostcontrol](https://github.com/StonedModder/Ghostcontrol-PS5-USB-Controller-Patcher),
with the [PS5 Payload SDK](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk) and
[kstuff-lite](https://github.com/EchoStretch/kstuff-lite).
See [NOTICE](NOTICE.md) for attribution. Licensed under [GPL-3.0-or-later](LICENSE).

## Donations & Support

Donations help with development, additional controllers and testing equipment.

- **PayPal:** [paypal.me/nblurf](https://paypal.me/nblurf)
- **Bitcoin (BTC):** `1CW8JWSnWc5w7yKhYk7ixAFG487nU5Jrzc`
- **USDT (TRC20):** `TRcrCeonXzgyxjR4LGzo4JdfEHYGGqD3gX`

Bug reports, test logs and contributions are also welcome.

## Disclaimer

PoorDS4 is an independent, open-source project for controller interoperability,
not affiliated with or endorsed by Sony. Product names and trademarks belong to
their respective owners and are used only to identify compatibility.

PoorDS4 does not supply games, Sony firmware or cryptographic keys and does not
endorse piracy or unauthorized access to copyrighted content. Use it responsibly
and in accordance with applicable law.

Provided **as is**, without warranty, to the extent permitted by law; see
[LICENSE](LICENSE), sections 15–17. Crashes or data loss are possible—back up
important saves. This notice does not alter the GPL license.

latestRelease.name: PoorDS4 v0.2.0
latestRelease.body:
# PoorDS4 v0.2.0

This release brings together the DS4 compatibility, controller-routing and
recovery fixes made since RC51.

After connecting additional controllers, hold **L1 + R1 + L2 + R2** to reset
PoorDS4 and refresh controller detection.

## Changes

- Improved emulator and homebrew input compatibility, including Eden.
- Fixed a false-disconnect cause affecting LEGO Party and games using the
  same empty-read input pattern.
- Corrected controller attribution and handle matching that could mix players'
  input or interfere with native DualSense input.
- Improved DS4 multiplayer joining, including clients opened after a game starts
  and controllers connected under an already signed-in profile.
- Fixed controller-table detection for longer library lookup loops, which could
  leave Isaac without input even after the DS4 active notification appeared.
- Preserved controller identities during source recovery and the reset shortcut,
  avoiding unnecessary game-side disconnects.
- Fixed inconsistent input and controller information across connection changes.
- Improved controller-source rediscovery, application handoff and handle cleanup.
- Fixed read-validation edge cases and recovery-shortcut controller attribution.
- Preserved first-failure diagnostics and added optional per-controller log
  summaries to help investigate reports without changing input handling.

## Files

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `PoorDS4.elf` | Main controller payload. |
| `PoorDS4-status.elf` | Export controller and bridge diagnostics. |
| `PoorDS4-stop.elf` | Stop the running bridge normally. |

The matching source archive and `SHA256SUMS.txt` are included.

## Updating

Stop any running PoorDS4 instance with `PoorDS4-stop.elf` before loading this
version. Connect the DS4 under the profile used by the game, load `PoorDS4.elf`
through your ELF loader, then start the game or homebrew application.

## Compatibility

Tests for controller routing, queued reads, reconnects and recovery pass on
Windows and Linux. All three payloads build successfully.

Console logs were checked in Eden, FC26, LEGO Party and Isaac Repentance on
firmware **11.60**. Earlier builds confirmed Eden input and Isaac gameplay with
a single DS4 or a DS4 + DualSense. Continuing a saved Isaac co-op run still
requires controllers for its existing players.

Mixed DS4/DualSense tests also covered both player orders, reconnecting either
controller, and reopening a saved co-op run. Both players kept independent input.

The current build was also checked in Eden on 11.60: connected input reads
continued with detailed logging enabled and disabled, and normal recovery kept
the existing game controller identity.

Multiplayer with several DS4s, other firmware versions, guest profiles and
additional connection orders need more testing.

The latest table-detection correction passes the recorded failure case on a
PS5. Live Isaac reads also receive connected DS4 input, with no handle mismatches
or disconnected output samples. Retesting gameplay in the affected tester setup
is still pending.

DS4 vibration does not work in this build. The DS4 also lacks the DualSense's
haptic actuators and adaptive-trigger hardware, so those effects are not
supported. Vibration support is a low priority for now, but ideas, technical
findings and pull requests are welcome.

Please include the firmware, application version, controller setup and fresh
diagnostics when [reporting an issue](https://github.com/ItsBlurf/PoorDS4/issues).

## Special Thanks

A huge shoutout to [reyzinhoplayoliver-design](https://github.com/reyzinhoplayoliver-design)
/ `ElCauaRey` on Discord for helping with a lot of testing and finding bugs!

## Donations & Support

If you find PoorDS4 useful and want to support future development, please
consider donating:

- **PayPal**: [paypal.me/nblurf](https://paypal.me/nblurf)
- **Bitcoin (BTC Network)**: `1CW8JWSnWc5w7yKhYk7ixAFG487nU5Jrzc`

repos.readme:
PS5 Payload Manager

A modern, web-based dashboard to easily manage, import, and automatically load payloads on your PS5.

## Features - **Web-Based Interface**: A modern dashboard to manage payloads from your PC, phone, or the PS5 itself. - **Import Payloads**: Easily add new payloads from a USB drive or download them from the cloud repository. - **Automated Startup**: Set up a list of payloads to load automatically whenever you start the manager. - **Home Screen Shortcut**: Installs a dedicated "Payload Manager" app icon to your PS5 home screen for quick access. - **Favorites and Process Management**: Keep favorite payloads at hand, inspect active processes, and terminate eligible processes. ## Installation ### Using an Autoloader (Recommended) It is highly recommended to use **Payload Manager** together with an **Autoloader**: [Y2JB](https://github.com/itsPLK/ps5-y2jb-autoloader) | [BD-JB](https://github.com/itsPLK/ps5-bdjb-autoloader) | [Lua](https://github.com/itsPLK/ps5-lua-autoloader) `pldmgr.elf` is already included as the default payload in the latest versions of the Autoloaders linked above. If you are using an older version and don't want to update the entire autoloader, you can simply: 1. Place `pldmgr.elf` into your `autoload` directory. 2. Add `pldmgr.elf` as the only entry in your `autoload.txt` config file. ### Standalone / Manual Loading You can also manually load the manager like any other `.elf` file. Grab the latest version from the [Releases](https://github.com/itsPLK/ps5-payload-manager/releases) page. ## Custom Repositories You can add third-party payload repositories to the manager. To learn how to create your own repository JSON and host it, see the [Custom Repositories Guide](CUSTOM_REPOSITORIES.md). ## Translations PS5 Payload Manager supports multiple languages. For the list of supported languages, how to report translation issues or suggest improvements, and past community translators, see [TRANSLATIONS.md](TRANSLATIONS.md). ## Credits - [John Törnblom](https://github.com/john-tornblom) - for the [PS5 Payload SDK](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk) and homebrew samples used as reference. - [All contributors](https://github.com/itsPLK/ps5-payload-manager/graphs/contributors) - for their contributions to the project. - Everyone else contributing to the PS5 homebrew scene. ## Donations If you'd like to support my work, please check out the [DONATE.md](DONATE.md) file. ## Development For build instructions and deployment details, see [DEVELOPMENT.md](DEVELOPMENT.md).
