repos.name: KIK-Trophy
repos.description: PS5 trophy backup inspector and owner-ID editor for Windows.
repos.readme: # KIK Trophy 1.0 **Move your PS5 trophy progress to another local user while preserving unlocked trophies and their original timestamps.** Useful after creating a new user or reinstalling/resetting your console, when you want to restore trophies from an earlier backup. Work with one game or several at once. [Download for Windows](https://github.com/kiikeep/KIK-Trophy/releases) · [Español](README.es.md) Windows 10/11 x64, Intel or AMD. Extract the entire ZIP and open **KIK Trophy.exe**. ## Which files do you need? The two `trophy2` folders serve different purposes: | PS5 path | Contents | | --- | --- | | `/user/trophy2/` | Each game's **catalog**: trophy names, descriptions, grades and images. | | `/user/home//trophy2/` | **That user's progress**: earned trophies, timestamps and owner identity. | These are the main files, using Ratchet & Clank as an example: **Game catalog — `TROPHY.UCP`:** ```text /user/trophy2/nobackup/conf/NPWR20842_00/TROPHY.UCP ``` **User progress — `TRPTITLE.DAT`:** ```text /user/home//trophy2/nobackup/data/NPWR20842_00/TRPTITLE.DAT ``` `NPWR20842_00` identifies the game's trophy set. `` is the folder belonging to a local user on your console. **KIK Trophy modifies only `TRPTITLE.DAT`. This is the file you copy to the new installation to restore trophy progress.** The catalog supplies trophy details in the app; it does not contain your personal unlock history. ## 1. Back up your files to the PC Copy both `trophy2` folders from the PS5 to your PC using FTP or your file manager. Keep them in a backup folder or ZIP archive. Preserve their separate paths: one belongs to `/user/trophy2/`, the other to `/user/home//trophy2/`. **Do not merge them into one `trophy2` folder.** If you plan to reset the console, make this backup first. Copying the folders preserves the files, but **the progress still belongs to the original user**. To restore it to another user—including after a system reinstall—you must adapt the DAT's owner IDs to the user in the new installation. ## 2. Get the destination user's IDs The app uses two values: **Local user ID** and **Account ID**. Enter them manually if you know them. If you do not: 1. Select the **local user who will receive the trophies** on your current PS5 installation. 2. Launch any game for the first time, then close it so the console can generate its trophy files. 3. Copy the resulting `TRPTITLE.DAT` for that user to your PC. For example, if the destination user were `1234abcd` and you used ASTRO BOT: ```text /user/home/1234abcd/trophy2/nobackup/data/NPWR24170_00/TRPTITLE.DAT ``` In KIK Trophy, click **Take IDs from another TRPTITLE.DAT** and select that file. The app reads both IDs. **A DAT from any game works, but it must belong to the destination user on the current installation.** It does not have to be from the game you are restoring. `1234abcd` is an example ID; use the one from your console. ## 3. Adapt your backed-up progress 1. Use **Open folder** for your backup folder, or **Add files** for its ZIP archive. 2. Select a game and click **Change owner**. For several games, select their checkboxes and click **Change IDs in batch**. 3. Enter the destination IDs or read them from the DAT obtained in the previous step. 4. Review the destination path and export to a folder on your PC. Your original files stay unchanged. The last valid IDs are remembered between app sessions. If multiple backups target the same game and user, select the history you want to restore. ## 4. Prepare the game and restore the DAT **Before restoring, launch the game you want to recover at least once with the destination user, then close it.** Letting the console generate the catalog and other files is recommended. Check that the catalog already exists on the current installation. For Ratchet & Clank: ```text /user/trophy2/nobackup/conf/NPWR20842_00/TROPHY.UCP ``` If it does not exist yet, launch the game and check again before continuing. Your export contains a structure like this: ```text user/home/1234abcd/trophy2/nobackup/data/NPWR20842_00/TRPTITLE.DAT ``` Back up the console's current DAT, then copy **only the exported `TRPTITLE.DAT`** to its matching destination: ```text /user/home/1234abcd/trophy2/nobackup/data/NPWR20842_00/TRPTITLE.DAT ``` Keep the filename `TRPTITLE.DAT` and check the user and game identifiers. The exported `user` folder corresponds to `/user` on the console. **Your backup can contain complete folders; this restoration uses only the adapted DAT.** Restoring other trophy files has not been tested: let your console generate them. Copying files back to the PS5 is done separately from KIK Trophy. --- Tested with **Ratchet & Clank: Rift Apart** and **ASTRO BOT**. The tool transfers existing progress; it does not unlock new trophies or sync with PSN. Created by **kiikeep** · [MIT License](LICENSE)

repos.readme:
# 🎬 ProsperoPlayer 1.0

**A homebrew media player for jailbroken PS5 systems.**

ProsperoPlayer lets you browse media from USB, play movies and music, view images, use subtitles, resume playback, and optionally launch directly from the PS5 **Media** row.

---

## ✨ Features

* 📁 Browse USB drives and folders
* 🎞️ H.264 / HEVC playback
* 📺 1080p + experimental 4K path
* ⏩ Seek bar + thumbnail scrub previews
* 💬 Embedded + external SRT subtitles
* 🎧 Multiple audio tracks
* 📑 Chapter support
* 🔄 Resume playback
* 🕘 Recent Files
* ⭐ Favorites
* 🎵 Music / Now Playing screen
* 🖼️ Image viewer
* 🖥️ Fit / Fill / Stretch
* 🛠️ Diagnostics + compatibility reports
* 🎮 Custom PS5-style UI

---

## 🏠 PS5 Media Tile

ProsperoPlayer can optionally appear directly under the PS5 **Media** section.

For the best experience, set the Media Launcher to autoload after jailbreak.

You can remove the tile from:

```text
Settings → Remove Home Tile
```

---

## 🎮 Controls

* `X` — Select / Play / Pause
* `O` — Back
* `← / →` — Seek
* `L1 / R1` — Long seek / Chapters
* `R2` — Change audio track
* `L2 / R3` — Subtitle delay

---

## ⚠️ Known Limitations

* Jailbroken PS5 required
* Jailbreak required again after reboot
* Media tile launcher must run each jailbreak
* E-AC3 / Dolby Digital Plus may be silent
* AAC audio is recommended
* FLAC / OGG support may vary
* 4K playback depends on the file
* Some firmware may briefly show **“Not Supported”**

---

## 📹 Videos

🎬 **ProsperoPlayer 1.0 Showcase**
`https://youtu.be/-lSXV9LAMx0`

---

## ⚠️ Disclaimer

ProsperoPlayer is an independent homebrew project and is **not affiliated with Sony or PlayStation**.

Use homebrew software at your own risk and only play media you own or have permission to use.

---

## 👑 Created by KINGDKAK

If ProsperoPlayer helps you out:

⭐ Star the repo
📺 Subscribe on YouTube
🐛 Report compatibility issues

repos.readme:
🚀 PS5 FFPFSC PRO

PS5 Game Compression Utility

📥 Download • 📺 YouTube • ☕ Ko-fi

--- ## 📦 About PS5 FFPFSC PRO is a cross-platform GUI for compressing PlayStation 5 game dumps using MkPFS and FFPFSC. The application supports Windows, Linux, and macOS. The goal is simple: make PS5 game compression easy without requiring command-line tools or complicated setup. Whether you're compressing a single game, batch processing multiple titles, or browsing community compatibility reports, everything can be done from one interface. --- ## 🖼️ Screenshots ### Main Window ![PS5 FFPFSC PRO Main Window](screenshots/main-window.png) ### Community Compatibility Database ![Community Database](screenshots/community-database.png) ### Compression Progress ![Compression Progress](screenshots/compression-progress.png) --- ## ✨ Features * Compress PS5 game dumps into .ffpfsc * Supports game folders, .exfat, .ffpkg, .zip, .rar, and .7z * Drag-and-drop support * Batch compression * Multi-image queueing * Compression tuning options * Compression presets (Fast, Balanced, Max Compression, Low RAM) * Automatic update checker * Live RAM meter * Automatic retry on out-of-memory errors * Detailed logs and progress tracking * Per-game output folders * Compact mode * Interactive feature tour * What's New dialog after updates * Community Compatibility Database * APR / AMPR game support --- ## 📂 Supported Inputs * PS5 game folders * `.exfat` images * `.ffpkg` images * `.zip` archives * `.rar` archives * `.7z` archives --- ## 🌐 Community Compatibility Database After a successful compression, you can optionally submit your results to the community database. The database allows users to: * Share compatibility reports * Report Working / Partial / Not Working / Not Tested Yet status * Search by game name * Search by Title ID * View report counts * View ShadowMount version information * Browse compatibility reports directly from the application * Duplicate submission protection * Vote-based reporting system * Submit results directly from the application * Filter by compatibility status * Browse over 5,000+ community compatibility reports Compatibility status is vote-based so one incorrect report cannot override community results. View the live compatibility database: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1dgu0p7U2yB_mhcUELz-Wkc7Yhs-avoWLY1Gcm0n5XJw/edit?usp=drive_web&ouid=115958744890792485831 Or access it directly from PS5 FFPFSC PRO. --- ## ⚙️ Compression Tuning Advanced users can fine-tune compression using: * Compression level selection * CPU core selection * Block size selection Available block sizes: * Auto * Auto-Fit * 16384 * 32768 * 65536 Smaller block sizes may improve results for games containing large numbers of small files. Compression Presets * 🚀 Fast * ⚖️ Balanced * 🗜️ Max Compression * 💾 Low RAM Presets automatically configure compression level, CPU cores, and block size. --- ## 🎮 AMPR / APR Support PS5 FFPFSC PRO can detect games that require the AMPR emulator. Features include: * Automatic PlayGo chunk detection * Automatic APR title detection * Automatic AMPR index generation * Dedicated AMPR folder configuration * Compatibility reporting support * Batch mode support --- 📊 Monitoring & Automation * Live RAM meter * Automatic update checking * Windows completion notifications * Automatic retry on memory errors * Real-time progress tracking --- 🎓 User Experience * Interactive feature tour * What's New dialog after updates * Full Help / FAQ section * Detailed logging * Resizable log panel * Compact mode --- ## 🚀 Getting Started 1. Download the latest release. 2. Run `PS5_FFPFSC_PRO.exe` 3. Add a game folder, archive, `.exfat`, or `.ffpkg` image. 4. Select your compression settings. 5. Click **Start**. The application handles the rest. --- ## 🛠️ Common Issues ### Out of Memory Try: * Lowering CPU cores * Lowering compression level * Closing other applications ### Disk Full Ensure sufficient free space exists in both: * Output folder * Temporary folder ### Write Errors Verify that: * Output locations are valid * Drives are writable * Storage devices have enough free space The application provides detailed error messages and recommended fixes whenever possible. --- ## 🙏 Credits ### Compression Backend * MkPFS * Bizkut ### Community Special thanks to everyone testing games, submitting compatibility reports, reporting bugs, and helping improve the project. --- ## 🔗 Links 📺 YouTube https://youtube.com/@KINGDKAK ☕ Ko-fi https://ko-fi.com/KINGDKAK 📥 Releases https://github.com/KINGDKAK/PS5-FFPFSC-PRO/releases --- ## ⚠️ Disclaimer This project is provided as-is. Only use content you legally own and follow all applicable laws in your region. --- ⭐ If you find the project useful, consider starring the repository and contributing compatibility reports to help the community.

repos.name: ps5-patchdl
repos.description: Official updates for your PS5 and PS4 games, from any browser. PatchDL runs on the PS5, finds the newest update for every installed game, downloads it with parallel connections and resume, and installs it on the console. Web UI for phone, laptop and TV, plus a home-screen tile. Runs on firmware 1.00 to 13.60.
repos.readme:
PatchDL

Downloads and installs official updates for PS5 and PS4 games, controlled from any browser.

If you like what I do, you can buy me a coffee*:
*It doesn't have to be a generous donation. A few cents are enough to show me who is interested in further development. So the motivation stays and I just know that I am not programming for the bin ;)

--- ## What it does PatchDL runs as a payload on the PS5 and serves a small web page. Open that page on your phone, your laptop or in the console's browser and you get a list of your installed games with their version and the latest update Sony has for them. Click Update, and PatchDL downloads the patch from Sony's servers and hands it to the console's own installer. A few things it does on top of that: - Update all queues every game that has an update and works through them one by one. - Downloads use several connections at once (4 by default, up to 16). - If the newest patch needs a firmware you don't have, PatchDL looks for the latest one that still runs on your console. Under Other versions you can pick any version of a patch yourself. - A download that gets interrupted continues where it stopped, also after a pause or a restart of PatchDL. - After a successful install the package is deleted. You can switch that off. - Optionally every piece is checked against Sony's checksums. - There's a switch for a PatchDL tile on the home screen. - The interface is available in ten languages. PatchDL only updates games installed from disc or the PlayStation Store. It doesn't download games, and it doesn't touch system software. ## Screenshots

Games with updates
All installed games

Picking another version
Settings

On a phone
Home screen tile
## Installation 1. Download `patchdl_.elf` from the [latest release](https://github.com/knutwurst/ps5-patchdl/releases/latest). 2. Send it to your PS5 with the ELF loader you already use. 3. The console shows a notification with the address, e.g. `http://192.168.0.42:12880/`. Open it in a browser on the same network. You need a PS5 that can load ELF payloads. PatchDL should run on firmware 1.00 to 13.60; I've tested it on 11.60 and 13.60. ## FAQ **Where do the updates come from?** From Sony's update servers, the same files the console would download itself. Nothing gets modified. To find Sony's servers PatchDL uses public DNS (Cloudflare, Google, Quad9) and leaves the console's DNS settings alone, so if you block system updates through DNS, that block stays in place. **How does it know about older patches?** Sony only tells the console about the newest patch. The version history comes from [Prospero Patches](https://prosperopatches.com/) for PS5 games and [Orbis Patches](https://orbispatches.com/) for PS4 games. PatchDL sends them the game's title ID, nothing else. **How do I get a specific version?** Open Other versions on the game, pick a version and follow the steps. You copy one link from the patch site (on the PS5 you scan a QR code and do that part on your phone), paste it, and PatchDL downloads that version from Sony. **Can I go back to an older version?** Yes. Older versions under Other versions have a Downgrade button. A PS5 update contains the whole game, so PatchDL removes the installed game and puts the older version on. A PS4 patch builds on the base game, so PatchDL removes only the installed patch and puts the older one on; the game stays. Your saves stay either way, but a save made with the newer version may not load in the older one. Turn off updates for that game afterwards, or Update all brings it back to the newest version. **The game is gone, but its download is still there?** PatchDL lists a finished PS5 download whose game isn't installed anymore, for example after a replace that stopped halfway. Press Install and it goes on as the whole game. **When is the package deleted?** Only after the console reports the new version and its installer has registered the package. Otherwise it stays. You can turn deleting off in Settings. **Do disc games work?** Yes. Keep the disc in the drive while the update installs. Some disc builds are older than the base the update expects. Then PatchDL asks once and installs the update as the whole game instead; your saves stay and the disc stays the license. **What if the power goes out during a download?** Start PatchDL again and press Resume. ## Disclaimer PatchDL is an independent project and not affiliated with or endorsed by Sony Interactive Entertainment. "PlayStation", "PS5" and "PS4" are trademarks of Sony Interactive Entertainment Inc. PatchDL downloads official, unmodified updates for games that are already installed. It doesn't download games, doesn't contain Sony software, keys or game content, and doesn't install unsigned or modified packages. Use it with games you own. Issues about pirated content will be closed. ## Building ```sh scripts/build_ps5.sh # builds patchdl-ps5.elf ``` This needs the [ps5-payload-dev SDK](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk) (0.44 or newer) with `libcurl` and `OpenSSL` from its [pacbrew-repo](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/pacbrew-repo). `libmicrohttpd` and SQLite are included in the repo. Every push is built by GitHub Actions, and tags become releases. To try a build on your console: ```sh PS5_HOST= scripts/deploy_ps5.sh ``` ## Credits Built on [libmicrohttpd](https://www.gnu.org/software/libmicrohttpd/), [libcurl](https://curl.se/), [OpenSSL](https://www.openssl.org/), [SQLite](https://sqlite.org/) and the [ps5-payload-dev SDK](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk). The patch history comes from [Prospero Patches](https://prosperopatches.com/) and [Orbis Patches](https://orbispatches.com/). Thanks to everyone working on these. ## Support If you like what I do, you can buy me a coffee*: [![Donate](https://img.shields.io/badge/Donate-PayPal-22c55e?style=flat-square&logo=paypal&logoColor=white)](https://paypal.me/oliverkoester) *It doesn't have to be a generous donation. A few cents are enough to show me who is interested in further development. So the motivation stays and I just know that I am not programming for the bin ;) ## License GNU General Public License v3.0 or later, see [LICENSE](LICENSE). Copyright © 2026 Knutwurst.

repos.name: wings-app
repos.description: A PS5 Frontend Solution for a Seamless & Frustration Free On-Device Experiences
repos.readme:
A native PS5 front end for Pegasus DL, made for the couch and a controller.

--- One clean page per game. See what every link is before you press it. Manage your files. Let Pegasus do the downloading. [Screenshots](#screenshots) · [Credits](#credits) · [Features](#features) · [Install](#install) · [Quick start](#quick-start) · [Guides](#guides) · [Controls](#controls) · [Privacy](#privacy) · [License](#license)
| What Wings is | What Wings is not | |---|---| | A PS5 app (title ID `PPSA99178`) that is a front end & performance patcher for a **Pegasus DL** on the same console, through its local API at `127.0.0.1:6970`. | Not Pegasus DL, not affiliated with its author, and not a replacement for it. Pegasus does the downloading, installing and extracting. | | A better way to browse what Pegasus already knows: games grouped one per tile, links explained, files managed with a controller. | Not a source of games. Wings ships **no catalogues, no sources and no download links**. Only play and use games you legally own and are permitted to install. | | Free software, GPL-3.0-or-later, built on the TV app of Orbit Store. | Not Orbit Store. The only part of Orbit's backend in Wings is its small self-update helper, adapted for Wings (see [Updating Wings](docs/guides/updating.md)). | > **Use it responsibly.** Wings is a front end: it ships no catalogues, sources or links. Use it only with content you own or have permission to download, the same as Pegasus DL asks. > > Wings never bundles or redistributes Pegasus DL, and does nothing if it is already running. If it is not running, the waiting screen offers three choices straight away: load it once, turn on Auto-Load, or load it yourself. Only when you choose, Wings downloads the author's official release from its own release page on github.com, checks it against the SHA-256 GitHub publishes, and sends it to the payload loader on this console (`127.0.0.1:9021`). It never sends while Pegasus answers and never writes into any payload manager's folder. See [Pegasus auto-load](docs/guides/pegasus-autoload.md). ## Screenshots > **Only download and install games you own.** Use Wings with your own backups and archives, or with content you have the right to download and install. Wings ships no games, catalogues, sources or links.

The games pictured are free and open-source games, shown with their own openly licensed art ([credits](app/host/fixtures/ART-CREDITS.md)); the pictures are rendered from a stand-in back-end, not a real catalogue. They show what Wings looks like, not where to get games: again, only download and install from your own archives or sources you are permitted to use. ## Credits Wings exists because of other people's work. Thank you. - **Orbit Store**, by **saawant12**: the TV app Wings began as, and the design language that made a controller-first PS5 app feel right. [orbit-store-ps5](https://github.com/saawant12/orbit-store-ps5) - **Pegasus DL**, by the developer(s) at [pegasus-ps5](https://github.com/pegasus-ps5/pegasus-dl): the download manager Wings is a front end for. - **PS5Upload**, by **phantomptr**: a great development environment while building and testing Wings. [ps5upload](https://github.com/phantomptr/ps5upload) - **ShadowMountPlus**, by **drakmor**: mounts and registers the app and your games. [ShadowMountPlus](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus) - **kstuff** ([ps5-payload-dev](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/kstuff)) and **kstuff-lite** (by **EchoStretch**, [kstuff-lite](https://github.com/EchoStretch/kstuff-lite)). - **BlackBearReloaded**: the PS5 UI kit, boilerplate and tooling (`ps5-homebrew-ui`, `ps5-native-app-boilerplate`, `ps5-opengl`). - **ps5-payload-dev** (SDK and ports) and **SvenGDK** ([SharpProspero](https://github.com/SvenGDK/SharpProspero)). - Popularity data: **IGDB.com**, **Steam** and **Wikimedia** (see [Popularity data and privacy](docs/guides/popularity-and-privacy.md)). Libraries, fonts and versions are listed in full in [CREDITS.md](CREDITS.md). If something you wrote is missing or wrong there, please open an issue. ## Features - **One game, one page.** The same game from several sources is merged into one tile. Its page groups what is available into Base, Update and DLC, then by release, with every mirror shown as a card. - **Know the link before you press it.** A card shows the host, region, the firmware it needs (and the lowest firmware a back-port runs on), format (exFAT, FPKG, PKG), version and how it will download. Where a link points at a known wrapper page, Wings takes the host from the link's name instead. - **A "Best" pick that explains itself.** A link that needs a newer firmware than yours is never Best while anything else exists. Then: native `.pkg`, debrid, automatic providers, browser capture; then firmware fit, region, format, fewer parts, known size, newest version, source order. The card says why, for example `Debrid · USA · 12.xx · exFAT · 1 file`. See [Link types and what Best means](docs/guides/link-types.md). - **Multi-part archives as one card**, with a warning when a numbered set has gaps, and a **Download all parts** action that asks first and can be stopped with Circle after the part in flight. - **Filters that fit the data.** On a game page: firmware ("Runs on my firmware"), region, format, host, source, single file only, no browser needed. The Store grid has its own filters and a "Single file only" switch. The sort of mirrors inside a release can be Best, newest, fewest parts or host. - **Search like the PlayStation one.** Triangle opens a search box with an on-screen keyboard, results update as you type, recent searches are kept as chips. The touchpad slides over the keys and a click types. - **A Files tab built for a controller.** One list from `/` with drive chips and a breadcrumb, multi-select, copy, move, rename, delete, extract, install `.pkg`, a "Where to?" destination browser, an operations list with a visible way to cancel. - **Archive passwords.** When an archive asks for a password Wings tries six well-known public passwords one at a time before it asks you. See [Archive passwords](docs/guides/archive-passwords.md). - **Everything Pegasus does, in one place.** Downloads queue, Library (installed games and APR Emu), Sources, Logs, and Settings split into **Wings** (kept on the console by Wings) and **Pegasus DL** (changes Pegasus, labelled as such). - **Cover art.** Store posters are downloaded over HTTPS by Wings itself and cached on the console (up to 96 MiB). **On by default**; turn it off in Settings. - **Optional popularity.** Sort by most popular or highest rated, and show a score and rating on tiles, from a small public data file. **On by default**; turn it off in Settings. See [Popularity data and privacy](docs/guides/popularity-and-privacy.md). - **Tile details setting.** Store tiles show their link tier and regions Always, On focus (default) or Never. - **Choose where art comes from.** Settings > Wings > Art sources: cover icons from the catalogue (default) or from Prosperopatches (each title's PS5 icon), and the wide picture behind a game's page from every source (default) or from Prosperopatches only (the PS5's own background). - **Updates itself, on your say-so.** Wings checks this project's latest release when it starts and tells you if a newer one exists. You can download it from Settings > Wings > Updates; Wings verifies it (size, SHA-256 and the image itself) and installs it only after you confirm, keeping the old file until the new one is in place. Where the console does not allow the swap, it shows the exact steps. See [Updating Wings](docs/guides/updating.md). ## Install **You need** a PS5 that can run homebrew, with: - **kstuff**, so a fake-signed app starts, and - **ShadowMountPlus**, so the package mounts and its tile appears. This is the same setup Orbit Store asks for. Pegasus DL must be running on the console when you open Wings. 1. Download `PPSA99178.ffpkg` from the [latest release](https://github.com/LaRazaDelSol/wings-app/releases/latest). 2. Check the file. On Windows, in PowerShell: `Get-FileHash .\PPSA99178.ffpkg -Algorithm SHA256`. The value must equal the SHA-256 shown on the release page (case does not matter). If it does not, download again. VirusTotal scans: [PPSA99178.ffpkg](https://www.virustotal.com/gui/file/7597dc7c53f4174302af89aafa1d049745564c0b8f76433b6fade88e4a05105d) · [PPSA99178-Alternative.zip](https://www.virustotal.com/gui/file/f14f05763f85e9863a8d9b63c0b4ce0c48344cc68b7fa8e2e17026aec84b610e) 3. Copy the file to `/data/homebrew/` on the console (FTP or your usual file transfer). Check that the size on the console equals the size on the release page. 4. Wait about ten seconds. ShadowMountPlus registers it and a **Wings** tile appears in the Games row. 5. Open **Wings**. Wings 0.1.3 and newer update themselves: when a new version is out, Wings offers it and does Download and Install for you; then close Wings and open it again (see [Updating Wings](docs/guides/updating.md)). By hand: replace the file, remove the staged copies ShadowMountPlus made, then close Wings and open it again. To remove Wings, close it, delete `/data/homebrew/PPSA99178.ffpkg` (or the folder `/data/homebrew/PPSA99178/`), and restart the jailbreak chain so the tile disappears. Optionally delete `/data/wings/` (diagnostics and a copy of the settings) and `/data/wings-helper/` (the update helper's download). Pegasus DL and its downloads are not touched. Wings writes only to its own folders: `/download0/wings/` (cover cache, settings, diagnostics, bad-link marks, inside the title's storage) and `/data/wings/` (diagnostics and a copy of the settings, so you can read them in the file manager). When you install an update, its helper also writes `/data/wings-helper/` and replaces `/data/homebrew/PPSA99178.ffpkg` (keeping the old one as `.old`). ## Quick start 1. Start Pegasus DL on the console and wait until its web UI answers. 2. Open Wings. A pill at the top right says "Connecting", then "Pegasus DL" with its version. If it says **Waiting for Pegasus DL**, Wings keeps trying; start Pegasus. 3. **Store**: tiles for your catalogue, one per game. Triangle searches, Options opens utilities, and the sort and filter button sits in the grid header. 4. Cross on a tile opens its page. The **Best** card is on top; Cross downloads it. Pegasus takes over: watch it in **Downloads**. 5. When it finishes, **Library** shows installed games and **Files** shows where things are. 6. First-run settings worth a look: Settings, **Wings** group, **Link ranking** (your firmware, region and format, so Best fits your console) and **Cover art** / **Popularity data** (both on by default). More detail: [Getting started](docs/guides/getting-started.md). ## Guides | Guide | | |---|---| | [Getting started](docs/guides/getting-started.md) | Tabs, first run, settings to set once | | [Finding and downloading a game](docs/guides/finding-and-downloading.md) | Search, filters, game page, queue | | [Link types and what Best means](docs/guides/link-types.md) | Colours, tiers, the ranking order | | [The Files tab](docs/guides/files-tab.md) | Browse, select, copy, move, extract, install, cancel | | [Archive passwords](docs/guides/archive-passwords.md) | The auto-try, the prompt, "choose what to keep" | | [After a download: ShadowMount scan](docs/guides/after-install-scan.md) | Why a new game waits for Wings to close, and the banner | | [Updating Wings](docs/guides/updating.md) | How Wings tells you about a new release, and how to install it | | [Popularity data and privacy](docs/guides/popularity-and-privacy.md) | What is fetched, from where, how to stop it | | [Troubleshooting and FAQ](docs/guides/troubleshooting.md) | Waiting for Pegasus, covers, "extraction failed", diagnostics | ## Controls | Button | In lists and grids | In the keyboard | |---|---|---| | Cross | Open / confirm | Type the key | | Circle | Back / up | Cancel (keeps your old search) | | Square | Favourite a game; select a file | Delete | | Triangle | Search; actions menu in Files | Space (shows the text in a password field) | | Options | Utilities (Store), Filters (game page), Operations (Files) | Run the search | | L1 / R1 | Switch tab | Move the cursor | | R2 | | Run the search | | L2 | | Shift | | R3 / L3 | | Symbols / Clear | | Touchpad | Swipe to scroll or switch tab; click to filter in Files | Slide over the keys, click to type | On a download in Downloads, Cross opens its actions (resume, retry, enter a password, choose what to keep). In Files, while an operation runs, Square cancels it and Triangle opens its destination. ## Privacy Wings has no account, no telemetry that this project operates, and no analytics. To the best of the source tree, the console connects to: | When | To | Why | |---|---|---| | Always | `127.0.0.1:6970` (Pegasus DL on the same console) | Everything Wings shows and does goes through it. | | Cover art **on** (default) | Cloudflare `1.1.1.1` and Google `8.8.8.8` over HTTPS (DNS-over-HTTPS) | Looking up cover servers. They see the host names, for example `image.api.playstation.com`. | | Cover art **on** | The cover servers named in your catalogue's poster URLs, over HTTPS | Downloading the images. Those servers see the console's IP address. | | Only when you press Check, or at most every 6 hours while Settings > Pegasus DL is open (needs Cover art on) | `api.github.com` (the author's release list, one small file) | Showing the latest official Pegasus DL version. GitHub sees the console's IP address. | | Only when you press Download and confirm | `github.com`, then GitHub's `objects.githubusercontent.com` | The official `Pegasus-dl.elf` (about 20 MB), checked against GitHub's SHA-256 before it is saved. Nothing else is accepted. | | Popularity **on** (default) | `larazadelsol.github.io` (GitHub Pages), one file, at most once per 24 hours and once after Wings is updated | Scores and ratings, keyed by title ID. GitHub sees the console's IP address. The file has no user data and Wings sends no identifier beyond a fixed `WingsTV/0.1` User-Agent. | | Known-problem notes or the featured carousel **on** (default) | `larazadelsol.github.io`, two more small files (`notes.v1.json`, `curated.v1.json`), on the same schedule | A short note on games known not to download, and the list of featured games, keyed by title ID. Same User-Agent, no user data. Turn them off in Settings > Wings > Store extras. | | Popularity **on** and Cover art **on**: game-page pictures | The hosts named in the popularity data: `cdn.prosperopatches.com`, `images.igdb.com`, `cdn.cloudflare.steamstatic.com` (HTTPS) | The 16:9 picture behind a game's page, fetched when you open the page and, ahead of time, for the one game your cursor rests on for half a second (at most one every 6 seconds). Those servers see the console's IP address and the picture asked for. Art sources > *Prosperopatches only* limits this to the first host. | | Art sources set to **Prosperopatches** (off by default; needs Cover art on) | `cdn.prosperopatches.com` over HTTPS | Cover icons and game-page backgrounds, for the titles the popularity data lists there. Prosperopatches sees the console's IP address and the image asked for. | | Update check **on** (default; needs Cover art on) | `api.github.com` (the latest release of this project, one small file), when Wings starts and then at most every 6 hours | Telling you when a newer Wings exists. GitHub sees the console's IP address and the same fixed User-Agent. Turn it off in Settings > Wings > Updates. | | Only when you press Download on the update page | `127.0.0.1:9021` (the payload loader on this console), then the update helper on `127.0.0.1:9178`, which downloads from `github.com`, `release-assets.githubusercontent.com` and `objects.githubusercontent.com` | The new Wings package (about 55 MB) and its `.sha256` file, checked before it is kept. GitHub sees the console's IP address. | | Only when you choose **Open TorBox website** | The PS5 browser opens `torbox.app`, through Pegasus DL | Checking what TorBox is preparing for you. Wings itself sends nothing to TorBox. | Turn **Cover art** off and Popularity (which needs it) stops too: Wings then makes **no internet connection at all**. Pegasus DL has its own network behaviour (sources, debrid, downloads); that is Pegasus, not Wings. Details: [Popularity data and privacy](docs/guides/popularity-and-privacy.md). The diagnostics report (`/data/wings/diagnostics.txt`) contains no tokens or links and is meant to be safe to share. The title log (`app.log`) can contain Pegasus log lines; read it before posting. ## Build from source From the repository root, inside WSL with Docker: `bash tools/build-wings-wsl.sh` (add `WITH_TEST=1` for the host unit tests and `WITH_PREVIEW=1` for the PNG preview). See [docs/build.md](docs/build.md). The core library (`core/`) builds with any C++17 compiler; see [core/README.md](core/README.md). ## License Wings is free software under the **GNU General Public License, version 3 or (at your option) any later version**, the same license as the Orbit Store TV app it is built on. See [LICENSE](LICENSE), [NOTICE](NOTICE) and [CREDITS.md](CREDITS.md). It comes with no warranty. Pegasus DL is not part of this project and is not covered by this license.

latestRelease.name: Wings v.0.1.3
latestRelease.body:
## Wings 0.1.3

### Wings updates itself

From now on you never copy files to update Wings. When a new version is out, Wings tells you when it starts and opens an update page with four steps:

1. **Check** - finds the new version.
2. **Download** - downloads it and checks it against the published SHA-256, with progress and Cancel.
3. **Install** - puts it in place in a few seconds. Your current version is kept until the new one runs, so nothing is lost if something goes wrong.
4. **Restart Wings** - close Wings and open it again. That's it.

A small helper inside Wings does the file work (the app itself may not write to `/data/homebrew/`). It only talks to Wings on the console itself, only downloads this project's official package from GitHub, and quits by itself when done. Details: `docs/guides/updating.md`.

### Downloads

- **Dropped downloads reconnect by themselves.** At high speeds some debrid hosts cut connections; Wings now restarts the download automatically (up to 3 tries without progress, more as long as data keeps flowing) and shows "Reconnecting in 8 s (try 2 of 3)". Real errors (file removed, disk full) are never retried. Switch: Settings > Pegasus DL > Auto-reconnect dropped downloads.
- **Circle cancels any waiting screen at once.** "Asking Pegasus DL...", checking a link, Download all parts, loading Pegasus: Circle goes back right away, and a request that answers late changes nothing.
- **.pkg links download fast, then install.** "PKG to PS5" links now go through Pegasus DL's fast download, then install, instead of the PS5's slower downloader. The .pkg is deleted after it installs (Settings > Pegasus DL > Keep PKG files after install). If the fast path is not available, Wings falls back to the PS5's downloader.

### Links

- **Bad links are remembered.** When a link fails for good (file removed, wrong file, broken archive, password never works), Wings marks it on your console and Best stops picking it. The card says "Failed for you on 14 Oct: file removed". Press **Triangle** on a link card to mark or clear one yourself; Settings > Wings lists them. Marks stay on your console and expire after 60 days.

### TorBox

- When TorBox is still preparing a file on its server, Wings now says so and asks again every 30 seconds (Circle stops it) instead of failing.
- **Open TorBox website**: Settings > Pegasus DL > TorBox opens your TorBox dashboard in the PS5 browser.

**Update from 0.1.2 (this one time by hand):** replace `/data/homebrew/PPSA99178.ffpkg` with the new file, remove the staged copies ShadowMountPlus made of the old one, close Wings and open it again. After this, Wings updates itself.

**You need:** a jailbroken PS5 with kstuff and ShadowMountPlus, and Pegasus DL (tested with 1.11.0).

Not affiliated with Pegasus DL, Orbit Store or Sony. GPL-3.0-or-later, built on the Orbit Store TV app. Please report bugs with `/data/wings/diagnostics.txt` attached (no tokens or links in it).

repos.readme:
# rpcs3-PS5

[![Follow @_roberth_ on X](https://img.shields.io/badge/follow-%40__roberth__-000000?style=for-the-badge&logo=x&logoColor=white)](https://x.com/_roberth_)

> [!CAUTION]
> **EXPERIMENTAL. EXPECT CRASHES, FREEZES AND BROKEN GAMES.**
>
> This is an early, unofficial port, tested on a single console with a handful of games.
> It is **not** supported by the RPCS3 team: do not report problems with it to them.
>
> - Most games are untested; many will crash back to the PS5 home screen or freeze.
> - It runs as a homebrew title on a jailbroken console. Jailbreaks, payloads and
>   unsigned titles carry their own risks; you use all of this **at your own risk**.
> - Back up anything on `/data/rpcs3/` (saves, settings) that you care about.

> [!WARNING]
> **Source only, personal use only.** Never share built `eboot.bin`/title folders,
> firmware, keys or games. The licenses involved forbid it (below).

Build scripts for running [RPCS3](https://rpcs3.net) (the PlayStation 3 emulator) as a
native title on a jailbroken PS5. RPCS3 renders through Vulkan on
[PS5_Vulkan](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Vulkan)'s RADV port, plays audio through
SceAudioOut and reads DualSense controllers through ScePad. The frontend is RPCS3's own
Big Picture Mode.

**Source only.** This repository holds no binaries, firmware, keys or games, and builds
from it must not be redistributed. RPCS3 is GPL-2.0-only, and PS5_Vulkan and
PS5_PayloadSDK are GPL-3.0: the combined title cannot be shared under either license.
Build it yourself, for your own console.

Tested on a PS5 Pro, firmware 13.60, with the Relapse jailbreak, etaHEN, ftpsrv and
ShadowMount+. Need for Speed Carbon (BLUS30016) is fully playable.

## Screenshots

Captured over Remote Play on a PS5 Pro (Need for Speed Carbon, BLUS30016).

| | |
| --- | --- |
| ![The RPCS3 title on the PS5 home screen](media/ps5-home-screen.jpg) | ![RPCS3 compiling Carbon's PPU and SPU code on first launch](media/carbon-compiling.jpg) |
| ![Carbon's main menu](media/carbon-main-menu.jpg) | ![Carbon gameplay at 60 fps with the performance overlay](media/carbon-gameplay.jpg) |

## What you need

- An Arch/CachyOS host (others work if you install the equivalents):

  ```bash
  sudo pacman -S --needed base-devel clang llvm lld make python python-pip git curl \
    unzip tar pkgconf cmake ninja nasm glslang \
    spirv-llvm-translator libclc spirv-headers python-ply
  ```

- About 20 GB of disk space. A first build takes about 10 minutes on a 16-core
  desktop (LLVM and RADV are the slow parts); expect longer on smaller machines.
- On the console: an FTP server on port 2121 (ftpsrv) and ShadowMount+ to register the
  title.
- Your own PS3 firmware (`PS3UPDAT.PUP` from playstation.com) and your own game dumps.

## Building

```bash
git clone https://github.com/lavavex/rpcs3-PS5.git
cd rpcs3-PS5
tools/bootstrap.sh
```

`bootstrap.sh` runs these steps in order; each one skips work it has already done, so
re-run it after fixing a failure:

| Step | Script | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pinned sources | `tools/fetch-deps.sh` | `deps/PS5_*`, RPCS3's submodules |
| PS5 payload SDK fork | `tools/install-sdk.sh` | `deps/sdk-rpcs3` |
| RADV driver, ps5-native-tool, libc.prx | `tools/build-driver-chain.sh` | `deps/PS5_Vulkan/.deps/native/radv-release` |
| LLVM for the recompilers | `tools/build-llvm.sh` | `deps/llvm-ps5` |
| zlib, libiconv, FFmpeg | `tools/build-{zlib,libiconv,ffmpeg}.sh` | `deps/*-ps5` |
| Per-game settings database | `tools/update-config-database.sh` | `deps/config_database.json` |
| RPCS3 | `tools/build-rpcs3.sh` | `dist/PPSA99300` |

After changing RPCS3's code, rebuild with `ninja -C build/rpcs3-ps5 rpcs3_ps5`.

## Installing

Close RPCS3 on the console first (a running title's files cannot be replaced), then:

```bash
PS5_HOST=192.168.x.x tools/deploy.sh
```

This uploads `dist/PPSA99300` to `/data/homebrew/PPSA99300`, and ShadowMount+ adds it to
the home screen.

## First run

Put these in `/data/rpcs3/` on the console over FTP:

- `PS3UPDAT.PUP`: installed on the next launch, then you can delete it.
- Games: copy disc game folders (each holding `PS3_GAME/`) to `/data/rpcs3/games/`, or to
  a `games/` folder on an exFAT USB drive.

RPCS3 opens in Big Picture Mode with your games listed. Players 1–4 are the DualSenses of
the signed-in users. Options + touchpad acts as the PS button.

For a custom home-screen background, convert a 16:9 image with
`deps/PS5_Vulkan/tools/prepare-assets.sh --background <image> --output-directory title/sce_sys`
and rebuild; `pic0.dds`/`pic1.dds` stay out of git.

Settings, logs and caches live in `/data/rpcs3/` (log: `/data/rpcs3/cache/RPCS3.log`).
To boot one game straight away, write its path (or a `.pkg` to install) into
`/data/rpcs3/boot.txt`.

## Known issues

- **Few games tested.** Need for Speed Carbon (BLUS30016) plays at 60 fps. inFAMOUS (BCUS98119)
  plays, but stutters and runs below full speed in places. Nothing else has been tried yet.
- **The first launch of a game is slow.** RPCS3 compiles the game's PPU and SPU code and its
  shaders, and stutters while it does. The caches in `/data/rpcs3/cache` make later launches
  faster.
- **No video previews.** A game's details page in Big Picture Mode shows its icon, not its
  preview video.
- **The CPU usage in RPCS3's log is wrong** (a constant 6.3%): the PS5 does not report process
  CPU time. The performance overlay's PPU/SPU/RSX figures are correct.
- **A crash or freeze closes the title** without a message. The reason is in
  `/data/rpcs3/cache/RPCS3.log` (copy it off before relaunching: each launch replaces it).

## Layout

| Path | What |
| --- | --- |
| `src/rpcs3` | Submodule: [lavavex/rpcs3](https://github.com/lavavex/rpcs3), branch `ps5` (upstream RPCS3 plus the PS5 port; the frontend is `rpcs3/ps5/`) |
| `cmake/ps5-rpcs3.cmake` | CMake toolchain for the title |
| `tools/link-title.sh` | Links the title with RADV and signs `eboot.bin` |
| `title/sce_sys` | Title metadata (`PPSA99300`) and icon |
| `docs/` | Notes on the PS5 memory model |
| `PINS.md` | Pinned revisions of every dependency, and how to update them (`tools/sync-forks.sh`) |

## Credits

- [RPCS3](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3) and its contributors.
- mihawk-99 for PS5_Vulkan, PS5_Mesa, PS5_PayloadSDK and PS5_LLVM, and the earlier RPCS3
  port notes this one follows.
- Swordpdf's [PS5SX2](https://github.com/Swordpdf/PS5SX2) for the memory model.
- [ps5-payload-dev](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev) for the SDK.
- blackbearreloaded's [ps5-opengl](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-opengl) for
  the shader compiler.

## License

The scripts in this repository are GPL-3.0-or-later (`LICENSE`). RPCS3 and the other
dependencies keep their own licenses.

repos.description: PS5 hardware H.264 game streaming prototype for firmware 13.60
repos.readme:
# Stream8

Stream8 is an open-source game-streaming payload for a jailbroken PlayStation 5.
It captures the active game through the console's hardware H.264/AAC capture
path and sends it over the local network to Edge or Chrome. It does not start a
Remote Play session or carry controller input: the DualSense stays connected
directly to the PS5.

## v0.4.2 at a glance

- Tested on PS5 firmware **13.60**.
- **1920×1080 at 60 FPS** using the console's hardware H.264 encoder.
- Approximately **30 Mbps** during motion, with live measured bitrate.
- **AAC-LC 48 kHz stereo** game audio, synchronized in the browser.
- Selectable 60/80/120/200/400 ms playback profiles.
- Short-burst protection and late-frame recovery for smoother playback.
- Live source FPS, displayed FPS, Mbps, buffer, queue, jitter and drop metrics.
- Windows setup app for settings, injection, bridge startup and the viewer.
- Dynamic `SceGameLiveStreaming` discovery; no fixed PID.
- Tested game switching with Red Dead Redemption 2 and Lego Batman.

The v0.4.2 hardware test at the 60 ms profile remained fluid with queue drops
and late drops at zero. Results depend on the game, network and receiving PC.

> [!WARNING]
> This release contains firmware-specific offsets and is for **firmware 13.60
> only**. Do not inject it on another firmware.

## Architecture

```text
Active PS5 game
       │ composited game video + audio
       ▼
SceGameLiveStreaming / libSceAvcap2
       │ hardware H.264 + AAC
       ▼
Stream8 payload, TCP :9070
       │ trusted local network
       ▼
PC bridge, HTTP :9090
       │ framed media packets
       ▼
Edge/Chrome WebCodecs → canvas + Web Audio
```

Stream8 runs inside `SceGameLiveStreaming`, not inside the game. It captures
the active game's output and leaves gameplay input local to the console.

## Requirements

- Jailbroken PS5 on firmware 13.60 with an ELF loader (normally port 9021).
- A firmware-compatible [NineS](https://github.com/buzzer-re/NineS) injector.
  The tested dynamic variant listens on port 9041 and includes the patch in
  [`patches/nines-fw1360-dynamic.patch`](patches/nines-fw1360-dynamic.patch).
- Windows PC with Python 3.
- Microsoft Edge or Google Chrome with WebCodecs.
- Wired Ethernet is strongly recommended.

NineS is a separate project and its binary is intentionally not distributed.
Place your compatible binary at:

```text
payloads/stream8-injector-dynamic-fw1360.elf
```

## Quick start: desktop app

1. Reboot the PS5 before replacing an older resident Stream8 build.
2. Apply the jailbreak and start the PS5 ELF loader.
3. Open a game and wait until gameplay is visible.
4. Put the compatible NineS ELF in `payloads` as described above.
5. On the PC, run:

   ```powershell
   .\start-stream8-app.ps1
   ```

6. Enter the PS5 address, confirm the ports and click **Iniciar Stream8**.
7. In the viewer, click **Activar audio** when prompted by the browser.

The app remembers machine-specific settings in `.runtime`, which Git ignores.
It does not perform the jailbreak and refuses an unsafe duplicate reinjection
when a resident instance appears unhealthy.

See [`docs/DESKTOP_APP.md`](docs/DESKTOP_APP.md) for all controls.

## Command-line start

With the injector binary in `payloads`, replace the example address with the
PS5 address:

```powershell
.\start-stream8.ps1 -Ps5Ip 192.168.1.50
```

The launcher loads NineS when needed, deploys Stream8, verifies port 9070,
starts the localhost bridge and opens a normal Edge/Chrome app window. Keep the
terminal open while streaming; `Ctrl+C` stops the PC bridge, not the PS5
payload.

## Changing games

1. Leave the viewer open while closing the old game.
2. Start the replacement game and wait until it is fully running.
3. Click **Reconectar video** in the viewer.

Stream8 v0.4.2 captures games, not the PS5 system menu. Reconnecting during the
menu or transition can leave Sony's title-bound capture source waiting, so
reconnect only after the new game is ready.

## Building the payload

Install the [PS5 Payload SDK](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk), set
`PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK`, then run:

```sh
make
```

The validated build is written to:

```text
payloads/stream8-v0.3.0-audio-1080p60-30mbps-fw1360.elf
```

Release ELF SHA-256:

```text
3B059DDA9333B7F615D7AC9138D74A2563EA617E1F2872A19A6A984AEBC458ED
```

## Safety and limitations

- Firmware 13.60 only. A reboot is the supported recovery and update path.
- Do not kill `SceGameLiveStreaming`; doing so can cause PS5 system software
  error `CE-108262-9`.
- Do not inject a second Stream8 instance over an unhealthy resident instance.
- No PS5 system-menu capture.
- One viewer connection is recommended.
- No authentication or encryption. Use only on a trusted LAN and never expose
  ports 9041 or 9070 to the internet.
- The 30 Mbps setting is a target/ceiling; measured bitrate varies by scene.
- Homebrew software is experimental and cannot be guaranteed risk-free.

## Documentation

- [`docs/RELEASE_V0.4.2.md`](docs/RELEASE_V0.4.2.md) — release notes.
- [`docs/DESKTOP_APP.md`](docs/DESKTOP_APP.md) — setup app usage.
- [`docs/DYNAMIC_INJECTOR.md`](docs/DYNAMIC_INJECTOR.md) — dynamic injector.
- [`docs/STREAM_FORMAT.md`](docs/STREAM_FORMAT.md) — media and viewer behavior.

## License

MIT. NineS and the PS5 Payload SDK are separate projects with their own
licenses.

latestRelease.body:
# Stream8 v0.4.2

Released on 2026-10-17 for PS5 firmware 13.60.

## Highlights

- 1920×1080 at 60 FPS through the PS5 hardware H.264 encoder.
- Runtime bitrate target of 30 Mbps, with live measured Mbps in the viewer.
- Synchronized AAC-LC 48 kHz stereo game audio.
- Windows setup app and one-command launcher.
- Dynamic `SceGameLiveStreaming` PID discovery.
- Selectable 60/80/120/200/400 ms playback profiles.
- A 300 ms grace window for short decoder/network bursts.
- Immediate recovery for frames that are genuinely late.
- Source FPS, displayed FPS, buffer, queue, jitter, burst and drop telemetry.

## Tested result

The 60 ms profile remained fluid during the final hardware test, with queue
drops and late drops at zero. Game switching was tested between Red Dead
Redemption 2 and Lego Batman by waiting for the replacement title to be fully
running and then using **Reconectar video**.

## Payload

```text
payloads/stream8-v0.3.0-audio-1080p60-30mbps-fw1360.elf
SHA-256 3B059DDA9333B7F615D7AC9138D74A2563EA617E1F2872A19A6A984AEBC458ED
```

The payload itself keeps its v0.3.0 media-format filename because v0.4.x
changes are in the PC setup application and browser playout layer.

## Upgrade note

Reboot the PS5 before replacing a resident payload. The desktop app can reuse
an already healthy matching payload, but it intentionally refuses to inject a
second instance over an unhealthy one.

repos.description: PKG Sender — install PS4/PS5 packages over LAN. Pick games on PC, auto-find the console, queue and install. No USB, no manual IP.
repos.readme: # PS4 PS5 PKG Sender **PKG Sender** installs PlayStation games over LAN from your PC: pick games, they queue up and install on the console. No USB juggling, no manual IP typing. PS5 **PKG** games install fine, no FPKG patching needed on your side. Disc images (`.exfat` / `.ffpfsc` / `.ffpkg`) copy straight to `/data/homebrew`. ## Download Get `PkgSender-Setup-X.Y.Z.exe` from [Releases](../../releases) — self-contained, no .NET needed, no admin needed. On Linux: the `.deb` from the CI workflow installs to `/usr/lib/pkgsender` with a `pkgsender` menu entry; the portable `PkgSender-X.Y.Z-linux-x64.tar.gz` and `PkgSender-X.Y.Z-linux-x64.AppImage` run from anywhere. All are self-contained, no .NET needed: ```sh tar -xzf PkgSender-X.Y.Z-linux-x64.tar.gz && ./PkgSender ``` > ⚠ **`pkg-receiver.elf` is PS5 ONLY.** PS4 does NOT need any ELF — it uses > Remote Package Installer or GoldHEN (see [Tutorial — PS4](#tutorial--ps4)). > Sending the ELF to a PS4 will not work. | Console | What runs on the console | Shipped where | | ------- | ------------------------ | ------------- | | PS5 | `pkg-receiver.elf` (send once via WebKit, stays listening on `12800`) | attached to the release + inside the PC install folder | | PS4 | **Remote Package Installer** homebrew (port `12800`) **or** GoldHEN with Payload Server on (ports `9090`/`9021`/`9020`) — install either yourself | not shipped, get it from its own release | On first launch the About window opens (support links live there). --- ## Screenshots ![PKG Sender compact view](docs/screenshot-compact.png) ![Sending ASTRO BOT to PS5](docs/screenshot-sending.png) ![Console browser — Images view](docs/screenshot-console-images.png) --- ## Tutorial — PS5 ### 1. Start the receiver on the console 1. Jailbreak your PS5 and send `pkg-receiver.elf` (it ships inside the PC install folder). 2. Wait for the console toast *listening on port 12800*. 3. On first run the receiver also installs a **pkg remote installer** shortcut on the PS5 home screen (Media category, `PKGS12800`). ### 2. Connect PC and console Put the console on the same network as this PC (Wi-Fi or LAN). The console itself needs no internet. See [LAN connection](#lan-connection) below for the direct-cable option. Open PKG Sender — it finds the console by itself (receiver beacon first, LAN sweep as fallback). If the console got a new DHCP address, it asks: *switch to it?* Press **Test** to verify (status dot goes green). ### 3. Install a PKG game 1. Press **Scan drives…** (or **+ Add folder**, or just drag files/folders onto the window), select games, press **Send PKG**. 2. Updates and DLCs stay glued to their base game (exact Title ID — regions stay separate). Click the 🔗 chip on a card to show only that family. 3. Watch the send queue: per-file progress, pause, reorder, retry. Tick **PS4 console** only for PS4 targets (see below) — PS5 queues natively. ### 4. Install from the console browser (no PC walking) 1. In PKG Sender press **Share to console**. The status bar shows the catalog URL (`http://:9898/catalog`). 2. On the PS5, open the **pkg remote installer** home-screen shortcut (or browse to `http://:12800/`). 3. **Games** tab: base games with covers; click one for details, install updates/DLCs individually or everything at once with **Install all**. 4. **Images** tab: disc images with a **Copy to homebrew** button each. Copy progress (percent + speed) shows above the list with **Pause** / **Cancel copy** — works even for copies started from the PC app. 5. The header shows `page X • receiver Y` — if they differ, resend the newest ELF. ### 5. Copy a disc image (PC side) Select `.exfat` / `.ffpkg` / `.ffpfsc` rows and press **Copy images** — they land in `/data/homebrew`. Each copy gets a queue row with live progress; ⏸ pauses the receiver, ✕ cancels it for real (partial file stays for resume). --- ## Tutorial — PS4 > No ELF, no USB, no FTP. The PS4 only needs a jailbreak plus one installer > service (below). PKG Sender pushes an install task to it; the PS4 then > downloads the PKG from your PC over plain HTTP (port `9898`). ### 1. Prepare the console Jailbreak the PS4 and start **one** of these (the app tries them in this order): 1. **Remote Package Installer (RPI)** — install the RPI `.pkg` on the PS4 and run it (serves its API on port `12800`). Easiest path, use this one. Get it from the author: (Releases page). 2. **GoldHEN with Payload Server enabled** — enable it in GoldHEN settings (ports `9090` / `9021` / `9020`). PKG Sender injects its installer payload itself; you install nothing extra. ### 1b. Install speed (measured, same gigabit LAN) | Path | Typical speed | Why | | ---- | ------------- | --- | | RPI (recommended) | ~75 MB/s | RPI's own downloader, 2 parallel 16 MB streams | | GoldHEN | ~50 MB/s | BGFT pulls the manifest pieces strictly one-by-one in 16 MB chunks — a console-side pipeline cap, not your network | Reference points on the same setup: USB install ~100 MB/s, plain LAN file transfer ~100 MB/s, PKG Sender's own HTTP server benchmarks at 2000+ MB/s loopback. So if install speed matters, do not use the GoldHEN path — use RPI. No PC-side tuning raises the GoldHEN path further. ### 2. Connect and test Same network as the PC (see [LAN connection](#lan-connection)). In PKG Sender type the console IP and press **Test** — it reports which mode it found (`RPI` or `GoldHEN`). ### 3. Install a PKG game 1. Drag & drop the `.pkg` file onto the window — it goes **straight to the send queue** (nothing is added to the library). Or scan/add a folder and select games, then press **Send PKG**. 2. Tick **PS4 console** above the queue — PS4 installs go strictly one-by-one (a PS5 queues natively, a PS4 does not). 3. What happens per mode: - **RPI**: the PC sends the file URL to `http://:12800/api/install`; the PS4 downloads and installs it itself. Watch it appear in RPI on the TV. - **GoldHEN**: payload injection over the binloader ports, then the PS4 pulls the PKG from your PC. If the console reports a BGFT error (`0x80990033`), it couldn't reach `http://:9898` — check the firewall rule and that the PC IP in the app is your real LAN address. 4. The queue row stays live until the download finishes; **Resume** continues a stopped one instead of starting over. No FTP is involved on either console — all transfers are plain HTTP from the PC's file server (port `9898`). --- ## LAN connection ### Method 1 — Through a router The easiest option — connect both your PC and console to the same router. ``` PC ─────┐ ├── Router PS5/PS4 ┘ ``` You don't need to configure IP addresses manually. 1. Connect your PC to the router using Ethernet or Wi-Fi. 2. Connect your PS5/PS4 to the same router. 3. Start the receiver (PS5) / RPI-HEN (PS4) on the console. 4. Open PKG Sender — it discovers the console on your local network automatically. ### Method 2 — Direct Ethernet connection PC straight to PS5/PS4 with an Ethernet cable, no router. ``` PC ───────── Ethernet ───────── PS5/PS4 192.168.10.1 192.168.10.2 ``` Because there is no router providing DHCP, you must manually assign an IP address to both devices. **1. Set the PC IP address.** On Windows: Settings → Network & Internet → Ethernet → IP assignment → Edit. Select Manual, enable IPv4, and enter (on Linux, use the IPv4 → Manual tab of your network settings, e.g. NetworkManager): - IP address: `192.168.10.1` - Subnet mask: `255.255.255.0` - Gateway: leave empty - DNS: leave empty **2. Set the console IP address.** Configure the console's Ethernet connection with: - IP address: `192.168.10.2` - Subnet mask: `255.255.255.0` - Gateway: leave empty - DNS: leave empty The important part is that both devices are on the same subnet (`255.255.255.0`). **3. Start the receiver** on the console, then launch PKG Sender on your PC. In the app pick the PC address from the PC box, type the console IP, press **Test**. > ⚠ Do NOT leave a direct cable on automatic IP assignment. Windows or the console may fall back to a `169.254.x.x` address when no DHCP server is available — PKG Sender ignores these automatic link-local addresses on purpose. If the cable is plugged in but nothing is found, this is almost always the cause. --- ## Features - Zero-config networking: auto PC address, console auto-detect with switch prompt, live status dot, re-scan (↻ Detect) button - Library: cover art, Title ID, version, size; filter PS5/PS4, sort name/size, search with in-bar clear (✕) - Add games three ways: **Scan drives…**, **+ Add folder**, or **drag & drop** files/folders onto the window - Family linking: updates and DLCs stay glued to their base game (exact Title ID — regions stay separate); 🔗 chip shows the family, click to filter, click again to go back - Send queue with per-file progress, pause, reorder, retry, clear-done (orphaned rows included) - Image copies with live progress, receiver-side pause, and real cancel (partial kept for resume) - Console browser page (PS5): logo header, 5-column grid, platform badges, details modal, install-all queue, copy progress with pause/cancel - Self-updating: silent check at startup, footer button lights up on new release (off switch in About for offline PCs) - Guide window with setup + troubleshooting, first-run About --- ## Receiver API (PS5) The receiver listens on `http://:12800`. File paths are jailed under `/data/homebrew`. This API is not stable and may change between versions. | Method | Path | Input | Reply | | ------ | ---- | ----- | ----- | | GET | `/api` | — | probe (online check, no action) | | GET | `/api/status` | — | `{"busy":bool,"active":N,"pull":bool,"pullName","pullGot","pullWant","pullPaused":bool}` | | GET | `/api/pc` | — | `{"pc":"1.2.3.4","age":N}` (last PC announce, `age` -1 = never) | | GET | `/api/version` | — | `{"build":"..."}` (compare with the page header) | | GET | `/api/space` | — | `{"free":N,"total":N}` (`/data` bytes) | | GET | `/logo.png`, `/favicon.ico` | — | sender logo PNG | | POST | `/api/install` | `{"packages":[""],"name":"...","icon_url":"..."}` (`name`/`icon_url` optional) | `{"status":"success"}` or `{"status":"fail",...}` | | GET | `/install?url=` | PKG URL as query arg (+`name`, `+icon`) | starts install, plain-text reply | | GET | `/api/files/stat?path=` | remote path | `{"exists":bool,"size":N}` | | POST | `/api/files/pull` | `{"url":"http://pc:9898/pkg/id","path":"/data/homebrew/f.pkg","mode":"overwrite"/"resume"}` | `{"ok":true,"started":true}` + console toast on finish | | POST | `/api/pull/pause` | `{"paused":1/0}` | `{"ok":true,"paused":bool}` | | POST | `/api/pull/cancel` | `{}` | `{"ok":true,"cancelled":true}` (partial stays for resume) | File-explorer endpoints (`/api/fs/*`, Files tab) are temporarily disabled in the receiver. Discovery: the receiver broadcasts `PKGSENDER v1` to UDP `255.255.255.255:12801` every 3 seconds. ## Console library (pkg remote installer, PS5) Browse and install the scanned PC library from the console's own browser — no need to walk back to the PC: 1. In PKG Sender, scan your folders, then press **Share to console**. The status bar shows the catalog URL (`http://:9898/catalog`). While shared, the PC also broadcasts `PKGSENDER-PC :9898` to UDP `255.255.255.255:12802` every 3 seconds, so the console finds it automatically (no manual IP entry). 2. On first run the receiver installs a **pkg remote installer** shortcut on the PS5 home screen (Media category, `PKGS12800`). Open it — or browse to `http://:12800/` manually. 3. **Games tab**: base games only (alphabetical, with covers, sizes and IDs); click a base game for details and its updates/DLCs, each with its own Install button, or **Install all** for the whole family. Search filters by title or Title ID; chips filter PS5/PS4. 4. The **Images** tab shows disc images (exfat/ffpfsc/ffpkg) with a **Copy to homebrew** button each, plus live progress with Pause/Cancel. Published endpoints on the PC file server (`:9898`, CORS-open): | Method | Path | Reply | | ------ | ---- | ----- | | GET | `/catalog` | `[{"id","title","titleId","version","size","sizeText","role","familyKey","platform","format","file","hasIcon"}]` (`role` = Game/Patch/DLC/Image) | | GET | `/icon/{id}` | cover PNG (`image/png`) | | GET | `/pkg/{id}` | file bytes (range-capable, same as pushes use) | --- ## Credits - [ps5-web-file-manager](https://github.com/owendswang/ps5-web-file-manager) (GPL-3.0) — the home-screen web-shortcut launcher idea; reimplemented here, no code copied. - [seregonwar/zftpd](https://github.com/seregonwar/zftpd) (MIT) — pointed at PS5 TCP socket-buffer tuning as the fix for slow bulk transfers; our pull-downloader buffering was rewritten from scratch, no code copied. ## Support If you enjoy what I build and want to support my work, you can donate — every bit means a lot. 💙 [☕ برام یه قهوه بخر — coffeebede.com/loopayeh](https://coffeebede.com/loopayeh) *(🇮🇷 برای ایران — حمایت تومانی)* - USDT (BEP-20) *(🌍 بین‌المللی)*: `0x839a30D52Ef7D2b53e818b9931efd7FE6F472e50` ([send via TrustWallet](https://link.trustwallet.com/send?coin=20000714&address=0x839a30D52Ef7D2b53e818b9931efd7FE6F472e50&token_id=0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955)) - More: [loopayeh.github.io](https://loopayeh.github.io/) ## Troubleshooting - **● No receiver (red)** — the elf isn't running on the console. Send it again. On the console page, `page X • receiver Y` mismatch means the same thing. - **○ No network (gray)** — this PC has no active LAN/Wi-Fi. - **Push goes through but download never starts** — allow inbound TCP port 9898: on Windows in Windows Firewall (the installer adds this rule plus UDP 12801 for beacons); on Linux, e.g. `sudo ufw allow 9898/tcp` or `sudo firewall-cmd --permanent --add-port=9898/tcp`. - **Console IP keeps changing (DHCP)** — reopen the app or hit Detect; it offers the new address. - **Image cards without covers** — the header bridge needs `pkgviewer.py` next to the installed app (ships since 1.2.5) plus a Python with `mkpfs`; rescan after installing. ## Build from source Needs .NET 8 SDK (+ Inno Setup 6 for the installer): ```bat Build-Release.bat ``` This publishes a self-contained single-file build to `dist\`, copies in `pkg-receiver.elf` + `pkgviewer.py`, and, if `iscc` is available, produces `PkgSender-Setup-X.Y.Z.exe`. The PS5 receiver rebuilds with the ps5-payload-sdk toolchain: ```sh cd payload && make PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK=/path/to/ps5-payload-sdk ``` On Linux the tar.gz and AppImage artifacts build with .NET 8 SDK only (`DOTNET=/path/to/dotnet ./Build-Release.sh` if the SDK is not on `PATH`): ```sh ./Build-Release.sh ``` This publishes linux-x64 to `dist/` and produces `PkgSender-X.Y.Z-linux-x64.tar.gz` and `.AppImage` there (the AppImage step downloads `appimagetool` when it is not installed). The `.deb` is built separately by the `Linux .deb` CI workflow. Automated tests (updater version/asset/network logic and the Linux tar.gz self-update contract) run with: ```sh dotnet test tests/coretests/CoreTests.csproj ``` ## How updates work The app checks GitHub releases for a `PkgSender-Setup-*.exe` asset newer than its own version. **Download + Install** fetches it to a temp dir, launches it silent, and exits so Setup can overwrite the running app. On Linux it looks for the `PkgSender-*-linux-x64.tar.gz` asset instead: a portable (tar.gz) install is swapped in place — the new binary lands next to the old one (kept as `PkgSender.old`, removed on next start) and the app restarts itself. The official `.deb` and AppImage installs skip the in-place swap and ask for the usual package/update path.

repos.name: pkg-viewer
repos.description: PKG Viewer by Loopayeh: view PS3/PS4/PS5 package info and cover art
repos.readme: # PKG Viewer — PS2 / PS3 / PS4 / PS5 / Switch / Wii U / Xbox 360 ![screenshot](screenshot.png) ![trophies](screenshot-trophies.png) **PKG Viewer** shows what's inside a PlayStation or Switch game file without extracting it: cover art, title, Title ID, region, version, and required firmware. Retail (original) PKGs fully supported — including split multi-part sets. Works with `.pkg` packages, PS2/PS3 `.iso` disc images, `.exfat` / `.ffpfsc` / `.ffpkg` images, Switch `.nsp` / `.xci` files, Xbox 360 (GOD/STFS/ISO/XEX), Wii U NUS folders, and game folders. ## Download Get `PKGViewer-Setup-X.Y.Z.exe` (Windows) or `PKGViewer-macOS-arm64-X.Y.Z.zip` (Apple Silicon) / `PKGViewer-macOS-x86_64-X.Y.Z.zip` (Intel) from [Releases](../../releases) — no Python needed, no admin needed. ## Windows security warning The builds are unsigned, so Windows may warn you before running them. This is about the missing publisher signature, not about the file being unsafe. - **Windows protected your PC** (SmartScreen, "Unknown publisher") — click **More info → Run anyway**. - **Smart App Control blocked an app** (Windows 11 with Smart App Control **On**) — this one has no "Run anyway" button and cannot be bypassed by unblocking the file or adding a Defender exclusion. Run [from source](docs/troubleshooting.md#option-1--run-from-source-fastest-keeps-sac-on) instead, or turn Smart App Control off. Full walkthrough and what does *not* work: [docs/troubleshooting.md](docs/troubleshooting.md). ## Why the installer ![file icons](screenshot-icons.png) Grab `PKGViewer-Setup-X.Y.Z.exe` from [Releases](../../releases) — no admin needed: - every format gets its own icon (`.pkg` / `.exfat` / `.ffpfsc` / `.ffpkg` / `.nsp` / `.xci`) and opens on double-click — no Open With setup - shows up in `Settings → Default apps`, so all six formats go Always in one place - updates itself in place, no reinstall hassle - uninstall wipes everything clean (files, icons, registry) ## Features - Cover art preview (icon0.png, pic0.png, …) with Save / Copy to clipboard — online covers (PlayStation Store, ps2-covers, GameTDB, XboxUnity, Nintendo IDBE), cached offline - Spec card: Title ID, Content ID, version, region, Min. System, SDK, DRM - Latest patch version per game (PS5/PS4) with PKG-vs-latest compare - Files tab: folder tree built from entry paths (PS3 discs/folders, ISOs), sized per folder — single-file Extract with rename, trophy00.trp contents - Trophies tab: decrypted trophy list (name, grade, hidden) with icons, banner art, Save icons export - OFC (Official) / FPKG (Fake) detection + badges for PS4 and PS5 (incl. split parts) - Details tab: curated param.sfo / param.json, Show all for the full dump - Drag & drop: PKG files, exFAT / ffpfsc / ffpkg images, Switch NSP / XCI files, and game folders onto the window - Rename: clean uniform names from PKG info (`Title - TID - vVersion - Region`, e.g. `Elden Ring - PPSA04863 - v1.06 - EU`) — single file via the Rename button (preview + header Undo), or many at once via the Batch button / dropping them all (batch dialog with preview + All/None + revert log); folders are scanned for game files; split multi-part sets stay together; Revert restores original names from any revert log - AMPR / LZ4 asset containers (LIZARD dumps): listed with size in the spec card + Files tab - Copy/paste works in every text field, on any keyboard layout - Self-updating: silent check at startup, header button lights up on new release - Rename patterns in both dialogs: `{title} {tid} {cid} {version} {region} {type} {orig}` presets (Title ID only, Content ID, append `[Title ID]` to the original name) or a custom pattern with live preview — the last preset, pattern and Title/Title ID/Version/Region ticks are remembered - CLI mode: `pkgviewer.py --info file.pkg` (also `.nsp` / `.xci`) — batch: `pkgviewer.py --batch-rename folder [--recursive] [--apply] [--name-pattern "{orig} [{tid}]"]` (dry run without `--apply`) — revert: `pkgviewer.py --revert batch_rename_*.log [--apply]` ## Usage Drag & drop a `.pkg` / `.exfat` / `.ffpfsc` / `.ffpkg` / `.nsp` / `.xci` file or a game folder onto the exe or the open window, or use Open. To run from source (needs Python 3 + Pillow + tkinterdnd2 + mkpfs + pytsk3 + cryptography): ```bat PKGViewer.bat ``` ## Supported formats - **PS2 disc images** (`.iso`) — SYSTEM.CNF serial/version/VMODE, file listing - **PS3 packages** (`.pkg`) — retail + debug NPDRM, decrypted listing - **PS3 game folders** — NPDRM and PS3_GAME layouts - **PS4 / PS5 packages** (`.pkg`) — game, DLC, update, retail + split parts - **PS5 disk images** (`.exfat`) — game dumps - **PS5 compressed images** (`.ffpfsc`) — game dumps - **PS5 UFS2 images** (`.ffpkg`) — game dumps (needs pytsk3 from source) - **PS5 app folders** — extracted game folder (incl. LIZARD AMPR/LZ4 dumps) - **Switch packages** (`.nsp`) — game, update, DLC; official title + icon from Control NCA with `prod.keys` (put it next to the exe or in `%APPDATA%\PKGViewer\`), raw file listing without keys; per-NCA type/key info, readable firmware requirement - **Switch gamecard images** (`.xci`) — partition + file listing, cartridge info, title/icon from the secure partition - **Wii U NUS folders** — TMD title/version/contents, official Nintendo icons - **Xbox 360 GOD folders + STFS packages** — title/Media/Title ID, data parts, embedded thumbnail, online XboxUnity covers - **Xbox 360 ISO / extracted folders / XEX** — XDVDFS listing, version/disc from XEX, TU check ## Build from source ```bat pip install pyinstaller pillow python -m PyInstaller --noconfirm --clean --onefile --windowed --name PKGViewer --icon assets\logo.ico --add-data "assets;assets" --add-data "assets_about.png;." --collect-submodules PIL pkgviewer.py ``` ## Support [☕ برام یه قهوه بخر — coffeebede.com/loopayeh](https://coffeebede.com/loopayeh) *(🇮🇷 برای ایران — حمایت تومانی)* If this tool was useful, you can also support me internationally with USDT (BEP-20 / BNB Smart Chain): `0x839a30D52Ef7D2b53e818b9931efd7FE6F472e50` [Pay via Trust Wallet](https://link.trustwallet.com/send?coin=20000714&address=0x839a30D52Ef7D2b53e818b9931efd7FE6F472e50&token_id=0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955) ## Credits - PS4 extract/build engine: `LibOrbisPkg` by maxton (via PkgEditor). Optional `orbis-pub-gen`/`orbis-pub-chk` (Sony/OpenOrbis SDK tools, user-supplied). - PS5 files are view-only (no extract/build, no outside tools). - `.ffpfsc` / inner-exFAT reading via `mkpfs` library by PSBrew (RenanGBarreto + contributors incl. rdmrocha, drakmor) — GPLv3, bundled. - `.ffpkg` (UFS) reading via `pytsk3` (Sleuth Kit bindings). - Switch NCA/NACP parsing follows `hactool` (SciresM) layout; decrypt needs user-supplied `prod.keys` (dump it yourself with Lockpick_RCM) — no keys bundled. - Patch-version lookup: prosperopatches.com / orbispatches.com. - PKG Viewer itself (parsing, UI, rename, trophies, Switch support) is original code — no vendored third-party code bundled. ## License MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE). ## Contact Telegram: [@loopayeh](https://t.me/loopayeh)
