repos.name: HLDRIVE
repos.description: Gerenciador homebrew de arquivos para PS5 com Google Drive publico, downloads para o console e interface web. Versao experimental.
repos.readme: # HLDRIVE Gerenciador de arquivos homebrew para PS5, com navegação em pastas públicas do Google Drive e download direto para o console. Interface, imagens e recursos estão incorporados em um único arquivo `HLDRIVE.elf`. > **Pre-release 1.1.3-rc.1 — teste com 48 conexões.** Limite de conexões por arquivo triplicado de 16 para 48 para comparação no PS5, mantendo segmentos de 8 MiB. Ganho de velocidade ainda não confirmado. [Baixar ELF](https://github.com/louro2023/HLDRIVE/releases/download/v1.1.3-rc.1/HLDRIVE.1.1.3-rc.1.elf) · [SHA-256](https://github.com/louro2023/HLDRIVE/releases/download/v1.1.3-rc.1/HLDRIVE.1.1.3-rc.1.elf.sha256) · [Notas e limitações](docs/releases/v1.1.3-rc.1.md). **Downloads:** [ELF 1.0.2](https://github.com/louro2023/HLDRIVE/releases/download/v1.0.2/HLDRIVE.elf) · [SHA-256](https://github.com/louro2023/HLDRIVE/releases/download/v1.0.2/HLDRIVE.elf.sha256) · [Release](https://github.com/louro2023/HLDRIVE/releases/tag/v1.0.2) Veja a [galeria de telas](docs/GALLERY.md), [histórico de alterações](CHANGELOG.md) e [instruções de compilação](docs/BUILD.md). **Miniatura no Payload Manager:** adicione a [fonte HLDRIVE](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/louro2023/HLDRIVE/main/repository/payloads.json) em **Settings → Manage Sources → Add Source**. Depois procure HLDRIVE em **Get Payloads**. [Instruções e funcionamento do ícone](repository/README.md). ## Funcionalidades - Selecionar Português (Brasil), English (US) ou Español (Argentina) pelo botão de bandeira no topo da interface. - Abrir links públicos do Drive e navegar por subpastas. - Salvar links de pastas com um nome opcional, reabrir pela lista e excluir links salvos. A lista fica armazenada no navegador utilizado; limpar os dados do site remove os links. - Selecionar arquivos e pastas e escolher o destino no PS5. - Acelerar arquivos grandes com até 48 conexões simultâneas por arquivo (limite experimental para testes), segmentos de 8 MiB e gravações agrupadas quando o Drive oferecer intervalos e um identificador forte; os arquivos escolhidos são baixados em fila. O painel mostra velocidade em Mbps/MiB/s, média, conexões ativas e motivo de usar conexão única. - Baixar itens selecionados ou copiar e colar arquivos no console. - Preservar pastas, acompanhar progresso e cancelar transferências. - Navegar, copiar, mover, renomear e excluir arquivos locais. - Abrir a interface no navegador e registrar um atalho na aba Mídia. - Encerrar ou remover os arquivos e configurações próprios do HLDRIVE. - Exibir QR codes discretos para inscrição no [canal do criador](https://www.youtube.com/@henriquelouro7848) e apoio financeiro. O console acessa o Drive e realiza os downloads. É necessária uma pasta compartilhada como “Qualquer pessoa com o link”; não há login Google/OAuth. ## Links salvos Cole o endereço público da pasta, informe um nome opcional e clique em **Salvar link**. Na lista **Links salvos**, use **Abrir pasta** para acessar novamente ou **Excluir** para remover somente o favorito. Excluir um link não remove arquivos do Drive nem downloads do console. Os links ficam neste navegador e endereço de acesso. Outro dispositivo, navegador ou endereço/IP terá sua própria lista; limpar os dados do site remove os favoritos. A lista impede duplicar a mesma pasta mesmo quando o link usa parâmetros de compartilhamento diferentes. ![Links salvos na interface, com dados de exemplo](docs/images/saved-links-desktop.png) ## Idioma da interface Clique na **bandeira no canto superior direito** e selecione Português (Brasil), English (US) ou Español (Argentina). O seletor reaproveita o estilo do Prospero Manager e usa bandeiras SVG incorporadas ao ELF, sem depender de emojis ou imagens externas. A mudança é imediata e preserva a seleção de arquivos. A preferência fica salva no navegador/dispositivo usado para acessar o HLDRIVE; outro navegador pode ter uma escolha diferente. O padrão é Português (Brasil). Menus, tela do Drive, transferências, gerenciador de arquivos e diálogos acompanham o idioma. Avisos conhecidos do Google Drive, como cota de downloads, permissão e arquivo indisponível, também acompanham a seleção, inclusive em transferências que já falharam. Avisos não reconhecidos do Google recebem uma mensagem genérica traduzida; o texto original permanece no log. Nomes de arquivos, caminhos e mensagens técnicas retornadas pelo backend são preservados; alguns diagnósticos podem continuar em português. [Veja as telas simuladas](docs/GALLERY.md). ## Requisitos e primeiro uso - PS5 com ambiente homebrew ativo e um método compatível para iniciar arquivos ELF. - Internet e espaço disponível no destino. 1. Baixe o arquivo `.elf` nos anexos da release e inicie-o pelo ambiente homebrew configurado no console. Nesta pré-release ele se chama `HLDRIVE.1.1.3-rc.1.elf`. 2. O payload tenta abrir `http://127.0.0.1:8081/?console=1`. Se necessário, acesse `http://IP_DO_PS5:8081` na rede local. 3. Na aba Google Drive, informe o link público da pasta. O PS5 busca e baixa os arquivos por conta própria. O atalho na aba Mídia abre a interface enquanto o processo estiver ativo; ele não inicia o ELF após reiniciar o console. Veja [compatibilidade](docs/COMPATIBILITY.md) e [validação](docs/TESTING.md). ## Downloads e exclusão Os downloads são gravados no destino escolhido. Interrupções abruptas podem deixar arquivos temporários `.part`. A fila de transferências não é retomada após reiniciar o processo. **Excluir HLDRIVE** remove o atalho, a cópia `HLDRIVE.elf` da pasta configurada e `/data/HLDRIVE`. Arquivos armazenados fora da pasta própria do HLDRIVE não são removidos. ## Limitações e segurança - O acesso ao Drive depende da disponibilidade do HTML público do Google e de `/system/common/cert/CA_LIST.cer`; a validação de certificados TLS permanece habilitada. - Pastas muito grandes, documentos nativos, atalhos, cotas ou exigência de login podem limitar downloads. - A interface local não possui autenticação. Use em rede confiável e não exponha a porta 8081 à internet. - Compatibilidade varia por firmware e ambiente homebrew. O teste relatado pelo usuário confirma o desempenho em seu console, mas não certifica outras configurações ou velocidades. ## Licença Código sob [GNU GPL v3](LICENSE). Componentes incluídos mantêm seus avisos e condições próprios; veja [avisos de terceiros](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md). O código-fonte acompanha a distribuição do ELF.

latestRelease.body:
# HLDRIVE 1.1.3-rc.1 — teste com 48 conexões

## Novidades

- Limite de download paralelo triplicado de 16 para 48 conexões por arquivo elegível, mantendo segmentos de 8 MiB e os critérios de validação de intervalos e identidade do arquivo.
- O número efetivo de conexões depende da quantidade de segmentos disponíveis e diminui ao final da transferência. A fila de arquivos permanece sequencial.
- Mantidos os links salvos, idiomas, avisos traduzidos e fundo animado da versão anterior.
- Corrigido o registro incorreto de velocidade acima de 500 Mbps: o usuário esclareceu que essa velocidade nunca foi alcançada.

## Instalação

Baixe **HLDRIVE.1.1.3-rc.1.elf** e seu **HLDRIVE.1.1.3-rc.1.elf.sha256**. Encerre o payload anterior e inicie o novo ELF pelo loader. Renomeie para `HLDRIVE.elf` se o seu método exigir esse nome.

Recarregue `http://IP_DO_PS5:8081`. A interface deve indicar **1.1.3-rc.1**; em arquivos elegíveis, o painel deve mostrar **até 48**.

## Validação e limitações

Os 21 cenários HTTPS locais passaram com verificação dos dados baixados, incluindo transferências de 400 MiB + 123 bytes usando 48 conexões, fallback sequencial, cancelamento e rejeição de respostas inválidas. Esses testes usam um servidor sintético e não medem a velocidade do Google Drive ou do PS5.

Build do frontend, checagem de traduções e compilação do ELF concluídos. A suíte offline completa não foi executada nesta alteração; há falha preexistente documentada envolvendo `RemoveSettingsAt`.

O aumento é experimental: não garante ganho de velocidade. Os buffers de escrita podem ocupar aproximadamente 48 MiB, além da memória de curl/TLS, sockets e stacks. Execução, estabilidade e desempenho precisam de teste no PS5. Compare o mesmo arquivo, rede e destino com a versão anterior.

O catálogo estável do Payload Manager permanece na versão 1.0.2. Esta pré-release é para instalação manual.

repos.readme:
# DOOM for PS5 (native) id Software's original DOOM source (`linuxdoom-1.10`) running as a native PS5 title: its own home-screen icon, drawn on the GPU through Sony's AGC driver and VideoOut, DualSense input with analog sticks and rumble, and the DOS-era FM music synthesised from the game's own instrument bank. It ships with the free shareware episode of DOOM and plays The Ultimate DOOM, DOOM II and Final DOOM from your own game files, which you can send from a PC or phone browser, download from a link or copy to the console, including straight out of ZIP, 7Z and RAR archives.

## Requirements A jailbroken PS5 with kstuff (fake-signed executables) and [ShadowMountPlus](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus). Tested on firmware 13.00. ## Install 1. Download `PPSA99666.zip` from the [releases](../../releases) and check it against `PPSA99666.zip.sha256`. 2. Extract it and copy the `PPSA99666` folder to `/data/homebrew/` (FTP, ps5upload or USB). 3. ShadowMountPlus registers it within a few seconds and **DOOM** appears on the home screen. ## Games DOOM opens on a game list. Out of the box it holds the shareware episode, *Knee-Deep in the Dead*; every game you add appears there too, and the last one you played stays selected. | File | Game | | --- | --- | | `DOOM.WAD`, `DOOMU.WAD` | DOOM, or The Ultimate DOOM when it has episode 4 | | `DOOM2.WAD` | DOOM II: Hell on Earth | | `TNT.WAD` | Final DOOM: TNT Evilution | | `PLUTONIA.WAD` | Final DOOM: The Plutonia Experiment | | `FREEDOOM1.WAD`, `FREEDOOM2.WAD` | [Freedoom](https://freedoom.github.io/) Phase 1 and 2 | The files from the original releases and from the 2024 *DOOM + DOOM II* re-release both work. ### Adding your games Whichever way, the game files can also be inside ZIP, 7Z or RAR archives: DOOM extracts the game WADs it recognises and skips everything else. - **Send them from a PC or phone.** In the game list choose *Add games...*, then *Send from PC or phone*. Open the address the screen shows (for example `http://192.168.1.50:9666/`) in a browser on the same network, or scan its QR code, and drop the files or whole folders on the page. Both the page and the console show what was added; archives are deleted once their games are out. The console only accepts files while that screen is open. - **Copy them to the console.** Put the files or archives in `/data/homebrew/PPSA99666/wads/` (FTP, ps5upload or USB). DOOM picks them up the next time it starts. - **Download them from a link.** In the game list choose *Add games...*, then *Link*, type an `http://` or `https://` address on the console keyboard and choose *Download*. The link can point at a WAD, an archive, or a folder; for a folder DOOM lists the files and you pick one or all.

## Controls | Input | In game | In menus | | --- | --- | --- | | Left stick | Move and strafe | Navigate | | Right stick | Turn (speed follows Mouse Sensitivity) | | | D-pad | Move and turn | Navigate | | R2 | Fire | | | Cross / Square | Use | Select, yes | | Circle | Strafe modifier | Back, no | | L1 / R1 | Previous / next weapon (automap zoom) | | | L2 | Run | | | Triangle / touchpad | Automap (Square: follow mode) | | | Options | Menu | Close menu | Prompts show the buttons to press, and *Read This!* in the main menu opens this list on the console. Saves and settings stay on the console, and each game keeps its own saves. Holding **L1+R1** at launch uses the CPU scaler instead of the GPU, should a firmware ever disagree with the GPU path. ## Building and internals See [DEVELOPMENT.md](DEVELOPMENT.md) for the build, the architecture, the console test loop and the PS5 behaviour learned along the way. Licenses and credits: [LICENSE](LICENSE) (GPL v2, id's source) and [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

latestRelease.body:
Sending games from a PC or phone now keeps full speed with large archives, and going back during a transfer no longer freezes the screen.

## What's new - **Large files at full speed.** A big archive used to slow down the longer it ran: the 643 MB *DOOM + DOOM II* collection 7Z fell to 0.4 MB/s past 400 MB and took over ten minutes. It now arrives at the network's speed the whole way, about a minute on a wired PS5, and its games are added a few seconds later. - **Circle stops a transfer at once.** Going back while a file was arriving froze the screen until the file was done. It now stops right away and removes the partial file. - **No stalls in the browser.** Browsers open spare connections, and the console waited on a quiet one for up to 30 seconds before answering anything else. It now answers whichever connection asks first, and replies no longer wait on Windows' delayed acknowledgements.

## Install 1. Download `PPSA99666.zip` and check it against `PPSA99666.zip.sha256`. 2. Extract it and copy the `PPSA99666` folder to `/data/homebrew/` (FTP, ps5upload or USB). Copying over an earlier version keeps your games, saves and settings. 3. ShadowMountPlus registers it within a few seconds and **DOOM** appears on the home screen. Needs a jailbroken PS5 with kstuff and ShadowMountPlus. Tested on firmware 13.00. The package contains no commercial game data. See the README for controls and `licenses/` in the package for the third-party notices. SHA-256 of `PPSA99666.zip`: `4d8e5b785b61696fbf1988c2d0d87c5c977734ff60b1ce11cc49134b0e711b5f`

repos.name: Stremio-Plus
repos.description: A PS5 Stremio homebrew app with a powerful torrent engine
repos.readme:
# Stremio Plus

> **Stremio Plus 0.5.20.** Improved Home loading, PS5 sign-in and 1080p playback,
> with right-stick volume control and a start/resume choice before playback.
> See the [release](https://github.com/LoZazaMastro/Stremio-Plus/releases/tag/0.5.20),
> [changelog](CHANGELOG.md) and [build instructions](BUILDING.md).

A native Stremio app for PlayStation 5, built around the way you watch on a TV.
Browse your catalogs, pick a stream, save something for later, and keep your
library together in an interface designed for the DualSense.

See the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md) for the latest changes and upgrade notes.

![Stremio Plus home screen](docs/images/home.jpg)

## Made for PS5

**Built with Prospero UI.** Stremio Plus uses BlackBearReloaded's
[ps5-homebrew-ui](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-homebrew-ui) to bring
fluid carousels, large artwork, smooth transitions, and translucent playback
controls to a native C++ interface. Films get room for their artwork; series
get a dedicated season selector and episode thumbnails.

**Your Stremio add-ons, including Torrentio.** Sign in with your Stremio
account to bring over your installed add-ons and library. Torrentio sources
appear alongside compatible providers, with quality, language, file size, and
seeder information when the add-on supplies it. Direct links and torrents
play on the console using its built-in playback and torrent support, without
a separate Stremio streaming server to configure.

**A dedicated torrent engine and offline downloads.** Stremio Plus has its
own native torrent engine, designed for high-throughput transfers directly
to the PS5. Download the selected movie or episode while you keep browsing,
then play it offline from a dedicated poster coverflow. Films appear as
individual covers, while a series has one cover for all its saved episodes.
Open a series to slide its poster to the left and browse episode thumbnails
in a floating panel. L1 and R1 select only the seasons represented in your
downloads. Completed films show their cover and title; saved episodes show
their thumbnail, episode number and title under the series heading. Progress,
speed, estimated time remaining, and connected peers and seeders appear only
while a transfer is unfinished. The queue
supports pause, resume, and deletion. Actual speed depends on the swarm,
connection, and storage; download performance is under active development.
Choose a download folder in Settings, including a mounted M.2 or external
volume, and create a **Stremio Plus Downloads** folder directly from the picker.
Changing that folder moves your existing downloads to the new destination.
Episode downloads keep the series title, season and episode numbers, and the
episode title together, including after a restart or when you are offline.

**VLC playback, inside the Stremio Plus interface.** The native player uses
VideoLAN's libVLC 3.0.24, adapted from [ZiZc3's VLC port for PS5](https://github.com/ZiZc3/VLC).
VLC handles media demuxing, decoding, and synchronization while Stremio Plus
keeps its Prospero UI, DualSense controls, and subtitle customization. The
PS5 modules supply hardware decoding for supported H.264, HEVC, and 8-bit
VP9 profile 0 streams. FFmpeg 8.1.2 and dav1d provide software decoding for
other supported formats.
The app follows the PS5's output resolution, with 1080p, 1440p, and 4K options.
Compatibility depends on the stream's profile and container. The OpenGL
presentation path outputs SDR, with HDR10 sources tone-mapped for display.
Playback controls appear when the first video frame reaches the GPU. If audio
starts without a video picture, the player retries the same source once using
software decoding, preserving the selected download and starting position.
If video output still fails, playback stops with an error instead of remaining
on the preparation screen indefinitely.
Slow input startup preserves the selected resume position. Changing or
automatically selecting a subtitle track does not seek or reopen the video.
Allocations of at least 1 MiB, including FFmpeg's internal buffers, decoded
pictures and video callback buffers, share a bounded, CPU-cacheable direct
memory pool. A smaller general arena leaves more of the console's memory
available on demand. Ownership tracking covers aligned allocations, resizing,
and failed kernel releases; a native-memory reserve remains available for
other resources. Critical video-decoder errors are reported to the app and
trigger one reopen at the last presented position. A repeated error stops
playback with an explicit message. Recovering from input buffering preserves HEVC reference
pictures; damaged decoder output is rejected while the last valid picture
remains visible. An explicit seek still resets the decoder as required.
Video textures are checked individually during allocation and released
when playback ends, including partial allocations from failed startup.
The app reduces its artwork cache during playback and restores the browsing
budget afterwards; saved poster images keep their original resolution.

**EVO Player contributions.** Dolby Vision Profile 5 reshaping, HDMI audio
transport, display refresh selection and native memory management incorporate
work from [EVO Player PS5 by sainsaji and contributors](https://github.com/sainsaji/EVO-PLAYER-PS5),
licensed under **GPL-3.0-or-later**. These components are adapted to Stremio
Plus's OpenGL renderer and libVLC pipeline. Their original authors, source
revision and local modifications are recorded in
[vendor/evo-player/NOTICE.md](vendor/evo-player/NOTICE.md).

**Discover without a background image.** The selected title's logo, year,
rating, runtime, genres, director, principal cast and description accompany
its catalog posters. Artwork lookups and decoding run away from the interface
thread, with selected artwork prioritized over adjacent covers and prefetch.
Downloaded series retain their cover and separate episode thumbnails for
offline browsing.

**Artwork that reaches your controller.** As you highlight a movie or series,
the DualSense light bar picks up a dominant color from its poster and eases
into the new shade. That color stays with you through loading and playback.
You can turn the effect off in Settings.

**Subtitles your way.** Choose a font, size, color, background opacity, and
effects such as an outline, shadow, or embossing. A live preview shows each
change before you return to the video. Audio and subtitle language preferences
are available separately.

**Quick add-on sync.** Your account's add-on collection loads in the background,
bringing existing configurations across without entering provider URLs on
the console. Install or configure add-ons in Stremio on your phone or computer,
then sync them in Stremio Plus.

## Screenshots

These PS5 captures show the 0.5.11 interface. Version 0.5.18 has a revised
Downloads coverflow with sharper posters, gallery sorting and simpler
completed entries, together with a revised Discover layout.

| Stream selection | Library |
| --- | --- |
| ![Torrentio stream selection](docs/images/streams.jpg) | ![Library](docs/images/library.jpg) |

| Discover | Subtitle customization |
| --- | --- |
| ![Discover with genre filters](docs/images/discover.jpg) | ![Subtitle settings and live preview](docs/images/subtitle-settings.jpg) |

![Downloads with transfer progress and connection statistics](docs/images/downloads.jpg)

## Getting started

You need a PS5 with a working native homebrew loader, a Stremio account, and
the add-ons you want to use configured on that account. Download the native
`PPSA74126.ffpfsc` image or folder archive from the
[latest release](https://github.com/LoZazaMastro/Stremio-Plus/releases/latest),
then install the format supported by your loader. Build instructions are in
[BUILDING.md](BUILDING.md). The application's title ID is `PPSA74126`.

App settings, the download directory registry, and streaming caches live in
**`/data/Stremio/appdata`**. Logs stay in **`/data/Stremio`**. The app prepares
these directories on launch. If your homebrew environment cannot create or
access the parent directory, create **`/data/Stremio`** and set its directory
permissions to **`0777`** with your file manager or FTP client. From a console
shell, the equivalent is:

```sh
mkdir -p /data/Stremio
chmod 0777 /data/Stremio
```

The homebrew environment must allow the app to access that directory and
provide a local ELF loader on port `9021`. The app uses that loader for its
filesystem grant and automatically starts a PS5 download writer when a
torrent download begins. Choose a video destination with the folder picker
in Settings before starting a new download. If no folder has been selected,
the download action shows a reminder with an OK button. Existing downloads
in `/data/Stremio/downloads/` are discovered and included when moving to your
chosen folder. Keep enough free space on the destination filesystem.

Installing the app itself on an M.2 volume, for example at
`/mnt/ext1/homebrew/PPSA74126`, does not change the settings or log paths.
To store videos on that volume, select a folder under `/mnt/ext1` in the
download folder picker.

On first launch, scan the sign-in QR code or open the displayed link on
another device. Once connected, Stremio Plus opens your home screen. The
interface follows the console language where supported, with English as the
fallback. English and Italian are currently available, and you can choose
either in Settings. Signing out returns to the sign-in screen.

## Controls

| Button | Action |
| --- | --- |
| D-pad | Move through items and controls |
| Cross | Open the selected item or confirm |
| Circle | Go back; hide visible playback controls before leaving the video |
| Triangle | Open search while browsing |
| L1 / R1 | Change top-level tabs, seasons, or stream providers, depending on the screen |
| L2 / R2 in Downloads | Cycle gallery sorting between title, release year and download date |
| L2 / R2 during playback | Adjust subtitle delay (unchanged) |
| Square on a cover | Add or remove it from your library |
| Square in Continue Watching | Remove that item from Continue Watching |
| Square on a stream | Download **only the selected stream** |
| Up / Down during playback | Show playback controls |
| Right stick up / down during playback | Increase / decrease PCM volume in 5% steps; center the stick after playback starts or system input returns |
| Options during playback | Open audio and subtitle controls |

Playback volume is saved independently of interface sound volume. The
temporary indicator shows the current level. Active HDMI bitstream
passthrough instead shows TV/receiver guidance: encoded audio is not scaled,
and the saved PCM level is preserved. Disable passthrough to use software
volume, or adjust the receiver when keeping encoded output.

The Sony PlayStation 5 Media Remote is read through its dedicated input port,
independently of the DualSense. Direction, Select and Back navigate the app;
Play/Pause, Rewind and Fast-forward control playback. Outside playback,
Rewind and Fast-forward move between tabs or seasons. Additional transport,
audio and subtitle commands are handled when reported by a compatible remote.
The Media Remote must first be paired in the console's system settings.

Playback skip intervals for the D-pad and L1 / R1 can be set independently.
Online streams and downloads ask before playback begins. When a valid saved
position exists, choose between starting from the beginning and resuming that
movie or episode; otherwise, choose to start or cancel. Each episode has its
own saved position, so watching another episode does not replace its bookmark.

In Downloads, L2/R2 cycles between title A-Z, release year newest first and
download date newest first. The app remembers the selected order and keeps
the same film or series selected. This changes the gallery order only;
transfers keep their queue order and episodes retain their season ordering.
The gallery uses dedicated 720x1080 covers and upgrades previously saved
posters when a better source is available, retaining the old offline image
until its replacement is ready.

In Downloads, Options starts playback of an active download once its confirmed
file prefix reaches 5%. Seeking stays within timestamps the player has already
read; a file percentage is not treated as a time limit. A previously viewed
position is offered again only when the same source and its saved byte prefix
are available. If a crash rolls a download back to an earlier checkpoint,
the later bookmark is preserved until the required prefix has been recovered.

When a series episode ends, an optional card shows the next episode's
thumbnail, title, and number. Its countdown defaults to 15 seconds. Choose
**Watch now** to open the start/resume choice or **Ignore** to dismiss the
card; Circle also dismisses it. When the countdown reaches zero, the same
choice opens and waits for confirmation before starting the next episode.
Autoplay and the countdown duration can be changed in Settings.

## Video and display options

Video frames are converted at their source resolution and displayed with
ordinary bilinear scaling. The PS5's configured resolution is the default.
These display and audio controls are available:

| Setting | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| **Video & Display → 120 Hz output** | Off, Auto or Playback only. The app checks output support and the resulting mode, restores the previous mode when required, and refuses changes that reduce the registered output resolution. |
| **Audio → Audio passthrough** | Opt-in HDMI bitstream transport for receiver-advertised AC-3, E-AC-3 and DTS core formats at 48 kHz. Unsupported formats or unavailable HDMI transport use decoded PCM. Changes apply to the next video. |

System refresh behavior and decoded audio are the defaults. The video
renderer presents decoded source frames directly.
The HDMI output keeps submitted audio buffers alive until they are released
and drains pending audio before pause, seek and closure. If the native port
cannot be closed or restored correctly, playback stops and audio remains
disabled until the application is restarted.

Dolby Vision Profile 5 metadata is carried with the decoded frame and used
for RPU-based GPU reshaping before SDR tone mapping. This does not enable
native Dolby Vision HDMI output. AV1 uses the bundled dav1d **software**
decoder, including supported 4K 10-bit input; this build does not claim an
AV1 hardware decoding path or guaranteed real-time playback for every file.
The native decoder can still reject a stream or platform configuration, in
which case the existing software fallback remains available.

The currently supported high-refresh request is 119.88 Hz. It gives a 5:5
cadence for 23.976 fps content; it is not an exact 120.000 Hz mode for 24.000
fps content. Display, cable, receiver and console support determine whether
the change is accepted.

## Downloads and recovery

### Choosing a folder

Open the download folder setting to browse accessible directories, including
mounted volumes under `/mnt`. Use the D-pad to move and Cross to enter a
folder. Left, or the `..` entry, goes to its parent; Circle closes the picker.
Triangle selects the folder currently
displayed. Square creates **Stremio Plus Downloads** in that folder and opens
it; press Triangle to select it. Options refreshes the directory listing.

Choosing a different folder moves all existing downloads there, including
completed videos, partial downloads, saved artwork, and queued items. The
queue is suspended while the move runs, and the picker shows its progress.
After a successful move, the files are removed from their old locations and
downloads continue from the new folder. Unrelated files in either folder are
left alone.

Moving between volumes requires enough free space at the destination. The
original files are kept until their transferred data is verified and saved;
the app does not leave a second copy after a successful move. If a drive is
disconnected or a write fails, the app reports the problem and preserves the
saved state needed to recover the move. Reconnect any source drive before
changing the destination. A directory must pass a write check before use.
For an interrupted move, reopen the download folder setting: the picker
returns to the pending destination. Confirm it again to continue. New
downloads and file deletion wait until that move has finished.
The app applies permissions `0777` to the selected folder, reads the mode
back, and performs a real write check before accepting it. Creating
**Stremio Plus Downloads** applies and checks the same permissions. Download
job directories receive the same verified mode despite a restrictive system
umask. Startup repairs the permissions of known download directories in place,
without recreating them. The picker does not recursively change permissions
on unrelated files or directories.

### Transfers and saved state

Torrent downloads use a dedicated writer process on the PS5, started
automatically through the homebrew environment's ELF loader. This moves bulk
file writes out of the native application's throttled storage context,
following the approach documented by
[ProsperoStore](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ProsperoStore).
The app keeps the torrent engine, queue, and playback controls; no external
computer or streaming server is involved.

The writer accepts one sequential, page-aligned block of up to 4 MiB at a
time. Progress advances only after the writer confirms the complete block.
The torrent engine continues receiving and verifying pieces within its
memory budget. Only the active download transfers media; queued titles wait
for their turn.

Progress is saved durably after 256 MiB or 30 seconds of new torrent data,
whichever comes first. Pausing, stopping the app normally, or finishing a
download also saves the current position. If the console loses power or the
app crashes, the next attempt resumes from the last durable checkpoint and
downloads any uncommitted tail again. A partially written file is never
marked complete. If the writer cannot start or its connection is interrupted,
the app reports an error and retains the recoverable partial download.

For downloads with a known file size, the app checks space on the destination
filesystem before starting or resuming. The check uses the remaining bytes,
plus a small allowance for saved state. If storage runs out during a transfer,
the last valid checkpoint is kept and queued transfers wait until you free
space and retry. Other apps can consume space after the check, so write errors
are still handled throughout the transfer.

Existing downloads remain listed whenever their folder can be read, even if
the app cannot write to it. Startup checks the saved inventory and its recovery
copies. If a download's information is missing or damaged, its files appear
as an **Unrecognized download**, with the storage they occupy when measurable.
These files are not played or restarted using guessed metadata. Press Square
to delete the selected download and its files; deletion can free space even
when there is no room to save new queue state. No existing download is deleted
automatically just because its information could not be read.

Selecting an online source which exactly matches a saved download reuses that
download. Completed videos play locally; an incomplete transfer resumes through
the existing queue and becomes playable at 5%. Source matching includes the
episode, torrent file index, and request headers. A different episode or source
does not reuse the wrong file, and playback does not start a second torrent
transfer for the same saved download.

Streaming torrents also recover automatically when an active reader has been
waiting for missing data for 30 seconds without useful progress. Recovery
refreshes stale connections and peer discovery while retaining verified and
partially received pieces. Repeated attempts back off to a maximum interval of
two minutes. Paused playback, a full read-ahead buffer, and pending disk writes
do not trigger this recovery simply because the displayed rate is zero.

App-owned storage, torrent cache and download directories use verified `0777`
permissions. Files containing account or source configuration keep private
permissions. Moving to another volume preserves this distinction.

### Installation storage

The native manifest sets `downloadDataSize` to `0`. Stremio Plus does not
reserve a private `/download0` volume on installation. Streaming caches grow
as received data is written, within their existing capacity limits; their
maximum capacity is not preallocated. Downloaded media occupies space only
on its selected destination filesystem.

Versions up to 0.5.5 requested a 16 GiB private volume. Replacing application
files may leave that volume registered by the loader. To reclaim an existing
reservation, close the app, uninstall the registered title using the normal
console or loader uninstall operation, then install the current build.
Simply deleting or replacing files through FTP may leave the registration.
Keep `/data/Stremio` and your video directories. Do not manually modify a
mounted private volume. An uninstall can remove account settings from the
old private volume, so you may need to sign in again.

## Troubleshooting

Logs are kept together in `/data/Stremio/`. For a bug report, include the app
version, the steps that triggered it, and these files:

- `boot-current.txt`
- `log.txt`
- `runtime.json`
- `crash-current.txt` and `crash-last.txt`, if present

For download problems, include when the slowdown started and whether a video
was playing at the time. Checkpoint failures record the operation that failed
and its system error code. Storage errors also record the measured capacity
of the destination filesystem when available. Startup logs show directory
permissions before and after filesystem access is established. The downloaded
media files are not needed.

Playback logs distinguish loading the PS5 video module, preparing its compute
queue, and actually opening the native decoder. They include decoder rejection
reasons and native memory diagnostics. When available, the crash file records
the application abort caller or assertion that triggered termination; retain
the matching version's symbols when investigating a crash.
Clean launches and memory snapshots do not replace the last fatal crash
record. If that record cannot be rotated safely, it is preserved and the
storage error is reported.
Playback logs also report direct picture-memory usage, fallback allocations
and failed releases. These figures distinguish picture storage from the
general-purpose heap recorded in the crash diagnostics.
Video-output records distinguish decoded frames from frames accepted by
the renderer and identify failed texture or framebuffer setup stages.
Seek requests and applied positions are recorded without media locations.
Diagnostic snapshots are synced before replacing the previous complete
file. Nonzero native immediate exits retain a bounded exit-status and
caller-address record when that path reaches the application hook.

## Credits and license

Stremio Plus is developed by [LoZazaMastro](https://github.com/LoZazaMastro)
and builds on [Sp9nky's unofficial Stremio PS5 port](https://github.com/Sp9nky/unofficial-stremio-ps5-port).
Its native playback engine incorporates [ZiZc3's VLC PS5 port](https://github.com/ZiZc3/VLC)
and [VideoLAN's libVLC](https://www.videolan.org/vlc/libvlc.html). Their original
copyright and license notices are retained; the PS5 adaptation, local changes,
and source provenance are documented in [vendor/vlc-ps5/NOTICE.md](vendor/vlc-ps5/NOTICE.md).
Stremio Plus is based in part on
[EVO Player PS5 by sainsaji and contributors](https://github.com/sainsaji/EVO-PLAYER-PS5),
which derives from [ProsperoPlayer by KINGDKAK and contributors](https://github.com/KINGDKAK/ProsperoPlayer).
The incorporated work uses **GPL-3.0-or-later**. The original copyright
notice, full license text, exact upstream revision and dated descriptions
of Stremio Plus's modifications are retained in
[vendor/evo-player/](vendor/evo-player/) and included in both application
packages under `licenses/evo-player/`. The libplacebo authors are also
credited for the Dolby Vision colour mathematics used by EVO Player;
their applicable notices and license text are retained there.
Special thanks to [BlackBearReloaded](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded)
for the UI kit, OpenGL implementation, native app tooling, and ProsperoStore's

components, retained VLC patches, dependency recipes, assets and build scripts.

latestRelease.body:
## Changes since 0.5.18

- **Stable Home loading.** Fixed the repeated flashing and repositioning of shelves during startup. The loading screen now stays visible until the first shelves and their artwork are ready, with bounded waits for slow add-ons. Later catalog updates preserve the current selection and scroll position.

- **Persistent PS5 sign-in.** Corrected phone pairing to exchange the approval credential for a PS5 device session and save it immediately. Failed exchanges and expired or cancelled approvals can no longer complete a stale sign-in attempt.

- **Smoother 1080p playback.** Removed the expensive per-frame texture upload path that caused dropped frames and reduced playback speed. Improved late-frame handling and removed an unnecessary video-output copy.

- **Right-stick volume control.** Move the right stick up or down to adjust playback volume in 5% steps. Added a dead zone, controlled repeat, a temporary volume indicator and a saved volume level. Audio passthrough displays TV/receiver volume guidance. L2/R2 keep their existing controls.

- **Consistent start and resume choices.** Every playback request now asks before starting, including online streams, downloads and the next episode. A saved position offers **Start from the beginning** or **Resume**; choosing the beginning starts at zero, and cancelling preserves the bookmark. Invalid or repeated confirmations cannot launch playback, and incomplete downloads retain their verified-data checks.

repos.readme:
# RPCN online configs for PS5SX3

Settings for playing PS3 games online through **RPCN**, RPCS3's replacement for PSN, on **PS5SX3**, the PS3 emulator for PS5. PS5SX3 has no Network settings screen, so these files set it up for each game.

There's one file per title ID: 1809 configs covering the 681 games on the RPCS3 wiki's [RPCN Compatibility List](https://wiki.rpcs3.net/index.php?title=RPCN_Compatibility_List), plus two Call of Duty games from the [RPCN Browser](https://rpcs3.net/rpcn). Find your game and its title IDs in [GAMES.md](GAMES.md).

## Install

1. Copy the files for your games from this repo's `game_configs` folder into the `game_configs` folder of PS5SX3 (next to its `eboot.bin`). They have to go directly in that folder, not in a subfolder. Copying all of them is fine.
2. In PS5SX3, sign in to RPCN on the official RPCN server.
3. Start the game.

If PS5SX3 already has a file with the same name, add the `Net:` section to that file instead of replacing it.

## What the files set

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Internet enabled | Connected |
| PSN status | RPCN |
| DNS address | 8.8.8.8, unless the game uses a custom server's DNS (see below) |
| IP swap list | Only for games whose RPCS3 wiki page gives IP/Host switches (see below) |
| UPNP Enabled | On, so RPCS3 can ask your router to open the game's ports |

Each file also has comments with the game's results from the RPCN Compatibility List: whether it connects, makes lobbies, matches players, and has online features working.

## Games that don't use 8.8.8.8

Most games use DNS 8.8.8.8, RPCS3's default. 86 games have a fan-made custom server listed on their RPCS3 wiki page, so their files point at that server instead, through either a custom DNS or IP/Host switches.

### Custom servers not reached through DNS

These games are listed with custom servers too, but their pages give no DNS or IP/Host switches. Most need a game patch instead, such as the OpenSpy patches in RPCS3's patch list, or a separate tool, and a few servers don't work yet. ## Games PS5SX3 already ships a config for

These title IDs aren't included, so that your copy keeps PS5SX3's own fixes for them. Add these lines to the end of the existing file in PS5SX3's `game_configs` folder instead.

**Killzone 2 (BCUS98116)** uses PS Rewired's custom server:

```yaml
Net:
  Internet enabled: "Connected"
  PSN status: "RPCN"
  DNS address: "67.222.156.250"
  UPNP Enabled: true
```

**Grand Theft Auto IV (BLES00229, BLUS30127, NPEB00882, NPUB30702) and Grand Theft Auto V (BLES01807):**

```yaml

  Internet enabled: "Connected"
  PSN status: "RPCN"
  DNS address: "8.8.8.8"
  UPNP Enabled: true
```

## Not included

- **MAG** and **Yakuza 0** are on the list, but RPCS3's database has no title ID for them. For Yakuza 0 it only has the demo.

## Sources

- RPCS3 wiki: the [RPCN Compatibility List](https://wiki.rpcs3.net/index.php?title=RPCN_Compatibility_List), [Help:Netplay](https://wiki.rpcs3.net/index.php?title=Help:Netplay) and each custom-server game's page, read on 15 October 2026.
- Title IDs: [RPCS3 compatibility database](https://rpcs3.net/compatibility). PlayStation Home's ID (NPIA00005) comes from its PlayStation Store listing.
- [RPCN Browser](https://rpcs3.net/rpcn), for the Call of Duty games not on the wiki's list.

repos.readme:
# PS5 PKG YT Update Blocker 

Permanently blocks YouTube app updates.

## Installation
1. Run `build.sh`
2. Install `yt_blocker.pkg` 

## Paths
- DB: `/system_data/priv/mms/appinfo.db`
- Backup: `/user/app/YTBLK0001/backup/`
- Log: `/user/app/YTBLK0001/log.txt`
- 


# YT Update Blocker

A simple GUI tool built with PyQt6 to block YouTube app updates on your PS5. This prevents accidental updates that could softlock the app if you connect to the internet unintentionally. The tool modifies the `appinfo.db` file to spoof the version and redirect update checks to a local address.

This project is a GUI wrapper around the core logic from [Gezine's Y2JB repository](https://github.com/Gezine/Y2JB/). Huge thanks to Gezine for the original `appinfo_editor.py` script—without it, this wouldn't exist!

## Features
- User-friendly GUI for selecting database and backup paths.
- Automatically creates a backup of the original `appinfo.db` file.
- Modifies the YouTube entry in `appinfo.db` to block updates:
  - Sets `CONTENT_VERSION` to `99.999.999` (a fake high version).
  - Sets `VERSION_FILE_URI` to `http://127.0.0.2` (a non-existent local URL).
- Real-time logging in the app window for transparency.
- Menu links to social channels for support and updates.
- Lightweight and easy to use—no advanced coding knowledge required.

## Requirements
- Python 3.6+ (tested on 3.12).
- PyQt6 (install via `pip install pyqt6`).
- SQLite3 (included in Python standard library).
- Access to your PS5 via FTP (e.g., using FileZilla or any FTP client).
- The YouTube PKG must already be installed on your PS5.

**Note:** This tool is for educational and personal use only. Modifying system files can risk database corruption—always follow the steps carefully and reboot if needed.

## Installation
1. Clone or download this repository:
   ```
   git clone https://github.com/sinajet/yt-update-blocker.git
   ```
   (Replace with your actual repo URL if different.)

2. Install dependencies:
   ```
   pip install pyqt6
   ```

3. Ensure the app icons (`app_pics` folder) and `icon.ico` are in the same directory as `yt_blocker.py`.

## Usage
### Important Notes
- If you're using a PS5 backup file version 1.2.1 or higher (from official releases), you can skip this process as updates might already be handled.
- Always close the YouTube app, navigate to Settings, and ensure no packages are installing/updating before replacing files via FTP to avoid corruption.
- If you encounter a database corruption notification after replacement, reboot your PS5.

### Step-by-Step Guide
1. **Retrieve the Database File:**
   - After installing the YouTube PKG on your PS5, connect to your PS5 via FTP.
   - Navigate to `/system_data/priv/mms/` and download `appinfo.db` to your computer.

2. **Run the Tool:**
   - Launch the script:
     ```
     python yt_blocker.py
     ```
   - The GUI window will open.

3. **Select Paths in the GUI:**
   - Click "Path..." next to "appinfo.db Path" and select your downloaded `appinfo.db` file.
   - Click "Path..." next to "Backup Path" and select a folder to save the original backup (e.g., your desktop).
   - Click "Start Process" to modify the file. The log window will show progress and any errors.

4. **Verify Changes:**
   - The tool will create a backup named `appinfo.org.db` in your selected backup folder.
   - It updates the YouTube entry (titleId: 'PPSA01650') to block updates.
   - Check the log for confirmation: It should show updated values and verification.

5. **Replace the File on PS5:**
   - Use FTP to upload the modified `appinfo.db` back to `/system_data/priv/mms/` on your PS5.
   - Overwrite the existing file.

6. **Test and Reboot:**
   - If no corruption notification appears, reboot your PS5.
   - Launch YouTube—it should now be protected from updates even if connected to the internet.

### Troubleshooting
- **Error: Paths are empty!** Ensure both paths are selected before starting.
- **Error: appinfo.db file not found!** Verify the file name and path.
- **Database Corruption:** Follow the notes above—close apps, check settings, and reboot.
- If issues persist, check the console/log output for details.

## Credits
- **Core Logic:** Massive shoutout to [Gezine](https://github.com/Gezine) for the original update-blocking script in [Y2JB](https://github.com/Gezine/Y2JB/). This project builds directly on that foundation.
- **GUI Implementation:** Developed by SinaJet as an enhanced, user-friendly version.

## About Us
- [Telegram Channel](https://t.me/sinajet) – For updates and support.
- [YouTube Channel](https://www.youtube.com/c/SinaJet) – Tutorials and more.
- [GitHub Page](https://github.com/sinajet) – Check out my other projects.

If you find this useful, star the repo or drop a message—feedback is appreciated! 🚀

repos.name: PS5-FM
repos.readme:
# PS5 File Manager

A desktop-style file manager for jailbroken PS5 consoles: movable windows,
tabs, a taskbar and a Start panel, driven by the controller.

Developed and tested on firmware 6.02. Other firmware versions are untested.

## Features

- Windows you can move, resize, snap side by side, minimise and merge as tabs
- Copy, move, rename, delete, with a recycle bin, undo, a job queue with
  pause, and a replace / skip / keep-both prompt on name clashes
- Read and write everywhere, including system partitions (deletes there are
  backed up to /data/ps5fm-backup)
- Video and music player with subtitles, audio tracks, speed control,
  frame step, resume, and saving a frame as a picture
- Picture viewer with zoom, rotate and slideshow
- Pictures, Videos and Music libraries scanned from every drive, with
  thumbnails
- ZIP create and extract; RAR, 7z, tar, tar.gz, xz and ISO extract
- Text editor and hex viewer
- Search across all drives, recent files, folder sizes, duplicate finder,
  folder compare and one-way sync, checksums, split and join
- Game names and icons in the app folders, save backup and restore to USB
- Six looks (Classic, Night glass, Graphite, Paper, Windows style,
  Mac style) plus a custom one, each in light and dark
- Home-screen tile; no web server needed

## Requirements

- A jailbroken PS5 with an ELF loader listening on port 9021
- A Linux PC with cmake, git, socat, make, python3 and nasm
- The ps5-payload-dev SDK in /opt/ps5-payload-sdk

## Build and install

    PS5_HOST=<console ip> ./build.sh run

The first build downloads and compiles SDL2, ffmpeg, zlib, xz and
libarchive into deps/, which takes several minutes. `./build.sh` alone
only builds; `./build.sh install` builds and installs without starting.

## Controls

| Control | Action |
|---|---|
| Left stick | Pointer |
| Right stick | Scroll |
| Cross | Click / open |
| Circle | Back / close |
| Square | Select; hold on a title bar to move, on an edge to resize |
| Triangle or R3 | Menu |
| L3 | Switch windows |
| L1 / R1 | Tabs, previous / next |
| Options | Exit |

## Warning

This app can modify and delete system files. Removing the wrong file can
stop the console from booting. Use it at your own risk.

## Licence

GPLv3. The launcher includes code from ps5-payload-dev/websrv (GPLv3).
The app links FFmpeg, libarchive, zlib, xz, SDL2, stb and miniz, each
under its own licence.

repos.readme:
ПОКА В РАЗРАБОТКЕ, Альфа.

FGG-PlayPods-GUI

Форк FGG-PlayPods с графическим интерфейсом для PS5.
Оригинальный проект: FGGstore/FGG-PlayPods
Цель форка — превратить текущий автоматический payload в полноценное приложение
с поиском Bluetooth-устройств, выбором устройства, ручным подключением,
сохранёнными устройствами и подробным отображением состояния и логов.

> ⚠️ **Статус форка:** сейчас это исходный код оригинального FGG-PlayPods без изменений в логике Bluetooth/audio. GUI и выбор устройства пока находятся в плане разработки. На этом этапе изменена только документация форка.

--- ## Что это Этот репозиторий — форк **FGG-PlayPods**. Оригинальный проект позволяет выводить игровой и системный звук PS5 на обычные Bluetooth-наушники через собственный Bluetooth-контроллер консоли, без USB-донгла. При этом DualSense продолжает работать по беспроводной связи. В оригинальной версии устройство выбирается автоматически: payload сканирует Bluetooth и подключается к первому найденному подходящему аудиоустройству. Именно эту часть планируется переработать в данном форке. Планируемая схема: ``` PS5 audio ──capture──► FGG-PlayPods-GUI ──A2DP/SBC──► выбранное Bluetooth-устройство │ ├── поиск устройств ├── выбор устройства ├── Pair / Connect ├── сохранённые устройства └── состояние и логи ``` ### Возможности оригинального FGG-PlayPods | Возможность | Описание | |---|---| | **Что передаётся** | игры, меню, уведомления — весь звук консоли | | **Устройства** | Bluetooth-наушники, гарнитуры и earbuds с A2DP / SBC | | **Аудио** | 48 кГц stereo, SBC высокого качества (bitpool 53) | | **DualSense** | остаётся беспроводным и полностью рабочим | | **Установка** | ничего не патчится и не устанавливается за пределами собственной папки | ## Планируемые изменения форка Главная задача — заменить автоматический выбор первого найденного устройства на управляемый графический интерфейс. ### 1. Поиск Bluetooth-устройств GUI должен уметь запускать сканирование и отображать найденные устройства: - имя; - MAC-адрес; - Bluetooth Class; - RSSI, если контроллер его предоставляет; - статус устройства; - признак сохранённого/сопряжённого устройства. ### 2. Выбор устройства Пользователь выбирает конкретное устройство из списка и запускает: **Подключить / Pair** Payload больше не должен автоматически брать первое найденное устройство. ### 3. Сохранённые устройства После успешного pairing планируется сохранять: - имя; - MAC-адрес; - link key; - дополнительные данные, необходимые для повторного подключения. Это позволит выбирать устройство без нового pairing при каждом запуске. ### 4. Повторное подключение Для ранее сопряжённого устройства: ``` Запуск → список сохранённых устройств → выбрать → Connect ``` Также можно будет предусмотреть автоматическое подключение к последнему выбранному устройству. ### 5. Логи В GUI планируется отдельный экран с событиями Bluetooth/audio. Например: ``` [12:49:15] Найдено устройство: JBL ... [12:49:15] Подключение... [12:49:16] Аутентификация... [12:49:16] Ошибка: authentication failed 0x05 ``` При этом существующий файл: ``` /data/fgg-playpods/playpods.log ``` будет сохранён. ### 6. Статус подключения GUI должен явно показывать: - Bluetooth controller; - поиск; - подключение; - pairing; - authentication; - A2DP; - streaming; - отключение/ошибку. --- ## Оригинальная реализация Оригинальный FGG-PlayPods решает несколько сложных задач непосредственно внутри payload. ### Захват аудио Используется внутренний audio capture PS5 таким образом, чтобы получать полный микс, включая игровой звук и системные звуки. Аудиоформат: - 48 кГц; - stereo; - 32-bit float внутри capture; - 1024 frames на запись. ### Bluetooth PS5 имеет Bluetooth, но штатно не предоставляет обычный Bluetooth Audio. FGG-PlayPods реализует собственный A2DP source внутри payload: - SSP pairing; - L2CAP; - SDP; - AVDTP; - SBC; - RTP audio. ### Совместное использование Bluetooth-контроллера Bluetooth-чип консоли предоставляет два HCI-контроллера. Системный драйвер использует один из них для DualSense, а FGG-PlayPods работает рядом с системным драйвером через другой интерфейс, не отключая системный Bluetooth-драйвер. Это принципиально важно для будущего GUI: при добавлении сканирования и выбора устройства нельзя нарушить текущую схему совместного использования контроллера. ### Поток данных ``` PS5 audio capture ↓ 48 kHz stereo ↓ SBC encoder ↓ A2DP / RTP ↓ Bluetooth controller ↓ Bluetooth headset ``` ## Структура проекта | Файл | Назначение | |---|---| | `src/capture.c` | захват аудио PS5 | | `src/hci.c` | USB-транспорт к Bluetooth-контроллеру | | `src/bt.c` | pairing, Bluetooth link, L2CAP и flow control | | `src/sdp.c` | SDP service record | | `src/a2dp.c` | AVDTP, SBC encoding и аудиопоток | | `src/log.c` | файловый лог и уведомления PS5 | | `src/main.c` | запуск, lock и основная сессия | | `third_party/sbc` | SBC codec | ## Установка FGG-PlayPods-GUI ### Payload Manager — основной способ Форк сохраняет тот же способ установки, что и оригинальный проект: 1. Собрать `fgg-playpods-gui.elf`. 2. Скопировать **оба файла** через FTP: ``` fgg-playpods-gui.elf fgg-playpods-gui.elf.json ``` в отдельную папку: ``` /data/pldmgr/payloads/fgg-playpods-gui/ ``` 3. Открыть **Payload Manager**. 4. Запустить **FGG-PlayPods-GUI**. Отдельное имя и отдельная папка нужны, чтобы форк мог находиться рядом с оригинальным **FGG-PlayPods** без перезаписи его файлов и состояния. Payload Manager использует каталог `/data/pldmgr/payloads` для хранения payload-файлов. citeturn0search2 ### Direct Для прямого запуска сохраняется стандартный вариант: ``` fgg-playpods-gui.elf → порт 9021 ``` То есть форк можно запускать и через Payload Manager, и напрямую через payload sender. > **Важно:** оригинальный FGG-PlayPods и FGG-PlayPods-GUI можно хранить одновременно, но запускать их одновременно не следует — оба используют общий Bluetooth-контроллер PS5. ## Использование оригинальной версии 1. Перевести Bluetooth-гарнитуру в режим pairing. 2. Запустить payload. 3. Payload автоматически найдёт подходящее аудиоустройство. 4. Выполнит pairing и начнёт передавать звук. 5. При следующих запусках будет использовать сохранённый link key. Для остановки оригинального payload достаточно выключить гарнитуру. > В будущей версии GUI автоматический выбор первого найденного устройства будет заменён на выбор пользователем. --- ## Ограничения оригинальной версии - **Одно устройство одновременно.** - Для pairing другого устройства необходимо удалить: `/data/fgg-playpods/headset.key`. - Передаётся только звук — микрофон не поддерживается. - Громкость регулируется на самой гарнитуре. - Bluetooth SBC добавляет задержку, поэтому решение не идеально для rhythm games. - Только Classic Bluetooth Audio / A2DP. LE Audio-only устройства не поддерживаются. ## Логи Каждый запуск записывается в: ``` /data/fgg-playpods/playpods.log ``` Получить файл можно по FTP. Для диагностики pairing особенно важны сообщения: ``` found ... connection complete ... authentication complete ... authentication failed ... disconnected ... chip vendor event ... ``` ## Сборка Требуется Linux или WSL и [PS5 Payload SDK](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk): ```sh sudo apt install clang lld llvm make unzip export PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK=/opt/ps5-payload-sdk make ``` Сборка выполняется с: ``` -Wall -Wextra -Werror ``` Единственный сторонний код — SBC codec из [BlueZ](https://www.bluez.org/), размещённый в `third_party/sbc`. ## Лицензия [GPL-3.0](LICENSE). Vendored SBC codec распространяется по LGPL-2.1-or-later. ## Credits Built by **FGG STORE**. Standing on the work of [ps5-payload-dev](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev) for the SDK and `ftpsrv`, of [BlueZ](https://www.bluez.org/) for the SBC codec, and of [idlesauce/ps5-self-pager](https://github.com/idlesauce/ps5-self-pager), which made reading the system software possible. > Not affiliated with Sony Interactive Entertainment or Microsoft. For use with > homebrew on consoles you own.

repos.name: HYPERHEN
repos.readme:
HyperHEN
An all-in-one HEN and Toolbox for PlayStation 5

Features · Run · Build · Configuration · Technical overview · Credits

---

HyperHEN is a modular payload stack for the PS5. One entry ELF prepares the system, injects a ShellUI Toolbox,
and then runs overlays, cheats, payloads, and background services.

HyperHEN v0.9.3 combines exact firmware routing, the source-built HyperCore, one common automount owner, firmware-gated Toolbox services, and a fully HyperHEN-branded native Settings interface. The visual system uses a unified 64 px icon family and a progressive APNG HyperCore emblem. Firmware image decoders that do not play APNG display its complete first frame, so animation never gates the UI. ### What's new in 0.9.3 - **HyperDeck Media dashboard** with Game Compressor, Web File Manager, CheatRunner, PS5Upload and package installation; expanded Advanced Debug controls include DNS tools, firmware spoof, NP Fake Sign-in, zFTPd/zHTTP and firmware-gated Garlic Save Manager. - **Firmware-aware engine choices** on legacy and 5.xx profiles, Toolbox continuation on legacy routes, dedicated 9.40/12.70 inputs and a restricted Kstuff-lite route for 13.40/13.42. HyperCore remains unavailable below 3.00. - **ShadowMountPlus 1.7 beta9**, stronger startup ownership/readiness checks, and engine selectors plus additional notifications that follow the console language while retaining the existing Toolbox translations. - **Toolbox startup and recovery improvements:** close WebKit manually, then allow the two-second quiet interval before injection. ShellUI lifecycle handling also improves recovery after payload launches. - **Consistent v0.9.3 branding**, including Console Information, and a dedicated experimental 13.60 Linux-loader input. See [RELEASE_NOTES.md](RELEASE_NOTES.md) for the complete comparison with the previous public 0.9.2 release, including the dashboard/tool work completed before the final stabilization update.
# Features HyperHEN is a practical homebrew stack for jailbroken PS5 consoles. The combined HyperCore has console-log validation on firmware **5.00**. Its additional firmware profiles are compatibility data, not proof of runtime validation. Exact modern profiles from 6.00 through 11.40 use A53/PPR except for the dedicated 9.40 route. The exact 11.60–12.60 entries use a reduced HyperCore route with PPR-dependent behavior disabled; 12.70 has dedicated inputs. Unsupported or non-exact profiles fail closed. ### Exact firmware profiles These are the **67 exact entries** declared by the router. The first hop still needs an external `elfldr` on **9021**. After that, HyperHEN starts its own private loader on **9020** for later ELF and user-payload launches. ### HyperLinux clean-boot mode Open **Advanced Debug → HyperLinux Boot** to arm the embedded Linux loader. Because the upstream Linux boot path is incompatible with kstuff already being active, the button deliberately does not launch it in the current session. Fully reboot the console and start HyperHEN once: the bootstrapper consumes the one-shot marker and hands off to HyperLinux before HyperCore starts. A prepared USB must contain `bzImage` and `initrd.img` either at its root or in `PS5/Linux/`. Rest Mode USB power must be set to **Always** and HDMI Device Link must be disabled. Exact profiles are 3.00, 3.10, 3.20, 3.21, 4.00, 4.02, 4.03, 4.50, 4.51, 5.00, 5.02, 5.10, 5.50, 6.00, 6.02, 6.50, 7.00, 7.01, 7.20, 7.40, 7.60, 7.61, plus the experimental 13.20 and dedicated 13.60 paths. Other firmware revisions fail closed; the experimental inputs are not hardware certification of those profiles.
# Run ### Requirements 1. A jailbroken PS5 2. An external [PS5 `elfldr`](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/elfldr) listening on port **9021** for the first hop ### Load HyperHEN 1. Run the kernel exploit and start the external `elfldr` service. 2. After a full reboot when changing versions, send the downloaded `HyperHEN-v0.9.3.elf` or locally built `HyperHEN.elf` through the loader your exploit host provides. 3. HyperHEN uses the exact firmware route and opens the legacy/5.xx engine selector where supported. On FW 13.00, 13.20, or 13.60, follow the HyperHEN Hypervisor notification: enter Rest Mode once and resume. Follow the component-specific notification on dedicated 9.40/12.70 routes; on exact 11.60–12.60 profiles, wait for the compatibility-mode notification and runtime check. 4. If the engine selector appears, confirm your choice, then **close the WebKit/browser window manually when prompted**. On other routes, manually close the payload-host browser after launching HyperHEN. 5. Keep the browser closed, allow the two-second quiet interval and let initialization finish before opening PS5 Settings and entering the HyperHEN Toolbox. FW 13.40 and 13.42 use the restricted lite route rather than utility-only mode. > **Important: close WebKit manually to finish startup.** HyperHEN does not > automatically close the browser after engine selection. Toolbox activation > waits for WebKit to exit and remain closed for **two seconds**. Keep the > browser closed while the remaining initialization finishes. This startup > handoff applies across the declared firmware profiles, including legacy and > 5.xx selectors. Startup is sequential. After the first hop, HyperHEN uses its own `hyperhen_elfldr.elf` on port **9020** and keeps **9021** only as a fallback. ```text HyperHEN.elf → bootstrapper → exact firmware route → HyperHEN Automount → daemon/Toolbox where available ``` External plugins are discovered and started by the daemon after the selected runtime is ready, subject to component-specific availability checks. ### Plugin compatibility The Toolbox **Plugins** page manages both native HyperHEN plugin ELFs and etaHEN-compatible `.plugin` containers installed in `/data/HyperHEN/plugins`. HyperHEN validates the container identity and its embedded ELF separately, launches only the embedded ELF through the private loader, and preserves the plugin ID as the spawned process name. The existing start, stop, reload, delete, and next-boot auto-start controls apply to both formats. Game-process `.prx` and `.sprx` modules remain isolated from standalone plugin processes. Their catalog is managed from **Toolbox → SPRX**, using `/data/HyperHEN/sprx/catalog.ini` with exact title-ID targeting. A structurally valid container does not guarantee compatibility with every game build or third-party plugin API. ### FTP server **Advanced Debug** includes three independent switches: the kernel-log server on TCP 3232, the FTP server on TCP 2121, and the LAN ELF loader on TCP 9025. HyperHEN installs the two verified upstream payload images under `/data/HyperHEN/tools`, builds the LAN loader from source, launches each through its private loader, and records the returned process identity so the same switch can stop only the service it started. These unauthenticated development services must be used only on a trusted local network. The separate [`onionHEN-ftpsrv-plugin`](https://github.com/OnionBuddies/onionHEN-ftpsrv-plugin) remains supported as an optional plugin when a separately configurable FTP instance is preferred. Do not enable two FTP listeners on the same port. The original service switches are retained. Additional Advanced Debug controls integrate Firmware Spoof, NP Fake Sign-in, NanoDNS, Chukei DNS, zFTPd/zHTTP and Garlic Save Manager, with component- and firmware-specific availability checks. ### Mount integration HyperHEN embeds ShadowMountPlus 1.7 beta9 and starts it only after the selected firmware route is ready. It is the sole active automount owner. Before HyperCore starts, the bootstrapper claims the kstuff automount sentinel; HyperCore's native scanner and integrated BackPork monitor then stay paused while HyperHEN Automount owns the lifecycle. Startup checks verify live ownership and the selected firmware/engine readiness before dispatch, avoiding conflicting mount owners and false-ready announcements. Existing configuration and explicit LAN binding are preserved; the default API binding is loopback. The optional SceShellCore bridge is enabled only for exact offsets present in the supplied ShadowMountPlus table. Missing revisions are not approximated; the base scanner/mount service remains separate from those optional hooks. Profiles 1.05, 1.10, 1.11, 1.13 and 4.02 retain an explicitly limited scanner/API path where supported, without inventing ShellCore offsets or claiming full on-demand hooks. Other initialization failures stop startup instead of advertising complete readiness. ### HyperDPI (network package installer) HyperDPI is compiled from the pinned GPL source, embedded in the main payload, and launched from memory after the HyperHEN daemon is ready. No `DPIV00001.elf`, sidecar download, or file under `/data/HyperHEN/plugins` is required. Its dynamic Toolbox page provides enable, API port, WebUI port, and restart controls. The browser retains chunked uploads, queue management, staged-file reuse, and SSE progress. The default WebUI URL is `http://:12800`. The listeners are disabled on first boot. HyperDPI has no client authentication and listens on all console interfaces when enabled, so use it only on a trusted local network and stop it when finished. Settings are stored in `/data/HyperHEN/HyperDPI.ini`; uploads are staged under `/user/data/HyperHEN/pkgs`. ### Remote Play Remote Play pairing is available from **Toolbox → Network → Remote Play**. The current account must already be activated. If it is not, HyperHEN blocks the Remote Play page and directs you to **Toolbox → Account → Account activation**. Once the account is activated, HyperHEN enables the Remote Play registry setting and displays the pairing PIN. Enter that PIN in the official Remote Play client while the page is open; HyperHEN uses the native PS5 Remote Play service to confirm the registered device. The feature provides pairing and registration only. Video streaming and client transport remain handled by Sony's native Remote Play service. ### Payloads Place standalone payloads in: ```text /data/HyperHEN/payloads/ ``` Only plain `.elf` files are supported. Auto-start can be turned on in the Toolbox; HyperHEN remembers that choice with a matching `.auto_start` file next to the ELF. All `.elf` filenames use the same Payload page, loader, and auto-start flow. A recorded running instance is left running by later launch and auto-start requests. HyperHEN plugins are a separate category and belong in `/data/HyperHEN/plugins/`. ### Cheats Put cheat files in one directory. Names are `TITLEID_VERSION`, with an optional process and 8-hex source ID: ```text /data/HyperHEN/cheats/_[_][_].json /data/HyperHEN/cheats/_[_][_].shn /data/HyperHEN/cheats/_[_][_].mc4 /data/HyperHEN/cheats/_[_][_].ShnExt ``` `PROCESS` is optional. `SOURCE_ID` is a stable physical-source discriminator. HyperHEN loads every compatible source for the title/version/process, so independent JSON, SHN, MC4 and ShnExt files can coexist. A source with an explicit process is only used for that process; a source without one is generic. Cheats load from disk. If a file changes, HyperHEN reloads it without restarting the whole stack. `DOWNLOAD_CHEATS` downloads a cheat catalog ZIP over HTTPS (GitHub or cnb.cool), extracts the `cheats/` tree, and copies `json/`, `shn/`, and `mc4/` files into this directory with their original names. `[cheats] mirror=auto` uses cnb.cool when the UI/system language is Simplified Chinese, otherwise GitHub.

The existing broader developer source-build recipe remains: ```shell export PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK=/path/to/ps5-payload-sdk ./scripts/build.sh --jobs 8 ``` That script validates the vendored dependencies, builds HyperCore and HyperHEN Automount locally, and then builds the embed chain in the required order. # Troubleshooting 1. Before loading HyperHEN, make sure the external `elfldr` is reachable on port **9021**. 2. Make sure the payload was built for this firmware with a complete PS5 Payload SDK. 3. If the Toolbox does not appear, close WebKit manually, wait for the selected engine → Automount → daemon startup to finish, and check the logs. FW 13.40/13.42 use the restricted Kstuff-lite / Automount-lite route with Toolbox support. 4. If HyperCore does not build, run `./scripts/sync_dependencies.sh`; it reports the exact missing vendored source. 5. When you report a problem, include firmware, exploit host, SDK version, build type, logs, and steps to reproduce.
