latestRelease.body:
# HyperHEN v0.9.3

HyperHEN continues to evolve as a single, firmware-aware PS5 homebrew stack.
This release brings together the additions made since public v0.9.2:
HyperDeck, expanded Advanced Debug tools, engine selectors, updated Automount,
broader localized notifications, and improvements to Toolbox startup and
ShellUI recovery.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Close WebKit manually and return to the PS5 dashboard.** After choosing an
> engine in the selector, close the browser yourself; HyperHEN does not close
> it automatically. On profiles without a selector, follow the startup
> notifications and close WebKit if it is open. The Toolbox waits until the
> WebKit content process has remained absent for a continuous **two seconds**
> before attaching to ShellUI. This shared startup rule applies to **all 67
> declared profiles**, not just 5.xx. Leaving WebKit open keeps the Toolbox
> waiting.

## What's new

- **HyperDeck Media dashboard:** a native-tool hub combining Game Compressor,
  PS5 Web File Manager, CheatRunner, PS5Upload, and package installation in one
  interface, accessible from its Media-tab entry.
- **Expanded Advanced Debug catalog:** PS5 Firmware Spoof, NP Fake Sign-in,
  NanoDNS, Chukei DNS, zFTPd/zHTTP, and Garlic Save Manager, with
  component-specific availability and firmware checks.
- **Legacy engine selector:** PS5HEN or HyperCore on the exact supported
  3.xx/4.xx entries. The declared 1.xx/2.xx entries retain PS5HEN only;
  HyperCore is unavailable below 3.00.
- **Separate 5.xx engine choices:** Bypervisor for the dedicated hypervisor
  session, or HyperCore for the compatibility stack. The Bypervisor choice
  skips HyperCore, A53/PPR, and BackPork, then continues to Automount and
  Dashboard services. The HyperCore choice follows its compatibility path
  directly.
- **Legacy Dashboard and Toolbox continuation:** the early firmware routes
  now continue to utility, daemon, Dashboard, and Toolbox services after
  engine readiness and Automount instead of stopping at the legacy stage.
- **HyperDeck Media-icon registration and Dashboard handoff improvements**
  across the declared routes, including the legacy and 7.xx profiles, with
  readiness checks and reuse of an existing owned service instance.
- **Safer WebKit and ShellUI lifecycle handling:** Toolbox startup waits for
  manual browser closure and the two-second quiet interval. ShellUI
  replacement is distinguished from actual standby/resume, improving
  recovery after payload launches from Advanced Debug or HyperDeck.
- **Selectors and additional notifications follow the console language.**
  Startup, readiness, handoff, and legacy-path messages extend the existing
  Toolbox translations. Rendering was checked for **31 system-language
  values using 28 catalogs**, including aliases and fallbacks.
- **13.40/13.42 lite route:** these exact profiles move from utility-only
  mode to Kstuff-lite, restricted Automount-lite, and Dashboard/Toolbox
  services. Backport/fakelib, emulator replacement, and automatic AMPR
  features remain disabled in this route.
- **Dedicated 9.40 and 12.70 startup routing and payload inputs**, with exact
  dispatch instead of borrowing neighboring firmware profiles.
- **ShadowMountPlus 1.7 beta9 integration:** standard and lite Automount
  variants, stronger checks for conflicting live owners, and firmware/engine
  readiness checks before startup. Existing configuration, customized
  notifications, and explicit LAN binding are preserved; the default API
  address remains loopback.
- **Dedicated experimental 13.60 Linux-loader input**, kept separate from
  the existing common clean-boot loader. This extends the existing Linux
  handoff; it does not establish hardware certification for that profile.

## Firmware profiles and startup order

Firmware detection is exact. Only the entries below are declared profiles;
nearby versions are never assumed compatible. The total of **67 profiles
already existed in v0.9.2**. This release updates routing, engine choices,
and service continuation rather than claiming 67 newly supported firmwares.

<!-- PROFILE_TABLE_BEGIN -->
| Route | Count | Exact firmware versions | Startup behavior |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| Legacy selector | 25 | 1.00, 1.01, 1.02, 1.05†, 1.10†, 1.11†, 1.12, 1.13†, 1.14, 2.00, 2.20, 2.25, 2.26, 2.30, 2.50, 2.70, 3.00, 3.10, 3.20, 3.21, 4.00, 4.02†, 4.03, 4.50, 4.51 | PS5HEN; HyperCore choice enabled only on the exact 3.xx/4.xx entries. Automount and Toolbox follow the selected engine's readiness checks. |
| 5.xx selector | 4 | 5.00, 5.02, 5.10, 5.50 | Bypervisor or HyperCore, then Automount and Toolbox after readiness. |
| A53/PPR | 25 | 6.00, 6.02, 6.50, 7.00, 7.01, 7.20, 7.40, 7.60, 7.61, 8.00, 8.20, 8.40, 8.60, 9.00, 9.05, 9.20, 9.60, 10.00, 10.01, 10.20, 10.40, 10.60, 11.00, 11.20, 11.40 | A53/PPR preparation and HyperCore, then Automount and Toolbox. |
| Dedicated 9.40 | 1 | 9.40 | Dedicated hypervisor and HyperCore inputs, then Automount and Toolbox. |
| HyperCore without PPR | 6 | 11.60, 12.00, 12.02, 12.20, 12.40, 12.60 | HyperCore with PPR-dependent behavior disabled, then Automount and Toolbox. |
| Hypervisor route | 4 | 12.70, 13.00, 13.20, 13.60 | Firmware-specific hypervisor stage, HyperCore, Automount and Toolbox. |
| Kstuff-lite | 2 | 13.40, 13.42 | HyperCore lite and restricted Automount lite, then Toolbox. |
<!-- PROFILE_TABLE_END -->

† **Limited on-demand ShellCore hooks:** 1.05, 1.10, 1.11, 1.13, and 4.02
retain the scanner/API path where supported; full on-demand hooks are not
claimed. The experimental Linux-loader inputs have their own exact-profile
gates and do not make every firmware in this table a Linux profile.

The Toolbox startup correction underlying this release was confirmed working
by the reported **9.05 tester**. Local validation covers the exact route
tables, startup gates, version metadata, notification rendering, and embedded
components. Source coverage does not mean that every firmware has completed
hardware testing.

## Integrated services

The existing kernel-log server on TCP **3232**, FTP server on TCP **2121**,
and debug LAN ELF loader on TCP **9025** remain available alongside the
expanded Advanced Debug catalog. The private loader on TCP **9020** remains
separate from the external first-hop loader on **9021**.

Plugin management, title-targeted SPRX modules, cheats, the performance
display, Remote Play pairing, HyperDPI package services, Linux clean-boot
handoff, and user-payload auto-start remain part of the stack. These existing
features are retained rather than presented as new additions in v0.9.3.

HyperHEN still requires an already jailbroken console and an external
[elfldr](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/elfldr) endpoint on TCP **9021**
for the first hop. Follow any firmware-specific startup notification before
continuing; the supported 13.00/13.20/13.60 hypervisor route requires its
Rest Mode/resume completion step.

## Updating and first launch

1. Perform a full reboot before loading the new ELF so the previous ShellUI
   module is replaced.
2. Launch **HyperHEN-v0.9.3.elf**, choose an engine where offered, and follow
   the firmware-specific notifications.
3. **Close WebKit manually and return to the PS5 dashboard.** Allow the
   continuous two-second quiet interval, then open **Settings → HyperHEN
   Toolbox** once startup completes.

If reporting a problem, include the exact firmware, the ELF version, and a
klog from the same boot.

## Credits and special thanks

HyperHEN integration, firmware orchestration, product identity, and release
engineering: **MICHELE MEDIA**. Every upstream component retains its original
authorship, copyright notices, and license terms. See the
[complete README credits](https://github.com/Michele-M-Media/HYPERHEN#credits)
and [third-party notices](https://github.com/Michele-M-Media/HYPERHEN/blob/main/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md)
for the developers and projects behind the integrated tools and services.

The added native-tool integrations credit their original developers:

- [PS5 Firmware Spoof](https://github.com/illusionyy/ps5-fw-spoof) — **illusionyy**.
- [NP Fake Sign-in](https://github.com/earthonion/np-fake-signin) and
  [Garlic SaveMgr](https://github.com/earthonion/garlic-savemgr) — **earthonion**.
- [nanoDNS](https://github.com/drakmor/nanoDNS) and
  [ShadowMountPlus](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus) — **drakmor and contributors**.
- [Chukei DNS](https://github.com/Al-Azif/chukei-dns) — **Al Azif (Al-Azif)**.
- [zFTPd + zHTTP](https://github.com/seregonwar/zftpd) — **Seregon (SeregonWar)**.
- [PS5 Game Compressor](https://github.com/juma-sayeh/PS5-Game-Compressor) — **Juma Sayeh**.
- [PS5 Web File Manager](https://github.com/owendswang/ps5-web-file-manager) — **owendswang**.
- [CheatRunner](https://github.com/notmaj0r/CheatRunner) — **notmaj0r (maj0r)**.
- [PS5Upload](https://github.com/phantomptr/ps5upload) — **PhantomPtr**.
- [websrv and the PKG installation helper](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/websrv) —
  **John Törnblom and the ps5-payload-dev contributors**.

Special thanks to [**@oG_LuckyXmods**](https://x.com/oG_LuckyXmods) for the
extensive help testing HyperHEN, and to the
[**PizzaClub testers**](https://t.me/+6SY-QLIzDkI1Mzg0) for their time,
support, and feedback throughout testing.

## One more thing

### HYPERHEN START.

# 🍕 PIZZA HEN v2.00

[Italiano](README_IT.md)

**PIZZA HEN** is an experimental all-in-one PS5 homebrew environment maintained by **Michele Media**.

The project keeps its own integration layer, runtime organization, Toolbox, service chain, build policy and branding while preserving the licenses and attribution of the upstream open-source projects it builds on.

> **Release status:** v2.00 public source checkpoint.  
> **Validation status:** the included v2.00 audit records a complete static I18N gate PASS. It does **not**, by itself, claim a fresh hardware PASS for this exact I18N-only checkpoint.

## v2.00 highlights

v2.00 is the **complete internationalization final-gate checkpoint** built on the hardware-working R7.25.2.16.1 runtime baseline.

- **31 locales** across the PIZZA HEN Toolbox with identical translation keysets.
- 31-locale coverage retained for the **KStuff selector**, **ShadowMount selector**, native **ShellUI locale table** and **service notifications**.
- **Arabic RTL** support preserved.
- Previously hard-coded Toolbox descriptions and status labels moved into the localization data.
- PoorDS4 and Fan Target / ps5-fan-control Toolbox UI localized across all 31 locales.
- Runtime behavior intentionally frozen while the I18N data layer was completed.
- All **91 ELF files** in the v2.00 checkpoint remain byte-identical to the R7.25.2.16.1 baseline.
- All **127 named JavaScript functions** in `toolbox_launcher.html` remain byte-identical to that baseline.
- Package Installer scan/install functions remain frozen.
- `debug_services_launcher.html` remains byte-for-byte frozen at its restored hardware-working bridge.

Full audit: [`V2_00_COMPLETE_I18N_AUDIT.txt`](V2_00_COMPLETE_I18N_AUDIT.txt)

## Main capabilities

PIZZA HEN brings the project components into one PS5-oriented environment:

- PIZZA HEN Toolbox and Media-tile workflow.
- Multiple KStuff paths through the graphical selector.
- ShadowMount selection, including the established stable/experimental paths and the supported skip path for compatible workflows.
- Integrated web service / Homebrew Channel path.
- FTP and ps5debug-NG services.
- ELF Loader service with runtime-state validation.
- Package Installer / DPIv2 integration.
- CheatRunner integration and cheat workflow.
- PIZZA HEN Payload Repository / Plugin Manager workflow.
- Fan-control integration.
- Remote Play helper service.
- Web File Manager, Linux Loader and Game Download integrations.
- SVT Play and optional media-player services.
- Additional user-supplied service payload integrations preserved according to the project freeze rules.

Not every component supports every firmware. Actual compatibility depends on the selected KStuff, ShadowMount and service/backend path.

## Runtime model

The primary PIZZA HEN data root is:

```text
/data/PIZZA_HEN
```

The project is designed around a selector-driven boot/runtime chain rather than forcing every optional component to start automatically:

```text
PIZZA HEN
  -> KStuff selector
  -> selected KStuff path
  -> ShadowMount selector / supported skip path
  -> PIZZA HEN Media / Toolbox environment
  -> websrv + selected services and tools
```

Several later integrations intentionally use **NO-PKG / NO-TILE** behavior so that PIZZA HEN can expose the underlying service or WebUI without installing an additional launcher application.

## Build

### Windows + WSL

Use the v2.00 final-gate wrapper:

```text
RUN_BUILD_V200_I18N_ONLY_FINAL_GATE_FIX.bat
```

### Linux / WSL / compatible host

The current release path is built through:

```bash
chmod +x build_v01_rebase_latest_toolbox.sh
./build_v01_rebase_latest_toolbox.sh
```

Some build-script filenames retain historical names for compatibility even though the repository checkpoint is v2.00.

PIZZA HEN keeps a capability-based **Multi-SDK** discovery policy rather than requiring one hard-coded Payload SDK release. See [`SDK_COMPATIBILITY.txt`](SDK_COMPATIBILITY.txt).

## v2.00 static validation

The published audit records:

- complete-I18N gate: **24/24 PASS**;
- **58 Python static tests PASS** across the build-script batches;
- Toolbox JavaScript syntax: PASS;
- Debug Services launcher JavaScript syntax: PASS;
- ShadowMount selector JavaScript syntax: PASS;
- KStuff selector JavaScript syntax: PASS;
- main build script Bash syntax: PASS.

The audit deliberately labels this checkpoint **STATIC-PASS** until a build/hardware result is separately recorded.

## Frozen third-party assets

PIZZA HEN does not rewrite text generated internally by frozen third-party ELF binaries. Where a component is tracked as frozen or user-supplied, its binary is preserved according to the project rules instead of being silently modified for branding or translation.

See:

- [`CREDITS.md`](CREDITS.md)
- [`THIRD_PARTY.md`](THIRD_PARTY.md)
- [`LICENSE`](LICENSE)

## Changelog and release notes

- [`CHANGELOG.md`](CHANGELOG.md)
- [`RELEASE_NOTES_v2.00.md`](RELEASE_NOTES_v2.00.md)

## Project direction

Project direction, integration work and PIZZA HEN branding: **Michele Media**.

PIZZA HEN is not affiliated with or endorsed by Sony Interactive Entertainment. This software is experimental homebrew; use it only in environments where you understand and accept the risks.

# PIZZA HEN v2.00 — Release Notes

PIZZA HEN v2.00 is the **Complete I18N Final Gate** source checkpoint.

The release is intentionally focused on completing the user-facing localization layer while preserving the runtime behavior of the R7.25.2.16.1 baseline.

## What changed

- Toolbox translation data completed across **31 locales**.
- KStuff selector, ShadowMount selector, native ShellUI locale table and service notifications remain covered across 31 locales.
- Arabic RTL behavior preserved.
- Previously hard-coded Toolbox descriptions/status labels moved into explicit localization mappings.
- PoorDS4 and Fan Target / ps5-fan-control Toolbox UI localized across all 31 locales.

## What did not change

The v2.00 I18N gate was designed to avoid runtime regressions:

- all **91 ELF files** remain byte-identical to the R7.25.2.16.1 baseline;
- all **127 named JavaScript functions** in `toolbox_launcher.html` remain byte-identical;
- Package Installer scan/catalog/install functions remain frozen;
- Debug Services launcher remains byte-identical to the restored bridge;
- no launch/stop behavior, `/hbldr`, websrv, Package Installer, KStuff, ShadowMount, Fan Control, PoorDS4, Storage, Themes Avatar, CheatRunner or payload-manager runtime logic was changed for this gate.

## Validation

The included audit records:

- **24/24** complete-I18N gate PASS;
- **58** Python static tests PASS;
- JavaScript syntax PASS for Toolbox, Debug Services and ShadowMount selector;
- KStuff selector JavaScript syntax PASS;

### Validation wording

9b800c4cffbbb7f6baa5e045cc77430b3bf5d11e

The v2.00 tree includes the current PIZZA HEN Toolbox, KStuff/ShadowMount selectors, Homebrew Channel/websrv path, FTP, ps5debug-NG, ELF Loader, Package Installer/DPIv2, CheatRunner, Payload Repository / Plugin Manager, Fan Control, Remote Play helper, Web File Manager, Linux Loader, Game Download, SVT Play and optional service integrations documented in the changelog.

## License and credits

PIZZA HEN preserves the license and attribution requirements of the upstream and bundled projects. See:

# RetroArch for PS5 **Your games on the TV. Your library in your hands.** 33 native cores · RetroArch & EmulationStation · A local WebUI [Download](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_RetroArch/releases) · [Get started](#get-started) · [Supported systems](#supported-systems) · [What’s new](releases/v1.0.0-beta.1.md)
![Important warning](assets/readme/important-warning.png) ## PS5 RetroArch is a passion project, not a piracy project. It exists so you can play the games you own on the console you own. - **Piracy is not condoned.** - **No games, BIOS files, console firmware or decryption keys are included, and they never will be.** - **Use only legally obtained backups of games you own**, made yourself from your own discs, cartridges or digital purchases. - **Use only BIOS and firmware files dumped from hardware you own.** - **Requests for, or links to, games, BIOS files, firmware or keys are not welcome** in this project's issues or discussions. ---

Your collection, beautifully organized.
Browse, add games, and manage artwork from your phone or computer.

A native RetroArch homebrew title for jailbroken PlayStation 5 consoles, made by [Mihawk](https://github.com/mihawk-99). Play through RetroArch or EmulationStation, with Vulkan graphics and up to four controllers. **Latest release: [v1.0.0-beta.1](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_RetroArch/releases/tag/v1.0.0-beta.1).** Read [what’s new](releases/v1.0.0-beta.1.md) or [download the package](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_RetroArch/releases/latest). > [!WARNING] > **Designed around ShadowMountPlus 1.7beta4 or later.** Use [ShadowMountPlus 1.7beta4](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus/releases/tag/1.7beta4) or newer for supported USB and extended-storage access. ##
Choose your frontend **RetroArch or EmulationStation.** Pick your preferred way to browse and play. Press **Square** to remember your choice. Hold **L1** during startup to return to the picker, or change it in **WebUI Settings → Start with**. ## At a glance | | Made for your collection | | --- | --- | | | **33 cores.** From NES and Mega Drive to Dreamcast, GameCube, PSP, and more. | | | **One shared library.** Artwork and game details across RetroArch, EmulationStation, and the WebUI. | | | **Easy game setup.** Add a game, find its details, and download missing artwork. | | | **DualSense stylus.** Use the touchpad for Nintendo DS and 3DS touchscreen controls. | **Explore:** [Get started](#get-started) · [WebUI](#webui) · [Systems](#supported-systems) · [Controls](#controls) · [Graphics](#graphics) · [Your files](#your-files) · [Known limits](#what-has-been-verified) · [Build](#build-from-source) ## Get started 1. **Install the complete title folder.** Extract a release and copy `PPSA99169` to your homebrew launcher’s location, usually `/data/homebrew/PPSA99169/`. A compatible jailbreak and launcher must already be set up. 2. **Choose your frontend.** Start RetroArch or EmulationStation from the picker. Press **Square** to remember your choice; hold **L1** during startup to return to the picker. XMB and RGUI are available in RetroArch. 3. **Open the WebUI.** Scan its QR code or visit `http://:6769` from a device on the same network. 4. **Add your games.** Use **Games → + Add Game** for one game backup, or **Content** for folders and multi-file games. Install any required BIOS files in the [system folders](#your-files), then load your game on the console. No games, BIOS files, firmware or decryption keys are included. Use your own legally obtained backups and system files dumped from hardware you own. Piracy is not condoned; requests for these files are not welcome in issues or discussions. ### Scan to connect | Menu | Open the WebUI QR code | | --- | --- | | **Picker** | Press **Triangle**; Triangle again or Circle closes it | | **RetroArch XMB** | **WebUI** tab to the left of Settings | | **RetroArch RGUI** | **WebUI** at the top of the main menu | | **EmulationStation** | **WebUI** in the main menu | ##
Your browser companion Stay connected while switching between the picker, RetroArch, and EmulationStation. A supported ELF loader or homebrew launcher keeps the WebUI running across menus; without one, it is available while RetroArch runs. | Page | What you can do | | --- | --- | | **Overview** | Check updates, alerts, recent transfers, and quick settings. | | **Games** | Browse cover art, search, filter by system or letter, and sort your collection. | | **Download Media** | Download artwork and game details for a few games or your whole library. | | **Content** | Browse folders, create subfolders, and upload or download files. | | **Transfers** | Follow uploads and their results. Downloads appear in your browser’s download manager. | | **Settings** | Adjust global preferences, core options, controller mappings, and the startup frontend. | > The WebUI is a local HTTP service without a login. Use a trusted network and > do not forward port **6769** to the internet. ##
Supported systems **33 native cores**, grouped below by family. Compatibility and performance vary by game. **Vulkan (GPU)** cores render on the GPU. **Software** cores render on the CPU, with Vulkan displaying the result. | Family | Systems | Core | Renderer | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | **Nintendo** | **NES / Famicom** | FCEUmm | Software | | | **Game Boy**

With [ShadowMountPlus](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus) 1.7beta4 or later running, it also lists each USB drive (**USB 0** to **USB 7**, `/mnt/usb0` onward) and extended storage (**EXTENDED 0** and **1**, `/mnt/ext0` and `/mnt/ext1`), only when a drive is mounted there. Without it, the sandbox hides them and **EXTERNAL** (`/mnt`) may be empty. ## Start a game from a home screen forwarder ### Make a tile in the WebUI The WebUI's **Game Forwarder** page makes home screen tiles that each open one game in RetroArch. Choose a system, then one of its games from your library, the name the home screen shows, the core (the game's own is chosen for you) and a picture: its box art, 3D box, logo, cartridge or disc, screenshot, title screen or fan art, filling the square or fitted in it, with the system's icon in the bottom right corner if you like. A picture the game has no file for yet is greyed out; **Download Media** can find it. Choose **Create tile**, then close RetroArch: the tile appears on the home screen. A new name or picture, and a tile you delete, reach the home screen the same way, a few seconds after RetroArch closes. A tile is a small title of its own, `PPSA99170` to `PPSA99269` in `/data/homebrew`, which [ShadowMountPlus](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus) 1.7 or later installs. The page needs it loaded with its API on (the default), and says so when it does not answer. ShadowMountPlus installs and removes nothing while a game runs, and RetroArch counts as one: that is why changes wait for RetroArch to close. Delete tiles from the page, which also removes their folder. A tile opens a game in the content folder or on a USB or extended storage drive. ### Make a forwarder by hand A forwarder is a small app with its own home screen tile that launches `PPSA99169` with launch arguments. The title then starts that game in RetroArch with the core given, instead of opening the picker or a frontend. | Argument | Meaning | | --- | --- | | `--rom ` or `--rom=` | The content to start: an absolute path (`/mnt/usb0/roms/snes/Game.zip`), or a path inside the title's `content/` folder (`/app0/content/`), such as `snes/Game.zip`. A folder is content for a core that opens folders, one whose info file lists `/` among its extensions: DOSBox Pure (`--rom /mnt/usb0/roms/dos/w95 --core dosbox_pure`), PUAE, VICE. A relative path may not contain `..`. | | `--core ` or `--core=` | The core to run it with, one of the title's: `snes9x`, `snes9x_libretro`, `snes9x_libretro.so` and `/app0/cores/snes9x_libretro.so` all name `/app0/cores/snes9x_libretro.so`. Without it, the core RetroArch's playlists associate with the content, or else the one core whose info file lists the file's extension (`.sfc` is Snes9x's; a Mega Drive `.md` or `.gen` is Genesis Plus GX's). An extension several cores take (`.cue`, `.chd`, `.iso`, `.zip`, `.bin`) needs `--core`. | | `--exit-after-game` | When RetroArch quits (Close Content or Quit), the title closes and the console returns to the home screen. Without it, the title then opens as from the home screen. | ```text --rom "snes/Game (USA).zip" --core snes9x --rom /mnt/usb0/roms/psx/Game.chd --core mednafen_psx_hw --exit-after-game ``` The game runs as a frontend's game does in game mode (`src/ps5_game.h`): the content and core are checked the same way, RetroArch starts with `-L ` and its own configuration, overrides and saves apply, and its log is `retroarch-game.log`. If the content is missing, the core is not one of the title's, or no core is named and none can be chosen, the reason is written to `trace.txt` (`forwarder: ... not run: ...`) and the title opens as from the home screen. A launch that names a mode (`--ps5-mode=...`) wins over `--rom`. The title's own restarts carry no arguments, so the forwarded game never starts twice. Arguments only reach a new process: if the title is already running, a forwarder should close it first. Parsing is in `src/frontend_mode_ps5.cpp`, checked by `tests/frontend_mode_ps5_test.cpp`. ## Compatibility and known limits Startup, controller input, audio, saved settings, and representative games have been tested on PS5. Compatibility and long-session testing are ongoing. - **Azahar:** a crash when closing content, switching to Azahar, and starting a game remains under investigation. - **RetroAchievements and NetPlay:** RetroArch starts its bundled Lapy service automatically through the console's local ELF loader, then reuses it on later launches. No Payload Manager autoload entry is needed. Files stay in their installation folder; existing `/app0` settings continue to work. Without the local loader or verified elevation, outgoing online features remain unavailable. See [service setup](platform/lapy/README.txt) and [online verification](evidence/online-features/README.txt). - Shader presets, disc swapping, and rumble still need broader testing. [Recorded evidence](evidence/) accompanies verified changes. For a bug report, include the core, file format, settings and reproduction steps. Preserve `retroarch.log` and `trace.txt` **before reopening RetroArch**: the frontend log is replaced on each launch. Remove private paths, addresses and credentials before sharing captures. --- ## Build from source
Build requirements and commands The current build uses Linux host tools and the project's cached public PS5 SDK. Start with `bash tools/doctor.sh` for host-tool checks. You also need `curl`, `patch`, `pkg-config`, ELF utilities such as `readelf`, and working host C/C++ compilers with sanitizer support for the tests. The target scripts currently use `/usr/bin/clang` through the SDK wrappers. Prepare and build [PS5_Vulkan](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Vulkan) following its own instructions, normally as a sibling directory: ```text workspace/ ├── PS5_RetroArch/ ├── PS5_Vulkan/ # The RADV release archive, its link recipe and dependencies ├── PS5_Mesa/ # My Mesa fork, which PS5_Vulkan builds RADV from └── PS5_PayloadSDK/ # My payload SDK fork and its platform layer, at a pinned revision ``` The cores that needed changes for the console build from my forks of them ([Libretro_PS5SX2](https://github.com/mihawk-99/Libretro_PS5SX2), [PS5_BeetlePSX](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_BeetlePSX), [PS5_Mupen64Plus](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Mupen64Plus), [PS5_BeetleSaturn](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_BeetleSaturn), [PS5_VICE](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_VICE), [PS5_MAME](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_MAME), [PS5_DeSmuME](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_DeSmuME), [PS5_Azahar](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Azahar) with [PS5_Dynarmic](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Dynarmic), [PS5_Flycast](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Flycast), [PS5_PicoDrive](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_PicoDrive), [PS5_BeetlePCE](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_BeetlePCE), [PS5_BeetlePCFX](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_BeetlePCFX), [PS5_BeetleVB](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_BeetleVB), [PS5_BeetleNGP](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_BeetleNGP), [PS5_BeetleWSwan](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_BeetleWSwan), [PS5_PokeMini](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_PokeMini), [PS5_Handy](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Handy), [PS5_VirtualJaguar](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_VirtualJaguar), [PS5_Stella](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Stella), [PS5_A5200](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_A5200), [PS5_ProSystem](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_ProSystem), [PS5_DOSBoxPure](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_DOSBoxPure), [PS5_Opera](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Opera), [PS5_PUAE](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_PUAE), [PS5_NeoCD](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_NeoCD), [PS5_ScummVM](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_ScummVM)), each pinned by revision in its build script. The script uses the sibling checkout when there is one, and `github.com/mihawk-99/` otherwise. The title build consumes PS5_Vulkan's RADV release archive (`tools/build-radv.sh release` there, built from PS5_Mesa at the revision it pins) and links it with that project's `tools/radv-link.sh`; it does not build the driver for you. `PS5_VULKAN_DRIVER=ps5vk` links ps5vk's driver, Vulkan runtime and shader-compiler archives instead, and `RADV_ARCHIVE` names another RADV archive. `PS5_VULKAN_DIR` can select an alternative checkout for the build; some host tests currently require the sibling layout above. Driver dependencies and setup requirements are documented in the driver repository. From the RetroArch repository root: ```bash make deps export PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK="$PWD/.deps/native/ps5-payload-sdk" export PS5_CLANG=/usr/bin/clang bash tools/fetch-retroarch.sh bash tools/build-title.sh # Create the artifacts inspected by the host tests bash tools/verify.sh ``` The five gates are **format → unit → build → integration → evidence**. The build pins RetroArch 1.22.2, fetches core sources/metadata with checked hashes, builds the frontend and thirty-three cores, and stages the native title in `dist/PPSA99169/`. The initial dependency/source fetch requires network access. To include the optional melonDS DS core, build with `PS5_WITH_MELONDSDS=1 bash tools/build-title.sh`. It uses pinned upstream sources and the software renderer with a native-memory JIT; DeSmuME remains available. `bash tools/build-melondsds.sh` builds and ABI-checks the core by itself. To include the optional SwanStation core, build with `PS5_WITH_SWANSTATION=1 bash tools/build-title.sh`. It uses pinned upstream sources, Vulkan and the x64 recompiler, with platform changes adapted from AngelXex's SwanStationPS5; Beetle PSX HW remains the PlayStation default. `bash tools/build-swanstation.sh` builds and ABI-checks the core by itself. The `ps5` microphone driver is the default. A core hears the DualSense microphone only while it turns its microphone on (melonDS DS while its microphone button is held, its default), the DualSense mute button silences it, and **Settings → Audio → Microphone** turns it off for every core. Capture stays in memory; the driver does not record files or send audio over the network. In melonDS DS, select `Microphone` as the input mode and `Always` as its button mode to use the DualSense mute button without assigning another game button. The core's screen-layout and microphone indicators can be hidden independently under **On-Screen Display & Notifications**. The optional melonDS DS port also accepts the DualSense touchpad as a relative stylus in Joystick or Auto touch mode. Slide to position the cursor, press to touch, and hold the press while sliding to drag. L2 remains available as Select; the touchpad click is reserved for the stylus while this core is running. For an already configured checkout: ```bash bash tools/build-title.sh # Build/stage the frontend and all shipped cores make genesis-plus-gx # Build and ABI-check one core only # Other core targets: fceumm, mgba, snes9x, fbneo bash tools/build-ppsspp.sh # The larger cores have scripts of their own: # build-ppsspp.sh, build-dolphin.sh, build-ps5sx2.sh, # build-beetle-psx.sh, build-mupen64plus.sh, # build-beetle-saturn.sh, build-vice.sh, # build-mame.sh, build-desmume.sh, build-azahar.sh, # build-flycast.sh, build-picodrive.sh, # build-beetle-pce.sh, build-beetle-pcfx.sh, # build-beetle-vb.sh, build-beetle-ngp.sh, # build-beetle-wswan.sh, build-pokemini.sh, # build-handy.sh, build-virtualjaguar.sh, # build-stella.sh, build-a5200.sh, build-prosystem.sh, # build-dosbox-pure.sh, build-opera.sh, build-puae.sh, # build-neocd.sh, build-scummvm.sh ``` When adding or updating a core, rebuild the title too: the frontend's native import table and build identity depend on the shipped core binaries. Source patches live in `patches/`; fetched and generated trees stay in ignored `vendor/`, `.deps/`, `build/` and `dist/` directories.

latestRelease.name: PS5_RetroArch-v4.0.0-beta-4
latestRelease.body:
# PS5_RetroArch-v4.0.0-beta-4 ## PS5 RetroArch is a passion project, not a piracy project. It exists so you can play the games you own on the console you own. - **Piracy is not condoned.** - **No games, BIOS files, console firmware or decryption keys are included, and they never will be.** - **Use only legally obtained backups of games you own**, made yourself from your own discs, cartridges or digital purchases. - **Use only BIOS and firmware files dumped from hardware you own.** - **Requests for, or links to, games, BIOS files, firmware or keys are not welcome** in this project's issues or discussions. --- ## Thank you This beta answers your reports. Each one below came with the logs or the steps that pinned the fault down. | Reporter | What they found | | --- | --- | |
**Kythros**
[@Kythros](https://github.com/Kythros) | **GameCube texture packs never showed** ([#5](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_RetroArch/issues/5)), with the exact line in Dolphin that gave them no memory. | |
**dann1k**
[@dann1k](https://github.com/dann1k) | **The PSP core crashed when its resolution changed** in the Quick Menu ([#63](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_RetroArch/issues/63)), with a trace that led straight to it. | |
**lomgth**
[@lomgth](https://github.com/lomgth) | **Renames that did not stick, games that could not be removed, and a RetroAchievements password that seemed lost** ([#55](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_RetroArch/issues/55), [#57](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_RetroArch/issues/57), [#58](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_RetroArch/issues/58)). | |
**Nek**
[@nekwebdev](https://github.com/nekwebdev) | **The WebUI's Update button never lit up** ([#69](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_RetroArch/issues/69)): releases lacked the checksum file the updater needs. | **Your games over the network. Frame generation without the doubled picture.** ## At a glance | What's new | What it brings | | --- | --- | |
**SMB** | Play games straight from a shared folder on your PC, chosen in the WebUI. | |
**Frame Generation** | No more doubled picture: the frames made in between now match the real ones. | |
**Your library** | Rename a game everywhere at once, and delete one from the WebUI. | |
**Fixes** | Texture packs for GameCube, PSP resolution changes, the WebUI's Update button. | ### In this release [SMB](#smb) · [Frame Generation](#frame-generation) · [Your library](#library) · [Fixes](#fixes) [Played on a Base PS5](#tested) · [Upgrading](#upgrading) · [Source and credits](#credits) ## SMB. Your games, from your PC. Keep your backups on your PC and play them on the PS5 without copying them over. RetroArch's file browser, Load Content included, has a new **SMB** entry after INTERNAL and EXTERNAL. 1. Share a folder on your PC (Windows file sharing, or Samba on Linux and macOS). 2. Open **SMB** in the WebUI and enter your PC's name or address under **Server**, with your user name and password (leave the user name empty to sign in as a guest). 3. Choose **Test connection**, then the **Share** and the **Folder** that holds your games, and **Save**. 4. In RetroArch, open **Load Content → SMB** and start a game. - **Most cores read the game straight from the share.** A core that opens files by itself gets a copy on the console first, removed when the game closes. - **Your password stays on your PS5.** The WebUI never shows it back to you, and it is sent only to your PC. - **Read-only.** Nothing on your share is changed. SMB support is inspired by [itsPLK's PS5 Package Manager](https://github.com/itsPLK/ps5-pkg-manager) and uses the same libsmb2 revision. ## Frame Generation without the doubled picture - **The frames made in between now match the real ones.** The GameCube core reported a smaller picture than it hands over, so every generated frame was a zoomed part of the real one. On screen the two alternated, which looked like a doubled image. - **A game below full speed shows its real frames again.** When a core fell behind, Frame Generation could show only frames made in between, never the game's own. - **Checked on every core.** Each core ran with Frame Generation on while every picture sent to the display was recorded and compared, generated with real. The results are below. ## Your library - **A rename reaches every list.** A name you edit in the WebUI's Games page now shows in RetroArch's playlists (XMB and RGUI) and in EmulationStation, every time you change it. - **Delete game.** The Files tab of a game in the WebUI deletes it from your PS5: the file, the track files its disc names, and its place in RetroArch and EmulationStation. Your saves and savestates are kept. When two copies share a name, the box art and details stay with the copy you keep. - **RetroAchievements shows you as signed in.** After you sign in, RetroArch keeps a sign-in token instead of your password; the WebUI now shows it as saved instead of "Not set". ## Fixes - **GameCube texture packs work.** Dolphin's custom texture cache had no memory on the PS5; it now has 512 MiB. Turn on **Load Custom Textures** in the Dolphin core options. - **PSP: changing Internal Resolution in the Quick Menu no longer closes RetroArch.** - **The WebUI's Update button works.** Every release now carries the checksum file the updater checks; v3.0.0-beta-3 has it too. ## Played on a Base PS5 | What | How it went | | --- | --- | | **SMB** | A share on a PC listed and saved in the WebUI, as a guest and with a password; a game on it started from Load Content > SMB. | | **Frame Generation** | All 35 cores tried, every picture sent to the display recorded. In 32, the generated frames sit between their real neighbours and the real frames are shown. DOSBox Pure at 70 Hz and ScummVM at 120 Hz correctly make none. NeoCD was not tried: no disc. | | **GameCube** | With a texture pack and Load Custom Textures on: no memory error, nothing unloaded, full speed. | | **PSP** | Internal Resolution raised from 6x to 8x during play, as the Quick Menu does: the game carried on at the new size. | | **Your library** | A game added from the WebUI, renamed (its playlist name followed), then deleted with its files and details. | ## Upgrading from v3.0.0-beta-3 1. **Back up your existing title folder**, especially configuration, saves, states, system files, content and any custom media. 2. **Use the WebUI's Update button**, or merge the complete `PPSA99169` folder from the package into your installation, keeping your own files and configuration. 3. Fully close and reopen PS5 RetroArch. **No games, BIOS files, console firmware, or decryption keys are supplied. Use only legally obtained backups of games you own and system files dumped from hardware you own.** ## Source, licences, and credits Changes since **v3.0.0-beta-3**. [Release source](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_RetroArch/tree/v4.0.0-beta-4); component source links and exact revisions are included in `licenses/components.json`. libsmb2 is built from its own repository at a pinned revision, under the LGPL-2.1-or-later. Snes9x, FinalBurn Neo, Genesis Plus GX, PicoDrive, Opera, and the Alekfull NX theme carry non-commercial restrictions. **This distribution may not be sold, and this release carries no donation link.** The package's `licenses/` directory records component licences and exact source revisions. RPCS3 is not included. Thank you to **itsPLK** for **PS5 Package Manager**, whose SMB client showed the way; to **Ronnie Sahlberg** and the **libsmb2** contributors; to everyone who reported a problem with the logs to find it; and to the RetroArch/libretro community, emulator and ES-DE developers, and the PS5 homebrew scene. Icons: Microsoft Fluent UI System Icons (MIT); system artwork: the [Linear ES-DE theme](https://gitlab.com/es-de/themes/linear-es-de). --- **Ready to get started?** [Available releases](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_RetroArch/releases) · [Installation guide](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_RetroArch#get-started) · [Source and credits](#credits)

repos.name: Breeze
repos.description: Custom fan curve for the PS5: a payload with a web panel and a home screen app. Live CPU and GPU temps, 24-hour history and presets.
repos.readme:
Breeze

A fan curve for your PS5.
Decide how loud the fan gets at every temperature, right from your PS5, phone or PC.

Download · Quick start · The app · Good to know · The panel · How it works · FAQ

--- ## Why Breeze
Your curve, your noise
Up to 30 points of temperature → fan %. Quiet when you're browsing, cool when you're gaming.		 Edit from anywhere
The Breeze app on the PS5 itself, or a web panel on your LAN: drag the curve on your phone or PC and hit Apply.		 Actually follows it
Reads the real fan speed every second and steers it to within 1–2% of your curve.
No sudden roars
Loading screens and sensor spikes are filtered, so the fan doesn't surge every scene change.		 Presets
Up to 10 curves. Apply saves your edits into the one in use, and the built-in one is always there to go back to.		 Safe by default
Stock fan until you turn the curve on, full cooling past 88 °C, and back to stock when you turn it off or Breeze stops, even if it's killed.
## Quick start There are three ways to run Breeze. The app is the easiest: it shows your curve on the screen and starts Breeze for you. ### The app from a store (easiest) 1. **Install it:** open **[ProsperoStore](https://github.com/darkxex/ProsperoStore)** or **[RecompStore](https://recompstore.com/game/PPSA92878)** on your PS5, search for **Breeze** and install it. The store keeps it up to date too. 2. **Open Breeze** from the home screen. It starts Breeze for you. 3. **Switch on Custom curve** (top right). Until you do, the fan stays fully stock. Breeze remembers the switch, so after that it runs your curve on every launch. The app needs [ShadowMountPlus](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus) and an ELF loader on port 9021 (elfldr). ### The app by hand, with the zip 1. **Download** `PPSA92878.zip` from the [latest release](https://github.com/MiladRTX/Breeze/releases/latest). 2. **Unzip it.** You get a folder called `PPSA92878`. 3. **Copy the whole folder** to `/data/homebrew/` on the console, over FTP for example (ftpsrv listens on port 2121). You should end up with `/data/homebrew/PPSA92878/eboot.bin`. 4. **Wait a few seconds:** ShadowMountPlus finds the folder and adds **Breeze** to the home screen, under **Media**. 5. **Open Breeze** and switch on **Custom curve** (top right). To update by hand, close the app and copy the new `PPSA92878` folder over the old one. Coming from a Breeze that sits under Games (1.9 and older)? Delete it first, then copy the new folder: the PS5 only moves an app to Media on a fresh install. ### Payload only No app, just the payload and the web panel on your phone or PC. 1. **Download** `breeze.elf` from the [latest release](https://github.com/MiladRTX/Breeze/releases/latest). 2. **Load it** with [Payload Manager](https://github.com/itsPLK/ps5-payload-manager): choose **Upload ELF Payload**, then launch it. 3. **Open the panel.** The console pops up the address: > Breeze running (stock fan)
> Turn the curve on at `http://:2878` On the first start Breeze also adds a **Breeze tile to your home screen** (unless the [Breeze app](#the-app) is installed): open it and the panel comes up in the PS5 browser. 4. **Switch on Custom curve** (top right). Until you do, the fan stays fully stock. Breeze remembers the switch, so after that it runs your curve on every launch. > [!TIP] > Add Breeze to Payload Manager's **Autoload** list so your curve is back after every reboot. To update, just launch the new version: it replaces the running one by itself.
Using elfldr directly instead
Send the ELF to the loader on port 9021: ```sh nc -q0 9021 < breeze.elf ```
## The app Breeze also comes as an app for the PS5 home screen: the same curve, history, presets and settings as the web panel, on the screen with the DualSense. **Install it** from [ProsperoStore](https://github.com/darkxex/ProsperoStore), [RecompStore](https://recompstore.com/game/PPSA92878) or by hand with `PPSA92878.zip`: see [Quick start](#quick-start). **It needs** [ShadowMountPlus](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus) and an ELF loader on port 9021 (elfldr): the app carries its own `breeze.elf` and starts it when Breeze isn't running. Breeze keeps running after you close the app, and the app takes the place of the browser tile. - **After a reboot,** open the app once to start Breeze again, or add `breeze.elf` to Payload Manager's **Autoload** list so it starts by itself. - **After an update,** open the app once: if an older Breeze is running, the app replaces it with its own copy. The version at the top of the app is the running Breeze's. - **It's a Media app,** so it stays open next to a game: check the fan mid-game and jump straight back. To start a *different* game while Breeze is open, close the current game first; picking the new one directly gives error CE-105773-3. Every Media homebrew app does this (Stremio too). | Tab | Controls | | --- | --- | | **Curve** | ←→ choose a point, ↑↓ fan, L2/R2 temperature, slide on the touchpad to move the point, △ add, □ remove, L3/R3 undo and redo, ✕ apply, ○ revert | | **History** | ←→ range (5 minutes to 24 hours), slide on the touchpad to look back | | **Presets** | ↑↓ choose, ✕ use, △ new preset from the curve, □ delete (asks for a second press) | | **Settings** | Custom curve on or off, reset to the built-in Breeze preset | L1 and R1 switch tabs. While the app is open the PS5 treats it like a game, so the fan minimum is the in-game 23%. ## Good to know - **The PS5 has a minimum fan speed:** 13% in the menus, 23% while a game or app runs. Breeze can add fan on top of that but never go below it, so in a game the fan only rises once your curve asks for more than 23% (from about 60 °C with the default curve). - **The fan settles within about 1–2% of your curve,** 10–20 s after a big change. - **Dots are joined by straight lines:** halfway between 60 °C at 30% and 70 °C at 40% is 35% at 65 °C. - **Past 88 °C Breeze always asks for full cooling,** whatever your curve says. - **Stopping Breeze hands the fan back to stock,** whether you turn Custom curve off, reboot, or kill it. ## The panel | Part | What it does | | --- | --- | | **Readouts** | CPU and GPU temperature, fan speed, what your curve asks for, and the target Breeze gives the PS5. The curve follows the CPU; the GPU is shown only. Hover (or tap) any of them for a short explanation. | | **Curve** | Drag points, double-click empty space to add one or a point to remove it, arrow keys to nudge. The dashed lines show where the temperature and fan are right now; the shaded band is the 23% in-game minimum. | | **History** | 5 minutes to 24 hours of temperature and fan speed. Hover to see any moment. | | **Presets** | Use, rename or delete saved curves, or start a new one from the curve in the editor. The one in use is marked **Active**: Apply saves your edits into it. The built-in **Breeze** preset never changes: edits of it are saved as a new preset, "My curve". | | **Points** | The same curve as a table, for exact values. | Nothing changes until you press **Apply** (or Ctrl + S). ## How it works The PS5 has no "set the fan to 40 %" switch. Its fan controller works like a **thermostat**: you give it a target temperature and it spins the fan to cool towards it. Breeze closes the loop around that thermostat. Every second it: 1. reads the CPU temperature and the **real** fan speed, 2. looks up what your curve wants at that temperature, 3. nudges the target up or down, in fractions of a degree, until the fan matches. Breeze makes small corrections and lets each one settle, ignores one-second spikes and dips, and backs off fast if the fan overshoots, so the fan stays within about 1–2% of your curve without jumping. When Breeze hands the fan back, it puts back the console's own target (91 °C on a PS5 Slim), which it learns from the console itself, and never anything warmer than 91 °C. ## FAQ
Is it safe for my console?
Breeze only changes the fan controller's target. Past 88 °C it always asks for full cooling, the console keeps its own minimum fan speed, and turning the curve off or stopping Breeze, even by killing it, hands the fan straight back to the console's own setting. Still, keep an eye on your temperatures, especially with very quiet curves.
Why isn't the fan exactly on my curve?
Breeze steers the PS5's thermostat, not the fan itself, so it gets the fan to within about 1–2% of the curve rather than exactly on it, and takes a few seconds after each change. Gaps of 2% or less are left alone on purpose, so the fan doesn't keep shifting. It also can't go under the console's minimum (13% in the menus, 23% in a game). Steep sections of the curve make the fan jumpy during loading screens, so add a dot where you want a gentler bend.
Why does the Fan readout say "console"?
Other parts of the console can ask for more fan. The PS5 cools some parts on its own, and when one of them needs more than your curve, the Fan readout says **console**. That's the PS5 protecting itself.
What is breeze-guard.elf?
The small helper next to breeze.elf in the process list. If breeze.elf is killed (from Payload Manager's process list, for example), the guard puts the console's own fan setting back within about a second. Leave it running: Breeze restarts it within 10 seconds if it's stopped, and it exits by itself once the fan is back.
The fan seems stuck after Breeze stopped
Launch Breeze again (it puts back what a stopped copy left behind), start or close a game, or reboot.
Known limitations
Breeze is new and has been tested on one console (a PS5 Slim), so expect some rough edges: - **Short spikes can still happen** for a few seconds right as a game launches. - **History is saved every 5 minutes,** so if Breeze is killed the last few minutes of the graph are lost. Found something off? [Open an issue](https://github.com/MiladRTX/Breeze/issues) and attach `/data/breeze/breeze.log` if you can.
Where are my settings stored?
| Path | What | | --- | --- | | `/data/breeze/breeze.conf` | Curve, on/off, panel port, panel token | | `/data/breeze/presets.conf` | Saved presets | | `/data/breeze/history.bin` | The last 24 hours of history, so the graph survives a restart | | `/data/breeze/stock.conf` | The console's own fan target, learned by Breeze (delete it to relearn) | | `/data/breeze/breeze.log` | Controller log, up to 256 KB; the one before is kept as `breeze.log.1` |
How do I build it myself?
Needs [ps5-payload-sdk](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk), CMake and Ninja: ```sh PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK=/path/to/ps5-payload-sdk ./build.sh # -> build/breeze.elf ``` The panel is plain HTML in [`web/panel.html`](web/panel.html) and gets embedded into the ELF. Opened on its own, it runs with sample data, which is handy for working on the design. The app builds in Linux or WSL with clang and lld 18, make and Python 3, after `build.sh`: ```sh app/build.sh # -> build/app/PPSA92878 and PPSA92878.zip ``` It fetches [ps5-native-app-boilerplate](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-native-app-boilerplate) at a pinned commit. `app/preview/run.sh` draws every screen as a PNG on a PC, without a console.
## Credits Made by **[Milad](https://github.com/MiladRTX)**. Thanks to [John Törnblom](https://github.com/john-tornblom) for the [PS5 payload SDK](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk), to [aydencharles](https://github.com/aydencharles) for [onionHEN](https://github.com/aydencharles/onionHEN), where the fan controller interface was first worked out, and to [BlackBearReloaded](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded) for [ps5-native-app-boilerplate](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-native-app-boilerplate), which the app is built on. The app uses the [Inter](https://rsms.me/inter/) and [JetBrains Mono](https://www.jetbrains.com/lp/mono/) fonts (SIL Open Font License). ## License [GPL-3.0](LICENSE) > [!WARNING] > Breeze is an unofficial homebrew project and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Sony Interactive Entertainment. It changes how your console's fan behaves: use it only on hardware you own, keep an eye on temperatures, and use it at your own risk. No warranty is provided.
