latestRelease.name: Beetle PCE PS5 1.1.1
latestRelease.body:
## Beetle PCE PS5 1.1.1

### Fixed

- **A card for a game without a cover shows a PC Engine pad** with its two round buttons (II, I). Before, it showed the four coloured buttons of a Super Nintendo pad, left over from Snes9x PS5. Thanks to [CroCop86](https://github.com/CroCop86) for the report ([genplusgxPS5#4](https://github.com/MisterTemaki/genplusgxPS5/issues/4)).
- CD games on network shares:
  - On a slow link, the running game's own read-ahead now goes before the CD's background prefetch.
  - Blocks already kept for an earlier track are no longer counted twice against the prefetch budget.
  - When a `.cue`'s `.bin` mixes 2048- and 2352-byte tracks, each track's start is now fetched ahead at the right place. Music tracks in `.wav`/`.ogg` files only have their own start fetched.
  - A socket's non-blocking switch now stays in step with the console's.

### Files

- `BeetlePCEPS5-v1.1.1.elf`: send it to your payload loader (port 9021).
- `BeetlePCEPS5-v1.1.1-PPSA99925.zip`: the app folder, used by Settings > Updates. You don't need to download it yourself.
- `pce-ps5-v1.1.1-src.zip`: the source, including libsmb2 and libnfs (LGPL-2.1).

### Status

It passes 429 host tests (the same code on Linux, the PS5 calls simulated). The new card was checked on the host's rendered screens. **The network shares and `.7z` support have not been run on a PS5 yet.** Please report what works and what doesn't, with Settings > Debug logs on (the logs are in `/data/pce/logs/`).

Licences: Beetle PCE (Mednafen) GPL-2.0-or-later, and the builds with it; the port's new code MIT; libsmb2 and libnfs LGPL-2.1-or-later; the LZMA SDK public domain. Port by [MisterTemaki](https://github.com/MisterTemaki).

repos.name: fbneo-ps5
repos.description: Port of Final Burn Neo for PS5
repos.readme:
# FBNeo PS5

> **The title ID is now PPSA99924** (it was PPSA99012 up to 1.8, which another app in the homebrew catalog uses). From 1.9 on the app installs in `/data/homebrew/PPSA99924/`; our old version under `/data/homebrew/PPSA99012/` stays as a separate icon until you delete it (check that the folder is ours first), and your games, saves and settings are kept. Replace the old ELF in your autoload. See [New title ID](#new-title-id-ppsa99924).

[![FBNeo for PS5](ps5/docs/banner.jpg)](ps5/app/sce_sys/background-source.png)

[FinalBurn Neo](https://github.com/finalburnneo/FBNeo) (FBNeo) 1.0.0.3, the arcade emulator, running on a jailbroken
PS5 as a **native home-screen app** with its own icon and background. It plays the arcade games FBNeo emulates --
8,379 drivers: Capcom CPS-1, CPS-2 and CPS-3, **Neo Geo MVS/AES**, IGS PGM and PGM2, Cave, Toaplan, Psikyo, Sega
System 1/16/18/24/32, X and Y boards, Konami, Taito, Irem, Data East, Midway, Kaneko, Seta, the classics of the 70s
and 80s, and many more -- from their ROM sets (`.zip` or `.7z`), named as FBNeo names them, on the console, a USB
drive or a network share (SMB or NFS).

**Inside the emulator, to access the main menu press L3 + R3.**

This port is for the **arcade games only**. FBNeo's home-console drivers (Mega Drive, PC Engine, Master System,
NES, SNES, MSX, ColecoVision, SG-1000, ZX Spectrum, Channel F, GBA, Neo Geo Pocket) and the Neo Geo CD are not built
in: Genesis Plus GX PS5, Snes9x PS5 and Mesen2 PS5 cover the consoles.

The PS5 layer follows the layout of PS5SX2 (the PCSX2 port) and of Snes9x PS5, Mesen2 PS5 and Genesis Plus GX PS5,
the ports it comes from:

- `ps5/coreorbis` holds `main-boot.cpp`, the `orbis-shims/` and `include-orbis/`;
- `ps5/frontend` holds the user interface, the 3D game shelf and the glue to FBNeo's core (`fe_burn.cpp`);
- `ps5/core.mk` and `ps5/core/` build FBNeo's core from its own build lists;
- `ps5/proto/native` builds and signs `eboot.bin`;
- `ps5/installer` is the installer and helper payload.

Everything outside `ps5/` is FBNeo's source, **unchanged**, apart from this README (the original one is
[README-FBNeo.md](README-FBNeo.md)). The core -- `src/burn` (the drivers), `src/cpu` and the libraries it uses -- is
compiled as it is, with the object lists of FBNeo's `makefile.burn_rules` and the generated sources its makefiles
make (the driver list, Musashi's 68000 core, the CPS, Neo Geo, Cave, Psikyo, Toaplan and PGM render functions).
`ps5/frontend/fe_burn.cpp` is the frontend FBNeo's core needs, written again for this port the way FBNeo's own
frontends (`src/burner`) and its libretro port host the core: ROM loading from the sets' zips and 7z archives, inputs, DIP
switches, states, NVRAM, the picture turned the right way up and the sound.

> **Status (2.1):** builds with the ps5-payload-dev SDK into a signed native app, and passes 532 host tests, which
> run the same code (FBNeo's core included) on Linux with the PS5 calls simulated: two arcade boards running a tiny
> test program each (a vertical and a horizontal game) are played through the whole chain -- the shelf, the pad,
> the core, the video and sound output -- and 26 more boards start, run, save and load a state under
> AddressSanitizer. The network shares and the `.7z` sets have run only in those tests (a local folder standing in
> for the share), not yet on a PS5; 2.1's choice of player per controller has run with up to four simulated pads,
> not yet with several real controllers. If something fails, the logs in `/data/fbneo/logs/` say where.

## How it works

The PS5 gives the controller only to the app in front, so FBNeo runs as a native app opened from its icon, and the
payload you send is its installer:

| Piece | What it is | In PS5SX2 |
|---|---|---|
| `eboot.bin` in `/data/homebrew/PPSA99924/` | **FBNeo itself**, a native app opened from its icon | PCSX2 (PPSA99203) |
| `sce_module/libc.prx` | the C runtime module every native app carries | the same file, byte for byte |
| `FBNeoPS5.elf` (payload) | the **installer**: installs or updates the app, then stays running as the **helper** | PS5SX2Installer.elf + PS5SX2Helper.elf |

FBNeo is big (`eboot.bin` is 43 MB), so the installer carries it and the background compressed and unpacks them
on the console: `FBNeoPS5.elf` is about 22 MB.

When it opens, the app asks the helper to let it out of its sandbox; without that an app sees neither `/data`
nor USB drives. The request is the one PS5SX2 makes:

- **Who is asked, in order:** the FBNeo helper (127.0.0.1:9092 since 1.9; 1.8's used 9082; older helpers used 9078 in 1.0 and 9079 up to
  1.7, and are left alone),
  then etaHEN (9028) and the daemon on port 9069.
- **If nobody answers:** the app carries a copy of the helper (`FBNeoPS5-helper.elf`), sends it to the ELF loader
  (127.0.0.1:9021) and asks again. So the icon keeps working after a reboot, as long as the ELF loader runs.
- **What the helper allows:** only title PPSA99924. It gives the process the system's root folder and uid 0, as
  elfldr does for payloads. No other app is touched.

FBNeo PS5 only uses `/data/fbneo/`, `/data/homebrew/PPSA99924/` and its own `/user/appmeta/PPSA99924/`. It sits
next to Snes9x PS5 (PPSA99922, helper port 9089), Mesen2 PS5 (PPSA99923, port 9091), Genesis Plus GX PS5 (PPSA99921, port 9088) and PS5SX2 (PPSA99203) without touching them.

## Versions

Every release carries its version in the file name: `FBNeoPS5-v2.1.elf` (`make dist`). When updating, replace the
old ELF with the new one in your autoload or Payload Manager. In this README, "`FBNeoPS5.elf`" always means the
current release's ELF.

**2.1:** **Choose which arcade player each controller plays** (thanks to gitloth, fbneo-ps5#3). The simple way:
**Choose players** in the pause menu (or at the top of Settings, CONTROLS, CONTROLLERS on the shelf) asks "Player 1:
press X on your controller", then Player 2, and so on: whoever presses X gets that player, as in many PS5 games. A
4-player game that ties each character to its cabinet's slot (The Simpsons, Sunset Riders) can be played by three
people on the slots they want. The advanced way: a row for each controller (its light bar's colour, and whether it is
connected) with the player it plays, Player 1 to 4 or none; choosing a player another controller has swaps them, so
nobody is left without one. There a single controller can play player 2 (the 2-player editions). Like the button layout, a change from a game's pause menu is kept for that game (and its clones), one from the
shelf's Settings for every game; **Default controls** (it was Default button layout) puts the buttons and the players
back. A game that starts with a controller on another player says so for a few seconds ("Controller 1: Player 3").
The pause menu (L3 + R3) stays on controller 1, whatever player it plays. When a user signs in or out during a game the
message comes again, and a pad that moves up a slot keeps working (it could stop answering for a few seconds before).
See [Controls](#controls).

**2.0:** **A button layout per game** (thanks to yuri310258, fbneo-ps5#2): change the buttons in Settings,
CONTROLS from a game's pause menu and the change is kept for that game only (`/data/fbneo/config/<set>.btn`); a
clone without its own uses its parent's, the others keep the general layout (the shelf's Settings). See
[Controls](#controls). **Auto now gives 6-button games Fighting (R1 R2)**, Capcom's PlayStation layout (punches
Square, Triangle, R1; kicks Cross, Circle, R2) instead of heavy kick on L1; a layout you chose stays, and Fighting
(6 buttons) is still there. **A game with no cover** gets a card with an arcade panel (a stick and six buttons)
instead of the SNES pad's four coloured buttons, and a long title starts below it (thanks to CroCop86,
genplusgxPS5#4). Also in 2.0, from 1.9.1 (not released on its own): the interface in English, Spanish, Portuguese
(Brazil), French and German, and debug logs off by default. And what the other ports have (CroCop86 asked for them on
Beetle PCE PS5, NES FCEUmm PS5 and Genesis Plus GX PS5), ported from NES FCEUmm PS5 1.1:

- **Sets on network shares (SMB and NFS):** keep your ROM sets on a NAS or PC and play them from the shelf (Settings,
  LIBRARY, Network shares, with an on-screen keyboard and Test connection). A set's parent and BIOS sets are found on
  the console first, then on the shares. A set is read as its driver starts; nothing is read from the share while it
  runs. Saves, states, NVRAM, high scores, DIP switches, button layouts, samples and covers stay on the console. The
  sets on a share are listed at once and checked in the background. After the design of
  [thatboialex](https://github.com/thatboialex)'s pull request to Snes9x PS5
  ([#3](https://github.com/MisterTemaki/snes9xPS5/pull/3)). See [Network shares](#network-shares-smb-and-nfs).
- **Shelf tabs:** Internal, USB and Network on **L1 / R1**, as in the other ports; the letters stay on Up / Down, **L2 /
  R2 now skip 10 games** (L1 / R1 did), and the makers moved to **L3 / R3** (the sticks pressed; L2 / R2 before).
  Square on the Network tab scans the shares again. See [Controls](#controls).
- **`.7z` sets:** a set can be a `.7z` (LZMA, LZMA2, PPMd...) instead of a `.zip`, as in FBNeo's own frontends, read
  with FBNeo's own LZMA SDK copy. See [7-Zip sets](#7-zip-sets).
- The new screens in the five languages. libsmb2 and libnfs (LGPL-2.1-or-later) are built in, as the other ports carry
  them.
- **Not tried on a PS5 yet:** the network shares and the `.7z` sets have run only in the host tests (a local folder
  standing in for the share).

**1.9.1** (not released on its own; in 2.0): **Interface languages:** English (the default), Spanish, Portuguese (Brazil), French and German
(Settings, SYSTEM, Language; see [Language](#language)). **Debug logs are off by default** (turn them on in
Settings, SYSTEM, Debug logs, to report a problem).

**1.9:** **New title ID: PPSA99924** (it was PPSA99012, which another app in the homebrew catalog uses; see
[New title ID](#new-title-id-ppsa99924)). Nothing under the old ID is touched (it may be
another app's): an earlier version of ours stays as its own icon until you delete it. Games, saves and settings are shared. The helper listens on port 9092.
**Updates from the app** (Settings, SYSTEM, Updates), as Porpoise does: see [Updates](#updates). A big library
no longer holds "Looking for games..." for long: each zip is looked at once per start (the ROM check of a set
keeps the size and date the folder walk read, instead of asking the drive again for every set, its parent and
its BIOS: 6613 file lookups for 2500 zips before, 2500 now), and the screen counts the zips found, then shows a
bar while the sets are checked.

**1.8:** **The helper downloads the covers with its own HTTPS.** Up to 1.7 the helper got nothing on the console:
the console's own HTTPS (libSceSsl) fails outside the app's sandbox, and every cover failed in a few milliseconds
while the counter went down. The helper now has its own HTTPS, as Genesis Plus GX PS5 1.6 and Snes9x PS5 2.3 do:
Mbed TLS, with Mozilla's list of certificate authorities, the server's certificate checked as a browser does. It
also keeps one connection for all its downloads. After updating, send `FBNeoPS5-v1.8.elf` once (or let the app
start its helper itself): the older helper keeps running until the console restarts, but 1.8 uses its own (port
9082).

**1.7:** **No hot keys on L2 and R2:** fast forward (R2) and the L2 combinations are gone. Save and load states,
change the slot, and press the machine's **Service** button or **Test** switch from the pause menu (L3 + R3), which
gains those two items. L2 and R2 do nothing unless the button layout puts a game button on them.

**1.6:** **L2 and R2 as game buttons**, handy in 6-button games: any arcade button can go to L2 or R2 in the
Custom layout, and a new **Fighting (R1 R2)** layout puts the punches on Square, Triangle, R1 and the kicks on
Cross, Circle, R2 (Capcom's own PlayStation layout). (See [Controls](#controls).)

**1.5:** **Settings, BIOS sets:** which BIOS sets your games need, and for each one whether its zip is there and
complete, with the missing ROMs named (see [ROM sets](#rom-sets)).

**1.4:**

- **Rewind removed.** Holding L2 + R2 does nothing now, and the setting is gone from the Settings screen. No
  snapshots are taken while you play, so no game spends any time on them (CPS-3's state is 10 MB). Save states
  (in the pause menu) are unchanged.

**1.3:**

- **CPS-3 (Street Fighter III and the rest) no longer slowed down by the rewind.** The rewind keeps a snapshot of the game every few
  frames, and 1.0 to 1.2 compressed each one on the game's own thread. CPS-3's state is 10 MB, so every third frame
  took several frames' time: the game crawled and stuttered. Now the game's thread only copies the state (a few
  milliseconds, every sixth frame for a state this big) and another thread compresses it; a snapshot that would
  have to wait is skipped. Every board with a big state (PGM2, Konami GX...) gains the same.

**1.2:**

- **The DIP switches are set before a game starts**, as in FBNeo's own frontends. 1.0 and 1.1 set them from the
  first frame on, so a driver that reads them while it starts saw them all off: the Neo Geo booted the first BIOS
  of its list instead of the one its BIOS switch names, and other drivers their first region. Your saved switches
  (`config/<set>.dip`) also go in before the start now, so they no longer need a Reset to take effect.
- A review of the frontend against FBNeo's own (what it must give a driver before and after it starts) found no
  other gap of the kind that left Cabal and Cobra Command black.

**1.1:**

- **Covers download in the background.** 1.0 downloaded them before the app opened (up to 30 s with the launch
  screen up) and restarted itself for new ones. Now the helper downloads them while you use the app: it starts at
  once, the covers around the selection come first, and each one appears on the shelf as it lands ("Downloading
  covers in the background... N left").
- **Black screen in Cabal (and other drivers that build their palette only when the frontend asks):** fixed.
  FBNeo's own frontends ask every driver for its palette once it starts; 1.0 didn't.
- From the 1.0 code review: merged sets (clones inside the parent's zip), a clone still listed with Show clones off
  when its parent isn't, repeated DIP switch names kept apart, ROMs read without a second copy, the set check
  redone after an FBNeo update.

After updating, send `FBNeoPS5-v1.1.elf` once (or let the app start its helper itself): 1.0's helper keeps running
until the console restarts, but 1.1 uses its own.

**1.0:** the first release.

## New title ID (PPSA99924)

Up to 1.8, FBNeo PS5 used the title ID PPSA99012. The homebrew catalog
([homebrew.page](https://homebrew.page/app/PPSA99012/)) lists that ID for another app, and two apps with one title ID
can't be on the console together: the second one's folder and home-screen icon take the first one's place. So
from 1.9 on the app is **PPSA99924**, an ID no listed app uses, and it installs in `/data/homebrew/PPSA99924/`.

**Nothing under the old ID is touched:** `/data/homebrew/PPSA99012/` may just as well be the other app's, so the
installer never renames, removes or unregisters it. When our own earlier version is still there (its
`param.json` carries FBNeo PS5's content ID), the notification says so: it is a separate icon, the old version. To
remove it, delete the folder `/data/homebrew/PPSA99012/` (over FTP, for example), then select the old icon on the home
screen, press **OPTIONS** and choose **Delete** (deleting only the icon isn't enough: ShadowMountPlus finds the folder
again and puts the icon back).

Games, saves, states, covers and settings live in `/data/fbneo/`, which doesn't depend on the title ID: the new
version finds everything where it was. The helper listens on a new port, because the helpers of 1.8 and older
only let PPSA99012 out.

**Replace the old ELF in your autoload** with the new ELF, or the old version keeps
being installed beside the new one.

## Updates

From 1.9 on, the app updates itself from this repository's GitHub releases, as
[Porpoise](https://github.com/elripalda/Porpoise-Dolphin-Emulator-for-PS5) does:

- **Settings, SYSTEM, Updates** shows the version you have and what to do: *Check now*, *Install 2.0 (60 MB)*,
  the download and install progress, then *Installed: restart* (Cross opens the new version).
- Once a day, when the app starts, it checks by itself; when a newer version is out, a notification says so.
  Nothing is installed without you choosing *Install*.
- The helper does the work (the app's own HTTPS doesn't work once it is out of its sandbox), with its own HTTPS
  (Mbed TLS, certificates checked). It asks `api.github.com/repos/MisterTemaki/FBNeo-PS5/releases/latest` for
  the newest release and takes its asset `FBNeoPS5-v<version>-PPSA99924.zip`. It is about 60 MB (the app's eboot.bin is stored as it is, so the console can check and write each file without unpacking).
- The zip is checked before anything is written: its size and SHA-256 against what GitHub gives, then every file
  against the zip's own list (`PPSA99924/manifest.sha256`). Each file is written beside the old one, then all are
  put in place with `eboot.bin` last; files the new version no longer has are removed, and the home screen's
  copy of the art is refreshed. If anything fails before that, nothing has changed.
- Only `/data/homebrew/PPSA99924/` changes. Games, saves and settings aren't touched.
- **Your autoload:** the app updated this way is newer than the ELF in your autoload. The older ELF sees that and
  leaves the app alone (its notification says so), and its helper still serves the newer app. Put the new ELF in
  your autoload when you can: a new version may come with a new helper.

For a release, `make dist` builds the zip (`build/dist/FBNeoPS5-v<version>-PPSA99924.zip`, the app
folder stored without compression, with its manifest). Attach it to the GitHub release, tagged `v<version>`,
next to the ELF. The same zip is what the homebrew catalog lists.

## Language

Settings (Triangle on the shelf), **SYSTEM**, **Language**: **English** (the default), **Español**, **Português
(Brasil)**, **Français**, **Deutsch**. The change applies at once, to every menu and message, and is kept in
`fbneo-ps5.ini` (`language=0` to `4`). The logs stay in English. Game names, board and maker names, DIP switch
texts (they come from FBNeo's drivers), the PS5's button names and the shaders' names are not translated; the
installer's and the helper's notifications stay in English.

## Requirements

- A jailbroken PS5 with **kstuff** (or kstuff-lite) and an **ELF loader** on port 9021: elfldr, etaHEN, or the
  one PS5 Payload Manager uses.
- **ShadowMountPlus**, so the icon appears on the home screen (the same one PS5SX2 uses).
- Your own ROM sets. None are included.

## Install and play

1. **Send `FBNeoPS5.elf`** with PS5 Payload Manager, or from a PC on the same network:
   ```sh
   nc -q0 PS5_IP 9021 < FBNeoPS5-v2.0.elf
   ```
   It installs the app in `/data/homebrew/PPSA99924/` (`eboot.bin`, `sce_module/libc.prx`, `param.json`, the
   icon and the backgrounds), shows **"FBNeo PS5 2.0 installed. Open it from the FBNeo PS5 icon on the home
   screen."** and stays running as the helper.
2. **Open the FBNeo PS5 icon.** The game shelf appears and the controller works.
3. **Copy your ROM sets** to `/data/fbneo/roms/` (over FTP, for example), or to `fbneo/roms/` on a USB drive.
   Subfolders are fine. The app makes the folders on its first start.

Tip: put `FBNeoPS5.elf` in your autoload, as PS5SX2 recommends for its payloads.

**Updating:** send the new `FBNeoPS5.elf` once. It compares every app file with the copy it carries and rewrites
only what changed; each file is written to a temporary file and then renamed, `eboot.bin` last. A deleted or
damaged file is put back the same way. A second copy sent while the helper is already running only installs and
exits.

**If "FBNeo PS5 has no access to /data" appears:** no helper answered and the ELF loader wasn't running. Send
`FBNeoPS5.elf` and open the icon again.

## ROM sets

FBNeo PS5 plays the ROM sets of FinalBurn Neo at the commit below, with the same names. "1.0.0.3" alone is not
enough: FBNeo keeps that version number while its sets change almost every day, so check your sets against the DAT.

**The list of sets: [`ps5/dat/fbneo-ps5-arcade.dat`](ps5/dat/fbneo-ps5-arcade.dat).** FBNeo PS5 doesn't use RetroArch
or the libretro core: it builds FBNeo's core itself, the arcade drivers only, from FinalBurn Neo 1.0.0.3 as of
commit [`658540d`](https://github.com/finalburnneo/FBNeo/commit/658540d46c1c0efce9627667c0f9236e7b2be916)
(2026-10-08). The DAT lists every set it plays: 8,378 sets for its 8,379 drivers (two are named `neogeo`, the
BIOS and the cartridge-less system), BIOS and board sets included, each ROM with its name,
size and CRC, parents and clones, samples. FBNeo's own DAT writer makes it from the same sources the app is built
from (ClrMamePro / Logiqx XML, like FBNeo's `FBNeo_-_Arcade.dat`; `make dat`). It describes the core of FBNeo PS5 2.1
exactly, and from now on each release carries it too (`FBNeoPS5-v<version>-arcade.dat`). Load it in ClrMamePro,
RomVault or RomCenter to check or rebuild your sets; merged, split and non-merged sets all work (below). Thanks to
JamesWestFR for asking ([fbneo-ps5#4](https://github.com/MisterTemaki/fbneo-ps5/issues/4)).

As in every FBNeo build:

- **One zip per set, named as FBNeo names it:** `sf2ce.zip`, `mslug.zip`, `pacman.zip` (or `sf2ce.7z`: see
  [7-Zip sets](#7-zip-sets)). The name is how the game is recognised; a renamed zip is not.
- **Clones need their parent:** `sf2ceua.zip` (a clone) loads what it shares with `sf2ce.zip` from there, so put the
  parent next to it (anywhere in the ROM folders: the console's, a USB drive's or a share's). Merged sets (the clones inside the parent's zip, as
  ClrMamePro's "merged" option makes them) work too: a clone with no zip of its own is listed when all of its ROMs
  are in its parent's zip with the right CRC (`boot.log`: `<parent>.zip#<clone>`).
- **BIOS sets:** the games of a board with a BIOS need the BIOS set too, anywhere in the ROM folders (a share's
  included):

  | Games | BIOS set |
  |---|---|
  | Neo Geo MVS / AES | `neogeo.zip` |
  | IGS PGM | `pgm.zip` |
  | other boards with a BIOS | the set FBNeo names for them: `decocass`, `skns`, `isgsm`, `bubsys`, `atarisy1`... and the chips' internal ROMs (`cchip`, `nmk004`, `ym2608`, `midssio`, `namcoc69`/`70`/`75`) |

  The BIOS sets are not games: they are not listed on the shelf. **Settings, BIOS sets** (Cross) shows them all:
  first the ones your games need, each **OK** (green), **Missing** (red: no zip) or **N ROMs missing** (red: the
  zip lacks some, named under the list), then the others. Under the list: where the zip is, how many of your games
  need it, and for `neogeo.zip` how many of its optional BIOS versions it has (the BIOS DIP switch picks one). The
  check is the one made when the shelf last read the game list; `boot.log` has it too (`[bios] ...` lines).
- **The set must match FBNeo 1.0.0.3** (the DAT above): ROMs are found by their CRC, then by their name. A set made for another
  emulator, or for a much older or newer FBNeo, can miss ROMs or have others.
- **Samples:** the few games that play recorded sounds (Donkey Kong's walk, for example) look for their sample set
  (`dkong.zip`) in `/data/fbneo/samples/`. Without it they play without those sounds.
- **High scores:** with FBNeo's `hiscore.dat` in `/data/fbneo/hiscore/` (from
  [libretro/FBNeo's metadata folder](https://github.com/libretro/FBNeo/blob/master/metadata/hiscore.dat)), the
  games it knows keep their high score tables (`<set>.hi`, same folder). Settings, "Save high scores", turns it
  off.

**Checked before they are listed:** at each start the shelf checks every set it finds the way FBNeo loads it (only
the archives' directories are read), and lists only the complete ones. The result is kept in
`/data/fbneo/config/romcheck.txt` and a set is checked again only when one of its archives changes (or after an update
to another FBNeo version), so later starts are quick. Sets on a network share are not checked before the shelf opens:
see [Network shares](#network-shares-smb-and-nfs).
The first start with a large merged collection takes longer: each clone is looked for in its parent's zip once. A set with ROMs missing is hidden unless
Settings, **Show incomplete sets**, is on; starting it then names the missing ROMs on the screen. `boot.log` lists
every set found (`[games] ... -> "<name>"`) and the ROMs a set is missing (`[games] <set>: N ROM(s) missing, first
<rom>`).

| Folder | Contents |
|---|---|
| `/data/fbneo/roms` | your ROM sets and BIOS sets (`.zip` or `.7z`), sub-folders included; on a USB drive, `fbneo/roms` |
| `/data/fbneo/shares.txt` | the network shares (Settings, Network shares; written with examples on the first start) |
| `/data/fbneo/saves` | NVRAM (`<set>.nvram`, written within 5 seconds of a change and when the game closes) and EEPROMs (`<set>.nv`) |
| `/data/fbneo/states` | save states, `<set>.state1` to `.state10` |
| `/data/fbneo/config` | the DIP switches you changed, per game (`<set>.dip`), the button layouts and players set in a game (`<set>.btn`), and `romcheck.txt` (the ROM check, of the console's sets and the shares') |
| `/data/fbneo/samples` | sample sets |
| `/data/fbneo/hiscore` | `hiscore.dat` and the high scores (`<set>.hi`) |
| `/data/fbneo/blend` | FBNeo's blend tables (`<set>.bld`, optional) |
| `/data/fbneo/covers` | covers: downloaded ones in `covers/FBNeo/`, your own as `<set>.png`; `wanted.txt` |
| `/data/fbneo/logs` | `boot.log` (the app), `installer.log` (installer/helper), `helper.log` (the helper the app starts), and the previous session's `.prev.log` files |
| `/data/fbneo/fbneo-ps5.ini` | the menu settings |

### The home-screen app

```
/data/homebrew/PPSA99924/
  eboot.bin              FBNeo (a native app, signed as PS5SX2's is), with the helper inside
  sce_module/libc.prx    the native app's C runtime (the same as PS5SX2's and ps5-native-app-boilerplate's)
  sce_sys/param.json     title "FBNeo PS5", ID PPSA99924
  sce_sys/icon0.png      the icon (512x512; ps5/app/sce_sys/icon0.png in the source)
  sce_sys/pic0.dds       the home-screen background while the icon is selected (3840x2160, BC7)
  sce_sys/pic1.dds       the launch background (the same image)
```

The icon and the background are the project's art. The icon, `ps5/app/sce_sys/icon-source.png` (512x512), is an
FBNeo arcade cabinet in an arcade hall; `icon0.png` is the same image. The background -- the large image behind the
icon when FBNeo PS5 is selected on the home screen, and the launch screen -- is the project's key art,
`ps5/app/sce_sys/background-source.png` (3840x2160), encoded to `pic0.dds`/`pic1.dds` as BC7 by
`ps5/tools/make_art.py` (bc7enc_rdo, as ps5-native-app-boilerplate's `tools/prepare-assets.sh --background` does).
To change them, replace `icon0.png` (512x512 PNG) or `background-source.png` (16:9), run
`python3 tools/make_art.py app/sce_sys frontend/assets/fonts/Roboto-Regular.ttf <bc7enc>` for the backgrounds, and
rebuild. For another title ID: `make ps5 TITLE_ID=XXXX00000`.

**Home-screen art:** ShadowMountPlus copies the art in `sce_sys` to `/user/appmeta/PPSA99924/` only when it first
registers the title. The installer keeps that folder current on every update, but if the title was registered
before the art changed, register it again once: select **FBNeo PS5** on the home screen, press **OPTIONS**, choose
**Delete** (your games, saves and covers in `/data/fbneo/` stay), then send `FBNeoPS5.elf` again.

## The game shelf and covers

![The FBNeo PS5 game shelf: letter tabs, covers and the selected game](ps5/docs/shelf.jpg)

The start screen is a 3D shelf of game covers, like PS5SX2's and Snes9x PS5's, with the author's line under the
wordmark: **github.com/MisterTemaki**.

- **Storage tabs:** **Internal** (the console's drive), **USB** (shown while a USB drive has sets) and **Network**
  (the shares), at the top; **L1 / R1** switch between them, and each keeps its own selection. The shelf opens on
  the tab it was left on (`last_tab` in `fbneo-ps5.ini`). The makers and the letters below work inside the tab.
- **A letter at a time:** with thousands of sets, the shelf shows one letter tab at a time -- **`#`** (titles that
  start with a digit or a sign: *1942*, *'99: The Last War*...) and **A** to **Z** -- sorted by title (a parent
  before its clones). The strip at the top shows every letter: the current one large, the ones with no games
  dimmed. **Up / Down** go to the previous / next letter that has games. Each game's line says its board, maker,
  year, the version (`World 920513`) and the set's name.
- **By maker:** **L3 / R3** (the sticks pressed; L2 / R2 up to 2.0) switch between "All games" and the makers and
  boards that have games: Capcom (CPS-1,
  CPS-2, CPS-3 and the rest), Neo Geo, Sega, Konami, Taito, "Toaplan, Cave, Psikyo", Data East, Irem, Midway, IGS,
  Classics (the 70s and 80s: Pac-Man, Galaxian and their kind) and Other; the letter tabs then show that maker's
  games (the letter is kept when the maker has games under it, else the nearest one). The shelf remembers the
  maker and the letter (and starts on the last game played).
- **Clones:** the other versions of a game (other regions, revisions, bootlegs) are listed after it; Settings,
  **Show clones**, hides them (a clone still shows when its parent isn't listed, so no game disappears).
- **Automatic covers, in the background:** the art comes from libretro-thumbnails' **FBNeo - Arcade Games**
  collection over HTTPS. For each game, in order: its flyer
  (`Named_Boxarts`), its parent's flyer (most clones have none of their own), then a picture of the game
  (`Named_Snaps`), its own or its parent's.
  - The console's own HTTPS (`libSceHttp2`/`libSceSsl`) only works inside the app's sandbox, and the app can't see
    `/data` until it is out of it. So the **helper** downloads the covers, while you use the app, with HTTPS of its
    own (since 1.8): Mbed TLS, the server's certificate checked against Mozilla's list of certificate authorities,
    one connection kept for all the downloads. The app opens at once and lists the missing covers in
    `/data/fbneo/covers/wanted.txt`, and the ones around the selection in `covers/priority.txt` (fetched first);
    the helper downloads them one by one, and each cover replaces its card on the shelf as it lands. The top right
    corner shows "Downloading covers in the background... N left". The helper keeps going while the app is closed.
  - With another jailbreak daemon instead of the FBNeo helper (etaHEN, 9069), 1.0's way still works: a prefetch
    before the app asks for `/data` (30 s), and a restart when new games need covers.
  - Covers are kept in `covers/FBNeo/<the game's full name>.png` and never downloaded twice. A cover the server
    doesn't have is marked (`.missing`) and only looked for again after 30 days; **Square** forces a new try.
  - Without a network nothing is tried and the shelf works the same.
- **Your own covers:** a `.png` or `.jpg` named after the set, in `/data/fbneo/covers/FBNeo/` or `covers/`
  (`covers/sf2ce.png`), or next to the zip (not on a share: the covers of a share's sets are kept on the console),
  takes priority over downloads.
- **No cover:** the game gets a card with its title and board, and an arcade panel (a stick and six buttons) at the
  top right.
- **Turning downloads off:** Settings, "Download covers".

### Downloading all the covers yourself

To fill the shelf without the console downloading anything, download the whole collection on a PC:

| | Link |
|---|---|
| All at once (zip) | [FBNeo_-_Arcade_Games master.zip](https://github.com/libretro-thumbnails/FBNeo_-_Arcade_Games/archive/refs/heads/master.zip) |
| Browse the flyers | [Named_Boxarts](https://github.com/libretro-thumbnails/FBNeo_-_Arcade_Games/tree/master/Named_Boxarts) |
| Browse the screenshots | [Named_Snaps](https://github.com/libretro-thumbnails/FBNeo_-_Arcade_Games/tree/master/Named_Snaps) |

1. Unpack the zip on the PC.
2. Copy the `.png` files of **`Named_Boxarts`** (not the folder itself) to `/data/fbneo/covers/FBNeo/`. For the
   games with no flyer, the `.png` of `Named_Snaps` can go there too (only those: a snap with a flyer's name would
   replace it).
3. Open the app: games pick their cover up at once, and nothing is downloaded for them.

Notes:

- The files are named after the game's full name in FBNeo (`Street Fighter II_ Champion Edition (World
  920513).png`), with the characters `` & * / : ` < > ? \ | " `` replaced by `_` as in the repository. `boot.log`
  lists each game's name (`[games] ... -> "<name>"`).
- A few `.png` files in the repository are git links: a small text file holding the name of another picture.
  The app follows them; in the zip they come out as text, so copy the picture they name under that file's name.
- One cover: `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/libretro-thumbnails/FBNeo_-_Arcade_Games/master/Named_Boxarts/<name>.png`
  (spaces as `%20`).

The shelf is drawn by the CPU in real 3D perspective (each cover a quad turned about the vertical axis, drawn
column by column with bilinear filtering, mipmaps and anti-aliased edges, split across several cores).

## Network shares (SMB and NFS)

ROM sets can be read from a Windows, Samba, NAS or router share instead of a drive: the network shares of NES FCEUmm
PS5 1.1 (and Beetle PCE PS5, Genesis Plus GX PS5), which come from Snes9x PS5, where they are by
[thatboialex](https://github.com/thatboialex) (pull request [#3](https://github.com/MisterTemaki/snes9xPS5/pull/3)).
Add one on the console: **Settings (Triangle on the shelf) > LIBRARY > Network shares > Add a share**. Pick SMB or NFS,
type the server's IP address, the share (or export) and, if it needs them, a user name and password with the
on-screen keyboard (D-pad and Cross; Square deletes, Triangle is a space, L1 / R1 move the cursor, L2 is Shift, R2 the
symbols page, OPTIONS is Done). **Test connection** says what is in the folder, or why it cannot be reached, before
you save. Open a share in the list to change or remove it. (In the settings opened from the pause menu the row can't
be chosen: changing the shares reconnects them.)

The screen keeps its shares in `/data/fbneo/shares.txt` (the first start writes it with examples). You can edit the
file instead, one address per line (up to 8); the screen changes only the line you edit and keeps your comments:

```
smb://192.168.1.50/games/arcade
smb://jason@192.168.1.50/games/arcade?password=secret
nfs://192.168.1.50/export/arcade
```

Use the server's IP address. Inside a user name, password or folder, write `& = % # @ ; / ? ` and spaces as `%XX`
(`p@ss` is `p%40ss`). The password sits in this file in plain text (it is never written to a log or shown).

- The share's sets appear on the **Network** tab as soon as it has connected (sub-folders included, as on a drive);
  the other tabs do not wait for it. While a share is connecting, or cannot be reached, the tab says so (and why, in a
  sentence), and with no share set up it points to Settings > Network shares. **Square** on the tab scans again: it
  forgets the folder listings and connects the shares that were down once more.
- **Parents and BIOS sets:** as on a drive, a set finds its parent and its BIOS set anywhere in the ROM folders: the
  console's first (`/data/fbneo/roms`, then the USB drives), then the shares (the same share or another). So a
  `neogeo.zip` on the console serves the Neo Geo games of every share, and a share that holds a whole romset needs
  nothing on the console. A set that is both on the console and on a share is the console's.
- **The ROM check:** listing a share reads its folders only. A set whose check needs an archive on a share (its own,
  its parent's or its BIOS's) is listed at once as it is ("ROMs not checked yet" on its line), and a background pass
  then reads each archive's directory once -- never a whole archive -- while the shelf is open, and keeps the result in
  `config/romcheck.txt` like the console's sets (by size and date: a set is read again only when it changes). The
  shelf updates when the pass is done (a set found incomplete then leaves it, unless Show incomplete sets is on); the
  BIOS sets screen says "Not checked yet" meanwhile. An archive that could not be read (a link that dropped) is tried
  again at the next visit of the shelf, never remembered as incomplete. The pass stops while a game runs and while
  Settings is open.
- **A set is read as its driver starts** (its ROMs go into the driver's memory, from the share through a block cache
  with read-ahead; "Reading the game from the network share..." meanwhile): a big set (a Neo Geo or CPS-3 one, 30 to
  100+ MiB) takes a few seconds on a home network. Nothing is read from the share while the game runs, except when a
  driver loads a ROM again at a reset (the Neo Geo's BIOS).
- A share is read-only. Saves (NVRAM, EEPROMs), states, high scores, DIP switches, button layouts, samples, covers and
  settings stay on the console.
- If a share cannot be reached, a notification says why (no answer, wrong password, share not found...) and the
  same sentence is in `/data/fbneo/logs/boot.log` (`[net]`); a set on it that won't start says so too. A share lost
  while a game runs is announced once; the game goes on.
- SMB uses libsmb2 and NFS uses libnfs; both are LGPL-2.1-or-later and sit in `ps5/third_party/` with their licence
  notices.

## 7-Zip sets

A set can be a `.7z` instead of a `.zip` (`sf2ce.7z`), as FBNeo's own frontends read them, and the parent or BIOS set
of a `.7z` set can be either. Its ROMs are found by the CRCs and names its directory keeps, as in a zip.

- **In one folder,** when a set is there as both `.zip` and `.7z`, the `.zip` is used.
- **Methods:** LZMA, LZMA2 (7-Zip's default), PPMd, with the BCJ / BCJ2 / ARM / Delta filters, and stored files. Not
  BZip2, Deflate or Zstandard (7-Zip's other choices), and not encrypted archives: such a set says on the screen why
  it can't start (the method, "encrypted", a damaged archive).
- **Solid blocks:** 7-Zip packs a set's files in one "solid" block by default, and the whole block is unpacked to reach
  one file. An archive (the set's, its parent's, its BIOS's) unpacks a block once and copies the driver's ROMs out of
  it; it lets go of the block as soon as the ROMs the driver needs from it have been read, and every block is let go
  once the driver has started (a reset that loads a ROM again, the Neo Geo's BIOS, unpacks it again and keeps it
  until the game closes). A block over
  **512 MiB** is refused before anything is unpacked: that takes every FBNeo arcade set but the biggest PGM2 ones
  (`kof98umh`, `kof98umhd`), which can be packed as a `.zip`, or as a `.7z` with smaller solid blocks (7-Zip's "Solid
  block size"). The blocks a set's archives hold at one time stay within those 512 MiB together (a block that would go
  over makes the others let go of theirs first; they are unpacked again if the driver asks for more of them), and the
  decoder's other needs (an archive's directory, PPMd's model) come out of 72 MiB more per archive: at most about
  600 MiB besides the driver's own copy of the ROMs. An archive listing more than 65,536 files is refused.
- A `.7z` on a network share is read through the share like any file.
- The 7z decoder is FBNeo's own copy of the [LZMA SDK](https://www.7-zip.org/sdk.html) (`src/dep/libs/lib7z`, 25.01,
  public domain, unchanged), with NES FCEUmm PS5's reader (`ps5/frontend/fe_7z.cpp`): FBNeo's `src/burner/un7z.cpp`
  is not used, because it copies the length a driver asks for out of the decoded block without checking it against
  the file's size, has no memory limit, keeps the decoded blocks of the last eight archives, and ignores a read that
  fails. No other LZMA code in the app has the same names (FBNeo's libchdr has its own, `CHDR_`-prefixed); the build
  checks it.

## Controls

**Inside the emulator, to access the main menu press L3 + R3.**

**On the shelf**

| Button | Does |
|---|---|
| Left / Right (D-pad or stick) | change game (hold to speed up) |
| Up / Down | previous / next letter tab (#, A-Z) |
| L1 / R1 | previous / next storage tab (Internal, USB, Network); up to 2.0 they skipped 10 games |
| L2 / R2 | skip 10 games; up to 2.0 they changed the maker |
| L3 / R3 (the sticks pressed) | previous / next maker (All games, Capcom, Neo Geo, ...) |
| Cross | play |
| Triangle | settings |
| Square | download this game's cover again (the cover it has stays until the new one has arrived); on the Network tab: scan the shares again |
| OPTIONS | quit FBNeo PS5 (asks first) |

**In a game:** the joystick is the D-pad or the left stick; **touchpad click = Coin**, **OPTIONS = Start**. The
buttons follow the **button layout** (Settings, CONTROLS):

| PS5 | Classic layout (games with up to 5 buttons) | Fighting (R1 R2) layout (6-button games: Street Fighter...) | Fighting (6 buttons) layout |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cross | Button 1 (Neo Geo A) | Button 4 (light kick) | Button 4 (light kick) |
| Circle | Button 2 (Neo Geo B) | Button 5 (medium kick) | Button 5 (medium kick) |
| Square | Button 3 (Neo Geo C) | Button 1 (light punch) | Button 1 (light punch) |
| Triangle | Button 4 (Neo Geo D) | Button 2 (medium punch) | Button 2 (medium punch) |
| L1 | Button 5 | -- | Button 6 (heavy kick) |
| R1 | Button 6 | Button 3 (heavy punch) | Button 3 (heavy punch) |
| R2 | -- | Button 6 (heavy kick) | -- |
| touchpad click | Coin | Coin | Coin |
| OPTIONS | Start | Start | Start |

The **Auto** layout (the default) uses **Fighting (R1 R2)**, Capcom's own PlayStation layout (punches on Square,
Triangle, R1; kicks on Cross, Circle, R2), for games with six buttons (since 2.0; up to 1.9 it was Fighting (6
buttons), heavy kick on L1) and the classic one for the rest. **Fighting (6 buttons)** is still there to choose. In
**Custom**, any arcade button can go to L2 or R2 too.
L2 and R2 do nothing unless the layout gives them a game button: there are no hot keys on them. Games with analog
controls (wheels, dials, trackballs, guns) read
the left stick (and the right stick for a second axis or pedal).

| Combination | Does |
|---|---|
| L3 + R3 | pause menu: save / load state, slot, **DIP switches**, **Choose players** (2.1), the machine's **service** button and **test** switch (its own setup menu, on the boards that have one), settings, reset, power cycle, back to the list, quit |

That is the only combination: there is no fast forward, and saving or loading a state goes through the pause menu.

**Up to four players, and which one each controller plays (2.1, thanks to gitloth, fbneo-ps5#3).** The
controllers are the signed-in users' pads: **controller 1** is the user in front (the one who opened FBNeo PS5),
controllers 2 to 4 are the other signed-in users, in the order the console lists them. Their **light bars** say
which is which: controller 1 **blue**, 2 **red**, 3 **green**, 4 **pink**. Every controller uses the same button
layout. By default controller N plays player N.

**Choose players (the simple way):** in the pause menu (L3 + R3, under DIP switches), or from the shelf at the top of
Settings, CONTROLS, CONTROLLERS (`Choose players (press X on each controller)...`). The screen asks **"Player 1: press
X on your controller"**, then Player 2, and so on up to the game's number of players (four from the shelf): whichever
connected controller presses **X** gets that player; a controller that has joined already is passed over (who
joined is kept by user, so someone signing out while the screen is open doesn't move the others' players). The screen
lists the players as they fill (`Player 1  Controller 3 (green light)`) and the controllers, connected and free or not.
It ends by itself once every player of the game has a controller or every connected controller has joined. On
**controller 1**: **OPTIONS** ends it now (the players left get no controller; with nobody in yet it changes nothing),
**Square** starts again, **Circle** cancels (nothing changes). When it ends, the connected controllers that didn't press
X get no player, and the controllers not connected get the players left over, in order (so someone who signs in later
still plays). The
other controllers can only join. From a game's pause menu the result is kept for that game (only its players: its
buttons stay as they are) and the game resumes with the message saying who plays whom; from the shelf it is the
general setting. The X that joined doesn't reach the game.

**The list (the advanced way):** Settings, CONTROLS, **CONTROLLERS**: each controller's row
(`Controller 2 (red light), connected`) takes **Player 1** to **Player 4** or **No player** (Left / Right).
Choosing a player another controller already has **swaps** them: that controller gets this one's old player (or, when
this one had none, the lowest player left free), so each player has one controller at most and nobody silently loses
control. Each Left / Right on a row is one swap from the players as they were when the cursor came onto that row, so
stepping through the players moves one other controller at most, and stepping back to where you started puts every
controller back. In a game with fewer players, a player it doesn't have is shown dimmed. Examples:

- three people on a 4-player Sunset Riders who want the slots 1, 3 and 4: controller 3 on Player 4 (one step right;
  controller 4 gets Player 3), then controller 2 on Player 3 (one step right; controller 4 gets Player 2);
- one person on a 2-player edition who wants player 2's character: controller 1 on Player 2 (controller 2 gets
  Player 1). Controller 1's stick, buttons, coin (touchpad) and start (OPTIONS) are then player 2's.

The players are kept with the button layout: changed from the shelf's Settings, for every game (`fbneo-ps5.ini`,
`controller_1`...`controller_4` = the player's number, 0 for none); changed from a game's pause menu, for that game
only (its `.btn`, the same keys), and a clone without its own file uses its parent's (see below). A game keeps players
of its own only when you change them there (to something other than the general setting): changing a button in a
game keeps it on the general players. A `.btn` without these keys (2.0's, or a game whose players you never changed)
uses the general setting's players. Editing the files by hand: `0` is no player; a value that isn't a number is
ignored (in `fbneo-ps5.ini` that controller plays its own number, in a `.btn` it keeps the general setting's player).
A player named twice goes to the controller whose line you changed (the one that differs from controller N = player N
in `fbneo-ps5.ini`, from the general setting in a `.btn`), and the other controller gets the player left free: setting
`controller_4=1` swaps controllers 1 and 4. The log says so. When a game starts with a controller on another player,
or with controller 1 on no player of that game, a message says so for a few seconds (`Controller 1: Player 3`;
`Controller 1: Player 4 (not in this game). This game has 2 players.`).

**When someone signs in or out during a game,** the controllers after them move up or down a slot (the slots follow
the console's list of signed-in users) and so play that slot's player; the light bars change colour with them. A
message then says again who plays whom (`Controller 1: Player 1, Controller 2: Player 2`). Before 2.1 a pad that moved
up a slot could also stop answering for a few seconds; its handle now moves with it.
**The pause menu stays on controller 1** (L3 + R3 on controller 1, whatever player it plays; the other controllers'
L3 + R3 do nothing), and the menus are driven by controller 1.

**A layout per game (2.0):** Settings, CONTROLS from the shelf sets the **general layout**, the one every game uses
unless it has its own. Opened from a game's pause menu, it says whose layout it shows ("For this game: ..." or "This
game uses the general layout"), and a change there is kept for **that game only**, in
`/data/fbneo/config/<set>.btn` (next to its `.dip`): set King of Fighters' buttons without touching Street
Fighter's. A clone without its own file uses its parent set's. Since 2.1 the file also keeps which player each
controller plays (see above). **Default controls** (Default button layout up to 2.0) in a game puts it back on the
general layout and players (its file is removed; a clone whose parent has a layout gets a file saying
`layout=general`).

**DIP switches:** the pause menu's **DIP switches** shows the game's switches (difficulty, lives, coinage, cabinet,
the Neo Geo's BIOS and region...) with their current setting; **Left / Right** change one (`*` marks a setting
that isn't the game's default), **Default DIP switches** puts them all back. Changes are kept per game in
`/data/fbneo/config/<set>.dip` and set before the game starts, every time. Most games read their switches when
they start: after changing them in the pause menu, choose **Reset** (or start the game again).

## Settings

Triangle on the shelf, or "Settings" in the pause menu:

- **Video:** **shader** (see [CRT shaders](#crt-shaders); CRT Easymode style by default), screen size (fit to
  screen, integer scale, stretch), aspect ratio (the game's monitor -- 4:3, or 3:4 for vertical games --, square
  pixels, 16:9 stretched), smooth picture and scanlines (for the plain picture, with the shader Off), FPS counter.
- **Audio:** sound on/off, volume.
- **Emulation:** save high scores.
- **Controls:** **button layout** (Auto, Classic, Fighting, Fighting (R1 R2), Custom), then the PS5 button of
  each arcade button (Button 1 to 6, Coin, Start: Cross, Circle, Square, Triangle, L1, R1, L2, R2, OPTIONS, the
  touchpad, or none). In a game the rows show the game's own names for its buttons (`Button 1 (Weak Punch)`).
  Changing a button makes the layout Custom, starting from the one shown. Then **CONTROLLERS** (2.1): **Choose
  players** (each controller presses X in turn), then the player each controller plays (Player 1 to 4, or none;
  choosing a taken player swaps the two controllers; see [Controls](#controls)). **Default controls** goes back to Auto and controller N = player N. L3 and R3 stay for the
  pause menu.
  Saved in `fbneo-ps5.ini` (`layout`, `btn_1`...`btn_start`, `controller_1`...`controller_4`; L2 is 9 and R2 is 10
  there). From a game's pause menu, the change is for that game only (`config/<set>.btn`, the same keys; see
  [Controls](#controls)), and Default controls puts the game back on the general layout and players.
- **Library:** download covers, show clones, show incomplete sets, **BIOS sets** (Cross: which BIOS sets your
  games need and whether each is there; see [ROM sets](#rom-sets)), **Network shares** (see
  [Network shares](#network-shares-smb-and-nfs); not from a game's pause menu).
- **System:** **Language** (see [Language](#language)); **Debug logs** (Off by default) -- see [Debugging](#debugging-logs-and-crashes); **Updates** -- see
  [Updates](#updates).

## CRT shaders

Every game starts through a CRT shader -- **CRT Easymode style** unless you pick another one. Twelve shaders are
built in, the same as Snes9x PS5's: the eleven CRT ones of Genesis Plus GX PS5 and ScaleFX + rAA + AA style. They
work only while a game is running (the shelf is drawn without them). Vertical games get them on their upright
picture.

**How to use them**

1. **In a game:** press **L3 + R3** to open the pause menu and choose **Settings** (on the shelf: **Triangle**).
2. **Shader** is the first row: **Left / Right** (or **Cross**) go through the list. The picture behind the menu
   changes at once, so you can compare them on the game you are playing.
3. **Circle** closes the settings; the choice is saved and used for every game from then on.
4. **Off** gives the plain picture; with it, the "Smooth picture" and "Scanlines" options apply.
5. The choice is kept in `/data/fbneo/fbneo-ps5.ini` as `shader=<number>` (the numbers below).

| `shader=` | Shader | Look | Weight | From |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Off | the plain picture | -- | -- |
| 1 | **CRT Easymode style** (default) | flat screen, sharp, scanlines that widen on bright colours, aperture grille | medium | written for this port, after the look of EasyMode's crt-easymode |
| 2 | crt-lottes | curved screen, Gaussian beam, shadow mask, a little bloom | heavy | Timothy Lottes (public domain) |
| 3 | crt-lottes-fast | lighter Lottes: curved, 4-tap beam, aperture mask, tone mapping | medium | Timothy Lottes (public domain) |
| 4 | crt-1tap | very light, contrasty dynamic scanlines | light | fishku (CC0) |
| 5 | crt-2tap | crt-1tap with exact blending between two lines | light | fishku (CC0) |
| 6 | crt-hyllian-fast | sharp Catmull-Rom picture, strong scanlines, magenta/green dot mask | medium | Hyllian (MIT) |
| 7 | crt-nobody | curved screen with rounded corners, beam scanlines, magenta/green mask | heavy | Hyllian (MIT) |
| 8 | newpixie-mini | strongly curved TV, colour bleed, vignette, film tone | heavy | Mattias Gustavsson (Unlicense) |
| 9 / 10 | crt-blurPi-sharp / crt-blurPi-soft | light blur and screen-space scanlines (sharp or bilinear) | light | Oriol Ferrer Mesià (MIT) |
| 11 | monoCRT | a monochrome monitor (made for black-and-white pictures) | light | hunterk (public domain) |
| 12 | ScaleFX + rAA + AA style | not a CRT: pixel art redrawn smooth -- staircase edges become clean lines and curves, flat colours stay exact, then a light edge smoothing and deblur | **very heavy** | ScaleFX + rAA post-3x (Sp00kyFox, MIT) from the scalefx+rAA+aa-fast preset; its final steps rewritten for these ports |

**ScaleFX + rAA + AA style** is libretro's `scalefx+rAA+aa-fast` preset: ScaleFX redraws the picture at 3x (edges
interpolated up to six pixels long, only colours of the original), rAA removes the remaining stair-steps, then a
smoothing along the edges, the scale to the screen and a deblur. The preset's last three passes (FXAA, guest(r)'s
AA shader 4.0 and deblur) can't be built in (GPL, or no permission to copy), so original code with the same
purpose replaces them: the result is close, not identical. It is the heaviest of all: the boards with large
screens (CPS-3, Midway's 400x256) may not keep full speed with it.

They come from libretro's [slang-shaders](https://github.com/libretro/slang-shaders) (`crt/`), with their default
parameters, rewritten in C++ for the CPU (`ps5/coreorbis/orbis-shims/ProsperoCrt.cpp`): the PS5 build draws the
picture with the CPU, so only single-pass shaders are fast enough, and only shaders whose licence can sit with
FBNeo's (public domain, CC0, Unlicense, MIT) are built in. crt-easymode itself is GPL, so "CRT Easymode style" is
original code aiming at the same look. Every minute in a game, `boot.log` says how long the shader took per frame
(`shader N ms`); if a heavy one slows a demanding board down, pick a lighter one.

## Picture and sound

- 1920x1080 output through `libSceVideoOut`, flipping on vsync. With little video memory it falls back to
  1280x720.
- The core draws in 32-bit colour (16-bit for the few drivers that need it); **vertical games are turned upright**
  (as FBNeo's own frontends turn them) and shown at their monitor's 3:4 shape in the middle of the screen.
- Sound through `libSceAudioOut` at 48 kHz, on its own thread; the core makes its sound at 48 kHz.
- **Speed:** boards between 58.5 and 61.5 Hz (CPS-1/2 at 59.6, the Neo Geo at 59.2, the many 60 Hz ones) run at
  the display's 60 Hz, paced by vsync -- smooth scrolling, the game up to 2.5% faster than the real board, its
  sound resampled to match (a small rate control, within 0.5%, keeps about 60 ms queued). The others (Mortal
  Kombat's 54.7 Hz, R-Type's 55 Hz, DoDonPachi's 57.55 Hz...) run at their own speed, paced by the sound.
- There is no fast forward and no rewind: one emulated frame per display frame.

## Debugging (logs and crashes)

**Turning the logs on or off:** Settings -> **SYSTEM** -> **Debug logs**. Off stops every log at once: the app
writes nothing more to `boot.log` (its last line says the logs were turned off), and the next starts -- the app,
the installer and the helper -- write no log files at all; the files of earlier runs are left as they are. The
setting is `debug_logs=0` / `debug_logs=1` in `fbneo-ps5.ini`; it is off by default (since 1.9.1), so turn it on
if you want to report a problem.

If something fails, send the files in `/data/fbneo/logs/`: `boot.log` (the app), `installer.log` and `helper.log`,
plus the previous session's `.prev.log` files. They record every step:

- the sandbox request and who answered;
- the covers, one by one (`helper.log`: the background downloads; `boot.log`: the prefetch, when there is one);
- every `sceVideoOut*` call, and the picture's size and place on the screen;
- the controller handle and its first read;
- the sets found, their names and boards, and the ROMs a set is missing;
- the core's own messages (`[burn] ...`, `[core] ...`): the driver started, its screen, frame rate and buttons,
  ROMs found with another CRC, NVRAM and DIP switches;
- frames per second, queued audio and underruns, and the shader's time per frame, every minute in a game.

If the app dies on a signal (the PS5's "Game or App Error" screen), a `== CRASH ==` block is written at the end of
`boot.log`: the signal, the address, the **stage** each part of the program was in (`stage[...]`: boot, shelf,
covers, emu, menu), and the return addresses, which map into `ps5/build/app/fbneo-pie.elf`.

## Known limitations

- Arcade games only: no console drivers, no Neo Geo CD.
- The PS and Create buttons are not reported by `scePadReadState`, so Coin is on the touchpad.
- No light-gun aiming beyond the left stick, no mouse, no keyboard games (mahjong panels, typing games).
- No cheats, no IPS patches, no FBNeo "romdata" files, no netplay, no input recording.
- `.7z` sets packed with BZip2, Deflate or Zstandard, encrypted, or in a solid block over 512 MiB are refused; sample
  sets (`samples/`) must be zips.
- Network shares: SMB 2/3 and NFS 3/4, read only, up to 8; names of servers often don't resolve on the console (use
  the IP address). Tested here with a folder of the test machine standing in for the share, and the NFS backend
  against a mock and loopback sockets; **not yet on a PS5**, nor against a real NAS in this port (Beetle PCE PS5,
  NES FCEUmm PS5, Genesis Plus GX PS5 and Snes9x PS5 run the same network code).
- The heaviest boards (CPS-3, PGM2, Konami GX, Midway's 3D ones) depend on the PS5's CPU running FBNeo's
  interpreters; not measured on a console yet.

## Building

Requirements: the [ps5-payload-dev SDK](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk) v0.42 or newer, clang/lld 18,
perl and python3 (FBNeo's generated sources), and g++ with ASan for the tests.

```sh
export PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK=/opt/ps5-payload-sdk
cd ps5
make ps5 -j$(nproc)              # build/ps5/FBNeoPS5.elf (installer + helper, with the app inside)
make send PS5_HOST=192.168.0.10  # sends it to elfldr (port 9021)
make dist                        # build/dist/FBNeoPS5-v<version>.elf + the release zip + the ROM DAT
make dat                         # ps5/dat/fbneo-ps5-arcade.dat, again (after a core update or a version change)
make app                         # only build/app/PPSA99924/, to copy by hand
make test                        # Linux builds (app, installer, helper, headless core) + 532 host tests (ASan/UBSan)
```

The first build compiles FBNeo's 1,039 core files (about 15 minutes on 2 cores; `make core-ps5` builds just those).
The build has three stages:

1. `FBNeoPS5-helper.elf`, the helper alone.
2. `eboot.bin`: a PIE with the boilerplate's `app_crt.cpp`, FBNeo's core and the frontend.
   - The core (`ps5/core.mk`) is compiled from FBNeo's own object lists (`makefile.burn_rules`), less the
     console drivers (`ps5/tools/fbneo_sources.py`), with `makefile.sdl2`'s defines for a little-endian 64-bit
     build; the generated sources come from FBNeo's own scripts and tools (`ps5/tools/gen_headers.sh`:
     `gamelist.pl`, `m68kmake`, `ctv_make`, `pgm_sprite_create` and the `*_func.pl` scripts).
   - It is linked against the SDK's stubs and static libc++, with `ps5-pie.ld` + `ehframe.ld` and every symbol
     local.
   - Then it goes through `ps5-native-tool link` and `self --sign`, exactly like PS5SX2's `link-vk.sh`.
   - `libc.prx` goes with it, generated by `libc_builder` and checked against the published SHA-256
     (`ps5/proto/native/libc.prx.sha256`).
3. `FBNeoPS5.elf`, with the app folder built in (`eboot.bin` and the backgrounds zlib-compressed,
   `ps5/tools/pack_file.py`).

## Source layout

- **`ps5/coreorbis/main-boot.cpp`**: the app's entry point (`eboot.bin`). Asks the helper for the covers (or prefetches them), asks to leave the
  sandbox, brings up log, folders, video, sound and pads, starts the core, and hands over to the frontend on a
  thread with a 16 MiB stack. Exits through the system (`sceSystemServiceLoadExec("exit")`), as PS5SX2 does.
- **`ps5/installer/installer_main.cpp`**: `FBNeoPS5.elf` (installs the app and stays as the helper, which also downloads the covers) and, built with
  `FBNEO_HELPER_ONLY`, `FBNeoPS5-helper.elf`.
- **`ps5/coreorbis/orbis-shims/`**: the PS5 layer (video, CRT shaders, audio, pads, the sandbox request and the
  helper, the install, crash reports, notifications, `/data/fbneo` and the logs), shared with Genesis Plus GX PS5.
- **`ps5/core.mk`**, **`ps5/core/`**: the core's build; `burn_frontend.cpp` holds what FBNeo's core takes from
  its frontend (its folders, and neutral stand-ins for IPS patches, the Neo Geo CD and recordings).
- **`ps5/frontend/`**:
  - `fe_burn.cpp`: the core behind a small API -- the drivers, the ROMs from the sets' zips (by CRC, then by name;
    the set, its BIOS set and its parents), inputs, DIP switches, the picture turned upright, the sound, save
    states and NVRAM (with their layout checked on load), hiscores;
  - `fe_emu.cpp`: the running game on the PS5 -- pads and button layouts, pacing, the resampler,
    the picture and its overlays;
  - `fe_games.cpp`: the library (sets, parents, BIOS sets, the ROM check and its cache, the tabs);
  - `fe_shelf.cpp`, `fe_covers.cpp`, `fe_prefetch.cpp`, `fe_http.cpp`: the 3D shelf and covers;
  - `fe_coverworker.cpp`, `fe_coverfetch.cpp`: the helper's background downloads, and the fetch code the app and
    the helper share;
  - `fe_tlshttp.cpp`, `fe_mbedtls_config.h`, `data/cacert.pem`: the helper's own HTTPS client (sockets, Mbed TLS,
    Mozilla's CA list);
  - `fe_menu.cpp`, `fe_settings.cpp`, `fe_text.cpp`: menus (the pause menu's DIP switches included), settings, text

  - `fe_netscreen.cpp`, `fe_osk.cpp`, `fe_ui.cpp`: Settings > Network shares, its on-screen keyboard and the screens'

  - `fe_7z.cpp`: sets inside a `.7z`, read through the app's stdio calls with FBNeo's LZMA SDK;

latestRelease.name: FBNeo PS5 2.1
latestRelease.body:
## FBNeo PS5 2.1

### New

**Choose which arcade player each controller plays** ([#3](https://github.com/MisterTemaki/fbneo-ps5/issues/3)). Thanks to [gitloth](https://github.com/gitloth) for the request.

- **The simple way: Choose players.** It's in the pause menu, or at the top of Settings > CONTROLS > CONTROLLERS on the shelf. The screen asks "Player 1: press ✕ on your controller", then Player 2, and so on. Whoever presses ✕ gets that player, as in many PS5 games.
  - Controller 1 can finish early (OPTIONS), start again (Square) or cancel (Circle).
  - A 4-player game that ties each character to its cabinet's slot (The Simpsons, Sunset Riders...) can be played by three people on the slots they want.
- **The advanced way: the CONTROLLERS rows.** Each controller has its own row, showing its light bar's colour, whether it is connected, and the player it plays (Player 1 to 4, or none).
  - Choosing a player another controller already has swaps them, so nobody is left without one.
  - A single controller can play player 2 (the 2-player editions).
- **Per game or for every game:** as with the button layout, a change made from a game's pause menu is kept for that game and its clones. A change made from the shelf's Settings applies to every game.
- **Default controls** (formerly Default button layout) puts both the buttons and the players back.
- **A message at game start** says so for a few seconds when a controller plays another player, including when the game doesn't have that player.
- **The pause menu** (L3 + R3) stays on controller 1, whatever player it plays.
- **Signing in or out during a game:** the message appears again, and a controller that moves up a slot keeps working. Before, it could stop responding for a few seconds.

To play with 3 or 4 people, start the game's 4-player version (e.g. `simpsons`, not `simpsons2p`). On some boards you also need to set the cabinet type in Pause menu > DIP switches.

### Files

- `FBNeoPS5-v2.1.elf`: send it to your payload loader (port 9021).
- `FBNeoPS5-v2.1-PPSA99924.zip`: the app folder, used by Settings > Updates. You don't need to download it yourself.

### Status

It passes 530 host tests (the same code on Linux, the PS5 calls simulated, with up to four simulated controllers). **It has not been run on a PS5 yet**, in particular with several signed-in users. Please report what works and what doesn't, with Settings > Debug logs on (the logs are in `/data/fbneo/logs/`).

Licences: FBNeo's licence (non-commercial); libsmb2 and libnfs LGPL-2.1-or-later; the LZMA SDK public domain. Port by [MisterTemaki](https://github.com/MisterTemaki).

repos.description: Port of FCEUmm for PS5
repos.readme:
# NES FCEUmm PS5

[FCEUmm](https://github.com/libretro/libretro-fceumm) -- the libretro NES / Famicom emulator with the widest
board support (FCE Ultra "mappers modified") -- running on a jailbroken PS5 as a **native home-screen app** with its
own icon and background, with the best of **Mesen** and **Nestopia** added for accuracy: Mesen's game database to
correct bad ROM headers, Mesen's and Nestopia's palettes, and Mesen's HD packs. One app plays:

| System | Files | BIOS needed (in `/data/fceumm/bios/`) |
|---|---|---|
| NES / Famicom (cartridges, VS. System games included) | `.nes` `.unf` `.unif` | none |
| Famicom Disk System | `.fds` | `disksys.rom` |

Games can also be inside a `.zip` or a `.7z` (see [Zip and 7-Zip archives](#zip-and-7-zip-archives)), and can be
played from a NAS or PC on your network (SMB or NFS shares: see [Network shares](#network-shares-smb-and-nfs)). A disk
started without the BIOS says which file is needed, and where it goes, on the screen.

**Inside the emulator, to access the main menu press L3 + R3.**

The PS5 layer follows the layout of PS5SX2 (the PCSX2 port) and of Genesis Plus GX PS5, Snes9x PS5 and FBNeo PS5,
the ports it comes from:

- `ps5/coreorbis` holds `main-boot.cpp`, the `orbis-shims/` and `include-orbis/`;
- `ps5/frontend` holds the user interface, the 3D game shelf and the glue to the FCEUmm core;
- `ps5/proto/native` builds and signs `eboot.bin`;
- `ps5/installer` is the installer and helper payload.

Everything outside `ps5/` is the original libretro-fceumm source, unchanged, apart from this README (the original
one is [README-FCEUmm.md](README-FCEUmm.md)). The core (`src/`: the CPU, PPU, APU, the 432 board files of
`src/boards/`, the Disk System, VS. System, Blargg's NTSC filter, the Mesen-format HD pack renderer) and its
libretro port (`src/drivers/libretro/libretro.c`) are compiled as they are. The frontend drives the core through its
libretro interface and plays the part RetroArch plays on a PC.

> **Status (1.1):** builds with the ps5-payload-dev SDK into a signed native app, and passes 394 host tests,
> which run the same code (the FCEUmm core included) on Linux with the PS5 calls simulated: a hand-assembled NES test
> program is played through the whole chain -- the shelf, the pad, the core, the video and sound output -- as an
> NES 2.0, iNES 1.0 and UNIF file, in NTSC and PAL, from a zip and a `.7z` and as a Disk System image; games are
> played from a network share standing in for a NAS. netfs's own 235 checks, the NFS backend's 36 tests and the 7z
> reader's 43 checks pass too. It has not yet been run on a console (nor have network shares or `.7z` archives). If something
> fails, the logs in `/data/fceumm/logs/` say where.

## What it takes from Mesen and Nestopia

FCEUmm is the core: it knows the most boards (including many unlicensed and pirate ones), runs on the PS5's CPU
with a lot of headroom, and its libretro port is complete. The other two emulators are more accurate in places;
what of them could be added without replacing the core, is:

- **Header corrections from Mesen's game database.** Many NES dumps carry an old iNES header that gives the wrong
  mapper, mirroring, battery or region, or can't describe the board at all (submapper, PRG-RAM, CHR-RAM). FCEUmm
  corrects the games it knows (`src/ines-correct.h`). Mesen's database -- NewRisingSun's NES 2.0 header database,
  NesCartDB and Nestopia's database, merged -- knows 9,361 more (its validated entries, for boards FCEUmm has).
  Before a game starts, a ROM with an iNES 1.0 (or older) header whose PRG + CHR CRC32 is in that table gets an
  NES 2.0 header made from it, in memory (the file is not changed), as Mesen does; FCEUmm then sets the board up as
  described. NES 2.0 headers are trusted as they are. `boot.log` says what changed (`header corrected from Mesen's
  database: mapper 4 -> 118.0, ...`). Settings, **Fix headers**, turns it off.
- **Palettes.** The default is **Mesen's palette**. Also built in: Mesen's Nestopia RGB and FirebrandX presets
  (Original Hardware, PVM Style, Unsaturated v6), Nestopia's palette files (Nostalgia, Hybrid, NTSC), and FCEUmm's
  own twenty (FCEUX, Nintendo RGB PPU, Sony CXA2025AS, NESCAP, Wavebeam, the other FirebrandX palettes, Wii VC...).
- **HD packs** in Mesen's format (`hires.txt`), drawn by the core: see [HD packs](#hd-packs).

## How it works

The PS5 gives the controller only to the app in front, so NES FCEUmm PS5 runs as a native app opened from its icon,
and the payload you send is its installer:

| Piece | What it is | In PS5SX2 |
|---|---|---|
| `eboot.bin` in `/data/homebrew/PPSA99013/` | **FCEUmm itself**, a native app opened from its icon | PCSX2 (PPSA99203) |
| `sce_module/libc.prx` | the C runtime module every native app carries | the same file, byte for byte |
| `NESFCEUmmPS5.elf` (payload) | the **installer**: installs or updates the app, then stays running as the **helper** | PS5SX2Installer.elf + PS5SX2Helper.elf |

When it opens, the app asks the helper to let it out of its sandbox; without that an app sees neither `/data`
nor USB drives. The request is the one PS5SX2 makes:

- **Who is asked, in order:** the NES FCEUmm helper (127.0.0.1:9085), then etaHEN (9028) and the daemon on port
  9069.
- **If nobody answers:** the app carries a copy of the helper (`NESFCEUmmPS5-helper.elf`), sends it to the ELF
  loader (127.0.0.1:9021) and asks again. So the icon keeps working after a reboot, as long as the ELF loader
  runs.
- **What the helper allows:** only title PPSA99013. It gives the process the system's root folder and uid 0, as
  elfldr does for payloads. No other app is touched.

NES FCEUmm PS5 only uses `/data/fceumm/`, `/data/homebrew/PPSA99013/` and its own `/user/appmeta/PPSA99013/`. It
sits next to Snes9x PS5 (PPSA99009, helper port 9083), Mesen2 PS5 (PPSA99010, port 9076), Genesis Plus GX PS5
(PPSA99011, port 9084), FBNeo PS5 (PPSA99012, port 9082) and PS5SX2 (PPSA99203) without touching them.

## Versions

Every release carries its version in the file name: `NESFCEUmmPS5-v1.1.elf` and `fceumm-ps5-v1.1-src.zip`
(`make dist`). When updating, replace the old ELF with the new one in your autoload or Payload Manager. In this
README, "`NESFCEUmmPS5.elf`" always means the current release's ELF.

**1.0:** the first release, with what the other ports learned built in: covers downloaded in the background by the
helper with its own HTTPS (Mbed TLS), CRT shaders, saves per system, the debug logs setting.

**1.0.1:** interface languages (English, Spanish, Portuguese (Brazil), French, German); the debug logs are off by
default.

**1.1:** network shares, shelf tabs and 7-Zip archives, as Beetle PCE PS5 1.1.1 has them (thanks to CroCop86 for
asking, [issue #1](https://github.com/MisterTemaki/fceummPS5/issues/1)); it also brings 1.0.1's languages, which were
not released on their own.
- **Games on network shares (SMB and NFS):** keep your NES games and disks on a NAS or PC and play them from the shelf
  (Settings, LIBRARY, Network shares, with an on-screen keyboard and Test connection). A game is read whole when it
  starts; nothing streams while it runs. Saves, states, `disksys.rom` and covers stay on the console. After the design
  of [thatboialex](https://github.com/thatboialex)'s pull request to Snes9x PS5
  ([#3](https://github.com/MisterTemaki/snes9xPS5/pull/3)). See [Network shares](#network-shares-smb-and-nfs).
- **Shelf tabs:** Internal, USB and Network; L1 / R1 switch tabs, Up / Down the letter, **L2 / R2 skip 10 games**
  (L1 / R1 did before), Square on the Network tab scans the shares again.
- **7-Zip:** games and Famicom Disk System disks inside `.7z` archives (LZMA, LZMA2, PPMd...), named and covered from
  the CRC the archive keeps, as zipped ones are. See [Zip and 7-Zip archives](#zip-and-7-zip-archives).
- A game with no cover gets a card with an NES pad on it (a grey plate, Select and Start, the red B and A buttons),
  no longer the SNES pad's four coloured buttons (thanks to CroCop86,
  [issue #4](https://github.com/MisterTemaki/genplusgxPS5/issues/4)).
- The new screens in the five languages. libsmb2 and libnfs (LGPL-2.1-or-later) are built in, as Beetle PCE PS5,
  Genesis Plus GX PS5 and Snes9x PS5 carry them; the 7z decoder is the LZMA SDK's (public domain).

## Language

English (the default), Spanish, Portuguese (Brazil), French or German: Settings -> **SYSTEM** -> **Language**
(Left / Right), saved as `language=0`...`4` in `fceumm-ps5.ini`. Menus, settings, messages and notifications follow
it at once; the logs stay in English.

## Requirements

- A jailbroken PS5 with **kstuff** (or kstuff-lite) and an **ELF loader** on port 9021: elfldr, etaHEN, or the
  one PS5 Payload Manager uses.
- **ShadowMountPlus**, so the icon appears on the home screen (the same one PS5SX2 uses).
- Your own games, and the Famicom Disk System BIOS (`disksys.rom`, 8 KiB) for disk games. None are included.

## Install and play

1. **Send `NESFCEUmmPS5.elf`** with PS5 Payload Manager, or from a PC on the same network:
   ```sh
   nc -q0 PS5_IP 9021 < NESFCEUmmPS5-v1.1.elf
   ```
   It installs the app in `/data/homebrew/PPSA99013/` (`eboot.bin`, `sce_module/libc.prx`, `param.json`, the
   icon and the backgrounds), shows **"NES FCEUmm PS5 1.1 installed. Open it from the NES FCEUmm PS5 icon on the
   home screen."** and stays running as the helper.
2. **Open the NES FCEUmm PS5 icon.** The game shelf appears and the controller works.
3. **Copy your games** to their system's folder, over FTP for example. The app makes the folders on its first
   start:

   | System | Games in | Your covers in |
   |---|---|---|
   | NES / Famicom | `/data/fceumm/roms/NES` | `/data/fceumm/covers/NES` |
   | Famicom Disk System | `/data/fceumm/roms/FDS` | `/data/fceumm/covers/FDS` |

   On a USB drive the same layout goes under `fceumm/roms` (`fceumm/roms/NES`...). Subfolders inside them are fine
   (`roms/NES/RPG/`). The game's system comes from its extension, so a game left directly in `roms/` or in another
   folder is still found. The Disk System BIOS goes to `/data/fceumm/bios/disksys.rom`.

Tip: put `NESFCEUmmPS5.elf` in your autoload, as PS5SX2 recommends for its payloads.

**Updating:** send the new `NESFCEUmmPS5.elf` once. It compares every app file with the copy it carries and
rewrites only what changed; each file is written to a temporary file and then renamed, `eboot.bin` last. A deleted
or damaged icon is put back the same way. A second copy sent while the helper is already running only installs and
exits.

**If "NES FCEUmm PS5 has no access to /data" appears:** no helper answered and the ELF loader wasn't running.
Send `NESFCEUmmPS5.elf` and open the icon again.

| Folder | Contents |
|---|---|
| `/data/fceumm/roms/<system>` | your games: `NES`, `FDS` |
| `/data/fceumm/bios` | `disksys.rom` for the Disk System; `HdPacks/` (see [HD packs](#hd-packs)) |
| `/data/fceumm/saves` | battery saves, one folder per system: `saves/NES/<game>.srm`; for a disk, `saves/FDS/<game>.srm` is the disk with what the game wrote to it (the `.fds` file itself is never changed). Written within 3 seconds of a change and when the game closes, an erase included |
| `/data/fceumm/states` | save states, one folder per system: `states/NES/<game>.state1` to `.state10` (a cartridge and a disk of the same name never share one) |
| `/data/fceumm/covers/<system>` | downloaded covers and your own, one folder per system (the same names as in `roms/`); `covers/` itself keeps `wanted.txt` and `crc-cache.txt` |
| `/data/fceumm/logs` | `boot.log` (the app), `installer.log` (installer/helper), `helper.log` (the helper the app starts), and the previous session's `.prev.log` files |
| `/data/fceumm/fceumm-ps5.ini` | the menu settings |
| `/data/fceumm/shares.txt` | the network shares (Settings, Network shares; see [Network shares](#network-shares-smb-and-nfs)) |
