latestRelease.body:
## Seedee5 1.23

### Fixed: connecting to a NAS

- **Entering a NAS address while "Find NAS" was still searching did nothing.** The request was refused, no shares appeared, and the old search's progress stayed on screen. A new request now stops the search and asks the NAS straight away.
- **Type the share path:** a NAS that doesn't list its shares (NFS 4 only, or listing turned off) can now be opened by typing the share's path on the Shares page, such as `/volume1/games`, with the on-screen keyboard. Then pick the folder with your games as usual.

Seedee5 speaks NFS 3 and NFS 4 (4.0). A NAS set to NFS 4.1 normally accepts 4.0 too: choose NFS 4 in Settings › NAS › NFS version.

### Updating

- **With ProsperoStore from 1.22:** your settings, NAS settings, saved games and BIOS come back by themselves. Copy games you keep on the console (`data/roms`) back from `/data/prosperostore/previous/PPSA99142/data/` over FTP.
- **From 1.21 or older:** copy everything in `/data/prosperostore/previous/PPSA99142/data/` back to `/data/homebrew/PPSA99142/data/` over FTP. The wheel reminds you.
- **By hand:** copy the `PPSA99142` folder from `Seedee5-1.23.zip` over the old one on your PS5 (`/data/homebrew/`).

No BIOS, games or keys are included. Check the downloads against `SHA256SUMS`.

repos.name: PS-Play
repos.readme:
# PS Play 2.1

**All-in-one media hub for jailbroken PlayStation 5** — DLNA receiver, DLNA/UPnP browser, native Stremio client, IPTV/Live TV and USB playback in a single native app with a minimal AMOLED-black UI.

> **Credits:** InsideMatrixDev / MounirHero  
> Based on [Prospero Player 1.0](https://github.com/KINGDKAK/ProsperoPlayer) by KINGDKAK (GPL-3.0)  
> Stremio integration ported from **Nuvio Portable** by **stuey-81**

---

## Features

### Four ways to watch
- **DLNA Hub** — UPnP MediaRenderer:1 cast target (find "PS Play" in BubbleUPnP or any DLNA controller) plus automatic discovery and browsing of LAN media servers, all in one menu.
- **IPTV / Live TV** — reads `.m3u` / `.m3u8` from USB (all ports usb0-usb3 in one list) and `/data/PS Play`, custom URL entry, built-in public HLS test channels. Dedicated channel list with TRIANGLE search and SQUARE reload (up to 2500 channels).
- **Stremio** — native addon client (Nuvio-style), no web engine. Movies & series with disk-cached posters and episode lists. Load addons via `Stremio_addons.txt` on USB or `/data/PS Play`, or enter manifests manually. Catalogs come from catalog-capable addons; streams are aggregated from **all** installed stream addons.
- **USB & Local** — browse all USB ports in a single list, recent files with resume position and restart prompt.

### Built for the couch
- **AMOLED pure-black UI** — horizontal icon-row menu, grayscale palette (black / gray / white), selected tile grows with a bright white outline.
- **Native PS5 system keyboard** — sceImeDialog for every text field; full symbols and all languages. Auto-reopens on invalid input; OPTIONS reopens manually.
- **Left analog stick navigation** — works like the d-pad with continuous auto-scroll when held.
- **Clean notifications** — only essential toasts ("PS Play READY", "CASTING", errors). Debug spam removed.
- **Accidental-press-proof** — during playback only X, D-pad LEFT/RIGHT, OPTIONS and CIRCLE are active; everything else lives inside the OPTIONS dialog.

### Playback engineering
- **FFmpeg-powered** — H.264, HEVC, AV1, VP9, MPEG-2/4, AAC, AC3, E-AC3, DTS, TrueHD, ALAC, FLAC, Opus, Vorbis, WMA, PCM. Protocols: HTTP/S, HLS, RTSP, RTP, UDP, RTMP, MMSH.
- **Network anti-freeze** — 8 MB socket buffer, 384-packet demux queues, PTS discontinuity re-anchoring (HLS restarts / source switches), auto-resync on >3s desync, deadlock prevention (stalled audio dropped to keep video flowing), 1.5s post-underrun buffer, auto-reconnect on 4xx/5xx errors.
- **Fast seeking** — 16 MB short-seek cache serves ±10s seeks from RAM without reopening the stream. Decoder threads park before touching codec state; the last frame stays visible instead of flashing black.
- **Subtitles & audio** — external SRT, embedded tracks, per-track selection, ±100ms delay nudging. Multiple audio tracks, aspect ratio (Fit / Fill / Stretch), media info panel, optional stats overlay.
- **Software volume** — 0-150%, also driven by DLNA SetVolume.

---

## Menu layout (7 entries)

**DLNA · IPTV / LIVE TV · WEB BROWSER · BROWSE USB · RECENT FILES · SETTINGS · ABOUT**

Navigate with **LEFT/RIGHT** or the **left analog stick**. **X** to open, **CIRCLE** back.  
CIRCLE on the main menu asks for exit confirmation (X quits, O cancels).

---

## Controls

| Context | Input | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Menu | D-pad / Left stick | Navigate |
| Menu | X / CIRCLE | Select / Back |
| Playback | X | Play / Pause |
| Playback | LEFT / RIGHT | Seek ±10s (hold to accelerate, X confirms) |
| Playback | OPTIONS | Playback settings dialog |
| Playback | CIRCLE | Stop and return (with "EXIT PLAYBACK?" confirmation) |
| OPTIONS dialog | UP / DOWN | Navigate rows |
| OPTIONS dialog | X, LEFT / RIGHT | Activate / adjust value |
| Text fields | — | PS5 system keyboard |

**OPTIONS playback dialog:** subtitles on/off, subtitle track, subtitle delay, audio track, software volume, aspect ratio, media info, statistics.

---

## Requirements

- An active jailbreak and a payload sender (port 9021)
- Like all homebrew on this firmware, **the ELF must be injected again after each reboot**
- It's not yet clear if there is PS5 firmwares that are not compatible, needs testing and report.
---

## Installation

1. Jailbreak your PS5 and start the payload listener.
2. Inject **`PSPlay.elf`** (the installer).
3. Watch the notifications: PS Play ready.
4. Open **PS Play** from the Media section of the home screen.

---

## Building from source

You need the [ps5-payload-sdk](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk) with its pacbrew packages (SDL2, FFmpeg, OpenSSL, libiconv, zlib, bzip2, xz) and a host LLVM/clang toolchain (15+).

```sh
export PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK=/path/to/ps5-payload-sdk
export PATH=$PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK/bin:$PATH

# 1. Player
make                        # produces PS5MediaPlayerPRO.elf
llvm-strip -o PSPlay.elf PS5MediaPlayerPRO.elf

# 2. Media launcher (embeds the player + assets)
cp PSPlay.elf prospero_media_standalone/assets/ProsperoPlayer.elf
cd prospero_media_standalone
make SDK=$PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK   # produces ProsperoPlayer_MediaLauncher.elf
```

---

## Tidier `/data`

All app data now lives in `/data/PS Play/` (log, resume state, web history, Stremio addons, poster cache) instead of flooding the system `/data` folder. Files from 2.0 are migrated automatically.

---

## License

GNU General Public License v3.0 (or later) — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).  
Based on [Prospero Player 1.0](https://github.com/KINGDKAK/ProsperoPlayer) by KINGDKAK (GPL-3.0) — see [NOTICE](NOTICE).

## Disclaimer

This is unofficial homebrew software, not affiliated with Sony or PlayStation. Use at your own risk on a console you own.

repos.description: Windows compatibility runtime for native PlayStation 5 homebrew.
repos.readme: **prospero-win — Windows gaming on your PS5** Bring PC classics to the big screen. **prospero-win runs Windows games locally on a homebrew-enabled PlayStation 5**, with DualSense controls, keyboard and mouse support, and a launcher for your game library. It carries its own copy of [Wine](https://www.winehq.org/). Built to bridge generations of Windows gaming—from 2000s classics to newer 32-bit and 64-bit software—with compatibility expanding game by game. ## What's supported - **32-bit Windows games** through our custom x86 translator. - **64-bit Windows applications** running natively on the PS5's x86-64 CPU through Wine. - **Direct3D 8, 9, 10 and 11** graphics through [DXVK](https://github.com/doitsujin/dxvk) and Vulkan. - **OpenGL games** through Mesa's [Zink](https://docs.mesa3d.org/drivers/zink.html) on top of Vulkan. - **Classic 2D games and Windows applications** through GDI. - **DualSense controls**, including Xbox-style XInput support, analog sticks, triggers and rumble. - **Custom controller mappings** for games originally designed for keyboard and mouse. - **USB keyboard and mouse**, usable alongside the controller. - **The console's on-screen keyboard** in a game, opened with a two-finger touchpad click, typed into the game as keys. - **Game audio** through the PS5's audio output. - **A game launcher** with individual profiles, graphics settings and control presets. - **Separate game installations**, with tools to transfer games and synchronize saves between PC and console. - **Community installation recipes and profiles** to make supported games easier to set up. See [controls](docs/CONTROLS.md) for input modes and mappings, and [installing games](docs/INSTALLING_GAMES.md) for library and save transfers. ## Already playable on PS5 - **Half-Life 2:** 60 FPS at High settings, tested with DualSense through Kleiner's lab. - **Grand Theft Auto IV: The Complete Edition:** around 55 FPS in the open city at 1080p, with DualSense. - **Half-Life, Counter-Strike 1.6 and OpenArena:** playable above 60 FPS. - **Warcraft III:** playable above 60 FPS, with DualSense or keyboard and mouse. - **Space Cadet Pinball and Wine Minesweeper:** playable. **Experimental, open source, and growing.** Compatibility depends on the game and its requirements; support for 32-bit and 64-bit software does not yet mean every modern Windows game works. See [game compatibility](COMPATIBILITY.md) for versions, graphics backends and controls. Translator benchmark results are in [DBT benchmarks](docs/DBT_BENCHMARK.md). Game profiles, controller presets and install recipes live in [prospero-win-profiles](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win-profiles). If you get a game running, a profile there is the best way to share it. ## Try it You need a PS5 that can run homebrew: an FTP server and ELF loader (for example from [ps5-payload-dev](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev)) with elfldr listening on local port 9021, and a loader that installs apps from `/data/homebrew` (such as [ShadowMountPlus](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus)). The app bundles its one-shot Lapy helper and requests `/data` during startup. You also need your own copy of the game, and a Linux PC to install it on. The app itself is a zip on the [Releases page](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/releases). [Getting started](docs/GETTING_STARTED.md) walks through the whole setup, and [installing games](docs/INSTALLING_GAMES.md) covers adding a game. ### Firmware The app itself doesn't use firmware-specific offsets. The parts that depend on your firmware are the jailbreak, the loader and the bundled Lapy helper's runtime layout checks, so use versions of those that support it. If something doesn't work on your firmware, please open an issue with the firmware version and what happened. ## How it works ```text Windows game (.exe) └─ Wine: its Windows DLLs, its Unix side and its server, all inside the PS5 app ├─ 64-bit code ─► runs natively on the PS5's x86-64 CPU ├─ 32-bit code ─► prospero-win's x86 translator (Wine's WoW64 CPU) ├─ Direct3D 8–11 ─► DXVK ─► Vulkan (RADV) ─► the TV ├─ 2D drawing (GDI), movies ─► the app's own display path ─► the TV └─ sound, DualSense, USB keyboard and mouse ─► the PS5's own services ``` Each game starts in a fresh process with its own Wine prefix, and closing it takes you back to the launcher. [Architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) and [Wine on the PS5](docs/WINE_PS5_BUILD.md) go into the details. ## Building from source Host contributions need x86_64 Linux, a C compiler, Clang, Make, Python 3 and PyYAML. No console or SDK is needed for these checks. ```sh python3 tools/check_setup.py make -j2 all # host tests, the publication audit, whitespace tools/build_native.sh # the PS5 app (needs the pinned PS5 payload SDK) tools/build_wine_ps5.sh # Wine's PS5 modules ``` [Development](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md) covers the toolchains and checks. Pull requests are welcome: [contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) explains the ground rules. ## What this project is not It doesn't bypass DRM or anti-cheat, it doesn't load kernel drivers, and it doesn't ship games. Please don't open issues or pull requests with Windows binaries, game files or keys. ## Credits - [BlackBearReloaded](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded) created the PS5 Native App Boilerplate the app is built on, and the PS5 OpenGL port that OpenGL games ran through before Zink. - [mihawk-99](https://github.com/mihawk-99) found and fixed several problems with Wine on the PS5 that prospero-win now includes: the floating-point state after a handled exception, memory reserved at a fixed address, decommitted memory, memory and processor usage reports, directory change notifications, and how threads share the console's CPUs. His Mesa WGL/Zink work for the PS5 is what OpenGL games now draw through. Third-party code and its licences are listed in the [third-party notices](NOTICE.md). ## License [LGPL-2.1-or-later](LICENSE), like Wine. See the [licensing notes](LICENSING.md) and [third-party notices](NOTICE.md). `PPSA99995` is a local title ID we picked, not one assigned by Sony.

latestRelease.name: prospero-win v0.3.0
latestRelease.body:
## New

- **Frame generation** with [MihawkGen](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_MihawkGen), thanks to [mihawk-99](https://github.com/mihawk-99): `[display] framegen = 2` (or `3`, `4`) shows 2x (3x, 4x) the frames a Vulkan game presents. DXVK, Zink and Vulkan games all work ([#722](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/722)).
- **Direct3D 12** through vkd3d-proton 3.0.1: `wine: {dxvk: true, vkd3d: true}` in an install script. Feature level 11_1 on the console ([#711](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/711)).
- **In-game menu** on L3+R3 (`[display] menu`), with a **keyboard input** entry. A **two-finger touchpad click** opens the PS5's on-screen keyboard and types the line into the game ([#707](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/707), [#726](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/726)).
- **Single-program titles:** one Windows program as its own app on the home screen, without the launcher ([#719](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/719)).
- **A second DualSense** as a second keyboard player ([#427](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/427)).

## Controls

- Hold **Options + Create** for 3 seconds to close a game ([#720](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/720)).
- The touchpad's left half is **Back** and its right half is **Guide**; mouse **wheel** works ([#721](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/721), [#715](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/715)).
- **L2/R2 vibrate** with the rumble, and the controller stays connected while the PS menu is open ([#712](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/712), [#725](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/725)).

## Memory and fixes

- Games see the console's real memory (12 GiB), instead of almost none, which some games refused to start with ([#688](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/688)).
- Wine's own heap moved out of the game's flexible memory, leaving 5–26 MB more of it for the game ([#470](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/470), thanks to [leolobato](https://github.com/leolobato)).
- Thread and fiber stacks use what Windows uses: 3000 fibers take 49 MB instead of 3.1 GB. 64-bit games can reserve up to 512 GiB of address space ([#727](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/727), with leolobato's patch).
- .NET and SMAPI games with large mod folders no longer run out of file handles ([#697](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/697)).
- Emulators like DuckStation that write-protect 4 KB pages work ([#718](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/718)), plus fixes to audio resampling, OpenGL games and closing ([#699](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/699), [#701](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/701), [#698](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/698)).
- Root certificates updated to Mozilla's 2026-10-20 store.

## Installing

1. Download `prospero-win-<version>.zip` below and unzip it. You get a folder
   called `PPSA99995`.
2. Upload that folder to `/data/homebrew/` on your PS5 and let your loader
   register it.
3. Follow [Getting started](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/blob/main/docs/GETTING_STARTED.md)
   to add your first game.

`SHA256SUMS` lets you check the download: `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS`.

Updating from an earlier version: replace the whole `PPSA99995` folder. Your
games, profiles and prefixes live in `/data/prospero-win` and are kept.

repos.name: ps5-linux-dma-bounce-fix
repos.readme:
# ps5-linux-dma-bounce-fix

A kernel patch for the PS5 Linux freeze that happens when you write to USB
storage — the one where the drive disconnects mid-download and the whole
machine locks up until you reboot.

The patch confines xHCI controller DMA to the swiotlb bounce buffer, which
keeps transfers away from the pages that cause the hang. It is three files and
about twenty lines.

## The symptom

You are downloading something, or copying a large file, onto the USB drive you
booted Linux from. After anywhere between one minute and an hour:

```
sd 1:0:0:0: [sda] tag#9 uas_eh_abort_handler 0 uas-tag 10 inflight: CMD OUT
sd 1:0:0:0: [sda] tag#9 CDB: Write(10) 2a 00 ...
xhci_hcd 0000:20:00.5: xHCI host not responding to stop endpoint command
xhci_hcd 0000:20:00.5: xHCI host controller not responding, assume dead
xhci_hcd 0000:20:00.5: HC died; cleaning up
usb 4-1: USB disconnect, device number 2
sd 1:0:0:0: Device offlined - not ready after error recovery
EXT4-fs error: Aborting journal on device sda1-8
```

The root filesystem goes read-only, SSH stops accepting connections, and the
screen freezes. Keyboard and mouse often still work, because they are on a
different controller — which is the first hint that the USB stack is not the
culprit.

## What is actually wrong

The xHCI controller is a **victim**, not the cause. Nine to fourteen seconds
*before* it gives up, the platform has already logged this:

```
mce: [Hardware Error]: CPU 0: Machine Check: 0 Bank 45: dc2030000002085b
mce: [Hardware Error]: TSC 0 ADDR 2ad0d00 MISC d01a000400000000 SYND 5b260028 IPID 2002e0000000d
```

`IPID 0x0002002e_0000000d` decodes to HWID `0x2E` / MCAType `0x2`, which the
kernel's SMCA tables name **Coherent Station** — a block of the AMD Data
Fabric. The extended error code is `0x02`. In short: **the Data Fabric refused
a DMA write from the USB controller.**

Two details explain why a refused write freezes the machine instead of
producing a clean error:

| bit | name | value | consequence |
|----:|------|-------|-------------|
| 60 | `EN` | 0 | this bank raises no `#MC` exception |
| 57 | `PCC` | 0 | the CPU context is intact |
| 44 | `DEFERRED` | 1 | the error is merely recorded |

Nothing aborts the transfer. Linux writes a line to the log and carries on,
while the controller waits for a completion that will never arrive. The USB
timeout machinery eventually declares the host dead, and the root filesystem
goes with it.

The refused addresses are the giveaway. Every failure reports sixteen MCE banks
covering **one single 4 KiB page**, sliced into 256-byte chunks interleaved
across the sixteen Coherent Station instances:

```
failure 1:  ADDR 1be50000, 1be50100, 1be50200 ... 1be50f00
failure 2:  ADDR 02ad0000, 02ad0100, 02ad0200 ... 02ad0f00
```

Both pages are declared `System RAM` by the e820 map, so Linux is entitled to
use them — and both sit below the first gigabyte. The page differs from one
failure to the next, so this is not one contiguous forbidden region but pages
scattered through low memory that the firmware keeps for itself and the boot
loader fails to mark reserved.

**The real upstream fix therefore belongs in the loader's memory map, not in
Linux.** This patch is a safety net that works today and does not depend on
anyone releasing the loader source.

See [docs/DIAGNOSIS.md](docs/DIAGNOSIS.md) for the full evidence, including the
eight hypotheses that were measured and ruled out first.

## Status — read this before you use it

| | Tested |
|---|---|
| Image | `ps5-ubuntu2604.img.xz` (Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS, *resolute*) |
| Kernel patch set | [rmuxnet/ps5-linux-patches-1](https://github.com/rmuxnet/ps5-linux-patches-1) |
| Kernel | `7.3.0-rc7-PinkSoup`, clang FullLTO |
| Console | PS5 *fat* |
| Storage | NVMe in a HIKSEMI enclosure (RTL9210, `0bda:9210`), USB-C front port, UAS |
| Controller | AMD Ariel USB 3.1 Type C `1022:13ed` at `0000:20:00.5` |

**It has not been tested anywhere else.** Not on a Slim, not on a Pro, not with
another distribution, not with another kernel branch, not with the drive on a
rear USB-A port.

What was measured, on that one console:

| Kernel | Load survived | `Hardware Error` lines | Display |
|---|---|---|---|
| unmodified | **failed in under a minute**, twice out of twice | 64 each time | works |
| `swiotlb=force` on the command line | 140 GB | 0 | **dead** |
| this patch | **295 GB written + ~295 GB read in 10 minutes, while a game was downloading** | 0 | works |

The last row is the test that matters. 585 passes of a 512 MB direct-I/O
write-then-read cycle, running *concurrently* with a game download, sustained
around 510 MB/s on the storage while the download kept its own 1.3–2.9 MB/s
throughout. No machine check, no storage error, no `swiotlb buffer is full`, no
`Salina: event ring appears stuck`, root filesystem still read-write at the
end, and `/sys/class/drm/` still holding its `card0`. Burst throughput without
the download competing: 648–728 MB/s, i.e. unchanged from the stock kernel.

For scale: the unmodified kernel died in under a minute under that same `dd`
load, and the first captured failure on this console came after about forty
minutes of nothing heavier than a download. The patched kernel passed both
marks with several hundred times the traffic.

**Two other people have since applied it and reported the freeze gone.** Their
hardware is not described here because I do not know it; take it as two
independent data points rather than coverage.

**What is still missing** is a multi-day, boringly normal usage report, and a
description of the hardware the patch has worked on beyond the single console
in the table above. If you try it, please open an issue either way — a negative
result is just as useful as a positive one, and the hardware details matter
more than the verdict.

## Why not just `swiotlb=force`?

Because it works and then takes your display with it. `swiotlb=force` applies
to every device, and amdgpu asks for single 2 MB mappings while swiotlb caps a
mapping at `IO_TLB_SEGSIZE * 2 KB = 256 KB`:

```
amdgpu 0000:20:00.0: swiotlb buffer is full (sz: 2097152 bytes), total 32768 (slots), used 33 (slots)
```

No DRM card is registered, `/sys/class/drm/` holds only `version`, and the
screen stays black. USB block I/O, by contrast, is already split into segments
of at most 64 KB (`max_segment_size`), comfortably below the limit — which is
exactly why the USB path tolerates what the GPU cannot.

That said, if you just want tonight's download to finish and you do not need
the screen, `swiotlb=force` on the kernel command line is one line and needs no
build.

## What you need

On Arch, rmux's README asks for:

```sh
sudo pacman -S --needed base-devel git bc cpio libelf clang lld llvm ccache mkinitcpio
```

The Debian/Ubuntu equivalent is:

```sh
sudo apt install build-essential git bc cpio libelf-dev clang lld llvm \
                 ccache initramfs-tools flex bison libssl-dev zstd kmod python3
```

Mapping, package by package:

| Arch | Debian / Ubuntu | note |
|---|---|---|
| `base-devel` | `build-essential` | Arch's group also pulls in `flex` and `bison`; apt does not, hence the two extra entries |
| `libelf` | `libelf-dev` | headers are a separate package on Debian |
| `mkinitcpio` | `initramfs-tools` | different generator, same job — `install.sh` handles `mkinitcpio`, `update-initramfs` and `dracut` |
| — | `libssl-dev` | needed to build the kernel's certificate tooling; on Arch openssl headers come with the base system |
| `bc` `cpio` `clang` `lld` `llvm` `ccache` | same names | |

Add `dwarves` if your config has `CONFIG_DEBUG_INFO_BTF=y`, and
`libncurses-dev` if you want `make menuconfig`. On the
`ps5-ubuntu2604.img.xz` image all of these are already installed.

## Usage

### Where to apply it

**On a kernel source tree.** Not on the `.img`, not on a running system: this
is kernel C, so it needs a rebuild and a cold boot.

If you built your kernel with rmux's `build.sh`, the tree you want is the one
that script created or reused -- normally `~/linux`, next to
`~/ps5-linux-patches`. If you are not sure which directory it is, look for the
marker `build.sh` leaves inside it:

```sh
find ~ -maxdepth 3 -name .ci-kernel-ref
```

`install.sh` finds the tree on its own in the common cases, and prints which
one it picked before touching anything. If it picks the wrong one, name it with
`--src`.

### Steps

```sh
git clone https://github.com/muftiomar/ps5-linux-dma-bounce-fix
cd ps5-linux-dma-bounce-fix

./install.sh --check          # verify the patch applies, write nothing
./install.sh                  # patch the source tree only
./install.sh --build          # patch, then build and install
./install.sh --revert         # restore the original files
```

Autodetection order: the current directory if it is a kernel tree, otherwise
`SRC_DIR` from a neighbouring `ps5-linux-patches/build.cfg`, otherwise
`~/linux`. Override with `--src /path/to/linux`.

Patching the source changes nothing by itself. Build afterwards, which on the
PS5 image means:

```sh
cd ~/ps5-linux-patches && ./build.sh
```

That rebuild takes roughly half an hour on the console and deploys the new
kernel itself, keeping your previous `bzImage` and `initrd.img` in
`/boot/efi-backup/<timestamp>/`. Then **cold boot**: rebooting from inside
Linux hands control back to the PS5 firmware, so you have to redo the
jailbreak and reload the loader.

With `--build`, if rmux's `build.sh` is present it is used, because that is the
only build path this patch has been validated through: it reuses your current
toolchain, LTO setting and `-march`, installs the modules, regenerates the
initrd and deploys to the boot partition with a backup. Without it, a generic
build runs instead — that path is **untested**, and the script says so before
starting.

Then cold boot the PS5. Rebooting from inside Linux returns you to the PS5
firmware, so you have to redo the jailbreak and reload the loader.

### Checking that it took effect

```sh
cat /sys/module/xhci_pci/parameters/force_dma_bounce   # expect: Y
ls /sys/class/drm/                                     # expect a card0, i.e. the GPU still works
dmesg | grep -c "Hardware Error"                       # expect: 0 after a heavy write
```

### Turning it off without rebuilding

Add this to the kernel command line:

```
xhci_pci.force_dma_bounce=0
```

## Two ways to apply it

The change itself is ordinary kernel C -- about twenty lines across three
files. It ships in both of the formats people expect, and they produce
byte-for-byte the same result:

**`patches/0001-usb-xhci-confine-controller-DMA-to-the-swiotlb-buffer.patch`**
is a normal `git format-patch` output. Use it to read the change, to review it,
or to send it somewhere:

```sh
cd /path/to/linux
git apply patches/0001-*.patch        # or: git am patches/0001-*.patch
```

**`patch-dma-bounce.py`** applies the same change by searching for text
anchors instead of line numbers. A unified diff carries line numbers, so it
drifts as soon as the tree is not exactly the one it was generated against --
and rmux's `linux.patch` has already moved things around. The script verifies
that each anchor appears exactly once, checks the result afterwards, and
**refuses to write anything if anything does not match**. It also detects which
flavour of `struct device` your kernel has. Prefer it if you are applying to a
tree you did not build yourself:

```sh
./install.sh --check    # dry run
./install.sh            # apply
```

## What the patch does

Three files, and nothing else:

- **`include/linux/device.h`** — adds a `DEV_FLAG_DMA_FORCE_BOUNCE` device flag.
- **`include/linux/swiotlb.h`** — `is_swiotlb_force_bounce()` honours that flag,
  *but only when a swiotlb buffer actually exists* (`mem->nslabs` non-zero). A
  kernel built without one degrades to the previous behaviour rather than
  failing every mapping, which would leave the machine unable to reach its root
  filesystem.
- **`drivers/usb/host/xhci-pci.c`** — sets the flag at `probe`, before any
  mapping is made, behind a `force_dma_bounce` module parameter that defaults
  to on.

Only **streaming** mappings are redirected. Coherent allocations — the xHCI
rings and device contexts — are untouched, which is correct: the failure
happens on data transfers, not on ring memory, and those rings have always
worked.

`patch-dma-bounce.py` does the editing with anchored regular expressions and
refuses to write anything unless every anchor matches exactly once. If your
kernel has moved on, it tells you and exits without touching a file. It also
detects which flavour of `struct device` you have: the `DEV_FLAG_*` bitmap used
by 6.17 and later, or the older plain `bool` bitfields — the latter path is
**untested**, and the script labels it as such when it takes it.

Requires a kernel with per-device swiotlb support, i.e. 5.19 or later.

## Risks and limitations

- **Bounce buffer exhaustion.** Under extreme concurrent USB I/O you could see
  `swiotlb buffer is full`, which surfaces as an I/O error rather than silent
  corruption. Not observed in testing. If it happens, enlarge the buffer with
  `swiotlb=131072` (256 MB instead of the default 64 MB).
- **`DMA_ATTR_MMIO` / `DMA_ATTR_REQUIRE_COHERENT`** mappings return an error
  under forced bouncing. No USB path is known to use them, and nothing was
  observed, but it is a theoretical hazard.
- **Every USB device on an xHCI controller is bounced**, not just storage. For
  keyboards, mice and Bluetooth the extra memcpy is irrelevant.
- **It does not fix the cause.** The pages are still mis-declared, so another
  device doing DMA — the GPU, the internal NVMe — could still trip the same
  Data Fabric refusal. It would no longer *freeze* the machine, because the
  freeze came from the xHCI waiting forever, not from the machine check itself.
- **No data corruption risk.** swiotlb bouncing is the standard path on every
  machine that has a 32-bit DMA device; this patch only changes *which* devices
  take it.
- **Not upstream material as written.** Defaulting the flag on for all xHCI
  controllers is fine for a PS5-only kernel but wrong in general; upstream
  would want it gated on platform detection.

## Credits

- [rmuxnet/ps5-linux-patches-1](https://github.com/rmuxnet/ps5-linux-patches-1)
  — the kernel patch set and build system this was developed against. Its
  `build.sh` does the real work of building and deploying.
- The PS5 Linux loader is sonic_iso's work. The memory map it hands to Linux is
  where this bug ultimately lives.

## Licence

`SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0` — the patched files are part of the Linux
kernel and this patch inherits its licence. See
<https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/latest/process/license-rules.html>.

repos.readme:
# Playstation 5 Save Mounter 2.0.1
Supports all jailbreakable PS5 FWs.  
Mounts PS1, PS2, PSP, PS4 and PS5 game saves.

Use this elf loader: https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/elfldr

## Instructions (mouting existing saves)
1) Load elfldr.
2) Load FTP.
3) Open the tool.
4) Enter the IP address of your PS5 and click 'Connect'.
5) Click 'Setup' and select your username.
6) Click 'Get Games' and select your game in the combobox.
7) Click 'Search'.
8) Select the save you want to mount in the combobox.
9) Click 'Mount'.
10) Your save is now mounted and accessible from FTP in `/mnt/pfs/`.
11) After copying or replacing the files, be sure to click 'Unmount'.

** Warning: Don't replace files in `sce_sys` directory, it is unnecessary and will probably corrupt your save**

---

# Credits:
* cow - based on his save mounting research using `sceFs*` internal PS5 functions
* earthonion - for his loading game titles code and save creation from [garlic-savemgr](https://git.etawen.dev/earthonion/garlic-savemgr)

## Features - **Web-Based Interface**: A modern dashboard to manage payloads from your PC, phone, or the PS5 itself. - **Import Payloads**: Easily add new payloads from a USB drive or download them from the cloud repository. - **Automated Startup**: Set up a list of payloads to load automatically whenever you start the manager. - **Home Screen Shortcut**: Installs a dedicated "Payload Manager" app icon to your PS5 home screen for quick access. - **Favorites and Process Management**: Keep favorite payloads at hand, inspect active processes, and terminate eligible processes. --- ## 这是什么 **NayePlmTools** 是基于 [itsPLK/ps5-payload-manager](https://github.com/itsPLK/ps5-payload-manager) 的 中文分支，由 **naye** 维护。原版是一个跑在 PS5 上的网页版 Payload 管理面板；本分支在保留其全部能力的 前提下，**补齐了「面板改了、主机没改」这一类断链的功能**，并针对中文用户与电视端（遥控器）做了适配。 - 仓库地址：**https://github.com/naye1120/NayePlmTools** - 上游项目：https://github.com/itsPLK/ps5-payload-manager --- ## 核心增强（相对原版） 原版有很多功能只改到「面板自己记着」，重启主机或 SMP 重扫就回到原样。本分支把这些功能**真正写进主机**。 ### 🎮 游戏管理 | 功能 | 说明 | | :--- | :--- | | **游戏改名（写回主机）** | 名称同时写回系统 `app.db` 与 `appinfo.db` 的**整套语言槽位**（`TITLE` + `TITLE_00..30`、`concept_name` + `concept_name_00..30`），电视主屏与 ShadowMountPlus 跟着变。简体中文系统读的是 `TITLE_11` —— 这正是「只有一个位置变了」的根因，已修复。 | | **背景音乐（写进游戏包）** | PS5 磁贴音乐只认游戏包里的 `sce_sys/snd0.at9`（ATRAC9）。本分支在**浏览器里**用内置的 ATRAC9 编码器转码后写进游戏包，并写入响度元数据、备份原件。以前只存在面板自己目录里，主机根本不读。 | | **自定义图标 / 背景** | 更换磁贴图标与背景图。 | | **置顶（写主机）** | 写进 `app.db` 的 `MyHome` 固定列表（`idx` 就是主屏位置），并放开「只能置顶内置软件」的限制 —— **游戏也能置顶**。 | | **拖拽排序** | 点「排序」进入排序模式，磁贴左上角显示位置号，拖到想要的位置松手即写回主机；电视端可用上移 / 下移 / 移到最前。 | | **多媒体管理 + 分享二维码** | 浏览 / 下载游戏内多媒体资源；分享按钮生成的二维码**扫码直接开始下载**（单文件直链，多选 / 全量先打包再给链接）。 | | **从 USB 移动** | 把游戏从 USB 移动到内置存储。 | ### 💾 存档管理 | 功能 | 说明 | | :--- | :--- | | **远程拉取 / 推送** | 支持 **FTP + HTTP + SMB** 三协议平权，远端布局 `//.zip`。 | | **本地快照** | 每次游戏退出后自动存一份，落 `/data/nayeplmtools/saves_snap/`，全局 512MB 预算。 | | **garlic 兼容导入** | 兼容 garlic 导出的存档镜像（PS5 裸 `sdimg_*` / PS4 zip），**逐文件合并**、保留主机记账文件；整包成功才落盘（先写暂存目录再 rename）。 | | **存档转换** | 把其它用户的存档一键转换到当前用户可用，逐文件合并而非整份替换。 | | **拉取前比新旧** | 纯函数判定「远端是否比本地新」，说不清一律按该拉处理，避免误覆盖。 | | **游戏运行中禁推拉** | 后端当场探测后拒绝，前端置灰并写明理由（电视端没有 hover，理由直接印在界面上）。 | | **自动存档** | 启动时拉取 / 退出时回传；**跳过自制应用（homebrew）**，避免误推镜像、误拉覆盖。 | | **拉取前冻结游戏** | 自动拉取前用**进程级 `SIGSTOP`** 冻住正在启动的游戏（不用 LncUtil 挂起 —— 那会让游戏跳后台且无法切回前台）。 | ### 🧩 其余模块 - **Payload 管理**：浏览 / 安装 / 更新 / 删除 payload；内置云端仓库与自定义来源；装完自动同步越狱引导器。 - **自动加载**：编排开机自动加载序列（延时行 + 载荷名），可上移 / 下移 / 插延时，写回幂等。 - **PKG 安装**：内嵌 PKG Manager，可在面板里上传、启停、更新版本。 - **账号工具**：登录 / 登出 / 反激活，头像上传与裁剪。 - **常用入口**：手动添加插件 / 局域网服务快捷卡片，逐条 TCP 探活，点卡片新标签打开。 - **风扇温控**：读风扇状态，向 `/dev/icc_fan` 下发目标温度。 - **其它**：远程游玩配对、SMP（ShadowMountPlus）探活与拉起、运行日志查看、活动进程查看。 ### 🖥️ 界面 - 深色主题；**电视端（遥控器）适配**；**移动端二级菜单**（手机端 PKG 安装 / 常用配置 / 游戏管理 / 活动进程 / 设置 / 关于 收进下拉菜单，桌面与电视端保持原侧栏）。 - 刷新后停在当前页；存档、多媒体等面板「铺满右侧」。 - 多语言：继承上游 [Crowdin](https://crowdin.com/project/ps5-payload-manager) 的全部语言，并叠加本分支的中文文案覆盖层。 ## Translations PS5 Payload Manager supports multiple languages. For the list of supported languages, how to report translation issues or suggest improvements, and past community translators, see [TRANSLATIONS.md](TRANSLATIONS.md). --- ## 安装 ### 配合 Autoloader（推荐） 推荐与 Autoloader 一起使用： [Y2JB](https://github.com/itsPLK/ps5-y2jb-autoloader) | [BD-JB](https://github.com/itsPLK/ps5-bdjb-autoloader) | [Lua](https://github.com/itsPLK/ps5-lua-autoloader) 把 `NayePlmTools_.elf` 放进 `autoload` 目录，并在 `autoload.txt` 里把它作为条目即可。 两个变体： | 文件 | 磁贴落点 | | :--- | :--- | | `NayePlmTools_-me.elf` | **媒体**栏（`NAYE00001`） | | `NayePlmTools_-ga.elf` | **游戏**栏（`NAYE00004`） | ### 手动加载 从 [Releases](https://github.com/naye1120/NayePlmTools/releases) 下载最新 `.elf`，像其它 payload 一样加载。 面板默认监听 `http://:8911`。 --- ## 自定义仓库 可以添加第三方 payload 仓库。自定义仓库 JSON 的格式与托管方式见上游的 [Custom Repositories Guide](CUSTOM_REPOSITORIES.md)。 --- ## 构建 前端为 React + Vite（产物是**单页 HTML**，会被内联进 ELF）；后端为 C + Prospero SDK。 ```bash # 1) 构建前端（产物 frontend/dist/index.html） make frontend-build # 2) 打包两个磁贴变体的 ELF（需要 PS5 payload SDK） bash tools/build_tiles.sh ``` 更细的构建与部署说明见 [DEVELOPMENT.md](DEVELOPMENT.md)； 接手维护前请先读 [HANDOVER.md](./HANDOVER.md)（本分支的事实来源与踩坑记录）。 --- ## 致谢 本分支的改动参考、移植或依赖了下列开源项目（按来源分组，只列作者与项目）： **上游与 SDK** - [itsPLK](https://github.com/itsPLK) —— [ps5-payload-manager](https://github.com/itsPLK/ps5-payload-manager)（原版 Payload Manager，本分支的上游）、[ps5_next_menu](https://github.com/itsPLK/ps5_next_menu)（侧栏与导航原型）、[ps5-pkg-manager](https://github.com/itsPLK/ps5-pkg-manager)、[ps5-bdjb-autoloader](https://github.com/itsPLK/ps5-bdjb-autoloader)、[ps5-lua-autoloader](https://github.com/itsPLK/ps5-lua-autoloader)、[ps5-y2jb-autoloader](https://github.com/itsPLK/ps5-y2jb-autoloader)。 - [John Törnblom](https://github.com/john-tornblom) —— [ps5-payload-sdk](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk) 与多个参考 payload。 - [ps5-payload-dev](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev) —— [pacbrew-repo](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/pacbrew-repo)（`libsmb2` 正式包）、[websrv](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/websrv)（`libsmb2` 用法参考）、[offact](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/offact)（离线账号激活，账号工具源自它）。 **游戏与存档** - [drakmor](https://github.com/drakmor) —— [ShadowMountPlus](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus)（挂载 / 游戏识别 / 详情跳转）、[ps5-hwinfo](https://github.com/drakmor/ps5-hwinfo)、[fan_target](https://github.com/drakmor/fan_target)。 - [earthonion](https://github.com/earthonion) —— [garlic-savemgr](https://github.com/earthonion/garlic-savemgr)（兼容导入的格式依据）。 - [manos555555](https://github.com/manos555555) —— [PS5-Upload-Suite](https://github.com/manos555555/PS5-Upload-Suite)。 - [Pharaoh2k](https://github.com/Pharaoh2k) —— [ps5debug-NG](https://github.com/Pharaoh2k/ps5debug-NG)。 **音频与图像** - [blackbearreloaded](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded) —— [ps5-at9-converter](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-at9-converter)（本分支的浏览器端 ATRAC9 编码器移植自该项目）。 - [Thealexbarney](https://github.com/Thealexbarney) —— [LibAtrac9](https://github.com/Thealexbarney/LibAtrac9)（ATRAC9 解码表来源，MIT）。 - [nothings](https://github.com/nothings) —— [stb](https://github.com/nothings/stb)（`stb_image` / `stb_image_write`）。 **风扇与系统** - [owendswang](https://github.com/owendswang) —— [ps5-fan-control](https://github.com/owendswang/ps5-fan-control)，以及上游贡献。 - [BenNoxXD](https://github.com/BenNoxXD) —— Disc Player 终止逻辑。 - [上游全部贡献者](https://github.com/itsPLK/ps5-payload-manager/graphs/contributors) —— 对本项目上游的贡献。 以及所有参与 PS5 homebrew 社区的开发者。 --- ## 捐赠 如果这个分支帮到了你，可以请我喝杯咖啡：

latestRelease.name: NayePlmTools v0.6.3.197
latestRelease.body:
## v0.6.3.197 (CN-FORK) — 2026-10-29 · 修「开机不自启」：引导器目录/清单按需创建 + 启动即登记

> 用户口径：「程序被拉起的时候没有自动创建 autoloader 文件夹，有文件夹也没有写入文件」。

### 修 bug：`/data/ps5_autoloader` 不建、清单不写、启动不登记
- **真机取证**（192.168.1.214）：目录**存在**（别的载荷建的），`autoload.txt` 只有一行 `@sync`
  —— 没有本工具条目、目录里也没有 ELF；本工具那份躺在**旧布局**
  `/data/nayeplmtools/payloads/NayePlmTools/NayePlmTools_0.6.3.196-me.elf`。
- **四个原因**（全在 `src/payload_mgr.c`）：
  1. `payload_mgr_bootstrap_self_sync()` 第一句 `stat(PS5_AUTOLOADER_DIR)` 失败就 `return`
     → 目录不存在时**永不创建**（`.196` 那版还专门写了「这个目录归引导器所有，我们不建」）；
  2. `payload_mgr_autoloader_sync()`：目录不存在 `return 1`；**目录在、`autoload.txt` 不在**
     时 `fopen(...,"r")` 失败 → `sync skipped` + `return -1` —— 就是「有文件夹也没写入文件」；
  3. 启动对账里「清单没有本工具条目 → leaving it alone」（旧口径「登记只发生在用户明确安装时」）
     → 换机、手清目录、引导器重建清单之后，本工具**永远不再自启**；
  4. 找自己那份 ELF 只扫 `payloads/pldmgr` 与 `local|repo` 槽位，**漏了旧布局
     `payloads/<工具名>/`** —— 真机上正好是后者，于是「找不到自己」。
- **改法**：
  - 新增 `autoloader_ensure_dir()`：目录不存在 `mkdir 0777`（容忍 EEXIST），成功/失败都留日志；
  - `payload_mgr_autoloader_sync()` 改用它，`autoload.txt` 不存在当成空清单继续
    （只有 ENOENT 这样，权限等错误仍算失败）；
  - `payload_mgr_bootstrap_self_sync()`：目录/清单按需建；**无条目 → 启动即登记**
    （`allow_register=1`：落 ELF + 写条目 + 自动补 `!1000` 延时行，与网页上传同一套）；
    新增旧布局扫描；条目在但文件缺失/残包 → **同版本才补**，在册版本更新则只留痕、绝不降级。
  - 护栏保留：找不到自己那份 ELF → 不写指向空气的条目；候选版本更旧 → 不动。

repos.name: PS5-Custom-Tool-Manager-
repos.readme:
# PS5 Custom Tool Manager V1

PS5 Custom Tool Manager V1 est une payload ELF autonome pour PS5, basee sur le tool PC original 

Elle lance une interface web locale sur la console pour scanner les jeux, apps et certains chemins systeme, puis modifier les icones, backgrounds, noms, visibilite, backups et fonts systeme.
  
> Le tool V1 fonctionne ( tester sur ma 6.02 ) des bugs peuvent probablement arriver . Les fonctions V2 sont travaillees separement. ( Formes des icones…) bientôt terminer
> 
## Vidéo de démonstration

Clique sur l’image pour voir la vidéo :

[![Vidéo de démonstration](https://img.youtube.com/vi/S3fAEIKSf-M/hqdefault.jpg)](https://youtu.be/S3fAEIKSf-M)


## Lancement

1. Lance ton payload loader sur la PS5 9021
2. Lance `PS5 Custom Tool Manager Launcher.bat` pour envoyer la payload ou envoyer ou installer la payload selon votre choix de configs
3. Envoie `PS5 Custom Tool Manager V1.elf` vers l'IP de ta PS5, vous rentrer juste votre IP
4. Ouvre via le raccourci XMB ou la page web:

```text
http://IP_DE_LA_PS5:8089/
```

La page peut etre ouverte depuis la PS5, un PC sur le meme reseau.

## Fonctions principales

- Serveur web local sur le port `8089`.
- Scan jeux/apps utilisateur.
- Scan de chemins systeme selectionnes.
- Preview PNG et DDS compatibles.
- Remplacement `icon0`, `pic0`, `pic1`, `pic2`, `save_data` et assets systeme .
- Redimensionnement automatique des images.
- Conversion selon le format cible: PNG ou DDS.
- Selection d'image depuis USB sur PS5.
- Selection d'image depuis PC hors navigateur PS5.
- Renommage des jeux/apps .
- Masquer / afficher quand les champs existent.
- Force DB pour certains chemins image quand ceux il ne sont pas present d'origine .
- Backups automatiques avant modification.
- Restauration des backups.
- Module fonts: backup, import TTF/OTF, preview, appliquer, restaurer.
- Bouton `Retirer tuile` pour retirer proprement la tuile XMB.
- Off coupe le serveur port 8089...

## USB

Dossier a la racine de la cle usb :

```text
PS5CustomToolManager/
```

Structure conseillee:

```text
PS5CustomToolManager/
  images/
  fonts/
  backups/
  font_backups/
```

### Images

Dossier conseiller :

```text
PS5CustomToolManager/images
```

Formats acceptes:

```text
.png .jpg .jpeg .bmp .webp .dds
```

Le tool possede un navigateur USB, donc les images peuvent aussi etre rangees dans d'autres dossiers de la cle.

### Fonts

Dossier exact pour importer depuis la PS5:

```text
PS5CustomToolManager/fonts
```

Formats acceptes:

```text
.ttf .otf
```

Sur PS5, `Importer TTF/OTF` recupere les fonts depuis la cle USB.  
Depuis PC, le meme bouton importe une font depuis l'appareil qui ouvre la page web.

## Backups

Backups locaux PS5:

```text
/data/PS5CustomToolManager/backups
/data/PS5CustomToolManager/backups/db
/data/PS5CustomToolManager/font_backups
```

Miroir USB si une cle est branchee:

```text
PS5CustomToolManager/backups
PS5CustomToolManager/backups/db
PS5CustomToolManager/font_backups
```

Le tool garde jusqu'a 5 backups par famille de fichier cible.

## Boutons importants

| Bouton | Fonction |
| --- | --- |
| `Jeux` | Scanne les jeux et apps utilisateur. |
| `Systeme` | Scanne les chemins systeme selectionnes. |
| `Fonts` | Ouvre le module fonts. |
| `Status` | Verifie le serveur payload. |
| `Retirer tuile` | Retire la tuile XMB du tool. |
| `OFF` | Coupe le serveur payload. |
| `USB` | Choisit une image depuis la cle USB. |
| `PC/Tel` | Choisit une image depuis PC/tel. |
| `Force DB` | Force un chemin image dans `app.db`. |
| `Renommer` | Renomme l'entree selectionnee. |
| `Masquer` / `Afficher` | Change la visibilite si supporte. |
| `Backups` | Affiche/restaure les backups image. |
| `Backup fonts` | Sauvegarde les fonts systeme originales. |
| `Importer TTF/OTF` | Importe fonts USB sur PS5 ou fichier local sur PC/tel. |
| `Restaurer Original SST` | Restaure les fonts SST originales sauvegardees. |

## Precautions

- Utiliser uniquement sur sa propre console.
- Garder des backups.
- Ne pas couper la console pendant une modification DB, image ou font.
- Le changement de font systeme est plus risque que le changement d'image.
- Faire `Backup fonts` avant d'appliquer une font custom pour garder l original 
- Le cache XMB peut garder certaines anciennes images jusqu'au redemarrage.


## Credits
   
Voir `CREDITS.txt`.

Ce projet n'est pas affilie a Sony Interactive Entertainment et n'est pas approuve par Sony Interactive Entertainment.
Projet a titre educatif et d'apprentissage

![AstraPlay Logo](astraplay-logo.png) # AstraPlay [![License: AGPL-3.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-AGPL--3.0-blue)](https://github.com/nileshchakraborty/AstraPlay/blob/master/LICENSES/AGPL-3.0-only-OpenSSL.txt) [![Platforms](https://img.shields.io/badge/platforms-Windows%20(x64%20%2B%20ARM64)%20%7C%20macOS%20(Apple%20Silicon%20%2B%20Intel)%20%7C%20Linux%20(x86__64%20%2B%20ARM64)%20%7C%20Android%20%7C%20iOS-brightgreen)](https://github.com/nileshchakraborty/AstraPlay/releases) [![Build Status](https://github.com/nileshchakraborty/AstraPlay/actions/workflows/release-on-merge.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/nileshchakraborty/AstraPlay/actions/workflows/release-on-merge.yml) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/nileshchakraborty/AstraPlay?color=purple)](https://github.com/nileshchakraborty/AstraPlay/releases/latest) **AstraPlay is a high-performance, 100% free and open-source PlayStation (PS4 & PS5) Remote Play client for Windows, macOS, Linux, SteamOS, Bazzite, Android, and iOS.** Engineered for ultra-low latency, crisp visuals, and cross-platform flexibility, AstraPlay delivers native hardware-accelerated video streaming, seamless local and Internet Play, gamepad navigation for handheld devices, and private self-hosted authentication options. --- ## Key Highlights - **100% Free & Open-Source**: Zero paywalls, zero locked features, zero subscription gates, and zero donation nags. All features are fully unlocked for everyone. - **True Multi-Platform**: Native binaries for Windows (x64 and ARM64), macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel), Linux (x86_64 and aarch64), Android (Phones, Tablets, and Android TV), and iOS/iPadOS. - **Handheld-First Design**: Tailored for the **ROG Xbox Ally X**, **Steam Deck**, **Lenovo Legion Go**, and **MSI Claw** with gamepad UI navigation, customizable controller bindings, and Quick Access Menu (QAM) integrations. - **Ultra-Low Latency & High Fidelity**: Hardware-accelerated decoding via **Vulkan**, **Metal**, **D3D11VA**, **VAAPI**, **VideoToolbox**, and **AMediaCodec** with full support for HDR, AV1, HEVC, and H.264 codecs. - **Inbuilt QR Code Authentication**: Pair and sign in to PlayStation Network seamlessly using the built-in, offline QR code generator directly inside the Settings and Login dialogs. - **Private Self-Hosted Token Relay**: Full support for self-hosting the authentication relay via `psstream-server` for zero third-party telemetry and complete network sovereignty. - **Seamless Settings Migration**: Automatically discovers and inherits configurations from legacy configurations so previously registered consoles, keys, and bitrate settings carry over instantly. - **Integrated In-App Updates**: Built-in background update checker (`UpdateManager`) in Settings with one-click download, automated package extraction, and stale file cleanup. --- ## Download

   

   

For full release notes, SHA-256 checksums, and all platform packages, visit the Releases Page.

--- ## Installation Guide AstraPlay supports flexible installation methods across every platform, matching standard application store channels and native package managers. ### ⚡ Quick 1-Line Automated Installers (Recommended) Get running immediately with one command in Terminal or PowerShell. These automated installers verify checksums, configure system shortcuts, bypass quarantine/Gatekeeper friction, and enable in-app updates: - **🍏 macOS (Apple Silicon & Intel — Zero Gatekeeper Warnings)**: ```bash /bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nileshchakraborty/AstraPlay/master/scripts/install-macos.sh)" ``` - **🐧 Linux, Steam Deck & Handhelds (Bazzite / SteamOS / Ubuntu / Fedora)**: ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nileshchakraborty/AstraPlay/master/scripts/install-appimage.sh | bash ``` - **🪟 Windows (10 & 11 — PowerShell)**: ```powershell irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nileshchakraborty/AstraPlay/master/scripts/install-windows.ps1 | iex ``` --- ## Detailed Platform Installation ### 🍏 macOS (Apple Silicon & Intel) - **1-Line Terminal Installer (Recommended — Zero Gatekeeper Warnings)**: ```bash /bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nileshchakraborty/AstraPlay/master/scripts/install-macos.sh)" ``` *Why this is recommended on macOS Sonoma & Sequoia*: Files downloaded through `curl` in Terminal are never quarantined by macOS Gatekeeper, avoiding *"Apple could not verify..."* errors completely. Installs to `/Applications`, applies local ad-hoc codesigning, and launches immediately. - **In-App Direct Updates (v2.12.16+)**: AstraPlay includes a built-in background updater in **Settings → Check for Updates**. Updates download lightweight `.zip` application bundles, extract via `ditto` without disk image mount locks, automatically prompt for Touch ID elevation if `/Applications` permissions require it, and restart seamlessly with clean code signatures. - **Direct Disk Image (`.dmg`)**: Download [`AstraPlay-macOS-arm64.dmg`](https://github.com/nileshchakraborty/AstraPlay/releases/latest) (Apple Silicon M1/M2/M3/M4+). - Open the DMG and drag `AstraPlay.app` into `Applications`. - If macOS displays *"Apple could not verify..."*, open **System Settings > Privacy & Security**, scroll down to **Security**, and click **Open Anyway**. - *Legacy Intel Mac Notice*: **v2.12.18** is the final release supporting Intel (`x86_64`) Macs. Intel users can download the final legacy binary from the [v2.12.18 Release](https://github.com/nileshchakraborty/AstraPlay/releases/tag/v2.12.18). All future releases exclusively target Apple Silicon. - **Homebrew Cask (Recommended for macOS — Automated Gatekeeper Bypass)**: Install via our official Homebrew tap. Homebrew automatically removes the quarantine attribute during installation so AstraPlay runs out-of-the-box without Gatekeeper warnings: ```bash brew install --cask nileshchakraborty/astraplay/astraplay ``` Or tap the repository first: ```bash brew tap nileshchakraborty/astraplay brew install --cask astraplay ``` - **Portable ZIP (In-App Updater Compatible)**: Download and extract `AstraPlay-macOS-arm64.zip` directly into `~/Applications`. --- ### 🐧 Linux, Steam Deck & Handhelds (Bazzite / ROG Xbox Ally X / Legion Go / Claw) - **1-Command User Installer (Recommended for Handhelds & Desktop)**: Run our verified installer script in terminal / Konsole. It automatically detects your CPU architecture (`x86_64` or `aarch64`), verifies release SHA-256 checksums, installs desktop menu shortcuts with high-resolution icons, and enables clean in-app updates: ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nileshchakraborty/AstraPlay/master/scripts/install-appimage.sh | bash ``` - **In-App Direct Updates**: AppImage installations update automatically inside the app via **Settings → Check for Updates** without requiring root privileges. Flatpak installations update via Discover or `flatpak update`. - **Direct AppImage**: Download [`AstraPlay-Linux-x86_64.AppImage`](https://github.com/nileshchakraborty/AstraPlay/releases/latest/download/AstraPlay-Linux-x86_64.AppImage), mark it executable, and launch: ```bash chmod +x AstraPlay-Linux-x86_64.AppImage ./AstraPlay-Linux-x86_64.AppImage ``` - **Flathub / Flatpak**: Install via Flatpak from terminal or your desktop software store (Discover / GNOME Software): ```bash flatpak install flathub io.github.nileshchakraborty.AstraPlay flatpak run io.github.nileshchakraborty.AstraPlay ``` - **Portable ZIP with `launch.sh`**: Extract `astraplay-linux-x86_64.zip` and run `./launch.sh`. Bundled libraries and OpenSSL runtime environments are initialized automatically. - **Steam Gaming Mode Setup (Steam Deck & Bazzite)**: 1. Switch to **Desktop Mode**. 2. Open **Steam** and click **Games → Add a Non-Steam Game to My Library...** 3. Select **AstraPlay** (or browse to `~/.local/bin/astraplay` or your extracted `launch.sh`). 4. Return to **Gaming Mode** — AstraPlay is now integrated into your Steam library with full gamepad controls and QAM support. --- ### 🪟 Windows (10 & 11) - **1-Line PowerShell Installer (Recommended)**: ```powershell irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nileshchakraborty/AstraPlay/master/scripts/install-windows.ps1 | iex ``` - **In-App Direct Updates**: Installed setups update automatically via **Settings → Check for Updates** with native UAC elevation and Mark-of-the-Web unblocking. - **Setup Installer (`.exe`)**: Download and run [`astraplay-windows-installer.exe`](https://github.com/nileshchakraborty/AstraPlay/releases/latest/download/astraplay-windows-installer.exe) (or `astraplay-windows-arm64-installer.exe` for Snapdragon / Windows on ARM devices). Follow the setup wizard to customize Start Menu and Desktop shortcuts. - **Windows Package Manager (`winget`)**: ```powershell winget install AstraPlay ``` - **Portable ZIP**: Download and extract [`astraplay-windows-x64.zip`](https://github.com/nileshchakraborty/AstraPlay/releases/latest), then launch `AstraPlay.exe` directly without administrative privileges. --- ### 📱 Android & Android TV - **Google Play Store**: Install directly from the [Google Play Store](https://github.com/nileshchakraborty/AstraPlay/releases/latest) for automatic background updates across phones, tablets, and Android TV / Google TV devices. - **Direct APK Sideload**: Download the latest [`AstraPlay-release.apk`](https://github.com/nileshchakraborty/AstraPlay/releases/latest) from GitHub Releases and open it on your device to install. - **Android TV / Fire TV Wireless Sideloading (ADB)**: Install to your television or streaming device over your local network: ```bash adb connect :5555 adb install -r AstraPlay-release.apk ``` --- ### 🍎 iOS & iPadOS - **Apple App Store / TestFlight**: Download via the [Apple App Store](https://github.com/nileshchakraborty/AstraPlay/releases/latest) or join the TestFlight community channel. - **IPA Sideloading**: Download [`AstraPlay.ipa`](https://github.com/nileshchakraborty/AstraPlay/releases/latest) and install using your preferred sideloading manager: - **AltStore / SideStore**: Add the IPA directly through the on-device AltStore manager. - **Sideloadly**: Connect your iPhone/iPad to a PC or Mac and install with automatic signing. - **LiveContainer / TrollStore**: Install the IPA directly without weekly resign requirements (iOS 14.0–17.0). --- ## Downloads & Supported Packages All release binaries, packages, and SHA-256 checksums are published on the [**GitHub Releases Page**](https://github.com/nileshchakraborty/AstraPlay/releases/latest). | Operating System | Architecture | Available Packages | Description | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Windows** | **x86_64** (Desktop, ROG Xbox Ally X) | [`.exe Setup Installer`](https://github.com/nileshchakraborty/AstraPlay/releases/latest)

[`.aab Play Store Bundle`](https://github.com/nileshchakraborty/AstraPlay/releases/latest) | Sideloadable release APK and Google Play Store App Bundle (`io.github.nileshchakraborty.astraplay`), with native binaries for `arm64-v8a`, `armeabi-v7a`, `x86_64`, and `x86`. | | **iOS / iPadOS** | **ARM64** (iPhone & iPad) | [`.ipa Package`](https://github.com/nileshchakraborty/AstraPlay/releases/latest) | Sideloadable unsigned IPA (AltStore, Sideloadly, LiveContainer, TrollStore) and TestFlight. | The Flathub listing is not published yet. For Steam Deck or Bazzite, use the [AppImage installer script](scripts/install-appimage.sh) to add AstraPlay to the desktop application menu, then add it as a non-Steam game for Gaming Mode. The portable ZIP and its `launch.sh` are another option. See the [Linux installation guide](docs/setup/installation.md) for steps. The Windows `.exe` setup asks whether to create Start Menu and desktop shortcuts (Start Menu is selected by default). The MSI creates a Start Menu shortcut by default; administrators can opt out or add a desktop shortcut with `msiexec /i astraplay-windows-x64.msi CREATE_START_MENU_SHORTCUT=0 CREATE_DESKTOP_SHORTCUT=1`. The standalone `.exe` and portable ZIP do not run an installer or create shortcuts. After installation, launch AstraPlay and use **Pin to taskbar** from its taskbar icon if desired; Windows requires that choice to be made by the user. Windows MSIX packages are being prepared for Microsoft Store distribution; they are not yet a published install option. The on-demand development MSIX is unsigned and intended only for build validation. Store-distributed MSIX updates are managed by Windows; the existing GitHub EXE/MSI installers retain their in-app updater. See [Windows MSIX packaging](packaging/windows-msix/README.md) for the preparation and validation steps. --- ## Features & Capabilities ### Console Discovery & Remote Play - **Local Network Broadcast**: Automatic discovery of PS4 and PS5 consoles on local networks via standard discovery protocols, with active multi-interface subnet broadcast routing on macOS, Linux, and Windows. - **PIN Pairing**: Fast pairing using the official PlayStation Remote Play registration PIN. - **Internet Remote Play**: Connect to your home consoles over WAN and mobile networks with port forwarding or UPnP. ### Video & Audio Performance - **Codec Support**: AV1, HEVC (H.265), and H.264 streaming up to 1080p @ 60 FPS (and PS5 Pro dynamic resolutions). - **Hardware Decoders**: - Windows: D3D11VA, Direct3D12, Vulkan - macOS & iOS: Apple VideoToolbox (Metal-backed) - Linux: VAAPI, VDPAU, Vulkan Video - Android: Android MediaCodec (AMediaCodec NDK) - **Contrast Adaptive Sharpening (CAS) & Upscaling**: In-stream sharpness quick toggle on Desktop QML HUD supporting FidelityFX CAS and EWA Lanczos Sharp shaders. - **Aspect Ratio Presets**: Flexible aspect ratio controls across Desktop, Android, and iOS supporting **Fit (16:9)**, **Fill / 16:10** (ideal for Steam Deck and handhelds), **20:9** (modern smartphones), **Zoom**, and **Stretch**. - **Dynamic Bitrate & Congestion Control**: Adaptive bitrate scaling heuristics in `libchiaki` that react in real-time to network congestion, packet drops, and RTT spikes to eliminate stuttering. - **Audio Engines & Latency Tuning**: Low-latency audio with SDL, Oboe (Android), CoreAudio (Apple), and PulseAudio / PipeWire (Linux). Configurable audio latency buffer size tuning (Ultra-Low, Low, Balanced, High) across mobile and desktop. - **In-Stream Microphone Mute**: Quick toggle to mute or unmute microphone pass-through on the fly during active streaming sessions. ### Controller & Input Support - **DualSense & DualShock 4**: Full support for haptic feedback, adaptive triggers, motion sensors (gyro/accelerometer), and touchpad navigation. - **Controller Battery Indicator**: Real-time battery status HUD overlay displaying charge level and state (Charging, Low, Normal) on Desktop, Android, and iOS. - **Xbox & Handheld Controllers**: Native mapping for Xbox wireless controllers, ROG Ally controls, Steam Deck controls, and third-party XInput / DirectInput controllers with deadzone calibration, stick sensitivity curves, and button remapping. - **Tactile Touch Haptics**: Virtual thumbstick haptic feedback using device vibration motors on Android and iOS when crossing stick thresholds or clicking virtual L3/R3. - **Customizable Virtual Touch Overlay**: Drag-and-drop repositioning with layout persistence, adjustable touch opacity and scale sliders, genre layout presets (Standard, Action/Shooter, RPG), and phone vibrator fallback for mobile grips. - **Touchpad Emulation**: Dedicated DualSense touchpad gesture and tap emulation for mobile controller grips and touch overlays. - **Android App Shortcuts**: Quick 1-tap launcher shortcuts on Android home screens directly into Remote Play and Cloud streaming sessions. --- ## Technical Documentation & Architecture Comprehensive architectural and design documents are available in the repository root: - [**PRD.md**](PRD.md) — Product Requirements Document, platform roadmap, and UX specifications - [**ARCHITECTURE.md**](ARCHITECTURE.md) — Subsystem architecture, cross-platform bridging, and data flow - [**DESIGN.md**](DESIGN.md) — Design systems, UI components, and handheld ergonomics - [**DATA.md**](DATA.md) — Configuration persistence, token management, and data contracts - [**SECURITY.md**](SECURITY.md) — Security guardrails, cryptographic keys, and credential boundaries - [**CODE_STYLE.md**](CODE_STYLE.md) — Engineering standards for C++, Qt/QML, Kotlin, Swift, and CMake - [**TESTING.md**](TESTING.md) — Testing methodologies, automation suites, and device verification - [**AGENTS.md**](AGENTS.md) — Developer operating guide and CI/CD policies --- ## Building from Source ### Prerequisites - **CMake** 3.25+ - **Ninja** build system - **Python** 3.10+ (with `protobuf`) - **Qt 6.6+** (`Core`, `Gui`, `Quick`, `Qml`, `Network`, `Svg`, `Widgets`) - **FFmpeg 6.0+** - **SDL 2.0+** ### Linux / macOS Desktop ```bash git clone --recursive https://github.com/nileshchakraborty/AstraPlay.git cd astraplay cmake -B build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release cmake --build build ``` ### Windows (MSYS2 MinGW64 / ClangARM64) ```bash cmake -B build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release cmake --build build ``` ### Android Build ```bash cd android ./gradlew assembleRelease # Or use the local automated build helper: bash build-local.sh ``` ### iOS / iPadOS Build ```bash bash ios/build.sh ``` --- ## Self-Hosted Token Relay (`psstream-server`) If you prefer to authenticate PlayStation Network accounts entirely within your local network without external cloud services: ```bash cd psstream-server npm install npm start ``` The server provides a local web UI on port `25525` to log in to PSN, capture authorization tokens, and relay them to AstraPlay securely. --- ## Responsible Use AstraPlay is intended for use with games and hardware you legally own and are licensed to access. It does not circumvent digital rights management (DRM), distribute proprietary firmware, or facilitate piracy. AstraPlay is an independent community project and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or certified by Sony Interactive Entertainment Inc. PlayStation, PS4, PS5, DualSense, and DualShock are trademarks or registered trademarks of Sony Interactive Entertainment Inc. --- ## Credits & Acknowledgments AstraPlay is built upon the foundational work of [Chiaki](https://git.sr.ht/~thestr4ng3r/chiaki) and [chiaki-ng](https://github.com/streetpea/chiaki-ng). Heartfelt thanks go to the original Chiaki authors, the chiaki-ng maintainers, and open-source contributors across the handheld gaming ecosystem.

## AstraPlay v2.12.21

Automated multi-device build release from `master` branch.

### ⚡ Quick 1-Line Automated Installation (Recommended)

- **🍏 macOS (Apple Silicon & Intel — Zero Gatekeeper Warnings)**:
  ```bash
  /bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nileshchakraborty/AstraPlay/master/scripts/install-macos.sh)"
  ```
- **🐧 Linux & Handhelds (Steam Deck / Bazzite / Ubuntu / Fedora)**:
  ```bash
  curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nileshchakraborty/AstraPlay/master/scripts/install-appimage.sh | bash
  ```
- **🪟 Windows (10 & 11 — PowerShell)**:
  ```powershell
  irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nileshchakraborty/AstraPlay/master/scripts/install-windows.ps1 | iex
  ```

---

### Platform Binaries & Packages

#### Windows (x86_64 — Desktop & ROG Xbox Ally X)
- **`astraplay-windows-installer.exe`** — Complete Inno Setup installer package
- **`astraplay-windows-x64.exe`** — Standalone 64-bit executable (in-app updater compatible)
- **`astraplay.exe`** — Standalone executable alias
- **`astraplay-windows-x64.zip`** — Portable zip archive with bundled Qt6 runtime libraries

#### Windows (ARM64 — Snapdragon X Elite, Surface Pro & WoA)
- **`astraplay-windows-arm64-installer.exe`** — Native Windows ARM64 Inno Setup installer
- **`astraplay-windows-arm64.exe`** — Native ARM64 standalone executable
- **`astraplay-windows-arm64.zip`** — Native ARM64 portable zip archive with bundled libraries

#### macOS (Apple Silicon — M1 / M2 / M3 / M4)
- **1-Line Terminal Install (Recommended)**: `/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nileshchakraborty/AstraPlay/master/scripts/install-macos.sh)"`
- **`AstraPlay-macOS-arm64.dmg`** / **`AstraPlay-macOS.dmg`** — Standard disk image installer
- **`AstraPlay-macOS-arm64.zip`** / **`AstraPlay-macOS.zip`** — Portable application bundle (in-app updater compatible)

#### macOS (Intel — x86_64)
- **1-Line Terminal Install (Recommended)**: `/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nileshchakraborty/AstraPlay/master/scripts/install-macos.sh)"`
- **`AstraPlay-macOS-x86_64.dmg`** — Standard Intel Mac disk image installer
- **`AstraPlay-macOS-x86_64.zip`** — Native Intel Mac application bundle (in-app updater compatible)

> [!TIP]
> **macOS Installation & Gatekeeper Note (Community Open-Source Build)**:
> - **Fastest 1-Liner (Recommended)**: `/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nileshchakraborty/AstraPlay/master/scripts/install-macos.sh)"` (downloads via curl, zero Gatekeeper friction, installs to `/Applications`, and opens automatically).
> - **Manual Drag & Drop (System Settings Bypass)**: Drag AstraPlay to Applications. If prompted with *"Apple could not verify..."*, open **System Settings > Privacy & Security**, scroll down to **Security**, and click **Open Anyway**.

#### Linux (x86_64 — SteamOS, Bazzite, ROG Xbox Ally X Linux & Desktop)
- **`AstraPlay-Linux-x86_64.AppImage`** — Standalone AppImage executable
- **`AstraPlay-Linux-x86_64.zip`** — Steam-compatible portable zip with `launch.sh` and bundled libs

#### Linux (ARM64 / aarch64 — Raspberry Pi 5, ARM SBCs & Handhelds)
- **`AstraPlay-Linux-aarch64.AppImage`** — Native ARM64 AppImage executable
- **`AstraPlay-Linux-aarch64.zip`** — Native ARM64 portable zip with bundled libs

#### Android (Phones, Tablets & Handhelds)
- **`AstraPlay-Android.apk`** — Sideloadable APK package
- **`AstraPlay-Android.aab`** — Google Play Store App Bundle

repos.name: kura
repos.description: Scan, identify, organize, and transfer your PS1-PS5 & Vita game library (Windows, macOS, Linux), with a bundled PS5 payload for installs, cheats, saves, and fan control
repos.readme: # Kura [![Latest Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/NookieAI/kura?label=latest&color=2ea44f)](https://github.com/NookieAI/kura/releases/latest) [![Downloads](https://img.shields.io/github/downloads/NookieAI/kura/total?color=2ea44f)](https://github.com/NookieAI/kura/releases) Kura is a free application that scans your drives, identifies every PlayStation game you own, and helps you organise, transfer, and install them — across PS1, PS2, PSP, PS3, PS4, PS5, and PS Vita, in a single library. No installer. No login. No account. Native builds for Windows, macOS (Apple Silicon + Intel), and Linux. ## Download Download the latest build for your platform from the [Releases](https://github.com/NookieAI/kura/releases/latest) page and run it — no installation, no administrator rights, no Node.js. Windows: `kura.exe` · macOS: `Kura-x.x.x-arm64.dmg` / `Kura-x.x.x-x64.dmg` · Linux: `Kura-x.x.x.AppImage`. Each release also includes `kura-loader.elf`, the Kura Loader payload for PS5 (see [Kura Loader](#kura-loader) below). ## Features - **Reads inside the files.** Kura parses the PKG header, the ISO9660 directory, the SFO metadata, the ZIP central directory, and the CSO sector index to extract the real title, title ID, versions, content ID, region, required firmware, SDK version, parental level, sizes, and cover art — and keeps the complete SFO / `param.json` so nothing is dropped. `FF7-REMAKE-PS4-FIXED-FIXED2.pkg` is identified as *Final Fantasy VII Remake*. - **Every PlayStation in one library.** PS1 disc images, PS2 ECM dumps, PSP UMDs and CSOs, PS3 JB folders and PKGs, PS4 fpkg/exFAT backups, PS5 folder installs, and PS Vita VPKs — the same library, filters, and workflow throughout. - **Library insights.** Built-in Stats views chart your collection — a Genome Map of connected franchises, Completion Constellations that reveal which numbered sequels you're missing, and health, storage, and curator overviews. - **Fast scanning.** Drives scan in parallel, and compressed formats use partial decompression (reading only the sectors needed for metadata), so a 1.8 GB CSO scans about as quickly as a plain ISO. - **Structural identification.** Games are classified by format-defined fields — the SFO TITLE_ID prefix, the PNG icon signature, the BOOT line in SYSTEM.CNF — not by filename. - **Layout presets.** Built-in presets for Itemzflow, webMAN, etaHEN, Dump Runner, GoldHEN, and others, plus a custom rename builder. - **Direct console transfer.** Transfer over FTP straight to the console and install packages through the correct endpoint for your firmware. PS5 transfers respect the PS5 FTP daemon's throttling to avoid stalls. - **Duplicate detection.** Groups the same game across drives, versions, and regions (by content ID, version, and region) and shows the differences side by side. ## Kura Loader Kura Loader is the companion PS5 payload, distributed as `kura-loader.elf` and included with every release. It is a single, self-contained ELF: one payload to load on a jailbroken PS5 that provides a web dashboard together with a complete jailbreak toolset, with no additional downloads. The desktop application communicates with it over the local network to enable Kura's PS5 features. When you connect a jailbroken PS5 that does not yet have it, Kura can fetch, push, and launch `kura-loader.elf` automatically. You can also trigger this on demand from **Menu → Set up my PS5**. ### ShadowMountPlus Kura Loader bundles and manages [ShadowMountPlus](https://github.com/drakmor/shadowMountPlus) by Drakmor, a mount engine that allows the PS5 to run titles directly from external, USB, or network storage without first copying them to the internal SSD. Mount a game to play it, and unmount it when finished — a practical way to maintain a large library on a console with limited internal space. Kura keeps ShadowMountPlus updated to the latest build. ### Included tools A jailbreak toolset in a single payload, operated from the dashboard or the desktop application: - **Installation** — PKG install and upload, URL-push install, disc and folder installs, and tile auto-install, for both PS4 and PS5 packages. - **Game library and app dumper** — reads the console's own database for real titles, and can dump installed games back out. - **Cheats and patches** — a built-in cheats engine (1,500+ cheats) and game patches (370+), with optional auto-fetch. - **Save manager** — back up and restore game saves (Garlic save-manager integration). - **Fan control and thermals** — live CPU temperature, custom fan curves, and silent / balanced / aggressive presets. - **Avatar maker** — set custom PSN profile avatars. - **Network tools** — LAN auto-discovery (mDNS), SMB shares, nanoDNS, and network diagnostics. - **Plugins and kernel log** — load plugins and stream the live kernel log for debugging. - **Health and recovery** — process monitor, crash logs, safe mode, and a built-in `elfldr` so Kura can relaunch the payload if it stops. ### Dashboard Open the dashboard from Kura (**Menu → Kura Dashboard**) or in any browser at `http://:8535/`. It provides a live view of the console — temperatures and fan, memory and storage, processes, library, installs, cheats, patches, save manager, network, and logs — updated in real time. ### Requirements and setup - Included with each [release](https://github.com/NookieAI/kura/releases/latest) as `kura-loader.elf`; the automatic setup in the app keeps it current. - Requires a jailbroken PS5 on compatible firmware with a payload loader (for example, etaHEN). Open the console from Kura, or let the automatic setup handle it. - A full walkthrough is available in the app under **Menu → Help & Guide → "Set up your PS5"**. PS5 console features are optional; the desktop application's scanning, organisation, and metadata features run without them. ### Credits Kura Loader builds on the work of the PS5 homebrew community, most notably [ShadowMountPlus](https://github.com/drakmor/shadowMountPlus) by Drakmor and the wider ps5-payload-dev ecosystem. Thanks to everyone who develops and shares these tools. ## Supported formats ISO, BIN/CUE, IMG, CHD, CSO/ZSO, ECM, PBP, PKG (PS3/PS4/PS5), fpkg, exFAT game images, folder dumps, VPK, and compressed archives (ZIP, RAR, 7z) — scanned in place using partial decompression. ## Privacy Core operation is fully offline. The only optional online requests are cover-art and GameDB lookups, which you initiate. There is no telemetry, no account, and no background connectivity. ## Platform Windows (`.exe`), macOS Apple Silicon (`arm64.dmg`), macOS Intel (`x64.dmg`), and Linux (`.AppImage`). All builds are portable — no installation required. ### macOS — first-launch note Kura is not yet signed with an Apple Developer certificate. On macOS 13+ you may see **"Kura is damaged and can't be opened"** when you first try to launch it. This is Gatekeeper blocking an unsigned download — the app is not actually damaged. **Fix:** open Terminal and run: ``` xattr -cr /Applications/Kura.app ``` Then launch Kura normally. You only need to do this once. ## Links - In-app Help & Guide (**Menu → Help & Guide**) — full walkthrough, layouts, console setup, and troubleshooting. - [Issues](https://github.com/NookieAI/kura/issues) — bug reports and feature requests. - Discord — the invite link is available from the **Discord** button in the application. --- Kura is built and maintained by Nookie.

![Kura — one library for every PlayStation](https://github.com/NookieAI/kura/releases/download/v1.6.51/kura-hero.png)

**Kura** is a free application that scans your drives, identifies every PlayStation game you own, and helps you organise, transfer, and install them — across **PS1, PS2, PSP, PS3, PS4, PS5, and PS Vita**, in a single library. It reads *inside* each file for the real title, cover art, and metadata (not the filename), finds duplicates, organises for any console layout, and installs straight to your console.

No installer. No login. No account. Native builds for **Windows, macOS (Apple Silicon + Intel), and Linux** — plus the `kura-loader-ps5.elf` PS5 payload and the `kura-loader-ps4.elf` PS4 payload.

![Kura — one library for every PlayStation, current view](https://github.com/NookieAI/kura/releases/download/v1.6.51/kura-screenshot.png)

## What's new in 1.6.51

### Reliability — async poll overlap fixes
- **Seven async poll overlap fixes in the desktop app.** Go-progress, install-progress, BGFT-progress, catalogue-poll, multi-source scan, log-stream timer and install-active re-entry all had race windows where a second poll could fire before the first returned — producing duplicate entries, stale state or silent failures. Each now has a busy guard or settled flag that prevents overlap.

### PS5 loader — 20r244
- Updated from 20r206 to 20r244 — includes all improvements made since the last app release.
- Deploy error reporting: network and HTTP errors are now surfaced in the deploy terminal output instead of failing silently.
- CSRF shim for the deploy page.

### PS4 loader — 20r107
- Fixed variable shadow warning in the accept loop (char array shadowing an int).
- Removed dead code branch in save listing.

### Security
- **XSS audit fix** — one innerHTML path in the Electron app was tightened during a comprehensive security review.
- Full security audit of both the app and both loader codebases confirmed clean: no eval/new Function, CSRF fails closed, path traversal guarded, shell.openExternal validates protocol, Electron sandbox properly configured.

---
*Bundles Kura Loader PS5 20r244 and PS4 20r107. Made by Nookie.*

repos.name: NX-Controller-Tester
repos.description: Nintendo Switch homebrew (.nro) to test your controllers: Joy-Con, DualShock 3 (PS3), DualShock 4 (PS4), DualSense (PS5) and PS1/PS2 controllers via the SuperBox 3 USB adapter. Buttons, sticks, drift, triggers, battery, rumble.
repos.readme:
# Controller Tester — Nintendo Switch

**Joy-Con · DualShock 3 (PS3) · DualShock 4 (PS4) · DualSense (PS5) · PS1 / PS2 (via SuperBox 3)**

**By Not_eFootballer**

Nintendo Switch homebrew (`.nro`) to test your controllers in real time. It runs from the Homebrew Menu, needs no sysmodule, and changes nothing on the console.

## Features

- **Controller**: every button, the D-pad, the sticks (X/Y values and %), the triggers, the battery, rumble (left, right, both) and the motion sensors.
- **Drift**: stick trails, ×10 center zoom, 3-second resting measurement with a verdict, circularity test.
- **USB**: diagnostics for controllers plugged in over USB.

## Tested controllers

| Controller | Connection |
|---|---|
| Joy-Con | Bluetooth / rail |
| DualShock 3 (PS3) | USB cable |
| DualShock 4 (PS4) | USB cable |
| DualSense (PS5) | USB cable |
| PS1 / PS2 | **SuperBox 3** USB adapter |

### PS1 / PS2 controllers

PlayStation 1 and 2 controllers have no USB port, so you need an adapter. Plug the controller into a **SuperBox 3**, then plug the SuperBox 3 into the Switch (into the dock, or through a USB-C OTG adapter in handheld mode). The app detects it automatically and shows the controller with the PlayStation layout.

### PS3 / PS4 / PS5 controllers

Just plug them in with a USB cable: they work in the app right away, even though the Switch doesn't support them on its own.

## Installation

1. Download `NXControllerTester.nro` from the **Releases**.
2. Copy it to `sd:/switch/NXControllerTester/`.
3. Open the Homebrew Menu (ideally by holding **R** while launching a game) and start **Controller Tester**.

## Controls

Hold **+** (or **−**), then:

| Button | Action |
|---|---|
| L / R | Previous / next page |
| Up / Down | Choose the displayed controller |
| A | Full rumble test |
| ← / → | Left / right motor |
| X | Resting drift measurement |
| Y | Reset statistics |
| **B held for 1 s** | **Quit** (or press HOME twice) |

The touchscreen also works for the tabs, the controller list and rumble.

Tested on firmware 21.0.1 with Atmosphère 1.10.1.
