repos.readme:
# PS5 Web File Manager A file manager for PS5 with a web UI. It is primarily intended for quickly and safely copying game dump folders from USB storage to internal storage. ## Brief PS5 web file manager payload. It runs an HTTP UI starting at port `8888`, registers a home screen launcher in the Media category on startup, and provides file operations from the PS5 browser or another browser on the same network. If `8888` is already in use, the payload tries the next port until one is available; the startup notification and home screen launcher use the actual listen port. ## Screenshots

## Features - List files and folders. - Sort the list by name, type, size, modified time, or permissions. The selected sort mode is saved in browser local storage. - Change read/write/execute permissions from the permissions column, using checkboxes or a validated four-digit octal mode. - Copy, move, delete, rename, create files, and create folders. - Edit UTF-8 text files up to 1 MiB using the built-in plain text editor. - Multi-select operations. - Copy/move by choosing sources first, then pasting or moving them into the current folder. - Conflict prompts for overwriting files and merging folders. - Extract archive files ending with `.7z`, `.001`, `.zip`, `.zipx`, `.rar`, `.part01.rar`, `.arj`, `.bz2`, `.bzip2`, `.tbz`, `.tbz2`, `.cab`, `.gz`, `.gzip`, `.tgz`, `.tpz`, `.lzh`, `.lha`, `.tar`, `.xz`, `.txz`, `.z`, `.taz`, `.zst`, `.tzst`, `.xar`, `.xip`, `.cpio`, `.lzma`, `.pmd`. Extraction requires the separately distributed [`wfm-7zip-helper.elf` helper](https://github.com/owendswang/wfm-7zip-helper) at `/data/wfm/wfm-7zip-helper.elf`. - Upload single files, multiple files, or folders from a remote browser using the file picker or full-page drag and drop. Upload is hidden in the PS5 browser because it is intended for another device on the network. - Download selected items individually: files download directly, and each folder downloads as its own `.tar` archive. Download is hidden in the PS5 browser. - Full-screen task overlay with delayed display, progress, speed, ETA, cancel support, and task recovery after reopening the browser while the payload process is still running. - Copied/moved files and folders are set to `0777` where the filesystem supports Unix permissions. FAT/exFAT-style filesystems may ignore chmod. - Uploaded files are written through temporary files and are renamed into place after the upload completes. - Chinese and English UI. The browser language is read from `navigator.languages` / `navigator.language`; Chinese uses `zh`, everything else uses English. - Responsive layout for narrow mobile browsers, including wrapped toolbars and horizontally scrollable file lists. - Startup notification showing the app name, version, and listen port. - Home screen launcher icon and browser favicon use the same embedded `icon0.png` data in the PS5 build to avoid storing the icon twice in the ELF. - Create/edit text files ending with `.txt`, `.json`, `.xml`, `.ini`, `.cfg`, `.conf`, `.md`, `.log`, `.lua`, `.js`, `.css`, `.html`, `.htm`, `.c`, `.h`, `.cpp`, `.hpp`, `.sh`, `.csv`, `.yaml`, `.yml`, `.shn`. - Preview image files ending with `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.gif`, `.bmp`, `.webp`. - Install/Preview PKG files ends with `.pkg`. - Launch payload files ending with `.elf` by sending them to the ELF loader at `localhost:9021` after confirmation. - Toggle the PS5 browser between fullscreen and its ordinary layout from the top-right button. The browser reopens the current folder. ## Build It depends on PS5 payload SDK first: [ps5-payload-dev/sdk](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk#quick-start) ```sh export PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK=/opt/ps5-payload-sdk ``` Initialize the pinned dependencies with `git submodule update --init --recursive`. This project uses `libmicrohttpd` for HTTP and `libsmb2` for SMB. `make` checks for `libmicrohttpd` before building and runs the installer script automatically if it is missing: ```sh make ``` If the build host has no network access, download the libmicrohttpd source tarball yourself and run the dependency installer once: ```sh LIBMICROHTTPD_TARBALL=/path/to/libmicrohttpd-1.0.1.tar.gz \ ./install-libmicrohttpd.sh ``` Then build again: ```sh make ``` The output is: ```text web-file-mgr.elf ``` For local browser/UI testing on Linux: ```sh make linux ./web-file-mgr-linux ``` The Linux build does not include the PS5 home screen installer. ## Usage Start an ELF loader on the PS5. The common listener port is `9021`. Send the built payload with netcat or NetCat GUI: ```sh export PS5_HOST=ps5_ip_address nc -q0 "$PS5_HOST" 9021 < web-file-mgr.elf ``` After the payload starts, the PS5 notification shows the app name, version, and actual listen port. Open the shown URL in the PS5 browser, for example: ```text http://${PS5_IP_ADDRESS}:8888/ ``` On startup the payload registers a `PS5 Web File Manager` web shortcut in the Media category. Missing launcher files are written; existing icons and names are preserved. Only the loopback URL in `param.json` is updated to the actual listen port, including fallback ports such as `8889`. ## Notes - Copy, move, delete, upload, and download run as single background tasks. While one task is running, other file operations are rejected. - Delete is recursive and permanent. There is no recycle bin. - Copy/move tasks can be canceled. A partially copied single file is removed, but partially copied folders are left in place to avoid deleting existing files when merging into an existing target folder. - Upload tasks can be canceled. A partially uploaded temporary file is removed when possible. - Selected files download individually, and each selected folder produces its own tar stream. The tar archives are generated by the payload and are not written to PS5 storage first. - The UI can recover the active task display if the browser is closed and reopened while the payload process is still running. - Text editing is limited to common text-file extensions. Non-UTF-8 and oversized files are rejected. - File names are transmitted as UTF-8 through the web API. The payload also attempts to preserve legacy byte-oriented names returned by mounted filesystems so mixed USB filename encodings can still be displayed and operated on. ## FAQ - The optional fullscreen button patches browser layout in RAM; it does not replace system files. - If you are using P2JB and this payload causes a kernel panic, avoid using it with that setup. Stability matters more than convenience when each retry takes a long time. - The preparing stage may calculate folder size and check available space. It can be slow when a folder contains many files, but it helps prevent starting a copy, move, upload, or download operation that cannot be completed safely. ## Credits This project was built with reference to these projects: - **[ps5-payload-dev/websrv](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/websrv):** HTTP server structure, static asset embedding ideas, PS5 browser/websrv behavior and PKG install function. SMB connection/authentication and SMB PKG installation reference. License: GPLv3+. - **[itsPLK/ps5-pkg-manager](https://github.com/itsPLK/ps5-pkg-manager):** HTTP PKG streaming, byte-range handling and installation metadata/icon URL reference. License: GPLv3. - **[ps5-payload-dev/ftpsrv](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/ftpsrv):** PS5 payload conventions, home screen launcher/install flow reference, process handling style and startup installation reference. License: GPLv3+. - **[seregonwar/zftpd](https://github.com/seregonwar/zftpd):** PS5 TCP socket buffer tuning and high-throughput transfer behavior reference. License: MIT. - **[itsPLK/ps5-payload-manager](https://github.com/itsPLK/ps5-payload-manager):** Payload building behavior and native browser launch reference. License: GPLv3. - **[owendswang/ps5-web-browser-fullscreen](https://github.com/owendswang/ps5-web-browser-fullscreen):** Browser fullscreen/restore implementation, including test-mode discovery and INI diagnostics. License: GPLv3+. - **[libmicrohttpd](https://ftp.gnu.org/gnu/libmicrohttpd/):** Used as the embedded HTTP server library. It is licensed by GNU under the LGPL; this payload links it as the SDK-provided static library. - **[libsmb2](https://github.com/sahlberg/libsmb2):** SMB2/3 client library. License: LGPLv2.1. - **[ps5-payload-dev/sdk](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk):** Payload building foundation. License: GPLv3+. - **[etaHEN](https://github.com/etaHEN/etaHEN):** ShellUI URI navigation used to return to the PS5 home screen before exit. License: GPLv3. - **[ezremote](https://github.com/cy33hc/ps5-ezremote-client):** Preview PKG info. License: GPLv2. ## License The project is distributed under GPLv3 or later, matching the GPLv3+ projects used as implementation references. See `LICENSE`. Third-party projects retain their own licenses. Do not copy assets or source from the credited projects into another distribution without preserving the corresponding license notices. If distributing binaries, comply with the LGPL terms for libmicrohttpd and libsmb2 in addition to this project's GPL license.

repos.readme:
# ESP32 PS5 WebKit Autoloader

A compact HTTP/HTTPS host for the PS5 WebKit Autoloader, packaged as 4 MB flash images for ESP32-PICO, ESP32-S2, ESP32-S3 and ESP32-C3 boards. All targets use LittleFS and do not require PSRAM.

The web content in `autoloader/` is based on a modified version of the [`ps5-webkit-autoloader`](https://github.com/itsPLK/ps5-webkit-autoloader) frontend. Its bundled [`slopkit`](https://github.com/itsPLK/slopkit), [`ps5-unified-autoloader`](https://github.com/owendswang/ps5-unified-autoloader/tree/feat/install-webkit-shortcut) components also contain project-specific modifications and therefore do not exactly match upstream.

## Firmware Version Supports

- poops        7.00 - 12.00
- relapse      7.00 - 13.60 (except 9.05 and 11.40)

You could choose to use poops or relapse if your FW supports both methods while caching. It would use Poops by default if you don't choose.

## Usage

1. [Download](/releases) and Flash the appropriate firmware for your device model with [`Flash Download Tool`](https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-test-tools/en/latest/esp32/production_stage/tools/flash_download_tool.html) or [`Online ESP Tool`](https://espressif.github.io/esptool-js/).
2. Plug the ESP32 into the USB port of PS5 or any other nearby. It only needs power supply and shouldn't be too far for Wi-Fi connection.
3. Connect the PS5 to the `ESP32_PORTAL` Wi-Fi network using the password `12345678`.
4. Open **Settings → Guide & Tips ... → Guide & Tips → User's Guide**.
5. Wait for the installation and caching process to finish. Do not disconnect the ESP32 while it is still running.
6. On success, Payload Manager opens automatically and a **WebKit Autoloader** shortcut appears in the **Media** section of the home screen.

After a successful installation, the web content is cached on the PS5. On subsequent boots, launch **WebKit Autoloader** directly from the Media section.

A network connection is still **REQUIRED** to complete the `Relapse` exploit process, as the exploit method relies on the PS5 having an active network interface and IP address. Internet access itself is not required. `Poops` method doesn't need that.

If an attempt fails, follow the on-screen instruction to reboot and try again. If the console freezes, crashes, or powers off, turn it back on and retry. Use this project at your own risk.

## Requirements

- Arduino CLI
- Arduino ESP32 core 2.0.11
- ~~Arduino ESP8266 core 3.1.2 (required for `make 8266`)~~

Install the Arduino CLI and required core:

```sh
./install-deps.sh
```

## Build

```sh
make
```

The default ESP32-S2/S3/C3/PICO firmware leaves native USB disconnected, so the board only draws power from its USB connection. Build the separate debug variant to enable USB CDC/Serial-JTAG output:

```sh
make debug
```

Debug firmware is written to `build/debug/`. For the ESP32-S2 alone, use `make debug-s2`. To timestamp every serial line from 00:00:00, run `python serial_timestamp.py COM4 115200` (requires pyserial).

DNS resolves `manuals.playstation.net`, `ena.net.playstation.net` and `www.msftconnecttest.com` to the ESP32; other names receive NXDOMAIN. The build creates a modified copy of Arduino ESP32 2.0.11's DNSServer under ignored `build/` using `prepare-dns-library.py`. That library retains its [upstream LGPL-2.1 license](https://github.com/espressif/arduino-esp32/blob/2.0.11/LICENSE.md).

The build copies `autoloader/` to a temporary `data/` directory, compresses the web assets, and creates:

- `build/pico/esp32-arduino.pico.merged.bin`: Intended to support generic ESP32-PICO series boards.
- `build/s2/esp32-arduino.s2.merged.bin`: Intended to support ESP32-S2 series boards.
- `build/s3/esp32-arduino.s3.merged.bin`: Intended to support ESP32-S3 series boards.
- `build/c3/esp32-arduino.c3.merged.bin`: Intended to support ESP32-C3 series boards.

Use `make pico`, `make s2`, `make s3`, `make c3`~~, `make 8266`~~, or `make clean` to build an individual target or clean generated files. ~~The ESP-12F target uses the Generic ESP8266 4 MB / 3 MB LittleFS layout and produces `build/8266/esp8266-arduino.esp12f.merged.bin`.~~

## Manifest updates

ESP32 serves `.appcache`, `.manifest`, and `.cache` files over HTTP and HTTPS
with a random 16-digit hexadecimal `# VERSION` comment generated once per boot
and HTTP no-cache headers. Resource lists are preserved; the generated version
is not written to flash. Manifests remain uncompressed in LittleFS.

## Credits

- [itsPLK/ps5-webkit-autoloader](https://github.com/itsPLK/ps5-webkit-autoloader)
- [itsPLK/ps5-unified-autoloader](https://github.com/itsPLK/ps5-unified-autoloader)
- [jordyidk/slopkit](https://github.com/jordyidk/slopkit)
- [ntfargo/Relapse-Exploit](https://github.com/ntfargo/Relapse-Exploit)

Credit also belongs to all projects, researchers, and developers referenced by these upstream projects.

repos.description: This is a full build of KB-RPCS3 source code with changes and new features.
repos.readme:
# RPCS3-5

RPCS3, the PS3 emulator, running natively on jailbroken PS5 consoles. It plays PS3 discs straight from the PS5's disc drive.

Built on [KB-RPCS3](https://github.com/kamb205/KB-RPCS3) v0.1.0-alpha. Latest: **v1.2.2 Beta**.

## Features
- Plays PS3 discs from the PS5's drive (Redump keys come as a separate download), as well as `.iso` files, game folders and PSN `.pkg` files
- The PS5 ejects the disc normally after you play, with no console restart
- Per-game settings
- One-command installer that works over the PS5 Upload app or FTP, with any console IP
- Diagnostic tools: helper and disc probes, log and FPS readers

## Tested
| Game | Status |
|---|---|
| Call of Duty: World at War (BLUS30192) | Plays |
| Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3 (BLUS30838) | Plays at 1280x720, mostly 45–60 FPS |

Tested on a PS5 Slim, firmware 13.60.

## Requirements
- A jailbroken PS5
- etaHEN
- kstuff lite
- ShadowMountPlus
- Your own `PS3UPDAT.PUP`

## Install
1. Download both zips from Releases, put them in one folder and extract the app zip there.
2. Open the PS5 Upload app and connect it to the PS5, or turn on etaHEN's FTP server (port 1337).
3. Run `.\Install-RPCS3-5.ps1 -Ps5 <PS5 IP>` in PowerShell.
4. On the PS5, go to RPCS3-5 > Install > PS3 firmware. Then, in Settings, set Clocks scale to 100 and Frame limit to Auto.

## Notes
- Swap discs only from the RPCS3-5 home screen.
- Call of Duty games: set the in-game resolution to 1280x720.
- This is beta software. Use it on your own consoles only and don't redistribute builds: KB-RPCS3's author asks this because the GPL-2.0-only RPCS3 core is combined with GPL-3.0 components.

## Credits
kamb205 (KB-RPCS3) · RPCS3 team · Mihawk (PS5 Vulkan driver, Mesa, payload SDK, LLVM)

latestRelease.name: Release 1.2.2 Beta  (Fixes)
latestRelease.body:
RPCS3-5 v1.2.2 Beta

*Smooth disc play.* The hitch every ~15 seconds when playing from the PS5's disc drive is gone. Modern Warfare 3 now plays at 1280x720, mostly at 45–60 FPS.

 ⚠️ **Beta, for your own jailbroken PS5 only.** RPCS3-5 is built on KB-RPCS3 v0.1.0-alpha. Its author asks that builds aren't shared, because RPCS3's GPL-2.0-only core is combined with GPL-3.0 PS5 components. Expect some crashes.

What's new

 Fixed
- **No more freeze every ~15 seconds while playing from the disc.** 1.2.1 released the drive whenever nothing had read it for 2 seconds. A game pauses its reading all the time, so the drive kept closing, and every next read had to open and spin it up again. That caused a hitch of a second or more, over and over.
  - The disc helper (**version 15**) now keeps the drive while a game is reading from it, and releases it 2 seconds after the game's last connection closes.
  - The disc still ejects once you're back on the RPCS3-5 home screen.
  - In Modern Warfare 3, 7 minutes of play went from a freeze every ~15 seconds to 2 slow disc reads, both during loading.

 Added
- **Slow-read logging:** any disc read that takes 200 ms or more is written to `ps5-boot.log` as `disc: slow read`. That way a disc hitch can be told apart from other stutter.
- **`tools/kb-loggrep-fps.elf`:** prints the current session's frame-rate history back to the PC.

Changed
- Disc helper version 15. RPCS3-5 replaces older helpers by itself when it starts, and `kb-helper-quit.elf` now retires any helper below version 15.
- App version `01.220.000`.

## Tested on RPCS3-5
PS5 Slim, firmware 13.60, games played from the disc drive.

| Game | ID | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3 | BLUS30838 | **Plays** at 1280x720: mostly 45–60 FPS in game, with occasional short stutters. At 1920x1080 it stops right at boot. |
| Call of Duty: World at War | BLUS30192 | **Plays** (since 1.2). Intros and menus run at 60 FPS. |

 Downloads

| File | Size | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `RPCS3-5-v1.2.2-beta.zip` | 90.7 MB | App, installer, tools and README (**required**) |
| `RPCS3-5-v1.2.2-beta-redump-keys.zip` | 1.2 MB | 4,460 Redump disc keys, needed to play PS3 discs from the drive |
| `SHA256SUMS.txt` | — | Checksums of both zips |

 Requirements
- Jailbroken PS5 (tested on a PS5 Slim, firmware 13.60)
- etaHEN (its ELF loader on port 9021 starts the disc helper)
- kstuff lite, loaded once per boot
- ShadowMountPlus
- Your own PS3 firmware, `PS3UPDAT.PUP` (not included)

 Install or update
1. Open the PS5 Upload app on your PC and connect it to the PS5, or turn on etaHEN's FTP server (port 1337).
2. Put both zips in one folder and extract the app zip there.
3. In PowerShell, from that folder, run:
   ```powershell
   .\Install-RPCS3-5.ps1 -Ps5 <your PS5's IP>
   ```

Updating from any earlier version:** close RPCS3-5 on the PS5 first, then run the installer. Games, saves and settings are kept, and the new helper takes over the next time RPCS3-5 opens.

Tips
- **Call of Duty:** set the resolution to 1280x720 in the game's own settings (Video > Resolution).
- **Swap discs only from the RPCS3-5 home screen.** If you swapped a disc in rest mode and RPCS3-5 says to restart, restart the console with the new disc inserted.
- **Check the helper:** run `.\tools\send-elf.ps1 -Elf .\tools\kb-helper-probe.elf`. A healthy result reports `version 15` and `disc OK`.

 Known issues
- Occasional short stutters in heavy scenes: the PS5's CPU is busy running the game's SPU code.
- Swapping a disc while a game is running isn't supported.
- A disc swapped in rest mode needs a console restart.
- RADV wait/spin figures in the timing log always read 0.
- `main_thread.eh_frame: Invalid function` at boot is a harmless RPCS3 analyser warning.

 Checksums (SHA-256)
```
ec3c2192ed699a0624dabfdd7f7fb77d6ae7f86b2782f07d375141ef38011dbf  RPCS3-5-v1.2.2-beta.zip
08e8d17a16bcdc4c9599f4153ceee7b1d43c07ec91bb4b42470c8b11a1d0e991  RPCS3-5-v1.2.2-beta-redump-keys.zip
```

Credits
- **kamb205**: [[KB-RPCS3](https://github.com/kamb205/KB-RPCS3)](https://github.com/kamb205/KB-RPCS3)
- **RPCS3 team**: [[the emulator](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3)](https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3)
- **Mihawk (mihawk-99)**: PS5 Vulkan driver, Mesa, payload SDK, LLVM

repos.readme:
# PS5 Notify (Android)

**Estado: beta.** PS5 Notify reenvía a la PS5 las notificaciones de las aplicaciones que selecciones en el móvil. La app recibe las notificaciones en tiempo real y, además, puede volver a consultar periódicamente las notificaciones que Android mantiene activas.

## Configuración

1. Instala el APK generado por GitHub Actions: pestaña **Actions** -> último **Build APK** -> **Artifacts** -> `ps5-notify-apk`.
2. Transfiere el archivo `notify-bridge.elf` a la PS5 usando el método de transferencia disponible en tu configuración.
3. Abre **Payload Manager** en la PS5, selecciona `notify-bridge.elf` y ejecútalo como payload. El bridge debe estar ejecutándose para que la PS5 reciba los mensajes.
4. En PS5 Notify, introduce la IP de la PS5 y el puerto del receptor. El puerto predeterminado es `9055`.
5. El token predeterminado es `ps5notify`. No lo cambies: debe coincidir con el token del `notify-bridge.elf`. El campo aparece bloqueado en la app.
6. Pulsa **Conceder acceso a notificaciones** y autoriza PS5 Notify en los ajustes de Android.
7. Selecciona las aplicaciones que quieras reenviar y guarda la configuración.
8. Usa **Guardar y enviar notificación de prueba** para comprobar la conexión.

Si reinicias la PS5 o vuelves a cargar el entorno de payloads, ejecuta otra vez `notify-bridge.elf` desde Payload Manager antes de usar la app.

## Recepción y comprobación

La recepción en tiempo real se mantiene activa. El intervalo adicional permite revisar de nuevo las notificaciones activas, con un mínimo de 1 minuto y un valor predeterminado de 2 minutos. Puedes cambiarlo desde **Verificar también cada (minutos)**; el nuevo intervalo se aplica al guardar.

Después de conceder el permiso, Android mantiene el servicio de notificaciones aunque la pantalla esté apagada o estés usando otra app, así que puedes dejar el móvil bloqueado mientras juegas. El teléfono debe permanecer encendido, con PS5 Notify instalada, el permiso habilitado y conexión a la misma red que la PS5. Apagar el móvil por completo o forzar la detención de la app impedirá recibir notificaciones.

La opción **Mostrar el contenido del mensaje en la TV** está desactivada por defecto para proteger la privacidad.

repos.readme:
![Pegasus DL+](./assets/pegasus-dlplus-banner.png)

# Pegasus DL+

Browse catalogs, download files and install compatible packages directly on
your PS5, using your controller.

**[Download Pegasus DL+ 2.0.5](https://github.com/pegasus-ps5/pegasus-dl/releases/download/native-v2.0.5/PPSA99998.ffpfsc)**

## Features

- Browse and search catalogs, compare available versions and choose a download link.
- Open provider pages in the built-in browser and capture downloads.
- Manage the download queue, choose destinations, and extract supported archives.
- Extract folder games for ShadowMount while preserving backport folders and hiding unfinished extractions.
- Connect Real-Debrid or TorBox, including account linking from your phone.
- Browse installed titles and manage files across mounted storage.
- Choose from ten languages, with localized keyboards and Arabic RTL support.

## Getting started

You'll need a homebrew-enabled PS5, a compatible ShadowMountPlus setup, and a
running ELF loader.

1. Copy `PPSA99998.ffpfsc` into your loader's homebrew folder.
2. Refresh the loader and launch **Pegasus DL+**.
3. Choose a download folder in Settings, review your catalogs in Sources, and
   start browsing in Store.

The app checks for updates at startup. Update preferences are in Settings.

Pegasus DL+ reports app launches and reliability diagnostics to help improve the app.
Selected failures may automatically attach a redacted diagnostic log, retained
for seven days.

Thanks to **nexgen infinity** for testing Pegasus DL+.

repos.name: ps5upload
repos.description: Send games, apps and homebrew to a jailbroken PS5, and manage the console from your computer, phone or browser.
repos.readme:
# ps5upload

PS5 Upload gets your games, apps and homebrew onto a jailbroken PS5 quickly and reliably: uploads resume after a dropped connection, installs pick the route that works, and you can browse files, manage the console and run cheats from your computer, phone or browser.

--- ## What it does - **Fast, resumable uploads** of games, folders, disk images and `.zip` / `.7z` / `.rar` archives (unpacked on the way, nothing extracted to your disk). Everything runs over **AVA1**, one encrypted connection on port 9120. Every file is verified, and an upload continues after a dropped connection, a helper restart or rest mode. A job that will not fit is refused up front, counting what is already on the console. Queue, live speed and ETA. - **Upload & Install.** One drop zone takes packages, game folders and dumps, disk images, archives and any other file, and works out what each is. PS4 `.pkg` and PS5 fake packages (base, update, DLC) install from your computer (**Stream & install** or **Upload & install**), a NAS/SMB share, a USB drive or a link. If the PS5 refuses one route, the app offers another. PS5 fake packages install but do not start on firmware later than 11.60; PS4 fake packages are fine. - **Games.** One grid with every game once: your copies in your folders (including folders on a NAS, scanned in place) grouped with their updates and DLC, what each PS5 has installed, and the games on its drives. Play (or close) an installed game right from its card. Each game's page holds everything you can do with it: install, play, mount, add to the home screen, move, back up, convert, dump. Organize, de-duplicate and clean up the drives. Replaces PS Game Library. - **Convert games (Workshop).** Build an installable package from a decrypted game folder or an image, or write a game folder as a game image (`.exfat`, `.ffpkg`, `.ffpfs`, or the smaller `.ffpfsc`) that ShadowMount+ mounts. A queue makes games one after another and hands each to Upload & Install to install or upload. - **Browse and manage.** Files, games, disk images (mount, edit in place), saves, screenshots and video clips; register, launch, stop and uninstall games; copy, move (Move to…), delete, set permissions. - **Remote Play.** Play the PS5 from your computer, phone or browser, no PS Remote Play app needed: - Start wakes a console in rest mode and signs your user in; the stream keeps playing while you use other screens, and a dropped connection rejoins by itself. - Play with a controller connected to this device, the keyboard (keys you can remap) or an on-screen controller on phones and tablets; the controller vibrates with the game. - Picture in picture: a small always-on-top window while you do something else (desktop app, Chrome and Edge; picture only in Safari). - 1080p or 720p at 60 or 30 fps, full screen, volume, stats on the picture, and low-delay sound. - A step-by-step setup in Accounts that checks each requirement on the console and fixes what it can (sign-in, account ID, Remote Play switches, pairing), plus a PIN for Sony's PS Remote Play app or chiaki-ng if you prefer those. - **Cheats, fan curve, hardware view,** payload sender with a catalogue and playlists, and backport tools. - **Power.** Rest mode, reboot, shut down, and wake over the network (optionally straight into your signed-in user). - **PS5Upload Minion.** A page the helper serves to the PS5's own browser (a tile on the home screen, port 9180), made for the controller: installed games and the games on your network shares and drives, save backups, files (SMB shares, archive extraction, package install, payload loading), cheats, fan, processes, clean-up and settings, with no PC nearby. - **Several devices, one PS5.** Computers, phones and Docker connect at once with no pairing code, see what the others are doing (Devices), share your consoles and settings, and stay out of each other's way. Settings are backed up daily, to the engine and to each console. **Mesh Drive** keeps a folder the same on all of them, at home on the console, with an optional join password and every device's state visible from any of them. - **Runs everywhere:** macOS, Windows, Linux, Android, iPhone (sideloaded), or any browser through the self-hosted Docker web UI ([compose file](engine/compose.yaml), see [Self-hosted engine and web UI](#self-hosted-engine-and-web-ui)). 21 languages. ## What it doesn't do - **System package patches** (NPXS Store or Settings updates). Use the PS5's own Settings → Debug Settings → Game → Package Installer. - **Sign packages with fake keys.** It only installs packages the console already trusts. ## A quick look ## Install Pre-built downloads land on the [Releases page](https://github.com/phantomptr/ps5upload/releases): | Platform | File | How to install | |---|---|---| | macOS (Apple Silicon / Intel) | `PS5Upload--mac-{arm64,x64}.dmg` | Open the `.dmg`, drag PS5Upload into Applications. See **First launch on macOS** below — Gatekeeper blocks downloaded apps the first time. | | Windows (x64 / ARM64) | `PS5Upload--win-{x64,arm64}-setup.exe` or `PS5Upload--win-{x64,arm64}.zip` | Run the `-setup.exe` installer (it updates itself later), or unzip the `.zip` and double-click `PS5Upload.exe` — portable, no installer. See **First launch on Windows** — SmartScreen warns on first run. | | Linux — Debian / Ubuntu (x64 / ARM64) | `PS5Upload--linux-{x64,arm64}.deb` | `sudo apt install ./PS5Upload--linux-.deb` — installs a normal app with a menu entry; pulls in the WebKitGTK deps automatically. | | Linux — Fedora / RHEL / Bazzite (x64 / ARM64) | `PS5Upload--linux-{x64,arm64}.rpm` | `sudo dnf install ./PS5Upload--linux-.rpm` (Bazzite/Silverblue: `rpm-ostree install`; to update, `rpm-ostree uninstall ps5-upload --install ./.rpm` and reboot, which Settings → Updates shows ready to copy) — menu entry + auto deps. | | Linux — any distro (x64 / ARM64) | `PS5Upload--linux-{x64,arm64}.zip` | Universal fallback (no install). Unzip, then `chmod +x PS5Upload.sh PS5Upload.AppImage` and run **`./PS5Upload.sh`** (the wrapper — handles the FUSE-less and WebKit white-screen cases for you). Running `./PS5Upload.AppImage` directly also works if your system has libfuse2 and a happy WebKitGTK. | | Linux — NixOS (x64 / ARM64) | no release artifact | Packaged in [NUR](https://github.com/GriefNorth/nur-packages) as `ps5upload` — see **NixOS** below. | | Android | `PS5Upload--android.apk` (older 32-bit phones: `-android-armv7.apk`) | Enable "install unknown apps" for your browser/file manager, then open the `.apk`. Same interface, mobile-friendly; connects to and manages your PS5 over Wi-Fi. On Android 17, allow local network access ("nearby devices") when asked. | | iPhone | `PS5Upload--ios-unsigned.ipa` | Sideload with AltStore or Sideloadly and an Apple ID (a free one works; it is re-signed every 7 days). AltStore, SideStore and Feather can also add the source `https://github.com/phantomptr/ps5upload/releases/latest/download/altstore.json` and update the app from there. Turn on Developer Mode and trust your Apple ID on the iPhone; see the FAQ. Copy games into the app's folder with the Files app. | ### NixOS No NixOS artifact is published on the Releases page, but ps5upload is packaged in [GriefNorth's NUR](https://github.com/GriefNorth/nur-packages) as `ps5upload` (x64 and ARM64) — it wraps the same `.AppImage` and needs no FUSE. With flakes: ```nix { inputs = { nixpkgs.url = "github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-unstable"; nur.url = "github:GriefNorth/nur-packages"; }; outputs = { nixpkgs, nur, ... }: { nixosConfigurations.myhost = nixpkgs.lib.nixosSystem { system = "x86_64-linux"; modules = [ ({ pkgs, ... }: { environment.systemPackages = [ nur.packages.${pkgs.system}.ps5upload ]; }) ]; }; }; } ``` Then `nixos-rebuild switch --flake .#myhost` and launch **ps5upload** from your app menu. Without flakes, call the package straight out of the repo — and note that ps5upload bundles UnRAR for `.rar` support, so nixpkgs needs `config.allowUnfree = true`: ```nix { pkgs, ... }: { nixpkgs.config.allowUnfree = true; environment.systemPackages = [ (pkgs.callPackage ((builtins.fetchTarball "https://github.com/GriefNorth/nur-packages/archive/refs/heads/main.tar.gz") + "/pkgs/ps5upload") { }) ]; } ``` Or try it without installing anything: ```bash nix run github:GriefNorth/nur-packages#ps5upload ``` The Nix expression pins one release version, so bump it there when a new ps5upload comes out. Prefer to run the AppImage yourself? Prefer the `./PS5Upload.sh` wrapper from the zip above — on NixOS the bare `.AppImage` usually renders an empty window, because its bundled `libwayland-client` shadows the host one and WebKitGTK then fails to create an EGL display. The Nix package works around that for you. ### First-launch warnings (and why they're there) ps5upload is not code-signed with paid OS certificates — same as every other PS5 scene tool. The OS's verification layers (Gatekeeper on macOS, SmartScreen on Windows) treat unsigned downloads as suspicious until you allow them once. The one-time bypass: **macOS** — "App is damaged" or "cannot be opened": ```bash xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/PS5Upload.app ``` That removes the *quarantine* attribute macOS slaps on every file downloaded from a browser. Alternatively, right-click PS5Upload in Applications → **Open** → click **Open** in the prompt. Either method only needs to be done once per install. **Windows** — "Windows protected your PC" SmartScreen prompt: - Click **More info** → **Run anyway**. - Only shown until SmartScreen builds reputation for the binary; subsequent launches are silent. - If your IT policy blocks "Run anyway", unzip + right-click `PS5Upload.exe` → **Properties** → check **Unblock** → **OK**. **Linux** — no equivalent warning. Just `chmod +x` and launch. ### System requirements - **macOS** 11 (Big Sur) or newer. No dependencies — ad-hoc signed, see *First launch* above for the one-line quarantine bypass. - **Windows** 10 (build 19041+) or Windows 11. Ships with the Microsoft Edge WebView2 runtime by default; LTSC / stripped installs may need [WebView2](https://developer.microsoft.com/microsoft-edge/webview2/) installed once. - **Linux** — the `.deb` and `.rpm` packages **pull in their dependencies automatically** (WebKitGTK 4.1, gtk3, libsoup3, etc.) via the package manager, so they're the easiest route on Debian/Ubuntu and Fedora/RHEL/Bazzite. The universal `.AppImage` instead expects those libraries already on the host (libfuse2, gtk3, webkit2gtk 4.1, libsoup3, libappindicator, librsvg2); install commands for Debian/Ubuntu/Fedora/RHEL/Arch are in [the FAQ](FAQ.md#prerequisites). **Minimum distro version:** all three Linux artifacts are built against **glibc 2.39**, so they need a reasonably recent distro — **Ubuntu 24.04+, Debian 13+ (trixie), Fedora 40+**, or equivalent. (This is a glibc floor, not a package dependency — the `.deb`/`.rpm` install fine on older releases but the app won't launch, and the AppImage bundles WebKitGTK yet still uses the host's glibc.) On an older distro, build from source with `make dist-linux` on that machine. The app checks GitHub for updates once per launch (Settings → Updates) and downloads a fresh archive to your Downloads folder when you click Download. Replace the old app and relaunch; the app then offers to update the helper. Building from source: ```bash git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/phantomptr/ps5upload.git cd ps5upload make install # bootstrap dev env (auto-detects host OS) make build # payload ELF + engine + client UI make run-client # launch the Tauri dev app ``` `make install` auto-detects your OS and runs one of: - **`make install-ubuntu`** — Debian / Ubuntu / WSL2: `apt` deps for Tauri (`libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev`, `libgtk-3-dev`, `librsvg2-dev`, `libayatana-appindicator3-dev`, `libxdo-dev`, `libssl-dev`, `build-essential`), Node.js 22 LTS via NodeSource (only if missing), Rust via rustup, and checksum-verified PS5 Payload SDK v0.45 → `~/ps5-payload-sdk`. - **`make install-macos`** — macOS: Xcode CLT, Homebrew, `node`, current `llvm` (LLVM 23 at this release), Rust via rustup, and checksum-verified PS5 Payload SDK v0.45. - **`make install-windows`** — Windows 11: Node.js LTS, Rust, VS 2022 Build Tools (C++ workload), WebView2 Runtime, 7-Zip, and PS5 Payload SDK via `winget`. Run from an elevated PowerShell (or any shell with `pwsh` / `powershell.exe` on PATH). All three install scripts are idempotent — re-running them after a partial setup is safe. A stale or unmarked SDK is upgraded to the repository pin and moved to a timestamped backup instead of being deleted. Local and GitHub Actions builds read the same tag and official release checksum from `scripts/ps5-sdk.env`. For per-platform bundles only (no full dev env): `make dist-mac`, `make dist-mac-x64`, `make dist-linux`, `make dist-linux-arm`, `make dist-win`, and `make dist-win-arm`. ## Quick start 1. Jailbreak the PS5 and keep an ELF loader running on port **9021**. 2. Launch ps5upload and open **Connection**. Enter the PS5's IP address. 3. Click **Check**, then **Send helper**. The app launches the helper and connects to it. (Other payloads, such as kstuff or etaHEN, are sent from **Payloads → Send payload**.) 4. Other computers, phones and Docker setups connect to the same helper with no code; the console remembers each one (**Devices**). To make new devices type a code shown on the TV first, turn on **Ask before a new device can connect** there. The helper stays until the PS5 reboots or enters rest mode. The app connects to ports **9120** (the helper) and **9021** (the loader); allow both in your firewall. For **Stream & install** the PS5 connects back to this computer on port **19113**, so allow the app through the firewall too (on Windows, for Private and Public networks). 6.0 cannot talk to a v5.x helper: the banner's **Send helper** replaces it in one click. ## Architecture ``` client/ (Tauri 2 · React · TypeScript) Android app · Docker web UI │ └── spawns ── ps5upload-engine (HTTP :19113) │ ▼ AVA1 (Noise-encrypted, port 9120) payload/ps5upload.elf (PS5 C payload) ``` - **`payload/`**: C payload on the PS5 (FreeBSD 11). Transfers, BLAKE3 verification, mounts, file operations and every management call, over [AVA1](https://github.com/phantomptr/ava1), the transfer protocol (its own repository, checked out as `third_party/ava1`). - **`engine/`**: Rust workspace with the AVA1 client, transfer logic, HTTP API and lab tools. - **`client/`**: Tauri 2 desktop app (and the Android and web builds), talking to the engine. ## Build and test All workflows go through the root `Makefile` (`make help`). | Command | What it does | |---|---| | `make build` | Payload + engine + client | | `make run-client` | Tauri dev app | | `make run-engine` | Engine on port 19113 (binds all interfaces; answers loopback, `PS5UPLOAD_ALLOW_IP` and the PS5-facing `/pkg-host/` only) | | `make test-engine` | Rust tests, no PS5 needed | | `make test-payload` | Console C code compiled and run on the host | | `npm run validate` | Full non-hardware gate | | `make dist` | Tauri bundle | See [`TESTING.md`](TESTING.md) for the full workflow, and [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md). ## Tech stack - **Payload**: C (FreeBSD 11), prospero-clang, PS5 Payload SDK v0.45 - **Engine**: Rust, tokio + axum - **Client**: Tauri 2, React, TypeScript, Zustand, Tailwind CSS v4, Vite - **Protocol**: AVA1 (Noise XX handshake, ChaCha20-Poly1305, BLAKE3 verification) ## Supported platforms - **Desktop:** macOS, Linux and Windows, x64 and arm64. - **Android:** the `.apk` from Releases. - **iPhone:** the unsigned `.ipa` from Releases, sideloaded with AltStore or Sideloadly (see the FAQ). New and not yet widely tested. - **Web UI:** the self-hosted Docker image, in any browser on your LAN (see below). - **PS5 firmware:** 1.00 through 14.10 on every model; one payload binary for all. Tested on 5.10, 9.60 and 13.60 (14.00 and 14.10 are new in SDK v0.45 and not tested yet). In practice the limit is your jailbreak's ELF loader on port 9021. Fake package install needs live kernel patches (kstuff / fpkg-enable) on the console; where they are missing the app says so instead of reporting a false success. ## Self-hosted engine and web UI Run the engine on a NAS or server and use it from a browser, or point the desktop app at it with **Settings → Engine URL**. - Images: `ghcr.io/phantomptr/ps5upload-engine-webui` (full web UI) and `ghcr.io/phantomptr/ps5upload-engine` (engine only). Every release tag pushes `:`; `:latest` and `:` move only when a pre-release is promoted to a release. - Start from [`engine/compose.yaml`](engine/compose.yaml). It uses host networking (stream installs need the PS5 to reach the engine). `PS5_ADDR` (the console) and `PS5UPLOAD_ALLOW_IP` (who may use the page) are required for a web UI used from other devices on the LAN; without the allowlist every browser but the host's own gets a `403`. - Open `http://:19113`. The file picker browses the engine's disk; mount your games folder into the container and set `PS5UPLOAD_BROWSE_ROOTS`. - Map `/data` to a host folder (on Unraid, `/mnt/user/appdata/ps5upload`): it holds the container's key, so the PS5 knows it as the same device (and its Mesh Drive folders) after the container is recreated. - An upload keeps running when you close the tab. - **No password.** Anyone allowed can read, write and delete on your PS5. Keep it on a trusted LAN, never on the internet. - For a dedicated reverse-proxy hostname, leave `PS5UPLOAD_BASE_URL` unset. It is a build-time **path prefix**, not a full URL. See [reverse-proxy setup](REVERSE_PROXY.md) for nginx, proxy authentication, Docker bridge networking, and sub-path hosting. - **Scripting it:** [ps5upctl](https://github.com/yuanzhengze/ps5upctl) is a community command-line client for the engine API (unofficial; the API can change between versions). ## FAQ Common questions (connection problems, install errors, USB drives, firmware) are in [`FAQ.md`](FAQ.md), also available inside the app. ## Contributing - Report bugs: [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/phantomptr/ps5upload/issues) - Pull requests welcome. Read [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md) and run the checks in [`TESTING.md`](TESTING.md) before opening. ## How this project is built ps5upload is a vibe-coded project. The code is written with AI coding tools, directed, tested on real consoles and released by one maintainer. That is what keeps the development cycle fast: bug reports, feature requests and enhancements are usually turned around in days, not months. The trade-off is that the code has not had the slow, line-by-line human review a hand-written project of this size would get. Every release is tested on hardware, but you should expect rough edges, read the [disclaimer](DISCLAIMER.md), keep backups of anything you care about on the console, and use the tool at your own discretion. ## Disclaimer > **ps5upload is provided for research, educational, interoperability, > and homebrew development purposes only.** It is not affiliated with, > endorsed by, or connected to Sony Interactive Entertainment Inc. > "PlayStation", "PS4" and "PS5" are trademarks of Sony Interactive > Entertainment Inc., used here for identification only. > > **Use this software entirely at your own risk.** It is provided > "as is", without warranty of any kind, express or implied, > including but not limited to warranties of merchantability, fitness > for a particular purpose, and non-infringement. **➡ Full terms: [DISCLAIMER.md](DISCLAIMER.md).** By downloading, building, installing, or using this software you accept them in full. latestRelease.name: v9.5.3
latestRelease.body:
- **Back up your users' information (Accounts).** A new **Back up user information** card
  downloads a text file with every user on the PS5: their names, user IDs, account IDs (in hex,
  decimal and the base64 form Remote Play uses), how each account is activated, its sign-in
  details (online ID, date of birth, age), and step-by-step instructions for giving a new user
  an old account ID. Saves are tied to the account ID, so after a console reset, or a crash that
  loses a user, the file is what you need to get your saves back. It holds no passwords or
  Remote Play keys; keep it private all the same.
- **Phone screens scroll all the way down.** Payloads, Tasks and Help (FAQ, About, What's new)
  now leave room under their last row, so nothing stays stuck behind the bottom tab bar.

repos.name: Spectrum-Library
repos.readme: # Spectrum Library Spectrum Library is a lightweight native PlayStation 5 content manager designed to organize and deliver supported game files through a simple, clean, and user-friendly interface. Its streamlined library brings together categories, cover artwork, file details, download controls, and installation status, making it easier to browse available content and manage downloads from one place. Thanks to the DLPS Team in particular Pippo https://x.com/Pippo26442999?s=20 for making the games available in an organized way on their website.

# pLinux5-NG

boot linux on PS5 consoles running high firmware (8.xx through 13.60) 

this project is a port/rework of the existing [ps5-linux-loader](https://github.com/ps5-linux/ps5-linux-loader) 
(which currently works on 3.00 though 7.61) to the new [byepervisor-reborn](https://github.com/PS5Dev/Byepervisor-Reborn) hypervisor escape 

- the linux boot path itself (bzImage/initrd relocation, `boot_params`/e820 setup,
  hardware bring up, SVM/IOMMU teardown, the jump to `startup_64`) is brought over
  from the existing ps5-linux-loader
- the *escape* -- how we get code running in hypervisor root mode on all cores on high firmware --
  is what has changed in this project. on 3.00 through 7.61 its flatz' ACPI-wakeup ROP
  chain; on high firmware it is a khook on the S3-resume `HV_MP_STARTUP_CALL` path. as implemented
  in Byepervisor-Reborn.

## usage

### **CRITICAL** 
ps5 configuration:
- enable rest mode features:
    - `settings` -> `system` -> `power saving` -> `features available in rest mode`, set `Supply Power to USB Ports` to `Always`
- disable HDMI device link:
    - `settings` -> `system` -> `HDMI`, set `Enable HDMI Device Link` to be `off` 
  

# installation

follow the [ps5-linux-loader installation guide](https://github.com/ps5-linux/ps5-linux-loader#installation) until you get to
step 4, then come back here.

### running the jailbreak

- set your playstations DNS to `45.56.67.85`:
  - `settings` -> `network` -> `settings` -> `set up internet connection` then click the `options` button on
  your controller, select `advanced settings`, from there set `primary DNS` to `45.56.67.85` then select `ok`, if
  done correctly, you will get a popup saying `internet connection failed`, thats good, continue.

- navigate to the users guide:
  - `settings` -> `Guide & Tips, Health and Safety, and Other Information` -> `User's Guide`.
  - when a popup appears saying: `the security of the page can't be confirmed...`, click `yes`
    
- you should end up on a page with big letters saying `RELAPSE`, click the `Jailbreak` button & wait for it to finish
  it finishing will be marked by elfldr starting.

now download the `pLinux5-NG.elf` file from releases, or see [building](#building) to build from source, then move to [sending](#sending)


# building

## locally
requires the [PS5 payload SDK](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk), the [pLabs5-SDK](https://github.com/pLabs5/pLabs5-SDK) and a C compiler:

```bash
export PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK=/path/to/ps5-payload-sdk
LLVM_CONFIG=/path/to/pLabs5-SDK/tools/nixos/llvm-config
make -j
```

the output is `bin/pLinux5-NG.elf`.

The shellcode blobs are compiled freestanding with the host `gcc`
(`-ffreestanding -nostdlib`) and embedded as C headers; `scripts/bin2c.py`
replaces `xxd -i`, which is not present in every environment.

## docker
run
```shell
docker buildx bake
```
the output will be at `bin/pLinux5-NG.elf`.

### sending

on linux/unix, use:
```bash
# (from the area with the repo + pLinux5-NG.elf)
cd scripts/
chmod +x send.sh
PS5_IP=<Playstation 5s IP> ./send.sh
```
on windows, if using powershell, use:
```powershell
.\scripts\send.ps1 -PS5IP <Playstation 5s IP> -Port 9021
```
otherwise, if using CMD/Command Prompt, use:
```cmd
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\scripts\send.ps1 -PS5IP <Playstation 5s IP> -Port 9021
```

**GPL-3.0**; those files retain their original authorship and are used here in
accordance with the GPL/AGPL compatibility provisions. The high-firmware escape
is adapted from **Byepervisor-Reborn**.

repos.name: PS5-PlayKaraoke-Player
repos.description: Karaoke player for jailbroken PS5: CDG and MP4, real-time key change, singer rotation and song requests from phones via QR code.
repos.readme:
PlayKaraoke for PS5

A karaoke player for jailbroken PS5 consoles: CDG (MP3+G) and MP4, real-time key change, a singer rotation, and guests requesting songs from their phones with a QR code on the TV.
Homebrew version of the PlayKaraoke Web Player.

> ⚠️ **Experimental beta — use at your own risk.** PlayKaraoke runs on a jailbroken console and writes to > system areas (it registers a dashboard tile and an app host). It has no affiliation with Sony. > Back up your saves and **close any running game before opening PlayKaraoke**.

> 💾 **Your songs must be on an external drive.** In this version, PlayKaraoke only finds songs on a > **USB hard drive or pen drive** plugged into the PS5 (formatted as **exFAT** or FAT32). Songs on the > PS5 internal storage are not listed. > 🎵 **No music included.** This project is only a player. It does not include, distribute or point to > karaoke files, artist names or songs. Only use files you have the right to use. ## Features - **Formats:** `.zip` with `.cdg` + audio (MP3+G) and `.mp4` video (up to 4K) - **Key change:** ±12 semitones in real time, without changing speed, for CDG and MP4 - **Phones:** guests scan the QR code, type their name, search the library and request songs; they see how many songs are left until their turn and can change the key or finish their song - **Singer rotation:** one song per singer per round, in order of arrival, up to 5 songs each - **Search:** accent-insensitive search by artist, title or code, CDG/MP4 filter, alphabetical results - **DualSense only mode:** you can run a whole night with just the controller - **Languages:** English and Portuguese (Brazil) ## Screenshots

Screenshots use the made-up demo songs from tools/make-demo-songs.py.

## Requirements - A jailbroken PS5 with an ELF loader (**elfldr**, port 9021). **Tested on firmware 13.60.** Earlier firmwares that run elfldr should work but are untested. - **A USB hard drive or pen drive with your karaoke files**, formatted as **exFAT** (or FAT32). This is where PlayKaraoke looks for songs; NTFS and APFS drives are not supported by the PS5. Any folder layout works: the whole drive is scanned. - Phones on the same Wi-Fi network as the PS5 (optional). ## Installation 1. Download `playkaraoke.elf` from the [latest release](../../releases/latest). 2. Send it to the PS5 elfldr (port 9021), the same way you load any payload. For example, from a computer: `nc -q0 9021 < playkaraoke.elf` (or use your favorite payload sender). 3. A notification says PlayKaraoke is ready. Open **PlayKaraoke** in the **Media** section of the home screen. The payload installs everything by itself (`/data/playkaraoke` and the Media tile) and stays resident to open the app. **Send it again after every jailbreak.** Sending a newer version updates it in place. When the app opens, the PS5 web browser also shows a quick guide on top of it: press **○** to close it. ## How to use 1. Plug the USB drive with your songs **before** opening the app. The first time, PlayKaraoke reads the drive in the background and builds the library (it is updated every time the app opens). 2. On the home screen, guests scan the **QR code** to request songs from their phones. You can also search with the controller (**△**). 3. Press **✕ Start** (or **▢ Start show** in the search) to start. A 10-second countdown shows who sings next. After the show starts, new requests start automatically when the queue is idle. ### Phones and the PS5 address Every PS5 has its own address (IP) on your network, so there is nothing to configure: when PlayKaraoke opens, it finds its own address and shows it under the QR code (for example `http://192.168.0.25:8000`). Guests just scan the code, or type that address in the phone browser. - The phones must be on the **same Wi-Fi** as the PS5 (no internet needed). - Each guest types a name once; the phone remembers it. One song per singer per round, up to 5 each. - On the phone: search and request songs, see how many songs are left until your turn, cancel your songs, change their key and, when it is your turn, change the key live or finish your song. - During a song, a small QR code stays in the bottom-right corner so new guests can join. - If the address changes (the router gives the PS5 a new one), the QR code updates the next time the app opens. ### Controller | Where | Button | Action | |---|---|---| | Home | △ / ▢ / ✕ / ○ | Search songs / Folders / Start / Quit | | Home | R1 | Language (🇺🇸 English / 🇧🇷 Português) | | Search | ✕ | Add to / remove from the queue | | Search | ▢ | Start the show | | Search | △ / R1 | New search (PS5 keyboard) / CDG, MP4 or both | | Anywhere | OPTIONS | Queue: see the rotation, move (✕) or remove (△) songs | | Countdown | ✕ / ○ | Start now / Skip this turn | | Playing | ✕ / ○ | Pause / End the song | | Playing | ↑ ↓ or left stick | Volume | | Playing | L1 / R1 | Key −1 / +1 | | Playing | Right stick ← → | Back / forward 10 seconds | | Playing | Touchpad | Show the controls bar | ### File names Song info is read from the file name: `Code - Artist - Title` ``` SC8123-05 - Artist Name - Song Title.zip → code, artist, title Artist Name - Song Title.mp4 → artist, title ``` A `.zip` must contain one `.cdg` and its audio (`.mp3`, `.wav`, `.ogg` or `.m4a`). ## FAQ **The drive does not show up.** Check that it is exFAT or FAT32 and connected before opening the app. Drives formatted on a Mac have a small hidden EFI partition; PlayKaraoke hides it and shows the main one. **A browser window stays on top of the app.** That is how the dashboard tile opens homebrew. Press ○ once. **Phones cannot open the page.** The phone must be on the same Wi-Fi as the PS5, and the app must be open. **Will it close my game?** No. If a game or app is open, PlayKaraoke shows a message and does nothing. ## Demo songs No karaoke files at hand? `tools/make-demo-songs.py` generates six royalty-free demo songs (CDG zips and MP4s with made-up lyrics and synthesized music). Needs Python 3 with Pillow and ffmpeg: ``` python3 tools/make-demo-songs.py demo-songs ``` Copy them to your USB drive and open the app. ## Building Requires Docker. The build uses the [ps5-payload-sdk](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk) and the [PacBrew](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/pacbrew-repo) libraries (`v0.41.1`). ``` scripts/ps5.sh release # dist/playkaraoke.elf (public build) scripts/ps5.sh build # development build (build/playkaraoke.elf) PS5_HOST= scripts/ps5.sh # build and send to elfldr tests/run.sh # unit tests (host) ``` ## Credits and licenses PlayKaraoke for PS5 is licensed under **GPL-3.0-or-later** (see [LICENSE](LICENSE)). | Component | License | Notes | |---|---|---| | BigApp loader core (`src/launcher/core`) from [ps5-payload-websrv](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/websrv) by John Törnblom | GPL-3.0-or-later | Commit `7748df9`; `hbldr.c` changed to use PlayKaraoke's own Media app host | | [qrcodegen](https://github.com/nayuki/QR-Code-generator) by Project Nayuki (`vendor/qrcodegen`) | MIT | v1.8.0, unchanged | | [ps5-payload-sdk](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk) | GPL-3.0-or-later | Toolchain and runtime | | SDL2, SDL2_ttf, SDL2_image, SDL2_gfx | zlib | Via PacBrew | | FFmpeg | LGPL/GPL | Via PacBrew | | libmicrohttpd | LGPL-2.1 | Via PacBrew | | minizip, zlib | zlib | Via PacBrew | | [Inter](https://github.com/rsms/inter) and [Montserrat](https://github.com/JulietaUla/Montserrat) fonts | SIL OFL 1.1 | `assets/fonts` | The CDG decoder, pitch shifter, queue rotation and file-name parsing are ports of the PlayKaraoke Web Player by the same author. The PlayKaraoke name and logo belong to their owner. ## Support PlayKaraoke is free. More from PlayKaraoke on [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/@playkaraoke).

## Requirements

repos.name: Common-FPS-for-PS5
repos.description: Common FPS for PS5 v1.0.0  First public stable release.  Universal real-time FPS overlay for PS4 and PS5 games on PS5.  This release includes both a standalone ELF and an etaHEN plugin.
repos.readme:
# Common FPS for PS5 v1.2.3

Real-time integer FPS overlay for PS4 and PS5 games on a modified PlayStation 5.
Available as a standalone ELF or etaHEN plugin.

## Download and installation

Download **one** file from the [latest release](https://github.com/porhe911/Common-FPS-for-PS5/releases/latest):

- `Common_FPS_PS5_v1.2.3.elf` — launch with your usual payload loader.
- `Common_FPS_PS5_etaHEN_v1.2.3.plugin` — install and enable through etaHEN.

Reboot before replacing an older version, then start one ELF or plugin and
launch a game. The overlay appears after the game and ShellUI readiness checks.
**Do not run the ELF and plugin together.**

## Features and settings

- FPS for PS4 and PS5 games, with VideoOut sampling and an adaptive DCE fallback.
- Compact bottom-left overlay by default: 22-unit font, purple label, white digits.
- Startup settling and filtering of brief FPS spikes; sustained 120 FPS is supported.
- Automatic game-process and ShellUI recovery on supported firmware.
- Offline **Media → Common FPS** settings shortcut, checked on activation and
  installed when missing (firmware below 12).
- Four corners, font size 14–64, adjustable edge margins, digits-only mode and
  separate colors for the label and numbers.
- Eight named colors in each palette, plus custom HEX colors.
- D-pad navigation, **✕** activation and **OPTIONS** to save.

Choose your settings, select **Save** and press **✕**, or press **OPTIONS**.
Saved changes apply on the next one-second update and persist across restarts
in `/data/CommonFPS/config.ini`.

The settings page is embedded and works offline while the counter is running.
Position and size use the PS5 interface's logical 1920×1080 canvas. Adjust font
size for viewing distance and margins for TV overscan; physical screen diagonal
is not queried. Other PUI canvas sizes still need hardware testing.

## Firmware status

| System software | Hardware validation |
|---|---|
| **11.60** | v1.2.3 tested by the user; working overlay and settings confirmed on 2026-10-16 |
| **4.51** | Previously confirmed PS4/PS5 FPS, game switching and Rest Mode recovery; v1.2.3 regression pending |
| **9.00** | Previously confirmed FPS and Rest Mode recovery; v1.2.3 regression pending |
| **9.60** | Previously confirmed FPS/lifecycle baseline; v1.2.3 regression pending |
| **7.60** | Fresh hardware test pending |
| **10.xx** | Experimental; hardware validation pending |

The latest FW 11.60 report confirms the user's tested workflow, not every game,
display mode or Rest Mode scenario. See the [release notes](release/RELEASE_NOTES_v1.2.3.md).

## Logs

- Controller: `/data/CommonFPS.log`
- Renderer: `/data/CommonFPS_shellui.log`

Both logs are overwritten on each activation and limited to **64 KiB each**.
Saved settings are kept separately.

## Source and license

See [BUILDING.md](BUILDING.md) for source builds and tests.
Common FPS-owned source is licensed under **GPL-3.0-or-later**;
see [LICENSE](LICENSE) and [third-party notices](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

latestRelease.name: Common FPS for PS5 v1.2.3
latestRelease.body:
## Changes since v1.2.1

- Working FPS overlay on FW 11.60, with checked ShellUI code access and deferred
  renderer startup.
- Compact default overlay: 22-unit font and lower bottom-left placement.
- Startup settling and filtering of brief FPS spikes while keeping sustained
  120 FPS support.
- Offline **Media → Common FPS** settings shortcut, installed when missing
  on firmware below 12.
- Four corners, adjustable size/margins, optional FPS label and separate colors
  for label and numbers. Settings persist across restarts and apply live.
- Explicit eight-color palettes plus custom HEX colors.
- Reliable D-pad/**✕** activation, duplicate-event suppression and **OPTIONS**
  saving. Opening a palette does not change the selected color.
- Improved renderer object lifetimes, selective style updates and recovery
  when the ShellUI root widget changes.
- Controller and renderer logs reset on each activation and are limited to
  **64 KiB each**.

## Installation

Choose **one** asset:

- `Common_FPS_PS5_v1.2.3.elf` — standalone payload.
- `Common_FPS_PS5_etaHEN_v1.2.3.plugin` — etaHEN plugin.

**Reboot before upgrading** to unload an older resident renderer. Use your
usual working loader, or enable the plugin through etaHEN. Do not run both.
Existing settings in `/data/CommonFPS/config.ini` are retained.

Open **Media → Common FPS**, choose your settings and press **✕** on **Save**,
or press **OPTIONS**. Changes apply on the next one-second update.

## Validation

FW 11.60: the user confirmed the tested v1.2.3 build working on 2026-10-16
and authorized publication. This confirms that tested workflow; every game, display mode and
Rest Mode scenario has not been newly verified. The precise cause of the
freeze reported in an earlier build was not established.

Previously confirmed FPS/lifecycle paths for FW 4.51, 9.00 and 9.60 are retained;
fresh v1.2.3 hardware regression tests are pending. FW 7.60 needs testing and
10.xx remains experimental. The Media installer is skipped on FW 12+.

Automated checks cover host behavior, controller interaction with the real
settings HTTP worker, source-built PS5 artifacts and the plugin wrapper.

## Logs and license

`/data/CommonFPS.log` and `/data/CommonFPS_shellui.log` are overwritten on each
activation, up to 64 KiB each. Settings are stored separately.

Common FPS-owned source: GPL-3.0-or-later.

repos.name: OpenNOW-PS5
repos.description: Experimental native PS5 GeForce NOW client: a working, console-tested prototype with hardware decoding and GPU presentation.
repos.readme: # OpenNOW PS5 > **This repository is archived.** Development now continues at > [OpenCloudGaming/OpenNOW-PS5](https://github.com/OpenCloudGaming/OpenNOW-PS5). > Please use that repository for future updates, issues and contributions. > This repository remains available for historical source code and releases. ![OpenNOW PS5 — native cloud gaming, 0.0.1-alpha functional prototype](docs/branding/opennow-social-preview.png) *Social preview artwork for the independent native PS5 prototype.* An experimental native PS5 homebrew client for GeForce NOW, based on the public [OpenNOW](https://github.com/OpenCloudGaming/OpenNOW) projects. Native hardware video decoding, GPU presentation, Opus audio and DualSense input are integrated. **This is a working, console-tested prototype, not a finished application.** You can sign in, launch a game and play. The interface is still rough and primarily exists to test that authentication, streaming, audio, video and controls work together. Expect an incomplete user experience, limited navigation and functionality that still needs further testing. **Latest prerelease: [0.1](https://github.com/Portablelle/opennow-ps5/releases/tag/0.1)** — development build `00.002.038`, title ID `PPSA99082`, with FTP-accessible launch-age configuration, persistent login, virtual keyboard/mouse and Auto / Stereo / 5.1 / 7.1 audio selection. This project is unofficial and unaffiliated with Sony or NVIDIA. ## What works - NVIDIA device authorization, game/store catalog, session allocation and cancellation. - Native H.264 and HEVC Main10 decoding, including 10-bit SDR and HDR10 presentation paths. - Qualified asynchronous Main10 decoding with owned input buffers and safe GPU surface leases. - Selectable 4K120, 4K90 and 4K60 HDR targets, 4K120/90 SDR targets, and lower-resolution compatibility profiles, with up to 100 Mb/s requested bitrate. - Full-screen GPU presentation, 48 kHz Opus audio and DualSense controls. In the latest console test, a 3840 × 2160 Main10 SDR stream was received, decoded and drawn at approximately **92 FPS and 51–52 Mb/s**. No RTP/AU loss, queue overflow, decoder reset or API error was recorded after more than 19 minutes. The tester reported fluid motion and the earlier recurring compression degradation was resolved. ## Prototype limitations - **The UI is a test interface.** It is not polished, feature-complete or representative of the final experience. Catalog navigation and the controller-driven search keyboard are intentionally basic. - **Real 120 FPS and HDR game streaming are not yet validated.** The tested game supplied SDR despite an HDR request. Startup fixture tests passed 4K, 119.88 Hz output and HDR scanout; these checks do not establish sustained game FPS or HDR source content. - The 90 FPS profiles are requests; earlier tests received 60 FPS. Server behavior can differ from the selected target. - The deeper pipeline currently applies to qualified UHD Main10. H.264 remains at depth one and does not inherit its measured throughput improvement. - NVIDIA login is saved and renewed automatically. Persistence through a full console reboot and app replacement still needs live validation. NVIDIA can require sign-in again if renewal credentials expire or are revoked. Audio falls back to stereo when GFN does not offer a supported surround layout. Live 5.1/7.1 negotiation and speaker placement, broader firmware/loader compatibility and more games need testing. Performance may differ by game, server, network, display and profile. Requested settings are targets, not guaranteed results. See [stream quality](docs/STREAM_QUALITY.md) for the measurements. ## Install the alpha 1. Download `OpenNOW-PS5-0.1.zip` and `SHA256SUMS` from [Releases](https://github.com/Portablelle/opennow-ps5/releases). 2. Verify the ZIP against its entry in `SHA256SUMS` using `shasum -a 256` or `sha256sum`. If you download every listed asset, you can use `shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS`. 3. Extract the archive. Install the included `PPSA99082` folder through a compatible native homebrew directory loader, such as ShadowMountPlus. Follow your loader's registration procedure and check that this title ID is unused. 4. Before replacing an existing installation, close OpenNOW completely and retain a backup of its title folder. 5. Open the app once to create `/data/opennow/config` (or repair directory permissions after an update), then upload `launch-age.txt` into that `config` folder via FTP containing your age as an integer from 0 to 120. Ensure the uploaded file is readable by the app (for example, mode `0644`). This personal configuration is required for session requests and is excluded from the release. Existing `/data/opennow/launch-age.txt` files remain supported when the new file is absent. Only the `config` folder allows uploads by other users; saved login files stay in the parent directory with owner-only file permissions. Do not delete `/data/opennow` to fix an upload problem, as it also holds your saved login. 6. Open the app and authenticate using NVIDIA's device authorization page shown on screen. Check that `ACCOUNT SAVED` appears. Circle in the menu closes the app while preserving the saved login; L1+R1 together signs out and removes it. Requires a PS5 environment that can run native homebrew titles, a GeForce NOW account with suitable streaming capabilities, and a compatible display for the requested mode. The package has been tested in one homebrew console environment; compatibility with other firmware/loader combinations is unverified. This is a directory package, not a retail PS5 store application or a PKG installer. ## Controls | Control | Action | | --- | --- | | Cross | Authenticate or launch the selected game/store | | D-pad | Select a game/store | | L1 | Cycle available stream profiles before launch | | Square | Load the catalog | | Triangle | Open the catalog search keyboard | | R1 | Load the next catalog page | | Circle | Close the app from the menu; cancel text entry in the search keyboard | | L1+R1 together | Sign out and remove the saved login | | Options + touchpad | Stop gameplay streaming | | Touchpad alone during streaming | Toggle virtual mouse / gamepad | | Right stick in virtual mouse mode | Move the remote pointer | | R2 / L2 in virtual mouse mode | Left / right mouse button (hold to drag) | | D-pad in virtual mouse mode | Vertical / horizontal scrolling | | Square in virtual mouse mode | Cycle slow / normal / fast pointer speed | | Triangle in virtual mouse mode | Open / close the remote keyboard | The remote keyboard uses US QWERTY, matching the session's requested layout. Navigate with the D-pad, press Cross to type, Square for Backspace, Options for Enter and Circle to close. L1 toggles Shift and R1 switches between letters and symbols. Enter, Escape, Tab, arrows, Shift, Ctrl and Alt also have selectable keys; Ctrl and Alt apply to subsequent strokes until toggled off. The local feedback always shows asterisks and never stores or logs a plaintext input string. Remote fields remain responsible for their own password masking. Closing the keyboard, leaving virtual mode, disconnecting the controller or stopping the stream cancels pending strokes and releases successfully sent keys and mouse buttons. Failed releases are retried while the input channel is available. This implementation targets launcher logins and menus. It includes software-video and native GPU overlays, but remote cursor capture, text entry and HDR overlay appearance still require console validation. USB keyboard/mouse support is not included. Virtual keyboard/mouse controls are included in 0.0.6. In the search keyboard, use the D-pad to select a character and Cross to type it. Square deletes a character, Triangle clears the text, Options submits the search and Circle cancels. R1 advances through search results; Square in the catalog returns to the full catalog. For existing installations, artwork files can be cached in the registered title metadata. Use the loader's supported refresh or re-registration procedure if the home-screen icon or background remains stale. Replacing the title folder alone may not refresh the background reference. ## Audio selection Press **R2** in the catalog before launch to cycle **Auto / Stereo / 5.1 / 7.1**. Auto probes the PS5 eight-channel AudioOut port; it does not detect physical speakers. GFN must offer a valid multichannel Opus layout before surround is selected. Unsupported offers fall back to offered stereo audio. All formats use 48 kHz; requested bitrate ceilings are 256 kb/s stereo, 384 kb/s 5.1 and 510 kb/s 7.1. Actual received bitrate remains server-controlled. The adaptive queue, RED recovery and in-band FEC/PLC protect continuity while bounding accumulated latency. Private diagnostics distinguish requested and negotiated channels, queue depth and received codec bitrate. See [stream quality](docs/STREAM_QUALITY.md) for details and remaining limitations. ## Privacy NVIDIA login credentials and the device identity are saved in `/data/opennow/account.bin`, outside the installed title, so closing the app, rebooting the PS5 and replacing the app preserve the login. The app restores and renews the saved login automatically; temporary network failures keep the saved credentials and retry. L1+R1 together in the menu signs out and removes the saved login; closing with Circle or stopping a game session keeps it. NVIDIA can still require a new sign-in if the renewal credentials expire or are revoked. The UI reports `ACCOUNT SAVED` or `ACCOUNT NOT SAVED`. The file uses owner-only permissions and contains sensitive credentials without encryption; keep it private. Public source and packages exclude local configuration, account data, session logs, console dumps and captured gameplay. Private bounded diagnostics can be written under `/data/opennow`; an explicit local marker enables a short video capture for troubleshooting. Do not upload that directory when reporting an issue. ## Build and test Host tests use synthetic fixtures and do not require a console or account: ```sh bash tools/test-port.sh ``` Native Docker builds in this project's workflow run on a separate Linux build host over SSH. Configure the `vps` SSH alias and remote workspace for your environment. The GPU build additionally requires preparing the pinned public GPU SDK/runtime; see [native hardware video](docs/NATIVE_HARDWARE_VIDEO.md) and [dependency/source provenance](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md). ```sh # Software compatibility build bash tools/build-vps.sh # GPU build, after preparing .deps/gpu/sdk on the build host bash tools/build-gpu-vps.sh ``` Generated packages are written to `dist/`. CI checks host behavior; it does not reproduce or validate PS5 hardware execution. No proprietary Sony SDK or firmware module is included. ## Development and licensing ### Credits **Credit goes to [OpenCloudGaming](https://github.com/OpenCloudGaming), the [OpenNOW](https://github.com/OpenCloudGaming/OpenNOW) authors and contributors, and the [OpenNOW-Switch](https://github.com/OpenCloudGaming/OpenNOW-Switch) contributors.** Their open-source work provides the authentication, streaming protocol and transport foundations that made this native PS5 adaptation possible. This repository is an independent PS5 port prototype, not the official OpenNOW application. The PS5 platform, decoder and GPU work also builds on public projects including ProsperoLight, the PS5 hardware video research, Kodi PS5, ps5-opengl and the native application boilerplate. Their specific roles, licenses and source revisions are retained in the third-party notices and source headers. See [port history and measured results](docs/PORT_STATUS.md), [release notes](docs/releases/0.1.md) and [contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md). Other boilerplate documentation covers optional tooling and may describe workflows outside the GPU release path. The combined native application is **GPL-3.0-or-later**. Third-party components retain their notices in [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md), `licenses/` and source headers. Exact upstream revisions and hashes are recorded in [upstream-lock.json](upstream-lock.json). Public dependency retrieval/build scripts and local GPU modifications are included; no captured game content is distributed.

latestRelease.name: OpenNOW PS5 0.1 — Final prerelease
latestRelease.body:
# OpenNOW PS5 0.1

This is the final planned prerelease before a stable release. It packages the
current repository, including the launch-age FTP fix from #1/#2. Public tag
`0.1` maps to native content version `00.002.038`, title ID `PPSA99082`.
The version number does not imply new console validation or stable compatibility.

## Changes since 0.0.7

- Create `/data/opennow/config` for launch-age uploads by FTP processes running
  as another user, and repair directory permissions at startup.
- Keep saved account files in the parent directory, writable only by its owner,
  with owner-only credential file permissions.
- Read `/data/opennow/config/launch-age.txt` first. Existing
  `/data/opennow/launch-age.txt` remains supported when the new file is absent.
- Bound configuration reads, reject symlinks and avoid waiting on FIFO writers.
  Invalid configuration still blocks launch rather than inventing an age.
- Explain the new configuration path and update procedure in the README.

The package retains persistent NVIDIA login, controller-driven catalog search,
video profile selection, virtual keyboard/mouse, Auto / Stereo / 5.1 / 7.1
audio selection, multichannel Opus decoding and adaptive audio buffering.

## Validation and limitations

Host streaming and protocol regressions passed with ASan/UBSan. Targeted
persistence/configuration regressions cover old directory migration, restrictive
umasks, preserved login contents and permissions, legacy fallback, invalid ages,
symlinks and FIFO inputs. The native GPU package builds on the Linux VPS and
passes its import audit. Release archives include a per-file manifest and
SHA-256 checksums.

This new build has not been installed or tested on a PS5. The FTP fix still
requires confirmation with the affected server/loader environment. Live surround
negotiation and speaker placement remain pending. Auto checks AudioOut port
capability, not physical speakers or HDMI receiver capabilities; some GFN seats
offer only stereo. Prior FPS/HDR observations do not establish new results for
this package. Native RTSP/NVST transport, a full A/V synchronization clock,
lossless audio and Atmos remain outside this build.

## Installation

Download `OpenNOW-PS5-0.1.zip`, `OpenNOW-PS5-0.1.manifest.json` and `SHA256SUMS`.
Verify checksums, close OpenNOW and retain a rollback copy before replacing the
complete `PPSA99082` folder through a compatible native homebrew directory loader.
Preserve `/data/opennow`, which contains your saved login and personal configuration.

Open the updated app once to prepare the configuration directory. Upload
`launch-age.txt` to `/data/opennow/config/`, containing your age as an integer
from 0 to 120, and ensure it is readable by the app (for example, mode `0644`).
An existing age file at the old path needs no migration unless you want to use
the new FTP location. An invalid new file will not fall back to the old age.

This is a directory package, not a retail PKG. The source archive contains tracked
sources, upstream pins and licenses. Assets exclude personal configuration,
credentials, diagnostics, captures, dumps and proprietary SDK binaries. This
project is unofficial and unaffiliated with Sony or NVIDIA; upstream and
third-party credits and licenses remain included.
