repos.name: ps5-dump-forge
repos.description: A toolkit for working with PS5 game dumps. Cross-platform - including the PS5 itself.
repos.readme: Runs on PS5, Windows, macOS and Linux, and can convert and edit any format: game `folders`, `exfat`, `ffpkg`, `ffpfs`, `ffpfsc` and `FPKG (pkg)` packages, straight from `zip`, `7z` and `rar` too, with `zstd` and experimental `LZ4` asset packs for AMPR games. Also supports **transfers and on-the-fly conversion** on all platforms, with the interface translated into **11 languages**. | Platform | Runs on | You get | |---|---|---| | **PS5** | With an ELF loader | The payload (`.elf`); the UI opens in any browser | | **macOS** | 11 or later, Apple Silicon and Intel (one universal zip) | App + CLI | | **Windows** | 10 or 11 on x86-64, 11 on arm64 | App + CLI | | **Linux** | x86-64 or arm64, glibc 2.35+ (e.g. Ubuntu 22.04+) | App (no install, no FUSE) + CLI | ## Features - **Any source to any target**, streamed straight through: no temporary copy, not even the image inside a `.ffpfsc` or a game in an archive. - **Every format ShadowMountPlus mounts**, created and read back, plus the debug FPKG. - **Archives as sources**: a `.zip`, `.7z` or `.rar` holding one game is browsed, converted or packed like a folder. - **Pack**: compress an AMPR game's assets into zstd packs, or experimental LZ4 packs, and unpack them again; a packed game converts to any format like any other. - **Storage**: a **Library** of your games to convert and edit, and a **File explorer** to rename, move and delete files and folders, on a computer a paired PS5's too, with drag and drop between them. - **Package installer on the PS5**: lists every `.pkg` on the console's storage and drives and installs one; a `.pkg` on a computer installs on a paired PS5 from Connect, read over the network. - **Edit** a dump or image: browse its files, rename, delete, add or replace files and folders, then apply the changes in place or by rebuilding the image; extract files and folders from any source. The game card shows the cover, title, required firmware, backport firmware (`fakelib/`), embedded DLC and `param.json`; leftover `.part` files from interrupted jobs are listed under it when there are any. - **Connect, transfers and on-the-fly conversion**: another Forge or a NAS (SMB, FTP, NFS), found by **Autodiscovery**, is a source and an output: convert straight between devices or copy files, nothing staged here. - **One-click install on the PS5** from the desktop app: the console downloads the matching Dump Forge release from GitHub and starts it. Any other ELF payload can be sent the same way. - **Additional content**: a DLC or an update (no `eboot.bin`, a valid `param.json`) is labelled everywhere, editable, and packs into a debug FPKG. - **Fast**: (and furious). ## Transfers and on-the-fly conversion A paired Forge (a computer or a PS5) and a saved NAS (SMB, FTP or NFS) are sources and outputs like a local folder. - **On-the-fly conversion**: Convert reads a game folder or image on one device and writes the new image or folder onto another, streamed over the network: nothing is copied to this device first, a debug FPKG included. An image is written as a `.part`, read back over the network to verify it, then renamed into place; a folder is written file by file. A `.pkg` or an archive source has to be on this device. - **File Transfer** (Connect tab) copies files and folders from any device to a folder on any other, a peer to peer copy relayed through this one. It runs beside a conversion, and every file is checked by its size when it lands. Nothing there is ever replaced. - **Phones and browsers**: in the web UI, File Transfer uploads files from the browser's device or downloads one to it. ## Pack: zstd and LZ4 asset packs Only for games whose `eboot.bin` imports `libSceAmpr` (AMPR titles). The app's **Pack** tab compresses a game's assets into packs that a runtime installed at `fakelib/libSceAmpr.sprx` reads back on the console while the game runs. Choose the kind of packs: - **zstd** (the default): zstd packs (`ampr_zstd.index` + `ampr_zstd-NNN.pak`) at **Fast** (zstd 5), **Medium** (9) or **Max** (19), into a game folder or straight into an `.ffpkg`, `.exfat` or `.ffpfs`. A zstd packed game gets **Unpack** instead, into a folder, `.ffpkg`, `.exfat`, `.ffpfs` or fpkg. - **LZ4** (experimental): ampr_emu's LZ4 packs (`ampr_assets.index` + `ampr_assets-NNN.pak`) at **Fast** (LZ4), **Medium** (LZ4 HC 9) or **Max** (LZ4 HC 12), into an LZ4 packed folder or straight into an `.ffpkg`, `.exfat` or `.ffpfs`. The runtime is **ampr-emu-ng** (the default) or the bundled [ampr_emu](https://github.com/drakmor/ampr_emu) 0.4.2.1, an upstream test build with which some games crash when saving. An LZ4 packed game gets **Unpack**. Both kinds are read by **ampr-emu-ng**, the bundled runtime that Pack installs (an LZ4 Pack with ampr_emu excepted). ShadowMount+ can update `fakelib/` and replace it: turn that off for packed games. ## Storage The **Storage** tab holds the **Library** (the games found in a folder you choose, or on the PS5's drives) and a **File explorer**. Both open a game in Edit or Convert, and the Library deletes one after you confirm. The File explorer renames, moves and deletes at once (a delete after you confirm): a delete is permanent (no Trash), a move stays on the same drive and never replaces anything, and anything an unfinished job uses is refused. On the PS5, images ShadowMountPlus has mounted are tagged **Mounted** in the File explorer and can't be edited, renamed, moved or deleted, and both views show the console's free space. On the PS5, the **Package installer** view lists every `.pkg` on the console's storage and drives, with its title, version and kind (game, patch, additional content). **Install** (also on a `.pkg` row of the File explorer) asks first, then hands the package to the console's installer, which fetches it from Dump Forge: keep Dump Forge running until the job ends. If the game is already installed, the console deletes that copy first. ## Editing a game The **Edit** tab lists a game's files. Rename or delete them, and add files or folders with **Add files**, **Add folder**, or by dragging them onto the list (onto a folder's row to add them inside it). A file of the same name is replaced once you confirm. Nothing changes until **Apply**: **Undo** takes back the last change (a drop of several files is one) and **Discard all** drops them all. New, replaced and renamed entries are badged. Before you press Apply the tab says how the changes will go in: - **In place**: written straight into the image. `.exfat` and `.ffpkg` take any change that fits the image's free space (an image never grows); `.ffpfs` takes deletes, renames and replacements that fit in the old file's space. The undo file needs room beside the image. An image marked unclean, or a `.ffpkg` not laid out the way Forge writes one, takes Rebuild instead. If the check after writing fails, or the computer or console stops part way, the image is put back from an undo file beside it (`.forge-undo`); one left by a crash is restored on the next edit. - **Rebuild**: a new image of the same format is written beside the original from the original plus your changes, verified, then put in its place. It needs free space beside the original for the new image (the tab says how much: for `.ffpfsc` and `.pkg` it can be more than the original's size). It is the only way for `.ffpfsc` and `.pkg`, and the way when the changes don't fit in place. - **Changed directly**: a game folder is changed file by file, with no undo file. ## Connect The **Connect** tab pairs this Forge with another one on the local network (**Autodiscovery**, which also runs at every start, or an address under **Add a device**), and you allow it on the other device when both screens show the same check number. A NAS (SMB, FTP, NFS) is saved the same way; one saved by IP that comes back on a new address under the same name moves there by itself. While online, paired and saved devices are tabs in the file pickers: their games are converted and their folders take outputs, but in Edit they are only browsed and extracted from. **File Transfer** copies files and folders between any of them. A paired PS5's **Install pkg** installs a `.pkg` from this computer on the console, which reads it over the network. In a browser, the tab's QR code opens the page on a phone, and File Transfer can upload to or download from the device serving the page. In the desktop app, **Dump Forge on PS5** installs Dump Forge on a console in one click: type its address and press **Install on PS5**, and the app downloads the release matching it (or the latest) from GitHub and sends it to the console's ELF loader, which starts it (the console needs no internet). **Send a payload** sends any other ELF file from the computer the same way. It needs an ELF loader that listens on the network (port 9021). ## Download and run Every release archive on the Releases page holds the app and the `ps5-dump-forge` command-line tool. Nothing to install; the app writes nothing beyond its own WebView data, so keep it in any folder you can write to. At every start the app and the console's page check GitHub for a newer release and offer it (on the PS5, **Update** downloads it and hands it to the ELF loader). ### PS5 (jailbroken, with an ELF loader) - **Load it** with any ELF loader: send `ps5-dump-forge--ps5.elf` to elfldr's port 9021 (`nc -w 3 9021 < ps5-dump-forge--ps5.elf`), or list it in an autoloader's `autoload.txt`, or use **Install on PS5** in the desktop app's Connect tab. A notification says Dump Forge is launched; open it from its icon. - **Open the UI** from the Dump Forge icon, or in any browser on the same network: `http://:8095`. In the console's browser, **L2** / **R2** switch tabs. ### macOS (11 or later) Get `ps5-dump-forge--macos-universal.zip` (Apple Silicon and Intel) and unzip it anywhere. The app is ad-hoc signed only (no Apple Developer ID, not notarized), so macOS blocks the first launch ("PS5 Dump Forge is damaged" or "cannot be opened"). Use **one** of these: 1. **Terminal** (every macOS version), in the folder that holds the app, then double-click it: ```sh xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "PS5 Dump Forge.app" ``` 2. **System Settings.** Double-click the app once and dismiss the warning, then in System Settings → Privacy & Security, scroll down to the message about PS5 Dump Forge and click **Open Anyway**. ### Windows (10 or 11 on x86-64, 11 on arm64) - x86-64: `ps5-dump-forge--windows-x86-64.zip` uses the Microsoft Edge WebView2 Runtime, which Windows 11 and most Windows 10 PCs already have. Without it, get `...-windows-x86-64-webview2.zip`: larger, with its own copy of the runtime in a `WebView2` folder. - arm64: `ps5-dump-forge--windows-arm64.zip` (uses the WebView2 Runtime Windows 11 ships). Extract it to a folder you can write to (not Program Files, not a network share): `PS5 Dump Forge.exe` keeps its WebView data in a `data/webview` folder beside itself. The app is unsigned, so SmartScreen may block the first launch: click **More info**, then **Run anyway**. If WebView2 is missing or broken, the app says what to do instead of showing a blank window. ### Linux (x86-64 or arm64, glibc 2.35 or later, e.g. Ubuntu 22.04 or newer) Extract `ps5-dump-forge--linux-x86-64.tar.gz` or `...-linux-arm64.tar.gz` (`tar -xzf`) to a folder you can write to and run `./forge.sh`. No FUSE, no install; keep `PS5 Dump Forge.AppDir` next to `forge.sh` (its WebView data goes in a `data/webview` folder beside it). ### Command-line tool Every desktop archive also has `ps5-dump-forge` (`ps5-dump-forge.exe` on Windows): ```sh ./ps5-dump-forge inspect PPSA01234.exfat ./ps5-dump-forge convert ~/Games/PPSA01234 --to ffpkg # folder | exfat | ffpkg | ffpfs | ffpfsc | pkg (debug FPKG) ./ps5-dump-forge convert ~/Games/PPSA01234 --to ffpfsc --inner ffpkg # inner: ffpkg (default) | exfat | ffpfs ./ps5-dump-forge convert ~/Games/PPSA01234 --to ffpfsc --level 6 # zlib level 0 (store) .. 9 (smallest), default 6 ./ps5-dump-forge convert ~/Games/PPSA01234 --to pkg --kraken fast # fast (default) | balanced | smallest | stored ./ps5-dump-forge convert ~/Games/PPSA01234 --to exfat --full-verify # check every byte, not a sample ./ps5-dump-forge convert Game.part1.rar --to ffpkg --password-stdin # archive source; password from stdin ``` ## Build Rust (latest stable) and Node.js: ```sh cargo test --workspace --release cd app && npm ci && npm run tauri dev ``` On Linux the app also needs Tauri's WebKitGTK build dependencies (Debian/Ubuntu package names, as CI installs them): ```sh sudo apt-get install libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev libgtk-3-dev librsvg2-dev libayatana-appindicator3-dev patchelf file ``` The PS5 payload builds in Docker (any macOS or Linux host with Docker and Node) with `ps5/build.sh`; the rest of its commands are in [ps5/README.md](ps5/README.md). See [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) for the layout and the format rules, and [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md) for the UI design system. ## Thanks Big thanks to **[PhantomPtr](https://github.com/phantomptr)** for **[ps5upload](https://github.com/phantomptr/ps5upload)**. Its Rust engine is the reference implementation this project learned the PS5 formats from: the FPKG package builder and reader (PFS, PFSC, Kraken, CNT/FIH, PlayGo, debug license), and the exFAT and UFS2 readers. Its crates are vendored here (`vendor/`, v7.0.22). Big thanks to **[drakmor](https://github.com/drakmor)**, author of **[ShadowMountPlus](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus)**, for the mount side this tool writes for and for help along the way: the image-building scripts (`mkexfat_macos.sh` and friends) whose sizing and layout rules the `.exfat`/`.ffpkg` writers follow, the format guidance in SMP's README and release notes, and ppr-patch, which makes debug `.pkg` installs possible. Thanks again to **[drakmor](https://github.com/drakmor)** for **[ampr_emu](https://github.com/drakmor/ampr_emu)** (GPL-3.0-or-later), the runtime that first made LZ4 asset packs work: its 0.4.2.1 release runtime is embedded unmodified, with its source archive in `vendor/ampr_emu/`. **[Lazy_AMPR](https://github.com/Nazky/Lazy_AMPR)** by Nazky was a reference for the pack rules (no code taken). The LZ4 library (BSD-2-Clause) that Forge and ampr_emu compile in, and the HDE64 notice, are in `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md`. Thanks to **[Xxcco](https://github.com/Xxcco)** for the logo. Credits for other references are in `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md`. ## License GPL-3.0-or-later. See `LICENSE`.

latestRelease.name: v0.5.0
latestRelease.body:
## The big one - new Pack tab, faster runtime and pkg install

## New

- **Custom ampr-emu runtime.** An optional runtime with up to 8x faster load speeds (more information here: [ampr-emu-ng](https://github.com/quer3q/ampr-emu-ng)).
- **New zstd pack format.** Compress an AMPR game's assets into the zstd pack format, close to fpkg in size and play speed.
- **LZ4 packs got a compression level selector.** Choose **Fast** (plain LZ4, the default), **Medium** (LZ4 HC 9) or **Max** (LZ4 HC 12): higher levels give smaller packs and take longer to pack.
- **Package installer on the PS5.** Storage has a new Package installer view that lists every `.pkg` on the console. Install it or delete it from there, or from a `.pkg` row in the File explorer.
- **Install pkg from a PC.** In Connect, a paired PS5 has an Install pkg button: pick a `.pkg` on the computer and the console installs it, reading it over the network.
- **PS5 tabs in the File explorer.** On a computer, each paired PS5 that is online gets a tab next to This device, with rename, move and delete. Drag a row onto another device's tab to copy it there, or drop files from the system to copy them in.
- **New logo** by [Xxcco](https://github.com/Xxcco).

## Changes

- **LZ4 traces removed.** LZ4 packing uses its built-in rules only.

repos.name: pico8-ps5
repos.description: Run the official PICO-8 (Linux build, bring your own license) as a native app on jailbroken PS5
repos.readme:
# PICO-8 for PS5

Runs the **official PICO-8 for Linux** on a jailbroken PS5 as a native app with its own icon on the Home screen. It boots straight into Splore and works with the DualSense, with sound, and with cart downloads from the BBS. This is a "bring your own license" project: PICO-8 itself is not included. You need your own copy of PICO-8 (the Linux 64-bit build, bought at ; tested with 0.2.7). **Unofficial project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Lexaloffle.** ## Installation No building and no commands: you copy one folder to the PS5. **Requirements on the PS5** (tested on a single console): - kstuff and ShadowMountPlus running; - elfldr listening on `127.0.0.1:9021`, which usually comes with kstuff/Payload Manager. The app uses elfldr to get access to `/data` (sandbox elevation); - a way to copy files to the PS5, such as an FTP server. **Steps**, with the `PPSA99808.zip` from the [latest release](https://github.com/RafaelNGP/pico8-ps5/releases/latest): 1. extract the zip and copy the `PPSA99808` folder, as a whole, to `/data/homebrew/`; 2. from your PICO-8 Linux zip, copy `pico8_dyn` and `pico8.dat` into `PPSA99808/pico8/`; 3. within ~15 s, ShadowMountPlus adds the **PICO-8** icon to the Home screen. ``` /data/homebrew/PPSA99808/ the app folder (named after its Title ID) eboot.bin the loader + SDL2 + libcurl/mbedTLS sandbox-elevator.elf elevation helper (only accepts PPSA99808) cacert.pem CA certificates for Splore's HTTPS sce_module/libc.prx boilerplate runtime sce_sys/param.json, icon0.png pico8/pico8_dyn, pico8.dat your PICO-8 files README.txt, LICENSE, licenses/ /data/pico8/ created by the app .lexaloffle/pico-8/ config, favourites, downloaded carts and saves loader.log log of the last run ``` If a file is missing, or if `pico8_dyn` is a different version, the app shows a notification. To update, close the app and copy the new `PPSA99808` folder over the old one. If the Home screen keeps the old icon, delete the PICO-8 icon from the Home screen (only the icon, not the folder): ShadowMountPlus adds it again within ~15 s. Saves live in `/data/pico8`, outside the app folder, so they are kept. ## Known limitations - USB keyboards and the on-screen keyboard don't work: `libSceKeyboard` and `libSceImeDialog` don't load inside an app. Splore and games work with the controller. - Tested on a single PS5. Other firmware versions may need adjustments. If the app closes or freezes, `/data/pico8/loader.log` shows which files were used and, after a crash, the registers, the stack and the last 256 libc/SDL calls. ## Building Only needed for development. To just play, use the zip. **On the PC** (Linux): - [ps5-payload-sdk](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk) in `/opt/ps5-payload-sdk`; - `make`, `ninja`, `cmake`, `clang`/`lld`/`llvm-ar`, `git`, `curl`, `wget`, `unzip`, `zip` and `python3`. On Fedora, `llvm-config` comes from the `llvm-devel` package; - your PICO-8 Linux copy in `~/pico-8/` (or in `PICO8_DIR`), used by `make upload-data`. ```bash cd pico8_loader export PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK=/opt/ps5-payload-sdk export PS5_HOST=192.168.0.50 # your PS5's IP (FTP on port 2121); or put # "PS5_HOST := " in pico8_loader/local.mk make # builds the app into pico8_app/build/PPSA99808 make install-app # builds the app and uploads it to /data/homebrew/PPSA99808 make upload-data # once: uploads pico8_dyn and pico8.dat to PPSA99808/pico8/ make log # prints /data/pico8/loader.log make release # builds release//PPSA99808.zip ``` The first build downloads and compiles the PS5 port of SDL2, libcurl, mbedTLS and the native app boilerplate, which takes a few minutes. `install-app` needs the app to be closed on the PS5, because FTP refuses to overwrite an `eboot.bin` that is in use. The `make release` zip has the `PPSA99808` folder at its root, as the [PS5 homebrew catalog](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-homebrew-catalog/blob/main/docs/artifact-formats.md) expects, with a `README.txt` and the license notices inside it. Raise `contentVersion` in `pico8_app/sce_sys/param.json` for every release: consoles use it to detect updates. ## Layout | Folder | What it is | |---|---| | `pico8_loader/` | the loader: loads `pico8_dyn` and binds its imports to the PS5's libc and SDL2. See its [README](pico8_loader/README.md). | | `pico8_app/` | packages the loader as a native app (`eboot.bin`), plus the package texts in `release/`. | | `deps/` | build scripts for SDL2, libcurl and the app, plus patches and dlmalloc. | | `mmap_probe/`, `app_probe/` | feasibility tests run on the console (fixed addresses and code execution). | ## License PICO-8 for PS5 is free software: you can redistribute it and/or modify it under the terms of the GNU General Public License, version 3 or (at your option) any later version. See [LICENSE](LICENSE). The app bundles code under other licenses, all compatible with the GPL-3.0: [ps5-native-app-boilerplate](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-native-app-boilerplate) (GPL-3.0-or-later), SDL2 (zlib), curl (curl license), mbedTLS (Apache-2.0) and dlmalloc (MIT-0). Their notices ship in the release zip under `licenses/`. PICO-8 is (c) Lexaloffle Games and is not included: you need your own copy. The app icon (`pico8_app/sce_sys/icon0.png`) is the PICO-8 logo, (c) Lexaloffle Games; it is not covered by the GPL.

latestRelease.name: v0.1.2
latestRelease.body:
**PICO-8 for PS5** runs the official PICO-8 for Linux (bring your own license) as a native app with its own Home icon on a jailbroken PS5.

**Unofficial project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Lexaloffle.** PICO-8 itself is not included: you need your own PICO-8 Linux 64-bit copy (tested with 0.2.7).

## Installation

1. Extract `PPSA99808.zip` and copy the `PPSA99808` folder, as a whole, to `/data/homebrew/` on the PS5.
2. From your PICO-8 Linux zip, copy `pico8_dyn` and `pico8.dat` into `PPSA99808/pico8/`.
3. Within ~15 s, ShadowMountPlus adds the PICO-8 icon to the Home screen.

**Requirements:** kstuff, ShadowMountPlus, and elfldr listening on `127.0.0.1:9021` (used to get access to `/data`). Full instructions are in `PPSA99808/README.txt`.

**Updating from v0.1.x:** close the app and copy the new `PPSA99808` folder over the old one. Your `pico8/` files and your saves are kept. If the Home screen keeps the old icon, delete the PICO-8 icon from the Home screen (only the icon, not the folder) and ShadowMountPlus adds it again within ~15 s.

## Changes since v0.1.1

- **PICO-8 logo as the app icon**, replacing the generic "P8" icon.
- **New package layout:** the asset is now always called `PPSA99808.zip`, with the `PPSA99808` folder at its root (the format used by the PS5 homebrew catalog). `README.txt`, `LICENSE` and `licenses/` are now inside that folder. Direct link to the latest version: https://github.com/RafaelNGP/pico8-ps5/releases/latest/download/PPSA99808.zip
- **`contentVersion` 01.001.002**, so consoles and stores can detect updates.

## Known limitations

- USB keyboards and the on-screen keyboard don't work.
- Tested on a single PS5. Other firmware versions may need adjustments.

**Reporting a problem:** please attach `/data/pico8/loader.log` and say which firmware you're on.

The app icon is the PICO-8 logo, (c) Lexaloffle Games; it is not covered by the GPL. The SHA-256 of the zip is in `PPSA99808.zip.sha256`.

repos.name: Visual-PS5
repos.description: IDE for PS5 homebrew visual composer
repos.readme:
# PS5 Homebrew Studio

**Release 1.1.56 · IDE visual local para Windows.** Integra un lienzo lógico redimensionable (inicia en 1920×1080), análisis de flujos, generación de código C# para SharpProspero, pantallas C++20 para OpenGL/Vulkan con salida adaptada a la superficie activa —incluido 4K—, grafos Vulkan Compute en GLSL 450, un editor visual especializado en niveles de plataformas 3D AGC y edición/compilación C/C++ de payloads PS5 a ELF con el SDK offline. El lienzo lógico de diseño es independiente del perfil de salida de referencia: se pueden previsualizar tamaños 720p, 900p, 1080p, 1440p, 4K o personalizados sin alterar las coordenadas del proyecto ni fijar la resolución de ejecución. ## Escena de juego 3D · 1.1.56 - Construye recorridos en una vista 3D orbitable; gira la cámara con el botón derecho, desplázala con Mayús + arrastrar, acerca con la rueda y usa los controles de órbita/altura o Restablecer cámara. - Arrastra plataformas y objetos sobre el plano del nivel: el editor convierte el movimiento de pantalla a coordenadas X/Z según la vista actual. - Añade seis mallas procedurales —cubo, cristal facetado, esfera, cilindro, cono y pirámide— desde Componentes. Selecciónalas o arrástralas en la escena y ajusta forma, posición, dimensiones, giro y color desde el inspector. La caja opcional bloquea los laterales y la cara inferior, y permite aterrizar encima. - Ajusta por plataforma el ancho X, grosor Y, fondo Z y desfase de su caja sólida; el lienzo muestra el volumen completo y los tiradores permiten cambiar X/Z. - La validación del IDE y de compilación avisa si el inicio, checkpoints, cristales o meta quedan fuera de una ruta alcanzable. Las cajas de colisión siguen sus tiradores en cualquier orientación de cámara. - Marca visualmente inicio, cristales, checkpoints y meta; configura movimiento, salto y gravedad sin editar constantes en C. - Ajusta cámara, paleta y condición de victoria desde el inspector; enlaza botones e interruptores con acciones de juego en Flujos y controla el juego con DualSense. - El IDE genera el motor AGC, la escena y el puente de interfaz desde el modelo visual. El fuente aparece en Código en modo de solo lectura; el código manual es una opción avanzada separada. - Antes de sustituir código manual existente, el IDE guarda una copia de seguridad dentro de `src/`. - Consulta [la guía de escenas de juego](docs/GAME_SCENE_EDITOR.md). El editor AGC actual está centrado en niveles de plataformas y no es todavía un motor general de escenas como Unity: no importa mallas arbitrarias ni ofrece animación esquelética, materiales PBR ni componentes de física de propósito general. Las colisiones son cajas alineadas con los ejes del mundo; no rotan con una malla girada. ## PS5 Payload SDK · 1.1.28 - Edita la entrada `src/main.c` o `src/main.cpp` desde el IDE y compílala con el `ps5-payload-dev/sdk` preinstalado en WSL, sin acceso a Internet. La imagen offline incluye las bibliotecas y cabeceras PacBrew fijadas para proyectos payload; una distro WSL existente obtiene una caché local desde el archivo versionado en `toolchains/`, sin modificar la distro. - El IDE conserva cada compilación, comprueba la cabecera ELF64 little-endian para x86-64 y ofrece el fichero `.elf` para descargar. - La autorización para escribir el proyecto y para ejecutar Make/Clang se solicita por separado en cada operación. El ELF no se despliega ni se ejecuta en la consola. - ShadowMountPlus puede abrirse como proyecto upstream de varios archivos: se conserva su `Makefile` y se ejecuta su target original. El IDE prepara `libmicrohttpd`, `libpng`, `sqlite3`, `json-c`, `zlib`, cabeceras y stubs desde el artefacto PacBrew fijado localmente; no instala paquetes en WSL ni descarga dependencias. ## Vulkan Compute · 1.1.28 - Edita grafos con pases ordenados, imágenes de almacenamiento, bindings, tamaño de grupo, despacho y resolución de destino. - Compila GLSL 450 a SPIR-V para Vulkan 1.2 con `glslangValidator` local en WSL; el flujo no descarga herramientas ni afirma que el shader se haya ejecutado en GPU. - Importa informes GPU con identidad de revisión y SHA-256 de cada shader, junto a métricas de tiempo, PSNR, SSIM y comparación de salida cuando el runtime las proporciona. - Consulta [el flujo Vulkan Compute](docs/VULKAN_COMPUTE.md) y [el esquema de informe GPU](docs/vulkan-compute-report.schema.json). ## Runtime nativo autónomo · 1.1.18 - Los títulos visuales OpenGL aplican un perfil de runtime propio del IDE. El framework upstream aporta el renderer y los componentes gráficos, pero su shell de galería deja de controlar el título generado. - L1, R1 y Touchpad no se reservan para cambiar de diseño ni abrir un panel informativo. El InputFrame llega a la pantalla generada sin filtrado; si el código generado no implementa una acción, esos botones no hacen nada. - El perfil se registra en .ps5hs-native-runtime.json, es idempotente y falla de forma segura si la estructura upstream cambia. - Se aplica al generar un título y al compilar proyectos visuales OpenGL anteriores reconocibles; no altera proyectos de galería importados que no proceden del lienzo de Homebrew Studio. - Vulkan conserva su pantalla directa; mantener OPTIONS para salir sigue siendo el comportamiento documentado de la plantilla. ## Control de modificaciones nativas · 1.1.11 - Antes de generar o compilar títulos nativos, autoriza por separado el generador, la integración del código visual, las herramientas de build y cualquier conversión de recursos de presentación o fuente TTF. - Las casillas parten desactivadas en cada operación. Un permiso concedido en una operación anterior no autoriza la siguiente. - Los cambios controlados por el IDE se registran en `.ps5hs-modifications.json`, con hashes SHA-256 anteriores y posteriores cuando cambian archivos. Desmarcar un permiso no revierte cambios ya aplicados. - La operación visual comprueba los permisos necesarios para recursos de presentación y fuentes personalizadas antes de crear o modificar el proyecto. ## Capas y lienzo · 1.1.9 - Los proyectos visuales antiguos sin orden explícito colocan paneles y tarjetas al fondo en vez de ocultar el contenido. - En **Jerarquía**, usa `◎` para aislar temporalmente cualquier capa y «Mostrar todas» para recuperar la composición. La selección no cambia el orden visual. - El lienzo conserva la proporción 16:9 y se ajusta al área visible. Los recursos importados muestran su transparencia real cuando contienen un PNG. - UltraPack muestra un estado de preparación distinto del inicio real del trabajo y registra el identificador de tarea. ## Fuentes Unicode para compilación nativa · 1.1.9 En **Recursos**, importa una fuente TrueType `.ttf` (máximo 20 MiB) y selecciónala en el control «Fuente Unicode para compilación nativa». Durante una compilación OpenGL/Vulkan, el servidor recopila los codepoints del modelo y hornea seis atlas SDF. Si la fuente no contiene un glifo requerido, la compilación falla con su codepoint en vez de emitir un título con texto incompleto. El máximo es de 2.500 codepoints únicos; confirma la licencia de la fuente antes de redistribuir el título. Esta función no añade shaping completo ni un IME multilingüe a la entrada en pantalla. ## Nueva vista Estructura · 1.1.6 - La pestaña **Estructura** muestra por separado las pantallas editables del modelo visual y los estados de interfaz detectados en código C++. - Permite buscar menús, consultar el mapa de transiciones, ver etiquetas encontradas y saltar a la declaración o función de dibujo correspondiente. - El mapa de C++ se obtiene mediante análisis estático: las rutas inferidas deben comprobarse en el código y no convierten automáticamente un menú dibujado a mano en componentes editables. ## Corrección urgente 1.1.5 - Se arregla el selector de botones de los diálogos UltraPack y Presentación: ambos quedan operativos en lugar de fallar antes de ejecutar la acción. - Se añade versionado a los scripts JavaScript para que el navegador cargue los archivos de la versión instalada. ## Correcciones y mejoras 1.1.4 - La generación OpenGL nativa ejecuta el `build.ps1` del propio proyecto y reutiliza su SDK local. Evita preparar otra copia del SDK en `toolchains/` antes de compilar y muestra la salida real del script. - En el diálogo **Generar y compilar pantalla nativa** puedes seleccionar antes del build el icono (`icon0.png`), fondo de selección (`pic0.dds`), fondo de lanzamiento (`pic1.dds`) y música (`snd0.at9`). Los conversores y validaciones siguen siendo los de la plantilla upstream. - El selector **Pantallas** permite crear y cambiar entre menús. **Gestionar** permite renombrar o eliminar pantallas; la pestaña **Jerarquía** muestra las capas de la pantalla activa y permite traerlas delante, enviarlas detrás o arrastrarlas para reordenarlas. ## Inicio en Windows 1. Extrae el ZIP en una carpeta con permisos de escritura, por ejemplo `D:\PS5-Homebrew-Studio`. 2. Ejecuta `start.bat`. El lanzador prefiere PowerShell 7 (`pwsh.exe`) y usa Windows PowerShell 5.1 solo como alternativa. 3. El lanzador analiza `runtime/server.ps1` con el parser de PowerShell antes de iniciar el servicio. Si detecta un error, muestra línea/columna y no arranca el servidor. 4. Se abre `http://127.0.0.1:47813/`. Mantén abierta la ventana de PowerShell; cerrarla detiene el servicio. El servicio escucha únicamente en `127.0.0.1`; no expone el sistema de archivos a la red local. Los proyectos del editor se guardan en `Documentos\PS5HomebrewStudio\Projects`. `Ctrl+S` guarda el modelo visual. El editor puede abrirse y usarse sin descargar ningún toolchain. ## Documentación 1.1.18 - [Auditoría de estabilidad y límites de validación](docs/STABILITY-AUDIT.es-ES.md) - Manual español: [docs/MANUAL.es-ES.md](docs/MANUAL.es-ES.md) - English: [docs/USER-MANUAL.en-GB.md](docs/USER-MANUAL.en-GB.md) - Français: [docs/USER-MANUAL.fr-FR.md](docs/USER-MANUAL.fr-FR.md) - Deutsch: [docs/USER-MANUAL.de-DE.md](docs/USER-MANUAL.de-DE.md) - 简体中文: [docs/USER-MANUAL.zh-CN.md](docs/USER-MANUAL.zh-CN.md) - 日本語: [docs/USER-MANUAL.ja-JP.md](docs/USER-MANUAL.ja-JP.md) - Русский: [docs/USER-MANUAL.ru-RU.md](docs/USER-MANUAL.ru-RU.md) - [Solución de permisos WSL](docs/WSL_PERMISSIONS.md) · [Guía de recursos de presentación](docs/PRESENTATION_ASSETS.md) · [Créditos y atribuciones upstream](docs/CREDITS.md) - [Ecosistema de proyectos upstream](docs/PROJECT_ECOSYSTEM.md) · [Matriz de SDK](docs/SDK_MATRIX.md) · [Registro de cambios](docs/CHANGELOG.md) - [Problemas conocidos y estado de validación 1.1.18](docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.es-ES.md) - Fuentes Unicode: [guía en español](docs/UNICODE-FONTS.es-ES.md) · [English guide](docs/UNICODE-FONTS.en-GB.md) La UI de esta versión todavía está en español; los manuales traducidos no representan una localización completa de la interfaz. ## Mejoras de desarrollo 1.1.2 (histórico) - Los títulos nativos incluyen **Presentación** para sustituir `icon0.png`, los fondos independientes `pic0.dds`/`pic1.dds` y la música `snd0.at9` mediante el conversor upstream. - Las imágenes se validan como PNG 512×512 o DDS BC7 3840×2160; el audio debe ser ATRAC9 48 kHz en bucle y ≤2 MiB. El IDE no descarga ni redistribuye el codificador de audio. - Guía: [recursos de presentación](docs/PRESENTATION_ASSETS.md). ## Mejoras de desarrollo 1.1.1 - El panel de proyectos detecta checkouts Git existentes, proyectos nativos y plantillas Vulkan, muestra el perfil de compilación y separa títulos compilables de SDKs, drivers y referencias. - Las plantillas compatibles pueden inicializarse mediante `tools/init-project.sh` o `make init`; los proyectos sin perfil seguro muestran el motivo y no ejecutan un `make` genérico. - La compilación OpenGL prepara Native App Boilerplate y PS5 OpenGL, compila el SDK si falta y configura `PS5_NATIVE_APP_TEMPLATE` y `PS5_OPENGL_PREFIX`. - El formulario de compilación permite ejecutar `make clean` antes de `make`, pero solo si el Makefile declara el target; no se borran artefactos por conjetura. Vulkan conserva su pipeline upstream si no hay un clean validado. - «Cerrar proyecto» descarga el modelo visual y deja el editor en blanco; ofrece guardar o descartar cambios y conserva las carpetas nativas, compilaciones y paquetes. - Se conserva la invocación de UltraPack que funciona en el entorno probado; la interfaz no añade `--verify` automáticamente. ## Cambios de 1.1.0 - Se retiró la integración de lanzamiento mediante emulador para mantener el IDE centrado en títulos comprobables en hardware real. - Se corrigieron los selectores de la interfaz que impedían iniciar las acciones de UltraPack. - El empaquetado se ejecuta como trabajo independiente con registro consultable sin bloquear el servidor local. - Se valida Python 3.10+, se mantiene compatibilidad de argumentos con PowerShell 5.1 y se verifica el artefacto final. - La compilación nativa solo se considera lista para empaquetar cuando hay un `eboot.bin` y `sce_sys/param.json`. - El backend Vulkan instala un runtime de búsqueda/carga de texturas incluso cuando el proyecto no incluye imágenes; el generador ya no emite funciones vacías. - Los flujos con destinos, acciones o pantallas inexistentes se rechazan antes de generar C++. ## Cambios de 1.0.9 - Kyty recibe la ruta de `eboot.bin` explícita y registra los argumentos de lanzamiento. - UltraPack se instala con un entorno Python aislado y dependencias CLI; se valida la ruta configurada. - El empaquetado `.pkg` detecta la ausencia del helper nativo de Windows antes de iniciar. ## Cambios de 1.0.8 - La invocación de UltraPack usa argumentos sin ambigüedad de comillas, ejecuta desde la carpeta del CLI y registra el comando y las salidas estándar/error. ## Cambios de 1.0.7 - Las acciones Kyty/UltraPack persisten en la barra superior y recuerdan la última compilación nativa correcta. - La lectura concurrente de los registros de compilación ya no interrumpe el seguimiento del build. - Se puede cambiar el nombre del destino o autorizar la sustitución de un proyecto propio compatible. - Los fallos de UltraPack incluyen salida, código de salida y estado del artefacto. ## Cambios de 1.0.6 - Compilaciones visuales y proyectos nativos C++ en segundo plano con registro real de WSL/Make/CMake/Ninja consultable durante el proceso. - Estado final explícito y acciones post-compilación para KytyPS5 y UltraPack. - Selector UltraPack para `.ffpfs`, `.ffpfsc` y `.pkg`; PKG puede tener limitaciones en Windows según upstream. - Atlas tipográfico europeo OpenGL de 2048 px para conservar acentos españoles. ## Qué incluye 1.0.4 - Corrige la entrada de compilación Windows de los proyectos nativos: `build.ps1` ejecuta `make -C app` en WSL en lugar de invocar `tools/build.sh` directamente. - Deja que el Makefile upstream aplique las rutas de inclusión `src/`, el SDK OpenGL, las bibliotecas y los import stubs predeterminados antes de compilar. - Conserva la normalización de finales de línea y la verificación SHA-256 del runtime introducidas en 1.0.3. - Corrige la generación de recursos visuales: elimina el uso de `.add()` sobre el mapa de IDs y conserva la detección de colisiones mediante `Map`. - Normaliza a LF los scripts, Makefiles, fuentes nativos y manifiestos `.sha256` de cada proyecto nativo generado, antes de inicializarlo y antes de compilarlo en WSL. - Añade `*.sha256 text eol=lf` a `.gitattributes` del proyecto generado y usa `core.autocrlf=false` al clonar fuentes para evitar que Windows cambie los finales de línea de manifiestos de integridad. - La validación del hash de `libc.prx` permanece habilitada; no se omite ni se debilita la comprobación de integridad. - Catálogo de 34 repositorios reales clasificados como bases, renderers, kits de UI, drivers, dependencias, complementos gráficos y aplicaciones de referencia. Los repositorios con asistencia de IA solo se etiquetan como tal cuando lo declaran explícitamente. - Inicializadores upstream para Native App Boilerplate, PS5 Homebrew UI y PS5 Vulkan Template. El IDE conserva los repositorios originales, sus licencias y los scripts de compilación. - Un generador nativo compartido que convierte las posiciones, dimensiones, estilos, controles y flujos del lienzo en una implementación de `hui::app::Concept`. - Backend OpenGL 4.6: inyecta el concepto generado en `ps5-homebrew-ui`, activa el registro de la pantalla generada y ejecuta `make` del proyecto upstream. Las imágenes vinculadas se predecodifican en el navegador, se limitan a 512×512, se empaquetan como RGBA8 y se suben como texturas OpenGL en tiempo de ejecución (hasta 16 recursos únicos). - Backend Vulkan/RADV: utiliza `PS5_VulkanTemplate` y su `new-title.py`, sustituye la pantalla del módulo UI fijado y ejecuta el build real mediante CMake/Ninja y los scripts de PS5_Vulkan/PS5_Mesa/PS5_PayloadSDK. - La compilación solo se marca correcta si el proceso upstream termina con código cero y existe un `eboot.bin` o ZIP verificable. Los logs reales y la ruta del proyecto permanecen disponibles cuando el build falla. - Reparación acotada de la cadena Vulkan: si la revisión de PS5_Vulkan descargada no contiene `tools/ninja-build.sh` o `tools/build-host-tools.sh` que el build referencia, el IDE restaura los scripts reales del boilerplate compañero y registra su hash y procedencia. No genera stubs vacíos. ## Empaquetado con PS5 UltraPack La barra superior y las tarjetas de proyectos nativos ofrecen **Empaquetar** cuando el título se ha verificado con `eboot.bin` y `sce_sys/param.json`. En **Herramientas** se configura Python 3.10+ y la CLI `backend\\cli.py` de PS5 UltraPack. El IDE permite crear `.ffpfs`, `.ffpfsc` y `.pkg`; el último formato requiere el helper nativo de fPKG y sus dependencias para Windows. Los trabajos se ejecutan fuera del bucle HTTP principal y su salida se consulta desde el IDE. La configuración queda en `.runtime/integrations.json`. Consulta [la guía de UltraPack](docs/INTEGRACION-ULTRAPACK.es-ES.md). La casilla **Verificar el contenido contra el origen** está activada por defecto y pasa `--verify` a UltraPack. La verificación puede requerir más tiempo y memoria. Si el log indica que se omitió o que se comprobaron cero hashes, no describas el resultado como una verificación íntegra del contenido. El mantenedor comunicó que un artefacto `.ffpfsc` concreto se generó y funcionó en hardware real; esto no garantiza compatibilidad universal. ## Editor visual y compilación El editor ofrece un lienzo configurable entre 640×360 y 7680×4320, cuadrícula, arrastrar/soltar, propiedades, jerarquía, temas, pantallas, vista previa, lógica visual, diagnósticos, recursos, guardado, importación/exportación y código inspeccionable. Al cambiar el tamaño se escala la distribución relativa de los componentes. **SharpProspero · Aplicación** genera C# y utiliza su pipeline NativeAOT. Requiere .NET SDK 10 en Windows y dentro de WSL, además del SDK correspondiente. El backend PS5 Payload SDK tiene un editor C separado; no traduce widgets ni acepta código C# como si fuera C. **Native UI · OpenGL 4.6 / C++20** genera una pantalla basada en el contrato real de `ps5-homebrew-ui`. Conserva las coordenadas virtuales y los flujos `notify`, `setText`, `toggleVisibility`, `setValue`, `changeColor` y `navigate`. Los recursos de imagen vinculados se convierten a RGBA8 con un máximo de 512×512 píxeles y se empaquetan en el título; se cargan como texturas OpenGL (máximo 16 IDs únicos por pantalla). **Native UI · Vulkan / RADV / C++20** genera una pantalla del contrato real del módulo `PS5_VKHomebrewUI`, dentro de un título creado por `PS5_VulkanTemplate`. Los componentes y los flujos funcionales se generan como C++; las imágenes se empaquetan como RGBA8, se registran en `ps5/assets.json` y se cargan mediante `VkRenderer::create_texture`. El paquete incluye una nota de licencia para recursos aportados por el usuario, que debe confirmar los derechos de redistribución. En los dos backends C++ el `input` visual incluye un teclado en pantalla que se abre al confirmar: permite letras A–Z, números, puntuación básica, espacio, borrar, limpiar, aceptar y cancelar. Es un teclado ASCII propio del proyecto, no un IME multilingüe del sistema. Los demás controles con valor (interruptor, deslizador, incrementador, selector, carrusel/lista) responden a la cruceta y al botón de confirmación. Las pantallas múltiples se cambian mediante flujos de navegación; el shell conserva su control de salida. La generación se ha probado con pruebas Node.js y la sintaxis del código C++ generado se ha comprobado con Clang contra interfaces de prueba compatibles. El entorno de preparación no dispone de PowerShell, .NET 10 ni un stack de toolchain PS5 completo: por ello **no afirmo haber ejecutado aquí el parser de PowerShell, el build real de PS5 ni una prueba en consola**. Al iniciar en Windows, `start.bat` ejecuta `runtime/check-syntax.ps1` para usar el parser oficial de PowerShell antes de lanzar el servidor. ## Pruebas locales del generador Si tienes Node.js, ejecuta desde la carpeta del proyecto: ```powershell node --check app.js node --check runtime/native-generator.js node runtime/test-native-generator.js ``` `test-native-generator.js` comprueba los dos backends, literales escapados, múltiples pantallas, componentes y flujos. El build real sigue requiriendo la cadena upstream indicada en cada plantilla. La primera compilación Vulkan puede ser pesada porque construye RADV desde los fuentes fijados. ## Requisitos y licencias - OpenGL: Windows + WSL/Linux, Git, Make, Clang/LLD, dependencias de `ps5-homebrew-ui` y el SDK `ps5-opengl` que prepara el upstream. - Vulkan: WSL/Linux, Git/submódulos, CMake/Ninja, Clang/LLVM, Meson, rsync, PS5_Vulkan, PS5_Mesa y la revisión fijada de PS5_PayloadSDK. - Los títulos generados integran kits que mantienen licencias GPL. Revisa `LICENSE`, `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` y las licencias de cada recurso antes de redistribuir. No se incluyen firmware de PS5, claves, ROMs, BIOS, datos de juegos ni binarios propietarios de Sony/NVIDIA. - El IDE solo escucha en `127.0.0.1`. El workspace se guarda en `Documentos\PS5HomebrewStudio\Projects`; las toolchains quedan en la carpeta del proyecto IDE. ## Ecosistema investigado ### Bases y SDKs - [SharpProspero](https://github.com/SvenGDK/SharpProspero): aplicaciones nativas, bibliotecas y payloads C#. - [PS5 Native App Boilerplate](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-native-app-boilerplate): base C++20, runtime shim reproducible y empaquetado de título. - [PS5 Vulkan Template](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_VulkanTemplate): generador C++, muestras Vulkan y UI opcional. - [PS5SDK](https://github.com/PS5Dev/PS5SDK): orientado principalmente a payload ELF y homebrew sencillo; upstream indica que todavía no genera títulos completos. - [ps5-payload-dev/sdk](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk): toolchain de payloads C/C++ y enlace dinámico. - [ps5link-sdk](https://github.com/Rufidj/ps5link-sdk): enlazador de títulos nativos, con dependencias adicionales. - [etaHEN-Plugins](https://github.com/etaHEN/etaHEN-Plugins): plugins/daemons de etaHEN, no aplicaciones GUI independientes. ### Gráficos y UI - [PS5 OpenGL 4.6](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-opengl) y su [kit de UI](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-homebrew-ui). - [PS5 Vulkan Template](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_VulkanTemplate), [PS5_Vulkan](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Vulkan), [PS5_Mesa](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Mesa) y [PS5 VKHomebrewUI](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_VKHomebrewUI). - [PS5 OpenGL de mihawk-99](https://github.com/mihawk-99/ps5-opengl), [ps5gl](https://github.com/Rufidj/ps5gl) y [ps5-vulkan alternativo](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/ps5-vulkan): proyectos diferentes, con niveles de compatibilidad distintos. - [Aurora](https://github.com/encounter/aurora): capa GX/WebGPU con SDL3, backends multiplataforma y UI; los ports de PS5 le añaden una capa de plataforma. - [PS5 FSR4](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-fsr4) y [PS5 HelixSR](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-helixsr): complementos experimentales de Vulkan compute que exigen revisar licencias, requisitos y procedencia de sus dependencias. ### Aplicaciones reales de referencia Incluye [ProsperoLight](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ProsperoLight), [Unofficial Stremio PS5 Port](https://github.com/Sp9nky/unofficial-stremio-ps5-port), [Nativehbl](https://github.com/Rufidj/Nativehbl), [Quake3e PS5](https://github.com/griches/PS5_Quake3e), [Ghostship](https://github.com/griches/PS5_Ghostship), [SwitchWaker](https://github.com/griches/PS5_SwitchWaker), [Dusklight](https://github.com/griches/PS5_Dusklight), [Sunshine](https://github.com/griches/PS5_Sunshine), [Porpoise/Dolphin](https://github.com/elripalda/Porpoise-Dolphin-Emulator-for-PS5), [PS5 RetroArch](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_RetroArch), [PS5X360](https://github.com/BrinooTk/PS5X360) y [Syobon Action PS5](https://github.com/kvaps/syobon-action-ps5). Consulta [la matriz de SDKs](docs/SDK_MATRIX.md), [el estudio del ecosistema](docs/PROJECT_ECOSYSTEM.md) y la guía de [generación visual OpenGL/Vulkan](docs/NATIVE_VISUAL_BACKENDS.md) para saber qué es una base, un renderer, un driver, cómo se genera el código y qué limitaciones conserva cada backend. Un repositorio de aplicación completa puede aportar patrones arquitectónicos, pero no es necesariamente reutilizable sin portar dependencias, verificar licencia y resolver diferencias de firmware. ## Procedencia de IA La etiqueta **IA declarada** está reservada a declaraciones explícitas. Por ejemplo, [ProsperoEden0](https://github.com/Tiang-88/ProsperoEden0) declara asistencia de herramientas OpenAI/Anthropic; [X360PS5 de polarco](https://github.com/polarco/X360PS5) documenta uso activo de Codex, pero el propio README indica que no se ha probado en una PS5 y que aún no carga juegos Xbox 360. Estos casos son evidencia de asistencia declarada, no garantía de calidad o compatibilidad. Los proyectos con `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` no se etiquetan automáticamente como generados por IA. ## Licencias, dependencias y artefactos externos - Cada fuente conserva su repositorio y avisos upstream; revisa `LICENSE`, `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` y licencias de subcomponentes antes de redistribuir. - No se incluye firmware PS5, llaves de Sony, `libc.prx` propietario, ROMs, BIOS, datos de juegos ni binarios de NVIDIA. Si un repositorio requiere recursos que el usuario debe aportar, el IDE lo indica en su ficha. - Clonar un repositorio no instala sus herramientas del sistema, ni garantiza que sus submódulos/dependencias puedan compilar en el equipo. - La compatibilidad depende del firmware, loader, stack gráfico y las dependencias exactas. Los resultados de pruebas y limitaciones se toman de los documentos upstream; no se extrapolan a todas las consolas. ## Archivos importantes - `start.bat`: comprueba sintaxis e inicia el IDE. - `runtime/server.ps1`: servidor loopback, gestor de fuentes, materializador RGBA y build providers de SharpProspero, payloads PS5 y títulos OpenGL/Vulkan. - `runtime/native-generator.js`: generador C++20 para el contrato Concept del kit UI upstream. - `runtime/test-native-generator.js`: pruebas automatizadas del generador y de las rutas OpenGL/Vulkan. - `runtime/check-syntax.ps1`: usa el parser de PowerShell disponible en Windows y muestra línea/columna de errores. - `index.html`, `styles.css`, `app.js`: editor visual y catálogo. - `docs/SDK_MATRIX.md`, `docs/PROJECT_ECOSYSTEM.md`: investigación técnica. **Validación de esta release:** pasan `node --check` sobre `app.js` y los módulos del runtime, las diez suites JavaScript de `runtime/` (incluida la nueva regresión de selectores de `test-build-flow.js`) y una prueba de navegador real del flujo Compilar → diálogo nativo → confirmar: la 1.1.17 reproduce el `TypeError: buttons.forEach is not a function` y la 1.1.18 lo elimina, desactiva los botones del diálogo durante el build y los reactiva en el `finally`. No se pudo ejecutar el parser oficial de PowerShell, una compilación C++20 real de PPSA19918 ni un empaquetado UltraPack de extremo a extremo porque esas herramientas no están disponibles en el entorno de preparación. Consulta `docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.es-ES.md` para separar las pruebas locales de las validaciones pendientes en Windows/WSL. ## Corrección 1.0.1 Corrige un error de parseo de PowerShell en la generación del README de proyecto: se delimita `${sourceName}` explícitamente en la cadena que produce `SaveProject`. Consulta `docs/patches/FIX-POWERSHELL-627.es-ES.md`.

repos.name: PS5Library
repos.description: Native PS5Library console storefront. Frontend source and automated ELF builds.
repos.readme:
*If my work helped you, a coffee keeps the next project coming.* **Native PS5Library console storefront. Frontend source and automated ELF builds.**
---

Use the native updater if you publish your app as an FPKG and want to deliver future updates through the PS5’s native update system, instead of requiring users to download and reinstall the full PKG for every release. # PS5Library PS5Library is a self-hosted library platform for a jailbroken PS5. It combines a private Library Server, a controller-first PS5 storefront and console agent, and an iPhone companion. PS5Library is for homebrew, your own dumps, private repositories, public releases, and other content you are legally authorized to use. It does not support piracy and does not provide, locate, scrape, or redistribute commercial game packages, dumps, package links, or copyrighted downloads. The maintainers do not provide a server address, hosted game catalog, or game packages. Every operator supplies and manages their own server and authorized content. [Download releases](https://github.com/rdiol12/PS5Library/releases) | [Build status](https://github.com/rdiol12/PS5Library/actions/workflows/client-checks.yml) ## Components | Folder | Purpose | | --- | --- | | [`server/`](server/README.md) | API, web UI, package worker, shared schemas, Docker stack, PostgreSQL, and Redis | | [`frontend/`](frontend/) | Native PS5 storefront and agent plus the iPhone companion | | [`tools/native-pkg-updater/`](tools/native-pkg-updater/README.md) | CLI for building and publishing native PKG updates | The local Library Server holds each operator's catalog and generated artifacts. The PS5 and iPhone connect only to the server address configured by that operator. Private central services are not included in this repository. ## Library Server quick start Requirements: Git, Node.js 22.23.2 (or a supported newer release), Docker Engine or Docker Desktop with Compose, and enough storage for source folders, temporary build data, packages, and a safety margin. ```sh git clone https://github.com/rdiol12/PS5Library.git cd PS5Library/server npm ci npm run setup ``` Review the generated `.env`, set `DATA_DIR`, `DUMP_ROOT`, and `SOURCE_ROOT`, then start the stack: ```sh npm run docker:up ``` Open the configured `PUBLIC_URL` and use the one-time bootstrap token from `.env` to create the first administrator. Administrators can invite members, prepare packages, manage sources, and administer the server. Members can browse shared entries and manage only their own consoles and jobs. The server supports startup controls for companion connections, PS5 connections, account registration, community connectivity, new downloads, the experimental Home update bridge, and automatic preparation. Each setting and its safe default is documented in the [server guide](server/README.md). ### Watch folders and backports Place authorized prepared releases below `DUMP_ROOT`. A typical release with a supplied compatibility overlay looks like this: ```text DUMP_ROOT/ My Game [PPSA12345]/ eboot.bin sce_sys/param.json backport/ eboot.bin sce_module/example.sprx ``` `backport/`, `fakelib/`, and `fakelib2/` are recognized inside the exact prepared release folder. Their relative paths are preserved and hashed against that title, content ID, version, and source. They remain separate from the clean FPKG so a compatible console does not receive an unnecessary overlay. The server does not guess that an unrelated neighboring folder belongs to a lone `.pkg` file. See [server setup and configuration](server/README.md) for folder permissions, automatic preparation, storage sizing, HTTPS, backup, and operations. ## PS5 installation GitHub releases provide the complete PS5Library base package and its matching agent ELF. A compatible jailbreak and FPKG runtime are required. 1. Install the complete `PS5Library-.pkg`. 2. Load the matching `ps5library-agent-.elf` after each reboot. 3. Open PS5Library from Home. 4. Enter your own Library Server address and complete the pairing flow, or use offline mode for supported local functions. 5. Wait for the **PS5Library Agent connected** notification before using local inventory or console actions. USB formatting is **experimental** and has been tested only on firmware **4.51**. Other firmware versions are unverified. Back up the entire drive before testing it. See the [PS5 build and capability guide](frontend/ps5/README.md). ## iPhone companion The iPhone app connects to an operator-owned Library Server. It supports multiple accounts, catalog browsing, console pairing and management, install selection, storage selection, notifications, and live preparation/transfer progress. Building the iPhone app requires macOS and Xcode. GitHub Actions produces an unsigned IPA on selected iOS changes; installation still requires signing with an appropriate Apple identity. See the [iPhone guide](frontend/ios/README.md). ## Building the PS5 client The public PS5 build uses Docker with Linux containers: ```sh docker build -t ps5library-build -f frontend/docker/ps5-build.Dockerfile frontend docker run --rm --network none -v "${PWD}:/workspace" -w /workspace/frontend ps5library-build bash scripts/build.sh ``` This builds and checks the storefront, agent, and installer ELFs. Creating a native app package requires separately obtained packaging prerequisites; this repository does not contain proprietary publishing tools, keys, or SDK files. The server worker builds supported game FPKGs with its bundled, source-available LibProsperoPKG implementation and does not use that proprietary publisher. ## License Original PS5Library code is licensed under **GPL-3.0-or-later**. Bundled dependencies retain their own licenses and notices. See [`LICENSE`](LICENSE), [`server/LICENSE`](server/LICENSE), [`NOTICE.txt`](NOTICE.txt), and the notices within `server/upstream/` and `frontend/licenses/`. ## Special thanks PS5Library learned from or builds on technical work published by: - [ps5-payload-dev/sdk](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk) - [ProsperoTV](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ProsperoTV) and [ps5-native-app-boilerplate](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-native-app-boilerplate) - [LibProsperoPKG](https://github.com/SvenGDK/LibProsperoPKG), [drakmor/LibProsperoPKG](https://github.com/drakmor/LibProsperoPKG), and [UFS2Tool](https://github.com/SvenGDK/UFS2Tool) - [PS5-FPKG-Builder](https://github.com/Phoenixx1202/PS5-FPKG-Builder) - [ShadowMountPlus](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus) and [BackPork](https://github.com/BestPig/BackPork) - [kstuff-lite](https://github.com/EchoStretch/kstuff-lite) - [ps5-ezremote-client](https://github.com/cy33hc/ps5-ezremote-client) and [ps5-ezremote-dpi](https://github.com/cy33hc/ps5-ezremote-dpi) - [OnionHEN](https://github.com/aydencharles/onionHEN) - [ooz](https://github.com/powzix/ooz) Thank you to their maintainers and contributors for publishing source, documentation, and research that made independent PS5 homebrew development possible. Their original licenses and notices remain in the relevant source directories.

repos.name: PKGMerge
repos.description: Join split retail PS4 and PS5 packages into a single PKG
repos.readme:
PKGMerge

Glorified replacement for cat and copy

Join split PS4 and PS5 packages into a single PKG - in a desktop app or from the command line!

## Features - **PS4 and PS5** - merges split PS4 packages and split PS5 packages, including the `_sc.pkg`. - **App and CLI** - a desktop app with drag and drop and a `PKGMergeCli` command-line tool that can merge a single package or every package in a folder. - **Merging in place** - turns the root file into the merged package and deletes each piece as soon as it's merged, so you need free space for about one piece instead of the whole package. - **Cross-platform** - works on Windows, Linux and macOS (Apple Silicon/Intel). ### Retail packages only PKGMerge merges **retail** packages, the split PKGs served by PSN: games, updates and DLCs. You can get them: - From your own entitlements, e.g. with [PSNav](https://github.com/RobbedColek/PSNav) 😉 - From [OrbisPatches](https://orbispatches.com) (PS4) or [ProsperoPatches](https://prosperopatches.com) (PS5). Patches from OrbisPatches and ProsperoPatches are retail updates, so they **won't work on FPKG games**. ## Download Prebuilt, self-contained single-file builds are published on the [Releases](https://github.com/RobbedColek/PKGMerge/releases) page. No installation or .NET runtime is needed. | Platform | App | CLI | |---|---|---| | Windows (x64) | `PKGMerge-win-x64.zip` | `PKGMergeCli-win-x64.zip` | | Linux (x64) | `PKGMerge-linux-x64.tar.gz` | `PKGMergeCli-linux-x64.tar.gz` | | macOS (Apple Silicon) | `PKGMerge-osx-arm64.tar.gz` | `PKGMergeCli-osx-arm64.tar.gz` | | macOS (Intel) | `PKGMerge-osx-x64.tar.gz` | `PKGMergeCli-osx-x64.tar.gz` | Extract the archive and run `PKGMerge` or `PKGMergeCli`. The nightly build is regenerated automatically from the latest commit and may be unstable. ## Usage ### App 1. Run `PKGMerge`. 2. Drop the root `_0.pkg` file (or a PS5 `.pkg` that isn't split) on the window, or click `Browse…` next to `Source PKG`. 3. The package card shows the game's name and icon, the platform, the number of pieces and the total size. Problems found in the files are listed below the progress bar. - Errors (red) must be fixed before you can start, e.g. a missing piece or a missing `_sc.pkg` file. - Warnings (yellow) are worth a look, e.g. an `_sc.pkg` file that was picked because it's the only one in the folder. 4. For a PS5 package, check the `*_sc.pkg` field and choose the file yourself if needed. 5. Click `Start`. You can `Cancel` at any time and closing the window during a merge asks before stopping it. ### Command line #### Arguments ``` PKGMergeCli [-o|--output ] [--sc ] [-y|--overwrite] [--in-place] [--buffer-size ] ``` | Argument | Description | |---|---| | `` | Merge one package, starting from its root file. | | `` | Merge every split package in the folder. | | `-o`, `--output` | Output file, or output folder for a directory. Default: `-merged.pkg` next to the source. | | `--sc` | PS5 only: the `_sc.pkg` file to use. | | `-y`, `--overwrite` | Replace existing files without asking. | | `--in-place` | Delete the pieces while merging. | | `--buffer-size` | Buffer size in MiB, `1`-`256`. Default: `64`. | | `-h`, `--help` | Show the usage. | #### Exit codes | Code | Meaning | |---|---| | `0` | Every package was merged. | | `1` | Bad arguments or nothing to merge (no split packages found, invalid root file). | | `2` | At least one package failed or was skipped, or the merge was cancelled. | #### Examples ```bash # Merge one package into CUSA00000-merged.pkg next to it PKGMergeCli "D:/Downloads/UP1001-CUSA03980_00-BIOSHOCKCOMPLETE-A0102-V0100_0.pkg" # Merge a PS5 package with an _sc.pkg file that has a different name, into game-merged.pkg PKGMergeCli "D:/Downloads/JP0367-PPSA11079_00-3630723653971843_0.pkg" --sc "D:/Downloads/EP3036-PPSA13737_00-0492129687439402_sc.pkg" # Merge a PS5 package that isn't split with its _sc.pkg file PKGMergeCli "D:/Downloads/UP6312-PPSA23943_00-6310269941751438.pkg" # Merge every package in a folder and write the results to another drive PKGMergeCli "D:/Downloads" -o "E:/Merged" -y # Merge without needing space for a full copy, deleting the pieces as they're merged PKGMergeCli "D:/Downloads/EP0177-PPSA03261_00-COMPANYOFHEROES3_0.pkg" --in-place ``` ## Building from source Requires the [.NET 10 SDK](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download). The app's UI comes from the ColekUI git submodule, so clone with `--recursive` before building. ```bash git clone --recursive https://github.com/RobbedColek/PKGMerge.git git submodule update --init # if you cloned without --recursive dotnet run --project src/PKGMerge/PKGMerge.csproj ``` The solution has three projects: | Project | What it is | |---|---| | `src/PKGMerge.Core` | The scanning and merging library, shared by the app and the CLI. | | `src/PKGMerge` | The desktop app, built with [Avalonia](https://avaloniaui.net/) and ColekUI. | | `src/PKGMerge.Cli` | The `PKGMergeCli` command-line tool. | To produce a single-file build of the app for your platform: ```bash dotnet publish src/PKGMerge/PKGMerge.csproj -c Release -r win-x64 -o publish ``` To produce a native build of the CLI: ```bash dotnet publish src/PKGMerge.Cli/PKGMerge.Cli.csproj -c Release -r win-x64 -o publish ``` Replace `win-x64` with `linux-x64`, `osx-arm64` or `osx-x64` as needed. ## Credits PKGMerge wouldn't exist without [pkg-merge](https://github.com/Tustin/pkg-merge) by [Tustin](https://github.com/Tustin). This project started from that work and its conventions. Many thanks to Tustin for creating it. ## Disclaimer PKGMerge is an unofficial tool and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Sony Interactive Entertainment. "PlayStation", "PS4" and "PS5" are trademarks of their respective owners. Use it only with content you own, and at your own risk. ## License Released under the [GNU General Public License v3.0](LICENSE).

repos.name: ps5-acestream
repos.description: Experimental native Ace Stream player for jailbroken PS5: the engine runs on the console, with hardware H.264 decoding and a phone page to send channels.
repos.readme:
# Ace Stream for PS5 > [!WARNING] > **This is experimental software. Expect bugs.** > It has been tried on one console and one home network, parts of it for a few hours only. It can hang, show no picture, or need the console restarted. See [Known limits](#known-limits) before you spend an evening on it. A native Ace Stream player for jailbroken PS5 consoles. Open it from the home screen, pick a saved channel or enter a content id, and the channel plays on the TV with sound. Nothing else is involved: the Ace Stream engine runs on the console itself. Channels can also be sent from a phone, through a page the console serves.

A channel playing with the statistics panel open, taken with the console's own capture.

Unofficial homebrew. Not affiliated with Ace Stream or Sony. The engine is proprietary and is **not** part of this repository; you fetch it from its publisher when you build the engine pack. No channels or content ids are included. ## What it does | | | |---|---| | Engine | Ace Stream 3.2.11 for Linux x86-64, unmodified, running under [blink](https://github.com/jart/blink) | | Video | H.264, decoded by the console's hardware decoder (VideoDec2). Tested at 1280×720, 25 fps | | Output | 1920×1080. Smaller pictures are scaled bilinearly; the picture is timed by the sound | | Audio | AAC (ADTS), decoded with FDK AAC, played at 48 kHz stereo | | Language | English or Spanish, following the console's language; the phone page follows the browser's | | Start of the engine | two to three minutes after the app is opened for the first time since the console started; it then stays up | | Start of a channel | 5 to 15 seconds, when the channel has peers | Not supported: HEVC, MPEG audio and AC-3 sound (the picture plays without sound), 4K, seeking, VOD. ## Install You need a jailbroken PS5 with an ELF loader on port 9021, an FTP server on port 2121 and a homebrew loader that picks titles up from `/data/homebrew` ([ShadowMountPlus](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus) was used). Two things go on the console: the app and the engine. 1. **The app.** Download `ace-stream-ps5-.zip` from the [latest release](../../releases/latest), unpack it, and upload the `PPSA96879` folder it contains to `/data/homebrew` over FTP. The homebrew loader picks it up and **Ace Stream** appears on the home screen. 2. **The engine.** It is proprietary, so no release carries it. Build the pack on a PC, which needs Python 3 with pip, curl and zstd but no PS5 toolchain, and upload it: ```sh make rootfs make install-engine PS5_HOST= # work/rootfs.pack -> /data/acestream/rootfs.pack ``` Open **Ace Stream** from the home screen. The first start unpacks the engine, which takes about half a minute more. If you build the app yourself (see [Build](#build)), `make install PS5_HOST=` uploads the folder. The app starts the engine by itself, by handing a payload to the ELF loader. Until the engine answers, the home screen says so and no channel can be opened. Each time it is opened, the app shows a notification with its version and whether a newer release exists. ## Use **Home.** The saved channels are a row of cards; the first card enters a new id. | Button | | |---|---| | Left, right | choose a card | | Cross | play the channel, or enter a new id | | Options | a menu for the channel: play, rename, forget | | Square | forget the channel | | Up | the top menu: Home, Settings | **Entering an id or a name.** The console's own keyboard opens; an id can be typed or pasted, alone or inside an `acestream://` link. For those who would rather not type with the controller, the same card shows the address of the phone page. **Playing.** Cross pauses, Square stops, Triangle shows the statistics (picture size, frames per second, peers, download rate, buffer), Circle hides the controls. **Phone.** Open `http://:6880`, paste an id or an `acestream://` link, optionally with a name. With the app open, the channel starts on the TV. Sent channels are remembered, and can be renamed or removed from the page. It has no password: anyone on your network can use it. ## Settings Up, then Settings. These are the settings of the engine's own web page, read from the engine and written back to it: | Setting | Values | |---|---| | Audio transcoding, MP3, AC-3 | on or off | | Preferred audio language | 28 languages | | Preferred video quality | 144p to 2160p | | Preferred video bitrate | under 1 Mbps to over 6 Mbps | | Output format, live and on demand | automatic, original, HLS, HTTP | | Access from the local network, from outside it | on or off | | Programme guide, automatic sync | on or off | Left and right change a value. The last row removes the engine's cache to free space; it asks for Cross twice, and the engine restarts afterwards. ## How it works ``` title (PPSA96879) services payload engine payload eboot.bin acestream.elf aceengine.elf ┌─────────────────────┐ loop- ┌──────────────────────────┐ ┌─────────────────────────┐ │ controller, screens │ back │ link to the title │ │ blink │ │ AudioOut │◀────────▶│ MPEG-TS demuxer, AAC │────▶│ └ Linux root filesystem│ │ VideoDec2, VideoOut │ 47330 │ phone page on :6880 │HTTP │ └ acestreamengine │ └─────────────────────┘ └──────────────────────────┘6878 └─────────────────────────┘ ``` Three processes, because none can do the job alone on this console. A title cannot listen on the network, and a payload cannot be heard nor use the hardware video decoder. - **The engine payload** is blink, an x86-64 Linux emulator, built for the console with a root filesystem of Ubuntu 22.04, Python 3.10 and the engine. The engine is not changed: blink translates its system calls. It serves the usual HTTP API on port 6878. - **The services payload** asks the engine for a channel, demuxes the MPEG-TS it returns, decodes the sound and sends both to the title, paced by the stream's own clock. It also serves the phone page, starts the engine payload and relays the engine's settings. A stop or a new channel interrupts whatever it was waiting for. - **The title** decodes the video, shows the picture that is due at the sound's playhead, and draws the screens. It starts the services payload through the ELF loader when it does not find it. ## Build Requirements: [ps5-payload-sdk](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk), LLVM 18, GNU make 4, Python 3 with Pillow and NumPy, and for the title what [ps5-native-app-boilerplate](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-native-app-boilerplate) needs (bash 4+, ninja; on macOS also coreutils, gnu-sed, findutils, gnu-tar and grep from Homebrew). ```sh make PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK=/opt/ps5-payload-sdk # build/ps5/acestream.elf (carries aceengine.elf) make title PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK=/opt/ps5-payload-sdk # build/title/PPSA96879 make rootfs # work/rootfs.pack, from Canonical, PyPI and acestream.media make dist # dist/ace-stream-ps5-.zip, what a release carries make probes PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK=/opt/ps5-payload-sdk # diagnostic payloads, see tests/ ``` Every push is built by GitHub Actions. A release is published by pushing a tag that matches the `VERSION` file: ```sh git tag v$(cat VERSION) && git push origin v$(cat VERSION) ``` `make rootfs` downloads Ubuntu 22.04 base, the packages of Python 3.10, the wheels the engine asks for and the engine itself, checks their digests where the origin publishes them, and reduces the result to the files the engine loads (about 190 MB). No Docker is used. The icon and the two backgrounds are drawn by `tools/make-icon.py` and `tools/make-background.py`. The screens can be drawn on a PC, without a console: ```sh mkdir -p build/host clang++ -std=c++17 -Ititle/src tests/ui/preview.cpp title/src/ui/*.cpp title/src/scale.cpp \ title/src/engine_settings.cpp title/src/lang.cpp -o build/host/preview build/host/preview title/assets/Inter-Regular.ttf title/assets/Inter-SemiBold.ttf ``` To try the engine without a console, build blink for your machine and point it at the tree: ```sh gmake -f tools/host.mk python3 tools/packrootfs.py --rootfs work/rootfs --tree work/rootfs-ps5 build/host/blink -m -C $PWD/work/rootfs-ps5 /opt/acestream/acestreamengine --client-console python3 tools/acetest.py 127.0.0.1 ``` ## What the console needed blink is vendored in `third_party/blink` (upstream commit in `UPSTREAM`) with these changes: - `brk` rounded to the host's 16 KiB pages, which glibc's allocator rejects. - `PEXTRW` left the upper bits of the destination register (SQLite crashed). - `futex` waits with an absolute deadline (`FUTEX_WAIT_BITSET`), which glibc uses for every timed wait. - `epoll`, built on `poll`, for hosts without it; `poll` and `select` now block in the host instead of sleeping 50 ms between looks. - `/proc` files that psutil reads; the engine does not start a download without them. - The JIT no longer recycles blocks when its memory is full (another thread could still be writing into one). It gets 384 MB instead and leaves new code to the interpreter when that is used up. - Private file mappings are copied into anonymous memory. The last one is a property of the console: **writing to a `MAP_PRIVATE` file mapping changes the file.** glibc's loader relocated the libraries in place and the next run found them already relocated. Other things measured on firmware 13.42 (`tests/host_probe.c`, `tests/at_probe.c`): - `/data` has no symbolic or hard links, so the root filesystem is built without any. - `F_DUPFD_CLOEXEC`, `faccessat` and `readlinkat` are not implemented. - Many syscall stubs of the SDK's libc (`openat`, `fstatat`, `renameat`, `dup`, ...) return the error number as the result instead of setting `errno`; `engine/compat.c` replaces the ones blink uses. - A process that ends by a default-action fatal signal stays stopped and cannot be killed. The payload exits instead. - Executable memory can be had (`mmap` with `PROT_EXEC`, `kernel_mprotect`), which is what makes the JIT possible; without it the engine is about ten times slower. - The hardware video decoder works from a title only: from a loader payload the decode call fails. - A title linked with the stubs in another order than ASCII imports from `libkernel_web` and dies at start: `tools/build-title.sh` sets `LC_ALL=C`. - The engine's settings API refuses calls from another machine; the services payload reaches it on the loopback. ## Logs Everything is under `/data/acestream`: | File | Written by | |---|---| | `service.log` | the services payload: requests, sessions, what the engine answered | | `title.log` | the title: a line every five seconds (screen, pictures decoded, errors, sound played) | | `stage.log` | the engine payload: how far its start got | | `engine.log` | the engine's own output | | `blink.log` | blink: unsupported calls | ```sh python3 tools/ps5.py tail /data/acestream/service.log python3 tools/ps5.py send build/ps5/probes/tail_logs.elf # the same, when FTP is down ``` ## Known limits - Tested on one console (firmware 13.42, ShadowMountPlus 1.7beta4, kstuff-lite) and one home network. - The settings screen and the cache clearing are new and have hardly been used. The engine's settings are passed on as they are; what each one changes is the engine's business. - 1920×1080 channels open, but were only watched for a few seconds, with frames dropped. - A channel without peers stays on the loading screen for up to two minutes before the app reports it. Square leaves at any time. - The engine takes minutes to start because it is emulated, and it uses about 650 MB of memory. - The home screen shows five cards and the settings ten rows at a time; the rest scroll. - The phone page has no authentication. - The update check does not verify TLS certificates. It only produces a notification. - The app's background sound is still the one of the boilerplate. ## Third-party code | Component | Use | License | |---|---|---| | [blink](https://github.com/jart/blink), vendored and modified | x86-64 Linux emulation | ISC | | [ps5-native-app-boilerplate](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-native-app-boilerplate), fetched at build time; `title/src/demo_renderer.*` comes from it | title toolchain, runtime and output surface | GPL-3.0 | | [FDK AAC](https://android.googlesource.com/platform/external/aac/), decoder only | AAC decoding | Fraunhofer FDK AAC license | | [stb_truetype](https://github.com/nothings/stb) | text rasterising | Public domain / MIT | | [Inter](https://rsms.me/inter/) | the typeface of the screens | SIL Open Font License 1.1 | | [ps5-payload-sdk](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk) | payload toolchain | GPL-3.0 | ## License GPLv3, see [LICENSE](LICENSE). Not affiliated with Ace Stream or Sony. ## Credits Part of the title comes from [ps5-mirage](https://github.com/holdmysocks/ps5-mirage) by holdmysocks (GPL-3.0-or-later, commit `34715f9`), an AirPlay receiver for the PS5: - `title/src/decoder/vdec.cpp` and `vdec.hpp`, the bring-up of the hardware decoder and its decode loop, are adapted from Mirage's `title/src/vdec.*`, nearly as they are. - The BT.709 colour tables in `title/src/scale.cpp` are those of its `mirror_view.cpp`. - The sound output (`title/src/audio.cpp`), the link's socket code (`title/src/link.cpp`) and the test launcher (`tests/launch/launch.c`) follow its `player.cpp` and `helper/launcher.c` in places. The use of the console's keyboard (`title/src/keyboard.cpp`) follows ProsperoTV's `iptv_ime.c` by blackbearreloaded, as ported in [Jelly5](https://github.com/02dnot/Jelly5) by 02dnot (both GPL-3.0-or-later). The update check and the notification are those of [ps5-airplay](https://github.com/rodri0x/ps5-airplay). The decoder's structure layouts and call order are, as Mirage's source notes, those of [ProsperoLight](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ProsperoLight) by blackbearreloaded, written up and verified on hardware in [EVO-PLAYER-PS5](https://github.com/sainsaji/EVO-PLAYER-PS5) by sainsaji.
