latestRelease.name: PS5 Dump & Image Converter v1.9.89
latestRelease.body:
## Neu

- Ziehen und Ablegen in die Felder Quelle, Ziel und Temp funktioniert auch, wenn das Programm als Administrator läuft; leere Felder zeigen einen grauen Hinweis, was man hineinziehen kann.
- Die Backport-Funktion wurde optimiert und verbessert: Der Backport lässt sich im Spiel integrieren oder separat als Ordner erstellen, der im Dump-Ordner des Spiels ausgetauscht wird (auch an die Konsole senden).
- Die Bibliothek zeigt die verlangte Firmware, liest `.ffpkg` ohne Einhängen und zeigt Update-Pakete (Delta) mit Titel und IDs.

## Geändert

- Die Pfad-Karte springt nicht mehr, BAUFORM steht direkt unter dem Formathinweis, die Knöpfe in Aufgabe 7 heißen „PS4 PKG“ und „PS5 PKG“, und große runde Flächen rechnen viel schneller (der erste Wechsel zu PS5 PKG erscheint sofort).

## Aktualisiert

- ShadowMount+ 1.7beta10, zftpd 1.7.0, PS5Upload 9.1.0, PS4Mount 0.7.2, PatchDL 0.3.11, NeoEnabler 0.5.3, WebKit Autoloader 0.6.2, ps5-unified-autoloader 0.1.7 und ps5-ultrapack 2.3.3.

## Behoben

- Gleichzeitiges Lesen von Abbild-Angaben in der Bibliothek konnte die Lesefunktion der Engine dauerhaft ersetzt zurücklassen, sodass sie nur noch einen Teil des Verzeichnisbaums las.

## Downloads

- **Windows:** `PS5_Dump_Image_Converter_v1.9.89.exe` (benötigt Administratorrechte beim Start).
- **Linux (x86-64):** `PS5_Dump_Image_Converter_v1.9.89_linux_x86_64` – nach dem Download mit `chmod +x` ausführbar machen.
- **macOS:** `PS5_Dump_Image_Converter_v1.9.89_macos_arm64.dmg` (Apple Silicon) und `PS5_Dump_Image_Converter_v1.9.89_macos_x86_64.dmg` (Intel). Meldet macOS beim ersten Start „Der Entwickler kann nicht überprüft werden“, hilft Abschnitt 19.3 im Benutzerhandbuch.

**Vollständiges Changelog**: https://github.com/strongt1me/PS5-Dump-Image-Converter/compare/v1.9.88...v1.9.89

repos.name: kabuki-ps5
repos.description: Kabuki: a native ShellUI control-centre overlay for the PS5 that homebrew can add tiles to
repos.readme:
Kabuki running on PS5, shown over a game.

A custom control centre + overlay hub for PS5 homebrew

Kabuki is a native control panel for homebrew that runs ShellUI code. Hold your configured shortcut (default: **L3 + R3**) and Kabuki pops in from the right, over the home screen or your game, using the console's own interface toolkit, fonts, icons, focus effects and sounds. Payloads can add their own tiles, display information and receive controller input through Kabuki. System readings and settings are built in; [librespot-ps5](https://github.com/stupiditytries/librespot-ps5) adds music controls, a queue and a library browser. **Tested on firmware 13.20.** Kabuki may work on firmware up to **13.60** and on other firmware versions, but those versions still need to be tested. There is no firmware version allowlist. Runtime method and hook checks still apply, so a version may refuse to load when its interface differs. Please report your firmware version and results. ## Get started **Download `kabuki-ps5.elf` from [Releases](https://github.com/stupiditytries/kabuki-ps5/releases).** Follow [Using it](#using-it) to load it on your console. ## What it does - *Opens over the home screen or a game.* Hold a configurable button shortcut to bring up the panel. - *Uses the console's native UI.* PUI widgets, SST fonts, system icons, UI3 glass focus and interface sounds. - *Keeps your controls together.* Choose and arrange up to seven visible tiles; the first tile opens with the panel. - *Shows system readings.* CPU load, memory, temperatures and frame rate where the console exposes it. - *Lets you make it yours.* Change the shortcut, its hold time, interface sounds and tile order from Kabuki Settings. - *Hosts homebrew tiles.* Providers can use ready-made media and list cards, or supply a native plugin for a custom card. ### With librespot-ps5 librespot-ps5 adds three tiles: - **Now Playing:** cover art, track information, play/pause, previous/next, seeking, volume, shuffle and repeat. - **Queue:** browse upcoming songs and choose what plays next. - **Library:** browse albums and playlists together in last-played order, then open their tracks. librespot-ps5 handles Spotify pairing, playback and artwork caching. Kabuki displays its cards and sends your commands back to the receiver. The modular receiver also includes a full-screen Music Player app. Use its own instructions for installation and features. ## What you need - A modified PS5 that can load ELF payloads. - A USB drive for the payload. - A compatible provider if you want additional tiles, such as librespot-ps5. Kabuki's System and Settings tiles work independently of a music receiver. ## Using it 1. Put `kabuki-ps5.elf` on a USB drive. If you use librespot-ps5, put it beside `librespot-ps5.elf`. 2. Load Kabuki manually with your payload loader. 3. Load any compatible providers you want to use. 4. Hold **L3 + R3 for half a second** to open the panel. | Control | Action | |---|---| | L3 + R3, held | Open or close Kabuki with the default shortcut | | D-pad | Move through the sidebar and the selected card | | Cross | Open a tile, select an item or use a control | | Circle | Go back within a card, return to the sidebar or close the panel | Opening the console's own control centre closes Kabuki's panel. Your shortcut, hold time, sounds and tile arrangement are saved in `/data/custom-overlays`. Kabuki does not add itself to autoload. The same folder holds its logs and runtime records. ## Adding your own tiles A provider connects to Kabuki's local broker and registers the tiles it owns. Kabuki handles navigation, layout and controller focus for the built-in card templates: - **Media cards** for playback information and controls. - **List cards** for menus, libraries and nested lists. The protocol is versioned, and a C SDK and example providers are included. Start with the [provider protocol](protocol/PROTOCOL.md), [C SDK](sdk/c/kabuki.h) and [hello-tile example](examples/hello-tile/). For cards the templates cannot express, the [native plugin API](sdk/plugin/kabuki_plugin.h) exposes widget creation, animation, data and actions. See [Writing a plugin](docs/WRITING-A-PLUGIN.md) and the [custom-card example](examples/custom-card/). **Native plugins are not sandboxed.** They run inside SceShellUI and can crash the home screen. Kabuki handles callback errors and repeated slow frames, but it cannot protect against arbitrary native memory faults. Use the template cards when they fit. ## Building Build on Linux or WSL with the [PS5 Payload SDK](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk), Python 3 and a C++20 host compiler for the tests. Set `PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK` to your SDK directory, then run: ```bash python3 tools/fetch-deps.py bash tests/run.sh bash build.sh ``` The payload is written to `build/kabuki-ps5.elf`. The build checks that it stays under the 2 MiB payload limit. GitHub Actions also builds and tests each push or pull request. Version tags create a draft release with the payload and checksums; see [Releasing](docs/RELEASING.md). See [Developing Kabuki](docs/DEVELOPING.md) for the development loop, logs and development builds, and [Architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) for how the daemon and ShellUI worker fit together. ## PC preview The console layout also runs on a PC, with keyboard and controller input. It uses the same layout and navigation code, so you can develop cards and check transitions before building a console payload. ```bash python3 tools/fetch_console_assets.py python3 preview/native_preview.py ``` Open `http://127.0.0.1:8765`. Space opens the panel, the arrow keys move, Enter is Cross and Esc is Circle. The preview uses fonts and UI resources copied from your own console. Those files stay local and are excluded from the repository. Native plugins can also be built for the host preview. ## Credits - The [PS5 Payload SDK](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk) and John Tornblom's [shsrv](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/shsrv). - [ps5-dualsense-overlay](https://github.com/erickdavestech/ps5-dualsense-overlay), whose loader work Kabuki's ShellUI loader is adapted from. Upstream sources and pinned revisions are listed in [src/loader/SOURCES.md](src/loader/SOURCES.md). - [JSON for Modern C++](https://github.com/nlohmann/json), used by the provider broker and settings. - [stb](https://github.com/nothings/stb), used by the PC preview. - [Plus Jakarta Sans](https://github.com/tokotype/PlusJakartaSans), used in the Kabuki wordmark, under the SIL Open Font License. ## License and disclaimer Kabuki is free software under the **GNU General Public License, version 3 or later**. See [LICENSE](LICENSE). Third-party components retain their own licenses. Kabuki is an unofficial homebrew project. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by or supported by Sony Interactive Entertainment. PlayStation and PS5 are trademarks of their respective owners. Kabuki comes with no warranty, as set out in the license.

latestRelease.name: Kabuki v0.2.0-rc.1 — Console test release
latestRelease.body:
Kabuki is a native control panel and overlay hub for PS5 homebrew. This pre-release is available for console testing.

**Tested on FW 13.20.** It may work on firmware up to **13.60** and on other firmware versions, but those versions still need to be tested. Kabuki has no firmware version allowlist; runtime method and hook validation still applies. Please report your firmware version and results.

## Get started

1. Download [kabuki-ps5.elf](https://github.com/stupiditytries/kabuki-ps5/releases/download/v0.2.0-rc.1/kabuki-ps5.elf).
2. Put the ELF on your USB drive and load it manually. If you use librespot-ps5, put the two payloads together and launch Kabuki first.
3. Hold **L3 + R3 for half a second** to open the panel.

If you are switching from a development build, restart the console before testing this release so the previous resident worker is cleared. This release does not include development takeover support.

See the [README](https://github.com/stupiditytries/kabuki-ps5#readme) for controls, settings and provider instructions.

## Included

- Native System and Settings cards, configurable shortcut, sounds and sidebar arrangement.
- Provider protocol with built-in media and list cards.
- C SDK, native plugin API and example providers.
- Now Playing, Queue and Library cards from a compatible librespot-ps5 receiver.
- Library navigation resets when the receiver changes account or session.
- Updated README with an actual console screenshot and download instructions.

Settings and logs live in `/data/custom-overlays`. Kabuki does not install itself into autoload.

## Build and verification

The ELF was compiled by GitHub Actions from [187180b](https://github.com/stupiditytries/kabuki-ps5/commit/187180b39c5490c1cbc1ed5979bd8d8f9ea6e9a1), after the host tests passed, using the pinned community PS5 Payload SDK v0.44. It is a normal release build, without `--dev`.

`SHA256SUMS.txt` verifies the ELF, build information and bundled release notes. `BUILD-INFO.txt` records the exact source revision and SDK version. The release assets contain no copied console fonts, firmware modules or private working files.

repos.name: padbridge
repos.description: Use controllers the PS5 does not accept as extra DualSense pads on a jailbroken PS5 (tested on 13.60): 8BitDo Ultimate 2C, 8BitDo USB Wireless Adapter 2 (DualSense, Switch Pro, GameSir G8...), wired XInput. Rumble in PS4 games, up to 4 pads, settings page.
repos.readme:
# padbridge **Use controllers the PS5 does not accept, on a jailbroken PS5, as extra DualSense controllers.** padbridge is a payload for a jailbroken PS5. It reads USB controllers and receivers plugged into the console and shows each controller to the system and to games as a **virtual DualSense**, up to four at once, next to your own DualSense: - the **8BitDo Ultimate 2C Wireless** through its 2.4G dongle; - almost **any Bluetooth controller** (DualSense, DualShock 4, Xbox, Switch Pro, 8BitDo, GameSir...) through the **8BitDo USB Wireless Adapter 2**; - **wired XInput (Xbox 360) controllers** on a USB cable. The console's own Bluetooth is never touched, so your DualSense stays paired. A **settings page**, opened from a phone or a computer, shows each controller live and lets you fix controllers with the Nintendo button layout. Up to 1.1.0 the project was called **pad2c**; see [Upgrading from pad2c](#upgrading-from-pad2c).

The settings page: the Ultimate 2C on its dongle, and a GameSir G8 through the USB Wireless Adapter 2 with the Nintendo layout on.

## Compatibility Everything below was tested on a **PS5 Slim (CFI-2114), firmware 13.60**. ### Through the 8BitDo USB Wireless Adapter 2 [8BitDo USB Wireless Adapter 2](https://www.8bitdo.com/usb-wireless-adapter-2/), firmware 1.10. Plug it in, pair a controller with it, switch the controller on: nothing to set on the adapter. | Controller | How it pairs with the adapter | Result | |---|---|---| | DualSense | its normal pairing (Create + PS) | ✅ all buttons; vibration in XInput mode; touchpad click in DInput mode (View + Menu in XInput) | | 8BitDo Ultimate 2C Wireless | Switch mode (Home + Y) | ✅ all buttons | | GameSir G8 Plus Galileo | Switch mode (its only mode the adapter accepts) | ✅ with **Nintendo layout** on (it sends A/B and X/Y by label); **vibration** with the adapter in its Switch mode | | Anything else the adapter accepts (DualShock 4, Xbox One / Series, Switch Pro, Joy-Con, Wii U Pro, 8BitDo) | | expected to work, untested: please report | ### 8BitDo Ultimate 2C Wireless on its own dongle | Connection | Result | |---|---| | 2.4G dongle, DInput mode (`2dc8:301c`) | ✅ all buttons, L4/R4 as the touchpad click; no vibration (the controller only rumbles in XInput) | | 2.4G dongle, XInput mode (`2dc8:310a`) | ✅ all buttons, **vibration** in PS4 games, View + Menu as the touchpad (the controller sends no L4/R4 in this mode) | | USB cable (`2dc8:310a`, XInput) | ✅ as XInput mode above | The 8BitDo Ultimate 2C **Bluetooth** Controller (the Switch edition, without a dongle) is a different product and is not supported directly; it works through the USB Wireless Adapter 2. The Ultimate 2C's **Star** and **Mapping** buttons never reach the console, in either mode: the controller keeps them for its own turbo and mapping settings. ### Vibration **PS4 games** rumble the controller (tested: Crash Bandicoot N. Sane Trilogy). padbridge reads what the game asks of the virtual DualSense (`scePadVirtualDeviceGetRemoteSetting`: the large and small motors, as on a DualShock 4) and sends it on: | Controller | Rumbles | |---|---| | Ultimate 2C on its dongle | in XInput mode (tested) | | Through the USB Wireless Adapter 2, Switch-type controllers (GameSir G8 tested, Switch Pro, Joy-Con) | with the adapter in its **Switch mode** (tested) | | Through the USB Wireless Adapter 2, PlayStation controllers (DualSense tested) | in XInput mode | **PS5 games do not rumble**: they send DualSense haptics, and the console turns even their classic rumble requests into haptic audio before the virtual DualSense sees them. Controllers in DInput mode do not rumble either. ### Not yet Vibration in PS5 games, light bar, motion sensors, audio. ## Install 1. Plug the dongle, the adapter or the controller's cable into a USB port of the PS5. 2. Send `padbridge-.elf` to your payload loader (elfldr listens on port 9021), or add it to Payload Manager and to its autoload list, so that it starts with the console. 3. A notification says it is running, with the address of the settings page. 4. Switch the controller on and press **Home** (or PS): the console asks who is using it. For a second player, pick a **second user** (a game takes one controller per user). padbridge remembers the choice per controller and gives it back to that user next time, as a DualSense does. It needs a console that already runs a payload loader; padbridge does not jailbreak anything itself. ## Settings page Open **http://<console IP>:8090** in a browser on the same network (phone, computer, the console's own); the address is in the notification when padbridge starts. For each controller: - its name, mode (DInput or XInput), slot and the user it is given to; - **Nintendo layout**: A/B and X/Y swapped, applied at once and kept, for controllers that send the Nintendo layout (A on the right), such as the GameSir G8 in Switch mode; - its buttons, sticks and triggers, live, to check a mapping. The page is open to the local network, without a password. Through the adapter, a setting belongs to the adapter: it holds for whatever controller is paired with it. ## The 8BitDo USB Wireless Adapter 2 The adapter shows a different USB identity for each mode and picks its mode from the host it sees. padbridge answers it as Windows does, so it settles in **XInput** by itself, and hides the keyboard and mouse the adapter adds in that mode, so the console's Accessories list shows only the controller. | Mode | How | Notes | |---|---|---| | XInput (`2dc8:3106`) | automatic | vibration in PS4 games for PlayStation controllers (DualSense tested); View + Menu as the touchpad | | DInput (`2dc8:3105`) | hold **View + Left** (Create + Left on a DualSense) for 3 s; the light blinks twice | passes a DualSense's touchpad click | | Switch (`057e:2009`, a Switch Pro Controller) | hold **- + L** (View + LB) for 3 s; the light blinks twice | **vibration for Switch-type controllers** (the adapter passes it on only in this mode); Capture as the touchpad; buttons by position, so a pad that sends them by label (GameSir G8) needs Nintendo layout | | back to automatic | hold the adapter's button until its light goes off, then pair the controller again | | | DualShock 4 (`054c:05c4`) | where it ends on a PS5 without padbridge's answer | does not work: it stops sending after a moment | Pairing a DualSense with the adapter unpairs it from the console: plug it into the console with its cable and press PS to pair it back. The adapter takes one controller at a time. ## The GameSir G8 Plus Galileo through the adapter The G8's Bluetooth modes are Android, Switch and G-Touch; the USB Wireless Adapter 2 accepts only its **Switch** mode. It then works in both of the adapter's modes, with two things to know: | Adapter mode | Buttons | Vibration | |---|---|---| | **Switch** (hold **- + L** for 3 s) | tick **Nintendo layout** on the "Pro Controller" card of the settings page | ✅ (PS4 games) | | XInput (automatic) | tick **Nintendo layout** on the "8BitDo USB Wireless Adapter 2" card | ❌ the adapter passes rumble in XInput to PlayStation controllers only | - **Nintendo layout:** in Switch mode the G8 sends its buttons by their printed letter (its bottom button is "A", which a Switch reads as the right one), not by position. A genuine Switch Pro Controller needs no setting. - **Weak rumble:** simple rumble motors like the G8's do not move below a certain strength, and the Switch format splits rumble into a low and a high band, of which such pads feel mostly the low one. In the Switch mode, padbridge sends the stronger motor to the low band and starts any rumble at about 40%, so a light request (Crash Bandicoot's spin asks 25%) is still felt. - The setting is kept per card, so the G8 and a DualSense can share the adapter: the DualSense uses the adapter's XInput mode, without Nintendo layout. ## The Ultimate 2C's two dongle modes The controller keeps the last mode chosen. With the controller on: - **DInput** (the default): hold **B + Home** until it switches off, then **B + Home** again until it switches on. - **XInput**: the same with **X + Home**. ## Button map | Controller | DualSense | |---|---| | A / B / X / Y (Xbox layout) | ✕ / ○ / □ / △ (by position) | | LB / RB / LT / RT | L1 / R1 / L2 / R2 (analog) | | View / Menu (Back / Start, - / +) | Create / Options | | Home / Guide | PS | | L3 / R3 | L3 / R3 | | Ultimate 2C L4 / R4 (DInput), DualSense touchpad (adapter, DInput) | touchpad click | | View + Menu pressed together, on XInput controllers | touchpad click | | Switch Pro (and the adapter's Switch mode): B / A / Y / X, L / R, ZL / ZR, - / +, Home, Capture | ✕ / ○ / □ / △ (by position), L1 / R1, L2 / R2, Create / Options, PS, touchpad click | ## Notes - "Turn off" in the console's menu disconnects the controller from the console, as with a DualSense, and Home connects it again. The controller itself stays on until it goes to sleep by itself. - Every notification reads "padbridge by Sub", then the controller, its mode and what happened. - On XInput controllers, View or Menu pressed alone reaches the console 60 ms late: padbridge waits that long for the other one, so that View + Menu (the touchpad) does not open the Create menu on the way. ## Files All in `/data/padbridge/` on the console: | File | | |---|---| | `padbridge.log` | the log | | `stop` | create it to stop padbridge (in rest mode it lets the controllers go and waits; it picks them up again when the console wakes) | | `owner`, `owner.1`... | the user the controller in each slot was last given to (delete to forget) | | `config` | the settings page's choices (`swap ` for Nintendo layout) | | `bind_user` | optional: `main`, `other` or a hexadecimal user id, to give controllers to that user at once | ## Upgrading from pad2c padbridge 1.2.0 is pad2c renamed. On its first start it asks a running pad2c to stop and moves `/data/pad2c` to `/data/padbridge`, remembered users and settings included. Replace `pad2c-.elf` with `padbridge-.elf` in Payload Manager's autoload list. ## FAQ **Can I use a non-Sony controller on a PS5?** Not on a stock PS5: it only accepts its own and a few licensed controllers. On a jailbroken PS5, padbridge makes them appear as DualSense controllers. **Does it work in games, or only in the menus?** In games too. Give each controller its own console user (the console asks when you press Home) and it is player 2, 3 or 4, like another DualSense. **Do I lose my DualSense?** No. Both work at the same time; padbridge does not use the console's Bluetooth. (Pairing the DualSense itself with the USB Wireless Adapter 2 is your choice; see above.) **A/B and X/Y are swapped on my controller.** Tick **Nintendo layout** for it on the settings page. **My controller does nothing.** `/data/padbridge/padbridge.log` lists every USB device plugged in that padbridge does not read, with its id and name: a controller in another mode (Switch, DS4) shows up there. **My controller is not listed.** Run `padbridge-probe.elf` with it plugged in and open an issue with `/data/padbridge/probe.log` (the issue template says what to include). ## How it works - `src/usbpad.c` opens each controller's `/dev/ugenB.A` node and reads its interrupt IN endpoint, up to four, each its own virtual DualSense. New devices are looked for every 100 ms. The console's own HID driver holds the interface but ignores the device. The internal Bluetooth chip (`ugen0.2`) is never touched. - `src/usbdesc.c` picks the interface from the USB descriptor: XInput (`ff/5d/01`) from any vendor first, then an Switch Pro Controller (`057e:2009`), then an 8BitDo HID interface, never a keyboard. `src/map8bitdo.c` (8BitDo DInput report 1), `src/mapxinput.c` (Xbox 360 report) and `src/mapswitch.c` (Switch Pro report 0x30) turn the reports into DualSense buttons. - A Switch Pro Controller gets the USB handshake (80 02, 80 03, 80 02, 80 04) and its subcommands (full reports, vibration, player light) at connection; without them it keeps enumerating again. Its rumble is HD Rumble, encoded as SDL does and sent again every 50 ms while on. - Rumble: `scePadVirtualDeviceGetRemoteSetting` is read every 16 ms per virtual pad (motors at [3] and [4]). - XInput devices get what Windows sends first (the Microsoft OS string and the XUSB vendor request, then the LED): the USB Wireless Adapter 2 keeps XInput when its host answers like that. A boot keyboard or mouse beside the pad is detached from the console's driver. - When a controller sleeps or switches off, the dongle or adapter enumerates again ("IDLE") and the open device ends. - `src/ps5_vpad.c` creates the virtual DualSense (`scePadVirtualDevice*`), finds its device id in the kernel log, gives it to a user (`sceMbusBindDeviceWithUserId`) and feeds it. It follows the kernel log while running: the console's choice of user is remembered, and its "turn off" (`sceMbusDisconnectDevice`) removes the virtual pad. - `src/web.c` serves the settings page without ever blocking the controllers; `src/config.c` keeps its choices. - `src/probe.c` is a read-only diagnostic payload: it dumps the USB descriptors, names and reports of whatever is plugged in. Useful to add support for another controller. ## Build Needs [ps5-payload-sdk](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk) and clang, lld and llvm. `tools/setup-wsl.sh` (Linux or WSL) or `tools/setup-macos.sh` (Homebrew) installs them and writes `~/.ps5sdk`: ``` . ~/.ps5sdk make test # button maps, interface choice, settings, status JSON, on the PC make # dist/padbridge-.elf and dist/padbridge-probe.elf ``` ## Credits - The virtual DualSense code (`ps5_vpad.c`) and the helpers `log.c`, `util.c`, `lock.c`, `ps5_power.c` and `pad.h` come from **AnyPad PS5** by **@elmonomalvad0** (sinfiltros), GPL-3.0-or-later, adapted here. - [ps5-payload-sdk](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk) by John Törnblom. - The Switch Pro Controller's USB protocol and HD Rumble: [dekuNukem's Nintendo Switch reverse engineering notes](https://github.com/dekuNukem/Nintendo_Switch_Reverse_Engineering), and [SDL](https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL)'s HIDAPI Switch driver, whose rumble tables `src/mapswitch.c` uses (zlib licence). - [Control4Free](https://github.com/MoHadiShibli/Control4Free) (GPL-3.0), whose notes showed that `scePadVirtualDeviceGetRemoteSetting` returns what a game asks of a virtual pad. ## Licence GPL-3.0-or-later. See [LICENSE](LICENSE). No Sony code, keys or firmware are part of this project. padbridge does not jailbreak anything: it needs a console that already runs a payload loader.

latestRelease.name: padbridge 1.3.1
latestRelease.body:
A fix for rest mode. Tested on a PS5 Slim (CFI-2114), firmware 13.60. See the [README](https://github.com/sub0x00001/padbridge#readme) for compatibility and the settings page.

**Files**
- `padbridge-1.3.1.elf`: the payload. Send it to your payload loader or add it to Payload Manager's autoload.
- `padbridge-probe.elf`: an optional read-only diagnostic that dumps the descriptors and reports of USB devices plugged into the console.

Check a download against its `.sha256` file.

**Changes since 1.3.0**
- **Rest mode no longer stops padbridge.** It used to stop before rest mode, and an autoload list only runs at a cold start, so after waking the console had no padbridge (a 2C dongle in XInput mode then showed up as a keyboard). Now padbridge lets the controllers go in rest mode, waits, and picks them up again when the console wakes.

Everything from 1.3.0 is unchanged: rumble in PS4 games, the Switch Pro Controller and the adapter's Switch mode, View + Menu as the touchpad.

repos.name: Prospero-Explorer
repos.description: A file explorer homebrew application for the PS5 console, written in C# on top of the SharpProspero SDK.
repos.readme: # Prospero Explorer A file explorer for the console, built on the SharpProspero SDK. It browses and manages the file system, unpacks and builds archives, plays audio and video, views and edits text, views and converts pictures, installs packages from the writable area and from removable devices, launches an installed title, serves the whole file system over the network, opens a web address, and reports what the machine is doing. The interface draws its text with the console's own font when the system provides it, falling back to the built-in one otherwise, and every page carries a breadcrumb of where you are and a header that says what its buttons do. It exercises most of the SharpProspero SDK end to end, so it doubles as a way to check that a build of the toolchain works on real hardware. ## Building The result is always a module folder, not an installable pkg file (for now). ```bash pwsh ./build.ps1 ``` The module lands in `out/module`. Copy the whole folder, not just `eboot.bin`: it carries the metadata and the modules the application needs beside it. The SDK is expected beside this project in the same checkout. Point elsewhere with `-SdkRoot`, or set `SHARPPROSPERO_ROOT`. An installer treats a title already on the machine as present and declines to replace it, so a build meant to sit beside the last one needs a title of its own (or replaced): ```bash pwsh ./build.ps1 -TitleId PPSA99108 ``` ## What it does | Area | What is there | |---|---| | Browsing | Listing with sizes and kinds, sorting, hidden names, find within a folder, multiple selection, copy, cut, paste, rename, delete, new folder, new file, properties, checksums | | Archives | Browse and unpack zip and tar, unpack a lone gzip or zlib stream, build a zip or tar from a selection | | Media | Audio and video playback with seeking, looping, volume and tags; WAV and VAG play through the decoders when the player will not take them | | Text | Viewer with line numbers, wrapping, a hex view and a table view for comma- or tab-separated files; editing by line, find, go to line, save and save as | | Pictures | PNG, JPEG, BMP, TGA and GIF; fit modes, panning and pinch-zoom by touch, rotate, flip, grayscale, invert, brightness, contrast, blur, a screenshot of the view, and conversion between every form that can be written | | Packages | Finds installable files in the writable area and on removable devices, installs them, reports whether a title is already present, and launches an installed title by its id | | Network | A file service over the network reaching the whole file system, with optional login, a read-only mode and a root it cannot climb above | | Web | Opens a web address in the system browser | | System | Console, users, network, memory, storage and display readings | | Settings | Every part of the above, kept between runs | ## Where it keeps things Settings and the log live in `/data/prospero-explorer`. Nothing else is written unless you ask for it. ## Controls D-pad moves, Cross selects, Circle goes back, and Circle on the first page leaves. Where a page offers more, its header says so: Triangle usually opens the actions for whatever is selected, and Square usually toggles a selection.

latestRelease.body:
## Prospero Explorer v1.0

### What is Prospero Explorer

Prospero Explorer is a file explorer for the PS5 console, built on the SharpProspero SDK. It browses and manages the file system, unpacks and builds archives, plays audio and video, views and edits text, views and converts pictures, installs packages from the writable area and from removable devices, launches an installed title, serves the whole file system over the network, opens a web address, and reports what the machine is doing.

### How to install & launch

- Unzip the file ```ProsperoExplorer-v1.zip``` **into a folder** and **move/copy the folder** to ```/homebrew``` on your USB **OR** ```/data/homebrew``` on the console
- Install using [dump_installer](https://github.com/EchoStretch/dump_installer)
- Launch from home screen

### Features

| Feature | Description |
|---|---|
| Browsing | Listing with sizes and kinds, sorting, hidden names, find within a folder, multiple selection, copy, cut, paste, rename, delete, new folder, new file, properties, checksums |
| Archives | Browse and unpack zip and tar, unpack a lone gzip or zlib stream, build a zip or tar from a selection |
| Media | Audio and video playback with seeking, looping, volume and tags; WAV and VAG play through the decoders when the player will not take them |
| Text | Viewer with line numbers, wrapping, a hex view and a table view for comma- or tab-separated files; editing by line, find, go to line, save and save as |
| Pictures | PNG, JPEG, BMP, TGA and GIF; fit modes, panning and pinch-zoom by touch, rotate, flip, grayscale, invert, brightness, contrast, blur, a screenshot of the view, and conversion between every form that can be written |
| Packages | Finds installable files in the writable area and on removable devices, installs them, reports whether a title is already present, and launches an installed title by its id |
| Network | A file service over the network reaching the whole file system, with optional login, a read-only mode and a root it cannot climb above |
| Web | Opens a web address in the system browser |
| System | Console, users, network, memory, storage and display readings |
| Settings | Every part of the above, kept between runs |

repos.name: Prospero-Multi-Tools
repos.description: PS5 Homebrew Backup Manager & Toolkit for PS1, PS2, PS3, PS4, PS5, PSP and PS Vita backups.
repos.readme:
# Prospero Multi Tools

A PS5 Backup Toolkit for PS1, PS2, PS3, PS4, PS5, PSP and PS Vita. Browse backups, inspect and modify metadata, install PS4/PS5 packages, launch PS1/PS2/PSP titles, and more. ## Contents - [Prospero Multi Tools](#prospero-multi-tools) - [Contents](#contents) - [What you need](#what-you-need) - [Download](#download) - [Install the app](#install-the-app) - [Set up the emulators](#set-up-the-emulators) - [First run checklist](#first-run-checklist) - [Where installed backups live](#where-installed-backups-live) - [Uninstalling a backup](#uninstalling-a-backup) - [Backup covers and icons](#backup-covers-and-icons) - [What every screen does](#what-every-screen-does) - [Settings you might want to change](#settings-you-might-want-to-change) - [Known limits](#known-limits) ## What you need - A PS5 running a firmware supported by the [`unjail`](https://github.com/SvenGDK/unjail-ps5app-payload)` payload. - The `unjail` payload sent to the console before you open the app. Without it, the app cannot widen its file view past its own sandbox: installs, emulator launches, and every scan of `/data` or a USB drive will refuse. The `unjail` payload is required for every launch. - An USB drive is enough to get started. The app also reads and writes `/data` and `/user` internally once the escalation daemon is running. ## Download Two files are available on the Releases page: - `ProsperoMultiTools.zip` — the homebrew app itself as a signed folder module ready to install on the console. - `EmulatorPack.zip` — the emulator folders and the shared `emulator-resources/`. ## Install the app 1. Unzip `ProsperoMultiTools.zip`. 2. Copy the resulting folder to an USB drive `/homebrew/PPSA99110` or the console's own storage `/data/homebrew/PPSA99110`. 3. Install the homebrew app with [`dump_installer`](https://github.com/EchoStretch/dump_installer) 4. Send the [`unjail`](https://github.com/SvenGDK/unjail-ps5app-payload) payload to the console once per boot before opening the app. ## Set up the emulators The launch paths for PS1, PS2 and PSP backups drive the emulators shipped in `EmulatorPack.zip`. 1. Unpack `EmulatorPack.zip`. 2. Copy the emulator folders you want (`ps1hd`, `psphd`, and any PS2 emulator folders such as `BULLY`, `JAK`, `MANHUNT`, `Siren`, `RotkV1`, ...) onto the console. The primary location is: `/data/homebrew/emulators//` USB alternatives are also accepted: `/mnt/usbN/homebrew/emulators//` (N = 0..7) 3. Copy the whole `emulator-resources/` folder from the same archive to: `/data/homebrew/emulator-resources/` on the console or to an USB drive `/homebrew/emulator-resources` 4. Open the app and check the `Diagnostics` screen. It lists every emulator folder the current install detected under `/data/homebrew/emulators/` and each USB root. ## First run checklist - Open the app. The bottom of the Home screen tells you how many storage locations answered. If it says zero, the escalation daemon has not been sent yet or no USB drive is plugged in. - Open `Diagnostics`. It reports whether the escalation daemon widened the file view, which storage roots are reachable, whether the file broker is answering, and which emulators the current install carries. ## Where installed backups live `/data/homebrew/games//` ## Uninstalling a backup Uninstalling a backup from the console's own home screen removes the shell registration only. The `/data/homebrew/games//` folder is left in place. Remove it by hand from a file manager if you want the disk space back. An automated cleanup step will be added into the app in a later version. ## Backup covers and icons PS3, PS4, PS5, PSP and PS Vita backups carry their icon art inside their own PKG file, so the app reads it directly. PS1 and PS2 backups do not carry that image. The first time a PS1 or PS2 backup is opened, the app fetches its cover from the network and stores it in an on-device cache. This means: - An active internet connection is required the first time a PS1 or PS2 cover is displayed. - Every subsequent open reads from the on-device cache; the network is not touched again for that title. ## What every screen does - `Backup Managers` — one entry per platform (PS1, PS2, PS3, PS4, PS5, PSP, PS Vita). Each opens a scan of every reachable storage root; the result is a split view with a cover preview on the left and metadata on the right. Selecting a backup opens the detail screen. - `Backup detail` — title, game id, content id, region, category, version, firmware, size, source file or folder, plus the SFO or `param.json` rows. Action buttons: `Launch from folder`, `Install package`, `Launch title`, `Configure and launch` (for the emulator-based platforms), `Copy backup`, `Move backup`, `Delete backup`, `Edit SFO`, `Edit param.json`. - `Emulator launch` — per-title options plus a live launch driver. PS1, PS2 and PSP each have their own option set (render scale, aspect, filters, multitap, disc count, VMC path, and so on). - `PS1 / PS2 Tools` — merge multi-BIN CUE sets into a single BIN, convert PS2 BIN/CUE images to ISO. - `PS5 Tools` — send an ELF payload over TCP, clear the console's error history, read the inserted disc's `param.json`, and probe the well-known homebrew TCP ports (payload, WebSrv, FTP, klog, kernel exploit, PKG installer, and so on). - `Console Utilities` — per-platform SFO / backup folder / PKG inspection for PS3, PS4, PSP and PS Vita. - `Shared Tools -> Shared Utilities` — browse any folder the file view exposes, and view a file's first bytes as a hex dump. - `System -> Settings` — display, behaviour, audio, payload-sender defaults, and a reset button. - `System -> Diagnostics` — the reachability report described above. - `System -> Refresh storage` — re-probes every root without leaving the app. - `System -> Unlock full storage access` — sends the escalation request again if it did not apply at boot. - `Exit` — close the app. ## Settings you might want to change - `Paths -> Start path` sets the folder the file pickers open at. - `Paths -> Backup search path` overrides the default scan set (`/data` plus every USB) with a semicolon-separated list of folders. - `Display -> Text scale` and `Display -> List rows` adjust the reading density. - `Behavior -> Confirm before delete / move` toggles the confirmation dialog for destructive actions. - `Behavior -> Show hidden files` toggles dotfile visibility in the picker. - `Behavior -> System notifications` toggles the top-screen toast messages the shell posts. - `Behavior -> Notification time` sets how long toasts stay on screen. - `Audio -> Play soundtrack when available` toggles the per-title soundtrack playback in `Backup detail`. - `Audio -> Volume` sets the soundtrack playback volume. - `Payload sender -> Host` and `Port` are the defaults `PS5 Tools -> Payload sender` picks up. - `Reset -> Reset all settings to defaults` restores every option above to its shipped default. ## Known limits - `/data` and `/user` are not offered by the file and folder browser yet. Every launch and install path still reaches them correctly through the file broker. - Uninstalling a backup from the console's home screen leaves `/data/homebrew/games//` behind. Remove the folder by hand for now. - The `unjail` payload must be sent again every time the console reboots. - PS1 and PS2 cover art needs an active internet connection the first time each title is displayed.

repos.name: ps5-library-browser
repos.description: Native PS5 Game Library Browser & Launcher with NFS support, ShadowMountPlus daemon lock, and Itemzflow-inspired UI
repos.readme:
# PS5 Library Browser

A high-performance, native PS5 library manager and game browser inspired by **Itemzflow**, engineered in modern **C++20**.

`ps5-library-browser` provides an intuitive interface for managing local and network-mounted game libraries, inspecting title packages (Base Games, Add-on DLCs, Title Updates), and managing multi-item installation queues with full **ShadowMountPlus** integration.

---

## 🌟 Key Features

### 1. Game, DLC & Update Package Inspector
- **Header & Outside Info**: Displays game title, Title ID (`PPSA` / `CUSA`), cover art, base game size, primary format (`PKG`, `exFAT`, `FFPKG`), and total package footprint.
- **Three Dedicated Section Tabs**: Quick navigation between **Game**, **DLC**, and **Update** package sections.
- **Formatted & Highlighted Package Details**: Displays filename, human-readable size, highlighted file format badges (`[.PKG]`, `[.EXFAT]`, `[.FFPKG]`), version numbers, and live installation status.
- **Per-Item Install Actions**: Install individual base games, specific DLC packages, or individual title updates directly.
- **DLC "Install All" Pipeline**: One-touch batch installation of all DLC add-ons with cumulative progress, item-level status tracking, cancellation, and granular failure reporting.

### 2. Dual-Mode Library Architecture
- **Installed Games Mode**: Instant local launcher for installed applications on the PS5.
- **Library Browser Mode**: Browses local storage (`/hostapp`), custom directories, and remote NFS mounts.
- **ShadowMountPlus Feature Lock**: Browsing remote libraries is gated behind a live health check to the local **ShadowMountPlus** daemon (`127.0.0.1:10101`). If the daemon is absent, the user is presented with a clear lock dialog explaining that ShadowMount Plus is required.

### 3. Native Dual-View Carousel & Block Grid
- **Coverflow Carousel**: 3D-styled cover art carousel with real-time scaling, depth ordering, and smooth scrolling.
- **5-Column Block Grid**: High-density library grid view optimized for large game collections.
- **Format Filters & Live Search**: Filter entries instantly by format (`PKG`, `exFAT`, `FFPKG`, `Folder`) or search by title and Title ID.

### 4. DualSense Input & Prompts
- Native mapping for DualSense D-Pad and analog stick navigation with deadzone and auto-repeat support.
- Dynamic contextual button prompt bar (`△ Toggle Mode / Install All DLCs`, `Touchpad View`, `L1/R1 Filter / Tabs`, `□ Inspect`, `✕ Select / Install`, `○ Back`).
- Modal dialogs for connection recovery and lock explanations.

### 5. High-Speed Scanner & Persistent Cached Indexing
- Scans `/hostapp`, local folders, and network mounts.
- Decodes `sce_sys/param.json` categories (`gd` base game, `gp` patch, `ac` DLC) and title ID tags (`PPSA` / `CUSA`).
- Atomic JSON cache engine ensures zero-latency library startup.

---

## 📂 Architecture

```
ps5-library-browser/
├── .github/workflows/ci.yml         # Automated host build & unit test CI workflow
├── CMakeLists.txt                   # Cross-platform CMake configuration
├── include/ps5_library/
│   ├── daemon_client.hpp            # ShadowMountPlus daemon probe & feature gate
│   ├── game_metadata.hpp            # Metadata parser, categories, and models
│   ├── scanner.hpp                  # Recursive multi-source scanner
│   ├── index_cache.hpp              # Atomic persistent cache & query filters
│   ├── input.hpp                    # DualSense pad mapping & prompt model
│   ├── views.hpp                    # Coverflow & Block Grid layout calculations
│   ├── installer.hpp                # Install pipeline, delegates & batch engine
│   ├── inspector.hpp                # Package inspector state, formatting & tabs
│   └── ui_shell.hpp                 # Native UI shell, state machine & dialogs
├── src/
│   ├── daemon_client.cpp            # Socket client & lock manager
│   ├── game_metadata.cpp            # Param parser & Title ID heuristics
│   ├── scanner.cpp                  # Directory scanner & grouping
│   ├── index_cache.cpp              # Atomic cache implementation
│   ├── input.cpp                    # Input processing & repeat timer
│   ├── views.cpp                    # Coverflow & Grid card positioning
│   ├── installer.cpp                # Install task queue & DLC batch execution
│   ├── inspector.cpp                # Package formatting & inspector navigation
│   └── ui_shell.cpp                 # UI shell flow & input routing
├── tests/
│   ├── daemon_client_test.cpp       # Milestone 1 tests
│   ├── scanner_cache_test.cpp       # Milestone 2 tests
│   ├── ui_shell_test.cpp            # Milestone 3 tests
│   ├── inspector_installer_test.cpp # Milestone 4 tests
│   ├── ps5_installer_persistence_test.cpp # PS5 install delegate, persistence & recovery tests
│   └── install_retry_preflight_history_test.cpp # Retry, preflight & searchable history tests
└── README.md
```

---

## 🛠️ Building & Testing

### Prerequisites
- Modern C++20 compiler (`gcc` 10+, `clang` 11+, or MSVC 2019+)
- CMake 3.16+
- POSIX-compatible host or PS5 homebrew SDK environment

### Build Commands
```bash
# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/sweenyxsky-oss/ps5-library-browser.git
cd ps5-library-browser

# Configure and compile
cmake -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build build -j$(nproc)

# Execute test suite
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
```

---

## 🛣️ Development Roadmap

- [x] **Milestone 1: Daemon Health Probe & Feature Lock Engine**
  - Socket HTTP client with non-blocking polling and timeout controls
  - Feature gating with mandatory prompt: *"ShadowMount Plus is required to unlock these features"*
  - Automated mock daemon test suite
- [x] **Milestone 2: High-Speed Game Scanner, Metadata Classifier & Atomic Index Cache**
  - Fast traversal of `/hostapp` and mounted paths
  - `sce_sys/param.json` parser classifying Base Games (`gd`), Updates (`gp`), and DLCs (`ac`)
  - Title ID validation (`PPSA`, `CUSA`, `LAPY`, `FAKE`)
  - Atomic JSON v2 cache with PID/timestamp temporary file write and atomic rename
- [x] **Milestone 3: Native Dual-Mode UI Engine & DualSense Navigation**
  - Mode toggle: Installed Games vs Library Browser
  - Gated remote browser requiring ShadowMountPlus daemon
  - Selectable views: Coverflow carousel and 5-column Block Grid
  - Format filters (PKG, exFAT, FFPKG, Folder) and live search
  - Contextual DualSense button prompt bar and input repeat handling
- [x] **Milestone 4: Game/DLC/Update Package Inspector & Multi-Installer**
  - Package Inspector with Game, DLC, and Update section tabs
  - Formatted package metadata with highlighted file extensions (`[.PKG]`, `[.EXFAT]`, `[.FFPKG]`) and human-readable sizes
  - Per-item install triggers for games, DLCs, and updates
  - "Install All DLCs" pipeline with progress callbacks, cancellation, and granular failure recovery
  - **PS5 Package Install Delegate & Capability Model**: Safe runtime probe checking kernel privileges and system service availability (`libSceAppInstUtil`); returns descriptive `UnsupportedPlatform` diagnostics and guidance on non-PS5 hosts
  - **Persistent Install Jobs Across Restarts**: Atomic JSON state tracking (`/tmp/ps5_library_install_jobs.json`) persisting queued/completed jobs; automatically restores `InProgress` tasks as `Interrupted` on restart
  - **Post-Install Library & Inspector Refresh**: Real-time promotion of item confidence and inspector state upon package installation completion
  - **Actionable Recovery Guidance**: Granular troubleshooting steps for every error code (unsupported platform, missing privileges, missing system services, out of storage, corrupted header, interrupted install)
  - **Install Preflight Validation**: Multi-stage verification inspecting file existence, readability, storage capacity against package size (with configurable safety margin), and header signature format (`.pkg` magic `\x7FPKG`/`PKG\0`, `.ffpkg`/`.exfat` header sizes); prevents corrupt package dispatches before calling target install delegates.
  - **Duplicate Prevention & Retry Workflow**: Preflight duplicate detection prevents queueing conflicting installs for already active/queued jobs, while dedicated retry actions preserve original task IDs, prior error codes/messages, retry counters, and timestamps.
  - **Searchable Install History & Diagnostics**: Full job diagnostic history recording submission/completion timestamps, package identifiers, failure reasons, retry provenance, and step-by-step remediation guidance; accessible via the UI Shell history dialog.
  - **CSV & JSON Install History Export**: Export complete diagnostic logs with timestamps, Title IDs, filenames, format, size/byte counts, outcomes, error details, recovery steps, and retry ancestry (`original_task_id`, `original_error_code`, `retry_count`) directly to file or string buffers.
  - **Granular History Filtering & Multi-Key Sorting**: Multi-criteria filtering by install outcome (`Completed`, `Failed`, `Interrupted`, `Cancelled`, `Queued`, `InProgress`), package format (`pkg`, `exfat`, `ffpkg`, `folder`), and ISO 8601 date ranges; sortable ascending or descending by timestamp or package filename.
  - **Retry Confirmation Modal with Live Preflight Verification**: Interactive UI modal surfacing prior failure diagnostics and re-executing live preflight checks to ensure errors are resolved before requeueing.
  - **Per-Check Preflight Summary**: Clear per-check diagnostic breakdown across File Readability, Package Metadata/Header, and Available Storage with safety margins before dispatching to the installer.
  - **Immediate Preflight Re-Check & Changed Results Diffing**: Automatically verifies package readability, format/metadata signatures, and storage capacity immediately before dispatch, detecting and reporting deviations from initial summary snapshots.
  - **Export File Picker & Configurable Filenames**: Interactive modal for selecting destination directories and filenames for CSV/JSON diagnostic logs with real-time feedback and remediation on failure.
  - **Cross-Session Filter & Sort Persistence**: Atomically preserves install history filter options (outcome, format, date ranges, query) and sort preferences across application restarts.
- [x] **Milestone 5: PS5 Payload Packaging & Cross-Compilation Workflow**
  - Dedicated CMake PS5 target (`ps5_library_browser_elf`) producing `ps5-library-browser.elf`
  - Target entrypoint (`src/main.cpp`) with DualSense event loop, headless verification, `/hostapp` default scanning, and daemon health probe
  - Homebrew metadata package manifest (`sce_sys/param.json`)
  - Automated PS5 cross-compilation CI workflow with `pacbrew-repo` and `ps5-payload-sdk` toolchain packaging
  - **Structured Startup Diagnostics**: Comprehensive boot-time health checks covering root scan mount availability, ShadowMountPlus daemon connectivity, network subsystem initialization, and persistence storage writeability.
  - **On-Screen Recovery Guidance**: Active diagnostic issues automatically trigger an interactive UI dialog with step-by-step remediation procedures and live diagnostics re-run capabilities.
  - **Automated Package & ELF Architecture CI Validation**: Dedicated release validator (`tools/validate_release_package.py`) enforcing archive integrity, required metadata (`sce_sys/param.json`), and 64-bit Little-Endian x86_64 ELF execution attributes.
  - **Tag-Triggered GitHub Release Publishing**: Automated release pipeline generating versioned GitHub Releases with verified release archives when a `v*` tag is pushed.

---

## 🚀 Installation & Setup on PS5

### Prerequisites
1. **PlayStation 5 Console**: Running compatible homebrew firmware (e.g. 3.xx–4.xx) with an active ELF loader or payload environment.
2. **[ShadowMountPlus](https://github.com/sweenyxsky-oss/ShadowMountPlus)**: Installed and running in the background. PS5 Library Browser requires the ShadowMountPlus local daemon (`127.0.0.1:10101`) to unlock remote NFS browsing and virtual mounting features.
3. **Network Connection**: PS5 connected to your local network with access to your NFS storage server (e.g., TrueNAS).

---

### Installation Methods

#### Method 1: Payload Injection via Netcat / ELF Loader
1. Download the latest release package (`ps5-library-browser_v*.zip`) from the [Releases](https://github.com/sweenyxsky-oss/ps5-library-browser/releases) page and extract it.
2. Launch the ELF loader on your PS5 (listening on port `9020` or `9021`).
3. Send `ps5-library-browser.elf` from your computer using `nc` (netcat) or any PS5 payload sender tool:
   ```bash
   # Linux / macOS
   nc -w 3 <PS5_IP_ADDRESS> 9020 < ps5-library-browser.elf

   # Windows (PowerShell with ncat or GUI payload sender)
   ncat -w 3 <PS5_IP_ADDRESS> 9020 < ps5-library-browser.elf
   ```

#### Method 2: Homebrew Directory Installation (FTP / Itemzflow)
1. Extract the release ZIP package containing `ps5-library-browser.elf` and the `sce_sys/` folder.
2. Connect to your PS5 via FTP (e.g., FTPS5 or Itemzflow built-in FTP server).
3. Transfer the extracted files to `/data/homebrew/ps5-library-browser/` or `/hostapp/`.
4. Launch the application from your PS5 homebrew menu (e.g., [Itemzflow](https://github.com/sweenyxsky-oss/Itemzflow) or [ProsperoMgr](https://github.com/sweenyxsky-oss/ProsperoMgr)).

---

### Startup & Controls Guide

On startup, the built-in **Diagnostics Engine** verifies the scan mount, network stack, cache files, and the ShadowMountPlus daemon. If ShadowMountPlus is offline, an on-screen recovery guidance dialog will appear explaining how to launch the daemon to unlock remote features.

| Button | Action |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Square** | Switch Mode: **Installed Games** ⇄ **Library Browser** |
| **Triangle** | Toggle View: **Coverflow Carousel** ⇄ **5-Column Block Grid** |
| **D-Pad / Left Stick** | Navigate Game Cards & Packages |
| **Cross** | Open Game / DLC / Update Inspector & Execute Install |
| **Circle** | Back / Close Dialog / Dismiss Guidance |
| **Options** | Open Filter & Sort History Modal |

---

## 🌟 Credits & Acknowledgments

This project is **inspired by [Itemzflow](https://github.com/LightningMods/Itemzflow) & [PS5 Library](https://github.com/victor-s-santos/ps5-library)**. We gratefully acknowledge and credit the creators and maintainers of the following open-source repositories and tools:

- **[Itemzflow](https://github.com/LightningMods/Itemzflow)** ([fork: sweenyxsky-oss/Itemzflow](https://github.com/sweenyxsky-oss/Itemzflow)) — by LightningMods & contributors. The iconic PS4/PS5 homebrew game manager and launcher that inspired this project's browsing, metadata organization, and package installation experience.
- **[ps5-library](https://github.com/victor-s-santos/ps5-library)** ([fork: sweenyxsky-oss/ps5-library](https://github.com/sweenyxsky-oss/ps5-library)) — by victor-s-santos. The foundation for game library scanning concepts, title ID resolution, and TrueNAS/NFS game repository browsing.
- **[ps5-homebrew-ui](https://github.com/victor-s-santos/ps5-homebrew-ui)** ([fork: sweenyxsky-oss/ps5-homebrew-ui](https://github.com/sweenyxsky-oss/ps5-homebrew-ui)) — by victor-s-santos. Modern native C++20 UI framework for PlayStation 5 homebrew, providing the architectural foundation for carousel, block-grid views, and controller navigation.
- **[ShadowMountPlus](https://github.com/Shadow-M0unt/ShadowMountPlus)** ([fork: sweenyxsky-oss/ShadowMountPlus](https://github.com/sweenyxsky-oss/ShadowMountPlus)) — Virtual mounting subsystem and background daemon (`127.0.0.1:10101`) providing remote NFS/network storage mounting and `sce_sys/param.json` metadata parsing.
- **[RemotePFS](https://github.com/flatz/RemotePFS)** ([fork: sweenyxsky-oss/RemotePFS](https://github.com/sweenyxsky-oss/RemotePFS)) — by flatz & contributors. Remote PFS mounting and network filesystem utilities for PlayStation 5.
- **[ps5-ezremote-client](https://github.com/G991/ps5-ezremote-client)** ([fork: sweenyxsky-oss/ps5-ezremote-client](https://github.com/sweenyxsky-oss/ps5-ezremote-client)) — by G991. Remote client utilities and network mounting integrations.
- **[libnfs](https://github.com/sahlberg/libnfs)** ([fork: sweenyxsky-oss/libnfs](https://github.com/sweenyxsky-oss/libnfs)) — by Ronnie Sahlberg. Robust userland client library for NFS network shares.
- **[fuse-nfs](https://github.com/sahlberg/fuse-nfs)** ([fork: sweenyxsky-oss/fuse-nfs](https://github.com/sweenyxsky-oss/fuse-nfs)) — by Ronnie Sahlberg. FUSE filesystem module for mounting NFSv3/4 shares.
- **[ProsperoMgr](https://github.com/idlesauce/ProsperoMgr)** ([fork: sweenyxsky-oss/ProsperoMgr](https://github.com/sweenyxsky-oss/ProsperoMgr)) — All-in-one manager for PlayStation 5 homebrew.
- **[ps5-payload-sdk](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk)** & **[pacbrew-repo](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/pacbrew-repo)** — Official PS5 homebrew SDK, toolchain wrappers (`prospero-clang++`), and runtime libraries for native ELF execution.
- **[JSON for Modern C++](https://github.com/nlohmann/json)** — by Niels Lohmann. Header-only JSON library used for atomic caching, param parsing, diagnostics reporting, and job persistence.

---

### Building & Cross-Compiling for PS5

#### Host Simulation & Testing (Linux / macOS)
```bash
cmake -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build build
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
./build/ps5-library-browser.elf --headless
```

#### PS5 Cross-Compilation (PS5 Payload SDK / Prospero)
```bash
cmake -B build-ps5 \
  -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=/opt/ps5-payload-sdk/toolchain/prospero.cmake \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DPS5=ON
cmake --build build-ps5 --target ps5_library_browser_elf
```

repos.name: PS5-Network-Mounting
repos.readme:
# PS5 Network Mounting

Network Share FUSE Mount Daemon & Prospero Web Interface for PlayStation 5

Mount remote NFS exports and SMB2/SMB3 shares read-only to /hostapp on PS5 homebrew.

--- ## Overview **PS5 Network Mounting** is a native PS5 homebrew payload and daemon that mounts remote network shares directly into the PlayStation 5 filesystem at `/hostapp` using a user-space FUSE adapter. Once mounted, the console and homebrew loaders can browse, read, and execute applications, games, and packages directly over the local network without transferring files to the internal SSD or USB storage. The daemon includes an embedded HTTP server serving a modern web control interface designed around the **ProsperoMgr** visual identity. The interface is accessible from the PS5 browser and other devices on the local network. The optional home-screen tile is registered through ShadowMountPlus and opens the local control panel only while this payload daemon is running. --- ## Key Features - **Console Integration & UX (ProsperoMgr Style):** - **WebKit Browser Launch:** On loading the ELF payload, the daemon attempts to open the PS5 browser at its LAN URL and exposes a manual retry action in the panel. - **On-Screen PS5 Toast Notifications:** Displays native on-screen toast notifications upon startup showing the payload version and the local network listening URL (`http://:18080`). - **Resilient Network Daemon:** Recovers gracefully if `sceNetInit` or net pools are already initialized by your payload launcher or earlier homebrew. - **Supported Protocols:** - **NFS (v3/v4):** Backed by `libnfs` and a low-latency PS5 FUSE adapter. Connects directly to TrueNAS, Synology, QNAP, or Linux exports. - **SMB2 / SMB3:** Backed by `libsmb2` and a dedicated FUSE adapter with guest and authenticated session support. - *FTP and SFTP are intentionally omitted to focus on high-throughput, kernel-mountable block/file protocols.* - **Kernel & Execution Compatibility:** - Regular files are mapped with executable permissions (`0555`), allowing native PS5 game binaries (`eboot.bin`), PRX shared libraries, and assets to execute seamlessly from `/hostapp`. - Directories are mapped with standard directory permissions (`0755`). - Automatic creation of the `/hostapp` mount target if missing. - **Embedded Web Control Panel (ProsperoMgr Theme):** - Styled to match the dark graphite/navy palette (`#0a0e16`, `#10161f`, `#161e2a`) and blue accents (`#2f8cff`) of ProsperoMgr. - Live mount health indicators with pulsing status pill (`.pmgr-live-dot`). - Fully embedded in the binary via `tools/embed_ui.py` — zero external runtime asset dependencies. - **Hardened HTTP Daemon & API:** - **Network-wide accessibility:** Binds to `0.0.0.0:18080` by default so any PC, phone, or tablet on your LAN can manage mounts. - **Concurrency:** Thread-pool dispatch supporting up to 32 concurrent requests with socket timeouts to prevent stalls. - **Standard JSON Parser:** Built-in RFC 8259 parser (`native/json.hpp`) replacing naive substring search, with validation against malformed payloads and key collisions. - **CSRF & Origin Protection:** Strict checks against cross-origin attacks with required `X-Requested-With: PS5NM` request validation. --- ## Architecture & Layout ``` ├── .github/workflows/ │ ├── ps5-full-nfs-smb-build.yml # Full PS5 target ELF cross-compilation CI │ └── source-checks.yml # Host build, JSON unit tests, smoke tests, FUSE syntax checks ├── docs/ │ ├── API.md # HTTP REST API specification │ ├── BUILD.md # Compilation guide & SDK requirements │ ├── IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md # Protocol & platform implementation details │ ├── NFS_TEST_PLAN.md # Test matrix for NFS exports │ └── THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md # Open-source licenses (libnfs, libsmb2, FUSE) ├── native/ │ ├── json.hpp # Zero-dependency, standards-compliant JSON parser │ ├── main.cpp # HTTP server, REST routing, socket worker threads │ ├── mount_backend.hpp / .cpp # Core mount orchestration & status state machine │ ├── nfs_fuse.hpp / .cpp # NFS FUSE adapter (libnfs) │ ├── smb_fuse.hpp / .cpp # SMB FUSE adapter (libsmb2) │ └── web_assets.hpp # Deterministically generated C++ header of the embedded UI ├── tests/ │ ├── http_smoke.py # Automated HTTP/REST and security test suite │ ├── net_stubs.cpp # Host networking stubs for Linux development │ └── test_json.cpp # JSON parser unit test suite ├── tools/ │ └── embed_ui.py # Compresses and embeds web/index.html into C++ header └── web/ └── index.html # Single-page web UI with ProsperoMgr styling ``` --- ## Quick Start & Usage ### 1. Launching the Payload on PS5 1. Send or run the compiled `ps5nm.elf` using your preferred PS5 payload sender (e.g. Netcat on port `9021` or payload loader). 2. The payload initializes networking (`sceNetInit`), starts the FUSE subsystem, and begins listening on `0.0.0.0:18080`. ### 2. Accessing the Control Panel - **From PS5 Browser:** Use the automatic browser launch or navigate to `http://:18080`. - **From PC / Phone / Mac:** Navigate to `http://:18080`. The console and client device must be on a reachable network. - **Home-screen tile:** The tile is a convenience shortcut to the panel, registered through ShadowMountPlus. It does not itself start the network-mounting ELF, so load the payload first after a reboot. ### 3. Mounting Shares - **NFS Share:** - **Server:** `192.168.1.50` - **Port:** `2049` (default) - **Export Path:** `/mnt/dataPool/games` (absolute path as exported on the NAS) - *Tip: Ensure the NFS export allows read permissions and `no_root_squash` or all-squash to a user with read access.* - **SMB Share:** - **Server:** `192.168.1.50` - **Port:** `445` (default) - **Share Name:** `games` or `games/PS5` (do not prefix with slashes) - **Username / Password:** Provide if your SMB server requires authentication, or leave blank for guest access. --- ## REST API Reference The web control panel communicates via JSON endpoints under `/api/v1`: | Endpoint | Method | Description | |---|---|---| | `/api/v1/status` | `GET` | Returns live mount status, active protocol, endpoint, and last error. | | `/api/v1/log` | `GET` | Downloads the latest bounded diagnostic log as plain text. | | `/api/v1/mount` | `POST` | Validates parameters and mounts the requested NFS or SMB share to `/hostapp`. | | `/api/v1/unmount` | `POST` | Safely detaches the active FUSE filesystem from `/hostapp`. | | `/api/v1/shortcut` | `POST` | Creates the HBRW homebrew folder and requests a ShadowMountPlus scan. | All `POST` requests require `Content-Type: application/json` and `X-Requested-With: PS5NM`. Detailed request/response schemas can be found in [`docs/API.md`](docs/API.md). --- ## Building ### Building on Host (Linux/macOS for Development & Testing) ```bash # Compile and run JSON unit tests g++ -std=c++17 -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Inative tests/test_json.cpp -o /tmp/test_json /tmp/test_json # Compile host binary with network stubs g++ -std=c++17 -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Inative \ native/main.cpp native/mount_backend.cpp native/shortcut.cpp native/diagnostic_log.cpp tests/net_stubs.cpp \ -pthread -o /tmp/ps5nm-host # Run automated HTTP test suite python3 tests/http_smoke.py ``` ### Building the PS5 ELF (Target Build) Target compilation requires the OpenOrbis / Prospero toolchain with ORBISDEV libraries (`libfuse`, `libnfs`, `libsmb2`, `mbedtls`, `zlib`). ```bash export OO_PS4_TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/openorbis export PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK=/path/to/ps5-payload-sdk make PS5NM_WITH_FUSE=1 ``` The automated GitHub Actions workflow (`.github/workflows/ps5-full-nfs-smb-build.yml`) builds the full production ELF release automatically on push. --- ## Acknowledgments & Credits - **[ProsperoMgr](https://github.com/Sweeney-development/ProsperoMgr):** UI design reference, color palette, and styling system. - **[Itemzflow](https://github.com/LightningMods/Itemzflow):** Reference implementation for PS5 FUSE / NFS integration (`fuse-nfs`). - **[ps5-ezremote-client](https://github.com/Sweeney-development/ps5-ezremote-client):** SMB client and `libsmb2` reference patterns. - **[libnfs](https://github.com/sahlberg/libnfs):** Client library for NFS. - **[libsmb2](https://github.com/sahlberg/libsmb2):** Client library for SMB2/SMB3.
