repos.readme:
# SymphonyStation5 **A native Navidrome music client for the PlayStation 5.** Stream your self-hosted music library from the couch, with a controller-first UI rendered in OpenGL 4.6. [![License: GPL v3+](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-GPLv3%2B-blue.svg)](LICENSE) ![Platform: PS5](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-PS5-003791) ![Title ID: PPSA17641](https://img.shields.io/badge/title%20ID-PPSA17641-555) ![C++20](https://img.shields.io/badge/C%2B%2B-20-00599C?logo=cplusplus) ![API: OpenSubsonic](https://img.shields.io/badge/API-OpenSubsonic-6c5ce7) [Features](#features) · [Install](#installing-a-release) · [Build](#building-from-source) · [Architecture](#architecture) · [Debugging](#debugging-on-hardware) · [License](#license)
--- > [!IMPORTANT] > SymphonyStation5 needs a reachable > [Navidrome](https://www.navidrome.org/) (or any OpenSubsonic-compatible) > server. It is not affiliated with Sony Interactive Entertainment or the > Navidrome project. ## Features - 🏠 **Dashboard** with five tabs you switch with **L1 / R1**: *Home*, *Albums*, *Artists*, *Settings* and *Now Playing*. - 🖼️ **Album art everywhere.** The server scales covers to one fixed size; they are decoded off the main thread and cached as textures. - 📻 **Home shelves** for *Recently played* and *Recently added* albums. - ▶️ **Streaming playback.** Songs arrive as MP3 from the server, are decoded with minimp3 on a dedicated thread, resampled to 48 kHz and fed to the audio mixer. Play/pause, next/previous and seeking are supported. - 📈 **Scrobbling.** Plays are reported to Navidrome, so *Recently played* stays accurate across all your clients. - 🔐 **Secure login** with Subsonic token auth (`md5(password + salt)`, fresh salt per request) over HTTPS via libcurl + OpenSSL. - 💾 **Remembers you.** The login is saved to title-local storage, so later launches go straight to your library. - 🎮 **Controller-first UI** built on [ps5-homebrew-ui](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-homebrew-ui) (Fresh theme), with an on-screen keyboard, UI sounds and rumble feedback. ## Controls | Button | Action | | --- | --- | | **D-pad / left stick** | Move focus | | **✕ Cross** | Select / confirm | | **◯ Circle** | Back | | **L1 / R1** | Previous / next tab | ## Requirements - Navidrome, or any server that implements the [OpenSubsonic API](https://opensubsonic.netlify.app/), reachable from the console's network. ## Installing a release 1. Download `PPSA17641.zip` from the [Releases](https://github.com/TsvetomirGT/SymphonyStation5/releases) page. 2. Unzip it and copy the `PPSA17641/` folder to `/data/homebrew/` on the console, for example over FTP. 3. The **SymphonyStation5** tile appears on the home screen. 4. Launch it and enter your server URL, username and password. > [!TIP] > You can pre-seed the login by placing a `config.json` next to `eboot.bin`: > > ```json > { > "server": "https://music.example.com", > "username": "alice", > "password": "correct horse battery staple" > } > ``` ## Building from source Development is **console-first**. The UI needs OpenGL 4.5+, which macOS lacks, so it only runs on the PS5. The platform-independent core (Subsonic client, HTTP, config, utilities) is unit-tested on the Mac. ### Host prerequisites (macOS) ```sh brew install llvm@18 coreutils findutils gnu-sed bash ninja ccache pkgconf curl ``` The Makefile puts the GNU tools and LLVM 18 first on `PATH`, so you don't need to change your shell setup. Pinned dependencies are fetched automatically into the git-ignored `.deps/` directory: | Dependency | Version | Purpose | | --- | --- | --- | | PS5 payload SDK | v0.42 | Toolchain headers and import stubs | | PacBrew | v0.40.2 | libcurl, OpenSSL, zstd, libpsl | | ps5-opengl SDK | 1.0.0 | OpenGL 4.6 on the PS5 GPU (Mesa) | | compiler-rt builtins | LLVM 18 (x86_64) | Runtime builtins Homebrew's clang lacks | | zlib | 1.3.2 | Compression for curl | ### Make targets ```sh make test # build + run the core unit tests on macOS make app # build the native title -> dist/PPSA17641/ make app-deploy PS5_HOST= # build + upload to /data/homebrew/PPSA17641 make app-launch PS5_HOST= # start the title remotely via websrv make klog PS5_HOST= # stream the kernel log (app logs + crashes) make clean # remove build/ and dist/ ``` A typical edit-run loop: ```sh make app-deploy app-launch PS5_HOST=192.168.1.50 && make klog PS5_HOST=192.168.1.50 ``` > [!NOTE] > `make app-launch` often reports HTTP 503 even when the title started. > Check `make klog` for `[NAVI]` lines. ## Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph PS5["PS5 · native title PPSA17641"] main["main.cpp
EGL 1080p · pad · audio loop"] subgraph navi["src/navi · app"] app["App
Login screen"] dash["Dashboard
Home · Albums · Artists · Settings · Now Playing"] player["Player
minimp3 → 48 kHz → mixer"] covers["CoverCache
stb_image"] tasks["TaskPool
worker pthreads"] end subgraph core["Core · unit-tested on macOS"] subsonic["subsonic::Client
token auth · JSON parsing"] http["net::http
libcurl + OpenSSL"] config["Config
config.json"] end kit["ps5-homebrew-ui
gfx · ui · audio · input"] gl["ps5-opengl
OpenGL 4.6"] end server[("Navidrome
OpenSubsonic API")] main --> app --> dash dash --> player & covers player & covers & dash --> tasks --> subsonic --> http app --> config navi --> kit --> gl http <-->|HTTPS| server ``` Each frame, `main.cpp` runs `app.update` → play UI cues → `app.compose` → `renderer.present` → `display.swap`. All network I/O happens on worker threads with 1 MiB stacks, because the console's default thread stacks are too small for TLS. ### Repository layout ```text src/ ├── navi/ The app: login, dashboard, player, cover cache, task pool ├── subsonic/ OpenSubsonic client (token auth, JSON parsing) ┐ ├── net/ Blocking HTTP GET on libcurl │ core, ├── util/ File I/O, MD5, UTF-8 helpers │ tested on ├── config.* Credentials JSON load/save ┘ macOS ├── native/ libc gaps for native titles (DNS, fcntl, CA list…) ├── main.cpp Platform loop └── gfx/ ui/ core/ audio/ platform/ runtime/ vendored ps5-homebrew-ui tests/ Core unit tests (CMake + ctest) assets/ Baked fonts and UI sound effects sce_sys/ param.json and home-screen icon tools/ tooling/ Build, deploy and FSELF tooling (vendored) third_party/ nlohmann/json, minimp3, stb ``` `tools/build.sh` compiles **every** `.c`/`.cpp` under `src/` with `-DNAVI_NATIVE`, C++20, `-fno-exceptions -fno-rtti`. New files are picked up automatically. ## Debugging on hardware - **Logs.** `sys::log("[NAVI] ...")` writes to the kernel log; stream it with `make klog`. - **Crashes** print registers and a backtrace to klog. Symbolize an address with: ```sh llvm-symbolizer --obj=build/llvm-pie.elf ``` - **Null-import crashes** (a jump to address `0`) usually mean a symbol was bound to a system module that native titles don't load, such as `libScePosixForWebKit`. Check imports with: ```sh llvm-readelf -d build/llvm-pie.elf | grep NEEDED ``` See [`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md) for the full list of native-title lessons learned on hardware. ## License SymphonyStation5 is free software, licensed under the **GNU General Public License v3.0 or later**. See [`LICENSE`](LICENSE). It builds on and statically links GPL-3.0-or-later components, plus several permissively licensed libraries. Every component, version and licence is listed in [`THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md), with full texts in [`licenses/`](licenses). ## Acknowledgements - [**BlackBearReloaded**](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded) for [ps5-homebrew-ui](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-homebrew-ui), [ps5-native-app-boilerplate](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-native-app-boilerplate) and [ps5-opengl](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-opengl), which this project is built on. - The **PS5 payload SDK** and **PacBrew** maintainers. - [**Navidrome**](https://www.navidrome.org/) and the [**OpenSubsonic**](https://opensubsonic.netlify.app/) community. - [nlohmann/json](https://github.com/nlohmann/json), [minimp3](https://github.com/lieff/minimp3), [stb](https://github.com/nothings/stb), [curl](https://curl.se/) and [OpenSSL](https://www.openssl.org/). ---
"PlayStation" and "PS5" are trademarks of Sony Interactive Entertainment Inc. SymphonyStation5 is an unofficial project and contains no Sony SDK files, keys or proprietary code.

repos.readme:
# Prospack Pack, verify and send PS5 game dumps as `.ffpfsc`, from your PC. [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/unicxrn/prospack?style=flat-square&color=9b7bff&label=release)](https://github.com/unicxrn/prospack/releases/latest) [![Downloads](https://img.shields.io/github/downloads/unicxrn/prospack/total?style=flat-square&color=3a3a40)](https://github.com/unicxrn/prospack/releases) [![Platforms](https://img.shields.io/badge/platforms-Windows%20%7C%20Linux-3a3a40?style=flat-square)](#download) [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/unicxrn/prospack?style=flat-square&color=3a3a40)](LICENSE)
Prospack takes a PS5 game dump, compresses it into a single `.ffpfsc` image on your PC, checks every file in that image against the original, uploads it to your PS5 and gets ShadowMountPlus to mount it. It's the same kind of image Game Compressor makes on the console, built on your PC's CPU instead, so it's a lot quicker. You also send one file that's usually 40 to 60% smaller than the dump, instead of tens of thousands of loose ones. ## Download | Platform | Download | | --- | --- | | **Windows 10 and 11** | [`Prospack-Setup.exe`](https://github.com/unicxrn/prospack/releases/latest) | | **Linux** | [`.AppImage`](https://github.com/unicxrn/prospack/releases/latest) for any distro, or the `.deb` for Debian and Ubuntu | Python and MkPFS are built in, so there's nothing else to install. Prospack checks for new versions when it starts and can update itself. The Windows installer isn't code-signed, so SmartScreen may say "Windows protected your PC". Click **More info**, then **Run anyway**. The checksums for every download are on the release page if you want to verify it first. ## What you need - A jailbroken PS5 with an FTP server running: ftpsrv (port 2121) or etaHEN (port 1337). - ShadowMountPlus running on the PS5. - A game dump: the folder with `sce_sys/` and `eboot.bin` in it, like `PPSA01234-app`. - Enough free space on your PC for the image while it's being written. It can need up to the size of the dump. ## Using it The first time you open Prospack, setup scans your network for the PS5, checks that ShadowMountPlus is there, and asks where to keep images. After that, drag a dump folder onto the window (or press Ctrl+O) and leave it running. Each game goes through four steps: | Step | What happens | | --- | --- | | **Compress** | [MkPFS](https://github.com/PSBrew/MkPFS) packs the dump into `.ffpfsc`: an exFAT image inside a compressed PFS container. | | **Verify** | Every file is read back out of the image and compared with the dump, byte for byte. If anything differs, the job stops before it uploads. | | **Upload** | The image goes to `/data/homebrew` under a hidden name and is renamed once it's complete. Interrupted uploads resume, and Prospack won't overwrite an image that's already there. | | **Mount** | Prospack registers the image with ShadowMountPlus and waits for the game to appear. | You can queue as many games as you like. The <kbd>?</kbd> button in the app explains every screen and walks through the common problems. <details> <summary><b>What Prospack changes on your PS5</b></summary> <br> It writes the same settings Game Compressor writes for its own images, and backs up every file on your PC before changing it: | File | Change | | --- | --- | | `/data/homebrew/<TITLE>.ffpfsc` | The image | | `/data/shadowmount/autotune.ini` | `image_sector=<TITLE>.ffpfsc:65536` | | `/data/shadowmount/config.ini` | `image_ro=<TITLE>.exfat` | | `/data/shadowmount/manual.lst` | The image path. Rewriting this file is what makes ShadowMountPlus scan for it. | | `/data/GameCompressor/validations/` | A record that makes Game Compressor show the game as validated, with the space saved. Only if Game Compressor is installed. | Your dump folder is only read. The one exception is an APR Emu game that has no `ampr_emu.index`: MkPFS adds one, because the game needs it. </details> <details> <summary><b>Troubleshooting</b></summary> <br> #### Prospack can't find my PS5 Check the PS5 is on and running its FTP server, and that the PC is on the same network. Guest Wi-Fi and VPNs often keep them apart. You can type the IP in yourself under Settings → Run setup again (the PS5 shows it under Settings → Network). #### Verify failed The image didn't match the dump, so nothing was uploaded. Use **Compress again**. If it keeps failing, copy the dump again; it may be incomplete or on a failing drive. #### ShadowMountPlus couldn't register the game The image is on the PS5, but ShadowMountPlus couldn't add it to the home screen. If the message mentions a lost system hook, that's a ShadowMountPlus 1.7beta4 (and older) bug after rest mode: update to 1.7beta5 or newer, or restart ShadowMountPlus, then use **Check again**. #### Mount not confirmed The image made it to the PS5, but ShadowMountPlus hadn't mounted it after five minutes. It often turns up a little later. Use **Check again**, or restart ShadowMountPlus. #### "The PS5 already has a different image" Delete or rename the old `<TITLE>.ffpfsc` on the PS5, then retry. #### The game shows up but won't start That's usually a firmware, backport or ShadowMountPlus version issue rather than the image. ShadowMountPlus logs to `/data/shadowmount/debug.log`. </details> ## Contributing Bug reports and pull requests are welcome. When you report a bug, the activity log for the game and your ShadowMountPlus version help a lot. To work on Prospack you need Node 22, Rust and Python 3.12: ```bash npm install pip install -r engine/requirements-build.txt && python engine/build.py npm run tauri dev ``` `npm run dev` runs the interface on its own in a browser, with a simulated PS5, which is the quickest way to work on the UI. [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) covers the project layout, the tests (which run against a fake PS5, never a real one) and the quirks of the PS5's FTP server. ## Credits Prospack is built on [MkPFS](https://github.com/PSBrew/MkPFS) and made to work alongside [ShadowMountPlus](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus), [Game Compressor](https://github.com/juma-sayeh/PS5-Game-Compressor) and [ftpsrv](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/ftpsrv). Thanks to everyone who works on them. Please only use dumps of games you own. ## License [GPL-3.0](LICENSE)

repos.description: Use o controle de PS5 (DualSense) no Switch com gatilhos adaptáveis, barra de luz, touchpad e perfis por jogo.
repos.readme:
# Control PS-5

Use o controle de PS5 (DualSense) no Nintendo Switch com **gatilhos adaptáveis, barra de luz, touchpad e perfis por jogo**.
Um app, um toque em Instalar.

**Página do projeto:** https://meowdev-mod.github.io/Control-PS-5/

## Instalar

**1. Levar o app para o cartão SD**

1. No pacote CNX, segure **R** e abra o **Álbum** para entrar no menu Homebrew.
2. Abra o **DBI** e inicie a **conexão MTP**.
3. Conecte o cabo USB do Switch ao computador.
4. No computador, abra o dispositivo **Switch**, entre em **1: SD Card** e depois em **switch**
   (`Este Computador\Switch: SD Card\switch`).
5. Copie para lá a pasta já descompactada **Control PS-5** (baixe o zip em
   [Releases](https://github.com/MeoWDev-MOD/Control-PS-5/releases/latest)).
6. Saia do DBI e volte ao menu Homebrew (**R** + **Álbum**). O Control PS-5 aparece na lista.

> Sem cabo: tire o cartão SD, coloque a pasta `Control PS-5` dentro de `switch` no computador e devolva o cartão.

**2. Instalar o driver e parear**

1. Na tela **Início**, toque no botão azul **Instalar**. Quando terminar, o app pede para reiniciar o Switch.
2. Com o Switch ligado de novo, abra o Control PS-5 outra vez.
3. Toque em **Parear controle** e escolha **Mudar ordem ou modo de segurar**.
4. No controle, segure **Create** e **PS** até as barras de luz piscarem.
5. Aperte **L1** e **R1**. Quando sincronizar, um controle preto aparece na tela e as barras de luz ficam fixas.
6. Volte ao app e configure gatilhos, luzes e perfis.

> Antes, faça uma cópia da pasta `atmosphere/contents/010000000000bd00` do cartão SD.
> Se algo der errado, **Desinstalar** no app restaura o MissionControl original.

## Capturas

| Início | Gatilhos | Luzes e vibração |
|---|---|---|
| ![Início](assets/screens/inicio.jpg) | ![Gatilhos](assets/screens/gatilhos.jpg) | ![Luzes](assets/screens/luzes.jpg) |

## Compatibilidade

- Switch com Atmosphère (pacote CNX).
- **Requer firmware 23.0.1 e Atmosphère 1.12.0** (versões em que o driver foi construído e testado).
- DualSense e DualSense Edge.

## Apoie

O app é gratuito. Pix: **21966547296**

## Créditos e aviso

Driver baseado no [MissionControl](https://github.com/ndeadly/MissionControl) (ndeadly, GPLv2) sobre o
[Atmosphère](https://github.com/Atmosphere-NX/Atmosphere), com libnx e devkitPro.
Projeto independente, sem afiliação com Sony ou Nintendo. Não habilita pirataria. Use por sua conta e risco.

Developed by **MeoWDev MOD**.

repos.name: PS5MC
repos.description: PS5MC is a PS5 port of Kodi, the award-winning free and open source home theater/media center software and entertainment hub for digital media. With its beautiful interface and powerful skinning engine.
repos.readme:
![Kodi Logo](docs/resources/banner.png)

website • docs • community • add-ons

Welcome to Kodi Home Theater Software!

Kodi is an award-winning **free and open source** software media player and entertainment hub for digital media. Available as a native application for **Android, Linux, BSD, macOS, iOS, tvOS and Windows operating systems**, Kodi runs on most common processor architectures. Created in 2003 by a group of like minded programmers, Kodi is a non-profit project run by the XBMC Foundation and developed by volunteers located around the world. More than 500 software developers have contributed to Kodi to date, and 100-plus translators have worked to expand its reach, making it available in more than 70 languages. While Kodi functions very well as a standard media player application for your computer, it has been designed to be the perfect companion for your HTPC. With its **beautiful interface and powerful skinning engine**, Kodi feels very natural to use from the couch with a remote control and is the ideal solution for your home theater. ## Give your media the love it deserves Kodi can be used to play almost all popular audio and video formats around. It was designed for network playback, so you can stream your multimedia from anywhere in the house or directly from the internet using practically any protocol available. Point Kodi to your media and watch it **scan and automagically create a personalized library** complete with box covers, descriptions, and fanart. There are playlist and slideshow functions, a weather forecast feature and many audio visualizations. Once installed, your computer or HTPC will become a fully functional multimedia jukebox.

## Getting Started Kodi's developers work hard to make it support a large range of devices and operating systems. We provide final as well as development builds. To get started, head over to the **[downloads section](https://kodi.tv/download)** and simply select the platform that you want to install it on. A **[quick start guide](https://kodi.wiki/view/quick_start_guide)** to help you get acquainted with Kodi is available in our wiki. ## How to Contribute Kodi is created by users for users and **we welcome every contribution**. There are no highly paid developers or poorly paid support personnel on the phones ready to take your call. There are only users who have seen a problem and done their best to fix it. This means Kodi will always need the contributions of users like you. How can you get involved? * **Coding:** Developers can help Kodi by **[fixing a bug](https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/issues)**, adding new features, making our technology smaller and faster and making development easier for others. Kodi's codebase consists mainly of C++ with small parts written in a variety of coding languages. Our add-ons mainly consist of python and XML. For more information, please have a look at our **[contributing guide](docs/CONTRIBUTING.md)**. * **Helping users:** Our support process relies on enthusiastic contributors like you to help others get the most out of Kodi. The #1 priority is always answering questions in our **[support forums](https://forum.kodi.tv/)**. Everyday new people discover Kodi, and everyday they are virtually guaranteed to have questions. * **Localization:** Translate **[Kodi](https://kodi.weblate.cloud/projects/kodi-core/kodi-main/)**, **[add-ons, skins etc.](https://kodi.weblate.cloud/)** into your native language. * **Add-ons:** **[Add-ons](https://kodi.tv/addons)** are what make Kodi the most extensible and customizable entertainment hub available. **[Get started building an add-on](https://kodi.tv/create-an-addon)**. * **Documentation:** Kodi's **[wiki pages](https://kodi.wiki/)** are the hub for information about Kodi and surrounding ecosystem. Help make our documentation better by writing new content or correcting existing material. **Not enough free time?** No problem! There are other ways to help Kodi. * **Spread the word:** Share Kodi with the world! Tell your friends and family about how Kodi creates an amazing entertainment experience. Stay up to date on the latest stories about Kodi reading our **[news](https://kodi.tv/blog)** section, follow us on **[Twitter](https://twitter.com/koditv)** and **[Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/XBMC/)**, or **star Kodi's repo** if you want to follow development. * **Donate:** We are always happy to receive a **[donation](https://kodi.tv/contribute/donate)**. Donations are typically used for travel to attend conferences, any necessary paperwork and legal fees, and the yearly XBMC Foundation Developers Conference, where a great deal of coding and planning for the following year occurs. Donations may also be used to purchase necessary hardware and licenses for developers, along with t-shirts, stickers, and other accessories for conferences. * **Buy Kodi merchandise:** Purchasing Kodi gear helps just as much as a donation, and you get something in return! Checkout our **[store](https://kodi.tv/store)** for Kodi branded gear. We regularly add new products so check back often. ## Building Kodi uses CMake as its building system but instructions are highly dependent on your operating system and target platform. Fortunately **[we've got you covered](docs/README.md)**. ## Acknowledgements Kodi couldn't exist without * All the **[contributors](https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/graphs/contributors)**. Big or small a change, it does make a difference. * All the developers that write the fantastic **software and libraries** that Kodi uses. We stand on the shoulders of giants. * Our **[fantastic community](https://forum.kodi.tv/)** for the never ending support, inspiration, feedback, and for keeping us on our toes when we screw up! * **[Our sponsors](https://kodi.tv/sponsors)**. Without them, keeping a huge project like this alive would be next to impossible. ## License Kodi is **[GPLv2 licensed](LICENSE.md)**. You may use, distribute and copy it under the license terms.

latestRelease.name: PS5MC 1.2
latestRelease.body:
### PS5MC 1.2

Kodi with the PS5 as a first-class platform, in two builds. Each comes as a
single-file `.exfat` image (recommended) or a `.zip` of the title folder:

| build | Kodi | title ID | home screen name | files |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Kodi 22 | 22.0 RC1 (Piers) | PPSA99420 | PS5MC (Kodi 22) | `PS5MC-1.2-kodi22-PPSA99420.exfat` or `.zip` |
| Kodi 21 | 21.3 (Omega) | PPSA99421 | PS5MC (Kodi 21) | `PS5MC-1.2-kodi21-PPSA99421.exfat` or `.zip` |

Pick **22** unless an add-on or skin you need only works on 21 (for example
skins that need Skin Shortcuts v2, such as Aeon Nox or Arctic Zephyr). The two
keep separate data and can be installed side by side.

### Changes since 1.1

**Video**
- **Three fixes listed in the 1.1 notes were missing from the 1.1 builds.**
  They are in 1.2:
  - 4K HEVC whose own stream headers differ from its container's (seen with
    x265 MKV encodes) was refused by the hardware decoder and fell back to
    software decoding, which is choppy at 4K. It now plays in hardware.
  - HEVC coded in tiles, which the PS5's decoder does not support, goes
    straight to software decoding instead of failing in hardware first.
  - Dolby Vision profile 7/8: the Dolby Vision layers are removed before the
    hardware decoder sees them, so playback starts without a failed first
    attempt.

**Kodi 21 build**
- **The skin now displays completely.** In 1.1 the Kodi 21 build showed black
  backgrounds and no icons, buttons or focus highlights: its images used a
  pixel format the PS5's graphics driver does not accept, and its skin
  textures were packed in Kodi 22's format, which Kodi 21 cannot read.

**Network**
- A network-share account that the server has **locked out** (too many wrong
  passwords) is now recognised as locked. Kodi no longer asks for the password
  again and retries, which kept the account locked; the log says so plainly.

**System**
- The Kodi 22 build is now called **PS5MC (Kodi 22)** on the home screen, and
  each build has its own boot splash.
- Each release carries its version number, so stores and updaters can offer it
  as an update.
- **`kodi-reset` and `kodi-uninstall` only touch the build they run in.** In
  1.1 they also erased the other build's library.
- Switch files (`kodi-debug`, `kodi-reset`, `kodi-uninstall`) also work from
  the build's data folder, `/data/ps5mc/kodi22` or `/data/ps5mc/kodi21`, so
  they work with the `.exfat` install too.
- Logs name the exact build, for bug reports.
- Under the hood: development diagnostics removed, per-frame video work
  streamlined.

**Releases**
- New: a single-file **`.exfat` image** per build.
- Each title folder ships a **`MANIFEST.sha256`** to check that a copy is
  complete.

### Install

ShadowMountPlus 1.7beta4 or later is needed for the `.exfat` image, and it
gives Kodi the `/data` folder where it keeps its library and settings.

- **`.exfat` (recommended), a single file.** Copy it to `/data/homebrew/`.
  One file can't partially transfer, so it avoids the dropped-file problems
  a folder copy over FTP can have.
- **`.zip`, the title folder.** Extract it into `/data/homebrew/` (creates
  `PPSA99420/` or `PPSA99421/`), replacing the whole folder. If you copy with
  FileZilla, set **Settings > Transfers > File exists action** to **Overwrite**,
  delete any old folder first, and check that the **Failed transfers** tab is
  empty. Run `sha256sum -c MANIFEST.sha256` in the folder to confirm the copy
  is complete.

Use one format per build: when switching between the folder and the image,
delete the other one first.

**Coming from 1.1:** same title IDs and data folders, so settings, library
and add-ons carry over. The Kodi 22 build also carries over from kodi-ps5 0.9.

### Known issues

- **Intermittent black screen on some 4K HDR films** (sound plays, the menus
  are not visible; one report is a letterboxed 3840x2076 film). Under
  investigation: if it happens, please send a log captured with `kodi-debug`
  on, and say whether the film is letterboxed.
- **Dolby Vision profile 5** files show the wrong colours (a green and purple
  tint): that profile has no HDR10 layer and needs per-frame Dolby Vision
  processing, not yet done. Profiles 7 and 8 play their HDR10 picture.
- **Kodi 21 build**: menus drawn over HDR video are not tone-matched to HDR
  (the same as Kodi 21 on any platform); HDR video itself is unaffected.
- **Binary add-ons** (`inputstream.adaptive`, Pillow, pycryptodome) do not
  load yet. Pure-Python add-ons work.
- **Kodi 22 skins**: Kodi 22 ships Skin Shortcuts v3. Skins that need v2 (Aeon
  Nox, Arctic Zephyr) install after downgrading Skin Shortcuts to v2, or use
  the Kodi 21 build.
- Add-on installs are slow; a dependency download can time out on the first
  attempt (retrying works).
- AV1 and tiled HEVC decode in software and can stutter at 4K.
- Without VRR, video plays at 59.94 Hz. Audio passthrough is unconfirmed.

Discussion and test reports: [Discord](https://discord.gg/YB58bUZrqu).

repos.name: elf-launcher
repos.description: Home screen and browser ELF payload launcher for a jailbroken PS5.
repos.readme: Home screen and browser ELF payload launcher for a jailbroken PS5. ![Elf Launcher home screen](docs/screenshots/home.png) ## Quick start 1. Jailbreak and start elfldr on port `9021`. 2. Send `elf-launcher.elf` from the [latest release](https://github.com/X-F1REBALL-X/elf-launcher/releases/latest). It installs the home screen tile. 3. Open the tile, or `http://:1000` from your phone or PC. Everything else is in the [guide](https://x-f1reball-x.github.io/elf-launcher/docs/guide/). ## Contents - [Features](#features) - [Gallery](#gallery) - [Requirements](#requirements) - [Installation](#installation) - [What's new in 2.0.5](#whats-new-in-205) - [Payload catalog and mirror](#payload-catalog-and-mirror) - [Companion apps](#companion-apps) - [Building from source](#building-from-source) - [License](#license) - [Credits](#credits) ## Features - Home screen tile and a launcher page served by the console on port `1000`. Open it from the tile, from the PS5 browser, or from a phone or PC on the same network. - Catalog of payloads in nine colored folders: Loaders, Jailbreak and HEN, Game Library, Mods and Saves, Files and Transfer, Network and Remote, Media and Audio, System, Dev Tools. Download once, load any time. - AutoPayload: choose payloads that load by themselves after every jailbreak. Several profiles, a start delay from 0 to 10 seconds, and a choice between opening the page or going back to the home screen. It runs once per jailbreak. - Quick launch: pin as many payloads as you like. Pinned payloads come first in every list. - Updates: saved payloads are checked against their latest releases, and you can update one or all. The launcher can update itself. - Console tools: file manager for the console, text viewer and editor with backups, running processes, event log with crash watch, and Restart, Rest mode and Power off. - Load file: send an ELF from your phone or PC, from a USB drive, or from a path on the console. - Backup and Restore of settings, profiles, pins and the payload list, to USB or `/data`. - Made for the DualSense: D-pad, Cross, Circle, Square and the Options button. - Seven themes and ten languages: English, Arabic, Spanish, French, German, Portuguese, Russian, Japanese, Chinese and Italian. - The page works on phones and tablets. ## Gallery Home with Quick launch, categories, power and AutoPayload: ![Home](docs/guide/img/home.png) All payloads: ![All payloads](docs/guide/img/all-payloads.png) Downloaded payloads: ![Downloaded](docs/guide/img/downloaded.png) AutoPayload with profiles: ![AutoPayload](docs/guide/img/autopayload.png) Pinned payloads: ![Pins](docs/guide/img/pins.png) Themes: ![Themes](docs/guide/img/themes.png) ## Requirements - A jailbroken PS5 with an ELF loader (elfldr) listening on port `9021`. - A PS5 browser, or a phone or PC on the same network, to open the page on port `1000`. - Optional: the Windows or Android companion app, see below. ## Installation 1. Jailbreak and start elfldr on port `9021`. 2. Send `elf-launcher.elf` from the [latest release](https://github.com/X-F1REBALL-X/elf-launcher/releases/latest) to port `9021` with any payload sender, or load it from WK Autoloader. It starts the page on port `1000` and installs the Elf Launcher tile under Games. 3. Open the tile, or `http://:1000` from your phone or PC. Updating: press Update in the launcher, or send the new `elf-launcher.elf` once. The new build takes over port `1000` from the old one, so no reboot is needed. More details are in the [guide](https://x-f1reball-x.github.io/elf-launcher/docs/guide/). ## What's new in 2.0.5 - Opens faster. It no longer goes online every time you open it. Payload and update checks only run when you press Update, or once every 6 hours. - `/version` now also reports the app version and the version of the copy saved on the console (`app` and `mirror_app`). Every version has its own notes on the [releases page](https://github.com/X-F1REBALL-X/elf-launcher/releases). ## Payload catalog and mirror The catalog is the file `payloads.json` in this repository. The launcher reads it from here. A GitHub Actions workflow (`catalog sync`) runs every day at 03:17 UTC and can also be started by hand. It does two things: - `tools/catalog_sync.py` checks the latest non-prerelease of each catalog payload that has a GitHub source. When the sha256 digest of the release file changed, it updates the URL, sha256, size and version in `payloads.json`. - `tools/mirror_sync.py` handles payloads that cannot be followed directly, for example because the author ships them only inside a ZIP or hosts them outside GitHub. It downloads the newest file from the author, checks the sha256 digest when one is published, uploads the ELF to the [`payload-mirror`](https://github.com/X-F1REBALL-X/elf-launcher/releases/tag/payload-mirror) release and updates `payloads.json`. The workflow only commits `payloads.json` when something changed. It never touches the `elf-launcher.elf` entry, which ships with the app release. Payloads in the catalog belong to their authors. Each entry links to the author's own release or to the mirror copy. ## Companion apps Both apps open the launcher page from your console in a native window. They are attached to the [latest release](https://github.com/X-F1REBALL-X/elf-launcher/releases/latest). - Windows (`clients/windows`): a window that hosts Microsoft Edge WebView2 and loads `http://:1000/`. It needs the WebView2 Runtime. When the console cannot be reached it offers the bundled page. - Android (`clients/android`): asks for the PS5 IP once, opens `http://:1000`, and falls back to the bundled page when the console cannot be reached. Long-press anywhere to change the IP. ## Building from source Only the pieces below have build files in this repository. The released files are the supported way to install. - Console payload (`host/hbinstall`): `make` with the PS5 Payload SDK. The Makefile needs `PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK` set and the elfldr sources at `/tmp/elfldr-src`. - Windows app (`clients/windows`): `build.sh` cross-compiles with Go and `go-winres`. It copies the current `index.html` into the app. - Android app (`clients/android`): `build.sh` runs Gradle `assembleRelease` and bundles the current `index.html` as the offline page. A signed release APK needs a keystore that is not part of the repository. ## License The `LICENSE` file contains the GNU General Public License, version 3. Payloads in the catalog are not part of this project. They keep their own authors and licenses. ## Credits - [elfldr](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/elfldr) by ps5-payload-dev. The repository includes the official `elfldr-ps5.elf` loader, and the console payload is built with elfldr sources. - [PS5 Payload SDK](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk) by ps5-payload-dev, used to build the console payload. - [go-webview2](https://github.com/jchv/go-webview2) by jchv, used by the Windows app. - Payload icons are the original icons of each project. repos.name: HearBridge-Browser
repos.description: Stream PS5 console audio to any browser on your local network
repos.readme:
**HearBridge family:** [PS5](https://github.com/X-F1REBALL-X/HearBridge-PS5) · [PS4](https://github.com/X-F1REBALL-X/HearBridge-PS4) · [Browser](https://github.com/X-F1REBALL-X/HearBridge-Browser) Listen to your PS5's audio on your phone, tablet or PC. No Bluetooth or extra hardware, just a browser (or the Android/Windows app) on the same Wi-Fi. HearBridge Browser is a small payload for a jailbroken PS5. It captures the console's audio output and serves it on your local network, together with a player page. Open the page, tap Play, and you hear the game. Full guide with setup, tips and FAQ: https://x-f1reball-x.github.io/HearBridge-Browser/ ## Features - **Works in any modern browser**: Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari, including iPhone and iPad. - **Android app**: finds your console on the network by itself, so you don't have to type the IP. - **Windows app**: a small portable `.exe` that opens the player in its own window. Nothing to install. - **Volume boost up to 500%**, with a soft limiter so it doesn't clip or distort. - **Sound modes**: Normal, Game, Music, Dynamic, Voice and Night. - **Automatic latency**: the Auto buffer learns the lowest delay your device can handle without dropouts. You can also pick Low, Stable or set it by hand. - **Record and export**: record what you hear and save it as WAV, FLAC, MP3 or Opus. - **Device detection**: the page checks what your browser supports, marks the recommended settings and greys out the ones that won't work. - Several people can listen at the same time, each with their own quality setting. ## Requirements - A jailbroken PS5 with an ELF loader listening on port **9021**. - A phone, tablet or computer on the same local network as the console. ## Install 1. Download `hearbridge-browser-1.0.0.elf` from the [Releases](../../releases) page. 2. Send it to the console's ELF loader on port 9021, for example: ``` nc -q0 9021 < hearbridge-browser-1.0.0.elf ``` or use any payload sender you already have. 3. Wait for the notification on the PS5, then on your device open: ``` http://:8096 ``` Or install `HearBridge-Browser-1.0.0.apk` on Android and pick your console from the list. ### Windows app Download `HearBridge-Browser-1.0.0-windows-x64.exe` from the [Releases](../../releases) page and run it. No install needed. - Needs Windows 10 or 11 (x64) with the WebView2 runtime. It's built into Windows 11 and current Windows 10, so you most likely have it already. - The exe isn't signed, so SmartScreen may warn you the first time. Click **More info**, then **Run anyway**. - If it can't reach the console, type your console's IP in the box and press Retry. It remembers the last IP that worked. The payload keeps running until you stop it or turn off the console. Sending it again replaces the running copy. ## Usage On a phone the page has four tabs. The mini player with the volume slider is always at the bottom. On a tablet or desktop everything is on one screen. **Play**: the big Play button, L/R level meters, and live stats (latency, bitrate, number of listeners). The volume slider goes from 0 to 500%; anything above 100% is boost. **Sound**: pick a sound mode, the stream quality (PCM 48k or 24k, or the lighter μ-law versions for weak Wi-Fi) and the buffer (Auto, Low, Stable or Manual). Your choices are saved per device. **Record**: start and stop a recording, listen to a preview, then export as WAV, FLAC, MP3 or Opus. You can keep the volume as you heard it, set a custom level, or normalize the file. **Info**: connection details, what your device supports, and links. If you prefer a media player, `http://:8096/live.wav` works in VLC or ffplay. ## FAQ **Do I need Bluetooth or any extra hardware?** No. Everything goes over your normal Wi-Fi or Ethernet network. **Does my audio go to the internet?** No. It only works on your local network. The console streams directly to your device and nothing leaves your network. The page doesn't load anything from outside either. **Why no Dolby or DTS?** Browsers can't decode Dolby or DTS streams, so the audio is sent as plain stereo. Set the PS5 audio output to stereo / linear PCM if you hear nothing. **I hear nothing on my iPhone.** Check the silent switch on the side of the phone and the volume buttons. HearBridge asks iOS to play even in silent mode, but some iOS versions still mute the browser when the switch is on. If iOS interrupts the audio (a call, Siri, etc.), tap "Tap to resume audio". **How do I stop it?** Send a POST to `http://:8096/api/stop`, or reboot the console. ## Screenshots
Play Sound Record Info
Tablet
## Building from source ### PS5 payload You need the [ps5-payload-sdk](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk) and Python 3. ``` export PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK=/path/to/ps5-payload-sdk ./build.sh # PS5 payload -> dist/hearbridge-browser-1.0.0.elf ./build.sh host # local test server for your PC -> build/hearbridge-browser-host ``` The PS5 build needs `PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK` set to your sdk folder, with the sdk's LLVM toolchain on your `PATH`. If it isn't set, `build.sh` stops with an error. The host build doesn't need the sdk. The player page (`web/index.html`) and the MP3 encoder are embedded into the ELF by `tools/embed.py`. The host build plays a test tone, so you can work on the page without a console. Use `HB_TEST=program ./build/hearbridge-browser-host` for something closer to real game audio. ### Android app Needs JDK 17+ and the Android SDK. ``` cd android ./gradlew assembleRelease ``` Release signing reads `android/keystore/keystore.properties`. Without it the APK is built unsigned. See [android/README.md](android/README.md). ### Windows app Needs Go 1.24+ and [go-winres](https://github.com/tc-hib/go-winres) (the script installs it if it's missing). Builds from Linux or Windows (Git Bash). ``` cd windows ./build.sh # -> windows/dist/HearBridge-Browser-1.0.0-windows-x64.exe ``` The icon and version info are generated into a `.syso` file during the build. See [windows/README.md](windows/README.md). ## Credits - The audio capture code comes from my earlier project [HearBridge PS5](https://github.com/X-F1REBALL-X/HearBridge-PS5), and the limiter in the page is a port of its `gain.c`. - MP3 export uses [lamejs](https://github.com/zhuker/lamejs) (LGPL-3.0, unmodified, in `vendor/lamejs`). ## Support If you like the project, you can buy me a coffee: - Ko-fi: https://ko-fi.com/XF1REBALLX - X: [X-F1REBALL-X](https://x.com/XxF1REBALLxX) ## License GPL-3.0-or-later. See [LICENSE](LICENSE) and [NOTICE](NOTICE).

repos.name: HearBridge-PS5
repos.description: Play PS5 game audio on any Bluetooth headphones or earbuds. Payload for jailbroken PS5
repos.readme:
**Bluetooth headphones for a jailbroken PS5: game and system audio, no dongle.** Developed by **X-F1REBALL-X** 🇺🇸 **English** · 🇸🇦 [العربية](README.ar.md)
**HearBridge family:** [PS5](https://github.com/X-F1REBALL-X/HearBridge-PS5) · [PS4](https://github.com/X-F1REBALL-X/HearBridge-PS4) · [Browser](https://github.com/X-F1REBALL-X/HearBridge-Browser) HearBridge PS5 is a payload (ELF) that plays your PS5's game and system audio on regular Bluetooth headphones, using the console's own Bluetooth or a USB stick. You control it from a web page served by the console.

## Highlights - One file for every PS5 (Marvell/NXP or MediaTek Bluetooth). - **USB Bluetooth adapters:** Realtek RTL8761BU (bundled firmware) and CSR8510, plus the console chip. - **Adapter picker** in Settings with instant switching; one pairing shared across adapters. - Single-screen UI for a 1080p TV: larger controls, Details panel for EQ, codecs and the log. - Game profiles, battery percent, night mode and one-tap headset switching. ## Install 1. Download **HearBridge-1.4.0.elf** from the [latest release](https://github.com/X-F1REBALL-X/HearBridge-PS5/releases/latest). 2. Send it to your ELF loader on port 9021. 3. Open **http://<console-ip>:8090** or the **HearBridge** tile, then pair your headphones in **Settings**. Everything else, from features to troubleshooting, is in the **[guide](https://x-f1reball-x.github.io/HearBridge-PS5/)**. ## USB Bluetooth adapter Plug in a USB stick and HearBridge can use it instead of the console chip. The stick is not shared with the DualSense, so the controller keeps connecting normally while audio streams. Supported sticks today: - **Realtek RTL8761BU** (UB500 / UB600, USB id `0BDA:B00C` / `0BDA:8771`) — firmware is **bundled in the ELF** and written to `/data/hearbridge/firmware/` on start. - **CSR8510** — works as a plain USB HCI adapter, no extra firmware. Under **Settings → Details → Bluetooth adapter** pick **Auto**, **Console chip**, or a listed stick (for example Realtek / CSR). The change is saved to `/data/hearbridge/adapter` and Bluetooth restarts right away. Pairing is shared across adapters, so you do not have to pair the same headset again after switching. You can still set the preference by hand with one line in `/data/hearbridge/adapter`: ```text auto # USB stick when present, else the console chip internal # always the console chip usb # always a USB adapter ugen1.2 # one specific ugen node ``` ### Realtek ROM-only adapters Some Realtek sticks start in ROM mode and need a patch before they can scan. HearBridge uploads it the same way Linux `btrtl` does. For RTL8761BU the files are bundled: ```text /data/hearbridge/firmware/rtl8761bu_fw.bin /data/hearbridge/firmware/rtl8761bu_config.bin ``` Other Realtek USB parts the loader knows still need their blobs from [`linux-firmware` `rtl_bt`](https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/firmware/linux-firmware.git/tree/rtl_bt) placed under `/data/hearbridge/firmware/`. Only RTL8761BU has been tested on hardware. ## Build ```sh export PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK=/opt/ps5-payload-sdk # ps5-payload-sdk v0.43 make ps5 # dist/HearBridge-.elf make test ``` ## Credits MediaTek scan-pause and USB pipe fix, plus HCI debug tool, by [ZiZc3](https://github.com/ZiZc3) ([#6](https://github.com/X-F1REBALL-X/HearBridge-PS5/pull/6)) USB Bluetooth adapter path and Realtek ROM uploader by [jamesst20](https://github.com/jamesst20) ([#45](https://github.com/X-F1REBALL-X/HearBridge-PS5/pull/45)) Bundled RTL8761BU firmware blobs are from the [linux-firmware](https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/firmware/linux-firmware.git/tree/rtl_bt) `rtl_bt` tree (Realtek Semiconductor Corporation). See [assets/firmware/LICENCE.rtlwifi_firmware.txt](assets/firmware/LICENCE.rtlwifi_firmware.txt). ## License GPL-3.0-or-later. See [LICENSE](LICENSE) and [NOTICE](NOTICE). [Support the project on Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/xf1reballx). The project stays free and open source.

repos.readme: Turns the PS5 Store tile into WK Autoloader: open the tile, start the jailbreak, and Elf Launcher opens when it finishes. ## Quick start 1. Send [`WK_Autoloader_Store_V1.2.0.elf`](https://github.com/X-F1REBALL-X/wk-autoloader/releases/download/v1.2.0/WK_Autoloader_Store_V1.2.0.elf) to elfldr on port `9021`. 2. Wait for the install to finish, then reboot. 3. Open the **Store** tile and press **Start Jailbreak**. ## Contents - [Features](#features) - [Requirements](#requirements) - [Installation](#installation) - [Restore the PlayStation Store tile](#restore-the-playstation-store-tile) - [What's new in 1.2.0](#whats-new-in-120) - [Known issues](#known-issues) - [Building from source](#building-from-source) - [License](#license) - [Credits](#credits) ## Features - Replaces the Store tile on the home screen with WK Autoloader. - Runs the Relapse jailbreak from the tile, then opens Elf Launcher by itself. - Works offline after install. Send the ELF again only to reinstall or update. - Each install clears the old WebKit cache first, so the cache is always filled from scratch. - A separate Restore ELF puts the original PlayStation Store tile back. ## Requirements - PS5 firmware 7.00–13.60 (Relapse). - elfldr listening on port `9021`. - A way to send an ELF to elfldr, for example after an earlier jailbreak. ## Installation 1. Send [`WK_Autoloader_Store_V1.2.0.elf`](https://github.com/X-F1REBALL-X/wk-autoloader/releases/download/v1.2.0/WK_Autoloader_Store_V1.2.0.elf) to elfldr on port `9021`. 2. Wait until the install finishes, then reboot the console. 3. Open the **Store** tile on the home screen. 4. Press **Start Jailbreak**. After Relapse completes, Elf Launcher opens automatically. ## Restore the PlayStation Store tile Send [`WK_Autoloader_Store_Restore_V1.2.0.elf`](https://github.com/X-F1REBALL-X/wk-autoloader/releases/download/v1.2.0/WK_Autoloader_Store_Restore_V1.2.0.elf) to elfldr on port `9021`, then reboot. This also clears the WK cache. ## What's new in 1.2.0 Changes since 1.1.4. - Install keeps the existing Store AppCache. No more automatic wipe. - A backup is made before any cache clear (/data/wkal/appcache_backup/). - Store Restore clears only the Store AppCache origin, nothing else. - The installer waits for "Offline cache complete" before it finishes. - When the firmware is unknown, the full manifest is used. - Faster jailbreak: about 3.3s down to about 2.9s (quicker elfldr poll and faster ELF copy). - Per-stage timing in ms, shown in the log and in Recent. All versions are on the [releases page](https://github.com/X-F1REBALL-X/wk-autoloader/releases). ## Known issues The first jailbreak right after installing the Store (or after a clean install or cache wipe) can occasionally freeze the console or cause a kernel panic. On that first run WebKit is still writing the Store's offline AppCache to disk while the exploit runs, and the extra disk and memory activity during its timing-sensitive phase can make it fail. Once the cache is fully written, later jailbreaks load from cache and are stable. If it freezes, hold the power button to restart the console and run the jailbreak again; it usually works from the second run. To lower the risk, wait until the Store install has fully finished before your first jailbreak; the freeze is most likely while the AppCache is still being written right after install or after a cache wipe. ## Building from source Needs the [PS5 payload SDK](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk) with libmicrohttpd. ```bash make store SDK=/path/to/ps5-payload-sdk BUILD_TYPE=stable make restore SDK=/path/to/ps5-payload-sdk ``` Outputs `WK_Autoloader_Store_V1.2.0.elf` and `WK_Autoloader_Store_Restore_V1.2.0.elf`. ## License [GNU GPL v3](LICENSE). ## Credits - Relapse (PS5 WebKit / kernel chain, vendored under `frontend/autoloader/relapse/`) - [ps5-elfldr](https://github.com/itsPLK/ps5-elfldr) by itsPLK - [elf-launcher](https://github.com/X-F1REBALL-X/elf-launcher) - SQLite (Store tile database remap) Developed by X-F1REBALL-X.

repos.name: PS5-TabShifter
repos.description: Standalone PS5 on-console payload to move apps between Games/Media tabs and hide offline PSN bloatware (Universal FW 5.00 – 13.60)
repos.readme:
# PS5 TabShifter (Universal FW 5.00 – 13.60)

A lightweight on-console utility and web interface for jailbroken PlayStation 5 consoles (FW 5.00 through 13.60) that gives you complete control over your PS5 Home Screen layout.

---

### Features

* **Move Apps Between Games and Media:** Keep emulators, homebrew, and utilities in the Media tab (or vice versa). Preserves native PS4 (CUSA), PS5 (PPSA), and FPKG entitlements alongside category types (0, 61440, 65536) so games never get locked.
* **Universal Firmware Engine:** Dual-schema database engine supporting both legacy field_list arrays (FW 5.00–10.xx) and modern flat JSON (FW 11.00–13.60). Updates all database layers simultaneously with proper Prospero concept bitmasks (1162 for Games, 2236 for Media).
* **Multi-User Profile Sync:** Automatically detects and updates all local user profiles on the console, keeping home screen arrangements uniform across all accounts.
* **Persistent Rest Mode Bloatware Cleaner:** Hides stock PSN bloatware (PlayStation Store, PS Plus, Remote Play, Share Play, Live TV) and stops them from returning after waking from Rest Mode or cold reboots.
* **Pin Icons to Home Screen:** Pin or unpin any app to lock your favorite titles onto the primary home bar so they never get pushed into the Game Library.
* **No-Scroll-Jump Web UI:** Viewport stays locked in place while queueing changes. Includes instant search, quick filter pills (All, Games, Media, Hidden, PS5, PS4, Homebrew), and a 1-click **Smart Tidy** button.
* **One-Click Padlock Repair:** Built-in recovery tool to instantly repair concept bitmasks across your entire library if another tool caused padlock icons on your games.
* **In-App Self-Updater:** Automatically checks GitHub Releases for new updates, displays release notes, and updates the payload directly on the console.
* **100% On-Console Operation:** Automatically installs the TabShifter ("TS") launcher tile directly onto your Media tab. Startup checks prevent black-screen shell reloads when re-launching.

---

### Why TabShifter?

On modern PS5 firmwares, Sony splits dashboard data across two synchronized databases:

* `/system_data/priv/mms/appinfo.db`
* `/system_data/priv/mms/app.db`

Modifying only one database causes the system shell to restore stale metadata from cache, corrupt concept bitmasks (causing game padlocks), or revert changes after entering Rest Mode. 

TabShifter updates all database layers simultaneously, applies the correct concept bitmasks (1162 / 2236), and safely reloads SceShellUI in ~1.5 seconds without causing database rebuild prompts.

---

### Installation & Usage

1. Download `TabShifter.elf` from the Latest Release.
2. Place `TabShifter.elf` into `/data/pldmgr/payloads/` on your PS5 (or send it via your favorite payload loader).
3. Run the payload. On first launch, it creates safety database backups and adds the **TabShifter ("TS")** tile to your Media tab.
4. Launch TabShifter from your **Media** tab (or open `http://<PS5_IP>:9095/` in any browser on your network).
5. Queue your changes, then click **Apply & Reload PS5 UI** at the top.

---

### Database Recovery & Safety

TabShifter creates safety backups on first initialization:

* `/system_data/priv/mms/app.db.tabshifter.bak`
* `/system_data/priv/mms/appinfo.db.tabshifter.bak`

If you ever need to restore your layout:

* **Fix Padlocks:** Click the orange **Fix Padlocks** button in the Web UI to restore concept bitmasks if game icons are locked.
* **Full Restore:** Click **Restore DB Backup** in the Web UI to revert back to your untouched original databases.

---

### Credits & Acknowledgments

* **ps5-payload-dev** for the ps5-payload-sdk toolchain.
* **itsPLK** for ps5-payload-manager and libSceAppInstUtil references.
* **John Törnblom** for ftpsrv and packaging patterns.

latestRelease.body:
**What’s New in v1.3.0**

**Universal Firmware Engine (FW 5.00 – 13.60):** Sony changed how dashboard JSON is stored between earlier firmwares and 11.40+. TabShifter now dynamically handles both legacy field_list arrays (FW 5.00–10.xx) and modern flat JSON (FW 11.00–13.60) across both app.db and appinfo.db.

**Permanent Rest Mode Bloatware Suppression:** Previously, hiding apps like PlayStation Store or PS Plus would revert after waking the console or cold booting. v1.3.0 sets native daemon flags (pushed: false), clears emsPushedFlag, and purges system group entries so hidden bloatware stays gone.

**Padlock Bug Resolved + One-Click "Fix Padlocks" Tool:** Padlocks happen when concept metadata is modified with standard app display IDs instead of Sony's native concept bitmasks (1162 for Games, 2236 for Media). v1.3.0 enforces proper bitmasks across all tables and includes an orange "Fix Padlocks" button in the dashboard to instantly restore entitlements across your entire library if another tool locked your games.

**Multi-User Profile Sync:** TabShifter now scans all profile tables (tbl_iconinfo_* / tbl_concepticoninfo_*), ensuring your customized layout and hidden tiles stay identical across every account on the console.

**Web UI Quality-of-Life Upgrades:**

1. No Viewport Jumping: Editing, pinning, or hiding titles near the bottom no longer scrolls the page back to the top.

2. Live Search & Filter Pills: Quickly filter your dashboard by All, Games, Media, Hidden, PS5, PS4, or Homebrew.

3. 1-Click "Smart Tidy": Automatically sweeps all installed homebrew and emulators to the Media tab and hides stock PSN bloatware in a single tap.
4. In-App Self-Updater: Checks GitHub Releases directly, previews the changelog, and updates the payload without manual FTP.

Zero Black-Screen Latency: Starting the payload no longer restarts SceShellUI if the TabShifter ("TS") launcher tile is already present on your Media tab, making re-runs instant.

repos.name: PS5_Audiobook_Reader
repos.description: The AEbook Reader bookshelf on PS5
repos.readme:
# Audiobook Reader for PS5

[![Build PS5 Audiobook Reader](https://github.com/Yahballon/PS5_Audiobook_Reader/actions/workflows/build.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Yahballon/PS5_Audiobook_Reader/actions/workflows/build.yml)

A native, controller-first M4B audiobook player by YAHBALLON, inspired by the bookshelf experience of the [PS5 Ebook Reader](https://github.com/Yahballon/PS5_Ebook_Reader). This application is separate from the Ebook Reader.

## HD PS5 Icon

![Audiobook Reader HD neon icon](sce_sys/icon0.png)

## Features

- **Live chapter tracking:** The Now Playing chapter number and title follow the decoded playback position automatically, including natural chapter changes, forward/backward seeks, and resume. The chapter list marks the currently playing chapter without overriding manual selection while browsing.
- **Library selection fix:** Pressing Cross opens the currently highlighted audiobook, not the first title when the shelf contains multiple items.


- **Local Books permission fix:** If the PS5 app cannot enumerate `/data/AudioBookReader/Books` (errno 1 / EPERM), the helper scans the folder and transfers selected books to the app's playable cache; local originals remain unchanged.
- Local helper protocol uses `LISTLOCAL` and `FETCHLOCAL` on the dedicated port 9179 through the existing elfldr on port 9021.
- **Cover fallback chain:** FFmpeg M4B attached-picture stream, direct iTunes `covr` MP4 atom parsing, then adjacent `cover.jpg`, `folder.jpg`, `front.jpg`, `cover.png`, or `<audiobook-name>.jpg/.jpeg/.png`.
- Companion artwork works on USB `ABooks` and local `Books`, without transferring the entire M4B first.
- New diagnostics: `LOCAL_HELPER_BEGIN`, `LOCAL_HELPER_DONE`, `LOCAL_HELPER_ERROR`, `COVER_COMPANION` and `COVER_MISSING`.



- M4B embedded album art (iTunes/MP4 covr as JPEG or PNG) decoded with native FFmpeg + stb_image, shown on the aluminum bookshelf and player.
- Persistent artwork cache under `/data/AudioBookReader/Covers/`; USB covers appear after the book is first cached or opened, then persist across restarts.
- Extended local `.m4b` scanning (recursive up to six levels) of `/data/AudioBookReader/Books/` and loose files in `/data/AudioBookReader/` without scanning Cache/Covers.
- `SCAN_LOCAL_DETAIL` diagnostics in `audiobook-reader.log`: scanned directory, file count, accepted M4B count, skipped small files, sample entry and errors.


- USB ABooks folder scanned via a dedicated read-only `abookscan.elf` helper launched through active `elfldr` on `127.0.0.1:9021` (USB helper port `9179`).
- Async transfer to `/data/AudioBookReader/Cache/` with progress percentage, cancellation, interrupted-transfer retry, and safe file-size validation.
- Application diagnostics at `/data/AudioBookReader/audiobook-reader.log`; persistent listening state at `/data/AudioBookReader/progress.tsv`.

- Brushed aluminum bookshelf, stainless steel rails and cyan focus highlights.
- Scans M4B audiobooks recursively (up to six levels deep) from the two dedicated sources: local `Books` and USB `ABooks`.
- Native FFmpeg AAC decoder with SDL2 audio output.
- Play/pause, skip ±15/30 seconds, seek ±60 seconds, chapter navigation (embedded MP4 chapters).
- Favorites, All and In Progress views, grid/list view and resume playback.
- Saves playback positions and favorite flags in `/data/AudioBookReader/progress.tsv` with atomic rename.
- Clear exit confirmation; saves when returning to library and periodically while playing.

## Controller

| Button | Library | Playback |
| --- | --- | --- |
| D-Pad | Navigate | Left −15s / Right +30s |
| Cross | Play selected book | Play / Pause |
| Circle | Exit prompt | Back to library |
| Triangle | — | Toggle chapters |
| Square | Favorite | Jump to highlighted chapter |
| L1 / R1 | Filters | Previous / Next chapter |
| L2 / R2 | — / Grid-list switch | −60s / +60s |
| Options | Rescan library | — |

## Install

Download `PPSA99784.zip` from [Releases](https://github.com/Yahballon/PS5_Audiobook_Reader/releases/tag/v0.2.5) after a successful CI release. Extract the `PPSA99784` folder to `/data/homebrew/`, register it with your supported loader, and copy DRM-free `.m4b` files into `/mnt/usb0/ABooks/` on USB or `/data/AudioBookReader/Books/` locally (optional: `/download0/ABooks/`).

USB books are enumerated by the included `abookscan.elf` helper and need an already-running elfldr on TCP port 9021. The app transfers selected USB M4B files to `/data/AudioBookReader/Cache` before decoding; originals on USB remain untouched. If the helper cannot start, local books remain usable and the app shows its USB status. Encrypted FairPlay M4B audiobooks cannot be decoded. Embedded chapters require compatible MP4 chapter metadata. Audio output requires the FFmpeg/SDL2 libraries available in the PS5-DevBridge toolchain.

## Build

Run `.github/workflows/build.yml` via GitHub Actions; uses `PS5-DevBridge/templates/simple-calc`, native `ps5-homebrew-ui` OpenGL renderer, FFmpeg and SDL2 PacBrew dependencies. The workflow packages and validates executable, assets, metadata and release archive. Host smoke tests cover library scanning and progress persistence.

**Version:** v0.2.5  
**Title ID:** PPSA99784  
**Content ID:** UP9000-PPSA99784_00-AUDIOBOOKREADER1

License: GPL-3.0-or-later. Code derived from the GPL-compatible PS5 homebrew UI and development boilerplate.

repos.readme:
# 📚 PS5 Ebook Reader ### Native PS5 Homebrew — by YAHBALLON **EPUB · PDF · CBR · CBZ** · DualSense navigation · USB & internal storage · Comics & Covers [![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-v0.2.6-daa04c)](https://github.com/Yahballon/PS5_Ebook_Reader/releases/tag/ebook-reader-v0.2.6) [![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-PlayStation%205%20Homebrew-5c3418)](#requirements) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-GPL--3.0-blue)](LICENSE) [**⬇️ Download latest PS5 ZIP**](https://github.com/Yahballon/PS5_Ebook_Reader/releases/download/ebook-reader-v0.2.6/PPSA99741.zip) · [**Releases**](https://github.com/Yahballon/PS5_Ebook_Reader/releases) · [**Report an issue**](https://github.com/Yahballon/PS5_Ebook_Reader/issues) *The Ebook Reader bookshelf on PS5 (v0.2.6). Screenshot supplied by the developer.*
## Overview **PS5 Ebook Reader** is a native C/C++ homebrew application for reading books and image-based comics on a compatible homebrew-enabled PlayStation 5. It uses a TV-friendly 1920 × 1080 console interface, real OpenGL rendering and full DualSense navigation. No web browser or separate PC-based reader is needed to read books already accessible to the application. | Format | Support | Notes | | :--- | :---: | :--- | | **EPUB** | ✅ | EPUB package parsing, readable text, inline images, cover artwork, adjustable single/double-page layout | | **PDF** | ⚠️ | Extractable text preview; **not** a full graphical PDF renderer | | **CBR** | ✅ | Comic images inside supported RAR4/RAR5 archives; image page navigation & zoom | | **CBZ** | ✅ | Comic images in ZIP archives; cover from an image page & full-screen reading | ## Features - **Visual bookshelf** with genre/category filters: All, Comics, Fiction, Novels and Favorites. - **Real cover art** for EPUB and supported comics, with asynchronous extraction and saved thumbnail cache. - **Native comic reader** with JPEG/PNG/GIF image decoding where supported. - **Single / double-page toggle** for EPUB/PDF text content, with full-width pages. - **Zoom and pan** using the DualSense; changing pages resets scrolling to the beginning of the new page. - **Reading progress** remembered across app sessions; favorites and saved library state. - **USB book discovery** including nested folders, using an existing compatible `elfldr` on port **9021** and a bundled read-only helper on local port **9176**. - **Progress bars** with actual bytes and percentages while a book is copied from USB; background loading keeps the UI responsive. - **Resumable large-file transfers** and bounded automatic cleanup of disposable cache files. - **Exit confirmation**: Circle in My Library displays Yes / No, preventing accidental exits. - **Debug logging** and user-owned folders in `/data/EbookReader/`. ## Controls ### My Library | DualSense button | Action | | :--- | :--- | | **D-Pad** | Select a book | | **✕ Cross** | Open selected book | | **◯ Circle** | Show Exit Ebook Reader? confirmation | | **□ Square** | Toggle Favorite | | **△ Triangle** | Open Storage / Import Books | | **L1 / R1** | Previous / next collection | | **R2** | Toggle bookshelf / list view | | **OPTIONS** | Rescan library and USB catalog | | **L3** | Request delete of an imported book (requires confirmation) | ### Reading a book or comic | DualSense button | Action | | :--- | :--- | | **L1 / R1** | Previous / next page | | **✕ Cross** | Next page | | **D-Pad Left / Right** | Turn pages at default zoom; pan when zoomed | | **D-Pad Up / Down** | Pan when zoomed | | **L2 / R2** | Zoom out / in (up to 400%) | | **□ Square** | Single / double-page toggle in EPUB/PDF; jump to last page in comics | | **△ Triangle** | Jump to first page | | **L3 / OPTIONS** | Reset zoom and pan | | **◯ Circle** | Return to library | ### Storage / import and Exit dialog | Screen | Button | Action | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Storage** | D-Pad Up / Down | Select available local import | | **Storage** | ✕ Cross | Import selected local file | | **Storage** | △ Triangle | Refresh storage catalog | | **Storage** | ◯ Circle | Back to My Library | | **Exit prompt** | ✕ Cross | **Yes** — save state and close | | **Exit prompt** | ◯ Circle | **No** — return to library | | **Loading** | ◯ Circle | Request cancellation of an ongoing USB transfer | ## Requirements - A **homebrew-capable PS5** with a compatible loader (e.g. TESTBUILD / ShadowMount setup). - An installation method capable of deploying and registering a homebrew title folder. **Title ID: `PPSA99741`**. - For USB scanning, an already-running compatible **ELF loader at port 9021**. The bundled `bookscan.elf` helper is launched by the app and exposes localhost port 9176. USB storage is optional if you use internal storage. - Sufficient writable storage for caching complete CBR/CBZ archives when importing from USB. This app is **not supported on an unmodified retail PS5**. ## Installation 1. Download **[PPSA99741.zip](https://github.com/Yahballon/PS5_Ebook_Reader/releases/download/ebook-reader-v0.2.6/PPSA99741.zip)** from the latest verified GitHub Release. 2. Extract the ZIP, keeping the top-level `PPSA99741` folder intact. 3. Copy the complete folder into `/data/homebrew/` on the PS5, resulting in `/data/homebrew/PPSA99741/eboot.bin`, `sce_module/`, `sce_sys/`, assets and `bookscan.elf`. 4. Register/launch the homebrew through your compatible PS5 loader, or install through your TESTBUILDS workflow if configured. 5. Add books using one of the locations below and restart or press **OPTIONS** to rescan. **Keep the full ZIP contents; an `eboot.bin` alone is not a complete installation.** Updating over an existing version should preserve book folders and reading progress. ## Where to put books | Purpose | Location | | :--- | :--- | | Internal books (recommended) | `/data/EbookReader/Books/` | | USB drive books | `/mnt/usb0/Books/` | | Large USB book cache (automatic) | `/data/EbookReader/Cache/` | | Saved comic cover thumbnails | `/data/EbookReader/Covers/` | | Diagnostic log | `/data/EbookReader/ebook-reader.log` | EPUB, PDF, CBR and CBZ files can be placed in the Books folder and nested subdirectories. USB books are catalogued through the helper and copied into a cache as necessary. **Do not put the only copy of your books in the cache**: its contents are intentionally disposable. ## Building from source The source and host regression tests are included in [`homebrew/ebook-reader/`](homebrew/ebook-reader/). The dedicated workflow [`build-ebook-reader.yml`](.github/workflows/build-ebook-reader.yml) runs unit/integration tests, retrieves the pinned PS5 development template and dependencies, builds `bookscan.elf` plus the native `eboot.bin`, validates the package, and publishes a versioned ZIP for eligible main-branch builds. The native application uses [PS5-DevBridge](https://github.com/Yahballon/PS5-DevBridge), the [ps5-homebrew-ui framework](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-homebrew-ui), zlib, libarchive and an stb_image decoder. Toolchain/bootstrap dependencies are fetched during CI. See the workflow for the exact build commands and pinned versions. The published **v0.2.6** package is the same verified ZIP as the original application release at [tmp_lap](https://github.com/Yahballon/tmp_lap/releases/tag/ebook-reader-v0.2.6); its SHA-256 is `25c6158761490fcb632379a1dd1808a9e0b3b9df5a680c4384af9e3010446aba`. ## Limitations / known issues - PDF support is for extractable text and does not reproduce every graphic element or scanned page. - Password-protected and multipart RARs are unsupported; some unusual comic page encodings may not display. - The first uncached USB comic cover can require downloading the complete archive and adequate cache space. - A successful GitHub Actions build is **not** a substitute for physical-console testing; compatibility depends on firmware, homebrew runtime and loader. - Only use books you have the right to copy/read. This project does not ship third-party commercial books. ## Troubleshooting If a book does not open, run **OPTIONS** to rescan, check your paths and verify that `elfldr` is available for USB sources. For failures, open `/data/EbookReader/ebook-reader.log` and include its last lines when submitting an issue. `USB_FETCH_OK` means the archive was copied successfully; `OPEN_OK` means it was parsed successfully. `No space left on device` means the cache filesystem is full. ## Credits & license Created by **YAHBALLON**. Developed using homebrew community tooling and open-source components under their respective licenses. **Project source: GPL-3.0** — see [LICENSE](LICENSE). This is an independent homebrew project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Sony Interactive Entertainment.

repos.readme:
PS5CLEAN

A little fan-powered fun for your PS5.
By YAHBALLON · v1.0.0.6 · (AI-assisted)

## What is PS5CLEAN? PS5CLEAN is a native PS5 homebrew **fun app** with a sci-fi dashboard and timed fan pulses. The idea is simple: let the fan alternate between high and low cooling, in the hope that the changing airflow might loosen a little dust inside the console. **That is the hope, not a proven cleaning effect.** PS5CLEAN is an experimental project, not a replacement for physical cleaning or maintenance. ## Dashboard ![PS5CLEAN dashboard](screenshots/dashboard.png) *Rendered from the actual app UI. This preview is not connected to a console, so live readings are blank.* ## Features - Blue glass dashboard with a rotating fan and an original center emblem. - Four animated cyan light segments around the fan. - Ten-minute cycle by default, with selectable duration and pulse interval. - Live CPU temperature, measured fan duty and a scrolling duty graph. - Start / Stop controls and automatic restoration of the original cooling target. - Direct temperature-target control with kstuff; etaHEN is not required. ## How the pulses work Press **Start Cleaning** to begin. The first half of each pulse interval requests high cooling using a **20 C** temperature target. The second half requests low cooling using a **60 C** target. The cycle repeats until the selected duration ends or you press Stop. The displayed request range is **100% to 0%**, but these are control requests: the console's automatic fan regulation determines the actual speed. **A physically stopped fan is not guaranteed.** The dashboard displays measured duty separately. The app does not stop simply because measured duty takes longer to reach maximum. Stop, completion, loss of app heartbeat, owner exit, device errors or invalid/over-limit temperature restore the original temperature target. Other fan-control apps should be closed while PS5CLEAN is running. ## Requirements - A jailbroken PS5 with kstuff and access to the fan device. - A loader capable of mounting native homebrew folders, such as ShadowMount Plus. - A localhost ELF loader on **port 9021** to start the included `fan-service.elf`, or manual loading of that service. Fan control has been tested on **firmware 5.10**. Compatibility with every firmware or console model is not established. ## Installation 1. Download the app ZIP from the release assets. 2. Extract the complete **PPSA99338** folder into your homebrew directory, for example `/mnt/usb0/homebrew/PPSA99338`. 3. Register or mount it through your loader, then launch PS5CLEAN. 4. Select your duration and pulse interval in Settings, then press Start Cleaning. **Title ID:** `PPSA99338` · **Content version:** `01.000.006` ## Controls | Button | Action | | --- | --- | | L1 / R1 | Switch Cleaning, Settings and About | | Left / Right | Select Start or Stop; change a selected setting | | Up / Down | Select a settings row | | X | Activate the selected button or setting | | Circle | Return to Cleaning, stop an active cycle, or exit while idle | | Options | Stop and exit | ## Build from source Build on Linux or WSL with Clang and the dependencies required by the included build scripts. The scripts fetch pinned public SDK dependencies; generated files are kept in `build/`, `dist/` and `.deps/`. ```sh make USE_CCACHE=0 BUILD_JOBS=4 app ``` Outputs: - `dist/PPSA99338/` - installable app folder. - `dist/PPSA99338.zip` - packaged app. The fan helper listens only on localhost port **7341** and checks the calling app title. Settings are stored in `/data/PS5CLEAN/settings.ini`. ## Credits and license - **YAHBALLON** - PS5CLEAN project. - [BlackBearReloaded / ps5-homebrew-ui](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-homebrew-ui) - UI renderer and native boilerplate. - [drakmor / fan_target](https://github.com/drakmor/fan_target) - fan interface reference. - Inter and Montserrat font licenses are included under `assets/fonts/`. - Artwork and development were AI-assisted; artwork notes are included in the source. Distributed under **GPL-3.0**. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).
