repos.readme:
# GBAXY — Game Boy Advance for PS5

**Game Boy Advance games on PS5 with a native neon 3D CoverFlow.** **v2.3.0 — by YAHBALLON** · **App ID: PPSA99209** PS5GBA is a native PS5 homebrew Game Boy Advance emulator using **mGBA 0.10.5**. It reuses the working PS5SNES frontend while keeping the PS5SX2 shelf, animated game cases, cover glow, reflections, menu sounds and settings panel. The integration and upstream components retain their respective licenses. **Release status:** the v2.1 ROM discovery fix requires a console retest. This repository contains source; installable application ZIPs must be built and attached separately to a GitHub release. See [RELEASE_NOTES.md](RELEASE_NOTES.md) and [TESTING.md](TESTING.md). ## GBAXY v2.3.0 — 7z archives, smarter cover matching, local artwork and stability - **New ROM format:** Safe loading of LZMA/LZMA2 7z archives containing exactly one GBA game, alongside GBA and ZIP. - **Better online cover matching:** Libretro index, scene-dump numbers and region tags, Pokémon variants and conservative fuzzy title matching. - **Custom covers beside ROMs:** Exact same-basename PNG/JPG/JPEG next to GBA/ZIP/7z takes priority over cached and downloaded covers; double-dot spelling is *not* accepted. - **Refresh art with Triangle:** Retry local covers, including images uploaded after the app started, and then retry online only if no local match is found. - **Settings stability:** Guard the first per-game settings save and synchronize the game-to-menu transition. - **Safe exit:** The main-menu Circle → Cross confirmation now asks the PS5 shell to close the title with `sceSystemServiceLoadExec("exit", nullptr)` instead of libc `exit(0)`, which caused **SIGSYS (signal 12)** on PS5. - **CRT fallback:** Also intercepts unexpected normal `main()` returns to prevent a second SIGSYS crash. - **No loss of data:** Title ID `PPSA99209`, game folders, cover cache, saves and themes are unchanged. - **Verification:** Builds and host tests validate the corrected exit code; hardware exit behavior must be retested on a PS5. ## GBAXY v2.2.0 — Previous release **GBA cover download:** Local artwork and the existing cache take priority. Online lookup now tries the [Libretro GBA Named Boxarts index](https://thumbnails.libretro.com/Nintendo%20-%20Game%20Boy%20Advance/Named_Boxarts/) and the upstream Libretro GitHub mirror, with up to three No-Intro region/name variations per game. Missing thumbnails are fetched on demand and cached locally. - **GBAXY identity** in the PS5 home screen, CoverFlow and animated startup screen. - **Adaptive 3D game cases**: genuine GBA portrait box art stays portrait; square, custom and landscape covers retain their real proportions, with uncropped artwork and reflections. - **Five exclusive themes**, all configurable under Settings → Appearance → Theme: Advance Wave (electric blue/teal), Pixel Mint (lime/green), Lava Pulse (orange/red), Silver Core (silver/white) and Cosmic Violet (purple/magenta). - **Advance Current**: original animated loading screen with five flowing pixel ribbons, a moving scanlight, handheld-inspired center emblem and real GBA ROM scan counts. - **Exit confirmation**: press ○ from the game library, then × to exit or ○ to cancel; does not trigger during gameplay. - All existing mGBA emulator modes, 4K graphics, saves, controls, NFS, ROM paths and cached Libretro GBA artwork are retained. - **Title ID PPSA99209 is unchanged**, as is the existing data folder `/data/PS5GBA/`. ## Features A native Vulkan interface with the supplied blue Game Boy Advance launcher logo. - Play **`.gba` ROMs** from internal storage, USB or an **NFSv3 share**. - Load ZIP archives containing **one GBA ROM**, decompressed directly into RAM. - Native GBA emulation at **240 × 160**, approximately **59.7275 FPS**. - Display output up to **3840 × 2160**, with 1080p selection and display-dependent fallback. - **ORIGINAL**, **4K HD SMOOTH** and **4K ENHANCED** graphics modes. - Aspect-ratio, stretch and integer scaling, plus adjustable sharpness, contrast and color boost. - Automatic Libretro GBA box-art downloads, ROM-adjacent local cover priority and **Triangle / R2 cover retry**. - Cached game library, visible loading progress, library reset/rescan and recent-first ordering. - Battery-backed saves and **one save-state slot per ROM**. - Configurable GBA buttons and save/load/menu shortcuts, globally or per game. - Fast forward with muted game audio. - Controller-operated NFS URL keyboard and a QR web settings page. - Bounded cover streaming for large libraries, with downloaded covers cached on disk. - Built-in BIOS fallback; an optional user-provided GBA BIOS is supported. ## Install 1. Download the **application ZIP** from the release assets and extract it. 2. Copy the complete **PPSA99209** folder to: ~~~text /data/homebrew/PPSA99209/ ~~~ 3. Launch it with your compatible PS5 homebrew launcher. Keep every packaged file, including `sce_module/libc.prx`, `lapy.elf`, `lapy-manifest.json` and `sce_sys/icon0.png`. Games, saves and settings live separately in `/data/PS5GBA/`. For an update, replace the application files and restart the app. Preserve the data folder. Refresh the launcher if it still shows the old icon. The filesystem helper is restricted to this app's title ID. If filesystem access is unavailable, the helper may require the local ELF loader on port **9021**. A normal retail PS5 cannot run this homebrew app. ## Add games **Supported ROM formats:** `.gba` (case-insensitive), single-GBA-ROM `.zip`, and (experimental on the 7z feature branch) single-GBA-ROM `.7z` archives. SNES extensions such as `.sfc` and `.smc` are not GBA ROMs. A source-code ZIP downloaded from GitHub is not an installable PS5 build. If games are not listed, check `/data/PS5GBA/logs/boot.log` for `[library]` scan errors. Restart after adding ROMs or request **Rescan library** in All games settings and restart. ### Internal storage ~~~text /data/PS5GBA/games/ ~~~ These folders are also supported: ~~~text /data/PS5GBA/roms/ /data/homebrew/PS5GBA/games/ /data/homebrew/PS5GBA/roms/ /data/homebrew/PPSA99209/games/ /data/homebrew/PPSA99209/roms/ /data/GBA/ ~~~ ### USB ~~~text /mnt/usb0/homebrew/PS5GBA/games/ ~~~ USB0 through USB7 are supported. Alternative folders include: ~~~text /mnt/usb0/homebrew/PS5GBA/roms/ /mnt/usb0/PS5GBA/games/ /mnt/usb0/PS5GBA/roms/ /mnt/usb0/homebrew/PPSA99209/games/ /mnt/usb0/homebrew/PPSA99209/roms/ /mnt/usb0/GBA/ ~~~ Subfolders are scanned up to five levels deep. Games found in these folders are presented in one library. ### NFS Open **Square → R1 / All games → Settings → Network → NFS URL**. Example: ~~~text nfs://192.168.1.10/GBA ~~~ Save the URL and restart PS5GBA. URLs can also be entered in `/data/PS5GBA/nfs.txt`, one share per line. The app connects directly to the server. ROMs are read into RAM when launched; no PS5 kernel mount is required. Clear saved URLs in All games settings when a share is no longer needed. ### ZIP and 7z support Use **one `.gba` image per ZIP**. Stored and Deflate compression are supported. - Maximum ROM size: **32 MiB**. - Maximum ZIP/file size: **64 MiB**. - Encrypted, multi-ROM and ZIP64 ZIP archives are not supported. - **7z (experimental, Issue #2):** LZMA/LZMA2 archives with exactly one `.gba` game can be read directly from internal storage, USB or NFS without writing an extracted ROM to disk. 7z archives must be at most 64 MiB and their decoded ROM at most 32 MiB. Solid folders that expand beyond 64 MiB, password-protected archives and multi-ROM archives are rejected. 7z requires PS5 hardware testing before inclusion in a stable release. - A ZIP containing an entire ROM collection must be unpacked into individual ROMs or individual game ZIPs on your server. ## Graphics settings Open **Square → Settings → Graphics**. Choose **All games** for global defaults or **This game** for an override. | Setting | v2 default | | --- | --- | | Output resolution | **4K** | | Graphics mode | **4K ENHANCED** | | Scaling | **Stretch** | | Integer scaling | **On** | | VSync | **Off** | | Adaptive sharpness | 25% | | Color boost | 15% | | Contrast | 105% | | Display color correction | Off | | FPS counter | Off | These five main defaults match a configuration reported to run smoothly on PS5. Existing explicitly saved choices are preserved. **Stretch takes precedence over integer sizing.** Integer scaling becomes effective when using the original 3:2 aspect ratio. Resolution and VSync are global startup settings and require an app restart. Other graphics choices apply when the next game starts. VSync-off requires an immediate presentation mode from the Vulkan driver; if unavailable, the app logs the FIFO fallback. ### Graphics modes | Mode | Presentation | | --- | --- | | ORIGINAL | Nearest-neighbor pixels, original colors and no sharpening. | | 4K HD SMOOTH | Independent edge-aware pixel-art filtering with diagonal interpolation. | | 4K ENHANCED | Edge-aware filtering with restrained color boost, contrast and adaptive sharpening. | 4K describes the **output framebuffer**. GBA emulation and original artwork remain **240 × 160**; filters do not create newly drawn HD sprites. The edge-aware shader is independently implemented. Experimental high-resolution mGBA OpenGL rendering is not enabled. ## Controls ### Game shelf | Action | Default | | --- | --- | | Browse games | D-pad / left stick, left and right | | Start game | Cross | | Open settings | Square | | Refresh selected cover | R2 | | This game / All games | L1 / R1 in settings | | Settings / Controls tab | L2 / R2 in settings | ### In game | GBA action | Default controller button | | --- | --- | | A | Cross | | B | Circle | | L | L1 | | R | R1 | | Start | Options | | Select | Create | | Directions | D-pad; left stick also enabled by default | | Emulator shortcut | Default | | --- | --- | | Save state | L3 + R3 + D-pad Up | | Load state | L3 + R3 + D-pad Down | | Return to shelf | Touchpad click | | Fast forward | Hold L2; game audio is muted | ### Customize your buttons Open **Square → R2 / Controls** to view and edit assignments. - Choose **All games** for global defaults or **This game** for an override. - Left/right or Cross cycles an assignment. - Fast forward has a configurable held-button assignment. - Each save/load/menu shortcut has up to three button fields. **None** skips a field; all None disables the shortcut. - Settings save immediately and apply when the next game is started. - Save/load shortcuts trigger once per press and consume their bound game inputs. - Holding **L1 + R1 + touchpad click for two seconds** remains an emergency route back to the shelf. Saving a new state overwrites that ROM's previous state slot. Battery saves are written periodically and when returning to the menu. Content-derived save names avoid collisions between similarly named games. Incompatible or unreadable existing battery saves are preserved rather than silently replaced. ## Library cache and recent games The first successful scan creates a local index. Subsequent starts reuse the NFS index while checking local/USB folders for changes. Offline server detection is bounded so local games remain available. After changing games on an NFS share, choose: **Square → R1 / All games → Settings → Network → Rescan game library** Then restart PS5GBA. Library reset and NFS URL removal are also available in All games settings. Changing the share configuration selects a separate cache. The loading bar indicates activity while the total directory size is unknown, with live game and entry counts. Under **Library**, choose **Recent games first** to show recently launched games at the front after restarting. The last played game is also remembered for selection. This is library ordering, not a separate recent-games screen. ## Covers Automatic box art uses the [Libretro GBA Named_Boxarts collection](https://thumbnails.libretro.com/Nintendo%20-%20Game%20Boy%20Advance/Named_Boxarts/). The app includes a **5,959-filename index**, with exact filename and normalized title/region matching. No-Intro-style ROM/ZIP names work best. Matching handles common accents, such as Pokémon, and ignores bracketed tags during normalized lookup. Images are downloaded on demand; the artwork itself is not bundled. Press **Triangle** on the shelf to retry the selected game's cover (R2 also works). This checks the ROM directory again, even while offline, before attempting a download. If a same-folder cover exists, it always wins and no network request is made. The previous image is retained if an online refresh fails. **Preferred: put a custom cover beside the ROM with exactly the same basename:** ~~~text /data/PS5GBA/games/marioland2.gba /data/PS5GBA/games/marioland2.png ~~~ The same rule works for `.zip` and `.7z` ROMs, for example `marioland2.7z` plus `marioland2.jpg`. It also works for USB ROM folders. Name comparison is case-insensitive (`.PNG`, `.JPG` and `.JPEG` are accepted), and PNG is preferred before JPG and JPEG. A corrupt or empty image falls back to other candidates. **Cover search order:** image next to the ROM → `/data/PS5GBA/covers/` → USB covers folder → cached download → online Libretro exact/fuzzy matching. For the shared covers folder, use the game file stem or displayed GBA serial as the image name. A same-folder user image is never overwritten by automatic cover downloads. Only nearby artwork is kept live; downloaded covers remain cached on disk. Successful cached covers are reused when no ROM-adjacent user image is present. The current negative-lookup cache is versioned separately to allow new name-matching improvements to retry earlier misses. ## BIOS A proprietary BIOS is **not required** for normal use: mGBA provides a built-in fallback. If you have your own GBA BIOS, place it at: ~~~text /data/PS5GBA/bios/gba_bios.bin ~~~ No BIOS is included in the release. BIOS skipping is enabled by default in the current runtime. ## App data and logs | Content | Location | | --- | --- | | Games | `/data/PS5GBA/games/` or `/data/PS5GBA/roms/` | | Battery saves | `/data/PS5GBA/saves/` | | Save states | `/data/PS5GBA/states/` | | Optional BIOS | `/data/PS5GBA/bios/gba_bios.bin` | | Global settings | `/data/PS5GBA/gs.ini` | | Per-game settings | `/data/PS5GBA/settings/` | | Recent games | `/data/PS5GBA/recent-games.txt` | | Custom covers | `/data/PS5GBA/covers/` | | Library, cover and shader caches | `/data/PS5GBA/cache/` | | Boot log | `/data/PS5GBA/logs/boot.log` | | Cover download errors | `/data/PS5GBA/logs/cover-download.log` | | NFS URLs | `/data/PS5GBA/nfs.txt` | If `/data` is unavailable, the app uses `/download0/PS5GBA/` as its fallback data folder. The QR settings page listens on **port 8844** and can provide logs. Routine mGBA BIOS/DMA DEBUG and INFO traces are suppressed in v2 to avoid continuous disk writes during gameplay. Core warnings and errors remain available. ## Build from source See [BUILDING.md](BUILDING.md) for the dependency layout and build instructions, and [RELEASING.md](RELEASING.md) for release preparation. ~~~sh PS5GBA_DEPS=/path/to/prepared/ps5-build bash gba/tools/build.sh ~~~ The active adapter/runtime is in **`gba/src/`**, the upstream core is in **`gba/third_party/mgba/`**, and the native interface uses **`ps5/frontend/`** directly. The GBA build does not compile a SNES or PS2 emulator core. The required PS5 SDK/Vulkan/network dependencies are prepared externally, as in the PS5SNES build. Run the host regression suite with: ~~~sh python3 gba/tools/test.py ~~~ ## Current limits and testing - One active player in the current integration. - One save-state slot per ROM; states are tied to the core/version. Keep battery saves for portability. - Tilt, gyro, solar-sensor controls and multiplayer are not exposed. - No separate in-game pause overlay or folder-tree browser; touchpad returns to the shelf and subfolders are scanned recursively. - General firmware compatibility and sustained PS5 GPU performance across games have not been established. - A user tested GBA games on PS5 and reported smooth gameplay after selecting the configuration now used as the v2 defaults. The new v2 build still needs a console retest. - Historical host test reports describe real ARM execution, 240 × 160 video, audio, GBA timing, controller input, SRAM/state persistence, ZIP loading, settings, audio resampling and actual Vulkan rendering through 4K. - Pokémon Emerald and the German Smaragd-Edition cover matches were checked against live, valid PNG downloads. - See [TESTING.md](TESTING.md) for the remaining console checklist, including Flash/EEPROM and RTC cartridges. - No commercial ROMs, proprietary BIOS files or console keys are included. ## Credits and license - **YAHBALLON** — project customization and supplied logo. - **Spyros and PCSX2 contributors** — original PS5SX2 interface and shared frontend. - [mGBA contributors](https://github.com/mgba-emu/mgba) — Game Boy Advance emulation; **MPL-2.0**. - [mihawk-99 / PS5_Vulkan](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Vulkan) — native Vulkan driver and runtime work. - [BlackBearReloaded / ps5-native-app-boilerplate](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-native-app-boilerplate) — native startup and packaging tooling. - [Lapy filesystem helper](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/PS5-Lapy-JB-Daemon) — restricted filesystem helper. - [Libretro thumbnails](https://thumbnails.libretro.com/) — box-art collection. - Libnfs, libcurl, OpenSSL, zlib, zstd, libpsl and the bundled font/library authors. SkyEmu was a presentation reference; no SkyEmu code was incorporated. The edge/color shader is independently implemented. PS5GBA integration code is **GPL-3.0-or-later**. Upstream components retain their own licenses and notices. See [COPYING.GPLv3](COPYING.GPLv3), [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) and the included license files. ## v2 by YAHBALLON (AI-assisted) Adds automatic Libretro GBA covers with normalized title/region matching, local caching and R2 refresh. Changes the default graphics configuration to **4K / 4K ENHANCED / Stretch / Integer Scaling on / VSync off**, based on the user's successful console configuration. Suppresses repeated core BIOS/DMA traces while retaining warnings and errors. Existing explicit settings and saves are retained. Earlier native builds, cover checks and host core tests were reported as passing; these have not been rerun for this checkout, and the updated release still needs console testing.

latestRelease.body:
# GBAXY v2.3.0 by YAHBALLON

(AI-assisted) Feature and stability release for PS5 Game Boy Advance homebrew (PPSA99209).

## Improvements

- **7z ROMs (Issue #2):** load single-GBA LZMA/LZMA2 archives from local storage, USB or NFS, with memory bounds and archive validation; existing `.gba` and `.zip` support remains.
- **Smarter cover search:** the Libretro GBA artwork index supports scene-dump prefixes (e.g. `1636 -`), No-Intro/GoodTools region labels, Pokemon aliases, and conservative fuzzy name matching that rejects ambiguous sequels.
- **Local ROM-folder cover override:** `My Game.gba`, `My Game.zip` or `My Game.7z` uses `My Game.png`, `My Game.jpg` or `My Game.jpeg` in the same folder. Image filenames are matched case-insensitively; PNG takes priority. Local covers override manual covers, cached thumbnails and automatic download. **Exact basename matching remains required** (the temporary double-dot filename workaround has been removed).
- **Triangle: Retry cover** updates the selected artwork, checks the same ROM folder first (also when offline), and can discover an image uploaded while GBAXY is already open.
- **Settings and stability:** avoid dangling settings-row references on first save and synchronize the GPU when returning from a game to the shelf. The console exit fix from v2.2.1 remains.
- **Diagnostics:** clearer cover decoding and local-file errors in `/data/PS5GBA/logs/boot.log`.

## Installation

Download `PPSA99209.zip` from the release assets, extract the `PPSA99209` directory and copy it to `/data/homebrew/`. Preserve `/data/PS5GBA/` to keep ROMs, save games, screenshots, settings and cache. The automatically generated GitHub source ZIP is not an installable application.

## Verification

The user reports that the tested homebrew and local cover detection now work on PS5. CI performs native PS5 compilation, source checks, archive tests and ZIP integrity checks before publishing. The specific published v2.3.0 package still requires on-console regression testing after version bump.

---
# GBAXY v2.2.1 by YAHBALLON

## Fix: PS5 SIGSYS crash when closing GBAXY

- Replace the C library `exit(0)` in the native CoverFlow close path with the PS5 system-service request `sceSystemServiceLoadExec("exit", nullptr)` **after resource shutdown**.
- Override `catchReturnFromMain` in the native CRT so an ordinary return from `main()` cannot fall through to the forbidden libc exit syscall.
- When the system service declines a shutdown, log the return code to `/data/PS5GBA/logs/boot.log` and wait for the shell instead of crashing.
- Keep `PPSA99209`, existing game ROMs, saves, settings, cache, GBA core and Porpoise UI unchanged.

**Validation:** CI compilation and tests do not prove the fix on real PS5 hardware. Verify pressing ○ then × closes without the CE-10 / SIGSYS error.

---
# PS5GBA v2.1 by YAHBALLON

(AI-assisted) Native PS5 Game Boy Advance emulator using mGBA 0.10.5.
App ID: **PPSA99209**.

- Fix Issue #1: correct cached `.gba` extension filtering (including `.GBA`), recognize internal `games/` and `roms/` folders, and fix old SNES-format text in the empty library screen.
- Automatic Libretro GBA box-art matching, disk caching and R2 cover refresh.
- Default graphics: 4K output, 4K ENHANCED, Stretch, Integer Scaling on,
  and VSync off. Existing explicit settings and saves are preserved.
- Routine mGBA DEBUG/INFO traces are suppressed; warnings and errors remain.
- Local, USB and NFS game loading, battery saves, save states and configurable
  controller shortcuts. See the README for controls and supported paths.

## Installation

Download the application ZIP attached to the release, extract it and copy the
complete `PPSA99209` folder to `/data/homebrew/`. Preserve `/data/PS5GBA/` when
updating. GitHub's automatic source archives are not installable applications.
No games or proprietary BIOS images are included.

## Validation status

Earlier native builds and host tests were reported as passing. These historical
results have not been rerun for this source checkout. Smooth gameplay was
reported with the selected graphics configuration; the v2.1 release build still
requires a PS5 console retest. General firmware compatibility and sustained
GPU performance across games have not been established. See `TESTING.md` and
`RELEASING.md` before publishing.

## Fresh build validation — 2026-10-10

(AI-assisted) Compiled in Ubuntu with Clang/LLVM 18 using the prepared PS5
dependencies. Native link, ELF memory parameters, signed-container integrity
and the PPSA99209 filesystem helper passed. The host regression suite passed
for the GBA core, library/settings, resampling and Vulkan rendering through 4K.
ZIP CRC, required files, title ID and all 16 build-manifest file hashes passed.
Package: `dist/PS5GBA-v2-by-YAHBALLON.zip`; SHA-256 is recorded in
`VERIFICATION.json` and the adjacent checksum file. PS5 hardware testing remains
pending; host rendering results do not establish console GPU performance.

repos.readme:
# GBCXY ### 8-Bit Colors. Next-Gen CoverFlow. **v2.0.0 · by YAHBALLON · PPSA99210** [![Native PS5 Build](https://github.com/Yahballon/PS5GBCX/actions/workflows/build-gbcxy.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Yahballon/PS5GBCX/actions/workflows/build-gbcxy.yml) [![GitHub releases](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/Yahballon/PS5GBCX?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/Yahballon/PS5GBCX/releases)
**GBCXY** is a PlayStation 5 homebrew emulator for **Game Boy and Game Boy Color**, powered by the mGBA 0.10.5 GB/GBC core and a 3D Vulkan CoverFlow frontend. It builds on the same modern frontend foundation as GBAXY, with five original themes and its own animated loading sequence. > **Compatibility:** the repository remains `PS5GBCX`, Title ID remains **`PPSA99210`**, and existing games, settings, cached box art and saves remain in **`/data/PS5GBC/`**. This is an in-place upgrade, not a new app title. ## Highlights | Feature | Description | | --- | --- | | **3D CoverFlow** | Animated glass cartridge cases, neon edges, cover reflections and wraparound browsing | | **Auto cover art** | GB and GBC use their **separate** Libretro Named_Boxarts libraries, with region/name fallbacks and a local disk cache | | **Five new themes** | Chromatic Shift, Pocket Forest, Berry Soda, Polar LCD and Retro Amber | | **Chromatic Pocket** | Original animated 8-bit boot: rotating color-pixel mosaic, LCD scanlines, cartridge emblem and genuine ROM scan counts | | **Native GB/GBC emulation** | mGBA 0.10.5 with GB/GBC core enabled; preserves ROM scanning, audio, saves and controller mappings | | **Flexible scaling** | Stretch to full screen, original GB/GBC aspect ratio or integer scaling | | **Safe PS5 exit** | In the library, Circle opens the close confirmation, Cross confirms, Circle cancels. Shutdown uses `sceSystemServiceLoadExec("exit", nullptr)` rather than unsupported libc `exit(0)`. | ### Choose your theme - **Chromatic Shift** — multicolor turquoise and purple; default - **Pocket Forest** — LCD greens and spring-leaf highlights - **Berry Soda** — pink, raspberry and sunset orange - **Polar LCD** — icy blue and white glass - **Retro Amber** — dark gold inspired by vintage handheld screens Select a theme under **Settings → Appearance → Theme**. The selection is stored in the existing global configuration. ## Box art sources GBCXY uses the existing local cover folder and cache first. For missing covers it looks up No-Intro names and common USA, Europe and Japan region variants in the correct system-specific directories: - **Game Boy (.gb):** [Libretro GB Named_Boxarts](https://thumbnails.libretro.com/Nintendo%20-%20Game%20Boy/Named_Boxarts/) - **Game Boy Color (.gbc):** [Libretro GBC Named_Boxarts](https://thumbnails.libretro.com/Nintendo%20-%20Game%20Boy%20Color/Named_Boxarts/) Game Boy artwork will not be incorrectly selected from the Game Boy Color library (or the reverse). Portrait art stays portrait, landscape artwork keeps its complete source image, and reflections follow the same geometry. Cover downloads happen on demand and are cached for the next boot. ## Installation / updating 1. Download the latest compiled **`PPSA99210.zip`** from [Releases](https://github.com/Yahballon/PS5GBCX/releases). A GitHub source-code ZIP is **not** an installable PS5 build. 2. Extract the **complete `PPSA99210` folder**, retaining `eboot.bin`, `sce_sys`, `sce_module` and the packaged helper. 3. Copy it to a supported PS5 homebrew install folder, commonly `/data/homebrew/PPSA99210/`, and start **GBCXY** from your jailbroken PS5. ### Game folders and saved data ```text /data/PS5GBC/games/ /data/PS5GBC/roms/ /data/PS5GBC/saves/ /data/PS5GBC/states/ /data/PS5GBC/covers/ /data/PS5GBC/cache/ /data/PS5GBC/logs/ ``` You can also scan USB game directories such as `/mnt/usb0/homebrew/PS5GBC/games/` and configured NFS shares. Use your own legally acquired GB/GBC game files; the repository includes **no ROMs**. ## Source layout and builds The [**GBCXY Native Build & Release**](.github/workflows/build-gbcxy.yml) workflow performs automated source/box-art/controller regression tests and compiles a genuine native signed PS5 package from source. Main-branch builds publish a release tagged `v2.0.0`; version metadata is maintained in `app.json` and `gbc/src/gbcxy_build_version.h`. ```text gbc/src/ GB/GBC core wrapper, emulator and Chromatic Pocket animation gbc/third_party/mgba/ Original open-source mGBA source gbc/tools/ Native PS5 build scripts and regression checks ps5/frontend/ Game library, cover worker, settings, native Vulkan bridge ps5/porpoise_original/ Licensed Porpoise 3D UI code ps5/frontend/assets/ GBCXY icon and embedded UI assets tests/ GBCXY visual, cover-provider and exit regression tests .github/workflows/ Automated signed build and release ``` GBCXY builds require the PS5 payload toolchain, native Vulkan dependencies and compatible Linux SDK tools. Host-only builds cannot produce an installable PS5 binary. ## Credits and licensing **GBCXY by YAHBALLON.** GB/GBC emulation is provided by [mGBA](https://github.com/mgba-emu/mgba), with a frontend adapted from [Porpoise](https://github.com/elripalda/Porpoise-Dolphin-Emulator-for-PS5) and open-source PS5 development frameworks. Preserve and consult bundled third-party licenses and notices. This independent community homebrew project is not affiliated with Sony or Nintendo. It does not distribute commercial ROMs, copyrighted BIOS files or pirated games. Console testing is needed before release builds should be considered fully verified.

# GBCXY v2.0.0 by YAHBALLON

- Updated Game Boy and Game Boy Color app with a 3D Porpoise-inspired CoverFlow, five bespoke GBCXY visual themes, natural-size cover art, automatic local/cache/Libretro GB and GBC box art resolution.

The repository remains named PS5N64X to preserve existing links. ## Features | | | | --- | --- | | **3D CoverFlow** | Original Porpoise Vulkan rendering, neon glass cases, reflections and scrolling | | **5 exclusive themes** | Quantum Lime, Nebula Purple, Retro Red, Ice Crystal, Golden Era | | **Animated boot** | Original 64-bit Orbital Gateway: independent orbit rings, floating satellites and actual ROM/USB/NFS scan status | | **Box art** | Automatically scans all games in the background, downloading missing box art to disk. repos.name: PS5NESX
repos.description: A native NES emulator for jailbroken PS5
repos.readme:
NESYX

Native NES emulation for a jailbroken PlayStation 5
Retro games. Neon covers. Modern PS5 homebrew.
v1.0.28 · by YAHBALLON · Title ID PPSA99204

> **NESYX** is an open-source homebrew emulator for compatible jailbroken PS5 consoles, built around **FCEUmm** and an original **3D neon CoverFlow** frontend. The GitHub repository retains the name `PS5NESX` to preserve existing links, while the app and its menus are branded **NESYX**. ## ✨ Highlights | Experience | What you get | | --- | --- | | **3D CoverFlow library** | Neon glass game cases, reflections, smooth wraparound navigation, original tiger emblem | | **Automatic box art** | Libretro NES box-art lookup, secondary cover sources, persistent caching and download progress | | **HD fallback art** | Full-resolution 1024 × 1536 NO COVER design if no matching artwork is found | | **Pixel Reactor boot** | Original animated neon loading sequence with a rotating 8-bit reactor, pixel particles and live library scanning stats | | **3 picture modes** | **16:9 Fullscreen** (default), classic **4:3**, or **Integer pixels** | | **Emulation and saves** | FCEUmm NES core, configurable controller bindings, battery saves and save/load states | | **ROM sources** | Internal storage, USB and NFS shares; NES, UNIF and compatible single-game ZIP files | | **Safe exit** | Press **○** in the library to open the exit confirmation; **× Yes**, **○ No** | | **HD packs (experimental)** | Mesen-format `hires.txt` support where compatible; not all packs are verified | ## 🛡️ Native PS5 exit fix (v1.0.28) Closing with **○**, then **×** now exits through `sceSystemServiceLoadExec("exit", nullptr)` after native graphics/audio/HTTP/controller teardown. This replaces libc `exit()` that could cause SIGSYS (signal 12); the CRT main-return path is protected too. All existing saves and ROM folders remain untouched. ## 🎮 Controller guide | Action | Input | | --- | --- | | Browse games | D-pad / left stick | | Play selected game | **×** | | Settings | **□** | | Exit confirmation (library) | **○** | | Confirm exit / Cancel | **× Yes** / **○ No** | | NES A / B | **×** / **○** in-game | | NES Start / Select | Options / Touchpad click or Create | | Save state | L3 + R3 + D-pad Up | | Load state | L3 + R3 + D-pad Down | | Return from game to library | L1 + R1 + Touchpad click | The menu's Circle-to-close shortcut is active **only in the library**, not while a NES game is running. Individual button and shortcut mappings can be customized under Settings. ## 📦 Install / Update 1. Download the latest **`PPSA99204.zip`** from [Releases](https://github.com/Yahballon/PS5NESX/releases). 2. Extract the ZIP and transfer its complete `PPSA99204` directory to the supported homebrew install location, typically `/data/homebrew/PPSA99204/`. 3. Start **NESYX** with your compatible PS5 homebrew launcher. The package must retain `eboot.bin`, `sce_sys/`, `sce_module/`, `lapy.elf` and the helper manifest. **Keep the existing `/data/PS5NES/` folder during updates**: this legacy data path is intentionally unchanged to protect saves, settings, artwork and games. ### Add your legally obtained games | Source | Example | | --- | --- | | Internal | `/data/PS5NES/games/` | | USB | `/mnt/usb0/homebrew/PS5NES/games/` (supported USB volumes also scanned) | | NFS | `nfs://192.168.1.10/NES` (configure in **Settings → Network**) | | Game saves / configuration | `/data/PS5NES/` | NESYX scans supported directories and caches thumbnails for faster subsequent launches. Use **Settings → Display → Picture → 16:9 Fullscreen** if an older installation retained a saved 4:3 preference. ## 🛠 Build from source The repository contains the native app's NES/FCEUmm sources, PS5 adapter, Porpoise-derived Vulkan UI, header dependencies, and build scripts. The automated workflow compiles the real PS5 executable, verifies the signed installation package, and publishes versioned releases — not placeholder ZIPs. - **Workflow:** [Build NESYX Native](.github/workflows/build-nesyx.yml) - **Build instructions:** [BUILDING.md](BUILDING.md) - **Native entry:** `nes/src/main_shelf.cpp` - **Pixel Reactor:** `nes/src/loading.cpp` - **UI and controller behavior:** `ps5/frontend/` - **Asset sources:** `ps5/frontend/assets/` - **Build script:** `nes/tools/build.sh` - **Release version authority:** `app.json` The GitHub Actions build restores pinned PS5 Vulkan/SDK dependencies, prepares shader and UI assets, compiles the native ELF, packages `PPSA99204.zip`, and uploads a versioned GitHub Release. It requires a suitable native PS5 SDK/toolchain; ordinary desktop compilation does **not** produce a PS5-installable application. New changes to native source on `main` automatically trigger the workflow. Releases use compatibility tags such as `ps5nesx-v1.0.28`. ## 🧾 Credits, rights and contributions **Developed and customized by YAHBALLON.** NES emulation is based on the open-source [FCEUmm](https://github.com/libretro/libretro-fceumm) core. The native frontend includes components derived from open-source PS5 and Porpoise projects; see [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) and original upstream licensing files. **NESYX does not distribute commercial ROMs, BIOS files or pirated content.** Bring your own legally acquired game files. This project is community homebrew; it is not affiliated with Nintendo or Sony. Licensed material remains under the terms in [LICENSE](LICENSE) and the bundled third-party notices. Bug reports and contributions are welcome through GitHub Issues and Pull Requests.

# SNESXY **16-Bit Memories. Next-Gen Homebrew.** **SNESXY v1.0.9 · by YAHBALLON · PPSA99205** [![Native PS5 Build](https://github.com/Yahballon/PS5SNESX/actions/workflows/build-snesxy.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Yahballon/PS5SNESX/actions/workflows/build-snesxy.yml) [![Releases](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/Yahballon/PS5SNESX?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/Yahballon/PS5SNESX/releases)
SNESXY is a native Super Nintendo emulator for jailbroken PS5 consoles, based on the **bsnes-mercury balanced** core. Its modern 3D CoverFlow frontend takes inspiration from our NESYX work, while using its own SNES-themed palettes and an original Hypercube startup animation. The repository stays named PS5SNESX to preserve existing links. ## What's new in v1.0.9 - **Native PS5 exit fix:** Closing with ○ then × now uses `sceSystemServiceLoadExec("exit", nullptr)` after native resource cleanup, not libc `exit()` (which can trigger SIGSYS). The CRT main-return path is protected too. Existing games, saves and title ID stay untouched. - **Native SNES box proportions:** Landscape SNES covers render on **wide glass cases**; rarer portrait artwork stays in taller cases. Every cover preserves its image ratio and full image without cropping, and reflections match the case size. Cached artwork is reused automatically—no cover-cache reset. - **Adaptive 3D glass CoverFlow:** landscape and portrait box art automatically use matching case shapes, uncropped textures, reflections, smooth movement and cover caching. - **Five SNESXY themes:** Royal Indigo (violet/pink), Sunset Arcade (orange/coral), Emerald Circuit (mint green), Glacier Glass (ice blue), and Midnight Gold (black/gold). Change them in **Settings → Appearance → Theme**; saved for the entire library. - **16-Bit Hypercube:** animated rotating wireframe cubes with colorful satellites, scanlines, and accurate NFS/ROM scanning counters; wholly separate from NESYX's Pixel Reactor. - **Additional SNES cover provider:** [Libretro Named Boxarts](https://thumbnails.libretro.com/Nintendo%20-%20Super%20Nintendo%20Entertainment%20System/Named_Boxarts/) alongside the original SNES collection and Libretro GitHub mirror. - **16:9 Fullscreen** by default for new installations; 4:3 and Integer pixels remain available. - **Close confirmation:** in the game library, press **○** to open the prompt, **×** to exit, or **○** to cancel. ## Install Download **`PPSA99205.zip`** from [Releases](https://github.com/Yahballon/PS5SNESX/releases). Extract the complete `PPSA99205` directory and install it using a supported PS5 homebrew launcher (commonly `/data/homebrew/PPSA99205/`). Do not omit `eboot.bin`, `sce_sys/`, `sce_module/` or the packaged helper files. > **Update safely:** Existing games, battery saves, save states, configurations, cover art and logs are intentionally kept in `/data/PS5SNES/`. **SNESXY does not rename that data directory or change the Title ID `PPSA99205`.** Place your own legally acquired `.sfc`, `.smc`, `.swc` or `.fig` games in `/data/PS5SNES/games/`; compatible single-ROM ZIP files are also supported. USB and configured NFSv3 directories can be scanned. For NFS, use **Settings → Network** and restart/rescan the library. ## Controls | Action | DualSense | | --- | --- | | Browse SNES games | D-pad / left stick | | Launch selected game | × | | Open Settings | □ | | Close app prompt (library only) | ○ | | Confirm exit / Cancel | × / ○ | | SNES A / B / X / Y | ○ / × / △ / □ in-game | | SNES L / R | L1 / R1 | | Start / Select | Options / Touchpad click or Create | | Save / Load state | L3 + R3 + D-pad Up / Down | | Return from SNES game | L1 + R1 + Touchpad click | | Refresh selected cover | R2 | ## Builds and source [**Native Build & Release workflow**](.github/workflows/build-snesxy.yml) runs the SNESXY regression tests, provisions the pinned open-source PS5 toolchain, builds the native executable and creates `PPSA99205.zip`. Main-branch builds publish a release tagged `snesxy-v1.0.9`. The version is recorded in `app.json` and `snes/src/snesxy_build_version.h`. ```text snes/src/ SNES core integration, runtime and Hypercube loader snes/third_party/ bsnes-mercury balanced source snes/tools/ Native build and host tests ps5/frontend/ SNESXY CoverFlow, settings, SNES cover worker ps5/porpoise_original/ Licensed Vulkan/Porpoise UI components ps5/frontend/assets/ Embedded icons and menu files scripts/ Pinned PS5 toolchain bootstrap .github/workflows/ Automated native build and release ``` For manual builds, see [BUILDING.md](BUILDING.md). A prepared PS5 SDK/Vulkan build environment is required; building on ordinary Windows without the appropriate console toolchain does not produce a usable PS5 package. ## Credits and legal **SNESXY by YAHBALLON.** Built using the open-source [bsnes-mercury](https://github.com/libretro/bsnes-mercury) core, PS5 homebrew frameworks and the appropriately licensed Porpoise frontend. Other upstream contributors and licenses are credited in [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md), [COPYING.GPLv3](COPYING.GPLv3) and the bundled dependency directories. No commercial SNES games, BIOS files or other copyrighted ROMs are provided. This community project is not affiliated with Sony or Nintendo.

repos.description: Animated backgrounds for PS5 home screen.
repos.readme:
LiveShell Engine

Animated video wallpapers for the PS5 home screen.

--- ## Features - **Discover**: hundreds of animated wallpapers to download right on the PS5, by category (Anime, Games, Movies, ...) the list updates by itself. - **Library** tab with all your games and apps, to give each one its own video (experimental). - **PS Store only**: the video shows only on the PlayStation Store tile, with its own video. - **Playlists**: your wallpaper changes by itself through the videos you pick. - **Sound**: videos with sound play it. - **Game music**: a game's own theme keeps playing when its video has no sound or Sound is on Mute - **Your clips** from internal storage or a USB drive - **Looks**: Dim, Vignette, Haze, all combinable - **Hide in Settings**: Settings keeps the normal PS5 background - **Pause while a game runs**, so games get the video decoder - **Parallax** effect when moving between games - **Random video** on every start - **Rest mode**: comes back on its own after waking the PS5 - **Home-screen app** to pick, delete and control everything - **Phone / PC page** to upload, play and delete videos ## Install Needs a jailbroken PS5 with a payload loader. 1. Copy `.mp4` files to `/data/LiveShell/video`, or to a `liveshell` folder on a USB drive. 2. Load `liveshell.elf`. 3. Open the **LiveShell Engine** on the home screen (Media). Videos: H.264 or HEVC, 8-bit, up to 4K, with or without sound. 4K / 2K play as the main wallpaper or in PS Store only mode, and hide while a game is open. ## Discover 1. Open the **Discover** tab. 3. Download and Press **Use**: it plays on the home screen or per game. Downloaded wallpapers also appear in **All** tab. ## A video for a game (experimental) 1. Open the **Library** tab and pick a game or app. 2. Choose its video. **Reset** gives it back the default background. Keep all videos in one place (internal **or** USB) for the quickest switching. **A video for every tile** - 🎮 **Games**: PS5 and PS4 - 🧩 **Homebrew and web-app tiles**: Payload Manager, etaHEN Toolbox, and more - 🛍️ **PlayStation Store**: with PS Store only. ## Folders on the PS5 | Path | What | |---|---| | `/data/LiveShell/video/` | Your videos | | `/liveshell/` | Videos on a USB drive | | `/data/LiveShell/config.txt` | Settings | | `/data/LiveShell/liveshell.log` | Log | ## Building Linux or WSL, with the [PS5 payload SDK](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk) and the [OnionHEN](https://github.com/aydencharles/onionHEN) v0.9.0-beta2 source tree. ```sh ONIONHEN=~/onionHEN-beta2 PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK=~/ps5-payload-sdk tools/build.sh ``` `src/` is copied into OnionHEN as `source/liveshell` and built as the `liveshell` target. ## Credits - **[OnionHEN](https://github.com/aydencharles/onionHEN/)**: payload injector, detour library and ShellUI groundwork - **[PS5 Payload SDK](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk)**: toolchain and PS5 libraries ## License GPL-3.0. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).

repos.name: Ruffle-Flash-PS5
repos.description: PS5 Flash Emulator.
repos.readme:
Ruffle Flash PS5

Flash games, running natively on PlayStation 5.
A port of Ruffle, the open-source Flash Player emulator, as a native PS5 app.

---

## Features - Plays `.swf` games and animations (ActionScript 1, 2 and 3), rendered on the PS5's GPU. - Library with **Recent**, **Games** and **Favorites** tabs, list or grid view, and covers taken automatically from your games. - **Controls per game**: map any DualSense button to a key or a mouse click. - **USB mouse and keyboard**: plug them into the PS5 and play; they work in the menus too. - **Quick menu** in game (touchpad): resume, restart, volume, retake cover, back to the library. - **Themes** (Ember, Midnight, Retro CRT, Newgrounds Dark) and **accent colours**, with calm, quiet menu sounds. - **Badges**: 34 goals to unlock while you play, each with its own medal (can be turned off), plus **play time** for every game. - **Search** your games (L2 or just type on a keyboard), and a **screensaver** with your covers drifting by. - **On-screen keyboard** L2 to run it in games, some games needs keyboard. - Ruffle's own player settings: quality, scale mode, letterbox, frame rate, player version and more. - Sound with MP3, AAC and Nellymoser support. ## Install You need a PS5 with **kstuff** running and a **[ShadowMountPlus](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus)**. Download the [latest release](https://github.com/ZiZc3/Ruffle-Flash-PS5/releases), then: 1. Copy the **`PPSA68091`** folder to `/data/homebrew/`. 2. Load **`ShadowMountPlus`** together with kstuff. 3. Put all your games (.swf) in `/data/ruffle/games/`. 4. Start **Ruffle Flash** from the home screen. ## Controls **Library** | Button | Action | |---|---| | D-Pad | Move | | ✕ | Play / select | | ○ | Back | | △ | Add to favorites | | □ | List / grid view | | Options | Controls for this game | | L1 / R1 | Switch tabs | | L2 | Search | **In game** (defaults; change them per game with Options in the library) | Button | Action | |---|---| | Left stick | Mouse cursor (or arrow keys / WASD) | | ✕ | Mouse click | | ○ / □ / △ | Z / Space / Enter | | L1 / R1 / R2 | Shift / X / O | | D-Pad | Arrow keys | | Options / Create / L3 | Esc / P / Ctrl | | Right stick | Scroll | | L2 | On-screen keyboard | | R3 | Take a new cover | | **Touchpad click** | Quick menu (resume, restart, volume, back to the library) | **USB mouse and keyboard** Plug them into the PS5 and they just work. In games the mouse points, clicks and scrolls and the keyboard types and plays; **Esc** opens the quick menu. In the menus: type to search, arrows move, **Enter** selects, **Esc** goes back, **Tab** switches tabs, **F2** favorites, **F3** list/grid, **F4** controls; the mouse pointer shows while a mouse is plugged in, and right click goes back. ## Folders on the PS5 | Path | What | |---|---| | `/data/ruffle/games/` | Your games (`.swf`) | | `/data/ruffle/covers/` | Covers (`.png` / `.jpg`, named like the game) | | `/data/ruffle/saves/` | Game saves (only games that supported) | | `/data/ruffle/controls/` | Per-game controls | | `/data/ruffle/ruffle.log` | Log of the last session (attach it when reporting a problem) | > Games that come with extra files (folders like `db/` or `media/`) go in a folder of their own, with all their files, e.g. `/data/ruffle/games/Happy Wheels/`. ## Good to know - There is no internet: online-only parts of games (ads, high scores, logins) are skipped. - Very heavy ActionScript 3 games can run below full speed; most games run at their full frame rate. - Flash videos in H.264 are not supported. - Compatibility follows Ruffle: if a game works in Ruffle on PC, it most likely works here. ## How Rust runs on the PS5 Ruffle is written in Rust, and Rust has no PS5 target. This is how the app gets there: | Problem | Solution | |---|---| | No Rust target for the PS5 | A custom target, [`x86_64-ps5-freebsd.json`](x86_64-ps5-freebsd.json) (FreeBSD-based, Zen 2), with Rust's `std` built from source (`-Zbuild-std`). | | No thread-local storage for apps | The target sets `has-thread-local: false`, so `std` keeps its thread locals in pthread keys. | | The PS5's libc is FreeBSD 11 | `std` built for FreeBSD 11's ABI (`libc_unstable_freebsd_version="11"`), with small wrappers for `stat` and `readdir`. | | Functions `std` expects but the PS5 lacks | Small C shims ([`ps5_rust_shims.c`](ps5/scripts/ps5_rust_shims.c)) kept private to the app. | | Linking a PS5 app | [`ps5-link.sh`](ps5/scripts/ps5-link.sh) is Cargo's linker: it links with the PS5 toolchain, the app runtime and RADV; [`package.sh`](ps5/scripts/package.sh) signs the `eboot.bin`. | | Start-up | [`ps5_early.c`](ps5/scripts/ps5_early.c) runs before Rust: log file, crash handler, helper request. | | Graphics | Ruffle's wgpu renderer on Vulkan, through [Mihawk-99](https://github.com/mihawk-99)'s RADV driver, shown on a 4K display swapchain. | | Controller and sound | DualSense through `libScePad`, sound through `SceAudioOut`, its thread on a CPU core of its own. | The few changes to Ruffle and wgpu are in [`patches/`](patches). ## Building On Linux (WSL2 Ubuntu works), with [PS5_Vulkan](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Vulkan) built in `~/ps5/PS5_Vulkan`, Rust nightly with `rust-src`, and Java (for Ruffle's build): ```sh bash ps5/scripts/build.sh ``` It downloads Ruffle, applies the patches, builds the app and writes `PPSA68091/` and `PPSA68091.zip`. The helper builds with `make` in [`helper/`](helper) (needs `PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK`). ## Credits - **[Ruffle](https://github.com/ruffle-rs/ruffle)** and its contributors: the Flash Player emulator. - **[Mihawk-99](https://github.com/mihawk-99)**: [PS5_Vulkan](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Vulkan), RADV on the PS5. - **[ps5-payload-dev SDK](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk)**, **[kstuff](https://github.com/EchoStretch/kstuff)**, **[etaHEN](https://github.com/LightningMods/etaHEN)**, **[ShadowMountPlus](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus)** and the PS5 scene. - **[Inter](https://rsms.me/inter/)** font by Rasmus Andersson. ## License Ruffle Flash PS5 is licensed under the **GNU General Public License v3.0** (see [`LICENSE`](LICENSE)). Ruffle itself is MIT or Apache-2.0 (see [`LICENSE-RUFFLE.md`](LICENSE-RUFFLE.md)). No games are included. Ruffle Flash PS5 is a fan project, not affiliated with Sony, Adobe or the Ruffle project.

latestRelease.body:
## v1.3.0

### Saves
- **Fixed:** game saves were lost when the console was turned off, put in rest mode or the app was closed while still in a game (#1). Saves are now kept every 3 seconds and whenever the quick menu opens
- Saves are written in the background, so games never stutter while saving

### Fixes
- The Recent tab now highlights the game you just played
- Games with the same file name (in different folders, or names) no longer share saves, covers and controls
- A cover cut off by a crash is now retaken instead of staying broken
- Closing the controls page without changing anything no longer says "Controls saved" or counts toward the Remapper

### Install
1. Extract `PPSA68091.zip` and copy the `PPSA68091` folder to `/data/homebrew/`.
2. Load **`ShadowMountPlus`** together with kstuff.
3. Put all your games (`.swf`) in `/data/ruffle/games/`.
4. Start **Ruffle Flash**.

repos.name: VLC
repos.description: VLC for PS5.
repos.readme:
VLC

VLC media player, running natively on PlayStation 5.
A port of VLC 3.0 as a native PS5 app, with a controller-first interface.

--- ## Features - Plays nearly anything VLC plays: H.264, HEVC (8 and 10-bit), AV1, VP9, VC-1, MPEG-2 and more, up to 4K, with every common audio format, including TrueHD, DTS-HD and Opus. - **Hardware decoding** on the PS5's video chip for H.264 and HEVC up to 4K, 10-bit HDR included. - **HDR**: HDR10 and HLG go to an HDR TV as HDR, and are tone mapped with natural colours on an SDR one. Dolby Vision files play as their HDR10 base. - **Upscaling to 4K** for smaller videos (Off by default): EWA Lanczos Sharp, AMD FSR, FSRCNNX for films and shows, and Anime4K for anime. - **Library** with Home, Videos, Music, Playlists and Browse: thumbnails, Continue watching, Favourites and search. - **Playlists**: make your own, add any video or song from anywhere with Options, reorder them; covers made from their videos; `.m3u` files on your drives play too. - **Subtitles** in every script, styled ASS/SSA, size and colour, delay, plus **OpenSubtitles** downloads. - **5.1 / 7.1 surround**, equalizer, night mode and audio delay. - **Network**: SMB shares, DLNA servers, network links (HTTP, HLS, DASH…), free TV channels and internet radio. - **Phone & PC page**: open `http://:8080` in any browser to send files to the PS5, download them back to your phone or PC, or add your OpenSubtitles key. - Music mode with covers and a visualizer, a photo viewer, DVD / Blu-ray folders, and ZIP / RAR / 7z archives. - Two looks (**Classic** and **Modern**) and **16 languages**. ## Install You need a PS5 with **kstuff** running, plus **[ShadowMountPlus](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus)**. Download the [latest release](../../releases/latest), then: 1. Copy the **`PPSA85300`** folder to `/data/homebrew/`. 2. Start **VLC** from the home screen. 3. Add your media: a USB drive, `/data/vlc/`, or send files from your pc/phone (Options › Send files from a phone). Optional full access. With etaHEN, OnionHEN or the Helper, VLC can lift its sandbox. This gives it all of /data and USB drives plugged in while it runs. download [helper.elf](https://github.com/ZiZc3/VLC-PS5/raw/refs/heads/main/patches/Helper.elf) ## All VLC Features ✅ In the app. ### 🎞️ Video | Feature | Status | |---|---| | H.264, HEVC 8/10-bit, AV1, VP9, VC-1, MPEG-2, MPEG-4 and every format FFmpeg knows | ✅ | | MKV, MP4, AVI, MOV, TS, WebM, FLV, OGG… | ✅ | | Up to 4K at 60 Hz output | ✅ | | Auto fast decoding when a file can't keep up | ✅ | | Fast keyframe seeking | ✅ | | Aspect ratios (fit, fill, stretch, 16:9, 4:3, 21:9) and zoom | ✅ | | Deinterlace (auto / yadif) | ✅ | | Picture controls: brightness, contrast, saturation, gamma, hue | ✅ | | Rotate, flip, sharpen | ✅ | | 360° videos (look around with the right stick) | ✅ | | Frame-by-frame step | ✅ | | Screenshots to PNG | ✅ | | Hardware decoding (H.264 / HEVC) | ✅ | | HDR → SDR tone mapping | ✅ | | HDR10 output to the TV | ✅ | | Hardware decoding (VP9 up to 4K) | ✅ | | Upscaling up to 4K (EWA Lanczos, AMD FSR, FSRCNNX, Anime4K) | ✅ | ### 🔊 Audio | Feature | Status | |---|---| | AAC, AC-3, E-AC-3, DTS, DTS-HD, TrueHD, FLAC, ALAC, Opus, Vorbis, MP3 | ✅ | | 5.1 / 7.1 surround output | ✅ | | Speaker test | ✅ | | Stereo downmix for headphones | ✅ | | Audio delay (lip sync) | ✅ | | 10-band equalizer with presets | ✅ | | Night mode (compressor) | ✅ | | Volume boost up to 200 % | ✅ | | Preferred audio language | ✅ | ### 💬 Subtitles | Feature | Status | |---|---| | SRT, ASS/SSA, embedded MKV/MP4, PGS, DVB, DVD, closed captions | ✅ | | Every script: Arabic, Hebrew, Cyrillic, CJK, Thai, Devanagari… | ✅ | | Styled ASS/SSA (libass: fonts, positions, karaoke) | ✅ | | Auto-load `movie.srt` next to the video | ✅ | | Add a subtitle file while playing | ✅ | | Subtitle delay | ✅ | | Size, colour, background box | ✅ | | Preferred subtitle language | ✅ | | OpenSubtitles download (your own free API key) | ✅ | ### ▶️ Playback | Feature | Status | |---|---| | Resume and Continue watching | ✅ | | Seek preview while scrubbing | ✅ | | Speed 0.25× – 4× | ✅ | | Playlists | ✅ | | Chapters (list, skip, marks on the seek bar) | ✅ | | Bookmarks inside a file | ✅ | | A–B repeat | ✅ | | Loop, repeat list, shuffle | file) | | △ | Tracks: audio, subtitles, playback, picture | | □ | Next frame (while paused) | | L3 | Screenshot | | Touchpad | Show the controls · swipe to seek or change the volume | | ○ | Back | ## Folders on the PS5 | Path | What | |---|---| | `/data/homebrew/PPSA85300/media/` | The app's own media folder | | `/data/vlc/` | Your media on the console (needs full access) | | `/mnt/usb0` … `/mnt/usb7`, `/mnt/ext0` | USB and extended storage | | `/data/homebrew/PPSA85300/vlc-ps5.log` | Log of the last session (attach it when reporting a problem) | ## Building On Linux (WSL2 Ubuntu works), with [PS5_Vulkan](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Vulkan) built in `~/ps5/PS5_Vulkan`: ```sh mkdir -p ~/ps5/vlc-ps5/src && cd ~/ps5/vlc-ps5/src curl -LO https://download.videolan.org/pub/videolan/vlc/3.0.24/vlc-3.0.24.tar.xz tar xf vlc-3.0.24.tar.xz && cd - # back to this repository TARGET=ps5 bash ps5/deps/build-deps.sh # the libraries (FFmpeg, GnuTLS, libass…) TARGET=ps5 bash ps5/configure-vlc.sh # libvlc 3.0.24 with every plugin linked in bash ps5/build-title.sh # dist/PPSA85300/ with a signed eboot.bin ``` The libraries are downloaded by `build-deps.sh`; the changes to VLC and FFmpeg are in [`patches/`](patches). `bash host/build-app.sh` builds a Linux version of the app for testing. ## Credits - **[VLC](https://www.videolan.org/)** latestRelease.body:
## v0.6.0

### What's new
- **Redesign by Juxtopposed**, a whole new look next to Modern and Classic (Settings › Interface › Look):
  - **Dark and Light** themes (Settings › Interface › Theme)
  - **Choose your look again**: the first time v0.6 starts, you can pick Modern, Redesign by Juxtopposed or Classic (once)
- **Equalizer bands**: Preamp and 10 bands from 31 Hz to 16 kHz, −20 to +20 dB each. Pick a preset, then move any band: it becomes your own Custom sound, saved
- **Volume on the player bar**: move to the speaker, 
  - ↑ ↓ change it, ✕ mutes
- **Controller vibration**: when you switch tabs, change settings, change the volume,
  -  Turn it off in Settings › Interface › Controller vibration

### Changed
- In Modern and Classic, the Audio button on the player bar has a new icon (the speaker is now the volume)

repos.name: XPSemu
repos.description: Original Xbox emulator (Xemu) port for the PS5
repos.readme:
The original Xbox, running natively on a PlayStation 5.
A port of xemu to the PS5 as a native app, with its own Xbox-style dashboard.

---

> **Alpha 2** is an early build. It boots and plays real games, but expect bugs, slow scenes in > CPU-heavy games, and missing features. Please report problems with your `xemu-game.log` attached (see [Logs](#logs-and-reporting-problems)). ## Table of contents - [What is XPSemu?](#what-is-xpsemu) - [Features](#features) - [Requirements](#requirements) - [Installation](#installation) - [Folder layout on the PS5](#folder-layout-on-the-ps5) - [Controls](#controls) - [Game patches](#game-patches) - [Performance notes](#performance-notes) - [Logs and reporting problems](#logs-and-reporting-problems) - [Known limitations](#known-limitations) - [What XPSemu changes in xemu](#what-xpsemu-changes-in-xemu) - [Building from source](#building-from-source) - [Credits](#credits) - [License](#license-and-legal) ## What is XPSemu? XPSemu is [xemu](https://github.com/xemu-project/xemu), the open-source original Xbox emulator, ported to the PlayStation 5 as a native application. the whole emulator (Xbox CPU through QEMU's TCG JIT, the NV2A GPU through xemu's Vulkan renderer, the MCPX audio, the controllers) runs as a PS5 app on top of an open-source Vulkan driver (RADV, from the PS5_Vulkan project). XPSemu adds its own controller-friendly dashboard, per-game settings, cover art, play time, game patches, a performance overlay, a per-game log and a set of CPU optimizations made for the PS5's Zen 2 processor. ## Features **Setup** - Only your MCPX boot ROM and BIOS are needed: a blank Xbox hard disk is created for you if you have none. - A setup screen shows which files are missing and updates by itself as you copy them over. - Games from `/data/xemu/games/` or from `xemu/games/` on any USB or external drive. **Dashboard** - Xbox-style dashboard made for the DualSense: animated green background, main menu, recently played shelf. - **Games** page: a 3D row of game cases with box art, reflections, smooth scrolling and a launch animation. - **Box Art Viewer**: the full game case in 3D (front, back and spine) to turn, zoom and flip. - Game names from the ISO file name (rename any game from its settings); covers downloaded automatically, or your own in a folder (`.jpg` / `.png`). - **Recently played** shelf and **play time** per game. - **Original Xbox Dashboard**: boots the dashboard on your HDD image: the original Microsoft one, You will need to have it installed on the HDD. - Menu sounds and dashboard music (can be turned off), title shine animation, app icon and background art. - XPSemu startup logo and sound; the original Xbox startup animation can be turned on in Settings. - Settings in categories: Video, Sound, Interface, Controller, Patches, Advanced. **Per-game** - Own settings per game: screen shape, fit, volume, performance overlay. - **Game patches** in Jay's Magic Patch (`.jmp`) format, applied in memory while the game loads: your ISO files are never modified. - Automatic checksum matching: patches that are not made for your copy are blocked and labelled. - **Patch Store**: get patches for each game from Jay's Magic Patches, checked against your copy first; all active patches in Settings > Patches. - **Home-screen shortcuts**: any game as its own PS5 title, with its cover and 4K background art, opening straight into the game. - Crash watcher: if a game crashes back to the Xbox dashboard, XPSemu tells you and notes it in the log. **System** - Xbox video modes (widescreen, 720p) set per game automatically, in the emulated Xbox's EEPROM. - DualSense button remapping with a live tester. - Blades side art beside 4:3 games (optional). - Resolution scaling 1x (480p) to 4x, with the resolution shown next to each option. - Performance overlay (FPS, frame time, CPU, memory). - Per-game log (`xemu-game.log`) with FPS, frame times and what the emulator spends its time on. - Shader, pipeline and driver caches on disk, so a second run of a game stutters much less. ## Requirements - A **jailbroken PS5.** - **`helper.elf`**: included in the release. - **[ShadowMountPlus](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus)**. - **Your own** original Xbox files, dumped from your own console (not included, never will be): - MCPX boot ROM: `mcpx_1.0.bin` - Xbox BIOS / flash ROM: `Complex_4627.bin` - Optional: your own Xbox hard-disk image `xbox_hdd.qcow2`. Without one, XPSemu creates a blank one for you. - **Your own games** as **XISO** images (`.iso` / `.xiso`). Full "redump" disc images must be converted to XISO first (for example with [extract-xiso](https://github.com/XboxDev/extract-xiso)). ## Installation 1. Download PPSA97358.zip, extract it, and copy PPSA97358/ to /data/homebrew/. 2. Load helper.elf with kstuff. Put mcpx_1.0.bin and your BIOS Complex_4627.bin in/data/xemu/. 3. Put your games in /data/xemu/games/ or in xemu/games/ on a USB drive. 4. Launch XPSemu from the home screen If the app closes right away or says "helper.elf didn't answer", check that kstuff + `helper.elf` are loaded, then start XPSemu again. If a file is missing, XPSemu shows a setup screen listing what's needed. ## Folder layout on the PS5 Everything XPSemu writes lives under `/data/xemu/` (an app's own folder is read-only on the PS5). | Path | What it is | |---|---| | `/data/xemu/xemu.toml` | Main settings (xemu's format; the dashboard edits it for you). | | `/data/xemu/games/` | Your XISO games. | | `/data/xemu/games/covers/` or `/data/xemu/covers/` | Cover art: `.jpg` same as the iso name or the title ID (e.g. `4D530064.jpg`) works too, png also supported. | | `/data/xemu/patches/` | `.jmp` game patches (subfolders are fine). | | `/data/xemu/sounds/` | Optional: your own menu sounds (`move`, `change`, `select`, `back`, `open`, `launch`, `error` `.wav`) replace the built-in ones. | | `/data/xemu/game-settings/` | Per-game settings and patch choices (written by the dashboard). | | `/data/xemu/playtime.txt`, `recent.txt` | Play time and the recently played list. | | `/data/xemu/cache/` | Shader (SPIR-V), Vulkan pipeline and driver caches. Safe to delete; they rebuild. | | `/data/xemu/xemu.log` | The emulator's log (previous run: `xemu.log.old`). | | `/data/xemu/xemu-game.log` | Per-game log of the last game you played (previous: `.old`). | ## Controls **In games** (DualSense → Xbox controller) | DualSense | Xbox | |---|---| | ✕ / ○ / □ / △ | A / B / X / Y | | L1 / R1 | White / Black | | L2 / R2 | Left / Right trigger (analog) | | Left / right stick, L3 / R3 | Left / right stick, stick clicks | | D-pad | D-pad | | OPTIONS | Start | | Create | Back | | **Touchpad click** | Open the XPSemu dashboard (the PS button belongs to the system) | **In the dashboard** | Button | Action | |---|---| | D-pad / left stick | Move | | ✕ | Select / launch / change a value | | ○ | Back | | △ (on a game) | That game's settings and patches | | L1 / R1 (Games page) | Jump 5 games | | Touchpad | Return to the running game | ## Game patches XPSemu reads patches in **Jay's Magic Patch** format (`.jmp`, as published on [JayXbox PatchHub](https://www.jayxbox.com/Retail-Game-Modification/PatchHub.php)) from `/data/xemu/patches/`. Open a game's settings (△) → **Game patches** to turn patches on or off. - Patches are applied **in memory while the game reads its executable**. Your ISO is never changed. - XPSemu computes your copy's checksum and compares it with the patch: - **Works**: made for your copy, or made for another release but every searched code pattern was found exactly once in yours. - **Other version** / **Not in this game** / **Not supported**: blocked, with the reason shown. - Patches that **append** new code to the executable (`APPEND` records, such as Halo 2 HD) are not supported. - A notification confirms when a patch was really applied while the game loaded. ## Performance notes On the PS5 the **emulated Xbox CPU is the bottleneck**: the Xbox CPU thread is busy 85-97% of the time while the PS5 GPU is mostly idle. That is why raising the resolution does not lower FPS (use 3x/4x freely). Tips: - **DSP Off**, always. - Leave **CPU pinning** always on. - The first time you play a game it compiles shaders; the second run is much smoother (caches in `/data/xemu/cache`). ## Logs and reporting problems After playing, copy `/data/xemu/xemu-game.log` (and `xemu.log`) from the PS5. The game log has: - a header with the game, title ID, file, settings, caches and patches, - every 5 s: FPS, slowest frame, CPU load per emulator thread, GPU work, and time spent per step, When reporting a problem, include the game name, what happened, and both logs. ## Known limitations - **Alpha**: expect bugs. - **CPU-bound**: heavy scenes in some games run below their cap (see above). - **64 MB Xbox memory only** (no 128 MB debug-kit mode). - **XISO only**: full redump images must be converted. - **Patches with APPEND records** are not supported. - No save states or save manager yet (games save to the HDD image as on a real Xbox). ## What XPSemu changes in xemu XPSemu is based on xemu `0.8.136` (upstream commit `478b4f4961`). Everything below is in this repository. PS5-only code is guarded with `#ifdef __PROSPERO__`, so the desktop build of xemu is unchanged by most of it. A full diff of the modified upstream files is in [`ps5/XPSEMU-CHANGES.diff`](ps5/XPSEMU-CHANGES.diff). ### Making xemu run on the PS5 - **Cross-build for the PS5**: meson cross file (`ps5/ps5-cross.ini`), `ps5/configure-ps5.sh`, and `ps5/deps/build-deps.sh`, which cross-compiles xemu's libraries (zlib, libiconv, GLib, pixman, libsamplerate, SDL3, libpcap, curl, libslirp) as static libraries with the PS5 toolchain. - **Vulkan-only build**: OpenGL/epoxy made optional (`meson.build`, pgraph GL renderer and gloffscreen guarded), Vulkan enabled on the PS5's FreeBSD-based OS, the DSP56300 Rust JIT made optional with the interpreter as fallback. - **New Vulkan presentation for the UI** (`ui/xui/vk-present.cc`, `ui/xemu-texture.h`, `hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/vk/vk-ui.h`): xemu's UI normally needs an OpenGL window; on the PS5 it draws with Dear ImGui's Vulkan backend onto a 4K `VK_KHR_display` swapchain, sharing the device and queue with the NV2A renderer. Screenshots and thumbnails read back through Vulkan. - **Linking as a PS5 title** (`ps5/build-title.sh`): relinks xemu's objects with RADV, the payload SDK's libc++ and platform layer, the CRT and AGC stubs from PS5_Vulkan, then makes the signed `eboot.bin`, `param.json` and art for `PPSA97358`. - **Missing C library pieces** (`ps5/compat/`): user-space `getcontext`/`makecontext`/`swapcontext` for QEMU's coroutines, `ppoll`, `pipe2`, `closefrom`, `timegm`, `mkstemp`, `fnmatch` and other gaps, and a startup scan that reports any unresolved system import. - **Memory** (`ps5/compat/mmap.c`, `tcg/region.c`, `util/oslib-posix.c`): `mmap` mapped onto the PS5's flexible/direct memory, allocations kept out of the GPU's address window, the TCG JIT buffer in executable shared memory, coroutine stacks from the heap, file-mapping fallback to read-into-memory. - **Sandbox**: requests the app from `helper.elf` at startup; all data under `/data/xemu`. - **DualSense input** (`ui/xemu-input-ps5.c`) through libScePad, mapped to an Xbox controller. - **Audio** through SceAudioOut (`hw/xbox/mcpx/apu/monitor.c`). - **Crash handler and logging**: crash address, backtrace and load address in `xemu.log`, kernel notifications on fatal errors, hide the PS5 splash screen after the first frame. - **Startup behaviour**: Xbox starts powered off (`-S`), no auto-resume of the last game, 64 MB forced, `geteuid`/`getegid` wrapped so Mesa's shader cache works after helper.elf grants access. ### New features (XPSemu's own code) | File | What | |---|---| | `ui/xui/dashboard.cc/.hh` | The dashboard: pages, carousel, shelf, settings, patches UI, crash watcher. | | `ui/xui/xiso.cc/.hh` | Reads `default.xbe` from XISO/redump images: title, title ID, checksum. | | `ui/xui/game-profile.cc/.hh` | Per-game settings and play time. | | `ui/xui/game-patches.cc/.hh` | `.jmp` parser, checksum matching, in-memory patching (hook in `block/raw-format.c`). | | `ui/xui/game-log.cc/.hh` | The per-game log and cache saves. | | `ui/xui/ui-sounds.cc/.hh` | Menu sounds (built-in, embedded, or your own `.wav`). | | `hw/xbox/xemu-eeprom.h`, `hw/xbox/smbus_storage.c` | Xbox video switches in the EEPROM (with checksum). | | `hw/xbox/xemu-timing.h` | Stopwatches used by the game log. | | `ui/xemu-os-utils-ps5.c` | PS5 startup, helper.elf request, blank hard disk, crash handler, pinning. | | `config_spec.yml` | New settings: performance overlay, menu sounds, CPU pinning, shader cache. | | `xpsemu-tools/` | Standalone app-request payload (`helper.elf`) | ## Building from source The build runs on Linux (tested on WSL2 Ubuntu). You need the PS5 toolchain and RADV from **PS5_Vulkan** (by [Mihawk-99](https://github.com/mihawk-99)) first. 1. **PS5_Vulkan**: clone it to `~/ps5/PS5_Vulkan` and build its toolchain, RADV release archive and host tools following its documentation. XPSemu uses: - the payload SDK: `~/ps5/PS5_Vulkan/.deps/native/ps5-payload-sdk` - RADV: `~/ps5/PS5_Vulkan/.deps/native/radv-release/lib/libvulkan_radeon.ps5.a` - the title packager: `~/ps5/PS5_Vulkan/build/host/ps5-native-tool` Other locations can be passed with `PS5_VULKAN`, `PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK` and `RADV_ARCHIVE`. 2. **Build tools**: `meson`, `ninja`, `python3` (with `pyyaml`), `curl`, `git`; Python `Pillow` and `numpy` only to redraw the art. 3. **Dependencies** (downloads and cross-compiles into `ps5/deps/prefix`): ```sh ps5/deps/build-deps.sh compat zlib libiconv glib pixman libsamplerate sdl3 vulkan libpcap curl libslirp ``` 4. **Configure** (into `build-ps5/`): ```sh ps5/configure-ps5.sh ``` 5. **Compile**: ```sh ninja -C build-ps5 qemu-system-i386 ``` The very last step, xemu's desktop link, **fails on purpose** (duplicate `ppoll` and similar symbols): the PS5 title is linked by the next step instead. 6. **Make the PS5 title**: ```sh bash ps5/build-title.sh ``` The result is `dist/PPSA97358/` (`eboot.bin`, `sce_sys/`, ...). `build-ps5/title/llvm-pie.elf` keeps the symbols for reading crash addresses: ```sh llvm-addr2line -f -C -e build-ps5/title/llvm-pie.elf 0x ``` Art: `ps5/art/make-art.py` draws the icon and background sources (converted with PS5_Vulkan's `tools/prepare-assets.sh`); `ps5/art/make-banner.py` draws this README's banner. Menu sounds: `ps5/sounds/embed-sounds.py` turns `ps5/sounds/*.wav` into `ui/xui/ui-sounds-data.h`. ## Credits - **[xemu](https://github.com/xemu-project/xemu)** ([xemu.app](https://xemu.app)) and its contributors: the emulator this is built on. - **[QEMU](https://www.qemu.org/)** ([source](https://gitlab.com/qemu-project/qemu)): the machine emulation and the TCG JIT under xemu. - **[Mihawk-99](https://github.com/mihawk-99)'s [PS5_Vulkan](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Vulkan) / PS5_Mesa**: RADV ([Mesa](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa)'s open-source AMD Vulkan driver) running on the PS5, the toolchain integration and title packaging XPSemu links against. - **[ps5-payload-dev SDK](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk)** (as pinned by Mihawk-99's PS5_PayloadSDK): the open PS5 payload SDK. - **[PS5SX2](https://github.com/Swordpdf/PS5SX2)** by Swordpdf: reference for the app protocol, CPU core layout, JIT memory and DualSense reading on the PS5. - **[etaHEN](https://github.com/LightningMods/etaHEN)** (LightningMods), **[kstuff](https://github.com/EchoStretch/kstuff)** (EchoStretch, from [ps5-payload-dev/kstuff](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/kstuff)), **[ShadowMountPlus](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus)** (drakmor) and the PS5 scene for making homebrew apps possible. - **Jay's Magic Patch / [JayXbox PatchHub](https://www.jayxbox.com/Retail-Game-Modification/PatchHub.php)**: the patch format and the community's patches. - **[Dear ImGui](https://github.com/ocornut/imgui)**, **[SDL3](https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL)**, **[GLib](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/glib)**, **[glslang](https://github.com/KhronosGroup/glslang)**, **[Vulkan Memory Allocator](https://github.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/VulkanMemoryAllocator)** and the other libraries xemu uses. XPSemu's icon, background and banner are original artwork (a green "X" emblem); they are not the Xbox logo. ## License XPSemu is licensed under the **GNU General Public License v2**, like xemu and QEMU (see [`LICENSE`](LICENSE) and [`COPYING`](COPYING)). Third-party components keep their own licenses. XPSemu **does not include** any Microsoft BIOS, MCPX ROM, dashboard, game or other copyrighted Xbox content, and never will. Use your own legally dumped files and games.

latestRelease.name: XPSemu Alpha 2.1
latestRelease.body:
## XPSemu Update 2.1

**Up to 4 players**
- Every signed-in PS5 user's controller (or a guest's) now works in games. Before, only the first controller was seen.
- Players 2-4 are plugged in within 2 seconds of signing in, even during a game, and unplugged when they sign out.
- Only player 1 controls XPSemu's menus; the other controllers are for the games.

**Game language** (#10)
- New setting: Settings > Interface > Game language (English, Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Japanese, Korean, Chinese).
- Games that include that language now start in it. Before, every game started in English.

**Saves**
- Saves are no longer lost when you leave a game. XPSemu now lets the Xbox finish writing before it stops the game.
- Broken saves are repaired automatically. A save cut off while it was being made could stop a game from saving at all. 
- A backup of every change is kept in `/data/xemu/save-repair/`.
- While the game finishes saving, the Now Playing bar burns away, and you can keep using the menu.

**Fixes**
- Crash after 15-20 minutes in playing games like Ninja Gaiden Black (#7).
- Crash when a game makes lots of new shaders.
- The Xbox hard disk survives a crash or closing XPSemu from the PS5 home screen. Before, games could hang on loading until `xbox_hdd.qcow2` was deleted.
- Far fewer graphics pipelines built, so fewer hitches in effect-heavy scenes.
- No needless ~8 MB cache save every time you leave a game.

**Requirements**

- [kstuff](https://github.com/EchoStretch/kstuff-lite) +`helper.elf`
- [ShadowMountPlus](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus)
- Your own Xbox MCPX boot ROM, BIOS and XISO games (not included)

**Installation**

1. Download `PPSA97358.zip`, extract it, and copy `PPSA97358/` to `/data/homebrew/.`
2. Load `helper.elf` with kstuff.
3. Put `mcpx_1.0.bin`and your BIOS`Complex_4627.bin`in`/data/xemu/`.
4. Put your games in `/data/xemu/games/`or in`xemu/games/`on a USB drive.
5. Launch XPSemu from the home screen.

**Note:** to use your own hard disk (for example with the original Xbox dashboard), put it at`/data/xemu/xbox_hdd.qcow2` before starting XPSemu.

repos.readme:
YouTube Max’d

YouTube for jailbroken PS5s. Runs on the console—no companion PC or Google Cloud setup.


Full guide

**Official release · v1.5.0** — intended for **firmware 11.00 with ShadowMount+**. PS5 testing is still needed, including playback, sign-in, microphone, lighting and 4K/HDR performance. **New in v1.5.0:** [Feed controls and playback rescue](docs/FEED_AND_PLAYBACK_HEALTH.md), smoother remote/bookmark controls, and [update notifications](docs/UPDATE_NOTIFICATIONS.md). ## How YouTube Max’d stands out **Also included:** local voice search, Smart playlists, optional Auto Max quality adjustment, and matching red-to-white DualSense effects. Also includes Google sign-in, subscriptions, playlists, captions, SponsorBlock, DeArrow, and video/audio selection from **144p to 4K**, where available. **Highlights:** - **Phone remote:** scan a QR to search, control playback and manage your queue. - **Bug-report export:** review and download technical details without account data or video URLs. - **Transcript search & bookmarks:** find and save video moments. - **In-app picture-in-picture:** optional viewing while browsing in Afterglow; off by default. - **Voice controls:** pause, resume, seek and change playback options. - **Session builder:** fit unwatched videos into a chosen time budget. - **Local family profiles:** PIN, approved-channel and viewing-time controls. - **Party queue:** phone QR joining, suggestions, votes and host approval. [Phone remote & reports](docs/PHONE_REMOTE.md) · [Feature instructions and limits](docs/MAXD_NEXT.md) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md). Linked Google child-profile import remains research. ## Install on PS5 1. Download the **PS5 app ZIP** above. 2. Extract it and copy the complete **PPSA99991** folder to your ShadowMount+ app location, commonly `/data/homebrew/PPSA99991`. 3. Start your compatible ELF loader on **TCP 9021** or resident **Lapy** service, then launch **YouTube Max’d**. Keep all included files. [Full installation instructions](docs/APP_GUIDE.md#install-on-ps5). **Controls:** Cross selects/pauses · Circle goes back · Square searches · Hold L3 for voice search · R2 opens playback options. ## Help & documentation [Google sign-in](docs/GOOGLE_LOGIN.md) · [Build from source](docs/BUILD.md) · [Testing & limits](docs/APP_GUIDE.md#testing-and-current-limits) · [Report an issue](https://github.com/HandshakeHackin/youtube-maxd/issues) ## Credits and licenses Built on **[ProsperoTube](https://github.com/LedyBacer/ProsperoTube)** by **BlackBearReloaded and contributors**, and **[EVO Player](https://github.com/sainsaji/EVO-PLAYER-PS5)**. Their work provides the YouTube client and player foundation. [Full credits](docs/APP_GUIDE.md#credits-and-licenses) · [Third-party notices](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) · [GPL-3.0-or-later](LICENSE)
