latestRelease.body:
# YouTube Max’d 1.5.0

- **Your feed, your way:** mute title phrases and put locally followed channels first.
- **Playback rescue:** check playback health and try a lower quality or AVC format without losing your place.
- **Smoother phone remote:** better reconnect, timeouts, queue focus and protection against repeated taps.
- **Better bookmarks and menus:** cleaner names, fewer duplicates, clearer save errors and improved Back navigation.
- **Update notices:** background checks for new stable releases, with manual checks and a download QR in About.

App data is preserved. Picture-in-picture stays off by default.

**Install/update:** download **PPSA99991.zip**, close the app, extract it and replace the complete **PPSA99991** app folder in your ShadowMount+ location. Keep your separate app data folder. The source ZIP is for developers.

Intended for PS5 firmware 11.00 with ShadowMount+. Automated checks, PS5 cross-compilation and ZIP validation are recorded with the release; physical PS5 acceptance remains pending. This version adds update notifications, rather than automatic installation. Older builds need this update installed first.

Built on [ProsperoTube](https://github.com/LedyBacer/ProsperoTube) by BlackBearReloaded and contributors, and [EVO Player](https://github.com/sainsaji/EVO-PLAYER-PS5). Matching source, licenses and checksums are included.

repos.name: ProsperoThemes
repos.description: Theme manager for the PS5 home screen (homebrew app, FW 13.00): community themes, apply and restore, USB import
repos.readme:
# Prospero Themes

A theme manager for the PS5 home screen, as a native homebrew app (title ID `PPSA90210`). Tested on firmware
13.00.

- **Library:** browse your theme packs (`.p5theme`), look at the details (what the theme changes) and a fullscreen
  preview, apply one and restore the original look at any time. The theme the console shows now is marked "Applied"
  and leads the row; Triangle sorts the rest by name or by newest. When you combine parts of several themes, the
  row ends with "Save current look", which keeps that mix as a theme of its own in your library.
- **Themes:** download themes other people published at [themes.darkatek7.com](https://themes.darkatek7.com),
  sort them by top rated, most downloaded or new, and like the ones you enjoy. More themes load as you scroll down.
  Downloads queue up: press X on several themes and they download one after another. Themes already in your library carry
  an "In library" badge; when a creator publishes a new version, the card says "Update". A theme you liked shows a
  heart, and Triangle on it removes the like. The Search chip finds themes by name, author or description.
  Themes with AI-generated pictures carry an "AI" badge; the No AI chip hides them, and the System tab's "AI themes"
  row keeps them hidden for good.
- **Avatars:** profile pictures for the account that starts the app, made in the Avatar Creator on the store website or
  downloaded on the Avatars tab. They sit in the Library under your themes; see [Avatars](#avatars).
- **USB import:** packs on a USB drive (its root or a `prospero-themes` folder) are checked and copied into the
  library. Avatar files (`.p5avatar`) go to your avatars.
- **What a theme can change:** the home-screen background, including behind the system tiles (Game Library,
  Media Gallery, All Apps and the rest), the backgrounds behind app tiles, PS4 games included (only apps without their own image, or
  all apps), system icons (top bar, control center and power menu), the system tile icons, the UI sounds and the home music.
- **Volume:** the System tab sets how loud a theme's UI sounds (25 % to start) and its home music (10 % to start)
  play. The app writes them again at that volume, from 10 % to 100 %.
- **No console restart:** new icons and sounds show once the home screen restarts. After an apply or restore the
  app offers that (a changed profile picture too); it takes a few seconds and the app stays open. If the home screen does not come back steadily,
  the helper puts the previous files back. Under OnionHEN the app does not restart the home screen; the changes show after
  the next console restart.

## Requirements

- A PS5 with a running jailbreak chain, tested on firmware 13.00.
- [ShadowMountPlus](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus), which registers apps from `/data/homebrew/`.
- An ELF loader on port **9021** (elfldr). The app hands it **ThemeHelper**, a small payload of its own that
  writes the theme files. It listens only on `127.0.0.1` and only writes inside the theme asset folders.
- A network connection for the Themes and Avatars tabs.

## Install

Install it from the homebrew catalog ([homebrew.page](https://homebrew.page/), ProsperoStore), or by hand:

1. Download `PPSA90210.zip` from the [latest release](https://github.com/Darkatek7/ProsperoThemes/releases).
2. Extract it and copy the `PPSA90210` folder to `/data/homebrew/` on the console (FTP or USB).
3. ShadowMountPlus registers it, and Prospero Themes appears on the home screen.

Your library, backups and settings live in `/data/prospero-themes/`, so updating the app keeps them. A release with
a new ThemeHelper (01.000.032 is the latest) needs one console restart after the update, because a running payload cannot
be replaced; the app says so when it finds the old helper.

## Update in the app

When the store knows a newer release, the System tab's **App update** row shows its version. X asks "Update now"; the app
then downloads the release ZIP from the store (checked against the size and SHA-256 the store announced), checks every
file name in it, and replaces its own files in the folder it is installed in. The new version starts the next time you
open the app: close it and start it again.

- It needs [ShadowMountPlus](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus), or a folder install in one of the places
  ShadowMount scans (`/data/homebrew`, `/data/etaHEN/games`, `/mnt/ext0` and `/mnt/ext1`, `/mnt/usb0` to `/mnt/usb7`, each
  also with `/homebrew` or `/etaHEN/games`). The app asks ShadowMount where it is installed; without an answer it looks in
  those places for its own `param.json`, and refuses when it finds none or more than one.
- Writing goes through ThemeHelper, which also sets the file mode the console needs to start an app (0777). Your library,
  backups and settings are not touched, and files in the folder that the release does not contain stay.
- An app **installed as a disk image** cannot be changed in place: the app says so, and you update it by hand.
- A release that comes with a new ThemeHelper (the first release with in-app update is one) needs **one console restart** after the update, because a
  running payload cannot be replaced. If an older helper is still running when you press Update now, the app says "Restart
  the console once, then try the update again."
- Each file is written to a new `.tmp` file first and renamed over the old one, the program (`eboot.bin`) and its
  `param.json` last, so an update that stops half-way still starts the old version and can be run again.

## Controls

| Screen | Buttons |
|---|---|
| Every screen | L1 / R1 switch tab (Library, Themes, Avatars, USB Import, System). D-pad or left stick moves. Circle goes back to the Library. |
| Library | X opens the details. Square opens the fullscreen preview. Triangle changes the order. Options reloads the library. On the "Save current look" card at the end, X saves the mix. D-pad up reaches the Search chip beside "Your collection": X opens a keyboard, Options filters your themes by name, author and description (no network), X on the chip with a term shows all of them again, Down or Circle goes back. |
| Library, "Your avatars" row | Down from the themes reaches the row (the screen slides up); Left and Right move along it, Up or Circle goes back to the themes. X on an avatar asks "Set as profile picture"; X on Console picture asks to put back the picture the console had before. Triangle removes an avatar (it goes to the attic folder, not deleted). Options reloads the library. The avatar in use is marked "In use". Avatars from the store show the store's name. |
| Details | X applies the theme (it asks first). Square opens the preview. Circle goes back. |
| Apply dialog | D-pad chooses, X confirms, Circle cancels. |
| Preview | Behind the system tiles it shows the theme's real home background, in full resolution once it is decoded. X shows or hides the home overlay. Square plays the theme's music (its preview excerpt, or else the first 30 seconds of its home music). Circle goes back. |
| Themes | X on a theme asks "Download", "Download and apply" or "Cancel" (an update says "Update"); the second goes on to the same apply questions as the Details screen, and nothing is applied before you confirm there. Square previews the theme without adding it to your library (picture, home row, sounds; Square again plays its music, Circle comes back). Triangle likes, or removes your like. Options refreshes the list. D-pad up from the first row reaches the chips (the footer says "Search · Filters"): Left and Right move, X filters, Square changes the sort, Down goes back to the themes. X on Search opens a keyboard; Options searches, and X on the chip with a term shows every theme again. X on No AI hides or shows themes with AI pictures. |
| Avatars | Square changes the sort (Top rated, Most downloaded or New). X on an avatar asks "Download", "Download and set" or "Cancel"; avatars already in your library say "In library". Triangle likes, or removes your like. Options refreshes the list. D-pad up from the first row reaches the Search chip: X opens a keyboard, Options searches the store's avatars, X on the chip with a term shows every avatar again, Down goes back. Circle goes back to the Library. |
| USB Import | X imports themes, avatars and original system files from USB. |
| System | D-pad picks a row, X acts on it. On Sound volume and Music volume, Left and Right change the volume. On AI themes, X switches between Show and Hide. On App update, X asks to install a newer release (see "Update in the app"), or asks the store when none is known. |

Results and progress ("Applying theme…", "Download failed (404).") appear as a short message at the bottom of the
screen.

**Applying asks first.** A theme with an app background asks where that background goes: "Apps without their own
image" or "All apps" (Cancel is the third choice). The answer is also saved as the App backgrounds setting on the
System tab, where X switches between the two. Themes without an app background get "Apply theme" or "Cancel".

**Restore defaults** is the last row on the System tab. X opens a dialog that asks first. Cancel is selected at the
start, so choose "Restore defaults" and press X to go ahead. It puts every changed file back from the backups the
app made before the first change. When a backup is gone, tile icons come back from the firmware's own copy; any
other file the app can no longer find an original for is left as it is and named in the result. Applying a theme starts from the defaults too: whatever an earlier theme changed
and the new one does not cover goes back to its original first, so themes never stack.

**Originals from USB.** A file stays themed when the console no longer has its original, for example when a backup was
made from a theme's file (a factory reset does not reset the system files). If you have the original files of your
firmware, for example the app's own backups from before (`/data/prospero-themes/backup/original/`), copy them to a USB
drive under `prospero-themes/originals/`, in the same folders (`prospero-themes/originals/vsh_asset/...`), and run the
USB import. The app takes a file only when its size and SHA-256 are exactly those of your firmware's original (from the
bundled catalog); anything else is skipped and counted. An imported original replaces the backup (the old one is kept
under `backup/replaced/`), and Restore defaults then puts it back. The app does not provide these files.

**Room first.** Each file is written next to the old one as a `.tmp` file and then renamed over it, so its folder needs
room for the whole new file. Before an apply writes anything, the app checks the free space for every file it will
write; when it is short it stops with "not enough space for <file>: X MiB needed, Y MiB free. Nothing was written."
A `.tmp` left by an earlier write that failed is deleted first, and a write that fails deletes its own `.tmp`. When there is
no room for the `.tmp` but the new file has exactly the size of the old one (the icon container, themed or stock),
the app overwrites only the parts that differ in place, which needs no free space, and checks the result as always.

## Other firmware versions

Tested on 13.00, but nothing in the app is tied to it: before anything is written, every file a theme
replaces is compared with the console's own copy (same image size and texture format). What does not fit
this console is skipped and listed, never written. After a system update the app notices files the update
replaced and takes those as the new defaults, so Restore defaults never puts an old firmware's file back.
It then offers to apply your theme again. Before 13.00 the file with the system icons and sounds is about 100 MB; the
app holds files that large outside its own memory, so preparing the backups no longer runs out of memory (issue #13).

On another firmware, please send a report. The first time you open the System tab on a firmware this app has no
measurements for, it asks once ("Send report" or "Not now"; it does not ask again for that firmware). You can also
send one yourself: on the System tab, X on the Firmware report row offers "Save" or
"Save and send". It saves `/data/prospero-themes/reports/firmware-<version>.json` (and a copy on a connected USB
drive); "Save and send" also sends it to the store and shows a short code. It only reads, and describes the files
a theme can change (sizes, hashes, formats, the icon list). Open an issue on this repository with the code, or
attach the file; `ThemePackCreator/theme_pack.py catalog-from-report` turns it into a catalog for that firmware.

## Avatars

An avatar is a profile picture for the account that starts the app. Avatars are kept apart from themes: a theme never
brings one, and setting a picture leaves the home screen's look alone.

- **Making one:** the Avatar Creator on the store website ([themes.darkatek7.com](https://themes.darkatek7.com)) crops a
  picture to a square, shows it round the way the console shows it, and gives you a `.p5avatar` file or publishes it to
  the store.
- **Getting one:** the Avatars tab lists the avatars people published, as a grid sorted by top rated, most downloaded or
  new. X asks "Download" or "Download and set". You can also copy a `.p5avatar` file to a USB drive; USB import takes it
  like a theme.
- **Your avatars:** the Library's second row, "Your avatars", holds the avatars in your library, with the console's own
  picture first. The first time you set one, the app keeps the console's picture, so "Console picture" can put it back.
  The picture in use is marked "In use".
- **Restart:** the home screen shows a new picture after it restarts. The app offers that restart; under OnionHEN it
  offers only "Later", and the picture shows after the next console restart.
- **Likes:** on the Avatars tab, Triangle likes an avatar the same way as a theme, and a second press takes the like back.

## Making themes

- In the browser: the creator at [themes.darkatek7.com](https://themes.darkatek7.com) builds a pack from your
  images and can publish it to the community store.
- On the PC: [`ThemePackCreator/`](ThemePackCreator/README.md) builds packs from the command line, including the
  icon, sound and video layers.

The pack format is described in [`Shared/README.md`](Shared/README.md).

## Repository

| Folder | What it is |
|---|---|
| [`ThemeApp/`](ThemeApp/README.md) | The app: UI, library, apply/restore, community store client, build and release scripts. |
| [`ThemeHelper/`](ThemeHelper/README.md) | The file helper payload the app loads through elfldr. |
| [`Shared/`](Shared/README.md) | The `.p5theme` reader and validator, shared by the app and the tests. |
| [`Shared.Tests/`](Shared.Tests/README.md) | PC unit tests. |
| [`ThemeApp.Preview/`](ThemeApp.Preview/README.md) | Runs the app's UI on the PC in a browser window. |
| [`ThemePackCreator/`](ThemePackCreator/README.md), [`ZstdWrap/`](ZstdWrap/README.md) | PC tools that build packs and handle the console's `.dds.zst` textures. |
| `catalog/`, `docs/` | The measured asset catalog and screen list for firmware 13.00. |

Some developer notes in these READMEs mention DevProbe and other research payloads from the author's private
research repository. They are not part of this repository, and neither building nor using the app needs them.

## Building

You need:
- .NET 10, PowerShell 7 and Python 3 (for the PC tools);
- the [SharpProspero](https://github.com/SvenGDK/SharpProspero) SDK, with `SHARPPROSPERO_ROOT` pointing at it.
  Until [SvenGDK/SharpProspero#6](https://github.com/SvenGDK/SharpProspero/pull/6) is merged, use that
  branch: without it the theme helper payload does not start on firmware 13.40 and later;
- a PS5-format `libc.prx` from a game package in `third_party/modules/` (not included here).

```powershell
$env:SHARPPROSPERO_ROOT = '<path to SharpProspero>'
pwsh -File ThemeApp/build.ps1 -Output Folder         # the app folder in ThemeApp/out/module
pwsh -File ThemeApp/package-release.ps1              # dist/PPSA90210.zip and the catalog record
cd Shared.Tests; dotnet test                         # PC tests
```

`python ThemeApp/deploy-shadowmount.py --deploy --ip <console-ip>` uploads a build over FTP and asks
ShadowMountPlus to register it.

## Privacy

The Themes and Avatars tabs talk only to the store address set on the System tab (default
`https://themes.darkatek7.com`). Likes of themes and of avatars are counted once per console through a random ID that
the app creates on first start (`/data/prospero-themes/settings.json`); each like sends that ID to the store. The ID is
anonymous and not linked to your account. The console also keeps its own lists of what it liked, in
`/data/prospero-themes/likes.json` (themes) and `/data/prospero-themes/avatar-likes.json` (avatars), so the hearts show
again after a restart. Those lists stay on the console.

On start the app asks the store for the number of the newest release, to say when an update is out; nothing is
sent with that question. A firmware report goes to the store only when you choose "Save and send".

## License

GPL-3.0, like the SharpProspero SDK it is built with. The Inter font is under the SIL Open Font License
(`ThemeApp/assets/fonts/OFL.txt`).

`Shared/Atrac9Codec.cs` and `Shared/Atrac9Tables.cs` (the home music volume and the music in the preview) are a C# port of the ATRAC9 encoder by
[Blaze414](https://github.com/Blaze414/ps5-theme), GPL-3.0-or-later, which in turn follows the MIT-licensed
[LibAtrac9](https://github.com/Thealexbarney/LibAtrac9) by Alex Barney.

The release ZIP contains a `libc.prx`, the system library every SharpProspero app has to carry, because the app
does not start without it. That file is Sony's and is not covered by this repository's license.

## Credits

- [SharpProspero](https://github.com/SvenGDK/SharpProspero) by SvenGDK: the SDK this app is built with.
- [ShadowMountPlus](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus) by drakmor: app registration.
- [Inter](https://github.com/rsms/inter) by Rasmus Andersson: the UI font.

repos.name: pscord
repos.description: PSCord: a native Discord client for the jailbroken PS5. Downloads: desstannsoftware.com
repos.readme:
# PSCord for PS5 A native Discord client for the jailbroken PS5. It is a standalone homebrew app, drawn with OpenGL and built around the controller. **Downloads:** [desstannsoftware.com](https://desstannsoftware.com/#pscord) · **Source / PRs:** this repository · **Chat:** [Desstann Homebrew Discord](https://discord.gg/wfTch3qUa6) > PSCord is unofficial and is not affiliated with Discord Inc. Discord's terms do not allow third-party clients, so use it at your own risk.

## Features - **Servers and DMs**: server rail, channels with unread and mention badges, member list with role colours, direct messages. - **Messages drawn like the desktop client**: markdown, mentions, replies, reactions, embeds, GIFs, stickers, custom emoji, attachments and avatars. - **Write messages** with an on-screen keyboard (Square). - **Voice channels**: join a call, hear everyone and talk with a headset mic. Call screen with a tile per person and speaking and muted marks, R2 to mute, Triangle to leave. Discord's end-to-end encrypted (DAVE) calls are supported. - **Sign in from your phone**: scan the QR code with the Discord mobile app. The token stays on the console. - **Built-in unblock**: works around DNS and SNI-based Discord blocking inside the app (split TLS handshake, unfiltered DNS). No proxy and no system changes on the console. - **Self-updating**: on launch it checks for a new version, verifies the download with SHA-256 and restarts into the new version. - **Coming back to a call**: if the console suspended PSCord, it rejoins the voice channel when Discord reconnects, and mentions and direct messages raise a system notification. - **Community**: every few launches, and from Settings, PSCord offers [Desstann Homebrew](https://discord.gg/wfTch3qUa6). ## Roadmap Checklist of work still ahead. PRs that move any of these forward are welcome. ### Background voice - [ ] Stable background audio via process-local PartyDaemon inject (replace fragile ptrace-per-grain pumping) - [ ] Idle silence, pump re-inject on PartyDaemon restart, and clear “in call in the background” UI state ### Game streaming - [ ] Watch Discord Go Live / Activity streams (video decode + overlay) - [ ] Share the PS5 screen to Discord Go Live (capture → encode → gateway) ### Security - [ ] Protect the on-console session token (encrypt `session.txt` or equivalent) - [ ] Harden LAN web login (`:8090`) with TLS or a one-time code instead of cleartext token handoff ### Voice UX - [ ] Deafen, server mute, push-to-talk / headset routing, and stage channels ### Chat and media - [ ] Edit and delete messages, file upload, threads, slash commands / sticker picker - [ ] Play video attachments; improve GIF and large-embed performance ### Project hygiene - [ ] Publish a CI ccache snapshot; keep the public repo in sync with the private app tree - [ ] Keep this roadmap and `docs/PARTY_DAEMON_BG_VOICE.md` accurate as background voice lands ## Screenshots

These are rendered from the app's own interface code with sample data (made-up users and messages). The interface is available in English and Turkish, switchable in the settings. ## Install 1. Download `PPSA99190.zip` from [desstannsoftware.com](https://desstannsoftware.com/#pscord) or from a [GitHub Release](https://github.com/desstannsoftware/pscord/releases). 2. Extract it and copy the `PPSA99190` folder to `/data/homebrew/`. 3. **PSCord** appears on the home screen, like the other apps in that folder. ## Contributing (PRs welcome) Pull requests are welcome. **You do not need a local PS5 toolchain.** GitHub Actions builds every PR and push to `main`: 1. Fork and open a PR against `main`. 2. Wait for the **Build** check (lint, host tests, packaged `PPSA99190.zip`). 3. Download the Actions artifact (`pscord-PR…`) to try the build on a console if you can. Details: [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) and [docs/PULL_REQUEST_BUILDS.md](docs/PULL_REQUEST_BUILDS.md). A version tag matching `sce_sys/param.json` `contentVersion` (`NN.NNN.NNN`) publishes a GitHub Release from CI. OTA upload to desstannsoftware.com is maintainer-only. ## Licence GPL-3.0-or-later (see [LICENSE](LICENSE) and [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md)). Built on [ps5-homebrew-ui](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-homebrew-ui) and [ps5-native-app-boilerplate](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-native-app-boilerplate). ## Support Questions and bug reports: [Desstann Homebrew Discord](https://discord.gg/wfTch3qUa6) or [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/desstannsoftware/pscord/issues). PSCord is free. If it is useful, you can [buy me a coffee](https://buymeacoffee.com/desstann).

repos.name: PS5_ArtSwap
repos.description: Change any PS5 title's home-screen icon and background with art from SteamGridDB, and refresh the home screen through ShadowMountPlus
repos.readme:
# Art Swap

[![stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/griches/PS5_ArtSwap?style=flat)](https://github.com/griches/PS5_ArtSwap/stargazers)
[![release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/griches/PS5_ArtSwap)](https://github.com/griches/PS5_ArtSwap/releases/latest)
[![licence](https://img.shields.io/badge/licence-GPL--3.0--or--later-blue)](LICENSE)

**Change the icon, background, logo and music of any title on your PS5's home
screen, with art from [SteamGridDB](https://www.steamgriddb.com), pictures and
songs of your own, and arrange the home screen itself.**

Art Swap lists every title on the console that has home-screen art, finds each
one on SteamGridDB, shows you that game's art, and writes the one you pick over
the title's own `icon0` or `pic0`/`pic1`. The original is kept beside it as an
`.old` file, so Restore can put it back. **Apply changes** (R2) then restarts
the home screen, and every change shows at once, whatever installed the game:
a folder, a disk image or a package. A **logo** (□) goes on the game's page in
place of its name in plain text, and shows straight away. Pictures of your own,
sent from a phone or computer, sit first in every tab, and the **Home screen**
page moves tiles between the Games and Media homes, hides them, and locks the
order of your games.

Title `PPSA99318`, version 1.4.0. Tested on a PS5 with firmware 13.60.

## What it does

- **Lists your titles**: PS5 and PS4 games from the home screen's own art folder
  (`/user/appmeta`, including `external/`), and homebrew from `/data/homebrew` and
  the `homebrew` folders on USB and extended storage. Each one shows its art as
  it is now and what form that art takes (for example "Icon PNG 512×512, 2 files ·
  Background DDS BC7 3840×2160, 4 files").
- **Finds the game on SteamGridDB** by its name, and remembers the match. If the
  match is wrong, □ in the picker lists other matches or searches for any name you type.
- **Icons** come from SteamGridDB's square grids, and **Backgrounds** from its
  heroes (art made for backgrounds). A PS5 background is 3840×2160, so the
  3840×1240 heroes are listed first and tagged 4K: a 1920×620 one is enlarged
  about 3.5 times to fill it, and the frame page says so.
- **Adds a background** to homebrew that has none (△, "Add background"), when
  ShadowMountPlus installed it from a folder: Art Swap writes `pic0.dds`
  (3840×2160 BC7, as the console writes its own) into the game's `sce_sys`,
  and Apply changes installs the game again, since the home screen takes a
  background in only at an install (its saved data and download data kept:
  see [Installing a game again](#installing-a-game-again)). There is no
  original, so Restore deletes it (the files are listed in
  `/data/artswap/added.txt`).
- **You choose the part kept** (△ in the picker opens the frame page): Fit (all
  of it, on a blurred fill of itself), the left, centre or right of a wide
  picture (top, middle or bottom of a tall one), or a part of your own: the
  left stick or D-pad moves it, L2 and R2 zoom out and in (up to 3×). The page
  shows the whole picture with the part kept lit, and the result beside it.
- **The preview is exact**: what you see under NEW is what the helper will
  write, beside the art there NOW.
- **Writes what the console expects**: each file keeps its format, size,
  channels and DDS layout (PNG, JPEG, or DDS in BC7, BC1, BC3 or RGBA, with the
  same header and number of levels). Every copy is changed together: the home
  screen's copy in `/user/appmeta` and, for homebrew, the one in the title's own
  `sce_sys`. A background changes `pic0` and `pic1` together.
- **Keeps the originals**: before a file is changed the first time, Art Swap
  copies it beside itself as `<name>.old` (`icon0.png.old`, `pic0.dds.old`). Later
  changes never touch an `.old` file, so it is always the art the title came
  with. Restore moves every `.old` file back over its original.
- **Applies changes** (R2): the home screen keeps its own copy of each game's
  art, so it restarts to show new art, every game's at once. Only the home
  screen restarts: see [Apply changes](#apply-changes). The top of the screen
  says how many games are waiting, and a changed game's page says it is not
  on the home screen yet.
- **Logos** (□): a game's page on the home screen shows its logo where it has
  one and its name in plain text where it has not, as with homebrew and
  installed backups. Art Swap puts a logo from SteamGridDB there, and it shows
  at once: see [Logos](#logos). Store games can also be offered their own
  logo from PlayStation Store, when you turn that on in Settings.
- **Music** (OPTIONS, Music): the tune a tile plays while it is selected. Send
  songs from your phone or copy them over FTP, choose the clip to keep, hear it
  as the home screen will, and Art Swap makes the `snd0.at9` on the console:
  see [Music](#music).
- **Your own pictures**: icons, backgrounds and logos sent from a phone or a
  computer (the first cell of the picker shows a QR code), or copied into
  `/data/artswap/pictures`, come first in every tab, for every game, and need
  no SteamGridDB key: see [Your own pictures](#your-own-pictures).
- **Arranges the home screen** (OPTIONS, Home screen): any tile on the Games
  home or the Media home, or hidden from both, and the Games row in an order
  of your own, locked if you like, so playing a game no longer moves it first:
  see [The home screen's layout](#the-home-screens-layout).
- **Renames homebrew** (OPTIONS, Rename) that ShadowMountPlus installed from a folder: the
  new name goes into the title's `param.json` (every language) and, at Apply
  changes, into the home screen's database, which holds the names it shows. No
  install, so nothing of the game is touched: see [Renaming](#renaming). The
  original is kept as `param.json.old`, and Restore puts it back too.

## Installing

You need the console's homebrew environment running: etaHEN (or kstuff),
ShadowMountPlus, and an **ELF loader on port 9021**. Art Swap starts its helper
through that loader.

1. Download `PS5_ArtSwap-v1.3.1.zip` from [Releases](https://github.com/griches/PS5_ArtSwap/releases/latest).
2. Copy the `PPSA99318` folder inside it to `/data/homebrew/` (FTP is fine).
3. ShadowMountPlus registers it and Art Swap appears on the home screen.
4. Start it. The first screen says "Starting the helper" for a moment.
5. Add your SteamGridDB API key when it asks (see [below](#the-steamgriddb-api-key)).

## Using it

Face buttons change the focused game's art, the shoulder buttons come in left
and right pairs, and the rest is in the OPTIONS menu, as on the console's own
game pages. Every hint row lists the buttons in the same order: moving, ✕ △ □,
L1 R1 L2 R2, OPTIONS, then ○.

| Where | Button | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Games | ← → (L1 R1 by six) | choose a game |
| | ✕ | change its icon |
| | △ | change its background, or add one to homebrew ShadowMountPlus installed from a folder |
| | □ | change the logo on its page (a game the home screen lists) |
| | L2 | the order of the games: the home screen's own (most recently used first, to begin with), A to Z, or the games Art Swap changed first; kept for next time, and the shelf starts again at its first game |
| | R2 | apply changes: restart the home screen so it shows them all (asks first) |
| | OPTIONS | Music, Rename (homebrew ShadowMountPlus installed from a folder), Restore originals, Home screen, Settings, Close Art Swap |
| | hold OPTIONS | close Art Swap |
| Pictures | L1 R1 | the Icons, Backgrounds and Logos tabs |
| | D-pad, left stick | choose a picture |
| | right stick | slide the part kept, when Fill cuts the picture |
| | ✕ | use it (asks first); on the first cell, send pictures of your own from a phone or computer (a QR code) |
| | △ | the frame page: which part of the picture is kept (not for a logo, which is used whole) |
| | □ | another game, or search by name with the keyboard (with no SteamGridDB key: add one) |
| | OPTIONS | on a picture of your own: delete it from the console (asks first) |
| | ○ | back to the games |
| Frame | left stick, D-pad | move the part kept |
| | ✕ | use it (asks first) |
| | L1 R1 | Fit, Left, Centre, Right (or Top, Middle, Bottom), Custom |
| | L2 R2 | zoom out, zoom in |
| | ○ | back to the pictures |
| Music | ↑ ↓ | choose a song |
| | ← → | move the clip's starting position a second |
| | ✕ | use the clip as the game's music (asks first) |
| | △ | play the clip as the home screen will, or stop it |
| | □ | send songs from your phone (a QR code) |
| | L1 R1 | move the starting position ten seconds |
| | L2 R2 | make the clip five seconds shorter, longer |
| | ○ | back to the games |
| Home screen | L1 R1, D-pad | Games, Media, Hidden, Order, and the tiles in one |
| | ✕ | move the tile: Games, Media or Hidden; on Order, lock the order or sort A to Z |
| | □ | on Games, pick a game up; ↑ ↓ carry it along the row, ✕ puts it down, ○ puts it back |
| | R2 | apply changes |
| | ○ | back |
| Settings | L1 R1, D-pad | the categories, and the rows in one |
| | ✕ | select |
| | ○ | back |

## Apply changes

The home screen draws each game's tile and background from its own copies of
the art (`/user/appmeta/<id>`, and `/user/app/<id>/sce_sys` for a game
ShadowMountPlus installed), and it keeps what it has drawn. Art Swap writes all
of those copies, as well as a homebrew folder's own `sce_sys`. To show them,
the home screen restarts: R2 opens a pop-up that says what will happen, and ✕
starts it.

1. Art Swap tells the helper, then closes.
2. Once Art Swap's process has ended, the helper ends the home screen's
   process (`SceShellUI`). The system starts it again within a few seconds.
3. The new home screen reads every game's art again, so every change shows,
   whatever installed the game.

Nothing else restarts: a game open in the background carries on, saved data is
not touched, and payloads such as ShadowMountPlus keep running (there is no
loader to run again). The helper keeps the titles changed since the last
restart in `/data/artswap/pending.txt`. A console restart is not needed.

A name is different: the home screen shows the names its database holds,
which an install writes, so a restart alone does not show a new one. Apply
changes writes a renamed game's new name there first: see
[Renaming](#renaming). A background or music Art Swap added to a game that had
none shows only after an install, so Apply changes installs that game again
first: see [Installing a game again](#installing-a-game-again).

## Renaming

Rename (OPTIONS) on homebrew that ShadowMountPlus installed from a folder asks
for the new name and writes it as `titleName`, in every language, into each
`param.json` the title has: its folder's, the home screen's copy in
`/user/appmeta/<id>` and the install's in `/user/app/<id>/sce_sys`. Each
original is kept once as `param.json.old`.

Apply changes then writes the name into the home screen's database
(`/system_data/priv/mms/app.db`), everywhere the title's install wrote it:
`titleName` and the `TITLE` names in `AppInfoJson` (`tbl_contentinfo`), the
concept's `conceptName` and `concept_name` fields in `ConceptInfoJson`
(`tbl_conceptmetadata`), and each user's `tbl_iconinfo_<user>` and
`tbl_concepticoninfo_<user>`. That JSON is edited as text: only the names and
their lengths change, everything else byte for byte. The database is copied
aside first (`/data/artswap/app.db.backup`). The restart shows the new name,
and it stays through a console restart. Nothing of the game is installed again
or touched. Restore puts the original name back the same way.

A rename needs **ShadowMountPlus 1.7 or later**, running, and a title it
installed **from a folder**: the name goes into the folder's `param.json` too,
so a later install by ShadowMountPlus keeps it. A package's or a disk image's
own `param.json` cannot be changed.

Art Swap 1.3.0 had ShadowMountPlus install a renamed game again instead. The
console's uninstall deletes the game's download data
(`/user/download/<id>/download0.dat`, the game's `/download0`), and some
homebrew keeps its saves there, so 1.3.1 renames without an install.

## Installing a game again

A background or music Art Swap added to homebrew that had none shows only after
an install: Apply changes has ShadowMountPlus install that game again, which
deleting the title and letting ShadowMountPlus add it back would also do.

1. Art Swap notes every file in the game's folder (each one's path and size)
   and copies aside the console's saved data of the title (every user's
   `savedata_prospero/<id>` and `savedata/<id>`) and Art Swap's originals in the
   home screen's copy, to `/data/artswap/saves/<id>-<time>/`. If it cannot read
   the whole folder or make the whole copy, it stops and changes nothing.
2. It moves the game's download data (`/user/download/<id>`), which the
   console's uninstall deletes, aside to `/user/download/<id>.artswap`: the
   same disk, so nothing is copied. If it cannot, it stops and changes nothing.
3. Art Swap closes: ShadowMountPlus will not take a title away while any game
   is open. The helper carries on from the home screen.
4. The helper asks ShadowMountPlus (its API on 127.0.0.1:10101) to uninstall the
   title. That removes only the home screen's entry; the game's folder, with
   its own saves and settings, stays where it is. A scan then adds the title
   back with its new art, and the helper waits until the install has finished.
5. The helper moves the download data back, before anything can start the
   game, checks every file of the folder against its notes, and puts back any
   saved data or original that went missing. The next time Art Swap starts it
   says if anything went wrong.

Nothing is deleted. If the game's folder had changed, Art Swap says so rather
than calling the install done (the folder itself is not copied: the uninstall
never touches it). The copy from the last install that went well is kept for
each title, and the copy from any that did not. If the helper ends while the
download data is aside, it moves it back when it next starts
(`/data/artswap/download-aside.txt` names it until then).

## Logos

A game's page on the home screen (the tile selected, with Play Game under it)
shows the game's logo, or else its name in plain text. The home screen draws
the picture its database names for the title (`logoImageInfo` in
`/system_data/priv/mms/app.db`). Store games get theirs from PlayStation
Network, which a jailbroken console does not reach, and homebrew has none.

□, or the Logos tab of the picker, lists SteamGridDB's logos for the game
(transparent PNGs, mostly white lettering), each on a dark plate, with the
page as it will look beside the logo there now. ✕ puts it on:

1. The helper writes the PNG as `logo.png` beside the title's art in
   `/user/appmeta/<id>` (the home screen cannot read the homebrew folders), and
   keeps its own copy in `/data/artswap/logos/`.
2. It points the title's `logoImageInfo` at it, editing the database in place
   with SQLite, which waits for the home screen's own locks. It is the only
   thing Art Swap changes there. Before its first change the database is
   copied to `/data/artswap/app.db.first`, and before each run's first change
   to `app.db.backup`.
3. The page shows it straight away: Apply changes is not needed.

A logo stays through a console restart. An install writes the title's entry
afresh and takes the logo away, so after an install (Apply changes, for an
added background or music) the helper waits for the entry to come back and puts the logo back, and each
time Art Swap starts it puts back any of its logos that went missing. Restore
takes the logo off and puts back what the page had before (most often
nothing). A title the home screen does not list has no page, so no logo.

Art Swap has a logo of its own, built into the helper: the first time Art Swap
starts and finds its page with no logo, it puts its own there, and from then
on it is a logo like any other. Choose another in the Logos tab, or Restore
it to have the name back for good. A page that already has a logo is left
as it is.

**PlayStation Store logos** (Settings, Games; off until you turn them on): for
a store game (one whose store concept is not just its own number, as
homebrew's is), the Logos tab starts with the game's own logo from
PlayStation Store's public catalog. The helper asks it as a web browser would,
with no account, key, cookie or anything that says Art Swap or PS5, but Sony
still sees the console's address and which game, so it is your choice. Each
game is asked about once; the answer is kept in `/data/artswap/store/`. Most
jailbroken consoles are kept from Sony's servers, to stop updates: on those
the store cannot be reached, the Logos tab says so once a run, and
SteamGridDB's logos show as before (it has the official logo of most store
games too). Settings says this under the switch.

## Music

A title can carry `sce_sys/snd0.at9`, music the home screen loops while its
tile is selected. Art Swap makes one from a song of yours, on the console:

1. **Songs.** OPTIONS, then Music, lists the MP3, FLAC, WAV and AIFF files in
   `/data/artswap/music`. □ shows a QR code: the phone's page sends the songs
   chosen on it straight into that folder, and they appear as they arrive.
   Copying files there over FTP works too. Use music that is yours to use.
2. **The clip.** The page shows how loud the song is along its length and the
   part kept, lit: ← → move its start a second at a time, L1 R1 ten seconds,
   L2 R2 make it five seconds shorter or longer, up to about 87 seconds (the
   2 MiB the home screen allows). △ plays it as the home screen will.
3. **The file.** ✕ has the helper decode the song (minimp3, dr_flac, dr_wav),
   make the clip stereo at 48 kHz, bring it to -28 LUFS with its true peak
   under -2 dBTP, fade both ends so the loop does not click, and encode it as
   ATRAC9 at 192 kb/s with a whole-track loop, as BlackBearReloaded's
   [ps5-at9-converter](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-at9-converter)
   does (its encoder ported to C, `helper/src/at9.c`). `pubtools.loudnessSnd0`
   goes into each `param.json` beside it.

A title that has music gets the new file over each copy of its own, the
original kept as `snd0.at9.old` for Restore, and Apply changes restarts the
home screen. A title with none has nothing for the home screen to play until
an install registers one, so, for homebrew ShadowMountPlus installed from a
folder, Art Swap adds `snd0.at9` to the game's `sce_sys` and Apply changes
installs it again, as for a background it never had; Restore deletes it.

## Your own pictures

The picker's first cell, in every tab, sends pictures of your own: ✕ shows a
QR code, the console's address and a four-digit code. A phone, or a computer
on the same network, opens a small page served by the helper (on port 9118,
as for the key and music), and the pictures chosen on it go straight into
`/data/artswap/pictures`; the sheet ticks each one off as it arrives. PNG and
JPEG go as they are; anything else the browser can show (WebP, HEIC on an
iPhone) is turned into a PNG on the phone first. Copying files into the folder
over FTP works too.

They come first in the Icons, Backgrounds and Logos tabs, tagged YOURS, newest
first, for every game, and go through the same frame page and preview as
SteamGridDB's art. A logo wants a PNG with a see-through background: the page
says when a picture has none. Without a SteamGridDB key the picker opens all
the same, with your own pictures, and □ adds a key. Use pictures that are
yours to use.

To delete one, choose it in the picker and press OPTIONS: it leaves
`/data/artswap/pictures`, so it is gone from every tab, for every game. A game
already using it keeps it.

## The home screen's layout

OPTIONS, then Home screen, shows the home screen's tiles as the console lists
them: on the **Games** home, on the **Media** home beside it, or **Hidden**
from both. ✕ on a tile moves it; tools, players and stores sit well on Media,
out of the way of your games. Art Swap itself can move to Media, but not be
hidden, as there would be no way back to it. The system's own tiles
(PlayStation Store, Game Library) can move or hide too.

**Order** locks the Games row: the home screen puts the game played last
first, and a locked row stays as it is. □ on a game on the Games page picks it
up, ↑ ↓ carry it along the row, and ✕ puts it down; Order can also sort the
games A to Z. Without the lock, the order you set holds until you next play a
game.

Nothing changes until **Apply changes** (R2), which writes the layout into the
home screen's database just before the home screen restarts. Art Swap keeps
what you chose (`/data/artswap/layout.txt`) and writes it again at each Apply
changes, so an install or a firmware update that put a tile back is put
right the next time. The database is copied aside first, as for a rename.

This follows elripalda's [psgfx](https://github.com/elripalda/psgfx), whose
Home layout found which fields the home screen reads: each tile's
`dispLocation` (Games or Media) and `visible`, the system tiles' places in the
`MyHome` group, and the dates and counters the Games row is sorted by.

## The SteamGridDB API key

SteamGridDB's API needs a key, and each person registers their own: it is free,
and SteamGridDB's terms do not cover sharing one. No key is built into Art Swap.

When Art Swap has no key it says so: on the first start, in the picker (which
still has your own pictures; □ there adds a key), and at the top of the
screen. It explains what the key is and how
to get one (steamgriddb.com, sign in, Preferences, API), and offers two ways to
add it:

- **From your phone**: the TV shows a QR code, the console's address and a
  four-digit code. The phone opens a small page served by the helper on port
  9118, takes the key, checks it with SteamGridDB and saves it; the TV notices
  and carries on. The page exists only while that screen is open (ten minutes
  at most), needs the code, and closes after ten wrong codes.
- **With the console's keyboard**.

Settings (OPTIONS, then Settings) shows whether a key is in, with its last four characters,
and can add, replace or remove it, refresh the game list, or show the helper's
log. The key is kept in `/data/artswap/apikey.txt`, which can also be copied
over FTP. Without a key, Art Swap still lists your games and restores original
art.

## How it works

A title runs in a sandbox and sees only its own folder, so it cannot read or
write `/user/appmeta`. Art Swap is therefore two programs:

```text
  Art Swap (the title, PPSA99318)           artswapd (the helper payload)
  the screens, drawn with the UI kit  <-->  reads and writes the art, talks to
  helper_client: 4 connections,      TCP    SteamGridDB, makes the pictures
  answers on the drawing thread   127.0.0.1:9117
          |
          '-- at start, if no helper answers: artswapd.elf --> ELF loader (127.0.0.1:9021)
```

The title carries the helper (`artswapd.elf` in its folder) and hands it to the
ELF loader when no helper answers. A helper of another version is asked to
leave and replaced. The helper leaves by itself 90 seconds after Art Swap
closes. It answers only on 127.0.0.1 (port 9117, or 9127 or 9137 when a helper
that crashed still holds one), apart from the key page above while it is open. Its requests are in
[`helper/protocol.md`](helper/protocol.md).

On the console the helper keeps its files in `/data/artswap/`:

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `helper.log` | what the helper did, each start (also in Settings, "Helper log") |
| `scan.txt` | every title found, and each art file with its format and size |
| `appmeta-files.txt` | every file in each title's `/user/appmeta` folder |
| `matches.tsv` | the SteamGridDB game chosen for each title |
| `pending.txt` | the titles changed since the home screen last restarted |
| `home.txt` | how the last Apply changes ended |
| `refresh.txt` | how the last install again ended |
| `saves/` | what each install again copied aside (see above) |
| `download-aside.txt` | a game whose download data is aside during an install, until it is back |
| `apikey.txt` | your SteamGridDB API key |
| `cache/` | downloaded pictures (trimmed to 192 MB when over 256 MB) |
| `logos/` | the logo Art Swap put on each title's page (`<id>.png`), and what it replaced (`<id>.orig`) |
| `added.txt` | the background and music files Art Swap added to titles that had none |
| `music/` | your songs, sent from a phone or copied over FTP |
| `app.db.first`, `app.db.backup` | the home screen's database before Art Swap first changed it, and before its last run's first change |
| `store-logos` | if present, PlayStation Store logos are on |
| `prefs.txt` | Art Swap's own choices, such as the order of the games |
| `store/` | what PlayStation Store's catalog said about each store game's logo |
| `no-appdb` | if present, the system's `app.db` is never read (no names from it, no logos) |

Names come from the title's `param.json` or `param.sfo`, then from a read-only
copy of the system's `app.db`, and otherwise the title id is shown. The same
copy says which titles the home screen lists and which are store games.

## Tested on the console

On a PS5 with firmware 13.60, ShadowMountPlus 1.7beta3: the title reaches the
helper on 127.0.0.1 and starts it through the ELF loader; the scan (20 titles
in 40-240 ms; `/user/appmeta/<id>/` holds `icon0.png`, `pic0.dds`, `pic1.dds`,
`param.json` for a homebrew title); HTTPS to SteamGridDB's API and CDN
(helper/tests/nettest.c); the key page from another machine on the network;
changing and restoring icons and backgrounds; the install again that 1.3.0's
renames used (new art on the tile within seconds, the game's saves identical
afterwards, file for file); and, with ShadowMountPlus 1.7beta7, Apply changes:
new and restored art shown for a folder game, a disk image game (`.ffpfsc`)
and a package game, the home screen back within about three seconds of Art
Swap closing, and a game open in the background carrying on. Logos: one from
SteamGridDB on a homebrew game's page at once, with no restart; a store
logo on a disk image game kept through a console restart; and a logo put back
17 seconds into a rename's install, when the game's entry came back. The
PlayStation Store lookup was tested from a Mac only. A background added to a
homebrew emulator that had none, shown after Apply changes. 1.3.1's renames
through the database and its keeping of download data were made without a
console: they were tested against a copy of the console's `app.db` and the
helper tests' made-up console.

What the console taught (helper/tests/tlstest.c, procs.c):

- A payload does not get the console's trusted roots: every HTTPS request
  fails with `0x8095F00C` (TLS `0x8095F00A`, verify error `0x20`, unknown CA).
  The helper's certificate callback accepts that one result and refuses any
  other (`http_ps5.c`). `sceHttpsDisableOption` crashes the process; HTTP/2
  fails the same way and is not used.
- A payload that crashes is stopped, not ended: it stays under the ELF loader,
  traced by it (`PT_ATTACH` gives `EALREADY`, SIGKILL leaves it), and keeps its
  sockets until the console restarts. So the helper takes the first free of
  9117, 9127, 9137 (and the key page of 9118, 9128, 9138), the title asks each
  for HELLO with a three-second limit, and starts the helper again when it has
  gone.
- ShadowMountPlus refuses to uninstall (`EBUSY`) while any game is in the
  foreground, Art Swap included, so an install again finishes from the home
  screen.
  Its game list says `installed` before the install has copied anything; the
  helper waits for the copies' change times instead.
- Folders a game writes (its saves, mode 0700) can be read only as the game's
  user, not even as root: the helper switches to the folder's owner to read
  them.
- The home screen registers a background only as `pic0.dds`: a title whose
  `sce_sys` has a `pic0.png` alone (PS5X360's, or one Art Swap wrote as PNG)
  has none on the home screen, and its `pic0Info` stays empty.
- An install writes the title's entry in `app.db` some seconds after
  ShadowMountPlus lists it as installed (17 s once), so the helper waits for
  the entry before it puts a logo back.
- The console's uninstall deletes a title's download data,
  `/user/download/<id>` (`download0.dat`, the game's `/download0`), and the
  game's next start makes an empty one. Some homebrew keeps its saves there
  (mshivam019's Ship of Harkinian, when it cannot write its own folder), so a
  1.3.0 rename lost them (reported on Reddit).
- The home screen shows the names its database holds, written there by an
  install, in several places (see [Renaming](#renaming)); a homebrew title's
  entry has `TITLE` and `TITLE_01` (US English), a store game's one for each
  language it names.
- OnionHEN keeps its toolbox inside the home screen's process. After Apply
  changes restarts it, OnionHEN takes it for coming out of rest mode, tries to
  load the toolbox again, can time out, and the console may then show "System
  Software Error" (CE-108262-9); OK dismisses it.

## Building

Everything builds in the Lima VM `ps5` (`~/ps5`: PS5_Vulkan, PS5_PayloadSDK,
the UI kit's fork), with this folder mounted at the same path.

```bash
ps5/tools/vm.sh build                  # dist/PPSA99318/ with eboot.bin and artswapd.elf
helper/tools/build.sh                  # the helper alone: build/helper/artswapd.elf
helper/tools/build.sh host             # the helper for this Mac (libcurl)
python3 helper/tests/test_helper.py    # the helper against a made-up console and SteamGridDB, the key page too
python3 helper/tests/test_at9.py       # the C ATRAC9 encoder against ps5-at9-converter (beside this folder)
tools/preview/run.sh                   # the screens with the real helper, drawn in the VM: build/preview/*.png
NOKEY=1 tools/preview/run.sh FILE      # ... as someone who has not added a key yet
```

The preview's tour is a script of presses (`tools/preview/preview_main.cpp`
has the default; `tools/preview/run.sh FILE` runs another). Put `SGDB_KEY=...`
in `.env` first: the tests and the preview talk to SteamGridDB, and put that key
into their made-up console's `apikey.txt`. It never goes into a build.

The title is made from the [PS5 Vulkan Template](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_VulkanTemplate)
at `b577e950`, with its UI module. Art Swap's code is in `examples/artswap/kit/`
(the screens `app.cpp`, the helper's client, the keyboard, the program) and
`helper/`.

## Credits and licences

- The **UI kit** is BlackBearReloaded's [ps5-homebrew-ui](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-homebrew-ui),
  drawn with Vulkan through PS5_VKHomebrewUI, GPL-3.0-or-later. Art Swap's
  screens follow its Aurora Shelf design. Its fonts are OFL-1.1 and Bitstream
  Vera (`ps5/ASSETS.md`).
- The **foundation** (Sascha Willems' Vulkan example base and the template's
  PS5 layer) is MIT (`ps5/licenses/MIT.txt`).
- The **helper** uses [stb](https://github.com/nothings/stb) (public domain or MIT),
  [bcdec](https://github.com/iOrange/bcdec) (MIT or Unlicense),
  [cJSON](https://github.com/DaveGamble/cJSON) (MIT) and [SQLite](https://sqlite.org)
  (public domain); `helper/third_party/SOURCES.txt` pins each. Its BC7 encoder
  follows PS5 RetroArch's `tools/make-title-art.py` (GPL-3.0-or-later). The
  keyboard follows PS5_WindWakerHD's.
- The **music encoder** is BlackBearReloaded's [ps5-at9-converter](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-at9-converter)
  (GPL-3.0-or-later) ported to C; its ATRAC9 tables follow
  [LibAtrac9](https://github.com/Thealexbarney/LibAtrac9) (MIT). Songs are read with
  [dr_wav and dr_flac](https://github.com/mackron/dr_libs) (public domain or MIT-0) and
  [minimp3](https://github.com/lieff/minimp3) (CC0).
- The QR code is drawn with [Nayuki's QR Code generator](https://github.com/nayuki/QR-Code-generator)
  (MIT), in `examples/artswap/kit/qrcodegen.*`.
- **The art Art Swap offers** is SteamGridDB's, made and uploaded by its
  community; each picture shows its author. Art Swap is not affiliated with
  SteamGridDB, Valve or Sony.
- The way to set a logo (the PNG beside the art, `logoImageInfo` in `app.db`)
  was found by ensamvarg360's [Spela](https://github.com/ensamvarg360/spela)
  (GPL-3.0).
- The **home screen's layout** (`helper/src/layout.c`) follows elripalda's
  [psgfx](https://github.com/elripalda/psgfx) Home layout (GPL-3.0-or-later).
- Art Swap's own icon and background were generated for this project
  (sources in `ps5/art/`).

Art Swap as a whole (the title and the helper) is GPL-3.0-or-later
([`LICENSE`](LICENSE)).

latestRelease.name: Art Swap 1.4.0
latestRelease.body:
## New in 1.4.0

### Your own pictures
- Use your own icons, backgrounds and logos. The first cell in the picker shows a QR code: scan it with a phone (or open the address on a computer on the same network) and choose pictures. They arrive on the console in seconds.
- PNG and JPEG go across as they are; anything else the browser can show (WebP, HEIC on an iPhone) is turned into a PNG on the phone first. Copying files to `/data/artswap/pictures` over FTP works too.
- They come first in the Icons, Backgrounds and Logos tabs, tagged YOURS, for every game, and use the same frame page and preview as SteamGridDB's art. A logo wants a PNG with a see-through background: Art Swap says when a picture has none.
- OPTIONS on one of your pictures deletes it. Games already using it keep it.
- No SteamGridDB key is needed for your own pictures: the picker opens with them, and □ adds a key.

### The home screen's layout
OPTIONS, then Home screen:
- Move any tile between the Games and Media rows, the system's own too (PlayStation Store, Game Library, Art Swap itself).
- Hide tiles you never use, such as PlayStation Plus or the Store.
- Carry a game along the Games row with □ to put it where you want, then lock the order, or sort it A to Z.
- Apply changes (R2) restarts the home screen with the new layout. No reboot is needed.
- The layout is written again at every Apply changes, so if an install or a firmware update puts tiles back, the next Apply changes puts them right.

Thanks to elripalda's psgfx, which first found where the home screen keeps its layout.

### Also
- Art Swap has its own logo on its home-screen page.
- Games installed by Playden (and other installers whose game folders only their own user may write) can have their art changed. Before, the console refused the write.
- Settings, About shows the right version.

## Known issue

- With OnionHEN loaded, Apply changes can bring up "System Software Error" (CE-108262-9): OnionHEN loads its toolbox into the home screen again when it restarts. OK dismisses it.

## You need

- etaHEN (or kstuff) and ShadowMountPlus (1.7 or later, for renames, added backgrounds and added music). Art Swap starts its own helper through the console's ELF loader on port 9021, which etaHEN and kstuff setups already have.
- For SteamGridDB's art, your own SteamGridDB API key (free: steamgriddb.com, Preferences, API). Your own pictures need none.

## Installing

Copy the `PPSA99318` folder from `PS5_ArtSwap-v1.4.0.zip` to `/data/homebrew/` (over an earlier version is fine), or update from ProsperoStore.

## Files

- `PS5_ArtSwap-v1.4.0.zip`: the title.
- `SHA256SUMS`: digests of the zip and the source archives.
- `*.tar.gz` and `SOURCES.txt`: the source of every part of the built title, at the revision it was built from (GPL-3.0-or-later).

Not affiliated with SteamGridDB, Valve or Sony.

repos.name: Breeze
repos.description: Custom fan curve for the PS5: a payload with a web panel and a home screen app. Live CPU and GPU temps, 24-hour history and presets.
repos.readme:
Breeze

A fan curve for your PS5.
Decide how loud the fan gets at every temperature, right from your PS5, phone or PC.

Download · Quick start · The app · Good to know · The panel · How it works · FAQ

--- ## Why Breeze
Your curve, your noise
Up to 30 points of temperature → fan %. Quiet when you're browsing, cool when you're gaming.		 Edit from anywhere
The Breeze app on the PS5 itself, or a web panel on your LAN: drag the curve on your phone or PC and hit Apply.		 Actually follows it
Reads the real fan speed every second and steers it to within 1–2% of your curve.
No sudden roars
Loading screens and sensor spikes are filtered, so the fan doesn't surge every scene change.		 Presets
Up to 10 curves. Apply saves your edits into the one in use, and the built-in one is always there to go back to.		 Safe by default
Stock fan until you turn the curve on, full cooling past 88 °C, and back to stock when you turn it off or Breeze stops, even if it's killed.
## Quick start There are three ways to run Breeze. The app is the easiest: it shows your curve on the screen and starts Breeze for you. ### The app from a store (easiest) 1. **Install it:** open **[ProsperoStore](https://github.com/darkxex/ProsperoStore)** or **[RecompStore](https://recompstore.com/game/PPSA92878)** on your PS5, search for **Breeze** and install it. The store keeps it up to date too. 2. **Open Breeze** from the home screen. It starts Breeze for you. 3. **Switch on Custom curve** (top right). Until you do, the fan stays fully stock. Breeze remembers the switch, so after that it runs your curve on every launch. The app needs [ShadowMountPlus](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus) and an ELF loader on port 9021 (elfldr). ### The app by hand, with the zip 1. **Download** `PPSA92878.zip` from the [latest release](https://github.com/MiladRTX/Breeze/releases/latest). 2. **Unzip it.** You get a folder called `PPSA92878`. 3. **Copy the whole folder** to `/data/homebrew/` on the console, over FTP for example (ftpsrv listens on port 2121). You should end up with `/data/homebrew/PPSA92878/eboot.bin`. 4. **Wait a few seconds:** ShadowMountPlus finds the folder and adds **Breeze** to the home screen, under **Media**. 5. **Open Breeze** and switch on **Custom curve** (top right). To update by hand, close the app and copy the new `PPSA92878` folder over the old one. Coming from a Breeze that sits under Games (1.9 and older)? Delete it first, then copy the new folder: the PS5 only moves an app to Media on a fresh install. ### Payload only No app, just the payload and the web panel on your phone or PC. 1. **Download** `breeze.elf` from the [latest release](https://github.com/MiladRTX/Breeze/releases/latest). 2. **Load it** with [Payload Manager](https://github.com/itsPLK/ps5-payload-manager): choose **Upload ELF Payload**, then launch it. 3. **Open the panel.** The console pops up the address: > Breeze running (stock fan)
> Turn the curve on at `http://:2878` On the first start Breeze also adds a **Breeze tile to your home screen** (unless the [Breeze app](#the-app) is installed): open it and the panel comes up in the PS5 browser. 4. **Switch on Custom curve** (top right). Until you do, the fan stays fully stock. Breeze remembers the switch, so after that it runs your curve on every launch. > [!TIP] > Add Breeze to Payload Manager's **Autoload** list so your curve is back after every reboot. To update, just launch the new version: it replaces the running one by itself.
Using elfldr directly instead
Send the ELF to the loader on port 9021: ```sh nc -q0 9021 < breeze.elf ```
## The app Breeze also comes as an app for the PS5 home screen: the same curve, history, presets and settings as the web panel, on the screen with the DualSense. **Install it** from [ProsperoStore](https://github.com/darkxex/ProsperoStore), [RecompStore](https://recompstore.com/game/PPSA92878) or by hand with `PPSA92878.zip`: see [Quick start](#quick-start). **It needs** [ShadowMountPlus](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus) and an ELF loader on port 9021 (elfldr): the app carries its own `breeze.elf` and starts it when Breeze isn't running. Breeze keeps running after you close the app, and the app takes the place of the browser tile. - **After a reboot,** open the app once to start Breeze again, or add `breeze.elf` to Payload Manager's **Autoload** list so it starts by itself. - **After an update,** open the app once: if an older Breeze is running, the app replaces it with its own copy. The version at the top of the app is the running Breeze's. - **It's a Media app,** so it stays open next to a game: check the fan mid-game and jump straight back. To start a *different* game while Breeze is open, close the current game first; picking the new one directly gives error CE-105773-3. Every Media homebrew app does this (Stremio too). | Tab | Controls | | --- | --- | | **Curve** | ←→ choose a point, ↑↓ fan, L2/R2 temperature, slide on the touchpad to move the point, △ add, □ remove, L3/R3 undo and redo, ✕ apply, ○ revert | | **History** | ←→ range (5 minutes to 24 hours), slide on the touchpad to look back | | **Presets** | ↑↓ choose, ✕ use, △ new preset from the curve, □ delete (asks for a second press) | | **Settings** | Custom curve on or off, reset to the built-in Breeze preset | L1 and R1 switch tabs. While the app is open the PS5 treats it like a game, so the fan minimum is the in-game 23%. ## Good to know - **The PS5 has a minimum fan speed:** 13% in the menus, 23% while a game or app runs. Breeze can add fan on top of that but never go below it, so in a game the fan only rises once your curve asks for more than 23% (from about 60 °C with the default curve). - **The fan settles within about 1–2% of your curve,** 10–20 s after a big change. - **Dots are joined by straight lines:** halfway between 60 °C at 30% and 70 °C at 40% is 35% at 65 °C. - **Past 88 °C Breeze always asks for full cooling,** whatever your curve says. - **Stopping Breeze hands the fan back to stock,** whether you turn Custom curve off, reboot, or kill it. ## The panel | Part | What it does | | --- | --- | | **Readouts** | CPU and GPU temperature, fan speed, what your curve asks for, and the target Breeze gives the PS5. The curve follows the CPU; the GPU is shown only. Hover (or tap) any of them for a short explanation. | | **Curve** | Drag points, double-click empty space to add one or a point to remove it, arrow keys to nudge. The dashed lines show where the temperature and fan are right now; the shaded band is the 23% in-game minimum. | | **History** | 5 minutes to 24 hours of temperature and fan speed. Hover to see any moment. | | **Presets** | Use, rename or delete saved curves, or start a new one from the curve in the editor. The one in use is marked **Active**: Apply saves your edits into it. The built-in **Breeze** preset never changes: edits of it are saved as a new preset, "My curve". | | **Points** | The same curve as a table, for exact values. | Nothing changes until you press **Apply** (or Ctrl + S). ## How it works The PS5 has no "set the fan to 40 %" switch. Its fan controller works like a **thermostat**: you give it a target temperature and it spins the fan to cool towards it. Breeze closes the loop around that thermostat. Every second it: 1. reads the CPU temperature and the **real** fan speed, 2. looks up what your curve wants at that temperature, 3. nudges the target up or down, in fractions of a degree, until the fan matches. Breeze makes small corrections and lets each one settle, ignores one-second spikes and dips, and backs off fast if the fan overshoots, so the fan stays within about 1–2% of your curve without jumping. When Breeze hands the fan back, it puts back the console's own target (91 °C on a PS5 Slim), which it learns from the console itself, and never anything warmer than 91 °C. ## FAQ
Is it safe for my console?
Breeze only changes the fan controller's target. Past 88 °C it always asks for full cooling, the console keeps its own minimum fan speed, and turning the curve off or stopping Breeze, even by killing it, hands the fan straight back to the console's own setting. Still, keep an eye on your temperatures, especially with very quiet curves.
Why isn't the fan exactly on my curve?
Breeze steers the PS5's thermostat, not the fan itself, so it gets the fan to within about 1–2% of the curve rather than exactly on it, and takes a few seconds after each change. Gaps of 2% or less are left alone on purpose, so the fan doesn't keep shifting. It also can't go under the console's minimum (13% in the menus, 23% in a game). Steep sections of the curve make the fan jumpy during loading screens, so add a dot where you want a gentler bend.
Why does the Fan readout say "console"?
Other parts of the console can ask for more fan. The PS5 cools some parts on its own, and when one of them needs more than your curve, the Fan readout says **console**. That's the PS5 protecting itself.
What is breeze-guard.elf?
The small helper next to breeze.elf in the process list. If breeze.elf is killed (from Payload Manager's process list, for example), the guard puts the console's own fan setting back within about a second. Leave it running: Breeze restarts it within 10 seconds if it's stopped, and it exits by itself once the fan is back.
The fan seems stuck after Breeze stopped
Launch Breeze again (it puts back what a stopped copy left behind), start or close a game, or reboot.
Known limitations
Breeze is new and has been tested on one console (a PS5 Slim), so expect some rough edges: - **Short spikes can still happen** for a few seconds right as a game launches. - **History is saved every 5 minutes,** so if Breeze is killed the last few minutes of the graph are lost. Found something off? [Open an issue](https://github.com/MiladRTX/Breeze/issues) and attach `/data/breeze/breeze.log` if you can.
Where are my settings stored?
| Path | What | | --- | --- | | `/data/breeze/breeze.conf` | Curve, on/off, panel port, panel token | | `/data/breeze/presets.conf` | Saved presets | | `/data/breeze/history.bin` | The last 24 hours of history, so the graph survives a restart | | `/data/breeze/stock.conf` | The console's own fan target, learned by Breeze (delete it to relearn) | | `/data/breeze/breeze.log` | Controller log, up to 256 KB; the one before is kept as `breeze.log.1` |
How do I build it myself?
Needs [ps5-payload-sdk](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk), CMake and Ninja: ```sh PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK=/path/to/ps5-payload-sdk ./build.sh # -> build/breeze.elf ``` The panel is plain HTML in [`web/panel.html`](web/panel.html) and gets embedded into the ELF. Opened on its own, it runs with sample data, which is handy for working on the design. The app builds in Linux or WSL with clang and lld 18, make and Python 3, after `build.sh`: ```sh app/build.sh # -> build/app/PPSA92878 and PPSA92878.zip ``` It fetches [ps5-native-app-boilerplate](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-native-app-boilerplate) at a pinned commit. `app/preview/run.sh` draws every screen as a PNG on a PC, without a console.
## Credits Made by **[Milad](https://github.com/MiladRTX)**. Thanks to [John Törnblom](https://github.com/john-tornblom) for the [PS5 payload SDK](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk), to [aydencharles](https://github.com/aydencharles) for [onionHEN](https://github.com/aydencharles/onionHEN), where the fan controller interface was first worked out, and to [BlackBearReloaded](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded) for [ps5-native-app-boilerplate](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-native-app-boilerplate), which the app is built on. The app uses the [Inter](https://rsms.me/inter/) and [JetBrains Mono](https://www.jetbrains.com/lp/mono/) fonts (SIL Open Font License). ## License [GPL-3.0](LICENSE) > [!WARNING] > Breeze is an unofficial homebrew project and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Sony Interactive Entertainment. It changes how your console's fan behaves: use it only on hardware you own, keep an eye on temperatures, and use it at your own risk. No warranty is provided.
