latestRelease.body:
## What's new in 1.9.1

### Breeze is a Media app now
- The app moved from Games to the Media section of the home screen.
- It stays open next to a game: check your fan and temperatures mid-game, then jump straight back where you left off. Before, opening Breeze closed your game.
- To start a different game while Breeze is open, close the current game first. Picking the new game directly gives error CE-105773-3. Every Media homebrew app does this (Stremio too).

### Install
- Coming from 1.9 or older? Delete Breeze first (Settings > Storage > Games and apps, or ShadowMountPlus), then install the new version. The PS5 only moves an app to Media on a fresh install; installing over the old one keeps it under Games.
- New install: copy the PPSA92878 folder from PPSA92878.zip to /data/homebrew on the console, then open the app once.
- Payload only: breeze.elf has no changes besides its version, so there's no need to update it.

repos.name: estante
repos.description: Native PS5 library organizer for jailbroken consoles: 3D shelf, collections, favourites, emulator libraries with covers. EN/PT/ES. Needs ShadowMountPlus + Elf Arsenal.
repos.readme:
# Estante

Organizador de biblioteca que roda no proprio PS5, com navegacao pelo controle.
*A native PS5 library organizer with controller navigation, for jailbroken consoles.*

**English:** Estante ("shelf" in Portuguese) is a controller-driven PS5 library organizer with a Home catalogue, a cover-flow shelf, a searchable and filterable Library, game details, trophies when the console has local trophy data, and personal collections. It reads PS5/PS4 titles through Elf Arsenal and can import games from the standard `/data` folders of PS5SX2, SwanStationPS5, Porpoise, and PS5-ECAM. For imported emulator titles, Play opens the emulator; select the game inside it. USB/M.2 game folders are not imported; Nintendo Switch games come from ProsperoEden; 3DS/DS lists depend on ECAM having scanned them. Each emulator must have been opened at least once. It requires Elf Arsenal and ShadowMountPlus; only firmware 11.60 has been tested. The GPU interface uses OpenGL via [ps5-opengl](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-opengl) and [ps5-homebrew-ui](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-homebrew-ui), with 3D cases, cover flow, a launch animation, five color themes, and English/Portuguese/Spanish localization. Portrait covers can be added with `tools/ps5_covers_sync.py`; otherwise the app uses available square art. The app has its own home-screen background (selected and launching). The console only reads it when the app is registered, so if you update from an older version and the background does not show, uninstall Estante and install it again. Downloads and install notes: [latest release](https://github.com/kauansilvalopes/estante/releases/tag/v0.5.5).

## Screenshots

Rendered by the real draw code through the GPU renderer on a PC (Mesa) with placeholder covers (no game art is bundled). Build: `make` fetches the pinned ps5-opengl SDK on its own; `bash tools/preview-estante-gl.sh` renders every screen on the PC.

| Home | Library |
|---|---|
| ![Home](docs/screenshots/home.png) | ![Library](docs/screenshots/library.png) |
| **Filters (touchpad)** | **Collections** |
| ![Filters](docs/screenshots/sidebar.png) | ![Collections](docs/screenshots/collections.png) |
| **Game details** | **Organize menu** |
| ![Details](docs/screenshots/details.png) | ![Menu](docs/screenshots/menu.png) |
| **Apps** | **Settings** |
| ![Apps](docs/screenshots/apps.png) | ![Settings](docs/screenshots/settings.png) |
| **Case turned by the right stick (spine)** | **Back of the case (R2 / L2)** |
| ![Spine](docs/screenshots/spine.png) | ![Back](docs/screenshots/back.png) |
| **Launch: the case opens, the disc comes out** | |
| ![Launch](docs/screenshots/launch.png) | |

O Estante organiza a biblioteca dentro do próprio aplicativo, sem mover jogos nem alterar o menu oficial. Lê jogos de PS5/PS4 pelo Elf Arsenal e importa títulos das pastas padrão em `/data` de PS5SX2 (PS2), SwanStationPS5 (PS1), Porpoise (GameCube/Wii) e PS5-ECAM (Wii U/3DS/DS). Ao selecionar um título importado de emulador, o Estante abre o emulador; a seleção do jogo é feita dentro dele. Não lê bibliotecas em USB/M.2 nem jogos de Switch; os títulos de 3DS/DS aparecem depois que o ECAM os escaneia. Abra cada emulador ao menos uma vez antes de atualizar o Estante. Requer Elf Arsenal e ShadowMountPlus; o teste de console disponível foi feito no firmware 11.60.

## Nova experiência

- Início com jogo em destaque, últimas escolhas feitas no Estante, jogos fixados e mosaicos de coleções.
- Biblioteca completa com busca sem distinção de acentos, filtros e ordenação.
- Coleções e subcoleções, seleção múltipla, favoritos, ocultos e classificação PS2/PS4/PS5.
- Coleções automáticas por plataforma, progresso manual e favoritos. Crie em Todos os jogos, sem busca textual ativa.
- Progresso manual: Quero jogar, Em andamento e Concluído. Não representa troféus ou leitura de saves.
- Fonte Inter com minúsculas e acentos; opção de texto maior e modo gravação persistentes.
- Capas locais PNG/JPEG, carregadas em segundo plano, com cache limitado. Nenhuma capa de jogo acompanha o projeto.
- Consulta ao estado do console antes de abrir um título e tentativa de confirmação posterior.
- Migração dos metadados v1 com cópia anterior preservada; exportação e restauração local.

As pastas existem dentro do Estante; os jogos não são movidos nem reorganizados no menu oficial.
PS2 instalado como PS4 exige classificação manual. O app roda no PS5 sem servidor no PC.
Recentes são pedidos feitos pelo Estante após a consulta inicial, não histórico global nem prova de abertura.

Veja [ESTANTE.md](ESTANTE.md) para controles, dados, instalação e limites e
[DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md) para as decisões de UX.

```sh
bash tools/test-estante.sh
bash tools/preview-estante.sh
```

Os previews `.local/preview-*.png` usam o renderizador real com dados e artes fictícias.
Servem apenas à validação de desenvolvimento; não são um aplicativo para o PC.

## Compilar (Linux / WSL Ubuntu)

```sh
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install clang-18 llvm-18 lld-18 make ninja-build ccache curl wget unzip
make
```

O build baixa dependencias publicas fixadas por versao e hash. Saidas:
`dist/PPSA99841/` e `dist/PPSA99841.zip`.
Saída em pasta para ShadowMount; também pode ser empacotada como imagem `.ffpfsc`. Não é PKG.

## Enviar ao PS5

Com ShadowMount e FTP ativos, envie a pasta para `/data/homebrew/PPSA99841`.
Para uma instalacao nova pelo script, substitua o endereco de exemplo:

```sh
python3 tools/deploy-estante.py --host 192.0.2.10
```

O script usa FTP anonymous na porta 2121, confere os arquivos por SHA-256 e recusa
substituir um titulo ja registrado. Nao troca os payloads instalados.
Aparecendo o titulo Estante, abra pelo menu ou pela Biblioteca de jogos.

## Controles e testes

Direcional navega; X confirma; quadrado seleciona titulos; triangulo/Options abre
as acoes; L1/R1 muda pagina; circulo volta. No teclado, Options salva o nome.
Veja [ESTANTE.md](ESTANTE.md) para detalhes e limitacoes.

Testes da logica de catalogo, classificacao e pastas:

```sh
mkdir -p build/tests
clang-18 -g -fsanitize=address,undefined -c src/cJSON.c -o build/tests/cjson-host.o
clang++-18 -std=c++20 -g -fsanitize=address,undefined tests/test_estante.cpp src/library.cpp build/tests/cjson-host.o -o build/tests/test-estante
build/tests/test-estante
```

Esses testes nao validam o funcionamento no hardware. Os workflows originais da
base estao arquivados em `docs/upstream-workflows`, sem execucao automatica.

## Creditos e licenca

Autor do Estante: Kauan ([@kndofc](https://instagram.com/kndofc)).

Derivado de [ps5-native-app-boilerplate](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-native-app-boilerplate),
de BlackBearReloaded, sob GPL-3.0-or-later. Os avisos de autoria foram preservados.
Documentacao original: [docs/UPSTREAM_README.md](docs/UPSTREAM_README.md).

- SDK publico: [ps5-payload-dev/sdk](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk), v0.42.
- stb_image: MIT / dominio publico; origem fixada em [third_party/stb/SOURCE.md](third_party/stb/SOURCE.md).
- cJSON 1.7.19: MIT, veja [LICENSE-cJSON](LICENSE-cJSON).
- Licenca do projeto: [LICENSE](LICENSE); demais avisos: [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

Dependencias baixadas, binarios gerados e dados pessoais do console nao sao versionados.

repos.name: Alembic
repos.description: Converts PS5 and PS4 packages and game dumps between FPKG, exFAT, FFPKG, FFPFS and FFPFSC images, on the console or with a PC.
repos.readme:
# Alembic

![Alembic's page in the PS5 browser: a library of games in several formats, with drives, an FTP server and a paired PC on the left](docs/screenshots/files.png)

Alembic converts PS5 and PS4 games between the formats homebrew loaders use:
packages (PS5 debug FPKG, PS4 fake PKG), dump folders, exFAT images, FFPKG
(UFS2), FFPFS (PFS) and FFPFSC (compressed PFS). It runs **on the console** as an app on the home
screen (from 0.3.0) or as a payload with a web page, both driven with the
controller, and on a PC (Windows, macOS, Linux) as a command-line tool or the
same engine and page. Engines on your network can
pair and work together: convert a package that sits on your PC, on the PC's
processor, straight into the console's storage.

> Work in progress. Back up anything you convert until you have checked the
> result on your console.

**Tried on a console so far:** FFPFSC images made from dumps and from
packages run through ShadowMount+; games that need the AMPR emulator start
once it is added; the console and a PC pair and convert for each other;
**Install** hands a debug package to the console's installer; a paused
conversion carries on after the engine is updated; the engine updates
itself from a release (loaded through Payload Manager); the console app
starts from ShadowMount+, starts and restarts the engine, and drives a
conversion on a paired PC.
PS4 games converted from their packages start from images through
ShadowMount+ 1.7beta8 (it shows "Trophy registration failed" for them: a
ShadowMount+ issue, [#97](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus/issues/97)).
**Not yet:** installing an FPKG that Alembic built, PS5 or PS4; PS4 updates
(patch packages) and DLC. LZ4 asset packs work for some games and not for
others.

## What it does

| From ↓ / To → | Folder | exFAT | FFPKG (UFS2) | FFPFS (PFS) | FFPFSC | Package |
|---|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|
| Dump folder | – | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| exFAT | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| FFPKG (UFS2) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| FFPFS (PFS) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| FFPFSC | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| PS5 FPKG (debug) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | `--rebuild` |
| PS4 PKG (fake) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | `--rebuild` |

The package a game becomes matches the game: a PS5 game (`sce_sys/param.json`)
a PS5 debug FPKG, a PS4 game (`sce_sys/param.sfo`) a PS4 fake PKG. The page
and the app mark each game with a **PS5** (white) or **PS4** (black) pill.

- **PS4 games** (from 0.3.2): fake PKGs with the usual all-zero passcode
  (from older and newer packaging tools alike) open
  like PS5 packages, as the game's files plus `sce_sys` (`param.sfo`, icons,
  trophies, licence) from the package, and convert to any image. Images and
  folders of a PS4 game get the `sce_sys/param.json` ShadowMount+ needs to
  start it (made from `param.sfo`, as
  [PS4pkg_to_ffpfsc](https://github.com/SadykovIV/PS4pkg_to_ffpfsc) makes
  it); tried on a console with ShadowMount+ 1.7beta8. A PS4 game
  in any format converts back to a PS4 fake PKG, built the way
  [LibOrbisPkg](https://github.com/maxton/LibOrbisPkg)'s `pkg_build` builds
  one: the game's licence is kept (generated only when missing), and the
  PlayGo files are made again. A package rebuilt from any image of it is the
  same, byte for byte. The keys come from LibOrbisPkg (Components, or
  `--ps4-keys FILE` on a PC). The AMPR emulator and LZ4 packs are for PS5
  games only. Which console a game is for comes from its title ID (`CUSA`,
  `PPSA`), else from the SDK its `eboot.bin` was built with (homebrew);
  `alembic game-info` shows both. Not yet: updates and DLC, and packages
  made with a passcode other than all zeros.
- **Streams:** every input is read as a file tree and written straight to
  the output, with no temporary copies, so a 100 GB package needs only the
  space of the result.
- **Byte-identical** to the reference tools: exFAT, FFPKG and FFPFSC match
  [PS5PKGTool](https://github.com/pearlxcore/PS5PKGTool); FFPFS matches
  [MkPFS](https://github.com/PSBrew/MkPFS) (`pack folder --raw
  --no-compress`); FPKG output matches
  [ProsperoPkgTool](https://github.com/pearlxcore/ProsperoPkgTool)
  (`img_create`, stored, with the same fixed seed); PS4 packages match
  [LibOrbisPkg](https://github.com/maxton/LibOrbisPkg)'s `pkg_build`, also
  when rebuilding a package from the project its `pkg_makegp4` extracts.
- **LZ4 asset packs** for drakmor's [ampr_emu](https://github.com/drakmor/ampr_emu)
  PackedStdio runtime (`--lz4`), byte-identical to its `ampr_pack.py`, with
  game profiles from
  [PS5-LZ4-Compression](https://github.com/theghostonline/PS5-LZ4-Compression).
- **AMPR emulator:** games that use the console's APR file reader need
  ampr_emu's `libSceAmpr.sprx` to start from an image or folder. Alembic
  adds it when converting, or to a game you already have.
- **Fast:** compression and package decoding use every core; AES, CRC32C
  and SHA-256 use the CPU's own instructions where it has them; zlib level 6
  by default (level 9 for exact PS5PKGTool output).

## On the PS5

The work is done by the engine (`alembic.elf`), a payload that keeps running
after you close what you drive it with: the **Alembic app** on the home
screen, or its web page in the console's browser (from a shortcut it adds to
the Media tab) or in any browser on your network at `http://<console-ip>:5940`.
The app and the page show the same things and work the same way.

![The Alembic app on the PS5: a homebrew folder with games in several formats, drives, an FTP server and a paired PC on the left](docs/screenshots/app.png)

**The app** (`PPSA99594`, from 0.3.0), installed either way:

1. **From ProsperoStore** (easiest): Alembic is listed in
   [ProsperoStore](https://github.com/darkxex/ProsperoStore), the console
   store for native homebrew ([Alembic's page](https://prosperostore.net/app/PPSA99594/)).
   Install it there; the store also updates it.
2. **As an image or folder**, through
   [ShadowMount+](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus): copy
   `alembic-app-<version>.ffpkg` from the releases to `/data/homebrew/` (or
   unzip `alembic-app-<version>.zip` there: the `PPSA99594` folder). Its tile
   shows up on the home screen after ShadowMount+'s next scan.

Start it. When no engine answers, it sends its own to the ELF loader on port
9021 (an app without one downloads the engine of its own version from the
GitHub release first, checked against `SHA256SUMS`).

**Without the app:**

1. Send `alembic-<version>.elf` (from the releases) to your console's ELF loader.
2. Open Alembic from the Media tab (or the address above).
3. In **Files**, pick a game on internal storage, USB, an FTP server or a
   paired engine's drive (a pill tells PS5 and PS4 games apart), then
   **Convert**, **Install** (packages), **Copy** or **Move**.
4. Jobs run one at a time in **Queue**: pause, resume (long jobs continue
   from a checkpoint), reorder, cancel. You get a notification when one
   finishes.

![The Convert dialog: target formats, compression level, the AMPR emulator switch, and the output path on a paired PC](docs/screenshots/convert.png)

![The queue: a running conversion with speed and time left, a paused one that continues from its checkpoint, a copy to FTP, and a job running on the paired PC](docs/screenshots/queue.png)

Also on the page:

- **Controller first:** the D-pad moves, ✕ chooses, ○ goes back, □ opens a
  file's options, L1/R1 switch sections and L2/R2 page through lists. To
  leave, press L2 + R2 together, then ○ (a page cannot close the console's
  browser itself). Settings has a controller test. On a PC: arrow keys,
  Enter, Esc, S, Q/E and Page Up/Down.
- **Places:** add any folder to Places from its Options; they show in the
  rail, in Save to, and on paired engines.
- **FTP servers** (Settings): games on a PC or NAS that runs an FTP server
  can be converted without copying them to the console first. The server
  only stores the files: the engine reads the game over the network and does
  the converting itself. exFAT, FFPKG, FFPFS and folder outputs can be saved
  back to the server. To have a PC do the work, run Alembic's engine on it
  instead (see [Working across engines](#working-across-engines)).
- **From this computer:** opened in a PC's browser, the page can share a
  file from that PC for the console to convert.
- **ShadowMount+:** new images can be picked up without a restart, and
  sources can be hidden from it once converted.
- **Components:** third-party files Alembic needs but doesn't ship (ampr_emu's
  runtime, ProsperoPkgTool's FPKG key files, LibOrbisPkg's PS4 package keys)
  are downloaded on request from
  their official source and kept only if their SHA-256 matches.
- **Engine** (Settings): **Restart the engine** starts the same version again
  through the ELF loader; the app also offers **Start the engine** once it
  has stopped.
- **Updates** (from 0.2.3): the engine looks for a newer release on GitHub
  when it starts and says so; **Settings → Updates** shows its notes.
  **Update** downloads the payload, checks it against the release's
  `SHA256SUMS` and the version written inside it, and replaces the copies
  your loader starts it from: Payload Manager's (renamed to the new version,
  with the name fixed in that payload's `meta.json`) and `ps5_autoloader`
  folders (same name); **Search the drives** finds copies elsewhere. Then
  the new engine starts through the ELF loader (port 9021) and takes over;
  a running job that keeps its progress continues. Sending a newer
  `alembic.elf` by hand also replaces a running engine. From 0.3.0 the same
  update replaces the app's `.ffpkg` too when the release's differs; while
  the app is open, that waits until it is closed (an app installed from
  ProsperoStore is updated by the store). An app older than its engine says
  so and offers **Update the app**.
- **Other engines:** a paired engine that is switched off stays listed as
  offline instead of disappearing.
- Languages: English, Español, Français, Deutsch, 日本語, Türkçe.

State (queue, settings, downloaded components) is kept in `/data/alembic`.

## Working across engines

Run `alembic-engine` on a PC as well as the payload on the console. Once
paired, each engine can read and write the other's files and hand it jobs.

1. In **Settings → Other engines**, switch on **Find engines on this
   network** on both (off by default), or add one by its address.
2. Press **Pair** next to the other engine. It shows a six-digit code
   (on the PS5 as a notification, on a PC in its window); type it in.
   Paired engines sign every request with the key they agreed on.
3. The other engine's drives and Places appear in **Files** under
   *Other engines*, as inputs and as places to save to.
4. In **Convert**, **Convert on** picks the engine that does the work (of
   those online right now). The
   source, the converting engine and the output can each be on a different
   engine; data streams between them, with no copy made first.

A job shows in the queue of every engine whose files it uses ("on Living
room PC"), and can be paused, resumed, cancelled or cleared from the history
on any of them. When a job deletes its source after checking the output,
engines compare SHA-256 digests instead of sending the files back. Files can also be sent between
engines without converting (Options → Send to another engine).

![Settings: Places, a paired PC and a Mac found on the network, and an FTP server](docs/screenshots/engines.png)

Engines of different Alembic versions work together as long as they talk to
each other the same way; when that changes in a release, Settings shows which
engine to update, and they refuse each other until it is.

The page itself has no password: anyone on your network can open it. Start
a PC engine with `--listen 127.0.0.1` to keep it to that computer; other
engines can't reach it then.

## On a PC

Each release has a package per system: `alembic-<version>-linux-x64.tar.gz`,
`-macos-arm64.tar.gz` (Apple silicon) and `-windows-x64.zip`, each with
`alembic` and `alembic-engine`. The macOS builds are not signed: after a
download from a browser, run `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine alembic
alembic-engine` once in their folder, or macOS refuses to start them.

```sh
alembic convert game.pkg game.ffpfsc              # format from the extension (PS5 or PS4 package)
alembic convert ps4game.exfat game.pkg --ps4-keys Keys.cs   # a PS4 game back to a PS4 fake PKG
alembic convert game.exfat game/ --to folder      # unpack to a folder
alembic convert game/ game.exfat --lz4 --lz4-runtime libSceAmpr.sprx
alembic ls game.ffpkg                             # list the files of any input
alembic same game.pkg game.ffpfsc                 # compare two inputs file by file
alembic game-info game.exfat                      # title ID, SDK and PS4 or PS5
alembic --help                                    # every command and option
```

`alembic-engine` is the same engine as the payload, with the same web page
(`http://localhost:5940`), for converting on a PC or pairing with the
console. `--root DIR` (repeatable) chooses the folders it shares (your
home folder by default); `alembic-engine --help` lists the other options.
Settings → Updates says when a newer release is out; on a PC, download it
and replace the files yourself.

## Building

Requirements: CMake 3.20+, a C++20 compiler, zlib (bundled for the PS5), and
Node.js 20+ with npm for the engine's web page (`src/engine/web`, Preact and
TypeScript bundled by esbuild; the first build runs `npm ci` there).

```sh
cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build build -j
./build/alembic_tests
```

Windows (`alembic.exe`, `alembic-engine.exe`) is cross-built with
[llvm-mingw](https://github.com/mstorsjo/llvm-mingw) from macOS or Linux; the
executables are statically linked and run on Windows 10 and later as they
are. `tools/windows/smoke.sh` checks them on Windows (Git Bash).

```sh
cmake -S . -B build-win -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=cmake/mingw-w64-x86_64.cmake \
      -DLLVM_MINGW=/path/to/llvm-mingw
cmake --build build-win -j
```

The PS5 payload needs LLVM 18 and
[ps5-payload-dev/sdk](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk) v0.44:

```sh
# macOS: brew install llvm@18 · Debian/Ubuntu: apt install clang-18 lld-18 llvm-18
export PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK=/path/to/ps5-payload-sdk   # default: .refs/ps5-payload-sdk
tools/ps5/build.sh                                # → build-ps5/alembic.elf
```

GitHub Actions builds and tests everything on every push that changes more
than the docs (see [.github/workflows/build.yml](.github/workflows/build.yml)).
Each run has the payload as a download of its own, `alembic-<version>.elf`,
and a bundle, `alembic-<version>.zip`: the payload in `ps5/`, `alembic` and
`alembic-engine` in `linux-x64/`, `macos-arm64/` and `windows-x64/` (`.exe`),
with the README and license files. The version is the tag (`v0.1.0`), else the branch and commit
(`main-a2fab12`). A `v*` tag publishes the payload, the bundle, a package per
PC system, the console app (`.ffpkg` and `.zip`) and `SHA256SUMS` as a release.
From 0.3.1 every release file carries a build attestation: `gh attestation
verify <file> --repo fthdgn-gh/Alembic` shows that this repository's workflow
built it, and from which commit.

### The web page

The engine's page is `src/engine/web`: Preact components in TypeScript
(`src/pages/` has one folder per section; `src/main.tsx` maps the rest),
bundled for the PS5's older browser into one HTML file that the engine
embeds. To work on it, run an engine and let the page rebuild on every
change:

```sh
build/alembic-engine --listen 127.0.0.1 &   # its API, on port 5940
cd src/engine/web
node build.mjs --serve                      # the page at http://127.0.0.1:5950
npx tsc --noEmit                            # type check (CI runs it too)
python3 ../../../tools/i18n_keys.py --check # every text translated
```

`tools/screenshots/shoot.sh` makes the README's screenshots against a
stand-in engine with made-up games.

### Checking against the reference tools

The scripts in `tools/` compare Alembic's output byte for byte with the tools
it follows. They need the reference projects checked out in `.refs/`
(git-ignored); [docs/NOTES.md](docs/NOTES.md) says how to recreate it.

```sh
tools/oracle/compare.sh        # exFAT, FFPKG, FFPFS, FFPFSC vs PS5PKGTool and MkPFS
tools/pkg-oracle/compare.sh    # FPKG reading vs packages built by ProsperoPkgTool / LibProsperoPKG
tools/lz4-oracle/compare.sh    # LZ4 packs vs ampr_emu's ampr_pack.py
tools/ps4-oracle/compare.sh    # PS4 packages vs LibOrbisPkg's pkg_build, pkg_extract and pkg_validate
```

## What Alembic does not include

- No Oodle, `libScePubTools`, closed-source package libraries or console keys
  in this repository or its binaries. FPKG output uses ProsperoPkgTool's
  published key files; PS4 package output uses LibOrbisPkg's `Keys.cs` (it
  also holds the debug licence key, used only to generate a licence for a
  game that has none). The engine downloads both on request.
- No third-party binaries: ampr_emu's `libSceAmpr.sprx` is downloaded from its
  official release, pinned by SHA-256.

## Credits

Alembic stands on the work of the PS5 homebrew scene. Thank you to:

- **pearlxcore** for [PS5PKGTool](https://github.com/pearlxcore/PS5PKGTool)
  (exFAT, PFSC and FFPFSC; the reference Alembic matches byte for byte) and
  [ProsperoPkgTool](https://github.com/pearlxcore/ProsperoPkgTool) (reading
  and writing debug packages, and its key files).
- **SadykovIV** for [PS4pkg_to_ffpfsc](https://github.com/SadykovIV/PS4pkg_to_ffpfsc)
  (how a PS4 game's image has to look for ShadowMount+, its `param.json`).
- **SvenGDK** for [UFS2Tool](https://github.com/SvenGDK/UFS2Tool) (the FFPKG
  reader and writer) and [LibProsperoPKG](https://github.com/SvenGDK/LibProsperoPKG)
  (test packages).
- **drakmor** for [ampr_emu](https://github.com/drakmor/ampr_emu) (the AMPR
  index, LZ4 asset packs and the runtime that reads them) and
  [ShadowMountPlus](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus) (the loader
  Alembic's images are made for, and its HTTPS download code).
- **PSBrew** for [MkPFS](https://github.com/PSBrew/MkPFS) (the PFS writer).
- **maxton** for [LibOrbisPkg](https://github.com/maxton/LibOrbisPkg) (PS4
  packages: the writer Alembic follows, its keys, and the tool it is checked
  against).
- **theghostonline** for
  [PS5-LZ4-Compression](https://github.com/theghostonline/PS5-LZ4-Compression)
  (LZ4 pack profiles and the engine-and-page idea).
- **danthespal** for the LZ4 game profiles posted with
  [MkPFS.CSharp](https://github.com/danthespal/MkPFS.CSharp).
- **ps5-payload-dev** for the [PS5 payload SDK](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk),
  [shsrv](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/shsrv) (package installs) and
  [websrv](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/websrv) (the Media-tab shortcut),
  with [owendswang/ps5-web-file-manager](https://github.com/owendswang/ps5-web-file-manager)
  and [itsPLK/ps5-payload-manager](https://github.com/itsPLK/ps5-payload-manager).
- **blackbearreloaded** for [ps5-homebrew-ui](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-homebrew-ui),
  the design the page follows.
- [zlib](https://zlib.net) and [LZ4](https://github.com/lz4/lz4), bundled
  with the engine, and [Preact](https://github.com/preactjs/preact) with its
  [signals](https://github.com/preactjs/signals), bundled into its page.

The games, engines and addresses in the screenshots are made up
(`tools/screenshots/shoot.sh` renders them against a stand-in engine).

## License

GPL-3.0-or-later ([LICENSE](LICENSE)). Alembic ports code from several GPL,
LGPL, MIT and BSD projects; [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) lists
each one, what was taken from it, and its license.

latestRelease.name: Alembic v0.3.2
latestRelease.body:
PS4 games: fake packages open like PS5 ones, convert to any image ShadowMount+ starts, and build back into PS4 packages.

### PS4 games
- PS4 fake packages (the usual all-zero passcode; older and newer packaging tools) open as the game's files plus sce_sys, and convert to a folder, exFAT, FFPKG, FFPFS or FFPFSC.
- Images and folders of a PS4 game get the sce_sys/param.json ShadowMount+ needs to start it, made from param.sfo. Tried on a PS5 with ShadowMount+ 1.7beta8; it shows "Trophy registration failed" for PS4 games, a ShadowMount+ issue (#97).
- A PS4 game in any format converts back to a PS4 fake package, byte-identical to LibOrbisPkg's pkg_build. The game's licence is kept (one is generated only when missing). The keys come from LibOrbisPkg: get "PS4 package keys" in Components first.
- The AMPR emulator and LZ4 packs are for PS5 games only and are left out for PS4 games.
- Not yet: updates (patch packages), DLC, and packages with a passcode other than all zeros.

### Page and console app
- Every game carries a PS5 (white) or PS4 (black) pill, first on its line, in Files, in the queue and in Convert.
- Which console a game is for comes from its title ID (CUSA, PPSA), else from the SDK its eboot.bin was built with, so homebrew is told apart too.

### PC
- alembic game-info shows a game's title ID, SDK and console.
- alembic fpkg-build and convert --to fpkg take --ps4-keys for PS4 games.

### Install
- The app is listed in ProsperoStore; install it from there, or copy alembic-app-0.3.2.ffpkg (or the .zip folder) to /data/homebrew for ShadowMount+.

repos.name: ps5-forever
repos.description: Battle.net launcher for World of Warcraft: Forever on PS5; Wine, RADV and automatic frame generation.
repos.readme:
# Forever Launcher

Run **Battle.net** on a jailbroken **PlayStation 5**.

Forever Launcher (`PPSA99030`) runs Battle.net and World of Warcraft through
Wine, using DirectX 12 on the PS5's own GPU. Choose the WoW version you want in
Battle.net: Retail, Classic, Classic Era, Anniversary, Forever, beta or PTR.
The launcher detects channel folders rather than keeping a list of versions.
The supplied settings use 4K output with HDR and frame generation.

In 01.000.014, Retail, Classic, Classic Era, Anniversary and the Forever beta
all start from Battle.net's **Play** button and were tested on a console.
Other channels, such as PTR or new versions, are detected the same way but have
not been tested; detection does not guarantee that every game build will render
or work online.

> [!NOTE]
> This launcher is for World of Warcraft. Other Battle.net games are not
> supported. A USB keyboard and mouse work in Battle.net and WoW.

> [!WARNING]
> **Alpha software.** Expect bugs. Forever Launcher is not made, approved or
> supported by Blizzard Entertainment, Sony Interactive Entertainment or Valve.
> Using unofficial software with an online game is at your own risk.

## Video

[![Watch Forever Launcher running on PS5](https://img.youtube.com/vi/hlHsBxf-G6Y/maxresdefault.jpg)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hlHsBxf-G6Y)

## What's new in 01.000.021

- **Adds PS5 VRR support for WoW at up to 120 Hz.** The game title now declares
  the retail VRR and high-frame-rate metadata instead of the older combination
  that disabled system VRR.
- **Keeps 119.88 Hz active in VRR mode.** Before the first frames, a VRR display
  may idle at its 48 Hz floor. Forever no longer mistakes that valid idle rate
  for failed 120 Hz and restores 59.94 Hz.
- On a compatible display, set PS5 **VRR** to **Automatic**. If VideoOut does
  not offer or accept the 119.88 Hz mode, Forever continues at 59.94 Hz.

01.000.020 repaired Battle.net signature setup, completed large add-on
downloads, and moved add-on staging into the bounded native worker.

Older release notes are on the [releases page](https://github.com/bizkut/ps5-forever/releases).

## What you need

- A **jailbroken PS5** that can run homebrew apps. Tested on firmware 5.50.
- **[ShadowMountPlus](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus)**, in a version that lets
  apps use `/data`. It installs the app; your games and settings live in `/data`.
- Enough **free space** on the console for the WoW versions you install: Classic
  versions need about 50–55 GB; Retail is much larger.
- A **Battle.net account** with access to the WoW version you want, with an
  **authenticator** enabled (see [Signing in to Battle.net](#signing-in-to-battlenet)).
- A **DualSense** controller. A USB keyboard also works.
- An **FTP server** on the console, only to add your own `Lossless.dll` or
  change settings files by hand. FSR 3 frame generation needs neither.

## Install

**ProsperoStore** (recommended): install
[ProsperoStore](https://github.com/darkxex/ProsperoStore/releases), then install
**Forever Launcher** from it. ProsperoStore also installs updates.

**By hand:**

1. Download `PPSA99030.zip` from the [latest release](https://github.com/bizkut/ps5-forever/releases/latest).
2. Unzip it. Copy the `PPSA99030` folder to a location ShadowMountPlus scans,
   such as `/data/homebrew/PPSA99030`. The app folder can also be on an external drive;
   games and settings remain in `/data/forever`.
3. Let ShadowMountPlus register it, then start **Forever Launcher** from the home screen.

## First start

1. The first start sets up the Windows files. This takes a few minutes. The app
   restarts by itself when it is done.
2. Forever Launcher downloads Blizzard's Battle.net installer and automatically
   continues past its fixed install-location page. Wait while Battle.net installs.
3. Sign in to Battle.net (see below).
4. In Battle.net, choose the World of Warcraft version you want, press
   **Install** and wait for the download, then press **Play**.

### Faster: copy WoW from a PC

If WoW is already installed on a PC, you can copy it to the console over your
home network instead of downloading it again. Battle.net then only checks the
files and downloads what is missing.

1. Start Forever Launcher once and install Battle.net (steps 1–3 above), then
   close the app.
2. On the PC, find your `World of Warcraft` folder. On Windows it is usually
   `C:\Program Files (x86)\World of Warcraft`. A Mac install
   (`/Applications/World of Warcraft`) works too; Battle.net replaces the Mac
   game files with the Windows ones.
3. With an FTP program, copy the whole folder, including the hidden files
   `.build.info` and `.product.db`, to the console as:

   ```text
   /data/forever/prefix/drive_c/Program Files (x86)/World of Warcraft
   ```

   Use a wired network if you can. Classic is about 50 GB; Retail is much larger.
4. Start Forever Launcher. In Battle.net, select the game. If it shows
   **Install**, use **Locate the game** below the button and choose
   `C:\Program Files (x86)\World of Warcraft`.
5. Battle.net checks the files and downloads only what is missing or newer.
   For a full check, use the gear next to **Play** → **Scan and Repair**.

Forever Launcher fixes the file permissions of copied folders at startup, so
you normally don't need to change them by hand. If it still says it can't
write to `/data/forever/prefix`, see [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting).

## Signing in to Battle.net

- Sign in with your **email address and password**, and choose to get a **code by email**
  when Battle.net asks to confirm the sign-in.
- Your account needs an **authenticator** enabled.
- Signing in with **Google, Apple, Facebook, Xbox, PlayStation or any other
  third-party account is not supported.**
- Forever Launcher does not implement credential capture. Battle.net keeps its
  own sign-in token in your user data folder so you stay signed in.

## Controls

| Press | Does |
| --- | --- |
| **Options** | Opens or closes the Forever menu while Battle.net is open |
| **F12** on a USB keyboard | Opens or closes the Forever menu while Battle.net is open |
| **L2** | Escape in Battle.net (closes an open Battle.net dialog or dropdown) |
| **L3 + R3** (press both sticks briefly) | Opens the on-screen keyboard |
| Hold the touchpad (still, about 0.4 s) | Voice-to-Text: speech is typed into WoW chat |

The controller is turned on in WoW by default (WoW's own gamepad mode).

With Voice-to-Text enabled, hold the touchpad still and speak into the DualSense
microphone. A red-dot **Listening** panel appears in the middle of the screen
while recording and disappears on release. While the text is in the chat box,
**Cross** sends it, **Circle**
cancels, and **Square** opens the on-screen keyboard to edit. **L1/R1** cycle
the chat channel through **/s /p /i /g /raid /r**. The DualSense **Mute** button
mutes the microphone: a muted mic types nothing.

In Battle.net, the mouse cursor hides after three seconds without pointer
movement. Move the pointer or click to show it again. A new visible cursor
shape also restarts the timer; the game's or app's own hidden cursor stays hidden.

## Forever menu

Open the menu over Battle.net with **Options**, or press **F12** on a USB
keyboard. Use the D-pad and Cross; press Circle or Options at the top level to
close, or click with a mouse. The menu can:

- turn frame generation, HDR and the performance overlay on or off;
- turn **Invert mouse scroll** on or off (USB mouse wheel only; on by default);
- turn **Voice-to-Text** On/Off (first use downloads a **190 MB speech model**);
- browse, install, update and remove add-ons for the selected WoW version;
- install a curated starter pack;
- remove Battle.net while keeping installed games and their settings;
- remove and reinstall Battle.net from a fresh installer download;
- close Battle.net and the app (**Exit Battle.net**).

**Proximity Voice Chat** is coming later; it is not available yet.

Each app start shows a ten-second hint for **Options** over Battle.net.

Open **Add-ons** before pressing Play. L1/R1 cycles through detected installed
WoW channels; Left/Right switches Installed, Updates, Find and Starter packs.
Cross opens or installs, Square updates the
selected add-on, Triangle updates all, and R3 removes after a confirmation whose
default is Cancel. In Find, type on a USB keyboard or choose **Search…** for the
on-screen keyboard (results filter as you type); **Add from GitHub link…** accepts `owner/repo` or its GitHub
URL. CurseForge-only rows say so and cannot be installed. GitHub, WoWInterface
and TukUI entries work without a key. Changes load the next time WoW starts, or
after typing `/reload` in WoW.

Install and update stream the ZIP through a dedicated native archive worker
instead of writing or unpacking it through Wine. The worker hashes the received
bytes, extracts into `C:\Forever\AddonStaging` with bounded parallel workers,
makes every file durable, and returns only a staged tree. AddonForge still
checks file types and the selected WoW client's TOCs before same-drive renames
replace live add-on folders. Interrupted replacements recover when Add-ons
reopens; backups are retained if recovery cannot finish safely.

If Battle.net needs another web renderer process, Add-ons pauses and releases its
helper process instead of blocking Battle.net. Close and reopen **Add-ons** to
resume; the process limit and Battle.net's updater/game reserve stay unchanged.

Add-ons are checked against the selected channel's product and client version,
and go into that channel's own `Interface/AddOns` folder. Find and Starter packs
cover Retail (including PTR/beta), Classic MoP, Anniversary, Classic Era and
Forever. Find uses [Forever's own GitHub add-on catalogue](https://github.com/bizkut/github-wow-addon-catalogue),
derived from [layday's GPL-3.0 catalogue](https://github.com/layday/github-wow-addon-catalogue),
and compatible WoWInterface/Tukui entries. Our list refreshes daily and the
launcher checks it at most once every 24 hours; offline use keeps the last good
cache or the build's bundled snapshot.
**Add from GitHub link…** remains available. Unknown products say “Add-ons aren't
supported for this WoW version yet”; they never receive another flavour's files.

For Wago add-ons, choose **Wago key** on the Add-ons page. Wago gives the key
for add-on managers to its Patreon supporters: subscribe at
[addons.wago.io/patreon](https://addons.wago.io/patreon), then copy the key it
gives you. The API key on Wago's account page is for publishing add-ons and
does not work here. Type the key, or choose **Read from file** after saving it
as the first line of `C:\Forever\Addons\wago-key.txt` (up to 256 characters).
A successful import deletes the file. The key is saved locally by AddonForge;
**Remove key** clears it. If Wago cannot be reached, it is saved as **set (not
checked)**. Without a key, Wago-only add-ons show **Wago key required**; all
other sources work without one.

If frame generation currently uses `fg=auto`, selecting it turns it off;
selecting it again turns it on. Frame generation and the performance overlay
use their live settings files; HDR applies the next time WoW starts. After
removing Battle.net, close and start Forever Launcher to install it again.

## Frame generation

Frame generation shows extra, generated frames between the frames WoW draws,
so motion looks smoother at up to 120 Hz. It is **on by default** (2x) and picks
its method by itself:

- With **your own copy of `Lossless.dll`** from
  [Lossless Scaling](https://store.steampowered.com/app/993090/Lossless_Scaling/)
  (version 3.2.2.0, or a build with the same shaders), it uses Lossless Scaling's
  frame generation. The file is not included and never downloaded.
- Without it, it uses **AMD FSR 3** frame generation, which needs no extra file.

The GPU game role declares PS5's retail **VRR + high-frame-rate** metadata.
With VRR set to **Automatic** in the PS5's Screen and Video settings and an
HDMI 2.1 VRR display, the console can vary refresh while WoW runs. The game
still requests the measured 119.88 Hz mode for 120 Hz/frame generation and
falls back to 59.94 Hz when the display does not take it. Battle.net's
maintenance desktop keeps its normal output path. There is no separate
Forever menu switch: the console and display settings remain authoritative.

To use Lossless Scaling:

1. On your PC, find `Lossless.dll` in your Lossless Scaling folder
   (Steam: `steamapps/common/Lossless Scaling/`).
2. Copy it by FTP to the console as:

   ```text
   /data/forever/prefix/drive_c/Lossless.dll
   ```

3. Restart WoW.

Settings live in `/data/forever/prefix/drive_c/wineps5-fg.txt`. Changes apply
while the game runs, within a second.

```text
fg=on method=auto mult=2 flow=1.0
```

| Option | Values |
| --- | --- |
| `fg` | `on`, `off`, or `auto` (on only while WoW renders below 70 fps) |
| `mult` | `2`, `3` or `4` frames shown for every frame WoW draws |
| `flow` | `0.25` to `1.0`: lower is cheaper, `1.0` looks best (Lossless Scaling only) |
| `method` | `auto` (Lossless Scaling when `Lossless.dll` is there, else FSR 3), `lossless`, or `fsr3` |

The on-screen display settings are in `/data/forever/prefix/drive_c/wineps5-hud.txt`
(`hud=on` or `hud=off`, `pos=tl`, `scale=2`); the Forever menu changes `hud`
without replacing the other options.

## WoW settings

WoW starts with settings tuned for the PS5: 4K output at half render scale,
HDR on, and the controller enabled. Each detected installed channel gets the
preset only when its own `WTF/Config.wtf` is missing. Existing settings are not
overwritten. The Forever menu changes only `HDROutput` for every detected
channel, leaving other settings, including `HDRFactor`, alone.

Automatic discovery currently scans
`C:\Program Files (x86)\World of Warcraft`. Custom C: or W: installations can
launch from Battle.net Play, but are not yet included in automatic settings,
Add-ons discovery or direct start.

### Start one channel directly

Create `/data/homebrew/PPSA99030/wine/direct-game` with just the channel folder
name, for example `_classic_era_` or `_retail_`, then start Forever Launcher.
The file is consumed once. If that channel is missing or incomplete, the log
explains why and Battle.net opens; another channel is never chosen instead.
An empty file prefers Classic beta, then Forever, then another complete
installed channel.

## Where your data is

Everything that is yours is in **`/data/forever`**: Battle.net, WoW, your
settings, `Lossless.dll` and the shader cache. The app folder
(`/data/homebrew/PPSA99030`) holds only the app.

Updating the app replaces only the app folder. Your games and settings stay.

## Updating

- **ProsperoStore** shows updates and installs them.
- **By hand:** close the app and replace only its `PPSA99030` app folder
  with the folder from the new zip. Do not delete `/data/forever`.

Every start checks the app's Windows files in `/data/forever`, including Wine's
system DLLs, and repairs any that differ from the app's own copies, because
mismatched copies can crash games during startup. The first start after an
update checks every file once (about 15–20 seconds); later starts take less than
a second.

## Uninstalling

Delete the app from the home screen (or delete `/data/homebrew/PPSA99030`), then
delete `/data/forever` to remove Battle.net, WoW and your settings.

## Privacy and support data

- Release logs retain aggregate input-health counters, not raw keyboard records,
  key usages or modifiers.
- Treat `/data/forever` as sensitive shared Wine-prefix storage. Never include
  registry hives, browser profiles, session/account files or saved credentials in
  support bundles, and review Wine/application logs and screenshots before sharing.

## Troubleshooting

- **"Forever Launcher can't write to ..." (permission denied)**: the app
  restarts its file helper once to repair folder permissions under
  `/data/forever`, then tries again. If the message remains, close the app and,
  on a PC, use FTP to set `/data/forever` and everything in it to permission
  `777`; then start Forever Launcher again.
- **Drives:** only `C:` and `W:` work inside Wine; `Z:` and network shares are
  not supported.
- **"Forever Launcher cannot use /data" (error 2 or 30)**: `/data` is missing
  or read-only. Update ShadowMountPlus to a version that lets apps use `/data`.
- **Battle.net sign-in fails**: use the email code and make sure an authenticator is
  enabled on your account. Third-party sign-in is not supported.
- **Battle.net reports only about 17 GB free**: Windows disk-space queries use the
  write broker's real storage counters for `/data/forever`. If the broker is
  unavailable or is from an older app version, they fall back to the title's
  synthetic 16 GiB free-space answer. The kernel log identifies the source with
  `wine: title disk space source=broker` or `source=synthetic`; restart the updated
  app so it can replace an older broker.
- **Frame generation does nothing**: check that `wineps5-fg.txt` says `fg=on`.
  Open the Forever menu from Battle.net to turn the performance overlay on; it
  shows `FG LOSSLESS` or `FG FSR3`. For Lossless Scaling, the file must be
  exactly `/data/forever/prefix/drive_c/Lossless.dll`.
- **Logs**: the console's kernel log (port 3232) shows what the app is doing.
  Lines starting with `forever:` describe setup.

## Building from source

The release is built by [GitHub Actions](.github/workflows/release.yml) from the
public sources listed in [`ps5/release/deps.json`](ps5/release/deps.json).
See [BUILDING.md](BUILDING.md).

## Credits

Forever Launcher is built on the work of many projects. Thank you to all of them.
Licences and details are in [NOTICE.md](NOTICE.md).

- [Proton](https://github.com/ValveSoftware/Proton) by Valve: the base this project starts from.
- [Wine](https://www.winehq.org/): runs Windows programs (LGPL-2.1-or-later).
- [vkd3d-proton](https://github.com/HansKristian-Work/vkd3d-proton) by Hans-Kristian Arntzen
  and contributors: DirectX 12 on Vulkan (upstream LGPL-2.1-or-later;
  this frame-generation build GPL-3.0-or-later).
- [DXVK](https://github.com/doitsujin/dxvk) by Philip Rebohle and contributors: DXGI (zlib).
- [Mesa](https://mesa3d.org/) and its RADV Vulkan driver (MIT).
- [PS5_Mesa](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Mesa), [PS5_Vulkan](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Vulkan)
  and [PS5_PayloadSDK](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_PayloadSDK) by mihawk-99: RADV, Vulkan
  and the SDK on PS5.
- [ps5-payload-sdk](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk) by John Törnblom.

  (GPL-3.0-or-later), with AMD [FidelityFX](https://gpuopen.com/fidelityfx-super-resolution-3/) shaders (MIT).
- [lsfg-vk](https://github.com/PancakeTAS/lsfg-vk) by PancakeTAS: the Vulkan Lossless Scaling frame-generation
  code that Eden's port builds on (GPL-3.0-or-later).

  used only from your own copy.

latestRelease.name: Forever Launcher 01.000.021
latestRelease.body:
### Forever Launcher 01.000.021

**Adds PS5 VRR support for WoW at up to 120 Hz.**

- The game title now declares the retail VRR and high-frame-rate metadata
  instead of the older combination that disabled system VRR.
- Before the first frames, a VRR display may idle at its 48 Hz floor. Forever
  now keeps the accepted 119.88 Hz mode instead of misreading that idle rate as
  failed 120 Hz and restoring 59.94 Hz.
- On a compatible display, set PS5 **VRR** to **Automatic**. If VideoOut does
  not offer or accept the 119.88 Hz mode, Forever continues at 59.94 Hz.

### Forever Launcher 01.000.020

**Repairs Battle.net signature setup and completes large add-on installs.**

- Incomplete Wine Trust and PE signature-provider registration is repaired
  through normal Wine setup before Battle.net starts. Verification now fails
  closed if no provider is registered.
- Continuously progressing add-on archives may download for up to 15 minutes,
  with a 30-second idle timeout. Errors identify body-transfer versus JSON
  failures.
- Polestar's full package includes all 24 folders, including the requested
  Brazilian Portuguese and database/navigation modules; Recorder remains a
  separate optional package.
- A bounded native worker hashes, extracts, synchronizes and activates add-ons
  outside Wine. Interrupted install and removal cleanup retains durable recovery
  proof instead of restoring partial folders.
- Existing 01.000.018 catalogue caches migrate automatically to the corrected
  package list.

### Forever Launcher 01.000.018

**Fixes missing multi-pack add-ons in Find.**

- Repositories that publish several independent add-ons now keep every release stream instead of showing only the first one.
- Spoken Books, Quests and Zones audio packs appear as separate Find entries, including **Spoken Zones Audio (All)** and **Spoken Zones Audio (Portuguese)**.
- Includes complete GitHub release pagination from 01.000.017, so older release streams install without silently selecting the wrong release.
- 01.000.017 was superseded before its homebrew-catalog submission after native testing found the same-repository listing bug.

### Forever Launcher 01.000.017

**More Spoken audio packs and complete GitHub add-on release discovery.**

- Find now includes **Spoken Zones Audio (All)** and **Spoken Zones Audio (Portuguese)** for English and Brazilian Portuguese place narration.
- Add-ons can now install from release streams older than a GitHub repository's first 100 releases. Forever follows every release page until it finds the requested stream.
- GitHub API, connection and malformed-response errors remain visible instead of silently installing the wrong release.

### Forever Launcher 01.000.016

**Faster Battle.net installs and Blizzard game downloads.**

- Reinstalling Battle.net took about 3 minutes instead of 12 on a test console: the update agent's many small writes are now combined into large ones, including its overlapped writes, which were never combined before.
- Downloads of every Blizzard game now combine their small writes too, not only WoW's. A StarCraft II download that spent 6–9 s of every 10 s waiting on the disk now spends about 3 s, so the connection is the limit.
- **Exit Battle.net** at the bottom of the Forever menu closes Battle.net properly and returns to the PS5 home screen, after a confirmation (Cancel is the default).
- **Invert mouse scroll** in the Forever menu reverses the USB mouse wheel. It is on by default; touchpad and stick scrolling are unchanged.
- Fixes a rare crash during Battle.net start-up when one of its processes ended at an unlucky moment.
- Battle.net's installer now continues automatically past its fixed install-location page, and its download follows web redirects itself, so a fresh install needs no controller input at that step.
- If Battle.net is reinstalled, Classic Era and Anniversary may need **Update** or **Scan and Repair** in Battle.net once before they start again.

**Add-ons: our own list, faster installs, instant removal.**

- The add-on list is now Forever's own, refreshed daily, with 408 Forever entries. Find and Starter packs include the Polestar, Lore Forever and Spoken packs, and each pack can be updated by itself.
- Large add-on installs are much faster: Lore Forever installs in about 2-3 minutes instead of more than 10.
- Installs and updates show progress text (download percentage and unpacked files).
- Removing an add-on is instant. The leftover files are deleted in the background once the Add-ons page is closed, and reopening the page pauses that cleanup.

### Forever Launcher 01.000.015

**New: Voice-to-Text for WoW chat.** Hold the touchpad and speak; your words are typed into WoW's chat box as you talk.

- Turn it on in the Forever menu (**Voice-to-Text: On**). The first time, it downloads a 190 MB speech model (Whisper small, multilingual) and checks it before use. It is off by default.
- In WoW, hold the touchpad still for about half a second. The controller buzzes, a red-dot **Listening** panel appears in the middle of the screen, and WoW's chat box opens on your last chat channel. Release when you finish speaking.
- The text waits in the chat box: **Cross** sends it, **Circle** cancels, **Square** opens the on-screen keyboard to correct it, and **L1/R1** switch the channel through /s, /p, /i, /g, /raid and /r.
- Speech is recognised on the PS5 itself, on the GPU, using whisper.cpp. Nothing is uploaded, and audio is never saved. The microphone is only open while you hold the touchpad.
- The DualSense **Mute** button still mutes the microphone: a muted microphone types nothing.
- Touchpad clicks and drags work as before. With Voice-to-Text on, a touchpad press held still for half a second starts dictation instead of holding the mouse button.
- Uses about 1 GB of graphics memory once you first dictate, until WoW closes. Tested in WoW on one console with English speech; other languages are recognised by the same model but have not been tested.
- **Proximity Voice Chat** is listed in the Forever menu as coming later.

Other changes:

- Add-ons Find: results now filter as you type with the on-screen keyboard, not only after you close it.
- Downloads follow web redirects themselves: the PS5's built-in redirect handling returned empty files. This fixes the speech-model download. The Battle.net installer uses the same handling but has not been retested on a console.

### Forever Launcher 01.000.014

- Detects installed WoW channels without a launch-version list, including Retail, Classic, Classic Era, Anniversary, Forever, beta, PTR and future channel names.
- A one-shot `wine/direct-game` file can select a channel folder such as `_retail_`; an unavailable selection never starts another version.
- Missing-only Config.wtf presets and the HDR switch apply to every detected channel.
- Add-ons lists installed channels and selects source flavours from the product and the client's own version resource. Installs, update records and removals stay in the selected channel. Unknown products are not supported for add-ons.
- Add-ons Find and Starter packs now cover every supported version: Retail, Classic (MoP), Classic Era, Anniversary and Forever. Find uses the community GitHub add-on catalogue (GPL-3.0), WoWInterface and Tukui. The GitHub list refreshes at most once a day and has a built-in copy for offline use.
- Pressing Play on Classic, Classic Era and Anniversary works again: Battle.net's `WoWClassic.exe` spelling now matches the files on disk.
- After a Play, the app remembers that version's safe start options (no sign-in data) for later direct starts.
- Fixes Battle.net crashing while the Add-ons page was open: Battle.net's own windows now get priority over the add-on manager.
- The start-up hint "OPTIONS Forever menu" shows on every start for 10 seconds.
- The mouse cursor hides after 3 seconds without movement on the Battle.net screen too.
- Faster Battle.net downloads and Scan and Repair: game data writes are buffered across several files and positions, and Battle.net's update agent reuses memory instead of preparing new memory each time. On one console a Retail download ran 21 MB/s against 12 MB/s on 01.000.013 when the disk was the limit.
- Automatic discovery is limited to the default WoW install root. Custom C:/W: paths can launch from Battle.net Play.
- Add-ons needs a recognized game version; an unknown or future version can launch but may not have a compatible catalogue. Installing from Wago with a real key, Update all and Reinstall/Uninstall Battle.net are not yet console-tested.
- Console checks on a private build: Retail, Classic (MoP), Classic Era, Anniversary and the Forever beta all start from Battle.net Play.

### Forever Launcher 01.000.013

- Options opens the Forever menu over Battle.net; F12 opens it from a USB keyboard. The menu controls frame generation, HDR, the performance overlay and Add-ons, and can Reinstall or Uninstall Battle.net.
- L2 is now Back in Battle.net. The old in-WoW overlay hold has been removed.
- Add-ons (AddonForge) has Find search by name or description, GitHub link installation and a personal Wago API key page. Installing from Wago with a real key is not yet tested.
- A short start-up hint shows the Options menu and L2 Back controls until the Forever menu has been opened once.
- The recommended `Config.wtf` now uses `RenderFormat 1`.
- Start-up repairs stale root-owned permissions under `/data/forever` without following symbolic links or changing hard-linked files.
- All prefix DLLs are kept identical to the app's Wine build.
- Faster Battle.net downloads with write buffering: measured about 3.9 → 12 MB/s on one console.
- Reinstall/Uninstall Battle.net has not been tested on a console yet.

### Forever Launcher 01.000.012

- Fixes WoW freezing on the loading screen about half the time at start (a startup crash): the app now keeps Wine's system DLLs in `/data/forever` identical to the ones it loads. The first start after updating copies these files once and takes about 2 minutes.
- Battle.net no longer asks to update installed games on every start: Wine now reports the folder permissions its Agent expects.
- WoW and Battle.net show their own mouse cursors, including WoW's gauntlet and Battle.net's text and link cursors, with the click point in the right place.
- On most Battle.net pages, the controller's D-pad moves between buttons and links, and Triangle presses.
- World of Warcraft Classic beta is the default game again; the final WoW: Forever channel still works when selected in Battle.net.
- Fixes the final channel's executable name (`_forever_/Wow.exe`), so its recommended settings install and direct start finds it.
- Faster parallel file writes: write-broker requests now use 16 connections instead of one shared by all Windows threads. PS5 benchmark: 32 KiB writes from 4–8 threads improved from ~16 to ~30 MiB/s; single-thread writes are unchanged.
  Real Battle.net download/update speedups have not yet been measured.
- Installs recommended `Config.wtf` independently for final and beta without replacing user settings.
- Fixes WoW 1.60.1.70425 black screen/Error #132 before D3D12.
- Reports a generic Wine/Linux system identity instead of Sony/PlayStation 5 branding while preserving real hardware capabilities.
- Release logs no longer include raw keyboard records.
- Fixes endless loading on Battle.net's password sign-in page.
- If the Battle.net installer download fails, the launcher retries from Blizzard's direct download link.
- Missing `Program Files` and `Program Files (x86)` folders are created at start, so the installer accepts its default location.
- The installer no longer flickers.
- Windows programs see the console's real free disk space.
- The purple desktop background is back.
- Drives: `C:` and `W:` only; `Z:` and network paths are not supported.

01.000.010 was not published: its build failed on a compiler warning in the new cursor code.

The `01.000.007` workflow failed before publication because of stale import-policy entries. `01.000.008` removed only the obsolete `wineps5` `strlen`/`strstr` policy rows; the remaining import checks stay enabled.

### About Forever Launcher

- This Battle.net launcher is designed for World of Warcraft: Forever.
- It might be used to install other games. A USB keyboard and mouse work in Battle.net and WoW.
- Your games and settings live in `/data/forever`; updating the app keeps them.
- Frame generation is on by default: AMD FSR 3, or Lossless Scaling when you add your own `Lossless.dll` at `/data/forever/prefix/drive_c/Lossless.dll`.
- Sign in to Battle.net with your email and a code sent by email; your account needs an authenticator. Third-party sign-in is not supported.

repos.name: console-shelf-ps5
repos.description: Native PS5 library for your games and emulators, with Grid, Swipe and a customisable Shelf play room. First beta tested on firmware 12.20.
repos.readme:
# isShelf

**Your consoles. Your games. Your play room.** isShelf by **Iswebro** brings your existing PS5 homebrew libraries together in Grid, Swipe and a customisable Shelf room.

A native C++/SDL app, tested on PS5 firmware **12.20**, with a separate [browser design preview](index.html). Choose your preferred installed emulator, keep your games in their existing folders and make the room your own. The catalogue has 52 system categories; a console illustration does **not** mean an emulator is available for it.

![isShelf running on PS5: PlayStation consoles arranged on deep shelves, with a personal video on the room TV](docs/images/ps5/shelf-room.webp)

*Actual PS5 capture, 26 October 2026. Manufacturer startup videos visible on the TV are personal overrides, supplied separately. isShelf includes its own original intro animations.* [More PS5 screenshots and a short recording](docs/SCREENSHOTS.md).

## Download for PS5

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [PPSA99541.zip](https://github.com/Iswebro/console-shelf-ps5/releases/download/v0.1.0-beta.1/PPSA99541.zip) | Installable PS5 app. |
| [Complete source and relink kit](https://github.com/Iswebro/console-shelf-ps5/releases/download/v0.1.0-beta.1/isShelf-v0.1.0-beta.1-Source-and-Relink.zip) | Matching source, objects, libraries and build instructions. |
| [SHA256SUMS.txt](https://github.com/Iswebro/console-shelf-ps5/releases/download/v0.1.0-beta.1/SHA256SUMS.txt) | Full SHA-256 values for every payload. |

Follow the [installation, recovery and removal guide](docs/PS5-INSTALL.md). Download [MANIFEST.json](https://github.com/Iswebro/console-shelf-ps5/releases/download/v0.1.0-beta.1/MANIFEST.json) for per-file verification and [HARDWARE-CHECKS.json](https://github.com/Iswebro/console-shelf-ps5/releases/download/v0.1.0-beta.1/HARDWARE-CHECKS.json) for tested scope. This beta is verified on **firmware 12.20** with the existing homebrew enabler, ShadowMountPlus, ELF loader and FTP service. No PC host is needed to run it. Emulators and games are supplied separately.

isShelf is also [listed on ProsperoStore](https://prosperostore.net/app/PPSA99541/). See [store submission status](docs/STORE-LISTINGS.md) for the other destinations.

## New to isShelf? Start here

| I want to… | Guide |
| --- | --- |
| Get started, learn the controls and choose an emulator | [Beginner's guide](docs/BEGINNERS.md) |
| Put my own videos or pictures on the room TV | [Personal TV media, step by step](docs/PERSONAL-TV.md) |
| Choose consoles, arrange a shelf, change logos or set the clock | [Room and customisation guide](docs/ROOM.md) |
| Install, update, back up or remove isShelf | [Installation and recovery](docs/PS5-INSTALL.md) |
| Find missing games or understand a launch message | [Troubleshooting](docs/BEGINNERS.md#troubleshooting) |

## Make it yours

- Browse 52 systems in Grid, a curved card-free Swipe carousel, or a lit display Shelf. Shelf places the console illustrations directly on deep walnut counters in one continuous gaming-lounge scene, with a subtle selection light. It pages through the collection instead of stretching a shelf photograph into each row. All layouts share sort, visibility and favourite choices. Grid can also use classic text cards.
- In Shelf, **L1/R1** (or Page Up/Down) swaps eight consoles at a time while the room stays still. **Sort & filter → Shelf pages** can instead show one curated display of up to eight consoles chosen in **Consoles**. All consoles, emulator/game availability, favourites, search and sorting apply to the collection. Small preview screens fit fewer systems per page.
- **Play room** settings customise the TV with selected-console artwork, original intro pictures and silent animations for all 52 systems, a personal PNG, a clock and Shelf logo, a personal message, or rotating favourite games. Personal intro clips and pictures take priority over the matching Shelf original. Mark a game with Triangle in the native library, or its star in the preview. TV content is clipped to the photographed screen with subtle glass reflections; the search bar ends before it. Intros can apply to installed emulators or all systems, and optional fine-grain static can mark missing emulators or games. [Room controls and personal media](docs/ROOM.md).
- Missing emulators use black-and-white console artwork by default. Appearance → Missing emulator artwork can keep everything in full colour instead. This does not hide systems or change launch support; the browser uses its dated demo inventory, while the native app uses discovery.
- In Swipe, the selected console sits forward in the centre; neighbours recede in size, depth and angle. Motion eases to a stop in 420 ms and retargets immediately when direction changes.
- Loop through Swipe using the stick/D-pad on a standard-mapped controller, keyboard arrows, mouse dragging or touch. Click a side console to centre it, then select the centre console to explore. The browser honours reduced-motion preferences and remembers the selected system. The final native navigation, settings, persistence and restart checks passed on firmware 12.20. Automated controller checks are simulated.
- Switch between **All consoles**, **Emulator or games**, and **Favourites**. Availability uses recorded emulator routes, built-in PS5/PS4 routes, or example games in the preview; the native app uses real discovery. Choices persist on the device.
- Search, filter by brand or evidence level, sort in several ways, and save favorites.
- Open the settings gear for Appearance, Sort & filter, Consoles and Play room. Search the console picker, toggle individual systems or whole brands, and show/hide search results in one click. These choices persist on the device.
- Open a console detail page, choose a preferred detected emulator and browse its discovered games. The separate browser demo uses an example inventory and never launches PS5 software.
- A persistent launch panel explains the action before selection: [Open emulator library](previews/launch-library-only.png) for menu-only routes, or [Play game](previews/launch-direct-play.png) for a direct RetroArch route. It follows the preferred emulator and stays on screen while browsing.
- Choose Vector, Gaming, Classic mint or Jade for the app logo. Vector is the default. The selected logo also appears on the room's clock/message screen and bundled intros; personal videos keep their own contents.

See the [mobile Swipe view](previews/carousel-mobile.png) and [Switch 2 icon](previews/switch2-3d-card.png). Nintendo's press photo informed the Switch 2 illustration but is **not** displayed or bundled.

## Inventory and compatibility

The [demo system catalogue](docs/SYSTEMS.md) comes from a dated PS5 setup snapshot. Its 46 RetroArch core mappings and example game names are **not** a live scan of another user's console. A mapped core or listed emulator does not guarantee a game runs. In the browser demo, “Emulator or games” shows 51 of 52 cards; Switch 2 is the hardware-reference-only card and has no launch route. The native app instead starts empty and can use its [read-only scanner](docs/DISCOVERY.md) for the owner's actual inventory.

The [first native PS5 beta](https://github.com/Iswebro/console-shelf-ps5/releases/tag/v0.1.0-beta.1) is available. Its C++/SDL runtime renders the three layouts, discovers existing libraries, saves preferences and explains each launch route before selection. The owner confirmed foreground PSXS5/PS5SX2/PS5SX3 libraries and direct Nintendo 64 play through RetroArch after a normal restart. Opening can still show black before the interface, and other emulator/native-title routes remain experimental. [Publication evidence](docs/verification/v0.1.0-beta.1-publication-2026-10-26.json) records all seven public download hashes, 242 app members and 507 source-archive members. The matching source kit cold-relinks to the installed program exactly.

![Nintendo systems in isShelf on a real PS5](docs/images/ps5/shelf-nintendo.webp)

![Choose which consoles to show individually in the native PS5 app](docs/images/ps5/settings-consoles.webp)

These are native PS5 captures. [The screenshot gallery](docs/SCREENSHOTS.md) also shows Appearance, Sort & filter and Play room settings. PC development previews remain under `previews/` and are labelled separately.

## PS5 home-screen artwork

[Glass and Light](assets/backgrounds/shelf-ps5-home-v2.png) is the new 3840 × 2160 selection background. A much larger Shelf mark sits directly over sculptural dark glass and restrained mint/cyan lighting, with a quiet left side and upper strip for the PS5 interface. The [logo is real SVG geometry with no background](assets/branding/shelf-gaming-mark.svg); a [transparent PNG](assets/branding/shelf-gaming-mark.png) is also included. The published app uses the Vector home tile; Gaming, Classic mint and Jade remain available as in-app choices.

The previous [static composition](assets/backgrounds/shelf-ps5-home-v1.png) is retained. The [prompt and composition notes](assets/backgrounds/shelf-ps5-home-v2.prompt.txt) record built-in image generation for the 1672 × 941 glass plate and direct 4K vector composition. Run `node tools/build-home-art.js` to reproduce the composition with Playwright and an available browser. The PS5-format `pic0.dds` and `pic1.dds` are included in the published app. The owner’s console captures confirm the Vector home tile and Glass and Light background.

## Development check

The preview itself needs no build step. With Node.js and npm, run `npm ci` and `npm test` for the browser interaction and icon-integrity check. The test uses an installed Microsoft Edge when available; otherwise install Playwright's Chromium with `npx playwright install chromium`. Tests leave the checked-in screenshots alone; set `SHELF_CAPTURE_PREVIEWS=1` to regenerate them intentionally. Run `npm run test:native` for the native model using an existing Visual Studio C++ toolset on Windows, or a C++17 compiler on Linux. See [native build notes](native/README.md).

## Credits and license

The application source in this repository is [GPL-3.0](LICENSE). The generated icons have separate [image credits and reuse terms](assets/CREDITS.md). [Third-party project credits](THIRD_PARTY.md) distinguish incorporated GPL platform/build source, rendering dependencies and emulator references. No emulator binaries, games, ROMs, BIOS, keys, proprietary firmware/runtime files or user credentials are included. Console and game names are used for identification; this project is not affiliated with their manufacturers.
