latestRelease.name: isShelf v0.1.0-beta.1 — first PS5 prototype
latestRelease.body:
isShelf by Iswebro is a native PS5 library front end for your existing games and emulators. This first public beta was tested on firmware **12.20**.

## Download and install

Download **PPSA99541.zip** to install the app. Compare its full SHA-256 with **SHA256SUMS.txt**, then follow **INSTALL.md**. The **MANIFEST.json** attachment lists every app file. **ROOM.md** explains TV displays and personal intro clips.

The separately named **Source-and-Relink.zip** is the complete matching source, application objects, replaceable libraries, build instructions and license notices; it is not the installable app.

## What is included

- Native C++/SDL interface with Grid, a curved Swipe carousel and a furnished Shelf play room.
- 52 system categories, real library discovery, search, sorting, favourites and individual console visibility. A category or illustration does not imply an emulator is available.
- Saved settings and preferred emulators; Vector, Gaming, Classic mint and Jade logos; optional monochrome artwork for missing emulators.
- Customisable TV displays, original silent isShelf intros and personal media overrides.
- Controller navigation and a three-second Circle hold to close. No PC preview or Node.js is needed to run the installed app.

## Requirements and verified launch scope

Use your existing homebrew enabler, ShadowMountPlus, console-local ELF loader on port 9021 and ftpsrv on port 2121. Discovery currently needs the console FTP service available on your trusted local network. This download does not set up a jailbreak or change your firmware, network settings or payload order.

In our tests I've verified a normal restart, saved settings, all three layouts, foreground opening of the **PSXS5, PS5SX2 and PS5SX3 emulator libraries**, and a selected **Nintendo 64 game through RetroArch**. Standalone emulators open their own library; the launch panel explains this before selection. See **HARDWARE-CHECKS.json** for the accepted scope.

## Known limits

Opening can still show a black screen before the interface. Other dedicated-emulator and native-title routes remain experimental. Only firmware 12.20 is currently verified. No emulators, games, BIOS files, disc keys, console firmware or personal startup videos are included.

## Source and credits

The executable is unchanged from compiled source [5c34e67](https://github.com/Iswebro/console-shelf-ps5/tree/5c34e67aba3e51ca209d56215f97b586ff58c1e5). All 242 installed files were verified by raw readback; matching source cold-relink and clean rebuild checks are recorded in the repository. Only the installation document changes for publication.

Original isShelf interface and features by **Iswebro**. Thanks to **SkaRift / Jewel Case**, **BlackBearReloaded**, **Kauan Silva Lopes / Estante**, the SDK, SDL and other upstream contributors. Full pinned provenance, licenses and artwork credits are in [THIRD_PARTY.md](https://github.com/Iswebro/console-shelf-ps5/blob/5c34e67aba3e51ca209d56215f97b586ff58c1e5/THIRD_PARTY.md) and the bundled notices.

repos.name: JewelCase
repos.description: A home-screen ROM launcher for jailbroken PS5 consoles. Browse every system's games as cartridges and discs with box art fetched automatically, and launch each one in the right emulator.
repos.readme:
A home-screen ROM launcher for jailbroken PS5 consoles.
Every system's games on one shelf, as cartridges and discs with box art, each started in the right emulator.

Download the latest release

--- ![Carousel](docs/screenshots/carousel.jpg) | | | |---|---| | ![A system tab](docs/screenshots/snes.jpg) | ![Details screen](docs/screenshots/details.jpg) | | ![Settings](docs/screenshots/settings.jpg) | | ## Features - **One launcher for everything.** NES to Xbox 360, sorted into tabs by system, with **Recently Played** and **Favorites** tabs. - **Real-looking media.** Every game is drawn as its system's cartridge, card or disc, with its cover printed on it, in a carousel with reflections on a glossy floor. - **Automatic box art.** Covers download from the [libretro thumbnail collection](https://github.com/libretro-thumbnails) and are matched by file name, ignoring region tags and punctuation. Systems that collection lacks (like Switch) get the box front from the [LaunchBox Games Database](https://gamesdb.launchbox-app.com). Your own art always takes priority. - **Labels, not boxes.** Cartridge labels show the box art without the box's system banner and ratings. Discs are printed edge to edge with the art and the game's title logo, inside a silver rim around a clear hub, with the system's band on PS1, PS2 and GameCube discs (GameCube discs are the smaller 8 cm size). When there's a scan of the real disc, that's used instead: from the [LaunchBox Games Database](https://gamesdb.launchbox-app.com) for every disc system, and from [GameTDB](https://www.gametdb.com) for GameCube and Wii, found by the game ID in the disc image. - **Standalone emulators first.** Jewel Case starts each game in a dedicated PS5 emulator app when you have one installed, and falls back to RetroArch with a matching core. - **Details screen** for each game: its year, genre, developer, players and description from the LaunchBox Games Database, an in-game screenshot behind it (from libretro-thumbnails, or its title screen when there's none), its emulator and when you last played it. Square shows the file, region and size. - **Updates and DLC** sit with their game instead of showing as extra games. With ProsperoEden, Switch updates and DLC just work from one folder; for other emulators an amber or green chip shows whether they're installed yet ([how it works](#updates-and-dlc)). - **Feels like a console menu.** Soft rain sounds (your own MP3s instead, if you add some), a low retro boop as you move between games, and a rain effect; each can be turned off. Starting a game sends it off the screen: discs spin up, cartridges turn, and both fly away. - **Native app.** It has its own home-screen icon, installs with ShadowMountPlus, and needs no browser or Homebrew Launcher. ## Requirements - A jailbroken PS5 with an **ELF loader** listening on port 9021. etaHEN has one built in; a standalone ELF loader works too. Jewel Case sends small helper payloads to it. Tested on firmware 13.42 with etaHEN. - **ShadowMountPlus**, or another way to install a homebrew app folder. - One or more emulators: | System | Emulator used (first one found) | |---|---| | PlayStation | SwanStationPS5, then PSXS5, then RetroArch (SwanStation, PCSX ReARMed, Beetle PSX) | | PlayStation 2 | PS5SX2, then RetroArch (LRPS2) | | Nintendo 64 | Mupen64Plus PS5, then RetroArch (Mupen64Plus-Next, ParaLLEl) | | GameCube / Wii | Porpoise, then RetroArch (Dolphin) | | DS / 3DS | PS5CEMU-HAR, then RetroArch (melonDS, DeSmuME, Azahar) | | Wii U | PS5CEMU-HAR | | Dreamcast | PSFlycast, then RetroArch (Flycast) | | Switch | ProsperoEden | | Xbox / Xbox 360 | XPSemu / PS5X360 | | Everything else | RetroArch (PPSA99169) with the matching core | ## Install 1. Download `PPSA75837.zip` from [Releases](../../releases). 2. Extract it and copy the `PPSA75837` folder to `/data/homebrew/` on your PS5. 3. Install it with ShadowMountPlus, then start **Jewel Case** from the home screen. To update, overwrite the files in the same folder. Your settings, favorites and downloaded covers are kept in `/data/jewelcase`, so an update never touches them. ## Adding games Put each system's games in its own folder under `/data/roms` (or `/mnt/usb0/roms` on a USB drive): ``` /data/roms/snes/Super Mario World (USA).sfc /data/roms/psx/Final Fantasy VII (USA).m3u /data/roms/ps2/Kingdom Hearts (USA).iso ``` **Settings → Create system folders** makes every folder for you. It also writes a guide in `/data/roms` listing each folder and the file types it takes. After adding games, use **Settings → Rescan games**. PS1 games in SwanStationPS5's and PSXS5's own `games` folders (`/data/SwanStationPS5/games`, `/data/PSXS5/games`, or a `SwanStationPS5` / `PSXS5` folder on a drive) are listed too. No-Intro / Redump style file names, such as `Super Mario World (USA).sfc`, match covers best. To use your own art, put a `.png` or `.jpg` named like the game next to its file, or in a `covers` folder there. Music: Jewel Case comes with a soft rain track (generated by `tools/make_rain.py`, no recording or license involved). To play your own instead, put MP3 files in `/data/jewelcase/music`. Jewel Case creates this folder on first run. ### Updates and DLC **Switch with ProsperoEden (v1.005 or newer): nothing to install.** ProsperoEden applies a game's newest update and all its DLC every time the game starts, from its own game files folder only: each game in a folder of its own in its `roms` folder, with the update and DLC files beside it (any names). ``` /roms/Super Mario Odyssey/ Super Mario Odyssey.nsp Super Mario Odyssey 1.1 update.nsp Super Mario Odyssey DLC.nsp ``` The game files folder is the one picked in ProsperoEden's **Settings → Game files** (`/data/prosperoeden` if you never picked one). Jewel Case reads that setting and lists the Switch games there too. Everything in a game's folder shows as that one game. A `firmware` folder in a Switch games folder is skipped. **Updates next to a game somewhere else** (such as `/data/roms/switch`) also show as part of that game, even with a hash for a name: Jewel Case reads the title ID inside each `.nsp` / `.nsz`. The game shows **Update available** in amber. Open its details (□), press □ again for **File info**, then **✕ Update**: Jewel Case moves the update and DLC into ProsperoEden's `updates` folder (renamed after the game, like `Super Mario Odyssey update [0100000000010800][v327680].nsp`), where ProsperoEden applies them every time the game starts. Still one copy of each file. The game then shows **Updated** in green, and Update isn't offered again. A game with no update files shows no update chip. An update in an `updates`, `update` or `dlc` folder of your own shows only with its game. **Other emulators** (Wii U in Cemu, older ProsperoEden versions) need updates and DLC installed into their own storage once, from their own menu. Jewel Case starts games; it doesn't install anything into an emulator. Keep the files next to the game: ``` /data/roms/wiiu/Some Game.wua /data/roms/wiiu/Some Game update.wua ``` Jewel Case shows these as one game. It recognises updates and DLC by "update", "upd", "patch" or "DLC" in the name, or by the Switch title ID in brackets (an update's ends in `800`). To install one, with no extra copies: 1. In the emulator, use its install option and pick the file straight from your Jewel Case games folder. 2. In Jewel Case, open the game's details (□), press □ again for **File info**, then **✕ Mark installed**. 3. Optional: delete the file from the games folder. The emulator keeps its installed copy, and Jewel Case still shows **Update 1.1 installed**. Amber **not installed** means the file is there but not marked yet; green **installed** means you've marked it. A newer update file turns it amber again. Jewel Case can't look inside the emulator, so "installed" is whatever you marked; **✕ Mark not installed** undoes it. Marks are kept in `/data/jewelcase/installed.json`. The update's version in that chip comes from its file name (`1.0`, `v1.2.0`, `[v131072]`). ## Controls | Carousel | | Details screen | | |---|---|---|---| | Left / Right | choose a game | Left / Right | previous / next game | | L1 / R1 | change system (only these) | Cross | play | | L2 / R2 | jump 10 games | Triangle | favorite | | Cross | play | Square | technical info | | Triangle | favorite | Circle | back | | Square | details screen | Square | file info (Update, or marking updates installed) | | Right stick | turn the game around | Right stick | turn the game around | | Options | settings | | | | Circle | close Jewel Case | | | ## Building from source See [BUILDING.md](BUILDING.md). In short, on Linux or WSL: ```sh make # builds the helpers and the app into dist/PPSA75837 make host # PC test build, needs SDL2 (build-host/jewelcase --fsroot ) ``` ## Known limitations - SwanStationPS5, PSXS5 (PS1) and PS5SX2 (PS2) open their own main menu instead of starting the game: pick the game again there. - Cover matching works from file names, so heavily renamed files may get no cover. Add your own art for those. - Jewel Case can't install updates or DLC into an emulator, or check what the emulator has installed. ProsperoEden applies them by itself from its game files folder; for other emulators, install them from the emulator's menu and mark them in File info. ## Credits Jewel Case by **SkaRift**. Built on [ps5-native-app-boilerplate](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-native-app-boilerplate) (BlackBearReloaded) and the [PS5 payload SDK](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk), with SDL2, cJSON, stb, dr_mp3 and the Poppins font; the cover helper's HTTPS uses curl and OpenSSL (from PacBrew) with Mozilla's root certificates. The rain music and the menu sounds are generated by Jewel Case's own code (`tools/make_rain.py`), not recorded. The cartridges, cards and discs are rendered from CC BY 4.0 models by Steven-Bennis, HippoStance, Karolina D, Vxcl, Pcwer, crocoman2019 and enjoyboy, and the N64 cartridge from a CC BY-NC 4.0 model by ejpman ([credits](assets/media/CREDITS.md)). Box art and logos come from [libretro-thumbnails](https://github.com/libretro-thumbnails), game info, more box art and disc scans from the [LaunchBox Games Database](https://gamesdb.launchbox-app.com) and [GameTDB](https://www.gametdb.com). Thanks to the etaHEN and ShadowMountPlus developers and to the authors of every emulator listed above. See [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md). Jewel Case includes no games, BIOS files or covers. Use backups you made yourself. ## License [GNU GPL v3](LICENSE).

latestRelease.name: Jewel Case 1.1.1
latestRelease.body:
# Jewel Case 1.1.1

SwanStationPS5 support, tidier Switch updates, and a few fixes.

## What's new

**PS1: SwanStationPS5**
- darkxex's SwanStationPS5 is now supported and used ahead of PSXS5. Like PSXS5, it opens its
  own main menu, where you pick the game.
- PS1 games in SwanStationPS5's and PSXS5's own folders (`/data/SwanStationPS5/games`,
  `/data/PSXS5/games`, or a `SwanStationPS5` / `PSXS5` folder on a drive) now show up in
  Jewel Case too.

**Switch**
- Update and DLC files with hash names (like `001d8d5a7fe8d0cbd148ff67d3b830a1.nsp`) no longer
  show as extra games. Jewel Case reads the title ID inside each file and groups it with its
  game.
- **Update** in File info (Square, then Square again) moves a game's update and DLC into
  ProsperoEden's updates folder, where ProsperoEden applies them. The game then shows
  **Updated**.
- A `firmware` folder in your Switch games folder no longer shows up as a game.
- Updates kept in an `updates`, `update` or `dlc` folder of your own only show with their game.

**Details screen and feel**
- Simpler update chip: **Update available** (amber) or **Updated** (green), and nothing when
  a game has no update files. No more confusing file version numbers like v0 or v327680.
- Turning a game round with the right stick now reflects its back on the floor, not its front.
- The rain music is quieter by default (40%).

## Install

1. Download `PPSA75837.zip` below.
2. Extract it and copy the `PPSA75837` folder to `/data/homebrew/` on your PS5 (to update,
   copy it over your existing one).
3. Install it with ShadowMountPlus and start Jewel Case from the home screen.

Needs an ELF loader on port 9021 (etaHEN's, or a standalone one). Tested on firmware 13.42.
Your settings, favorites and covers in `/data/jewelcase` are kept. See `README.txt` in the app
folder for folders, controls and troubleshooting.

## Known limitations

- SwanStationPS5, PSXS5 (PS1) and PS5SX2 (PS2) open their own main menu instead of starting the
  game; pick it again there.
- Jewel Case can't install updates or DLC into an emulator itself; ProsperoEden doesn't need
  it, other emulators install them from their own menu.

repos.name: Prospero-Hi-Fi
repos.description: A Music Player for hombrew enabled PS5 with lossless audio as the main focus. It's heavily based on my MiSTer Hi-FI project.
repos.readme:
# Prospero Hi-Fi

Prospero Hi-Fi is a music player for PS5 homebrew, based on my NX Hi-Fi project and its MiSTer Hi-Fi roots. It brings internal, M.2, USB and network music playback, physical audio CDs, album artwork, an equalizer and remote control from a browser or NX Hi-Fi.

Supported audio formats and codecs: **MP3, FLAC, PCM WAV and Ogg Vorbis**.

## Getting started

1. Extract the ready-to-use ShadowMount+ folder ZIP on your computer.
2. Copy the complete `PPSA99287` folder to `/data/homebrew/PPSA99287/` on your PS5. Keep all included files and subfolders together.
3. With your jailbreak, kstuff and ShadowMount+ active, scan/register the homebrew folder and launch **Prospero Hi-Fi** from the PS5 home screen.
4. Put music in the appropriate folder below, choose its source and select a song.

| Storage | Default music folder |
| --- | --- |
| Internal Storage | `/data/music` |
| M.2 Storage | `/mnt/ext1/Music` |
| USB Storage | `/mnt/usb0/Music` through `/mnt/usb7/Music` |
| USB Extended Storage | `/mnt/ext0/Music` |

Create the `Music` folder on an external drive if it does not exist. Select a storage source and press **Triangle** to choose a different folder. Each external mount remembers its own music folder.

Internal Storage is always visible. M.2 and USB entries appear only when the corresponding volume is mounted and accessible. Physical Disc appears only when a supported USB optical drive is detected, even if no CD is inserted. Drive detection refreshes in the background.

The current target setup is **PS5 firmware 13.60 with Y2JB and ShadowMount+**. Older firmware compatibility depends on the homebrew setup and has not been fully verified. If your setup does not already grant storage access, a local ELF loader must be listening on port **9021**; Prospero submits its bundled access helper automatically.

For network features, connect your PS5 through its system settings first. Existing settings are kept when you replace the application folder. Use the ready-to-use folder download for installation; the source ZIP is for development.

## Playing music

Play supported music files from Internal Storage, M.2 Storage, USB storage or an SMB network share.

Selecting a song plays the supported music files in that folder, starting from your selection. Use the player controls to pause, skip, stop, change volume, shuffle or repeat. Repeat cycles between Off, Repeat All and Repeat One.

You can keep browsing while music plays. Open the fullscreen player by pressing **R3** or selecting the expand button. Press **Circle** or **R3** to return.

The interface scales to the PS5's active output resolution. Prospero Hi-Fi must remain running to play music; it does not provide background music while playing PS5 games.

## Controls

| DualSense control | Action |
| --- | --- |
| L1 / R1 | Switch sections |
| D-pad / left stick | Move through lists |
| Cross / Circle | Select / Back |
| Left / Right | Jump through lists, adjust EQ, or select a player control |
| Options | Play / Pause |
| L2 / R2 | Previous / Next song |
| Square | Toggle shuffle |
| Touchpad click | Switch between browsing and player controls |
| R3 | Open or close fullscreen |
| Triangle | Edit the selected source; otherwise stop playback |

While player controls are focused, Up/Down seeks in five-second steps. On-screen hints show the controls available on each screen.

### On-screen keyboard

The controller keyboard includes lowercase, uppercase and symbol pages, plus Space, Delete and Done keys.

| Control | Action |
| --- | --- |
| D-pad / left stick | Select a key |
| Cross | Type the selected key |
| Square | Delete the previous character |
| Triangle | Insert a space |
| L1 / R1 | Change keyboard page |
| Options | Confirm |
| Circle | Cancel without saving changes |

## Music from a network share

Open **Sources > Add SMB share**, enter the server and share details, test the connection and select **Save share**.

For a network folder such as `\\NAS\Music\Albums`, enter:

- **Server:** `NAS` or its IP address
- **Share:** `Music`
- **Subfolder:** `Albums` — optional

Enter a username and password, or enable Guest if your server allows it. SMB2/SMB3 shares are supported. Select a saved share and press **Triangle** to edit or remove it.

## Artwork and appearance

Artwork is read from supported MP3 and FLAC files. You can also place `cover.jpg`, `folder.png` or `front.jpg` beside your music; JPG, JPEG and PNG variants are supported.

Settings includes Light, Dark and OLED themes, accent colours, artwork preferences, a visualizer, a clock and a screensaver. **Blue is the default accent colour.** The Equalizer section provides presets and manual adjustment of five frequency bands.

Settings are saved automatically. The screensaver turns the display black while playback continues; press a button to wake it.

## Control Prospero Hi-Fi from a browser

Enable **Web Remote** in Settings and open the displayed address on a phone or computer on the same network:

```text
http://PS5-IP:8182
```

The Web Remote controls playback on the PS5. It provides:

- Music browsing and playback from the detected storage sources, SMB shares and physical audio CDs.
- Play/pause, stop, previous/next, seeking, volume, shuffle and repeat.
- Now-playing information and album artwork.
- Equalizer presets and manual adjustment.
- Appearance, playback and other application settings.
- Storage-folder editing and SMB-share management.

The browser also offers **Screen Control**, which mirrors the current interface and lets you operate it remotely. Remote text prompts let you enter text when the PS5 opens a supported input dialog.

Prospero Hi-Fi must stay open for the Web Remote to work. Playback and audio stay on the PS5; the remote does not stream audio to your browser.

## Control Prospero Hi-Fi from NX Hi-Fi

On your Switch, open **NX Hi-Fi > Remote** and add the PS5 using its IP address and port **8182**, or choose **Scan for remote clients**. Prospero must be running with Web Remote enabled, and both devices must be on the same network.

Choose between:

- **Independent control:** browse and control playback on the PS5 through NX Hi-Fi's own remote interface. Playback controls, artwork, equalizer, supported settings and source management are available through the target's capabilities.
- **Screen Control:** follow and control Prospero's current on-screen interface, including its detected storage-source list and supported text-entry prompts.

Existing NX Hi-Fi clients use their original source list in Independent control. To access the separate M.2 and USB storage entries, use **Screen Control** or the browser Web Remote.

In NX Screen Control, hold **Minus for three seconds** to open the local menu. Use it to disconnect or switch modes. Disconnecting leaves music playing on the PS5.

Prospero accepts incoming remote control. It does not include an outgoing Remote section for controlling another Hi-Fi instance.

## Physical audio CDs

Connect a USB CD/DVD drive. Once **Sources > Physical Disc** appears, insert an audio CD and open it. Use a powered hub or a separately powered drive if additional power is needed.

The disc is streamed as CDDA (44.1 kHz, 16-bit stereo); no ripping or temporary audio files are required. Pause, seeking, previous/next, shuffle, repeat, EQ and the visualizer work with CDs. **Gapless audio CD playback** is enabled by default and can be changed in Settings. Data tracks on mixed-mode CDs are skipped.

MusicBrainz supplies album, artist and track names from the disc's table of contents. Artwork uses Cover Art Archive, then a matching iTunes album. Metadata and artwork are cached in `/data/prospero-hifi/cd-cache/`. Offline or unknown discs use Track 01-style names. Unknown-disc results expire after seven days; network/server failures are not cached.

To refresh after inserting or changing a disc, reopen Physical Disc from Sources. Read errors or drive removal stop playback and display an error. Physical Disc is also available through the browser and compatible NX remote clients.

This feature uses an external USB optical drive. Compatibility depends on the drive, USB bridge and firmware; the PS5's built-in disc drive is not supported as an audio CD source.

## Helpful notes

- **Local format support:** M4A/AAC/ALAC and Opus are not supported for local playback. Some files may have limited seeking or an estimated duration.
- **Missing drive:** check that the drive is connected, powered and accessible to homebrew. An empty mount directory alone does not make a storage source appear. A detected drive can be shown even if its Music folder is missing or empty.
- **Connection problems:** check that both devices are on the same network, the address is correct and Prospero's Web Remote is enabled. The default remote port is **8182**.
- **Settings and passwords:** configuration is stored in `/data/prospero-hifi/config.json`. It can contain saved network credentials, so do not share your personal configuration file. Leave a saved password field blank to retain it where indicated.
- **Upgrading:** replace the complete `PPSA99287` application folder and rescan ShadowMount+. Settings and CD metadata remain in `/data/prospero-hifi/`. A previously selected combined USB music path is migrated to its separate storage source.

## Building from source

See `scripts/bootstrap-ps5.sh` and `Makefile.ps5` for the public-SDK build. On Linux or WSL with the required build tools installed:

```sh
bash scripts/bootstrap-ps5.sh
export PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK="$PWD/.deps/ps5-payload-sdk"
make -f Makefile.ps5 -j4
```

The ready-to-use homebrew folder is generated in `dist/PPSA99287/`. See `VALIDATION.md` for build checks and console testing notes.

## License

repos.readme:
ProsperoRadio

A native Internet-radio application for PlayStation 5 homebrew
Browse and search the Radio Browser catalogue with resilient disk-backed caching, native PS5 audio playback, and a controller-first OpenGL interface.

## Project preservation and maintenance **ProsperoRadio was originally created and developed by BlackBearReloaded.** This repository is a continuation of the original ProsperoRadio project, established to preserve the application and its source code after the original GitHub repository became unavailable. The goal is to keep ProsperoRadio accessible, working and available for future development on PlayStation 5 homebrew systems. **Original developer:** BlackBearReloaded **Current maintainer:** [bornaradusin](https://github.com/bornaradusin) All original copyright notices, third-party acknowledgements and GPL-3.0-or-later licensing are retained. Credit for the original application and its development belongs to BlackBearReloaded. ![ProsperoRadio's home screen with a station playing: the Now Playing header, the Popular list and the letter rail](docs/images/prosperoradio.png) **Project maintenance:** Originally created by **BlackBearReloaded**, who has stepped down. **[bornaradusin](https://github.com/bornaradusin)** now develops and maintains ProsperoRadio. Original copyright and licences are preserved. ## Features - Browse Popular, Trending, Top rated, Favorites, and Discover views. - Search live Radio Browser data by text, country, genre, language, and bitrate, with mirror failover and server-side paging. - Keep a large SQLite catalogue and favourites on `/data/prosperoradio`; a failed sync leaves the last verified catalogue untouched. - Navigate entirely with the DualSense D-pad or left analogue stick; the PS5 IME handles text entry. - Draw station names in every script (Arabic, Cyrillic, Chinese, Persian and more) with the console's own fonts, HarfBuzz shaping and right-to-left ordering. - Keep everything it writes in one place outside the app folder, `/data/prosperoradio`, so an update never touches it. See [Where ProsperoRadio keeps its files](#where-prosperoradio-keeps-its-files). - Play AAC/AAC+ and MP3 through native PS5 decoding; play Opus through the native Opus/CELT decoder route; play Vorbis and FLAC/Ogg-FLAC with bounded CPU decoders. - Resolve bounded M3U/PLS indirection, strip ICY metadata, and support the audio-only AAC HLS subset. App-specific codec limits and validation are documented in [Architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md), [Codec investigation](docs/CODEC_INVESTIGATION.md), and [Roadmap](ROADMAP.md). ## App details | Identity | Value | | --- | --- | | Shell title | `ProsperoRadio` | | Title ID | `PPSA99001` | | Category | Media | | Current release version | `01.000.010` | | Release-version source | [`sce_sys/param.json`](sce_sys/param.json) | | Writable data | `/data/prosperoradio` | ## Installation and updates 1. Fully close ProsperoRadio. 2. From the [latest release](https://github.com/bornaradusin/ProsperoRadio/releases/latest), download `PPSA99001.zip`. 3. Extract it locally, then upload the entire `PPSA99001/` folder over FTP so its destination is `/data/homebrew/PPSA99001/`, and wait for the transfer to finish. Do not upload the ZIP file itself. 4. If an earlier release was installed as `/data/homebrew/PPSA99001.ffpfsc`, remove that image: do not keep it beside the folder. Restart ShadowMountPlus cleanly or restart the PS5. 5. Start the approved services normally, wait for ShadowMountPlus to rediscover `PPSA99001`, then launch ProsperoRadio and confirm the version shown below the app name. Do not relaunch immediately after replacing the app: ShadowMountPlus may still have the previous folder mounted. The catalogue, favourites and settings are in `/data/prosperoradio`, outside the app, so they are kept; Shell presentation metadata may remain cached. Automatic-update compatibility with [Prospero Store](https://prosperostore.net/) has not been verified. For updates, use GitHub Releases. ## Where ProsperoRadio keeps its files The app itself stays in `/data/homebrew/PPSA99001` (or wherever ShadowMountPlus mounts it from). Everything it writes is in `/data/prosperoradio`: ```text /data/prosperoradio/ ├── config/ settings.txt, the favourites, the update check's sequence number ├── catalog/ the station catalogue (rebuilt by a refresh) └── logs/ Application logs ``` Favourites and the catalogue an earlier version kept in its sandbox are copied over on the first start. Without filesystem access (no resident Lapy service and no ELF loader on port 9021) the same files stay in the title's sandbox, `/download0`, as in release 01.000.005. ## Requirements Build from Linux, WSL, or a Linux CI runner. On Ubuntu, Debian, or WSL: ```bash sudo apt update sudo apt install curl git make pkg-config python3 python3-venv tar unzip wget zip \ clang-18 clang-format-18 clang-tidy-18 lld-18 libsqlite3-dev ``` The repository downloads, verifies, and caches the public PS5 Payload SDK, zlib, PacBrew's SQLite and libcurl ports, the interface kit, the ps5-opengl SDK, HarfBuzz, the pinned upstream Lapy helper sources, and GoogleTest below ignored `.deps/`. No proprietary SDK, system module, key, or game asset is included or fetched. ## Build `sce_sys/param.json` is the only identity and release-version source. Do not change `PPSA99001` when updating ProsperoRadio: changing it produces a separate PS5 title rather than an update. ```bash make app ``` The output is the complete title folder: ```text dist/PPSA99001/ ``` ## Tests ```bash make test # C++ unit tests, UI/metadata tests, 16 codec/catalogue checks make lint # formatting, static analysis, metadata, and shell checks make check # lint + all host tests + complete folder build ``` The test suite runs entirely on the host and never contacts a console. It covers RML/UI asset consistency, catalogue persistence, mirror/query parsing, AAC timing, MP3 framing, ICY metadata, PCM/retry behaviour, Ogg/Opus, Vorbis, FLAC, HLS/MPEG-TS, controller input, and Arabic/RTL text ordering. The PS5-only boundary is documented in [Testing](docs/TESTING.md). ## Credits and licence Original developer: **BlackBearReloaded**. Current developer and maintainer: **bornaradusin**. Copyright 2026 BlackBearReloaded. GPL-3.0-or-later; see [LICENSE](LICENSE) and [third-party notices](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

repos.name: OliSePlayer
repos.description: OliSe Player: a FastTracker II flavoured tracker-music radio for jailbroken PS5s, streaming MOD/XM/S3M/IT from The Mod Archive
repos.readme:
# OliSe Player

Tracker music radio for the PS5, in FastTracker II style.

![logo](assets/logo.png)

OliSe Player grabs random MOD, XM, S3M and IT tunes from
[The Mod Archive](https://modarchive.org) and plays them one after the
other on your PS5. Pick a genre (chiptune, trance, jazz, whatever you feel
like), pick a format, or just let it run. While a tune plays you see the
pattern data scroll by, like in the old tracker days, with a starfield, a
chrome logo, a scroller, copper bars and VU meters around it.

You need a jailbroken PS5 with
[ShadowMountPlus](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus). Internet is
needed for The Mod Archive; without it the player plays the files from its
own `music/` folder.

## Installing

OliSe Player is a native PS5 app with title ID PPSA01153. The release zip
contains a `PPSA01153` folder with `eboot.bin` and `sce_sys`. Copy that
folder to `/data/homebrew/` on the console (FTP works fine) and
ShadowMountPlus adds it to your home screen like any other game. Local
modules go in `/data/homebrew/PPSA01153/music/`. Close the app with the PS
button like any other game.

## Controls

Press the touchpad for this list on screen.

| Button | What it does |
|---|---|
| R3 | Next track |
| L3 | Previous track |
| Triangle | Choose a source and station, or the next preset while the visualiser runs |
| L2 + Triangle | Previous preset (R2 + Triangle picks a random one) |
| Cross | Pause / play |
| Circle | Browse the local `music/` folder |
| L2 + Circle | Keep the playing radio track in `music/` |
| L1 / R1 | Previous / next local file (page up / down in lists) |
| Options | Switch the right panel between instruments and scopes |
| L2 + Options | Automatic preset change every minute, on or off |
| Square | Visualiser: off, behind the interface, full screen |
| R2 | CRT scanlines on / off |
| D-pad left / right | Scroll through the channels |
| D-pad up / down | Volume (hold L2 to jump through the song) |

On the desktop build: `n` / `p` next and previous, `g` stations, space
pause, `o` file list, `s` scopes, `f` effects, `c` CRT, `b` next preset, `k` keep this track,
arrows for channels and volume, `h` help, Esc quits.

## The visualiser

Square turns on a MilkDrop visualiser. With the preset pack installed those
are the real presets from the last official MilkDrop release, run by
projectM: the same scripts and shaders, reacting to the module that is
playing. Without the pack the app falls back to its own effect, which works
the same way MilkDrop does (warp the previous frame, dim it, draw the
waveform over it) but with 24 built-in presets instead of 552.

The presets ship inside `PPSA01153.zip`, so an install has them straight
away. They are also attached to each release on their own as
`OliSePlayer-presets.zip`, for adding them to an install that has none.
`make presets` fetches them from the projectM project, and `make gl` ships
whatever ends up in `presets/`.

The pack carries projectM's own statement on their licence, which comes down
to this: almost no MilkDrop preset was released under a specific licence, and
after two decades of free circulation they are treated as public domain. A
preset author who objects can have theirs removed; see
`presets/PRESETS-LICENSE.md`.

## Where the music comes from

Triangle asks which archive to listen to first, then which station within it.
The two are kept apart because they are organised differently, and one merged
list of genres would not be honest about where a tune comes from.

**The Mod Archive** holds around 160.000 modules, sorted by genre. The player
reads the normal website pages, the same ones a browser shows, because the XML
API needs a key. A genre station picks a random page from that genre and a
random module on it; featured and top rated pick from the current charts.

**Modland** is the larger archive and is organised by format and artist. The
player uses its playlists, which are plain text files of direct links: the
favourites of some 850 modules, a chiptune selection, netlabel releases, and a
few musicdisks and demoparty compos. One request gets the list, a second gets
the tune, so it tends to be quicker than the Mod Archive route.

A track plays once and then the next one from the same station starts. The
last 20 tracks stay in memory, so L3 goes back without downloading again.
If the network drops, the player keeps trying with longer pauses and plays
local files in the meantime.

## Building it yourself

You need Linux or WSL with clang-18, lld-18, cmake, ninja (`pip install
ninja` is enough) and Python 3. The first build downloads the public PS5
Payload SDK and the PacBrew ports (about 350 MB) into `.deps/`.

```sh
make deps        # libxmp-lite, SDK and PacBrew
make presets     # download the MilkDrop preset pack (optional)
make             # dist/PPSA01153/ and dist/PPSA01153.zip
make gl          # the OpenGL build, needed for the visualiser
make ffpfsc      # also a compressed .ffpfsc image
make upload      # copy the folder to the PS5 over FTP (port 1337)
make native      # desktop version, plays files from music/
```

Releases are tagged with the `contentVersion` from `sce_sys/param.json`
(for example `01.000.001`); the same number is shown in the app.

The native title build uses the tooling from BlackBearReloaded's
[ps5-native-app-boilerplate](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-native-app-boilerplate):
it links with LLVM, converts the ELF to a PS5 module, signs it as a
development FSELF and adds a source-built `libc.prx`. See
`THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` for all licenses.

`make gl` needs two things the plain build does not:

- The [PS5 OpenGL SDK](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-opengl),
  unpacked so that `deps/ps5-opengl/sdk/include/EGL` exists, or pointed at
  with `make gl PS5_OPENGL_PREFIX=/path/to/sdk`.
- projectM built for the PS5 in `deps/projectm/`, for the real MilkDrop
  presets. Without it the app uses its own visualiser instead, and `make gl`
  says nothing about it. `docs/decision-log.md` records how projectM was
  ported, including the three changes its build needed.

The OpenGL build is about 27 MB against 2.6 MB for the plain one: Mesa is
linked statically, and that is the price of running shaders at all.

`make assets` regenerates the logo and the icon with the Python scripts in
`tools/` (needs Pillow). `tools/netxm_test.c` tests the page parsing
without a network.

## Thanks

- The Mod Archive and everyone who uploaded music there
- [libxmp](https://github.com/libxmp/libxmp) for playing the modules
- [font8x8](https://github.com/dhepper/font8x8) by Daniel Hepper
- [ps5-payload-dev](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev) for the toolchain and SDL2
- BlackBearReloaded for the native app tooling and the homebrew catalog
- Triton, for FastTracker II

## License

GPL-3.0-or-later. See `LICENSE` and `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.

latestRelease.name: OliSe Player 02.001.000
latestRelease.body:
Two archives to listen to, and a scroller that tells you what is playing.

## Modland as a second source

Triangle now asks which archive first, then which station. The two are kept
apart because they are organised differently: the Mod Archive by genre and
chart, Modland by curated playlist.

Modland is read through its playlists, which are plain text files of direct
links. Eight stations: the favourites of around 850 modules, a chiptune
selection, netlabel releases, a couple of musicdisks and a demoparty compo.

## The scroller says what is playing

The greeting runs its one pass at startup and is never cut short. After that
the band carries the track: title, source, the tracker that wrote the module,
channels, instruments, patterns, running time, and the genre and artist where
the archive gave them. A new track fades the band out, swaps the line and
fades it back in.

## Visualiser

Stepping through presets follows a shuffled order instead of the alphabet.
Sorted by filename, stepping meant working through one author at a time. The
visualiser also moves on by itself every minute; L2 + Options turns that off.

## Keep a track

L2 + Circle writes the playing module into `music/` and adds it to
`index.txt`, so a tune that would otherwise scroll out of the 20 track history
can be kept.

## Fixed

The interface named The Mod Archive everywhere, including while downloading
from Modland. Each track now carries where it came from.

## Installing

Copy the contents of `PPSA01153.zip` to `/data/homebrew/PPSA01153/`, reload
the jailbreak chain and start it from the home screen. The 552 MilkDrop
presets are in the zip; `OliSePlayer-presets.zip` is the same pack on its own,
for adding to an install made without it.

Drop your own modules in `music/` and add their names to `music/index.txt`:
the sandbox will not let the app list a folder, so it reads that index.

repos.name: CD-Player
repos.description: Rediscover your audio CDs and fall in love with your music again. A native PS5 CD player with a minimal digital interface.
repos.readme: # CD Player **Rediscover your audio CDs. Fall in love with your music again.** I wanted to listen to my audio CDs on my PS5. Sony no longer includes that simple feature on its recent consoles, so I decided to bring it back with an external USB drive, and with as much attention to the design as to the sound. CD Player is a native PS5 homebrew app built around the album: a large cover, a reflective spinning disc, a clear track list and a minimal digital interface. Put a CD in, settle into your favourite chair, and listen. Designed by **LoZazaMastro**. [Download the latest release](https://github.com/LoZazaMastro/CD-Player/releases/latest) | [What's new](docs/CHANGELOG.md) | [Installation](#installation) | [Controls](#controls) | [Build from source](docs/BUILDING.md) ![Blunderbuss by Jack White in CD Player](docs/screenshots/album.png) ## A player made for listening - Play audio CDs from a compatible external USB optical drive, including Apple USB SuperDrive. - Keep listening when the controller turns off or disconnects. - Find album artwork, artist, year, track titles and editions through MusicBrainz and Cover Art Archive. CD-Text is used when available. - Open the album cover to read a description, when one is available. Notes come from MusicBrainz or its linked English Wikipedia article. - Enjoy a reflective 3D disc that enters with the album, accelerates into playback and slows down gently when paused. - When available for your edition, the printed CD label fades onto the spinning disc. Press **L3** to turn the 3D case over and see its back and spine. Missing artwork stays blank. - Choose from **161 individual audio-reactive visualizers**, one at a time, or let the app shuffle them when the track changes. - Use **OLED mode** to hide fullscreen labels, gently move the effect, and switch to a black screen after a minute of inactivity while playback is stopped. - Adjust a ten-band equalizer, volume, gapless playback and optional stereo-to-7.1 upmix while listening. - Balance all eight speakers independently in Speaker setup, including the front pair, center, surround, side and subwoofer channels. - Read lyrics in Doto with R3 from the fullscreen visualizer. Timed phrases follow the music when available through LRCLIB. - **Circle** returns straight from lyrics to the album page. Reopening fullscreen restores your last lyrics or visualizer choice. - Enable **Autoplay disc** if you want a newly inserted CD to start on its own. - Hide the Eject button if you prefer: the remaining buttons fill the same space, while their icons keep the same size. - The track list brings the playing track into view when it changes. You can then browse freely without the list pulling you back. - Keep your settings and chosen visualizer between launches. All interface text is in English. - Choose an accent from 40 named colors. The interface and visualizers change immediately and remember your choice. ## A quiet interface Settings open from the right over a softly blurred album view. The equalizer has its own page. In fullscreen, the effect name and control hints disappear after two seconds without input, leaving the music, the picture and the clock. | Listening settings | Ten-band equalizer | | --- | --- | | ![Settings drawer](docs/screenshots/settings.png) | ![Graphic equalizer](docs/screenshots/equalizer.png) | | Album notes | Five-button layout | | --- | --- | | ![Album notes for Blunderbuss](docs/screenshots/album-info.png) | ![Transport with Eject hidden](docs/screenshots/album-no-eject.png) | | The back of the case | Individual speaker levels | | --- | --- | | ![Blunderbuss back cover and printed disc](docs/screenshots/album-back.png) | ![Eight individual speaker controls](docs/screenshots/speaker-setup.png) | ![Fullscreen visualizer with Jack White metadata](docs/screenshots/visualizer.png) ![Fullscreen lyrics with the current phrase highlighted](docs/screenshots/lyrics.png) Lyrics view with sample text to show phrase highlighting and scrolling. The screenshots are rendered by the app's own preview build, using the same interface and shaders as the PS5 version, with **Blunderbuss by Jack White**. Album artwork belongs to its rightsholders; it is downloaded when needed and is not included as an asset in the application package. ## Installation You need a PS5 with a compatible, active homebrew environment and an external USB optical drive capable of reading audio CDs. CD Player does not use the console's internal disc drive. 1. Download **PPSA98427.zip** from [Releases](https://github.com/LoZazaMastro/CD-Player/releases). 2. Extract the **PPSA98427** folder into a location scanned by your homebrew loader, such as `/data/homebrew/`. 3. Check that the executable is directly at `/data/homebrew/PPSA98427/eboot.bin`, rather than inside another nested folder. 4. Open **CD Player** from the PS5's **Media** section and insert an audio CD. Close CD Player before replacing its files. The ZIP records the open file permissions required by the homebrew loader. If your FTP client changes them, set the app folder and its contents to `0777`. **Updating to 1.1.2:** this release fixes an oversized storage reservation. If an older installation still occupies about 18 GB, remove CD Player through the PS5's storage settings, then install the new release again. Replacing the files alone does not shrink an existing reservation. Reinstallation may reset saved settings and cached artwork. The included one-shot access helper is restricted to this app's title ID. Your homebrew environment may need a local ELF loader on port **9021**. Start the console with the USB drive empty, then insert the CD after boot; PSSwanStation documents drive lockups when a disc is already present at boot. ### Apple SuperDrive and other USB drives Apple USB SuperDrive has no physical eject button. The app's **Eject** control is especially useful for it: select the icon or press **Triangle** to remove the disc. Apple-specific initialization is included; no Apple Boot Camp drivers are bundled. Other compatible USB drives can use the same eject command. USB access follows the CAM/SCSI approach adapted from PSSwanStation. That does not establish compatibility with every drive model: audio-CD reading still depends on the USB bridge, drive firmware and console environment. ## Controls | Button | Action | | --- | --- | | D-pad | Navigate; scroll album notes; change fullscreen visualizer with Left/Right | | Cross | Select a track or control; open the cover when album notes are available | | Square | Play / pause | | Triangle | Eject the disc | | L1 / R1 | Previous / next track | | L2 / R2 | Seek backward / forward by 10 seconds | | Touchpad click | Enter / leave the fullscreen visualizer | | R3, in fullscreen | Switch between the visualizer and lyrics | | L3, on the album page | Turn the case over; press again to return to the front | | Right stick up / down | Raise / lower the master volume from any screen | | Options | Open settings | | Circle | Back | | Hold Options, then press Circle | Close the app | A Play icon in the accent color marks the track you are hearing. When paused, its track number returns. Hiding the Eject icon also hides its control hint; the Triangle shortcut remains available. ## Sound and saved settings Audio CDs contain stereo PCM at 44.1 kHz. CD Player resamples it to 48 kHz for the PS5 audio output. The optional 7.1 upmix derives surround channels from stereo; it is not an original multichannel recording. The control is unavailable when the output accepts only stereo. Speaker setup opens inside the settings drawer and provides eight independent sliders: front left/right, center, surround left/right, side left/right and LFE (subwoofer). Each runs from mute to +24 dB. At 0 dB the channel keeps its original level; the front pair stays unchanged unless you adjust its own sliders. Changes fade in smoothly, with peak protection on the generated channels and deliberately boosted front channels. Previously saved upmix gains carry over to their corresponding speakers, including mute. Front controls also work with stereo output; generated speakers require 7.1 output and upmix enabled. Press R3 in the fullscreen visualizer to open lyrics. When LRCLIB has timed lyrics for the track, the current phrase is highlighted and scrolls smoothly to the center, following the CD's playback position through pauses and seeks. If only untimed text is available, it can be scrolled with the D-pad. Some tracks have no lyrics available. Lyrics need an Internet connection on first lookup and are cached for later use. Temporary server errors are retried automatically while the loading message remains on screen; leaving lyrics or changing tracks cancels further retries. Returning to lyrics already loaded for the current track opens them directly. Equalizer settings, upmix, all eight speaker gains, volume, gapless playback, autoplay, reduced motion, visualizer selection, shuffle, Eject-button visibility and accent color are saved automatically. They are checked for saving once per second and restored on the next launch. Updating the app leaves this data outside the installation folder: - Settings, metadata, artwork cache and session log: `/data/cdplayer-PPSA98427` - Sandbox fallback: `/download0/cdplayer` Online album information and covers need an Internet connection on first lookup. Cached information remains available afterwards. HTTPS certificates and hostnames are verified against the console's trust store. ## Tested configuration CD playback, artwork and album descriptions have been confirmed with an Apple USB SuperDrive on the owner's PS5 running **firmware 13.60**. The tested Media configuration runs at approximately **60 Hz**. A renderer request for a higher refresh rate is not a claim of 120 fps support in this release. Other drive models, firmware versions and surround output configurations need their own hardware checks. [Build and validation notes](docs/BUILDING.md) explain the host tests and the distinction between a compiled build and a console test. ## Credits **Based on PSSwanStation by Press5elect.** Its USB optical-drive work made this possible. - [PSSwanStation](https://github.com/Press5elect/PSSwanStation) ? Press5elect; optical-drive access and preserved additional attribution terms. - [Prospero Homebrew UI](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-homebrew-ui) and [PS5 Native App Boilerplate](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-native-app-boilerplate) ? BlackBearReloaded; interface, native runtime and build foundation. - [ps5-opengl](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-opengl), Mesa and OpenGNM PSBC ? native graphics infrastructure. - [iwrzwr Visual Archive](https://github.com/kaganin/iwrzwr-visual-archive) ? Kagan Yaldizkaya; the original drawing programs adapted into the visualizer catalog. - [Doto](https://github.com/oliverlalan/Doto) ? Oliver Lalan and the Doto Project Authors; [Inter](https://github.com/rsms/inter) ? Rasmus Andersson and the Inter Project Authors; typography and fallback glyphs. - Alfredo Sandoval ? the documented Apple SuperDrive initialization protocol. - [PS5 Payload SDK](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk) ? John T?rnblom and contributors; public homebrew toolchain. - [PS5-Lapy-JB-Daemon](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/PS5-Lapy-JB-Daemon) ? Arksama (Team PHU) and upstream contributors; the pinned exact-title access helper. - [QuickJS](https://bellard.org/quickjs/) ? Fabrice Bellard and Charlie Gordon; local execution of drawing programs. - MusicBrainz, Cover Art Archive, Wikidata and Wikipedia contributors ? album information and artwork services. Fixes the oversized storage reservation that made CD Player occupy about 18 GB on PS5. The app now reserves 256 MiB for its data instead of 16 GiB.

Tested on PS5 firmware 13.60.

repos.name: ProsperoLight
repos.description: An unofficial Moonlight port (game streaming) for PS5
repos.readme:
ProsperoLight

Moonlight game streaming, natively on PlayStation 5.
Stream games and your desktop from a Sunshine-compatible PC to a homebrew-enabled PS5.


Features and fixes in the `main` branch may not be available in the [latest published release](https://github.com/LedyBacer/ProsperoLight/releases). Check the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md) and the release notes before updating. ## Features - **Native PS5 video:** hardware-accelerated H.264 and HEVC (including HDR10) through VideoDec2 and AGC, with 1080p, 1440p and 4K stream options. - **High-refresh streaming:** 30, 60, 90 and 120 FPS presets, plus Custom 30–120 FPS. Actual performance depends on codec, bitrate and hardware. - **Frame pacing and VRR:** Unpaced, fixed-refresh Paced and adaptive Paced+VRR modes. Current source builds include Low Latency, Balanced and Smooth VRR timing profiles and low-FPS frame repetition. - **PyroWave:** an optional Vulkan GPU decoder with SDR/HDR and 4:2:0/4:4:4 profiles, requiring a compatible Vibepollo/Vibeshine host. - **Controllers and input:** up to four DualSense controllers, supported haptics/adaptive triggers, USB keyboard and mouse, plus on-screen keyboard and controller-driven mouse mode. - **Audio:** selectable stereo or 5.1-channel Opus playback. - **A console-first launcher:** automatic LAN discovery, multiple saved PCs, application artwork, persistent settings, and a UI available in 31 languages. - **Wake an offline PC:** after pairing with Sunshine and refreshing once while the PC is awake, its MAC is remembered; an offline PC with that MAC offers an explicit IPv4 **Wake PC** action. Packet emission and the PC coming online are reported separately. - **Updates and diagnostics:** in-app update support for compatible folder installations, performance overlay, and optional timing/log capture. ## Get started 1. **Prepare your PS5.** You need a console with a compatible homebrew environment and title loader already configured. ProsperoLight does not install or provide an exploit. 2. **Install ProsperoLight.** Get `PPSA99002.zip` from [Releases](https://github.com/LedyBacer/ProsperoLight/releases), extract it, and copy the complete `PPSA99002/` folder to `/data/homebrew/`. Close the app before replacing an older installation; refresh your homebrew loader's title registration. 3. **Start Sunshine** (or a compatible host) on your PC. A wired local network is strongly recommended. 4. **Pair and play.** Open ProsperoLight, select a discovered PC or add its address, and enter the pairing PIN in your host's web interface. Open **Games** and choose an app or Desktop. Press **Touchpad + L1** to end the stream and return to the launcher. Pairings and settings normally remain in `/data/prosperolight` when updating the app. **[Full user guide →](docs/USER_GUIDE.md)** — installation, pairing, updates, controllers, settings and saved data. ## Controls | During streaming | Action | | ----------------------- | --------------------------------- | | **Touchpad + L1** | Return to ProsperoLight | | **Touchpad + R1** | Toggle performance overlay | | **Touchpad + Square** | Toggle controller/mouse mode | | **Touchpad + Triangle** | Open/close the on-screen keyboard | Touchpad means pressing the touchpad **until it clicks**. See the [complete controls reference](docs/USER_GUIDE.md#controls), including the host Back/Guide shortcuts and multi-controller behavior. ## Video quality and compatibility ### Bitrate limits **H.264/HEVC decoding and PyroWave have different performance characteristics.** In measured native 4K HEVC sessions, bitrates above roughly 80 Mbps at 120 FPS can exceed the PS5 decoder's real-time budget. Increasing bitrate is not always an improvement. PyroWave has different host and network requirements. ### VRR and frame timing VRR support depends on the console, firmware, TV and actual output mode; a successful VideoOut API call does **not** prove physical HDMI VRR or a particular latency improvement. For a starting point, try a wired network, native HEVC, and conservative bitrate before experimenting with higher refresh rates. **[Performance and video guide →](docs/PERFORMANCE_GUIDE.md)** — codec selection, measured bitrate limits, pacing modes and VRR caveats. ## Documentation | For | Start here | | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | **Players** | [User guide](docs/USER_GUIDE.md) · [Performance guide](docs/PERFORMANCE_GUIDE.md) · [Troubleshooting](docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md) | | **Advanced users** | [PyroWave](docs/PYROWAVE.md) · [DualSense](docs/DUALSENSE.md) · [Frame pacing tests](docs/PACING_TEST_MATRIX.md) · [Home-screen forwarders](docs/FORWARDER.md) | | **Developers** | [Getting started](docs/GETTING_STARTED.md) · [Architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) · [Testing](docs/TESTING.md) · [Deployment](docs/DEPLOYMENT.md) | | **Maintainers** | [Configuration](docs/CONFIGURATION.md) · [Validation](docs/VALIDATION.md) · [Release packaging](docs/RELEASE_ZIP.md) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) | | **Project** | [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) · [Roadmap / ideas](docs/ROADMAP.md) · [Third-party notices](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) | ## Build from source See [Getting started](docs/GETTING_STARTED.md) for Linux/WSL prerequisites and reproducible dependencies. Once set up: ```bash git submodule update --init --recursive make doctor make check ``` The build produces a complete `dist/PPSA99002/` app directory. For the safe FTP deployment workflow, see [Deployment](docs/DEPLOYMENT.md). ## Support and contributions Found a bug? [Open an issue](https://github.com/LedyBacer/ProsperoLight/issues) with your PS5 firmware, host version, codec/settings and reproduction steps. For stream problems, enable **Diagnostic logs** and attach relevant logs after reviewing [Troubleshooting](docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md). Logs can contain local host addresses and app names; review them before sharing. Contributions and testing across different TVs, firmwares and network setups are welcome. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). > [!IMPORTANT] > This is an independent homebrew project, not an official Sony, Moonlight or Sunshine product. It requires a compatible homebrew-enabled console and includes no exploits, proprietary Sony SDK, firmware, keys or game assets. Use at your own risk and only with hardware and content you are entitled to use. ## Credits **Original creator:** [BlackBearReloaded](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded). **Current maintainer (since October 2026):** [LedyBacer](https://github.com/LedyBacer). Special thanks to BlackBearReloaded for creating ProsperoLight, building its native PS5 foundation, and entrusting the project's continued development to a new maintainer. The original author's contributions remain credited throughout the repository. Thanks to ProsperoLight contributors, including Nikita Dybov, KrisEnigma, and everyone who has contributed code, testing, and feedback. Built with the [PS5 Payload SDK](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk) by John Törnblom (ps5-payload-dev). Third-party components, authors and licenses are listed in [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md). ## License Copyright © 2026 BlackBearReloaded and respective contributors. Licensed under GPL-3.0-or-later; see [LICENSE](LICENSE). The repository transfer does not alter existing copyright or license notices. Third-party components keep their own licenses. Binary releases are built from the tagged source in this repository. ## Disclaimer - **No affiliation.** This is an independent homebrew project. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Sony Interactive Entertainment. "PlayStation", "PS5" and related marks are trademarks of Sony Interactive Entertainment Inc. This project is not affiliated with or endorsed by the Moonlight or Sunshine projects. - **No proprietary material.** No Sony SDK, firmware, encryption keys or decrypted system modules are included. - **No warranty.** This project is provided "as is", without warranty of any kind, to the extent permitted by law. See sections 15 and 16 of the GPL. - **Use at your own risk.** Running homebrew requires a modified console, which may void its warranty, breach the platform's terms of service, or cause data loss. - **Legal use only.** Use it only with hardware, accounts and content you own. This project does not support or enable piracy. ## AI assistance This project was developed with AI assistance from OpenAI and/or Anthropic tools.

latestRelease.name: ProsperoLight 01.000.110
latestRelease.body:
### Stable: Punktfunk hosts, more box art, no wait before the stream

### New

- **Punktfunk hosts:** the decoder now reserves six pictures by default, so Punktfunk's GameStream stream (five reference frames) decodes on a release build. Before, it showed no picture. Streams from other hosts are unaffected.
- **JPEG and WebP box art:** covers that hosts such as Punktfunk pass through as JPEG or WebP now appear, as PNG covers always did.
- **PyroWave from punktfunk:** punktfunk's PyroWave revision is accepted; its shaders and bitstream code are the same as the supported one.

### Changed

- **No wait before the stream:** the check for a newer version runs on its own. When homebrew.page could not be reached, starting a stream, a home-screen forwarder included, waited about a minute for that check to give up.
- **Box art:** covers over 1 MiB load, and covers already fetched are kept in memory, so scrolling back through a large library does not download them again.
- Built on ps5-opengl SDK 1.0.2.

### Installation / update

Title ID remains `PPSA99002`; saved PCs, settings and pairing are kept. Close the app before updating. Extract `PPSA99002.zip` and copy the complete `PPSA99002/` folder to `/data/homebrew/`. Keep only one installation for this title. `SHA256SUMS` verifies the download.

repos.name: xbox-cloud-gaming-ps5
repos.description: Xbox Cloud Gaming app for PS5 Homebrew
repos.readme:
PSBox Cloud Gaming

Xbox Cloud Gaming, running natively on PlayStation 5.

A native Xbox Cloud Gaming client for jailbroken PS5 consoles: browse the cloud catalog and stream games at 1080p60, with the DualSense as an Xbox controller. - **Sign in on your phone** with a code shown on the TV; no password on the console. - **Game Pass and Your games** tabs, search, and free-to-play games. - **My consoles**: play your own Xbox (Remote Play), its screen, games and apps. - **Sharp picture**: upscaled to 4K on the GPU (AMD FSR 1 or Anime4K), with compression blocks smoothed. - **DualSense**: rumble, adaptive-trigger vibration, light bar in the game's colour, up to four controllers. - **In-game menu** (OPTIONS + TOUCHPAD): statistics, picture options, stream resolution; the PS5 keyboard for games' text fields. - **Reconnects** by itself after a short network drop. - Six languages. Requires a homebrew-enabled PS5 that can run directory-style apps (for example through ShadowMountPlus), and a Microsoft account with a Game Pass plan that includes cloud gaming. Since October 2025 all three do: Essential and Premium stream at up to 1080p with a smaller catalog, Ultimate has the largest one. Reported working on firmware 13.00 and 13.60 with ShadowMountPlus. Other loaders that run directory apps from `/data/homebrew` should work too; please report your firmware and loader in an issue if it doesn't. ## Installation No building needed: download `PPSA99810.zip` from the [latest release](https://github.com/RafaelNGP/xbox-cloud-gaming-ps5/releases/latest). 1. Extract the zip and copy the `PPSA99810` folder, as a whole, to `/data/homebrew/` on the PS5 (for example over FTP). 2. Wait for the loader (e.g. ShadowMountPlus) to add the **PSBox Cloud Gaming** icon to the Home screen, then launch it. Or install it from **ProsperoStore** (the homebrew store, listed on [homebrew.page](https://homebrew.page)). 3. Sign in: open on your phone or computer (or scan the QR code) and enter the code shown on the TV. New versions install from inside the app (it asks after sign-in, and Settings > Updates): only a package signed with the project's key is accepted, and your sign-in is kept. By hand: close the app and copy the new folder over the old one. Since v0.9.7 the sign-in, settings, caches and log live in `/data/psbox`, outside the app's folder: updating, reinstalling or uninstalling the app (also from ProsperoStore) keeps them, and the first start moves them there from older versions. The sign-in is `/data/psbox/account.json`: never share that file. To remove everything the app keeps, delete `/data/psbox` too. More details, controls and troubleshooting are in the `README.txt` inside the folder. ## Building Clone with the submodules (Mbed TLS, libdatachannel, FFmpeg): ```bash git clone --recursive https://github.com/RafaelNGP/xbox-cloud-gaming-ps5.git cd xbox-cloud-gaming-ps5 ``` Requirements: CMake 3.20+, Ninja, Clang/LLVM (clang, clang++, llvm-ar, llvm-ranlib), Python 3 and curl. NASM is built automatically if missing. FFmpeg is configured and built by `tools/build-ffmpeg.sh` the first time CMake runs. ### Desktop build (Linux) Used to develop and check the protocol and the UI on a PC. The app is becoming multiplatform (PS5, Linux, Windows): see `docs/multiplatform.md`. ```bash cmake -S . -B build-host -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo ninja -C build-host build-host/xcloud-tests # unit tests build-host/xcloud-cli login # sign in build-host/xcloud-cli stream BALATRO 30 # stream a title for 30 s (--720p, --region=EASTUS) build-host/xcloud-cli ui-preview /tmp/ui # render every screen to PNG build-host/psbox-headless # the app with no window or devices (Ctrl+C closes it) bash tools/check-platform-boundaries.sh # PS5 calls only in the PS5 backends ``` ### Linux (preview) **Download:** releases may carry `PSBox-vX.Y.Z-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` (x86-64, glibc 2.39 or newer: Ubuntu 24.04, Fedora 40, Debian 13 or later; X11 or Wayland). Unpack it anywhere and run `PSBox/psbox`: SDL3 is bundled in `PSBox/lib`, nothing else to install. `PSBox/README-linux.txt` covers the menu entry and the udev rule some systems need for the DualSense's rumble, triggers, light bar and gyro. Each push's build is also an artifact (`psbox-linux-x86_64`) of the CI's `linux-app` job. **From source:** `psbox` is the app in a window, on SDL3 (3.2 or newer, with its development files: `SDL3-devel` on Fedora, `libsdl3-dev` on Debian / Ubuntu). It is built with the desktop build above whenever CMake finds SDL3 (`-DXCLOUD_DESKTOP_APP=ON` to require it, `OFF` to skip it). ```bash build-host/psbox # F11 or Alt+Enter: fullscreen; --fullscreen, --data-dir SDL_VIDEO_DRIVER=offscreen SDL_AUDIO_DRIVER=dummy build-host/psbox --selftest /tmp/psbox-selftest ``` Sign-in, settings and the log live in `~/.local/share/psbox` (or `$XCLOUD_DATA_DIR`); the fonts and certificates are copied to `assets/` beside the executable. Controllers (DualSense, DualShock 4, Xbox, Switch...), keyboard and mouse are supported (a preview: not checked on every pad yet); options the PC can't honour (light bar without a DualSense, 120 Hz, the PS5's upscalers) are hidden. It doesn't update itself: Settings > Updates opens the release page. See `docs/multiplatform.md` (M1). `tools/desktop/package-linux.sh ` makes and checks the tarball (M3). ### PS5 build The console build uses the toolchain of [PS5_Vulkan](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Vulkan) (the PS5 payload SDK, the PS5 linker recipe and `ps5-native-tool`). Clone and build it next to this repository, as its README describes, so that it sits at `../PS5_Vulkan`; or set `PS5_VULKAN` to point elsewhere. ```bash cmake -S . -B build-ps5 -G Ninja -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=cmake/ps5.toolchain.cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release ninja -C build-ps5 xcloud_app tools/ps5/link.sh build-ps5 # -> build-ps5/eboot.bin tools/ps5/package.sh build-ps5 # -> build-ps5/pkg/PPSA99810/ ``` **120 Hz output** (Settings and each game's settings, off by default; only while a game streams, the menus stay at 60 Hz) needs RADV with `tools/ps5/patches/mesa-videoout-vrr-120hz.patch` (two commits): with the console's VRR on, a 120 Hz request becomes VRR 119.88 Hz, whose idle vblank (the TV's VRR floor, ~48 Hz) the unpatched check takes for 60 Hz and undoes; and `wsi_videoout_set_high_refresh()` switches the open output at a stream's start and end. Apply it to PS5_Mesa at PS5_Vulkan's pinned revision on a local branch, then `PS5_MESA_REVISION= tools/build-radv.sh release` in PS5_Vulkan. Without it the option stays at 59.94 Hz (or, turned on in Settings, applies to the whole app from its next start). A release is built, signed and checked with `tools/release.sh ` (see the script's header); it publishes nothing. The signing key stays with the maintainer: the app trusts only its public half (`src/app/updater.cpp`). ## License GPL-3.0-or-later; see `LICENSE`. The PS5 binary statically links the PS5 app runtime and payload SDK platform layer, which are GPL-3.0-or-later, so the project as distributed must be too. All other components are compatible (Mbed TLS, libdatachannel, FFmpeg under the LGPL, stb, qrcodegen, the Inter font, Mozilla's CA bundle); `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` lists each one with its version and license. This is an unofficial project, not affiliated with, endorsed or sponsored by Microsoft or Sony. Xbox, Xbox Cloud Gaming and Game Pass are trademarks of the Microsoft group of companies; PlayStation and PS5 are trademarks of Sony Interactive Entertainment. Game names and artwork are loaded from Microsoft's public catalog at runtime and are not distributed with this project. Microsoft may change or block the services this client relies on at any time.

latestRelease.name: PSBox Cloud Gaming v1.5.4 - Experimental PS4 Preview
latestRelease.body:
## 🎮 PSBox Cloud Gaming - Experimental PS4 Preview (v1.5.4)

This is an experimental pre-release build of PSBox Cloud Gaming packaged natively for **PlayStation 4** (`PSBX00001`).

> [!NOTE]
> This pre-release is intended for testing the PS4 port and reporting feedback. PS5 users should continue using the official stable releases ([v1.5.4](https://github.com/RafaelNGP/xbox-cloud-gaming-ps5/releases/tag/v1.5.4)).

### 🛠️ Key Fixes & Additions in this Build
- **Dynamic Module Resolution**: Replaced static linker binding of `libSceVideodec2` with dynamic runtime resolution (`dlsym`), preventing initial loader `CE-34878-0` crashes on real consoles.
- **OpenOrbis System Stubs**: Bundled mandatory OpenOrbis `libc.prx` and `libSceFios2.prx` stubs in `sce_module/`, resolving the *"Cannot continue using the application. The data is corrupted"* error.
- **PS4 Pro 4K Display Handling**: Added fallback handling for video output initialization when running on 4K/HDR displays or PS4 Pro consoles.
- **Early-Boot Logging**: Direct early diagnostics written to `/data/psbox/boot.log` and `/data/homebrew/PSBOX00001/boot.log`.
- **Scanout Parity**: Native linear frame buffer readback and display pipeline matching the PS5 codebase.

### 📦 Installation
1. If you had any previous version installed, delete it from your PS4 Home Screen (<kbd>OPTIONS</kbd> > **Delete**).
2. Download `PSBox Cloud Gaming - PS4.pkg` below.
3. Install via GoldHEN Package Installer on your PS4.
4. If you encounter any unexpected behavior, connect via FTP (port 2121) and share the contents of `/data/psbox/` (`boot.log`, `xcloud.log`, `crash.marker`).

repos.name: ProsperoEden-Switch-UI
repos.description: Independent Switch-inspired PS5 interface edition of ProsperoEden, maintained by KernelForgeLabs
repos.readme:
ProsperoEden — Switch UI Edition

A Switch-inspired PS5 launcher edition of ProsperoEden

**ProsperoEden Switch UI Edition** is an independently maintained interface edition of [BlackBearReloaded's ProsperoEden](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ProsperoEden), the unofficial PS5 port of [Eden](https://github.com/eden-emulator/mirror). The original PS5 port and its many dependencies remain the work of their respective developers. Switch UI modifications are provided by **KernelForgeX**. This project is not affiliated with or endorsed by Nintendo, Sony, Eden, or BlackBearReloaded. > [!IMPORTANT] > **Public beta release preparation — version `06.000.000`, based on ProsperoEden `v1.005.000`.** This edition has been compiled, packaged, validated and tested on PS5 hardware, including launcher navigation, game discovery and game launching. It has its own title ID, `PPSA99186`, separate from the original ProsperoEden title `PPSA99008`. Both applications use `/data/prosperoeden/` for shared data. Back up configurations and saves before switching versions, and do not run both simultaneously. Fresh installation, updating and rollback still require final release acceptance testing. Catalog reservation PR #302 was approved and merged on October 18, 2026. Automatic in-app update checking and installation remain disabled; releases will be distributed through ProsperoStore after the downloadable listing is approved. The v1.005.000 integration is the current PS5-tested Switch UI release candidate. Compatibility and performance vary by game. Known upstream issues observed in both the original emulator and this edition include intermittent controller shortcuts across consecutive game sessions and frame-generation method selection when a required backend is unavailable. Lossless Scaling and MihawkGen performance have not been fully qualified on PS5 hardware. See the [beta installation and rollback test plan](docs/BETA_INSTALL_AND_ROLLBACK.md), [RC installation and testing](docs/SWITCH_UI_V6_RC.md), and [release-readiness checklist](docs/SWITCH_UI_RELEASE_READINESS.md). ## Source code The complete ProsperoEden source is in this repository: the PS5 frontend and launcher in `headless/`, and the build and packaging tools in `tools/`. To build it yourself, run `make` on Linux (Ubuntu 26.04; WSL works). It fetches every dependency at its pinned revision and writes the release files to `dist/`; `make help` lists the other targets. See [docs/BUILDING.md](docs/BUILDING.md). A release ZIP built by this fork’s GitHub Actions can be checked with `gh attestation verify -R KernelForgeLabs/ProsperoEden-Switch-UI` (GitHub CLI). This describes CI-built artifacts, not binaries built by the upstream repository. For how we selectively integrate improvements from BlackBearReloaded without overwriting Switch UI, see [Upstream integration policy](docs/UPSTREAM_INTEGRATION.md). Local-wireless multiplayer through Eden rooms is new in v1.000.110 and experimental. See the [setup guide and current limitations](docs/MULTIPLAYER.md) and the [validation status](docs/MULTIPLAYER_IMPLEMENTATION.md); Tailscale forwarding is not yet qualified. ## Project foundation > [!IMPORTANT] > **Built on the [PS5 Native App Boilerplate](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-native-app-boilerplate), the same native foundation used by ProsperoLight.** > It provides the native PS5 application structure, runtime, packaging, and homebrew deployment foundation. > [!IMPORTANT] > **Graphics are powered by [ps5-opengl](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-opengl).** > This OpenGL implementation provides the native PS5 rendering layer used by the Eden graphics backend. > [!IMPORTANT] > **Vulkan is powered by Mihawk's [PS5 Mesa](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Mesa) and [PS5 Vulkan](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Vulkan).** > Mihawk's Mesa/RADV driver for the PS5 runs ProsperoEden's Vulkan renderer. Many thanks to Mihawk for this work and for [all of the PS5 projects](https://github.com/mihawk-99) behind it. > [!IMPORTANT] > **Thanks to [ps5-vulkan](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/ps5-vulkan) by mpereiraesaa**, an experimental Vulkan graphics and compute API for native PS5 homebrew. ## Features - **Vulkan renderer (recommended)** - the default backend, running on Mihawk's PS5 Mesa (RADV) driver. - **OpenGL renderer** - still available through ps5-opengl. Switch between them in **Settings > Video**. - **Resolution and upscaling** - render at 0.5x to 4x of the game's resolution and choose the filter that scales it to your TV (Bilinear, AMD FSR, Bicubic or Nearest) in **Settings > Video**. Textures in a format the PS5's GPU cannot read (ASTC) are kept compressed (as BC3), which takes a quarter of the graphics memory they would need decoded. **ASTC textures** in **Settings > Video**, and in each game's settings, can be set to **Full quality** instead: those textures are then kept decoded, which uses four times the graphics memory for them and can make a game run out of memory above 1x. - **Output resolution** - the picture is made at 1080p, 1440p or 2160p: **Output resolution** in **Settings > Video**. The menu is drawn at that size too, and the PS5 scales it to your TV. - **A steadier frame rate in heavy scenes** - some games time their own frames and drop to a lower frame rate (30 to 20, or 60 to 30) as soon as a frame takes a little too long. ProsperoEden lets the game's clock give by up to 15% in those moments, so the game keeps its frame rate and runs a few percent slower instead of losing a third of its frames. - **120 Hz output** - on a display that shows 120 Hz, games can run on a 120 Hz output: **Refresh rate** in **Settings > Video**, or in one game's settings. A frame that is a little late is then shown 8 ms later instead of 17 ms, and patches for more than 60 FPS need it. The menu stays at 60 Hz. - **Frame generation** - between two of a game's own pictures ProsperoEden can show one made up from them, so a 30 FPS game looks like 60: **Frame generation** in **Settings > Video**, or in one game's settings.
