It now keeps them until graphics memory is really short. - **Smoother heavy scenes.** The renderer hands its work to the Vulkan worker in larger batches, and the emulated cores wait less on the GPU caches' locks. In the heaviest area of a test walk this removed drops to 26-28 FPS and cut the GPU thread's work by about a quarter. - **Touchpad as Minus in games.** A tap of the touchpad presses the game's Minus button, and a longer press holds it. The Touchpad + L1 and Touchpad + R1 shortcuts never reach the game as a press. - **A crash a few seconds into some games is fixed.** The motion sensors' updates could reach a part of the controller service that was not set up yet. - **Games' own system screens.** A game's error dialog, profile picker and similar screens use Eden's built-in versions, and its error dialog now answers the game instead of leaving it waiting. The firmware's versions could end a session with an out-of-memory error. - **More graphics memory.** The PS5 gives an app one pool of memory that the CPU and the GPU share, and ProsperoEden held about 3 GiB of it without using it: its heap took 3 GiB at start and the emulated console's page table 1 GiB. Both now take memory as they need it, which gives graphics about 2.6 GiB more in the largest game tested. That game ran out of graphics memory while loading at 2x; it now runs at 2x with the AMD FSR filter at a steady 30 FPS, with about 2 GiB to spare. The texture cache also measures its memory use from what is really left of the pool, instead of a driver figure that counted every allocation twice. - **A clearer message when a game runs out of graphics memory.** If a game still needs more than there is at a high resolution, give it its own lower one: Triangle on it in the Library, then **Resolution**. - **Games that accept only single Joy-Cons** now get one, and L1 and R1 are its SL and SR buttons, which those games ask for on their controller screen. - **Mods.** A game's patches, replacement files and cheats load from `mods/<title ID>/` next to `roms/`, and the game's settings list them with a switch each. `.ips` and text `.pchtxt` patches, which the emulator core could not apply, now work. The Library has one switch per game for all of its mods. See [Mods](#mods). - **120 Hz output.** **Refresh rate** in **Settings > Video**, and in each game's settings, asks the display for 120 Hz while a game runs. A display that cannot show it stays at 60 Hz, and the menu always runs at 60 Hz. After a game at 120 Hz the menu takes about five seconds to come back while the display changes rate. - **Output resolution.** **Settings > Video** has a new **Output resolution** row: 1080p (as before), 1440p or 2160p. It is the size of the picture ProsperoEden puts out, for the menu and for games. Until now a game's picture was made at 1080p and enlarged, whatever its internal resolution; at 2160p the upscaling filter scales the game straight to a 4K picture. A larger picture needs more graphics memory. - **3x and 4x resolution.** The internal resolution now goes up to 4x. These need far more graphics memory than 2x; a game that runs out says so, and can be given its own lower resolution. - **Patches for more frames than the display shows.** A game patched to run faster than the output refreshes keeps its pace: the frames the display has no refresh for are left out. - **Crash reports.** If ProsperoEden stops because of an error, it writes `crash-<date>-<time>.txt` to `/data/prosperoeden/logs`, starts again and says on the home screen where the report is. That session's logs are kept beside it, and the five newest reports stay. A report holds what failed, where in the app's code, and what was running; it never holds the contents of memory. - The launcher and the OpenGL renderer use the PS5 OpenGL 4.6 SDK 1.0.0. - The graphics driver's shader cache moved to `/data/prosperoeden/cache`, so a read-only package install keeps it. - **Experimental: block list.** With an empty file named `block-list.txt` in `/data/homebrew/PPSA99008`, ProsperoEden saves which code a 64-bit game compiled and compiles it again on a spare CPU when the game next starts. In a repeat session of a large open-world game, the emulated cores then compiled 426 blocks during play instead of 138,262, and gameplay started at 30 FPS instead of 22. It is off by default until more games have run with it. ## Changes in v1.000.030 - **New launcher.** Every screen is redrawn with OpenGL: smooth transitions between screens, text that stays sharp, panels that blur the artwork behind them, and sound effects for moving, selecting and going back. **Settings > Audio > Menu sounds** sets their level. - **Controllers on the home screen.** Four controller icons show which controllers are connected, and change as one joins or leaves. - **Loading screen.** An animated scene shows while a game starts, on both renderers. - **The Library opens at once.** The game list is read in the background, and the home screen shows each game's own name instead of its file name. - **New music** on the PS5 home screen. - **Smoother first-time gameplay.** The emulated CPU cores now share the code they compile, so each part of a game is compiled once instead of once per core. In large open-world games this halves the compile work and removes most of the stutter when gameplay starts or a new area loads. - **Faster compiling.** Compiling a game's code now takes about 40% less CPU time, which shortens the remaining stutter when gameplay starts or a new area loads. - **Startup hang fixed.** A game could stop for good right after starting, because the emulator's memory allocator could leave high-priority threads waiting on each other forever. Development builds also report where a slow start is stuck. - **Games close in about a second.** Touchpad + L1 used to take 10-25 seconds to return to the library; logging no longer waits on the console's storage, and the emulator skips needless teardown work. - **Up to four controllers.** Each signed-in PS5 user's controller becomes the next player (player 1 is whoever launched the game); controllers can join or leave during a game, and games that ask for controllers connect every one in use. - The Touchpad + L1 and Touchpad + R1 shortcuts work from any controller. - **Vibration and motion.** DualSense rumble for games that use it (turn it off in **Settings > Controls**), and the controller's gyro and accelerometer for motion controls. - **Resolution and upscaling.** **Settings > Video** now sets the internal rendering resolution (0.5x to 2x) and the filter that scales it to the TV: Bilinear, AMD FSR, Bicubic or Nearest. - **Per-game settings.** Press Triangle on a game in the Library to give it its own renderer, resolution and upscaling filter. - **Language setting.** **Settings > Language** picks the language games use (18 languages), with the console region that goes with it. It applies when a game starts. - **Game updates and DLC.** Put update and DLC files (NSP or XCI) in the `updates` folder next to `roms`; the newest update and all DLC apply when the game starts, and the game details show them. - **Build it yourself.** `make` fetches every dependency at its pinned revision and builds the release. The OpenGL renderer now uses the published PS5 OpenGL 4.6 SDK 0.6.0. ## Changes in v1.000.020 - **Vulkan is now the recommended and default renderer.** OpenGL remains available in Settings. - **Choose where your game files live.** The new **Settings > Game files** browser selects any folder, including external drives and USB devices. The old `assets/` folder keeps working until you choose one. - **App data moved to `/data/prosperoeden`.** Config, logs, covers, and saves now live outside the app folder, so updating the app never touches them. - **Settings are now stored in one JSON file.** Earlier text settings are migrated automatically on first launch. - **Faster Library navigation**, and covers and recent games that survive folder moves. - **New icons** for controller actions, pages, and the Handheld / Docked mode. **Known issues:** Ending a game with Touchpad + L1 can take several seconds. Some games can still hang on the loading screen, and some demanding games remain slow. This is a testing pre-release, not a compatibility guarantee. ## In-game shortcuts The touchpad is pressed as a button. On its own, a tap of the touchpad presses the game's Minus button (with the usual [button mapping](#button-mapping)), and a longer press holds it; a shortcut never reaches the game. | Shortcut | Action | |---|---| | Touchpad + R1 | Toggle the performance HUD | | Touchpad + L1 | End the running game and return to the library | ## Roadmap - **FPKG support** - install ProsperoEden as a fake package, alongside the current homebrew folder install. - **More performance** - CPU and GPU work to keep demanding games at their target frame rate: the short stutter when a game reaches new areas (the block list, **Compile ahead** in **Settings > Performance**, once it has run in more games and can be on by default), heavy cutscenes, and games that run slower in Docked mode than in Handheld. - **More reliable game loading** - a game that hangs while it loads can now be left with Touchpad + L1; the hangs themselves still need a log from a game that does it. - **Game names in the menu's language** - a game carries a name for each language; the Library shows the first one that is text. Show the one in the menu's language, and the name from an installed update when it has one. - **Real Joy-Cons and Pro Controllers (investigation)** - play with the original controllers connected to the PS5. The PS5 does not pair them itself, so this first needs to find out whether a homebrew app can read them: a wired Pro Controller over USB looks more likely than Joy-Cons, which only connect over Bluetooth. - **Keyboard as a controller** - map a USB keyboard's keys to the game's buttons, like the DualSense's. Text entry itself is done: it uses the PS5's on-screen keyboard. - **Multiplayer with Eden on other systems (investigation)** - join Eden's multiplayer rooms from the PS5 and play with Eden players on PC, Linux and Android, entering a room's address by hand, including a room hosted on your local network (no PSN needed). Rooms only accept the same Eden version on every side, so each release would name the matching PC version. - **DualShock 4 controllers** - use DualShock 4 controllers as players too, next to the DualSense, so multiplayer games do not need four DualSense controllers. - **Controller type for each player** - choose, for each of the four connected controllers, which controller the game sees: a Pro Controller, a pair of Joy-Cons, a single left or right Joy-Con, a GameCube controller, or Handheld mode, as Eden does on other systems. - **Better OpenGL performance** - make the OpenGL renderer faster, and add tuning options for it. - **More game compatibility** - validate more games on the PS5, and fix what keeps them from running well, such as games that crash at launch. ## Issues and reports Problems and ideas go to [GitHub issues](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ProsperoEden/issues). Reports about a particular game are welcome: name the game, and say what happens and where. A report that can be acted on has: - the game and its version (and any update or mod in use); - the ProsperoEden version, the PS5 model and system software version, and what the console runs (kstuff-lite or etaHEN, ShadowMountPlus version); - the renderer, resolution and Performance switches; - the debug logs, attached as a ZIP: turn on **Settings > Diagnostics > Detailed logging**, make the problem happen again, then zip `/data/prosperoeden/logs` (after a crash, the crash report and the logs beside it); - for a problem at a certain spot in a game, your save data from just before it, attached as a ZIP: Triangle on the game in the Library, **Save data**, **Export a copy**, then zip the folder it writes in `/data/prosperoeden/save-export`. With it the spot can be reached without playing the game up to there. **No piracy.** ProsperoEden is for games you own and dumped yourself. Do not ask for, post or link to game files, keys or firmware, here or in any of the project's channels, and do not ask where to find them. Such posts are removed. ## Elevation credits Filesystem elevation uses [PS5-Lapy-JB-Daemon](https://github.com/ArkSama/PS5-Lapy-JB-Daemon), created by ArkSama. ProsperoEden follows the cooperative owned-root design and implementation from [ProsperoEden's Lapy fork](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/PS5-Lapy-JB-Daemon), based on [mpereiraesaa's cooperative helper](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/PS5-Lapy-JB-Daemon). The build pins that source, builds its exact-title one-shot helper without local payload changes, verifies the upstream-generated manifest, and includes the resulting ELF in the release. The donor-release and firmware 13.60 fixes pinned here were merged upstream in [PS5-Lapy-JB-Daemon PR #48](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/PS5-Lapy-JB-Daemon/pull/48) and [PR #49](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/PS5-Lapy-JB-Daemon/pull/49). The pinned `57fcc19` helper also includes the guarded target-lifetime and fail-closed accounting changes from [PR #50](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/PS5-Lapy-JB-Daemon/pull/50). The previous `54a095c` helper passed five automated launch/elevate/close cycles on firmware 6.02 and five on 12.70 with root access and balanced donor references. The pinned helper completed the target-exit stress and a full one-shot elevation on firmware 12.70; it still requires an attended ProsperoEden qualification run on firmware 6.02. ## Thanks Thank you to the people who test ProsperoEden on their own consoles and report what they find: - **Jones** ([X](https://x.com/Jonesskulls), [GitHub](https://github.com/AgentJonesy)), for helping with testing. - **Phronesis**, for helping with testing. - **szampan** ([GitHub](https://github.com/heni0xyz)), for helping with testing. - **BunkinBacon**, for helping with testing. - **Cold** ([GitHub](https://github.com/JMUtechnologies)), for helping with testing. - **Bauls Deep** ([GitHub](https://github.com/bawsdeep)), for helping with testing. - **OverkillLabs**, for helping with testing. And to the people who contribute code: - **Mihawk** ([GitHub](https://github.com/mihawk-99)), besides the driver the Vulkan renderer runs on: cheats that can be chosen one by one, the fix for the crash when a game with cheats stops, the driver's shader cache working on the console, a fix for games that come without control data, and the driver build reading its versions from one place. - **quatrixone** ([GitHub](https://github.com/quatrixone)), for the Performance settings and their seven switches, also per game, and for a much faster first compilation of a game's code. - **Martin Pham** ([GitHub](https://github.com/MartinPham)), for starting a game straight from its path, which is what forwarders on the home screen use. - **matschi95** ([GitHub](https://github.com/matschi95)), for the RomM integration (browsing, downloading and playing games from your own server, and save sync) and for finding and fixing the stutter that log writes caused every few seconds. - **v0ltfault** ([GitHub](https://github.com/v0ltfault)), for tracking down why every game ended at its first picture on system software 7.40, with a fix and a write-up of the findings. - **gyn7561** ([GitHub](https://github.com/gyn7561)), for bringing frame generation to the PS5, with its settings, and for the log lines that say why it is or is not running. - **Bauls Deep** ([GitHub](https://github.com/bawsdeep)), for the Nix shell that sets up the whole build environment with one command. - **lunar-me** ([GitHub](https://github.com/lunar-me)), for a correction to the README. - **EIREXE** ([GitHub](https://github.com/EIREXE)), for the RNG seed per game, which lets mods that tell an emulator from a console by where the game is loaded (HewDraw Remix for one) work. <!-- bbr-footer:start --> <!-- Generated by ps5-homebrew-dev-protocol/scripts/readme-footer. latestRelease.name: ProsperoEden v1.000.111
latestRelease.body:
This is a mirror of the last version of ProsperoEden by BlackBearReloaded. Until the upstream ProsperoEden repository is made public again this will serve as ProsperoEden distribution

- **A new title ID: PPSA99016.** ProsperoEden used to be PPSA99008, the ID of the earlier ProsperoEden listed in the homebrew catalog, whose repository is not public currently. This version installs to `/data/homebrew/PPSA99016` as a title of its own. Your settings, saves, keys, firmware and covers are in `/data/prosperoeden` and are found as before. If you had the PPSA99008 version, it stays installed beside this one; delete its folder (`/data/homebrew/PPSA99008`) once this one works. Anything you kept inside that old folder (an early version's `assets`, a `block-list.txt`, a `language.txt`) is not moved: copy it to `/data/homebrew/PPSA99016`.
- **Builds again now that the original repositories are gone.** The game and launcher are those of v1.000.110; only where the build fetches three of its inputs changed. The PS5 OpenGL SDK comes from [darkxex/ps5-opengl](https://github.com/darkxex/ps5-opengl), a mirror of the original, at its version 1.0.2 (1.0.0 is no longer published anywhere official; its headers and exported functions are the same). The Native App Boilerplate and the Lapy helper are fetched from [drakmor/ps5-native-app-boilerplate](https://github.com/drakmor/ps5-native-app-boilerplate) and [ArkSama/PS5-Lapy-JB-Daemon](https://github.com/ArkSama/PS5-Lapy-JB-Daemon), at the same commits as before.

repos.name: PS5-ECAM
repos.description: Wii U, 3DS, DS, and Switch emulation for PS5 homebrew (Cemu + Azahar + Melon DS + Eden)
repos.readme:
PS5-ECAM plays your Wii U, Nintendo 3DS, Nintendo DS and Nintendo Switch games on a jailbroken PS5,
with Cemu, Azahar, melonDS and Eden in one launcher made for the TV and the DualSense.
Made by its co-founders, premohq and JMUtechnologies. It was called PS5CEMU-HAR until 5.0.0.

Download 5.1.0 (ZIP) · Release notes · Website · Install · Guide · Compatibility · Credits · Support

--- ## What's new in 5.1.0 A folder for each system, everything on a USB drive, and the Switch's updates and DLC wherever they are. The details are in the [release notes](https://github.com/premohq/PS5-ECAM/releases/tag/v5.1.0). - **A folder for each system:** `/data/cemu`, `/data/azahar`, `/data/melonds` and `/data/eden`. An install from before keeps working where it is, and **Reorganize** moves it in a moment, and back ([System folders](docs/SYSTEM-FOLDERS.md)). - **Everything on your USB drive:** with the app on a drive, every system's files go beside it there, the Switch's too (its keys and saves on the console stay in use). An older copy of the app left in `/data/homebrew` is no longer started or updated in place of the one you run. - **Switch:** updates and DLC are found beside a game in any games folder, a USB drive's too, and its page shows the update's version and DLC; frame generation with Lossless Scaling and your own `Lossless.dll` ([#81](https://github.com/premohq/PS5-ECAM/issues/81)); mods, cheats, players, and saves to USB and back (Ryujinx's too), from JMUtechnologies ([#86](https://github.com/premohq/PS5-ECAM/pull/86)); a game with a mods folder starts ([#77](https://github.com/premohq/PS5-ECAM/issues/77)); fixes from ProsperoEden's open pull requests (several updates of one game, a full audio buffer, Metal Gear Solid: Master Collection). - **Updates in a minute** ([#78](https://github.com/premohq/PS5-ECAM/issues/78), [#73](https://github.com/premohq/PS5-ECAM/issues/73), [#72](https://github.com/premohq/PS5-ECAM/issues/72)): Check for updates answers at once, and an update installs in about a minute and can be cancelled. - **Library:** 3DS and DS games come back to it without the app starting over; each game's play time, and **Settings > Play time** with each side's time and the most played games; **Hide from the Library** and **Surprise me** in a game's Options and Sort; Library and Settings beside the players and the clock; one layout, Light by default; graphic packs downloaded when Cemu first needs them, so the app is smaller ([#74](https://github.com/premohq/PS5-ECAM/issues/74)); network shares looked through only when you ask ([#75](https://github.com/premohq/PS5-ECAM/issues/75)); Azahar's compressed 3DS files with their names and box art. - **Settings:** fewer pages down the left, and related rows behind one row (›), every setting kept. - **Remove its update or DLC** from a Wii U ([#58](https://github.com/premohq/PS5-ECAM/issues/58)) or 3DS ([#80](https://github.com/premohq/PS5-ECAM/issues/80)) game's Options menu. - **DS:** the right stick as the stylus; from [#86](https://github.com/premohq/PS5-ECAM/pull/86), a GBA game in Slot-2 for Pal Park, a recorded microphone, touch calibration. - **Wii U:** each player's DualSense light bar in a colour of its own. **Switch:** Saves in a game's Options. - **Fixes:** stripes on empty screens ([#76](https://github.com/premohq/PS5-ECAM/issues/76)); one label size in Cyrillic ([#79](https://github.com/premohq/PS5-ECAM/issues/79)); a renamed Wii U account's name is the one games show; a Switch shader the driver refuses no longer crashes the game (This War of Mine); the Swedish menus reviewed by yeager ([#83](https://github.com/premohq/PS5-ECAM/pull/83)). Changes in earlier versions are in their [release notes](https://github.com/premohq/PS5-ECAM/releases). ## Support PS5-ECAM is free. If it brings your games back, you can support it: - **Ko-fi:** [ko-fi.com/premohq](https://ko-fi.com/premohq), for a one-off tip or the [$3 a month Early Access tier](https://ko-fi.com/premohq/tiers): highly experimental builds, builds of ECAM for other platforms, and new features before anyone else. - **PayPal:** [paypal.me/empthe](https://www.paypal.com/paypalme/empthe), or scan the code (the same one as in the app's **Settings > About**): ## Features | | Wii U | Nintendo 3DS | Nintendo DS | Nintendo Switch | |---|---|---|---|---| | **Emulator** | Cemu, x64 recompiler, Vulkan | Azahar, dynarmic recompiler, Vulkan | melonDS, ARM recompiler | Eden (ProsperoEden), dynarmic, Vulkan | | **Plays** | `.wua`, `.wud`, `.wux`, unpacked games (also in `.zip`, `.7z` and `.rar` archives) | `.3ds`, `.cci`, `.cxi`, `.app`, `.3dsx`, `.elf`, compressed `.z*`, also in `.zip`, `.7z` and `.rar` archives; installed `.cia` | `.nds`, also in `.zip`, `.7z` and `.rar` archives | `.nsp`, `.xci`, each alone or in a folder with its update and DLC | | **Picture** | 4K output, 120 Hz, FSR 1, graphic packs, ReShade, frame generation | up to 10x resolution, texture filters, layouts, borders, red-cyan 3D, frame generation | sharp, smooth or square pixels, layouts, borders | up to 4x resolution, FSR 1, anti-aliasing, docked or handheld, frame generation | | **Extras** | mods, accounts, amiibo, Skylanders portals, updates and DLC | save states, cheats, amiibo, mods, cameras, Artic Base | save states, cheats, RetroAchievements | amiibo, online rooms, mods, cheats, updates and DLC (from their folders) | - **One launcher for all four:** box art and game info from GameTDB, search, sorting and favourites, a page for each game, settings for each game, and an in-game menu on every system. - **Made for the DualSense:** every button remappable, motion controls, rumble, the touchpad as the touch screen, and up to four players on the Wii U. - **Updates itself:** a new release installs from inside the app. ## Install 1. **A PS5 that runs homebrew.** Any firmware up to 13.60, with etaHEN, OnionHEN, or an ELF loader on port 9021. See the [firmware and setup guide](docs/HEN-SETUP.md). 2. **Copy the app.** Download the [5.1.0 ZIP](https://github.com/premohq/PS5-ECAM/raw/releases/PS5-ECAM-v5.1.0.zip) ([release notes](https://github.com/premohq/PS5-ECAM/releases/tag/v5.1.0)), extract it and copy the `PPSA99360` folder to `/data/homebrew/PPSA99360`. 3. **Let your HEN in.** etaHEN: add `PPSA99360` to its app jailbreak list. OnionHEN: add `PPSA99360` at the end of `exact_title_ids` in `config.ini`, with no comma after it. Any other: have an ELF loader on port 9021. 4. **Add your games** (below), and start PS5-ECAM from the home screen. The Setup check shows what's ready and what to do about the rest. Each system keeps its files in a folder of its own: `/data/cemu`, `/data/azahar`, `/data/melonds` and `/data/eden`, with the launcher's settings, covers and logs in `/data/ps5cemu`. Updating, from PS5CEMU-HAR too: the app offers new releases itself, and the title ID stays `PPSA99360`. An install from before keeps everything where it is, in `/data/ps5cemu`, and goes on working. The app offers to give each system its folder (**Reorganize**, or later from **Settings > Game files**): the files are moved in a moment, never copied or deleted, and can be put back. [System folders](docs/SYSTEM-FOLDERS.md) has the details. Installed on a USB drive or the extended storage? A `PS5CEMU-HAR-data` folder at the top of that drive (its name from before 5.0.0, kept so nothing moves) keeps the launcher's files there instead of in `/data`, with `cemu`, `azahar`, `melonds` and `eden` beside it (the Switch's stay in `/data/eden` when they are there already). [The guide](docs/GUIDE.md#everything-on-the-apps-drive) says how. ## Your games | | Games folder | Also needs | |---|---|---| | **Wii U** | `/data/cemu/games` | disc keys in `/data/cemu/keys.txt` for encrypted `.wud` and `.wux` | | **3DS** | `/data/azahar/games` | nothing: games must be decrypted dumps; `.cia` files install from Settings | | **DS** | `/data/melonds/games` | nothing: your own BIOS and firmware in `/data/melonds/bios` are optional | | **Switch** | `/data/eden/roms` | your Switch's `prod.keys` (and `title.keys`) in `/data/eden/keys`, and its firmware in `/data/eden/firmware` | An install from before has these in `/data/ps5cemu` (`games`, `keys.txt`, `azahar/games`, and so on) until it is separated. [System folders](docs/SYSTEM-FOLDERS.md) has each system's whole folder. Any other folder, a USB drive or a network share (not for Switch games) works too: **Settings > Game files** on each system. No games, keys or firmware are included. Use dumps of games and hardware you own. ## Controls | | | |---|---| | **L1 / R1** | Library and Settings | | **Touchpad click** | The next system | | **Cross / Circle** | Play or open / back | | **Options** | A game's menu: game settings, saves, graphic packs, mods, home screen tile | | **Touchpad click + Options** | The in-game menu | | **Touchpad** | The touch screen (GamePad, 3DS and DS) | Every shortcut, the in-game menu and the rest are in the [guide](docs/GUIDE.md). ## Documentation - [Guide](docs/GUIDE.md): the launcher, each system, controls, saves, mods, the remote touch screen and where files are kept - [Firmware and setup](docs/HEN-SETUP.md) · [Mods](docs/GUIDE.md#mods) · [Compatibility](docs/COMPATIBILITY.md) - [Building from source](docs/BUILDING.md) · [Driver performance](docs/DRIVER-PERFORMANCE.md) · [Roadmap](docs/ROADMAP.md) - Problems: **Settings > Diagnostics > Copy logs to USB**, then [open an issue](https://github.com/premohq/PS5-ECAM/issues/new/choose) ## Building `make release` on Ubuntu 24.04 (WSL works) downloads every dependency at its pinned version, builds the four emulators (Eden as a program of its own, `eden/eboot.bin`) and the launcher, and writes the app to `build/app/PPSA99360` and a ZIP to `dist/`. See [docs/BUILDING.md](docs/BUILDING.md). ## Join the Discord The server at [discord.gg/grrqkv4xWw](https://discord.gg/grrqkv4xWw) is the quickest way to get help and to hear about new versions: - **Help with your setup:** ask in the support forum, one post per problem, tagged by system. - **What runs, and how well:** tested-games has a post per game with its speed, its glitches and the settings that work. - **New versions first:** every release is posted in announcements the moment it's published. - **The developer and other players:** suggest features, share your setup and hear what's coming. Bugs still go in [GitHub issues](https://github.com/premohq/PS5-ECAM/issues/new/choose), with the log from *Copy logs to USB*. ## Credits ### Founders - **[premohq](https://github.com/premohq)**, co-founder, who started the app as PS5CEMU-HAR - **[JMUtechnologies](https://github.com/JMUtechnologies)**, co-founder: a folder for each system (the Wii U's, 3DS's, DS's and Switch's files in folders of their own, Eden's side of it, an install from before still found, and the PC tool that separates one); the Switch side's mods, cheats, ReShade presets and players, and its saves to and from a USB drive, Ryujinx's too; the DS's GBA cartridge in Slot-2, its recorded microphone and touch screen calibration; and the tools that compare performance captures ([#86](https://github.com/premohq/PS5-ECAM/pull/86), [#84](https://github.com/premohq/PS5-ECAM/pull/84)) ### Contributors Big thanks to the people who sent code and fixes to PS5-ECAM itself: - **[dolphin78](https://github.com/dolphin78)**, with a massive shoutout: Artic Setup works on the PS5 because of him ([#70](https://github.com/premohq/PS5-ECAM/pull/70)). He found and fixed why the 3DS's system update failed and why a New 3DS's setup crashed, and tested it all on his own PS5 with a New 3DS XL. He also made crash reports survive a crash on the 3DS side ([#70](https://github.com/premohq/PS5-ECAM/pull/70)), fixed Artic Base's connections ([#45](https://github.com/premohq/PS5-ECAM/issues/45)), and came up with the remote touch screen and its first prototype ([#38](https://github.com/premohq/PS5-ECAM/issues/38)) - **[Mafiacoding](https://github.com/Mafiacoding)** for archived games: the ZIP support for the Wii U, 3DS and DS sides that 5.0.0's archives build on ([#53](https://github.com/premohq/PS5-ECAM/pull/53), [#50](https://github.com/premohq/PS5-ECAM/issues/50)) - **[3lmerx503](https://github.com/3lmerx503)** for finding and testing the rumble fix ([#41](https://github.com/premohq/PS5-ECAM/issues/41)) - **[yeager](https://github.com/yeager)** (Daniel Nylander) for his review of the Swedish translation ([#85](https://github.com/premohq/PS5-ECAM/pull/85)) ### Built on - [Cemu](https://github.com/cemu-project/Cemu) by the Cemu team and contributors (MPL-2.0) - [Azahar](https://github.com/azahar-emu/azahar) by the Azahar team and the Citra contributors before them (GPL-2.0-or-later), with dynarmic by MerryMage and contributors - [melonDS](https://github.com/melonDS-emu/melonDS) by Arisotura and the melonDS team (GPL-3.0), with its FreeBIOS replacements - [Eden](https://github.com/eden-emu/mirror), the Switch emulator, by the Eden team (GPL-3.0-or-later), and [ProsperoEden](https://github.com/Swordpdf/ProsperoEden), its PS5 port and launcher, by **Sword** ([Swordpdf](https://github.com/Swordpdf)), **BlackBearReloaded**, **bawsdeep**, **Rockiu0** and its contributors (GPL-3.0-or-later; the Switch side runs it with `patches/eden`) - **Mihawk** for RADV on PS5 ([PS5_Mesa](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Mesa), [PS5_Vulkan](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Vulkan), the payload SDK fork and its platform layer) and the PS5 ports of Azahar and dynarmic ([PS5_Azahar](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Azahar)), with contributions from **mpereiraesaa** - **BlackBearReloaded** for ProsperoEden, which the launcher's layout, artwork, Eden theme and software renderer build on, and the PS5 Native App Boilerplate for the app runtime, packaging and sandbox elevation (its repository went with their account: [drakmor's copy](https://github.com/drakmor/ps5-native-app-boilerplate) is the one the build fetches) - **heydemoura** for the [PS5 Forwarder Format](https://github.com/heydemoura/ps5-forwarder-format) the home screen tiles use - **John Törnblom** for the [PS5 Payload SDK](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk), and **pacbrew** for their PS5 libraries - [libsmb2](https://github.com/sahlberg/libsmb2) and [libnfs](https://github.com/sahlberg/libnfs) by Ronnie Sahlberg for the network shares, and [rcheevos](https://github.com/RetroAchievements/rcheevos) by RetroAchievements - **Swordpdf** for the etaHEN jailbreak request from PS5SX2 - **Dimok** for the Wii U Homebrew Launcher's background, and the authors of the 3DS Homebrew Launcher, which inspired the 3DS side's - The [Lexend](https://github.com/googlefonts/lexend) authors for the launcher's font (SIL OFL 1.1) - [GameTDB](https://www.gametdb.com/) for box art and game information, and the authors of the [Cemu community graphic packs](https://github.com/cemu-project/cemu_graphic_packs) ## License The app's own code is GPL-3.0-or-later (see [LICENSE](LICENSE)). Files derived from Cemu keep Cemu's MPL-2.0, as their headers say; Azahar is GPL-2.0-or-later, melonDS GPL-3.0, and Eden and ProsperoEden GPL-3.0-or-later (their notices are in the app's `eden/` folder), and the app that includes them is distributed under GPL-3.0-or-later. Other third-party components keep their own licenses. PS5-ECAM is an independent homebrew project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Sony Interactive Entertainment, Nintendo, or the Cemu, Azahar, melonDS, Eden or ProsperoEden projects. latestRelease.name: PS5-ECAM 5.1.0
latestRelease.body:
## Download

**[PS5-ECAM-v5.1.0.zip](https://github.com/premohq/PS5-ECAM/raw/releases/PS5-ECAM-v5.1.0.zip)** (75.0 MB), on the [`releases` branch](https://github.com/premohq/PS5-ECAM/tree/releases).

SHA-256: `c6a0c0b50617d923a5e7a5cb37d799c746118342cd850d5bca634c3670a6562f`

From 3.0.0 or later, the app offers this update itself as it starts (**Settings > Online > PS5-ECAM updates** checks again). Otherwise extract the ZIP and copy the `PPSA99360` folder to `/data/homebrew/PPSA99360`, replacing the old one. Your settings, saves and games stay where they are.

## What's new

### A folder for each system
- **New installs keep each system's files in a folder of its own:** `/data/cemu`, `/data/azahar`, `/data/melonds` and `/data/eden`, each with its own games, updates, DLC, keys and firmware or BIOS folders. The launcher's settings, logs, covers and downloads stay in `/data/ps5cemu`. This is JMUtechnologies's work.
- **An install from before keeps working where it is.** At a start the app offers to **Reorganize** (or **Later**), and **Settings > Game files > A folder for each system** does it at any time. The app starts again and renames the files into their folders, so it takes a moment whatever their size and copies or deletes nothing. A move cut short by a power cut finishes at the next start, and the same row puts everything back. Your games folder settings, Cemu's game folders and home screen tiles follow the files. It works on a PS5 without a HEN too. [System folders](https://github.com/premohq/PS5-ECAM/blob/PS5-ECAM/docs/SYSTEM-FOLDERS.md) has the details.

### Everything on your USB drive
- With the app on a USB drive or the extended storage, every system's files go beside it there, **the Switch's too** (its keys, firmware, updates, saves and shader cache). Switch keys and saves already on the console stay in use.
- An older copy of the app left in `/data/homebrew` is no longer started after a game, or updated, in place of the one you run.

### Switch
- **Updates and DLC are found wherever they are:** in any games folder (a USB drive's too), and loose beside a game. A game's page and Recently played show its update's version ("Update v1.2.0") and how many DLC it has.
- **Frame generation with Lossless Scaling** (#81): with your own `Lossless.dll` (from the Lossless Scaling you bought) in `/data/eden/user/lossless`, the Switch's frame generation is Lossless Scaling's, steadier and with fewer artefacts on grass and water. Without it, it's MihawkGen's as before. `boot.log` says which.
- **From JMUtechnologies** (#86): each game's mods and cheats, with a switch each; Eden's ReShade presets for the side or one game; Eden's players (choose, create, rename and remove); and a game's save copied to a USB drive and back, as a plain folder or Ryujinx's. **Saves** is in a game's Options menu too.
- **A game with a mods folder starts** (#77), such as Mario Kart 8 Deluxe with its Booster Course. This is upstream ProsperoEden's PR #288 by Oliv3rmoon.
- **More fixes from ProsperoEden's open pull requests:** a game with several updates beside it takes the newest (#287, Oliv3rmoon); a full audio buffer drops old audio instead of stopping the game (#289, Oliv3rmoon); and games made of several programs, such as Metal Gear Solid: Master Collection, go from their launcher to the game (#298, Holland-exe).
- **A shader the driver refuses no longer crashes the game.** This came from a crash report of This War of Mine.
- ProsperoEden's own launcher never opens from the app, and its 26 MB of menus are out of the ZIP.

### Updates in a minute (#78, #73, #72)
- **Check for updates answers at once, and an update installs in about a minute.** dolphin78 found why an update took 20 to 30 minutes: each request then waited for GitHub to drop its idle connection. Every request now asks for the connection to be closed (his fix: 74 s on his console).
- **The update's files are unpacked and moved four at a time.** A download can be cancelled with **Circle**, and one that stalls fails instead of hanging. The restart after an update works the way the library's does, and if the old version starts again, the app says so instead of offering the same update again.
- Every network call (updates, graphic packs, box art, RetroAchievements, rooms, shares) gives the PS5's name lookup 2 s a try, three tries (#73).

### Library and launcher
- **One layout**, with **Light** by default: Recently played as a row of box art, then every game as a list. The themes are skins over it: Light, Link Jack, Classic (3.0), Midnight and Eden. The library's filters are optional, and off by default.
- **Hide from the Library** in a game's Options, and **Surprise me** in Sort to pick a game for you.
- **Play time:** each game's time, and **Settings > Play time** with each side's time and the ten most played games.
- **3DS and DS games come back to the library** without the app starting over.
- Library and Settings sit at the bar's right, beside the players and the clock.
- **The app is smaller** (#74): the Wii U's community graphic packs are no longer in the ZIP. The first time Cemu starts without them, it downloads the latest in the background. Packs you copied in by hand are left alone.
- **Network shares are looked through only when you ask** (#75): each side shows the list from its last look until **Settings > Game files > Look for games now**. **Look on network shares at every start** brings the old way back.
- **Azahar's compressed 3DS files** (`.zcci`, `.zcxi`, `.z3dsx` and `.zcia`) show with their names, icons and box art, and `.zcia` installs as a `.cia` does.
- **No more lines crossing the screen** (#72) and **no stripes on empty screens** (#76): the backdrop's grain holds still. The dark gradients have no bands, and Terminal's scanlines are crisp without the flicker.

### Settings
- **Fewer pages down the left:** each side's list fits without scrolling (the Switch's 16 pages are 12), and related rows sit behind one row (**›**). Every setting is kept.
- **One label size in each list** (#79, #76), so a Russian or Ukrainian page no longer has rows of different sizes.

### Remove its update or DLC
- In a **Wii U** game's Options (what's installed in `mlc01`, #58) and a **3DS** game's (#80): pick the update, the DLC or both. **Install a CIA file** puts a 3DS one back.

### 3DS and DS
- **Screen gap:** the two screens held apart, as the console's hinge holds them (**Settings > Screens**, or a quick action in the in-game menu).
- **DS: the right stick as the stylus** (**Settings > Screens > Touch**, off by default), for games like Metroid Prime Hunters.
- **DS, from JMUtechnologies** (#86): a GBA game in Slot-2 for Pal Park, the microphone as noise, silence or a recorded WAV, and touch calibration for each game.
- The DS's screens are centred to the pixel.

### Wii U
- **Each player's light bar has its own colour** (blue, red, green and pink, as the PS5 lights them), so four players can tell who is who.
- **A renamed account's new name is the one games show.**
- A game the library leaves out now says why in Cemu's log (missing files, no disc key, folders named in capitals).

### Other
- **Swedish** reviewed by yeager (Daniel Nylander) (#83, #85), and every new text in all of the app's languages.
- A start no longer waits the HEN's full 3 s when it has what it needs, and the boot log times each wait.
- Performance tools for comparing captures, for developers (#84, JMUtechnologies).

## Notes

- **Updating from 5.0.1 inside the app uses 5.0.1's updater**, which can sit at "0 of 0 MB" for many minutes before it goes on (#78). Let it run, or copy the folder by hand. Updates from 5.1.0 on take about a minute.
- With an install from before, the first start offers **Reorganize**. **Later** keeps everything where it is. Before you **Go back** to an earlier version, put the folders back from the same row.
- Report problems with the logs from **Settings > Diagnostics > Copy logs to USB**. Known issues are in the [guide](https://github.com/premohq/PS5-ECAM/blob/PS5-ECAM/docs/GUIDE.md#known-issues).
- Join the Discord for help and news: https://discord.gg/grrqkv4xWw
- Support PS5-ECAM on Ko-fi: https://ko-fi.com/premohq

## Thanks

**JMUtechnologies**, PS5-ECAM's co-founder, for a folder for each system, the Switch's mods, cheats, players and save transfers, the DS's Slot-2, microphone and touch calibration (#86), and the performance tools (#84).

**dolphin78**, for finding why updates took half an hour and fixing it (#78), and for pinning down the stripes on empty screens (#76).

**yeager** (Daniel Nylander), for the Swedish review; **Oliv3rmoon** and **Holland-exe**, whose ProsperoEden fixes are in; and **Sword** and the [ProsperoEden](https://github.com/Swordpdf/ProsperoEden) team.

Thanks also to asp0909, pankosoknap, gaoyimin1980, TigerHobbes and CroCop86 for the reports, and to everyone testing on the Discord.

repos.name: PS64
repos.description: View and control a Commodore 64 Ultimate from a PS5 (and macOS): video/audio streams, controller input, file browser, search, favourites, Assembly64
repos.readme:
# PS64

Play the Commodore 64 on a jailbroken PS5 (or a Mac), with or without the real hardware.

- **Stream**: show a **Commodore 64 Ultimate**'s picture and sound and drive it from the
  DualSense: on-screen keyboard, file browser, search, favourites.
- **VICE C64**: no C64? PS64's **built-in emulator** (VICE) runs one. Copy in games or download
  them from Assembly64.
- **SID**: a **music player** for C64 tunes, on PS64 itself or on the Ultimate's SID chips.
- **VICE VIC20**: the C64's little brother, built in too. Copy in its games.

Both machines can search the online **Assembly64** database and start what you find straight
away.

*The emulators in PS64 are deliberately simple. For something more feature-rich,
use a dedicated emulator.*

## Install

**PS5** (jailbroken, with [ShadowMountPlus](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus)):
install **PS64** from the [Prospero Store](https://prosperostore.net/app/PPSA06464/), and
update it there. It gets its own tile on the PS5's home screen. PS64 keeps your settings and
files in **`/data/ps64/`**, so updates don't touch them. Copy files there with an FTP client
(the PS5's FTP server, port 2121).

**Mac** (Apple Silicon): build PS64 yourself; see [docs/BUILDING.md](docs/BUILDING.md).
Run as an app, it keeps its settings and folders in **`~/Documents/PS64`** (the Mac paths
below).

**C64 Ultimate** (for Stream): turn on **Web Remote Control** (the REST API) in its network
settings, and **FTP** for the file browser. PS64 finds it on the network by itself.

## The home screen

PS64 starts on a 3D home screen, a carousel: **SID** (the music player), **VICE C64** (the
emulator, in the middle) and **Stream** (the C64 Ultimate, shown live on the monitor once
found), with **VICE VIC20** (the old TV) waiting behind. Left/Right turn it (it goes round),
Cross starts the one in the middle. **Options > Home** goes back there from a machine.

- **Quit**: hold Circle (a ring fills round it; on the Mac, hold Esc or press Cmd+Q).
- **Settings** (Options): the C64 Ultimates found (pick one, enter an
  address, or give its network password) and the **Home music** volume.
- **Home music**: a random tune from your SID folder plays on the home screen (one of
  Assembly64's latest if the folder is empty). Square plays another, Triangle turns it off
  or on; volume 1 to 10 in Settings (0 is off). It stops when you open a machine.

## Controls

| Controller | On the C64 |
| --- | --- |
| D-pad / left stick, Cross | Joystick and fire |
| Square / Triangle / Circle | SPACE / RETURN / RUN/STOP |
| L1 / R1 / L2 / R2 | F1 / F3 / F5 / F7 |
| Touchpad click | On-screen keyboard (every key, with Shift / C= / CTRL) |
| L3 | File browser |
| R3 | The Ultimate's own menu |
| Options | PS64's menu |

**On-screen keyboard**: D-pad moves, Cross types, Circle closes, Square DEL, Triangle SPACE,
R2 RETURN, L1 Shift (twice locks), R1 C=, L2 CTRL. Keys show what they'll type with the
current modifiers. The shortcut buttons can be changed (`button-square = f2`, etc.).

**The menu (Options)**: Home, Resume, browse and search files, Search Assembly64, Favourites,
Recents, Disk (multi-disk games), Reset C64, Reboot / Switch off and on, D-pad mode (emulators),
Cartridge, Audio level (Left/Right; Cross mutes), Joystick port, Update search index, About,
Quit. On screens with lists, the hint line at the bottom shows the buttons.

**On the Mac**, any SDL-supported controller works, and so does the keyboard on its own:

- **Typing**: in a machine the Mac keyboard is the C64's. Keys are held as you hold them in
  the built-in machines (so they work in games); on a C64 Ultimate they're typed into its
  keyboard buffer. Esc is RUN/STOP, Option is C=, Control is CTRL, PgUp (fn+Up) is RESTORE,
  Home (fn+Left) is CLR/HOME, F1-F8 the C64's function keys (fn+F1... on a laptop keyboard).
- **Joystick**: **Cmd+J** turns the arrows into the joystick, with Space or Right Shift as
  fire (other keys still type); Cmd+J again for typing. Starting a game turns it on.
- **PS64's keys**: **Cmd+O** menu (on the home screen: Settings), **Cmd+B** file browser,
  **Cmd+K** on-screen keyboard, **Cmd+F** fullscreen, **Cmd+M** mute, **Cmd+Q** quit. In PS64's
  screens: arrows, Return, Esc, Space, PgUp/PgDn, Tab, F (favourite) and L.
- With no controller connected, the hints show these keys instead of controller buttons.

## Stream: the C64 Ultimate

PS64 starts the Ultimate's video and audio streams, shows them, and stops them when you quit.
It remembers the C64 you chose.

- **File browser** (L3, or Options > Browse files): the Ultimate's storage (`/SD`, `/Flash`,
  `/Temp`, USB). Cross opens a folder or starts a file; Square shows more actions; Circle
  goes up; L1/R1 page.

  | File | Cross | Square |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | `.prg` | Run | Load |
  | `.d64 .d71 .d81 .g64 .g71` | Mount & run (reboots, mounts on drive A, `LOAD"*",8,1`, `RUN`) | Mount on A or B only |
  | `.crt` | Run cartridge | |
  | `.sid` / `.mod` | Play | |

- **Search files**: finds files by name across the C64's storage. The first time, it builds
  an index of the folders in `search-roots` (default `/SD`, e.g. `/SD,/USB0`); you can search
  while it builds. **Update search index** refreshes it.
- **Reset C64** restarts it (a running cartridge restarts too); **Reboot C64** also clears
  the cartridge.
- **Typing**: on the C64 Ultimate's firmware 1.1.0, keys go into the C64's keyboard buffer.
  That works in BASIC, loaders and most menus, but not in games that read the keyboard
  directly, and there's no joystick. Real key presses and the joystick come with firmware
  that has the Ultimate's input command; PS64 uses it automatically when it's there.

## VICE C64: the built-in emulator

A C64 inside PS64: keyboard and joystick work in games, multi-disk games swap disks, and
disks load at full speed. **Options > Home** pauses it; **VICE C64** carries on where it was.

- **Games folder**: `/data/ps64/games` (Mac: `~/Documents/PS64/games`). Copy in D64, G64,
  D71, D81, PRG, T64, TAP and CRT files, in folders if you like. **Browse games folder** and
  **Search games folder** work like the Ultimate's; Square on a disk offers **Insert into
  drive 8** without starting it.
- **USB drives** plugged into the PS5 appear at the top as **USB0**, USB1...
- **Assembly64** downloads are kept (in `emulator/downloads/`) and start from there next time.
- **Multi-disk games**: starting a disk also loads the folder's other disks, in name order;
  **Options > Disk: < 1 of 2 >** swaps them.
- **D-pad**: joystick by default (port 2; **Joystick port** in the menu). **Options > D-pad**
  switches it to cursor keys and RETURN for BASIC and menus.
- **Reset C64** resets; **Switch off and on** also removes disks and cartridge games.
- No ROM files are needed. SID and MOD files play in the SID player, not in the emulator.

## VICE VIC20

**VICE VIC20** on the home screen (turn the carousel to the TV) is a second built-in emulator,
VICE's VIC-20. It works like VICE C64 (keyboard, joystick, the menu, browse and search,
favourites), with its own folder and without Assembly64 (which has C64 software only). The two
each wait where they were while you use the other.

- **Games folder**: `/data/ps64/vic20` (Mac: `~/Documents/PS64/vic20`), with USB drives at the
  top. It runs PRG, D64, TAP, T64 and cartridge images (`.crt`, `.20`, `.40`, `.60`, `.a0`,
  `.b0`).
- **Memory expansion** is chosen from the program's size. To force one, put it in the file or
  folder name: `(8k)`, `[16k]`, or a folder called `24k`.
- One joystick port, so no **Joystick port** in its menu.

## Cartridges (fast loaders)

**Options > Cartridge: < Off >** puts a cartridge such as **Epyx FastLoad** in the expansion
port and leaves it there; Left/Right choose, and the C64 restarts with it. PS64 doesn't
include any (cartridge ROMs are copyrighted): bring your own `.crt` files.

- **VICE C64**: copy them into `/data/ps64/carts` (Mac: `~/Documents/PS64/carts`). The choice is
  saved and stays through loads; a cartridge game (CRT) takes its place while it runs.
- **C64 Ultimate**: copy them into the Ultimate's `/flash/carts` folder. PS64 sets its
  Cartridge setting and reboots it. That isn't saved to the Ultimate's flash, so switching
  the C64 off takes the cartridge out (save it from the Ultimate's menu to keep it).

## SID: the music player

Plays C64 tunes (.sid files) with the reSIDfp emulation of the 6581 and 8580 chips. Its lists,
switched with Left/Right:

- **Local**: the SID folder, `/data/ps64/sids` (Mac: `~/Documents/PS64/sids`), with USB
  drives at the top.
- **Assembly64**: search for tunes (R1 shows the latest); the results become the playlist.
- **C64 Ultimate** (while connected): the Ultimate's storage.

Cross plays, L1/R1 change the subtune, L2/R2 the tune, Square pauses, Triangle cycles in
order / shuffle / repeat-one, Circle goes home. Tunes end on time (HVSC song lengths; 3
minutes if unknown) and the list plays on. The screen shows the title, author, chip, time,
each voice and an oscilloscope.

With a C64 Ultimate connected, the first row, **Play on**, sends tunes to its real SID chips
instead (the sound comes back through the stream).

## Assembly64, favourites and recents

- **Search Assembly64** (Options): type a name, choose a category with L2 (it starts on
  Games), R2 searches. Cross opens an entry's files; Cross on a file downloads and starts it,
  Square shows other actions. Screenshots of CSDb releases show alongside.
- **Favourites**: Triangle on a title (in the browser, search results, Assembly64, Recents)
  adds or removes it; favourites have a star. **Options > Favourites** has **Games** and
  **SIDs**. A favourite folder or Assembly64 entry starts its first runnable file.
- **Recents**: the last 25 things started, newest first.

## Settings file

PS64 saves your choices in `ps64.cfg` (`/data/ps64/ps64.cfg`, Mac
`~/Documents/PS64/ps64.cfg`), one `key = value` per line. You rarely need to edit it, but
useful keys include:

| Key | What |
| --- | --- |
| `c64`, `password` | The C64 Ultimate to stream from, and its network password |
| `stream-volume`, `emulator-volume`, `sid-volume` | Levels in dB (0 to -30; -12 to start) |
| `home-music` | Home music volume, 0 (off) to 10 |
| `search-roots` | Folders the Ultimate's search index covers |
| `games-dir`, `vic20-dir`, `sids-dir`, `carts-dir` | Other folders for games, VIC-20 games, tunes, cartridges |
| `dpad`, `vic20-dpad` | `keys` makes the D-pad cursor keys in VICE C64 (and the stream) or VICE VIC20 |
| `button-square` (etc.) | A C64 key for a shortcut button |
| `usb-prefix` | Where USB drives are mounted (`none` turns them off) |

## Building, releasing

- [docs/BUILDING.md](docs/BUILDING.md): building for the Mac and the PS5, command-line
  options, testing, source layout.
- [docs/RELEASING.md](docs/RELEASING.md): releases to the Prospero Store.

## Licence and credits

PS64 is free software under the GNU General Public License v3.0 (`LICENSE`). It includes or
builds with:

- [VICE](https://vice-emu.sourceforge.io) (GPL-2.0-or-later), through its
  [libretro core](https://github.com/libretro/vice-libretro) and the
  [PS5 port](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_VICE), for the C64 and the VIC-20 (their ROMs
  come with VICE); `tools/get_vice.sh` names the exact
  source commit. Binaries that include it are distributed under GPL-3.0 with that source.
- [libsidplayfp](https://github.com/libsidplayfp/libsidplayfp) 3.1.1 and
  [libresidfp](https://github.com/libsidplayfp/libresidfp) 1.2.3 (GPL-2.0-or-later).
- Song lengths from the [High Voltage SID Collection](https://hvsc.c64.org)
  (`Songlengths.md5`); no tunes are included.
- SDL2 (zlib licence); on the PS5, the ps5-payload-sdk and the
  [PS5 Native App Boilerplate](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-native-app-boilerplate)
  (GPL-3.0-or-later), with dlmalloc by Doug Lea (public domain / MIT-0 style).
- Screenshots of CSDb releases from [CSDb](https://csdb.dk), decoded with
  [stb_image](https://github.com/nothings/stb) (public domain / MIT).
- Controller button icons: Kenney's [Input Prompts](https://kenney.nl/assets/input-prompts)
  1.5 (CC0), rasterised with [nanosvg](https://github.com/memononen/nanosvg) (zlib).
- The overlay font includes `font8x8_basic` (public domain).
- Searching uses [Assembly64](https://hackerswithstyle.se) (PS64 sends its own client ID).

repos.readme:
# SwanStation - PlayStation 1, aka. PSX Emulator
[Features](#features) | [System Requirements](#system-requirements) | [Disclaimers](#disclaimers)

SwanStation is a hard fork and open-source Libretro core implementation of DuckStation, which is an emulator of the Sony PlayStation(TM) console, focusing on playability, speed, and long-term maintainability. The goal is to be as accurate as possible while maintaining performance suitable for low-end devices. "Hack" options are discouraged, the default configuration should support all playable games with only some of the enhancements having compatibility issues.

A "BIOS" ROM image can be used, but is not required. You can use an image from any hardware version or region, although mismatching game regions and BIOS regions may have compatibility issues. A ROM image is not provided with the emulator for legal reasons, you should dump this from your own console using Caetla or other means. If no ROM image is provided, [OpenBIOS](https://pcsx-redux.consoledev.net/openbios/) will be used instead.

## Features

SwanStation features include:

 - CPU Recompiler/JIT (x86-64, armv7/AArch32 and AArch64)
 - Hardware (D3D11, OpenGL, Vulkan) and software rendering
 - Upscaling, texture filtering, and true colour (24-bit) in hardware renderers
 - PGXP for geometry precision, texture correction, and depth buffer emulation
 - Adaptive downsampling filter
 - Post processing shader chains
 - "Fast boot" for skipping BIOS splash/intro
 - Save state support
 - Supports bin/cue images, raw bin/img files, MAME CHD, single-track ECM, MDS/MDF, and unencrypted PBP formats.
 - Direct booting of homebrew executables
 - Direct loading of Portable Sound Format (psf) files
 - Digital and analog controllers for input (rumble is forwarded to host)
 - Namco GunCon lightgun support (simulated with mouse)
 - NeGcon support
 - Emulated CPU overclocking
 - Multitap controllers (up to 8 devices)
 - RetroAchievements
 - Automatic loading/applying of PPF patches

## System Requirements
 - A CPU faster than a potato. But it needs to be x86_64, AArch32/armv7, or AArch64/ARMv8, otherwise you won't get a recompiler and it'll be slow.
 - For the hardware renderers, a GPU capable of OpenGL 3.1/OpenGL ES 3.0/Direct3D 11 Feature Level 10.0 (or Vulkan 1.0) and above. So, basically anything made in 2013 or later.

### Region detection and BIOS images
By default, SwanStation will emulate the region check present in the CD-ROM controller of the console. This means that when the region of the console does not match the disc, it will refuse to boot, giving a "Please insert PlayStation CD-ROM" message. SwanStation supports automatic detection disc regions, and if you set the console region to auto-detect as well, this should never be a problem.

The region checking can be disabled in the console options tab. This is the only way to play unlicensed games or homebrew which does not supply a correct region string on the disc, aside from using fastboot which skips the check entirely.

Mismatching the disc and console regions with the check disabled is supported, but may break games if they are patching the BIOS and expecting specific content.

### LibCrypt protection and SBI files

A number of PAL region games use LibCrypt protection, requiring additional CD subchannel information to run properly. libcrypt not functioning usually manifests as hanging or crashing, but can sometimes affect gameplay too, depending on how the game implemented it.

For these games, make sure that the CD image and its corresponding SBI (.sbi) file have the same name and are placed in the same directory. SwanStation will automatically load the SBI file when it is found next to the CD image.

For example, if your disc image was named `Spyro3.cue`, you would place the SBI file in the same directory, and name it `Spyro3.sbi`.

## Tests
 - Passes amidog's CPU and GTE tests in both interpreter and recompiler modes, partial passing of CPX tests

## Disclaimers

"PlayStation" and "PSX" are registered trademarks of Sony Interactive Entertainment Europe Limited. This project is not affiliated in any way with Sony Interactive Entertainment.

latestRelease.body:
# PSSwanStation build 25

## Added

- **GameShark codes typed in.** "Add a GameShark code" in a game's Cheats asks for a name, then the code on a keypad; it is switched on at once and kept in the game's own `cheats/<serial>.cht`.
- **Cloud saves** (Settings, Games and saving): memory cards, and save states if wanted, kept in Google Drive or Dropbox too, both ways. Signing in takes a phone and a code.
- **Sound delay** (Settings, Sound): the game's sound kept 60, 32 or 16 ms ahead of the speakers.
- **MMPX**, a scaling filter for pixel art.
- **The PlayStation Mouse**: the touch pad (or the right stick) moves it; the touch pad pressed, Cross or R1 is its left button, Circle or L1 its right.
- **"Differs from the original"** (Settings, Picture; "Look" in the menu over a game): every setting in force that is not as the PlayStation had it, put back one by one or all at once.
- **Console tuning** (Settings, System): sound and the USB controllers ahead of the emulator and background jobs after it, the graphics driver on its own thread, and how long the driver checks and sleeps while it waits for the GPU. All off, or the driver's own, unless chosen.
- **The boot log measures the game**: with "Measure the game in the boot log", a line every five seconds of play (speed, worst frame, what each part of a frame took, draws, render passes and barriers per frame); always, a line when a game has run under 95 % for two seconds, and its average speed when it closes.

## Changed

- **A new install looks and runs as the PlayStation did**: the software renderer at the console's resolution, its interlacing, the cracks between polygons, the edges a television hid cropped, no texture pack, the CPU's instruction cache. An install from before keeps its settings.
- **Picture presets**: Original, Original on a TV (composite signal, curved picture tube), Fast (2x), Normal (4x), Enhanced (6x), Beautiful (8x) and Speedrun.
- **The CPU's instruction cache as the PlayStation has it**: a line takes 4 to 7 cycles to fill from RAM (it took 1 cycle a word), and the same code reached through either of its addresses is cached once.
- **The graphics driver is Mesa 27's RADV** with Crux2's fixes for this console: the GPU's GFX10.1 hardware workarounds (against wrong shader results and GPU hangs), memory kept until the GPU is done with it (against a whole-console hang), a shader cache that stays on, cheaper draw calls.
- **While a game falls behind the screen** a third frame may wait to be shown, so a late frame no longer holds the next one back.
- Newer parts: SwanStation's newest (libretro/swanstation 631f0fb), libsmb2 (727feaa) and libnfs (371333f).

## Fixed

- Closing a game no longer brings every file up to date with the network share: only its memory card and save states. The rest is brought up to date when PSSwanStation starts.
- A save state with an impossible timing event, MDEC command or video timing is refused instead of running on broken.

## Source

This ZIP was built from PSSwanStation commit `3e258156af8b0e351d365f68cb0e41d2c1bb988d`, this release's tag. The title is distributed under the GNU General Public License, version 3, as a whole; the source of every part is public at the revision it was built from:

repos.readme:
# chiral-ftp **The ultimate file manager and FTP interface, on every machine you own.** chiral-ftp is cross-platform: it runs on the **PS5**, the **Nintendo Switch**, the **Mac** and **Linux**. It's used with a controller on the TV (or a keyboard and mouse on a computer) and works in the spirit of FileZilla. And every copy finds the others on your network: **Quick connect** opens one from another in two presses. | | | |---|---| | **PS5** | a native title on the dashboard, via ShadowMountPlus | | **Nintendo Switch** | homebrew (`.nro`) from hbmenu | | **Mac** | `chiral-ftp.app` (macOS 27 or later, Apple silicon) | | **Linux** | an `.AppImage` (x86_64 or ARM64) | | **Windows** | one `.exe` (Windows 10 or 11, x64; runs on Windows on ARM too) | Android, PS4 and other platforms are next. When it opens, you choose what to do: - **FTP server**: turn the console into an FTP server. The screen shows the address and login; change the username, password or port, or allow anonymous logins. Connected clients, transfers and speed are shown live. - **Web app**: open chiral-ftp in a browser on your PC or phone. Browse the console's files, download them, upload from the browser (drag and drop works), copy, move, rename and delete. An FTP client tab is also there. - **File manager**: two panes for copying and moving files: internal storage, Homebrew, USB drives and extended storage on the PS5; the SD card and USB drives on the Switch. Free space is shown for each drive. - **FTP / SFTP client**: connect to a laptop, PC or NAS and transfer both ways. Saved sites and recent connections, resume, and up to 30 simultaneous transfers (5 by default). - **Quick connect**: see the other copies of chiral-ftp on your network and browse one of them, with a code to confirm on its screen. See [Quick connect](#quick-connect). The servers keep running while you use another mode. Closing chiral-ftp stops them. | On the PS5 | On the Nintendo Switch | |---|---| | ![The start screen on the PS5](docs/screenshots/ps5-start.png) | ![The start screen on the Switch](docs/screenshots/switch-start.png) | | **On a computer** (Windows, Mac and Linux) | **The web app**, in any browser | | ![The computer interface: the SFTP server page](docs/screenshots/computer-server.png) | ![The web app's FTP / SFTP client](docs/screenshots/web-client.png) | Every screen, on every platform: [Screenshots](#screenshots). What's new in each version is in [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md). ## Languages Settings → Language; "Automatic" follows the system language. | | PS5 | Switch | Mac and Linux | |---|:---:|:---:|:---:| | English, Spanish, French, Italian, Russian | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | | Japanese, Korean, Chinese, Arabic | ✓ | | ✓ | ## PS5 **Requirements** - A jailbroken PS5 with **ShadowMountPlus** and an **ELF loader (elfldr) listening on port 9021** when chiral-ftp starts. chiral-ftp uses it to get full access to the console's storage (see Lapy under [Thanks](#thanks)); without it, the app only sees its own sandbox. - Tested on PS5 firmware **13.60**. Other firmware may work but hasn't been tested. **Install** 1. Download `chiral-ftp-ps5-1.1.zip` from the releases and unpack it. It contains the folder `PPSA96024`. 2. Copy that folder to `/data/homebrew/PPSA96024` on the PS5. 3. Make sure the folder and **every file in it are 777**. The PS5 refuses to start a title otherwise ("can't start the game or app"). The zip stores all modes as 777, but some FTP clients don't keep them. 4. Start chiral-ftp from the dashboard. The start screen should say "Full access to the console's storage", and how it was granted. **Updating:** close chiral-ftp completely before you replace its files. Most FTP clients overwrite `eboot.bin` in place, and the console silently refuses that while the title is in use. Upload it under another name and rename it over the old one, or use `make PLATFORM=ps5 deploy` (see [Building](#building)). Settings, saved sites and history are kept in `/data/chiral-ftp`, so updates keep them. Every file chiral-ftp writes to the PS5 is set to 777, so homebrew you copy starts; files it uploads to a server are set to 777 there too, when the server allows it. ## Nintendo Switch **Requirements:** a Switch running custom firmware (Atmosphère) with **hbmenu**. **Install** 1. Download `chiral-ftp.nro` from the releases. 2. Copy it into `/switch` on the SD card. To update, replace it. 3. Start it from hbmenu. Started from the album, homebrew runs with its memory capped near 448 MB. That is enough for chiral-ftp, but for the console's full memory hold **R** while launching a game and pick chiral-ftp from the menu that opens. The start screen says which one you got. **USB drives** show up in the drive list as soon as they're plugged in (FAT32, exFAT, NTFS and ext2/3/4), as `/usb0`, `/usb1`…, in the file manager, over the FTP server and in the web app. Settings, saved sites, history and host keys are kept in `/switch/chiral-ftp`, so updates keep them. ## Windows, Mac and Linux **Mac** 1. Download `chiral-ftp.app` from the releases. 2. Drag it to Applications. It carries its own libraries. 3. The app isn't notarized by Apple, so the first time macOS says it can't check it: open **System Settings > Privacy & Security** and choose **Open Anyway** (or run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/chiral-ftp.app` once). It needs **macOS 27 or later on Apple silicon**, and keeps its settings in `~/Library/Application Support/chiral-ftp`. **Linux** 1. Download `chiral-ftp-1.1-x86_64.AppImage` from the releases, or `chiral-ftp-1.1-aarch64.AppImage` for an ARM computer (a Raspberry Pi 4 or 5 on 64-bit, for example). 2. Make it executable (`chmod +x chiral-ftp-*.AppImage`, or Properties > Allow executing as a program) and run it. It runs on Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 12, Fedora 36 or newer, and others like them. It keeps its settings in `~/.local/share/chiral-ftp`. **Windows** 1. Download `chiral-ftp-1.1-windows-x64.exe` from the releases. It also runs on Windows on ARM PCs, through Windows' own x64 emulation. 2. Run it; nothing needs installing. The program isn't signed, so the first time Windows SmartScreen says it doesn't recognise it: choose **More info > Run anyway**. When Windows Firewall asks, allow private networks, so a console or phone can reach the server. It keeps its settings in `%APPDATA%\chiral-ftp`. To keep everything on a USB stick instead, settings included, make a folder named `data` next to the `.exe`: chiral-ftp then keeps its settings there. On a computer, the window has a sidebar instead of a start screen: the server, the web app, Quick connect, the message log and Settings, each a page with ordinary switches, fields and buttons. On a computer, chiral-ftp is a server first: - **FTP / SFTP server**: shares your home folder over SFTP, or FTP if you switch the protocol. **Choose…** shares another folder; **Whole computer** shares everything, after a confirmation. chiral-ftp's own settings (saved passwords, the server's login and its key) are never shared. SFTP is on port 2222; an app connecting the first time asks you to trust the key shown on the screen. - **Web app**: the file manager and the FTP / SFTP client, opened in your browser. By default only this computer can reach it; switch "Reachable from" to your home network to use it from a phone or another device. - **Network**: on a computer with several networks (Wi-Fi, Ethernet, a VPN), Settings > Network chooses the address shown. Automatic prefers your home network. To build it yourself instead, see [Building](#building): `make PLATFORM=sdl` (it needs libssh, `brew install libssh`, for the SFTP server), then `make PLATFORM=sdl app` for the Mac app. ## Quick connect Every copy of chiral-ftp on your network shows up in every other one, PS5, Switch, Mac or Linux alike, whatever it's doing. Nothing has to be running and nothing has to be set up. 1. **Open Quick connect.** On a console: press **Up** on the start screen. On a computer: **Quick connect** in the sidebar (**⌘K** on a Mac). The devices nearby are listed, with their names and addresses. | On a console (PS5) | On a computer (Mac) | |---|---| | ![Quick connect on the PS5: the Mac and the Switch nearby](docs/screenshots/ps5-quick-connect.png) | ![Quick connect on a Mac: the Switch and the PS5 nearby](docs/screenshots/computer-quick-connect.png) | 2. **Pick one and press Connect** (Cross on the PS5, A on the Switch). Your screen shows a 4-digit code while it waits. | The PS5 asks the Mac | The Mac asks the Switch | |---|---| | ![The PS5 asking the Mac, code 3810](docs/screenshots/ps5-quick-connect-asking.png) | ![The Mac asking the Switch, code 2425](docs/screenshots/computer-quick-connect-asking.png) | 3. **On the other device, check the code and press Allow.** It starts its server and hands your device a login of its own. You're connected and browsing its files: in the client on a console, in the web app on a computer. | The Mac, asked by the PS5 | The Switch, asked by the Mac | |---|---| | ![The Mac shows the PS5's request with the same code, 3810](docs/screenshots/computer-quick-connect-request.png) | ![The Switch shows the Mac's request with the same code, 2425](docs/screenshots/switch-quick-connect-request.png) | The login it hands out works **only from the device that asked**, and only while that server runs. **Deny**, or let the request run out (30 seconds), and nothing is shared. A console is visible while chiral-ftp is open on its start screen; a computer, whenever the app is open. Quick connect uses UDP port 47121 on your local network. ## Using it | | PS5 | Switch | Keyboard | |---|---|---|---| | Move | D-pad / sticks | D-pad / sticks | Arrow keys | | Open or select | Cross | A | Enter | | Back | Circle | B | Esc | | Menu | OPTIONS | Plus | M | | Mark | Square | Y | Space | | Copy / transfer the marked items | Triangle | X | T | | Switch sides | R1 | R | Tab | | Transfer queue | Touchpad | Minus | G | A game controller works on a computer too, with the same layout. So does the mouse: what it is over is highlighted, a click opens it, a right click opens the menu, the wheel scrolls, and clicking outside a panel closes it. On a Mac, the menu bar has the server (⌘1), the web app (⌘2), Quick connect (⌘K), Settings (⌘,), Transfers (⌘T) and the message log (⌘L). - Every screen's menu starts with **Start screen**, which always brings you back; holding **Back** does the same. On the start screen, the menu opens Settings and About. - On the Switch, the touch screen works as well: tap to select, drag to scroll. - Text is typed with the system keyboard. **Security.** The FTP server and the web app run on your local network. The FTP server's login is shown on its screen: change it from the default. The web app has no login: anyone on your network can use it while it runs, so stop it when you're done. Both can change anything on the console's storage. ## Screenshots ### On the consoles The PS5 and the Switch share one layout, made for the TV and a controller. What changes is the buttons shown at the bottom, the drives, and what the start screen and About say about the console. | PS5 | Nintendo Switch | |---|---| | **Start screen**

![The server page, SFTP running](docs/screenshots/computer-server.png) | **Web app**
